          DerivedCategory.Q.map
            (image.ι (Stacks.AdicSystem.IdealPowerTensorComparison.idealPowerMultiplication K I n))

declarations.name: Stacks.ProjectiveDimension.Additivity.projectiveDimension_restrictScalars_quotient_eq_add
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0929.** Let `R` be a Noetherian local ring, `I` an ideal of `R`, and `E` a
nonzero finite `R ⧸ I`-module. If `R ⧸ I` has finite projective dimension over `R` and `E` has
finite projective dimension over `R ⧸ I`, then the restriction of `E` to `R` has finite
projective dimension, equal to the sum of the two given projective dimensions.
declarations.statement:
theorem projectiveDimension_restrictScalars_quotient_eq_add
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [Small.{v} R]
    (I : Ideal R) (E : Type v) [AddCommGroup E] [Module (R ⧸ I) E]
    [Nontrivial E] [Module.Finite (R ⧸ I) E]
    (hRI : Module.projectiveDimension R (R ⧸ I) ≠ ⊤)
    (hE : Module.projectiveDimension (R ⧸ I) E ≠ ⊤) :
    let E_R := (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{v} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj
      (ModuleCat.of (R ⧸ I) E)
    Module.projectiveDimension R E_R ≠ ⊤ ∧
      Module.projectiveDimension R E_R =
        Module.projectiveDimension R (R ⧸ I) + Module.projectiveDimension (R ⧸ I) E

declarations.name: IsAbsolutelyFlat
declarations.doc: **Stacks 092B.** A commutative ring is absolutely flat if every module over it is flat.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAbsolutelyFlat (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : Prop

declarations.name: flat_of_flat_of_mul_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 092C.** Let `A → B` be a ring map such that the multiplication
map `μ : B ⊗_A B → B` makes `B` a flat `(B ⊗_A B)`-module. Let `N` be a
`B`-module. If `N` is flat as an `A`-module, then `N` is flat as a
`B`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_of_flat_of_mul_flat
    (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (hB : Algebra.MulFlat A B)
    (N : Type*) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
    [Module A N] [IsScalarTower A B N]
    (hN : Module.Flat A N) :
    Module.Flat B N

declarations.name: HasWeakDimensionLE
declarations.doc:
A commutative ring has weak dimension at most `d` if every module over it has Tor
dimension at most `d`.
declarations.statement:
def HasWeakDimensionLE {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (comparison : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N) ⟶
        ((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} A)).obj N).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison N)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (d : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: hasWeakDimensionLE_of_weaklyEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 092E.** A weakly étale algebra over a commutative ring of weak dimension at most
`d` also has weak dimension at most `d`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasWeakDimensionLE_of_weaklyEtale
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (derivedTensorA :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (comparisonA : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensorA.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N) ⟶
        ((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} A)).obj N).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerivedA : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      (derivedTensorA.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparisonA N)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (d : ℕ) (hAB : Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B)
    (hA : HasWeakDimensionLE derivedTensorA comparisonA isLeftDerivedA d) :
    ∃ (derivedTensorB :
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} B) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} B) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} B))
      (comparisonB : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{v} B,
        DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
            derivedTensorB.flip.obj
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) 0).obj N) ⟶
          ((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{v} B)).obj N).mapHomologicalComplex
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
      (isLeftDerivedB : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{v} B,
        (derivedTensorB.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} B) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
          (comparisonB N)
          (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{v} B) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))),
      HasWeakDimensionLE derivedTensorB comparisonB isLeftDerivedB d

declarations.name: absolutelyFlat_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a commutative ring `A`, the following are equivalent: `A` has weak dimension at most
zero; `A` is absolutely flat; `A` is reduced and every prime ideal is maximal; and the
localization of `A` at every prime ideal is a field.

Weak dimension is `HasWeakDimensionLE`, which carries the derived tensor product, its comparison
with termwise tensor product, and the universal property certifying that the comparison exhibits
the derived tensor product as a total left derived functor. Those data are part of the statement,
exactly as in the source and as in `weakDimensionLE_one_tfae` (Stacks 092S).
declarations.statement:
theorem absolutelyFlat_tfae (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (comparison : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N) ⟶
        ((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} A)).obj N).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison N)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    [ HasWeakDimensionLE derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived 0,
      (∀ (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M], Module.Flat A M),
      IsReduced A ∧ ∀ p : Ideal A, p.IsPrime → p.IsMaximal,
      ∀ (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime], IsField (Localization.AtPrime p) ].TFAE

declarations.name: product_of_fields_absolutely_flat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 092G.** A product of fields is an absolutely flat ring: every module
over `∏ i, K i` is flat.
declarations.statement:
theorem product_of_fields_absolutely_flat {I : Type*} (K : I → Type*) [∀ i, Field (K i)]
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module (∀ i, K i) M] : Module.Flat (∀ i, K i) M

declarations.name: mulFlat_baseChange
declarations.doc:
If the multiplication map `μ_{B/A} : B ⊗[A] B → B` is flat, then the multiplication map
`μ_{B'/A'} : B' ⊗[A'] B' → B'` of the base change `B' = A' ⊗[A] B` is flat.

Under the canonical `A'`-algebra isomorphism
`e : (A' ⊗[A] B) ⊗[A'] (A' ⊗[A] B) ≃ₐ[A'] A' ⊗[A] (B ⊗[A] B)` one has
`μ_{B'/A'} = (id_{A'} ⊗ μ_{B/A}) ∘ e`, and `id_{A'} ⊗ μ_{B/A}` is flat by
`RingHom.Flat.tensorProductMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mulFlat_baseChange (A : Type u₁) (B : Type u₂) (A' : Type u₃)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing A']
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A A']
    (h : Algebra.MulFlat A B) :
    Algebra.MulFlat A' (A' ⊗[A] B)

declarations.name: weaklyEtale_baseChange
declarations.doc:
If `A → B` is weakly étale, then `A' → B'` is weakly étale, where `B' = A' ⊗[A] B` is the
base change. This is Mathlib's base-change instance for `Algebra.WeaklyEtale`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyEtale_baseChange (A : Type u₁) (B : Type u₂) (A' : Type u₃)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing A']
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A A']
    (h : Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B) :
    Algebra.WeaklyEtale A' (A' ⊗[A] B)

declarations.name: absolutelyFlat_and_isReduced_of_flat_lmul'
declarations.doc:
If the multiplication map `B ⊗[A] B → B` is flat, then an absolutely flat base
ring makes `B` absolutely flat. Under the same hypothesis, if `A` is reduced and
`A → B` is weakly étale, then `B` is reduced.
declarations.statement:
theorem absolutelyFlat_and_isReduced_of_flat_lmul'
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (hμ : (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B)).Flat) :
    ((∀ (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M], Module.Flat A M) →
      ∀ (N : Type v) [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N], Module.Flat B N) ∧
    (IsReduced A → Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B → IsReduced B)

declarations.name: mulFlat_comp
declarations.doc:
If the multiplication maps `μ_{B/A}` and `μ_{C/B}` are both flat, then the multiplication
map `μ_{C/A}` is flat.

After reducing to a single universe with `Algebra.MulFlat.ulift_iff`, this is the
factorisation `μ_{C/A} = μ_{C/B} ∘ (C ⊗_A C → C ⊗_B C)` together with
`RingHom.Flat.mapOfCompatibleSMul` and `RingHom.Flat.comp`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mulFlat_comp (A : Type u₁) (B : Type u₂) (C : Type u₃) [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [CommRing C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    (hAB : Algebra.MulFlat A B) (hBC : Algebra.MulFlat B C) : Algebra.MulFlat A C

declarations.name: weaklyEtale_comp
declarations.doc:
If `A → B` and `B → C` are both weakly étale, then the composite `A → C` is weakly étale.
This is Mathlib's `Algebra.WeaklyEtale.trans`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyEtale_comp (A B C : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    (hAB : Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B) (hBC : Algebra.WeaklyEtale B C) :
    Algebra.WeaklyEtale A C

declarations.name: flat_lmul'_and_weaklyEtale_of_faithfullyFlat
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B → C` be compatible maps of commutative rings and suppose that `C` is
faithfully flat over `B`. Then flatness of the multiplication map `C ⊗[A] C → C` descends
to the multiplication map `B ⊗[A] B → B`; consequently, if `A → C` is weakly étale, then
`A → B` is weakly étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_lmul'_and_weaklyEtale_of_faithfullyFlat
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (C : Type w)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    [Module.FaithfullyFlat B C] :
    ((Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := C)).Flat →
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B)).Flat) ∧
    (Algebra.WeaklyEtale A C → Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B)

declarations.name: weaklyEtale_of_comp
declarations.doc:
If `A → B` and `A → C` are weakly étale, then a compatible algebra map `B → C`
is weakly étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyEtale_of_comp (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (C : Type w)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra B C] [Algebra A C] [IsScalarTower A B C]
    (hAB : Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B) (hAC : Algebra.WeaklyEtale A C) :
    Algebra.WeaklyEtale B C

declarations.name: formallyUnramified_of_flat_lmul
declarations.doc:
If the multiplication map `B ⊗[A] B → B` is flat, then `B` is formally unramified
over `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallyUnramified_of_flat_lmul (A : Type u) (B : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (h : (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' A (S := B)).Flat) :
    Algebra.FormallyUnramified A B

declarations.name: weaklyEtale_of_isLocalization_etale_filteredColimit
declarations.doc:
A localization and an étale algebra over a commutative ring are weakly étale, and an
arbitrary filtered colimit of weakly étale algebras is weakly étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyEtale_of_isLocalization_etale_filteredColimit
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    (∀ (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] (M : Submonoid A)
      [IsLocalization M B], Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B) ∧
    (∀ (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B],
      Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B) ∧
    (∀ (J : Type w) [SmallCategory J] [IsFiltered J] [Small.{max u (w + 1)} J]
      (F : J ⥤ CommAlgCat.{w} A) (c : Cocone F), IsColimit c →
      (∀ j, Algebra.WeaklyEtale A (F.obj j)) → Algebra.WeaklyEtale A c.pt)

declarations.name: isSeparable_of_flat_lmul
declarations.doc:
Let `L/K` be a field extension. If the multiplication map `L ⊗[K] L → L` is flat,
then `L/K` is algebraic and separable.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparable_of_flat_lmul (K : Type u) (L : Type v)
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    (h : (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' K (S := L)).Flat) :
    Algebra.IsSeparable K L

declarations.name: flat_lmul_weaklyEtale_filteredColimitEtale_tfae
declarations.doc:
Let `B` be an algebra over a field `K`. The following are equivalent: the multiplication
map `B ⊗[K] B → B` is flat; `B` is weakly étale over `K`; and `B` is a filtered colimit of
étale `K`-algebras. Under these equivalent conditions, every finitely generated
`K`-subalgebra of `B` is étale over `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem flat_lmul_weaklyEtale_filteredColimitEtale_tfae
    (K : Type u) (B : Type v) [Field K] [CommRing B] [Algebra K B] :
    [ (Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' K (S := B)).Flat,
      Algebra.WeaklyEtale K B,
      ∃ (J : Type v) (_ : SmallCategory J) (_ : IsFiltered J)
        (F : J ⥤ CommAlgCat.{v} K) (c : Cocone F) (_ : IsColimit c),
        Nonempty (c.pt ≅ CommAlgCat.of K B) ∧ ∀ j, Algebra.Etale K (F.obj j) ].TFAE ∧
      ((Algebra.TensorProduct.lmul' K (S := B)).Flat →
        ∀ A : Subalgebra K B, A.FG → Algebra.Etale K A)

declarations.name: isSeparable_and_isAlgebraic_residueField_of_weaklyEtale
declarations.doc:
If `A → B` is weakly étale and a prime `q` of `B` lies over a prime `p` of `A`, then the
canonical residue field extension `κ(p) → κ(q)` is separable algebraic.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparable_and_isAlgebraic_residueField_of_weaklyEtale
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (h : Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B) (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime]
    (q : Ideal B) [q.IsPrime] (hpq : p = q.comap (algebraMap A B)) :
    letI := (Ideal.ResidueField.map p q (algebraMap A B) hpq).toAlgebra
    Algebra.IsSeparable p.ResidueField q.ResidueField ∧
      Algebra.IsAlgebraic p.ResidueField q.ResidueField

declarations.name: weakDimensionLE_one_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 092S.** For a commutative ring, weak dimension at most one, flatness of all
ideals, flatness of all finitely generated ideals, flatness of submodules of flat modules, and
the valuation-ring property for all localizations at prime ideals are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
theorem weakDimensionLE_one_tfae
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (derivedTensor :
      DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤
        DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A))
    (comparison : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      DerivedCategory.Q ⋙
          derivedTensor.flip.obj
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N) ⟶
        ((tensoringRight (ModuleCat.{u} A)).obj N).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    (isLeftDerived : ∀ N : ModuleCat.{u} A,
      (derivedTensor.flip.obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj N)).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
        (comparison N)
        (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    List.TFAE
      [ HasWeakDimensionLE derivedTensor comparison isLeftDerived 1,
        ∀ I : Ideal A, Module.Flat A I,
        ∀ I : Ideal A, I.FG → Module.Flat A I,
        ∀ (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M],
          Module.Flat A M → ∀ N : Submodule A M, Module.Flat A N,
        ∀ (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime],
          ∃ _ : IsDomain (Localization.AtPrime p),
            ValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime p) ]

declarations.name: weakDimensionLE_one_and_isLocalization_pi_fractionRing
declarations.doc:
A product of valuation rings has weak dimension at most one, and the product of their
fraction fields is the localization at the componentwise non-zero-divisors.
declarations.statement:
theorem weakDimensionLE_one_and_isLocalization_pi_fractionRing
    (J : Type v) (A : J → Type u) (K : J → Type w)
    [∀ j, CommRing (A j)] [∀ j, IsDomain (A j)] [∀ j, ValuationRing (A j)]
    [∀ j, Field (K j)] [∀ j, Algebra (A j) (K j)] [∀ j, IsFractionRing (A j) (K j)] :
    HasWeakDimensionLEOne (∀ j, A j) ∧
      IsLocalization
        (.pi Set.univ (fun j ↦ nonZeroDivisors (A j)))
        (∀ j, K j)

declarations.name: exists_isPullback_with_weakDimensionLE_one
declarations.doc:
A normal domain and its fraction field fit into a cartesian square whose lower-left ring has
weak dimension at most one and whose lower map is flat, injective, and a ring epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPullback_with_weakDimensionLE_one
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A]
    (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] :
    ∃ (V L : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing V) (_ : CommRing L)
      (_ : Algebra A V) (_ : Algebra K L) (_ : Algebra V L)
      (_ : Module.Flat V L) (_ : Algebra.IsEpi V L),
      HasWeakDimensionLEOne V ∧
        Function.Injective (algebraMap V L) ∧
        IsPullback
          (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A K).ulift)
          (CommRingCat.ofHom
            ((algebraMap A V).comp ULift.ringEquiv.toRingHom))
          (CommRingCat.ofHom
            ((algebraMap K L).comp ULift.ringEquiv.toRingHom))
          (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap V L))

declarations.name: isIntegrallyClosedIn_of_isEpi_of_flat_of_weakDimensionLE_one
declarations.doc:
A flat injective epimorphism of commutative rings whose source has weak dimension at most one
makes the source integrally closed in the target.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegrallyClosedIn_of_isEpi_of_flat_of_weakDimensionLE_one
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Module.Flat A B] [Algebra.IsEpi A B]
    (hA : HasWeakDimensionLEOne A)
    (hinjective : Function.Injective (algebraMap A B)) :
    IsIntegrallyClosedIn A B

declarations.name: isIntegrallyClosedIn_tensorProduct_fractionField_of_weaklyEtale
declarations.doc:
A weakly étale algebra over a normal domain is integrally closed in its scalar extension
to any fraction field of the domain.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIntegrallyClosedIn_tensorProduct_fractionField_of_weaklyEtale
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (K : Type w)
    [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra A B] [Algebra A K]
    [IsDomain A] [IsIntegrallyClosed A] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (hAB : Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B) :
    IsIntegrallyClosedIn B (B ⊗[A] K)

declarations.name: RingHom.exists_henselianLocalRing_of_isIntegral_of_isDomain
declarations.doc:
An integral homomorphism from a henselian local ring to a domain makes the target a
henselian local ring and is a local homomorphism. If the source residue field is separably
closed, then the target residue field is separably closed and its extension along the induced
residue-field homomorphism is purely inseparable.
declarations.statement:
theorem RingHom.exists_henselianLocalRing_of_isIntegral_of_isDomain
    {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [HenselianLocalRing A] [IsDomain B] (f : A →+* B) (hf : f.IsIntegral) :
    ∃ (hB : HenselianLocalRing B) (hlocal : IsLocalHom f),
      letI : IsLocalRing B := hB.toIsLocalRing
      letI : IsLocalHom f := hlocal
      IsSepClosed (ResidueField A) →
        IsSepClosed (ResidueField B) ∧ (ResidueField.map f).IsPurelyInseparable

declarations.name: isLocalRing_tensorProduct_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 092Y.** Let `A → B` and `A → C` be local homomorphisms of local
rings, with `A → C` integral and at least one of the induced residue field
extensions `κ(m_C)/κ(m_A)`, `κ(m_B)/κ(m_A)` purely inseparable. Then
`D = B ⊗_A C` is a local ring and the canonical maps `B → D`, `C → D` are
local homomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalRing_tensorProduct_of_isIntegral
    (A B C : Type*) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C]
    [IsLocalRing A] [IsLocalRing B] [IsLocalRing C]
    [Algebra A B] [Algebra A C]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A C)]
    [Algebra.IsIntegral A C]
    (hins :
      @IsPurelyInseparable (ResidueField A) (ResidueField C) _ _
        (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (algebraMap A C)).toAlgebra ∨
      @IsPurelyInseparable (ResidueField A) (ResidueField B) _ _
        (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map (algebraMap A B)).toAlgebra) :
    IsLocalRing (TensorProduct A B C) ∧
      IsLocalHom (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom : B →+* TensorProduct A B C) ∧
      IsLocalHom ((Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight : C →ₐ[A] TensorProduct A B
          C).toRingHom)

declarations.name: bijective_algebraMap_of_weaklyEtale_of_isLocalHom
declarations.doc:
A local weakly étale algebra over a strictly henselian local ring has bijective structure
homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_algebraMap_of_weaklyEtale_of_isLocalHom
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [HenselianLocalRing A]
    [IsSepClosed (ResidueField A)] [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] (hAB : Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B) :
    Function.Bijective (algebraMap A B)

declarations.name: Stacks.NoncommChangeOfRings.Silver.restrictScalars_fullyFaithful_of_epi
declarations.doc:
Restriction of scalars along an epimorphism `α : R ⟶ R'` of sheaves of rings on a site is
fully faithful. Equivalently, for any two sheaves of `R'`-modules every morphism of their
restrictions to `R` is uniquely `R'`-linear. The site is assumed small relative to the universe
of the sections of the rings (`Small.{u} C`, `LocallySmall.{u} C`).
declarations.statement:
theorem restrictScalars_fullyFaithful_of_epi [Epi α] :
    Nonempty (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{v} α).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: Stacks.PresheafOfModules.CoextendScalars.restrictScalars_coextendScalars_adjunction
declarations.doc:
The adjunction `φ*_res ⊣ φ_*^coext`: restriction of scalars along `φ` is left adjoint to the
coextension-of-scalars functor `φ_*^coext = coextendScalars φ`, with Hom-bijection `homEquiv`
(forward `α ↦ (g ↦ a' ↦ α(a' • g))`, inverse `β ↦ (g ↦ β(g)(1))`). This is the
presheaf-of-modules analogue of `ModuleCat.restrictCoextendScalarsAdj`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrictScalars_coextendScalars_adjunction (φ : O ⟶ O') :
    PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u} φ ⊣ coextendScalars φ
declarations.comment: the presheaf case: Hom_O(G, F) = Hom_O'(G, SheafHom_O(O', F)) for C a category and O ⟶ O' a map of presheaves of rings

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.CoextendScalars.sheafRestrictCoextendAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0932 / Lemma 18.27.8, sheaf case.** For a morphism `φ : O ⟶ O'` of sheaves of
rings on a site, restriction of scalars along `φ` is left adjoint to coextension of scalars
`F ↦ SheafHom_O(O', F)`, i.e. `Hom_O(G_O, F) = Hom_{O'}(G, SheafHom_O(O', F))` naturally in the
sheaf of `O'`-modules `G` and the sheaf of `O`-modules `F`. This is
`restrictScalars_coextendScalars_adjunction`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sheafRestrictCoextendAdjunction (φ : O ⟶ O') :
    SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u} φ ⊣ sheafCoextendScalars φ
declarations.comment: the sheaf case: Hom_O(G, F) = Hom_O'(G, SheafHom_O(O', F)) for C a site and O ⟶ O' a map of sheaves of rings

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.cechShortComplex_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0934**, exactness in the middle. For a covering family
`{U_i → U}` with existing pairwise fibre products, the Čech sequence
`⊕_{i, j} j_{U_i ×_U U_j!} O_{U_i ×_U U_j} ⟶ ⊕_i j_{U_i!} O_{U_i} ⟶ j_{U!} O_U` is exact at
`⊕_i j_{U_i!} O_{U_i}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechShortComplex_exact (h𝒰 : 𝒰.sieve₀ ∈ J U) :
    (cechShortComplex.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R 𝒰).Exact
declarations.comment:
exactness in the middle, i.e. the relations among the generators
  `j_{U_i!} O_{U_i}` of `j_{U!} O_U` are generated by the fibre products

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.epi_cechShortComplex_g
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0934**, exactness at `j_{U!} O_U`. This is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.epi_sigmaDesc_extensionByZeroUnitMap` — the surjectivity half of
Stacks 0G1W, which needs neither the fibre products nor quasi-compactness — read off the
Čech short complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_cechShortComplex_g (h𝒰 : 𝒰.sieve₀ ∈ J U) :
    Epi (cechShortComplex.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R 𝒰).g
declarations.comment: exactness at `j_{U!} O_U`, i.e. the right-hand map is an epimorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.sheafOfModules_sections_preserves_coproducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0935, part (2).** For a sheaf of rings, sections of sheaves of modules over a
quasi-compact object preserve arbitrary direct sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafOfModules_sections_preserves_coproducts
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (R : Sheaf J RingCat.{r}) (W : C) (hW : J.IsQuasiCompactObject W) (ι : Type w) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete ι)
      (SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{s} R ⋙
        (sheafSections J AddCommGrpCat.{s}).obj (op W))

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.isColimitSectionsFiniteSubcoproductsCocone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0935, the content of the proof of part (1).** Let `W` be a quasi-compact object of
a site and let `f` be a family of sheaves of sets. Sections over `W` carry the presentation of
`∐ f` as the filtered colimit of its finite sub-coproducts to a colimit of sets: the sections
over `W` of `∐_{i ∈ I} f i` are the filtered colimit, over the finite subsets `E ⊆ I`, of the
sections over `W` of `∐_{i ∈ E} f i`.

This is the whole of the source's argument for part (1). Part (1) itself, that sections over `W`
commute with coproducts, is false as stated; see the module documentation and
`not_preservesColimitsOfShape_pempty_of_bot_mem`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isColimitSectionsFiniteSubcoproductsCocone (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (W : C) (hW : J.IsQuasiCompactObject W) {ι : Type max u v}
    (f : ι → Sheaf J (Type max u v)) :
    IsColimit (((sheafSections J (Type max u v)).obj (op W)).mapCocone
      (finiteSubcoproductsCocone f))
declarations.comment:
part (1), the assertion the source's proof establishes: sections over a
  quasi-compact object carry the presentation of an arbitrary coproduct of sheaves of sets as the
  filtered colimit of its finite sub-coproducts to a colimit of sets. The source's part (1), that
  sections commute with coproducts, is false as stated; see the module documentation.

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.bijective_colimit_post_sheafSections_of_isQuasiCompactObject_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0935, part (1), corrected.** Evaluation of sheaves of sets at a quasi-compact object
carries a filtered colimit whose transition maps are monomorphisms to a colimit of sets: the
canonical map `colim_i F_i(U) ⟶ (colim_i F_i)(U)` is bijective.

This is the approved erratum for part (1). The source's part (1) — that sections over a
quasi-compact object commute with *arbitrary* coproducts — is **false**; the counterexamples are
in this module's documentation and `not_preservesColimitsOfShape_pempty_of_bot_mem`. The corrected
statement is Stacks 0738 part (3), so this is an exact wrapper of that theorem's third conjunct
and introduces no new machinery.

`isColimitSectionsFiniteSubcoproductsCocone` below is this statement specialized to the filtered
diagram of finite sub-coproducts, whose transition maps are monomorphisms; that specialization
alone does not state the corrected part (1), which is why it is registered separately.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_colimit_post_sheafSections_of_isQuasiCompactObject_of_mono
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) {I : Type w₁} [Category.{w₂} I] [IsFiltered I]
    [HasColimitsOfShape I (Type max u v)] (F : I ⥤ Sheaf J (Type max u v)) (U : C)
    (hU : J.IsQuasiCompactObject U)
    (hmono : ∀ (i j : I) (f : i ⟶ j), Mono (F.map f)) :
    Function.Bijective (colimit.post F ((sheafSections J (Type max u v)).obj (op U)))
declarations.comment:
part (1), CORRECTED per the approved erratum: evaluation at a quasi-compact object
  carries a filtered colimit with monomorphic transition maps to a colimit of sets, which is
  Stacks 0738 part (3). The source's part (1), that sections commute with arbitrary coproducts, is
  false; the counterexamples are preserved in this module's documentation and in
  `not_preservesColimitsOfShape_pempty_of_bot_mem`.

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.homFromExtensionByZeroUnit_preservesCoproducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0936.** On a ringed site, morphisms out of the extension by zero of the structure
sheaf of the slice site over a quasi-compact object commute with arbitrary direct sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem homFromExtensionByZeroUnit_preservesCoproducts
    (hU : X.J.IsQuasiCompactObject U) (ι : Type w) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete ι)
      (preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (op
        ((SheafOfModules.pullback.{u}
          (F := Over.forget U)
          (𝟙 (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).over U) :
            (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).over U) ⟶
              (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).over U))).obj
            (SheafOfModules.unit
              (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).over U)))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.QuasiCompactObjectsSituation
declarations.doc:
A site together with a distinguished collection of its objects. This is the standing data
of the Stacks Project's discussion of presentations of sheaves of modules.
declarations.statement: structure QuasiCompactObjectsSituation (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C]

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.QuasiCompactObjectsSituation.HasEnoughObjects
declarations.doc:
Condition (1): every object of the site has a covering family all of whose members belong
to the distinguished collection.
declarations.statement: def HasEnoughObjects (S : QuasiCompactObjectsSituation C) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.QuasiCompactObjectsSituation.ObjectsAreQuasiCompact
declarations.doc: Condition (2): every object of the distinguished collection is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement: def ObjectsAreQuasiCompact (S : QuasiCompactObjectsSituation C) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.QuasiCompactObjectsSituation.CoverPullbacksAreQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
Condition (3): for a covering family of a distinguished object whose members are
distinguished, every pairwise fibre product exists and is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement: def CoverPullbacksAreQuasiCompact (S : QuasiCompactObjectsSituation C) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.QuasiCompactObjectsSituation.CoverPullbacksAreQuasiCompact
declarations.doc:
Condition (3) of Stacks Project, Tag 0937: for a cover whose source objects and target
belong to the distinguished collection, every pairwise fibre product is quasi-compact.

The `HasPullback` conjunct records the existence implicit in the source. The second conjunct
is quantified over the instance used to choose a pullback, so the condition does not depend
on a global choice of pullbacks.
declarations.statement:
def QuasiCompactObjectsSituation.CoverPullbacksAreQuasiCompact {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (S : QuasiCompactObjectsSituation C) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_epi_sigma_moduleShriekConstant_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093B part (2) for sheaves of `Λ`-modules on the small étale site.** Every sheaf of
`Λ`-modules on the small étale site of a scheme `X` is a quotient of a direct sum
`⊕ j_{U_a!}\underline{\Lambda}_{U_a}` of extensions by zero of constant free rank-one module
sheaves at *quasi-compact quasi-separated* étale objects `U_a` of `X`.

The source takes the objects of the direct sum from a collection which covers the site and
consists of quasi-compact objects; on the small étale site that collection is the quasi-compact
quasi-separated étale objects, which cover every étale object by
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.hasEnoughObjects_quasiCompactObjectsSituation`. Maps out of
`j_{U!}\underline{\Lambda}_U` are sections over `U` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.moduleShriekConstantCoyonedaIso`, so the index set is the pairs of a
quasi-compact quasi-separated étale object and a section of the sheaf over it.

This strengthens `AlgebraicGeometry.epi_desc_moduleShriekConstant`, whose direct sum runs over all
étale objects, and it is the generation step of Stacks 093C for sheaves of modules: compactness of
the generators, `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinitelyPresentable_moduleShriekConstant`, is available
exactly at the quasi-compact objects.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_epi_sigma_moduleShriekConstant_qcqs (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme)
    (Λ : Type r) [CommRing Λ]
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r} Λ)) :
    ∃ (A : Type max (u + 1) r) (U : A → SmallEtale B X.1 X.property),
      (∀ a, IsQCQSEtaleObject B X (U a)) ∧
        ∃ p : (∐ fun a => moduleShriekConstant.{u, r, r} B X Λ (U a)) ⟶ F, Epi p
declarations.comment: part (2), sheaves of modules, generation by qcqs étale objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_epi_sigma_moduleShriekConstant_affine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093B part (2) for sheaves of `Λ`-modules, generation by affine étale objects.**
Every sheaf of `Λ`-modules on the small étale site of `X` is a quotient of a direct sum
`⊕ j_{U_a!}\underline{\Lambda}_{U_a}` of extensions by zero of constant free rank-one module
sheaves at *affine* étale objects `U_a` of `X`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_epi_sigma_moduleShriekConstant_qcqs` with the distinguished
collection of the source taken to be the affine étale objects rather than the quasi-compact
quasi-separated ones; they cover every étale object just as well.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_epi_sigma_moduleShriekConstant_affine
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r} Λ)) :
    ∃ (A : Type max (u + 1) r) (U : A → SmallEtale B X.1 X.property),
      (∀ a, SmallEtale.IsAffine B X.1 X.property (U a)) ∧
        ∃ p : (∐ fun a => moduleShriekConstant.{u, r, r} B X Λ (U a)) ⟶ F, Epi p
declarations.comment: part (2), sheaves of modules, generation by affine étale objects

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.exists_epi_coproduct_extensionByZeroUnit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093B (2).** Every sheaf of `R`-modules is a quotient of a direct sum
`⊕ j_{U_i!} R|_{U_i}` of extensions by zero of the restricted structure sheaf at distinguished
objects: one summand for each pair of a distinguished object and a section of the module over
it. This is the generation step on which the presentations of Tag 093C rest.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_coproduct_extensionByZeroUnit
    (S : QuasiCompactObjectsSituation C) (hEnough : S.HasEnoughObjects)
    (R : Sheaf S.topology RingCat.{w}) (M : SheafOfModules.{max u₁ v₁ w v} R) :
    ∃ (A : Type (max u₁ v₁ w v)) (U : A → C), (∀ i, U i ∈ S.objects) ∧
      ∃ p : (∐ fun i => extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, w, v} R (U i)) ⟶ M, Epi p

declarations.name: Stacks.exists_epi_coproduct_sheafifiedYoneda
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093B (1).** Every sheaf of sets is covered by a coproduct of sheafified
representables from the distinguished collection: it is the target of a surjective map whose
source is a coproduct of the sheaves `h_{U_i}^#` with `U_i` distinguished.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_coproduct_sheafifiedYoneda
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    (S : QuasiCompactObjectsSituation C)
    (hEnough : S.HasEnoughObjects) (F : Sheaf S.topology (Type max u v)) :
    letI : HasColimitsOfSize.{max u v, max u v}
        (Sheaf S.topology (Type max u v)) := CategoryTheory.Sheaf.instHasColimitsOfSize
    ∃ (I : Type max u v) (U : I → C),
      (∀ i, U i ∈ S.objects) ∧
        ∃ (f : (∐ fun i ↦ (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda S.topology).obj (U i)) ⟶ F),
          Epi f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.moduleSheavesAreFilteredColimitsOfPresentations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093C for sheaves of `Λ`-modules on the small étale site.** Every sheaf of
`Λ`-modules on the small étale site of a scheme `X` is a filtered colimit of sheaves carrying a
finite shriek presentation by quasi-compact quasi-separated étale objects, that is, of cokernels
of maps between finite direct sums of the sheaves `j_{U!}\underline{\Lambda}_U` at such objects.

This is the source's own proof. Two applications of Stacks 093B part (2),
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_epi_sigma_moduleShriekConstant_qcqs`, write `F` as the cokernel of a map
`g` between two direct sums of the sheaves `j_{U!}\underline{\Lambda}_U` at quasi-compact
quasi-separated étale objects: the first gives an epimorphism `p` onto `F`, the second an
epimorphism `q` onto the kernel of `p`, and `q ≫ ker p` has cokernel `F`. Those generators are
compact, by `AlgebraicGeometry.isFinitelyPresentable_moduleShriekConstant` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.hasFiniteQuasiCompactCoverings`, so `g` restricts to maps between
finite subsums; and the cokernels of those restrictions form a filtered diagram with colimit the
cokernel of `g`, which is
`CategoryTheory.Limits.exists_isFilteredColimit_cokernel_finiteSubcoproducts`.

The quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `X` are used only for the compactness of the
generators, which asks for
`AlgebraicGeometry.SmallEtale.hasFiniteQuasiCompactCoverings`; the generation step itself needs
neither. This discharges the hypothesis `h093C` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleModuleSheaf`, Stacks 03SA (3), which
carries the same two assumptions on `X`.

[Stacks Tag 093C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/093C) part (2) is stated for an arbitrary
situation of Stacks 0937 and an arbitrary sheaf of rings by
`Stacks.Sites.isFilteredColimit_of_hasEnoughQuasiCompactObjects`, which carries the tag; this is
that statement at the small étale site with constant coefficients `Λ`, in the shriek spelling the
étale development consumes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem moduleSheavesAreFilteredColimitsOfPresentations :
    ModuleSheavesAreFilteredColimitsOfPresentations B X Λ
declarations.comment: part (2), sheaves of modules on the small étale site, shriek spelling

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.setSheavesAreFilteredColimitsOfPresentations
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093C (1) for the small étale site.** Every sheaf of sets on the small étale site of
`X` is a filtered colimit of sheaves which are coequalizers of a pair of maps between finite
coproducts of sheaves represented by quasi-compact quasi-separated étale objects of `X`.

This is the hypothesis `h093C` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isFilteredColimit_isConstructibleSetSheaf`, Stacks 03SA (1). It is the
specialisation to the collection of quasi-compact quasi-separated étale objects of
`Stacks.isFilteredColimit_of_hasEnoughQuasiCompactObjects`, which states
[Stacks Tag 093C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/093C) part (1) for an arbitrary
situation and carries the tag.
declarations.statement:
public theorem setSheavesAreFilteredColimitsOfPresentations :
    SetSheavesAreFilteredColimitsOfPresentations B X
declarations.comment: part (1), sheaves of sets, étale site

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.isFilteredColimit_of_hasEnoughQuasiCompactObjects
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093C (modules).** Every module sheaf is a filtered colimit
of finite cokernel presentations by extensions by zero from distinguished objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFilteredColimit_of_hasEnoughQuasiCompactObjects
    (S : QuasiCompactObjectsSituation C)
    (hEnough : S.HasEnoughObjects) (hqc : S.ObjectsAreQuasiCompact)
    (R : Sheaf S.topology RingCat.{w}) (F : SheafOfModules.{v} R) :
    ∃ (I : Type (max u₁ v₁ w v)) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : IsFiltered I)
      (D : I ⥤ SheafOfModules.{max u₁ v₁ w v} R)
      (ι : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj ((moduleULift.{max u₁ v₁ w v} R).obj F)),
      Nonempty (IsColimit (Cocone.mk ((moduleULift.{max u₁ v₁ w v} R).obj F) ι)) ∧
        ∀ i, HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation S R (D.obj i)

declarations.name: Stacks.isFilteredColimit_of_hasEnoughQuasiCompactObjects
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093C (1).** Under conditions (1) and (2) of Situation 0937,
every sheaf of sets is a filtered colimit of coequalizers between finite coproducts of
sheafified representables of distinguished objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFilteredColimit_of_hasEnoughQuasiCompactObjects
    (S : QuasiCompactObjectsSituation C)
    (hEnough : S.HasEnoughObjects) (hqc : S.ObjectsAreQuasiCompact)
    (F : Sheaf S.topology (Type max u v)) :
    ∃ (I : Type max u v) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : IsFiltered I)
      (D : I ⥤ Sheaf S.topology (Type max u v))
      (ι : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj F),
      ∃ (_ : IsColimit (Cocone.mk F ι)),
        ∀ i, HasFiniteRepresentableCoequalizerPresentation S (D.obj i)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Equation 18.30.7.2 (Tag 093D).** A sheaf of `R`-modules *has a finite
presentation by extensions by zero* if it is isomorphic to the cokernel of a morphism between
two finite direct sums of extensions by zero `j_{U!} O_U` of the structure sheaf at
distinguished objects `U`.
declarations.statement:
def HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation.{u₁', v₁', w', t'} {C : Type u₁'} [Category.{v₁'} C]
    (S : QuasiCompactObjectsSituation C) (R : Sheaf S.topology RingCat.{w'})
    (G : SheafOfModules.{max u₁' v₁' w' t'} R) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation
declarations.doc:
A finite presentation as a cokernel between finite coproducts of extensions by zero
of the structure sheaf restricted to distinguished objects. All comparisons take place
after the canonical universe lift; no size assumption is imposed on `G`.
declarations.statement:
def HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation
    (S : QuasiCompactObjectsSituation C)
    (R : Sheaf S.topology RingCat.{w}) (G : SheafOfModules.{v} R) : Prop
declarations.comment: the modules of Equation 18.30.7.2, after the canonical universe lift

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.hasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation_cokernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093E.** On a site with a distinguished collection of objects which
covers every object and consists of quasi-compact objects, the cokernel of a morphism between
two sheaves of modules with finite presentations by extensions by zero again has a finite
presentation by extensions by zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation_cokernel (hEnough : S.HasEnoughObjects)
    (hqc : S.ObjectsAreQuasiCompact) {F G : SheafOfModules.{max u₁ v₁ w t} R} (f : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} S R F)
    (hG : HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} S R G) :
    HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} S R (cokernel f)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_finite_refinement_isIso_cokernelMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093F.** A finite presentation by extensions by zero can be changed
along coverings of its target generators without changing its cokernel: finite subfamilies
`K'_i` of the given coverings and a finite family `{W_l}` of distinguished objects can be chosen
so that the resulting square over `f` induces an isomorphism on the cokernels of its horizontal
maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_refinement_isIso_cokernelMap
    (hEnough : S.HasEnoughObjects) (hqc : S.ObjectsAreQuasiCompact)
    (hqs : S.CoverPullbacksAreQuasiCompact)
    {n m : ℕ} {U : Fin n → C} (V : Fin m → C)
    (hU : ∀ i, U i ∈ S.objects) (hV : ∀ j, V j ∈ S.objects)
    (𝒰 : ∀ i, PreZeroHypercover.{max u₁ v₁} (U i))
    (h𝒰 : ∀ i, (𝒰 i).sieve₀ ∈ S.topology (U i))
    (h𝒰obj : ∀ i k, (𝒰 i).X k ∈ S.objects)
    (f : (∐ fun j ↦ extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R (V j)) ⟶
      ∐ fun i ↦ extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R (U i)) :
    ∃ (T : ∀ i, Set (𝒰 i).I₀) (𝒱 : ∀ i, PreZeroHypercover.{max u₁ v₁} (U i)),
      (∀ i, (T i).Finite) ∧
        (∀ i, 𝒱 i = (𝒰 i).restrictIndex (Subtype.val : T i → (𝒰 i).I₀)) ∧
        (∀ i, (𝒱 i).sieve₀ ∈ S.topology (U i)) ∧
        ∃ (L : Type (max u₁ v₁)) (_ : Finite L) (W : L → C), (∀ l, W l ∈ S.objects) ∧
          ∃ (g : (∐ fun l ↦ extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R (W l)) ⟶
                ∐ fun x : Σ i, (𝒱 i).I₀ ↦ extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R ((𝒱 x.1).X x.2))
              (p : (∐ fun l ↦ extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R (W l)) ⟶
                ∐ fun j ↦ extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R (V j)),
            g ≫ refinementAugmentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R 𝒱 = p ≫ f ∧
              Epi (refinementAugmentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R 𝒱) ∧
              ∀ h : g ≫ refinementAugmentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R 𝒱 = p ≫ f,
                IsIso (cokernel.map g f p (refinementAugmentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R 𝒱) h)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.hasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093G.** On a site with a distinguished collection of objects which
covers every object, consists of quasi-compact objects and whose coverings have quasi-compact
pairwise fibre products, the sheaves of modules with a finite presentation by extensions by zero
are stable under extensions: if `E` is a short exact sequence of sheaves of modules whose outer
terms have such presentations, so does its middle term.

This is Stacks' own argument. Choose presentations `⊕A_{V_j} ⟶ ⊕A_{U_i} ⟶ F₁ ⟶ 0` and
`⊕A_{T_j} ⟶ ⊕A_{W_i} ⟶ F₃ ⟶ 0`. Since `F₂ ⟶ F₃` is an epimorphism, each generator `A_{W_i}`
lifts to `F₂` after passing to a covering of `W_i` by distinguished objects
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_hypercover_lift_extensionByZeroUnit`), and Stacks 093F
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_finite_refinement_isIso_cokernelMap`) replaces the `W_i` by a
finite subfamily of that covering without changing the cokernel. The rest is
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.hasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation_of_lifted_generators`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation_of_shortExact (hEnough : S.HasEnoughObjects)
    (hqc : S.ObjectsAreQuasiCompact) (hqs : S.CoverPullbacksAreQuasiCompact)
    (E : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{max u₁ v₁ w t} R)) (hE : E.ShortExact)
    (h₁ : HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} S R E.X₁)
    (h₃ : HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} S R E.X₃) :
    HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} S R E.X₂

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.isWeakSerreClass_hasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093H.** On a site with a distinguished collection of objects which
covers every object, consists of quasi-compact objects and whose coverings have quasi-compact
pairwise fibre products, the sheaves of modules with a finite presentation by extensions by zero
form a **weak Serre subcategory** of the category of all sheaves of modules, as soon as the
kernel of every morphism between finite direct sums of extensions by zero of the restricted
structure sheaf at distinguished objects has such a presentation.

Closure under cokernels is Stacks 093E and closure under extensions is Stacks 093G; closure
under kernels is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.isClosedUnderKernels_of_presentations` applied to the
family of finite direct sums of extensions by zero at distinguished objects, which is exactly
where the hypothesis enters.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakSerreClass_hasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation (hEnough : S.HasEnoughObjects)
    (hqc : S.ObjectsAreQuasiCompact) (hqs : S.CoverPullbacksAreQuasiCompact)
    (hKernel : ∀ (n m : ℕ) (U : Fin n → C) (V : Fin m → C),
      (∀ i, U i ∈ S.objects) → (∀ j, V j ∈ S.objects) →
      ∀ f : (∐ fun j => extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R (V j)) ⟶
          (∐ fun i => extensionByZeroUnit.{u₁, v₁, w, t} R (U i)),
        HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} S R (kernel f)) :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass
      (fun F : SheafOfModules.{max u₁ v₁ w t} R =>
        HasFiniteExtensionByZeroPresentation.{u₁, v₁, w, t} S R F)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.surjective_constantSections_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 093J**, surjectivity half. If `f : M ⟶ N` is a surjection of `R`-modules then
the induced map on the sections over `U` of the associated constant sheaves is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_constantSections_map {M N : ModuleCat.{x} R} (f : M ⟶ N)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f.hom) (U : C) :
    Function.Surjective ((constantSections J U).map f).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.injective_constantSections_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 093J**, injectivity half. `constantSections` takes injections of modules to
injections.
declarations.statement:
theorem injective_constantSections_map {M N : ModuleCat.{x} R} (f : M ⟶ N)
    (hf : Function.Injective f.hom) (U : C) :
    Function.Injective ((constantSections J U).map f).hom

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.range_constantSections_map_eq_ker
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 093J**. The functor of sections of a constant sheaf of modules is exact: an exact
pair of morphisms of `R`-modules is taken to an exact pair.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_constantSections_map_eq_ker (U : C) {A B D : ModuleCat.{x} R}
    (α : A ⟶ B) (β : B ⟶ D) (h : LinearMap.range α.hom = LinearMap.ker β.hom) :
    LinearMap.range ((constantSections J U).map α).hom =
      LinearMap.ker ((constantSections J U).map β).hom

declarations.name: constantSheaf_shortExact_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**(1) Exactness as abelian sheaves.**

Given a short exact sequence `0 → A → B → C → 0` of abelian groups (a short complex `S`
with `S.ShortExact`), applying the constant sheaf functor yields a short exact sequence
of abelian sheaves `0 → A → B → C → 0` on the site `C`.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantSheaf_shortExact_of_shortExact
    (S : ShortComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    (S.map (constantSheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u})).ShortExact

declarations.name: constantSheaf_sections_shortExact_of_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**(2) Exactness as abelian presheaves.**

The same induced sequence of constant sheaves is exact as a sequence of abelian
presheaves: for every object `U` of `C`, the sequence of abelian groups obtained by
taking sections over `U` is short exact. In particular `B → C` is objectwise surjective
on sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantSheaf_sections_shortExact_of_shortExact
    (S : ShortComplex AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (hS : S.ShortExact) (U : C) :
    ((S.map (constantSheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u})).map
        ((sheafSections J AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj (op U))).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.bijective_tensorComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 093K.** Tensoring with a finitely presented external module commutes with taking
sections of a constant sheaf: the canonical comparison is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_tensorComparison (M : ModuleCat.{x} R) (Q : ModuleCat.{y} R)
    [Module.FinitePresentation R Q] (N : ModuleCat.{x} R)
    (e : TensorProduct R M Q ≃ₗ[R] N) (U : C) :
    Function.Bijective (tensorComparison J M Q N e U).1

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.flat_constantSections

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isFlat_completedConstantSheaf
declarations.doc:
The completed constant sheaf `R̲^∧ = lim (R/Iⁿ)̲` is flat over the constant
sheaf of rings `R̲`. By Tags 03ES and 03ET this follows from the objectwise flatness of
`flat_completedConstantSheaf_sections`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFlat_completedConstantSheaf :
    AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlat (completedConstantSheafOverConstantRing J I)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantTensorAction_comp_completedConstantSheafResidueMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093M**, the inclusion `I̲ · R̲^∧ ⊂ I̲^∧`: the canonical map `R̲^∧ ⟶ (R/I)̲`, read
over `Osharp`, kills the multiplication `I̲ ⊗_{Osharp} R̲^∧ ⟶ R̲^∧`. Since `I̲^∧` is the kernel
of that canonical map, this says that the product of the constant sheaf of ideals with the
completed constant sheaf is contained in the completed constant ideal sheaf.

The multiplication is killed by any map annihilating every constant multiple, and the residue
map is such a map: an element of `I` acts as zero on `(R/I)̲`, hence `a (m)` acts as zero on its
bridge.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantTensorAction_comp_completedConstantSheafResidueMap :
    constantTensorAction J a (ModuleCat.ofHom I.subtype) (completedConstantSheaf J I) ≫
        sheafOfModulesOfConstantRingMap J (associatedRingMap J a)
          (completedConstantSheafResidueMap J I) = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.idealSmulMap_comp_of_constantTensorAction_comp_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093M**, the inclusion `I F ⊂ I̲ · F`: a map out of `F` over `Osharp` which kills the
multiplication `I̲ ⊗_{Osharp} F ⟶ F` also kills the map `∐_{f ∈ I} F ⟶ F` of multiplication by
the elements of `I`, whose image is `I F`.

Multiplying by a single element of `I` is tested on the images of the sheafification unit, where
the multiplication's value is known; the passage from the elements of `I` to the single map out
of the coproduct is the preservation of coproducts by the bridge, read off its adjunction.
declarations.statement:
theorem idealSmulMap_comp_of_constantTensorAction_comp_eq_zero (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} R))
    {Z : SheafOfModules.{w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Osharp)}
    (g : (sheafOfModulesOfConstantRingFunctor J (associatedRingMap J a)).obj F ⟶ Z)
    (hg : constantTensorAction J a (ModuleCat.ofHom I.subtype) F ≫ g = 0) :
    (sheafOfModulesOfConstantRingFunctor J (associatedRingMap J a)).map
        (idealSmulMap J I F) ≫ g = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isColimitCokernelCoforkConstantTensorAction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093M**, the identification `R̲^∧/I̲ · R̲^∧ = (R/I)̲`: the canonical map
`R̲^∧ ⟶ (R/I)̲`, read as a map of sheaves of modules over `Osharp`, is a cokernel of the
multiplication `I̲ ⊗_{Osharp} R̲^∧ ⟶ R̲^∧` by the constant sheaf of ideals `I̲`.

A map out of the bridge of `R̲^∧` which kills the multiplication kills the multiplications by
the elements of `I` as well, so its transpose across the bridge adjunction factors through
`(R/I)̲` by the identification `R̲^∧/I R̲^∧ = (R/I)̲`; transposing back gives the
factorisation, which is unique because the canonical map is an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def isColimitCokernelCoforkConstantTensorAction :
    IsColimit (CokernelCofork.ofπ
      ((sheafOfModulesOfConstantRingFunctor J (associatedRingMap J a)).map
        (completedConstantSheafResidueMap J I))
      (constantTensorAction_comp_completedConstantSheafResidueMap J a I))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.completedConstantSheaf_quotientByConstantIdealSmul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093M.** The canonical isomorphism `R̲^∧/I̲ · R̲^∧ ≅ (R/I)̲` from the quotient of the
completed constant sheaf by the product of the constant sheaf of ideals with it to the constant
sheaf of the quotient ring, as sheaves of modules over `Osharp`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def completedConstantSheaf_quotientByConstantIdealSmul :
    cokernel (constantTensorAction J a (ModuleCat.ofHom I.subtype)
        (completedConstantSheaf J I)) ≅
      (sheafOfModulesOfConstantRingFunctor J (associatedRingMap J a)).obj
        ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I)))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.completedConstantSheaf_quotientByConstantIdealSmul_hom_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093M.** The isomorphism `R̲^∧/I̲ · R̲^∧ ≅ (R/I)̲` intertwines the cokernel
projection with the canonical map `R̲^∧ ⟶ (R/I)̲`, so it is the identification of Tag 093M and
not a bare existence statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem completedConstantSheaf_quotientByConstantIdealSmul_hom_comp :
    cokernel.π (constantTensorAction J a (ModuleCat.ofHom I.subtype)
          (completedConstantSheaf J I)) ≫
        (completedConstantSheaf_quotientByConstantIdealSmul J a I).hom =
      (sheafOfModulesOfConstantRingFunctor J (associatedRingMap J a)).map
        (completedConstantSheafResidueMap J I)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.range_sections_completedConstantIdealSheafInclusion
declarations.doc:
On every object `U` of the site the sections of the completed constant ideal sheaf inside
`Γ(U, R̲^∧)` are exactly `I · Γ(U, R̲^∧)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem range_sections_completedConstantIdealSheafInclusion (U : C) :
    LinearMap.range (((sheafSections J (ModuleCat.{w} R)).obj (op U)).map
        (completedConstantIdealSheafInclusion J I)).hom =
      I • (⊤ : Submodule R (((sheafSections J (ModuleCat.{w} R)).obj (op U)).obj
        (completedConstantSheaf J I)))
declarations.comment: I Λ̂(U) = Î(U) on every object

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.epi_completedConstantIdealSheafLift
declarations.doc:
The elements of `I` generate the completed constant ideal sheaf over the completed constant
sheaf: the factorisation of `∐_{f ∈ I} R̲^∧ ⟶ R̲^∧` through `I̲^∧` is an epimorphism, i.e.
`I · R̲^∧ = I̲^∧` as subsheaves of `R̲^∧`.
declarations.statement: instance epi_completedConstantIdealSheafLift : Epi (completedConstantIdealSheafLift J I)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.completedConstantSheaf_quotientByIdealSmul
declarations.doc:
The canonical isomorphism `R̲^∧/I R̲^∧ ≅ (R/I)̲` from the quotient of the completed constant
sheaf by the ideal it is completed at to the constant sheaf of the quotient ring.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def completedConstantSheaf_quotientByIdealSmul :
    cokernel (idealSmulMap J I (completedConstantSheaf J I)) ≅
      (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.completedConstantSheaf_quotientByIdealSmul_hom_comp
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism `R̲^∧/I R̲^∧ ≅ (R/I)̲` carries the cokernel projection to the canonical map
`R̲^∧ ⟶ (R/I)̲`.
declarations.statement:
theorem completedConstantSheaf_quotientByIdealSmul_hom_comp :
    cokernel.π (idealSmulMap J I (completedConstantSheaf J I)) ≫
        (completedConstantSheaf_quotientByIdealSmul J I).hom =
      completedConstantSheafResidueMap J I

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.completedConstantSheafResidueMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `R̲^∧ ⟶ (R/I)̲` from the completed constant sheaf to the constant sheaf of
the quotient ring: the projection to the level `n = 1` of the completion, followed by the
identification `R/I¹ = R/I`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def completedConstantSheafResidueMap :
    completedConstantSheaf J I ⟶
      (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))
declarations.comment: the canonical map from the completion to the constant sheaf of Λ/I

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.shortExact_completedConstantIdealShortComplex
declarations.doc: The sequence `0 → I̲^∧ → R̲^∧ → (R/I)̲ → 0` of sheaves of `R`-modules is short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_completedConstantIdealShortComplex :
    (completedConstantIdealShortComplex J I).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the completed ideal sheaf is the kernel of the map from the completion to (Λ/I)̲

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.completedConstantSheaf_quotientByCompletedIdeal
declarations.doc:
The canonical isomorphism `R̲^∧/I̲^∧ ≅ (R/I)̲` from the quotient of the completed constant
sheaf by the completed constant ideal sheaf to the constant sheaf of the quotient ring.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def completedConstantSheaf_quotientByCompletedIdeal :
    cokernel (completedConstantIdealSheafInclusion J I) ≅
      (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} R)).obj (ModuleCat.of R (R ⧸ I))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.completedConstantSheaf_quotientByCompletedIdeal_hom_comp
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism `R̲^∧/I̲^∧ ≅ (R/I)̲` intertwines the cokernel projection with the canonical
map `R̲^∧ ⟶ (R/I)̲`.
declarations.statement:
theorem completedConstantSheaf_quotientByCompletedIdeal_hom_comp :
    cokernel.π (completedConstantIdealSheafInclusion J I) ≫
        (completedConstantSheaf_quotientByCompletedIdeal J I).hom =
      completedConstantSheafResidueMap J I

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheaf_idealAction_sections
declarations.doc:
The image of the constant ideal sheaf on each object is the ideal acting on sections of the
constant ring sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantSheaf_idealAction_sections (U : C) :
    LinearMap.range
      ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} R) ⋙
        (sheafSections J (ModuleCat.{w} R)).obj (op U)).map
          (ModuleCat.ofHom I.subtype)).hom =
      I • (⊤ : Submodule R
        ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} R) ⋙
          (sheafSections J (ModuleCat.{w} R)).obj (op U)).obj (ModuleCat.of R R)))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheaf_quotientByConstantIdeal
declarations.doc:
The canonical isomorphism from the quotient by the constant ideal sheaf to the constant sheaf
of the quotient ring.

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheaf_quotientByConstantIdeal_hom_comp
declarations.doc:
The quotient isomorphism intertwines the cokernel projection with the constant sheaf of the
ring quotient map.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantSheaf_quotientByConstantIdeal_hom_comp :
    let f := (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} R)).map (ModuleCat.ofHom I.subtype)

The canonical isomorphism from the quotient by the image ideal subsheaf, equivalently the

The image-ideal quotient isomorphism intertwines its quotient projection with the constant

declarations.statement:
theorem constantSheaf_quotientByIdealAction_hom_comp :
    let f := (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} R)).map (ModuleCat.ofHom I.subtype)
    cokernel.π (image.ι f) ≫ (constantSheaf_quotientByIdealAction J I).hom =

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Constant.constantModuleSheaf_isFiniteType_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093N, part (1).** On a site whose topos is not empty, a constant sheaf
of modules is of finite type if and only if its value is a finitely generated module.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantModuleSheaf_isFiniteType_iff
    [∀ U : C, HasWeakSheafify (J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ U : C, (J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (hJ : ∃ U : C, ¬ (⊥ : Sieve U) ∈ J U) (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (constantModuleSheaf J M) ↔ ModuleCat.isFG R M

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Constant.constantModuleSheaf_isFinitePresentation_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093N, part (2).** On a site with an object that is not sheaf
theoretically empty, a constant sheaf of modules is of finite presentation if and only if its
value is a finitely presented module.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantModuleSheaf_isFinitePresentation_iff
    (hJ : ∃ U : C, ¬ (⊥ : Sieve U) ∈ J U) (M : ModuleCat.{w} R) :
    SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation (constantModuleSheaf J M) ↔
      Module.FinitePresentation R M

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsLocallyConstant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093Q (2).** A sheaf is locally constant if every object of the site has a covering
on each member of which its restriction is a constant sheaf.
declarations.statement: class IsLocallyConstant [∀ U : C, HasWeakSheafify (J.over U) D] (F : Sheaf J D) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteLocallyConstant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093Q (3).** A sheaf with values in a concrete category is finite locally constant
if every object of the site has a covering on each member of which it is a constant sheaf with
finite underlying value. For `Type` and `Grp`, this is respectively the source's notion for
sheaves of sets and sheaves of groups.

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.IsConstant
registrations.comment: part (1): a constant sheaf is an object in the essential image of the constant sheaf functor

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isConstant_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093R, the constant case.** The inverse image of a constant sheaf of sets along a
morphism of topoi is constant.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isConstant_inverseImage (G : Sheaf K (Type w)) [Sheaf.IsConstant K G] :
    Sheaf.IsConstant J (f.inverseImage.obj G)
declarations.comment: constant sheaves of sets, for an arbitrary morphism of topoi

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isLocallyConstant_sheafPullback
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R, for a morphism of sites.** The inverse image of a locally constant sheaf along a
continuous functor of sites is locally constant, for arbitrary coefficients.

The trivializing covering is taken over the final object of `C`, whose image is final in `D`
because `G` is left exact; no object with a final image has to be supplied.

The source states the tag for an arbitrary morphism of topoi, whose inverse image need not be
induced by a functor between the two sites; the attribute is qualified accordingly.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isLocallyConstant_sheafPullback (F : Sheaf J A) [hF : IsLocallyConstant J F] :
    IsLocallyConstant K ((G.sheafPullback A J K).obj F)
declarations.comment: locally constant sheaves with arbitrary coefficients, for the inverse image along a morphism of sites

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isFiniteLocallyConstant_sheafPullback_of_coverPreserving
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R.** The inverse image of a finite locally constant sheaf along a continuous functor of
sites is finite locally constant, for arbitrary concrete coefficients. In particular this holds for
sheaves of abelian groups, which is the case Tag 03RZ (2) needs.

One trivializing covering `{X i ⟶ ⊤_C}` is enough, by
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isFiniteLocallyConstant_of_cover`. Its image under `G` covers `G.obj ⊤_C`,
which is final in `D` because `G` is left exact, and on a member the restriction of `G^* F` is
constant with the same finite value, by
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantIsoOverPullbackSheafPullback`.
declarations.comment: finite locally constant sheaves with arbitrary concrete coefficients, for the inverse image along a morphism of sites

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isConstant_abelianInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093R, the constant abelian case.** The inverse image of a constant sheaf of abelian
groups along a morphism of topoi is constant.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isConstant_abelianInverseImage (G : Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{w}) [Sheaf.IsConstant K G] :
    Sheaf.IsConstant J ((CategoryTheory.Sites.abelianInverseImage f).obj G)
declarations.comment: constant sheaves of abelian groups, for an arbitrary morphism of topoi

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isFiniteLocallyConstant_abelianInverseImage_of_smallSites
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R, the finite abelian case.** The inverse image of a finite locally constant sheaf
of abelian groups along an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on
two small sites is finite locally constant.

No functor between the two sites is assumed. Finite local constancy of an abelian sheaf is a
property of its underlying sheaf of sets by
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isFiniteLocallyConstant_iff_forget`, the underlying sheaf of sets of the
abelian inverse image is the geometric inverse image of the underlying sheaf of sets, and the
latter preserves finite local constancy by
`MorphismOfTopoi.isFiniteLocallyConstant_inverseImage_of_smallSites`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isFiniteLocallyConstant_abelianInverseImage_of_smallSites
    [∀ U : C, HasWeakSheafify (J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    [∀ V : D, HasWeakSheafify (K.over V) AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (G : Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{w}) [hG : IsFiniteLocallyConstant K G] :
    IsFiniteLocallyConstant J ((CategoryTheory.Sites.abelianInverseImage f).obj G)
declarations.comment: finite locally constant sheaves of abelian groups, for an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two small sites

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isLocallyConstant_abelianInverseImage_of_smallSites
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R for locally constant sheaves of abelian groups.** The inverse image of a locally
constant sheaf of abelian groups along an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of
sheaves of sets on two small sites is locally constant.

No functor between the two sites, no final object in either, and no finiteness of the local
values is assumed. The covering of an object `U` of `C` is the one
`Stacks.Topos.exists_cover_inverseImage_sections` produces for the family of sheaves represented
by the objects of `D` over which `G` is trivialized as an abelian sheaf, and on a member `V` of
it the section it carries trivializes the abelian inverse image over `V`, with the same
trivializing group, by
`MorphismOfTopoi.abelianConstantIsoOverPullbackInverseImageOfSection`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isLocallyConstant_abelianInverseImage_of_smallSites
    (G : Sheaf K AddCommGrpCat.{w}) [hG : IsLocallyConstant K G] :
    IsLocallyConstant J ((CategoryTheory.Sites.abelianInverseImage f).obj G)
declarations.comment: locally constant sheaves of abelian groups, for an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two small sites

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isLocallyConstant_grpInverseImage_of_smallSites
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R for locally constant sheaves of groups.** The inverse image of a locally constant
sheaf of groups along an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two
small sites is locally constant.

No functor between the two sites, no final object in either, no commutativity of the local
values and no finiteness of them is assumed. The covering of an object `U` of `C` is the one
`Stacks.Topos.exists_cover_inverseImage_sections` produces for the family of sheaves represented
by the objects of `D` over which `G` is trivialized as a sheaf of groups, and on a member `V` of
it the section it carries trivializes the inverse image over `V`, with the same trivializing
group, by `MorphismOfTopoi.grpConstantIsoOverPullbackInverseImageOfSection`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isLocallyConstant_grpInverseImage_of_smallSites
    (G : Sheaf K GrpCat.{w}) [hG : IsLocallyConstant K G] :
    IsLocallyConstant J ((CategoryTheory.Sites.grpInverseImage f).obj G)
declarations.comment: locally constant sheaves of groups, for an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two small sites

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isLocallyConstant_moduleInverseImage_of_smallSites
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R for locally constant sheaves of modules over a fixed ring.** The inverse image of a
locally constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules along an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of
sheaves of sets on two small sites is locally constant.

No functor between the two sites, no final object in either, no commutativity of `Λ` and no
finiteness of the local values is assumed. The covering of an object `U` of `C` is the one
`Stacks.Topos.exists_cover_inverseImage_sections` produces for the family of sheaves represented
by the objects of `D` over which `G` is trivialized as a sheaf of `Λ`-modules, and on a member `V`
of it the section it carries trivializes the inverse image over `V`, with the same trivializing
module, by `MorphismOfTopoi.moduleConstantIsoOverPullbackInverseImageOfSection`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isLocallyConstant_moduleInverseImage_of_smallSites (Λ : Type r) [Ring Λ]
    (G : Sheaf K (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)) [hG : IsLocallyConstant K G] :
    IsLocallyConstant J ((CategoryTheory.Sites.moduleInverseImage f Λ).obj G)
declarations.comment: locally constant sheaves of modules over a fixed ring, for an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two small sites

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isLocallyConstant_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R.** The inverse image of a locally constant sheaf of sets along a morphism of
topoi which is equipped with a localization datum is locally constant.

A trivializing covering of the distinguished object of the target site is carried forward by
cover preservation to a covering of a final object of the source site, which is enough for
local constancy there (`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isLocallyConstant_of_cover`), and on a member the
restriction of `f⁻¹G` is constant by
`MorphismOfTopoi.LocalizationDatum.isConstant_overPullback_inverseImage`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isLocallyConstant_inverseImage (d : LocalizationDatum f) (G : Sheaf K (Type w))
    [hG : IsLocallyConstant K G] : IsLocallyConstant J (f.inverseImage.obj G)
declarations.comment: locally constant sheaves of sets, for a morphism of topoi equipped with a localization datum along a functor of sites

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isFiniteLocallyConstant_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R.** The inverse image of a *finite* locally constant sheaf of sets along a
morphism of topoi which is equipped with a localization datum is finite locally constant.

The constant values are unchanged by
`MorphismOfTopoi.LocalizationDatum.constantIsoOverPullbackInverseImage`, so their finiteness
needs no argument.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isFiniteLocallyConstant_inverseImage {FA : Type w → Type w → Type*}
    {CA : Type w → Type wc} [∀ P Q, FunLike (FA P Q) (CA P) (CA Q)]
    [ConcreteCategory.{wc} (Type w) FA]
    (d : LocalizationDatum f) (G : Sheaf K (Type w))
    [hG : IsFiniteLocallyConstant (FD := FA) (CD := CA) K G] :
    IsFiniteLocallyConstant (FD := FA) (CD := CA) J (f.inverseImage.obj G)
declarations.comment: finite locally constant sheaves of sets, for a morphism of topoi equipped with a localization datum along a functor of sites

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isLocallyConstant_inverseImage_of_smallSites
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R.** The inverse image of a locally constant sheaf of sets along an arbitrary
morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two small sites is locally constant.

No functor between the two sites, and no final object in either, is assumed: the covering of an
object `U` of `C` is the one `Stacks.Topos.exists_cover_inverseImage_sections` produces for the
family of sheaves represented by the objects over which `G` is trivialized, and on a member of
it the section it carries trivializes `(f⁻¹G)|_V` by
`MorphismOfTopoi.constantIsoOverPullbackInverseImageOfSection`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isLocallyConstant_inverseImage_of_smallSites (G : Sheaf K (Type w))
    [hG : IsLocallyConstant K G] : IsLocallyConstant J (f.inverseImage.obj G)
declarations.comment: locally constant sheaves of sets, for an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two small sites

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isFiniteLocallyConstant_inverseImage_of_smallSites
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R.** The inverse image of a *finite* locally constant sheaf of sets along an
arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two small sites is finite
locally constant.

The constant values are unchanged by
`MorphismOfTopoi.constantIsoOverPullbackInverseImageOfSection`, so their finiteness needs no
argument; the covering is the one of
`MorphismOfTopoi.isLocallyConstant_inverseImage_of_smallSites`, taken for the objects over which
`G` becomes constant with a finite value.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isFiniteLocallyConstant_inverseImage_of_smallSites {FA : Type w → Type w → Type*}
    {CA : Type w → Type wc} [∀ P Q, FunLike (FA P Q) (CA P) (CA Q)]
    [ConcreteCategory.{wc} (Type w) FA] (G : Sheaf K (Type w))
    [hG : IsFiniteLocallyConstant (FD := FA) (CD := CA) K G] :
    IsFiniteLocallyConstant (FD := FA) (CD := CA) J (f.inverseImage.obj G)
declarations.comment: finite locally constant sheaves of sets, for an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two small sites

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isLocallyConstant_ringInverseImage_of_smallSites
declarations.doc:
**Tag 093R for locally constant sheaves of rings.** The inverse image of a locally constant
sheaf of rings along an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two
small sites is locally constant.

No functor between the two sites, no final object in either, no commutativity of the local
values and no finiteness of them is assumed. The covering of an object `U` of `C` is the one
`Stacks.Topos.exists_cover_inverseImage_sections` produces for the family of sheaves represented
by the objects of `D` over which `G` is trivialized as a sheaf of rings, and on a member `V` of
it the section it carries trivializes the inverse image over `V`, with the same trivializing
ring, by `MorphismOfTopoi.ringConstantIsoOverPullbackInverseImageOfSection`.
declarations.statement:
public lemma isLocallyConstant_ringInverseImage_of_smallSites
    (G : Sheaf K RingCat.{w}) [hG : IsLocallyConstant K G] :
    IsLocallyConstant J ((CategoryTheory.Sites.ringInverseImage f).obj G)
declarations.comment: locally constant sheaves of rings, for an arbitrary morphism of topoi between the topoi of sheaves of sets on two small sites

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_abelian
declarations.doc:
A morphism of locally constant sheaves of abelian groups whose source is finite locally
constant is, on a covering of any object, obtained from a homomorphism of abelian groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_abelian
    (F G : Sheaf J Ab.{w}) (φ : F ⟶ G)
    [hF : IsFiniteLocallyConstant J F] [hG : IsLocallyConstant J G] (U : C) :
    ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (X : I → C) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U),
      Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J U ∧ ∀ i,
        ∃ (A B : Ab.{w}), Finite (A : Type w) ∧
          ∃ (g : A ⟶ B)
            (eF : (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) Ab.{w}).obj A ≅
              (J.overPullback Ab.{w} (X i)).obj F)
            (eG : (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) Ab.{w}).obj B ≅
              (J.overPullback Ab.{w} (X i)).obj G),
              (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) Ab.{w}).map g ≫ eG.hom =
                eF.hom ≫ (J.overPullback Ab.{w} (X i)).map φ
declarations.comment: part (2), sheaves of abelian groups; assumes pointwise right Kan extensions along the localization functors, a limit-existence side condition implied by fibre products in the site

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_abelian_smallSite
declarations.doc:
On a small site `C : Type u`, with the abelian groups in the universe `u`, a morphism of
locally constant sheaves of abelian groups whose source is finite locally constant is, on a
covering of any object, obtained from a homomorphism of abelian groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_abelian_smallSite
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (F G : Sheaf J Ab.{u}) (φ : F ⟶ G)
    [IsFiniteLocallyConstant J F] [IsLocallyConstant J G] (U : C) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (X : I → C) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U),
      Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J U ∧ ∀ i,
        ∃ (A B : Ab.{u}), Finite (A : Type u) ∧
          ∃ (g : A ⟶ B)
