            (eF : (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) Ab.{u}).obj A ≅
              (J.overPullback Ab.{u} (X i)).obj F)
            (eG : (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) Ab.{u}).obj B ≅
              (J.overPullback Ab.{u} (X i)).obj G),
              (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) Ab.{u}).map g ≫ eG.hom =
                eF.hom ≫ (J.overPullback Ab.{u} (X i)).map φ

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_modules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093S (3).** A morphism of locally constant sheaves of `R`-modules whose source is
locally constant of finite type is, on a covering of any object, obtained from a homomorphism of
`R`-modules.

Carries one hypothesis the source does not state: the family of pointwise right Kan extensions
along `(Over.map t).op` out of which `Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheafOverMapIso` is built. It is
a limit-existence side condition on the coefficient category, implied both by `UnivLE.{max u v, w}`
and by fibre products in the site; see this file's implementation notes, and
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_modules_of_hasPullbacks` for the
form carrying no universe condition at all.
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_modules_smallSite` is the form on
a small site, where that side condition is a theorem rather than a hypothesis, and is what part (3)
of the tag is registered on.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_modules
    (F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} R)) (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant R J F) [hG : IsLocallyConstant J G] (U : C) :
    ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (X : I → C) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U),
      Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J U ∧ ∀ i,
        ∃ (A B : ModuleCat.{w} R), ModuleCat.isFG R A ∧
          ∃ (g : A ⟶ B)
            (eF : (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) (ModuleCat.{w} R)).obj A ≅
              (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{w} R) (X i)).obj F)
            (eG : (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) (ModuleCat.{w} R)).obj B ≅
              (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{w} R) (X i)).obj G),
              (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) (ModuleCat.{w} R)).map g ≫ eG.hom =
                eF.hom ≫ (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{w} R) (X i)).map φ
declarations.comment: part (3), sheaves of Λ-modules, with `of finite type` in the equivalent locally-constant-with-finitely-generated-values form of Tag 093N; assumes pointwise right Kan extensions along the localization functors, a limit-existence side condition implied by fibre products in the site

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_modules_smallSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093S (3).** A morphism of locally constant sheaves of `R`-modules whose source is
locally constant of finite type is, on a covering of any object, obtained from a homomorphism of
`R`-modules.

Stated on a small site, `C : Type u` with `SmallCategory C` and the modules in the same universe,
which is the setting of the source and this library's convention for a small site. In it the
statement carries *no* hypothesis beyond the source's: the pointwise right Kan extensions along the
localization functors `(Over.map t).op`, which
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_modules` takes as an input, are
limits over `u`-small index categories and so exist in `ModuleCat.{u} R` by
`ModuleCat.hasLimitsOfShape`; sheafification on each localized site is automatic for the same
reason. Neither `UnivLE` nor fibre products in the site are needed.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map_modules_smallSite
    {R : Type r} [Ring R] {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} R)) (φ : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant R J F) [IsLocallyConstant J G] (U : C) :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (X : I → C) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U),
      Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J U ∧ ∀ i,
        ∃ (A B : ModuleCat.{u} R), ModuleCat.isFG R A ∧
          ∃ (g : A ⟶ B)
            (eF : (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj A ≅
              (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{u} R) (X i)).obj F)
            (eG : (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) (ModuleCat.{u} R)).obj B ≅
              (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{u} R) (X i)).obj G),
              (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) (ModuleCat.{u} R)).map g ≫ eG.hom =
                eF.hom ≫ (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{u} R) (X i)).map φ
declarations.comment: part (3), sheaves of Λ-modules, with `of finite type` in the equivalent locally-constant-with-finitely-generated-values form of Tag 093N

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map
declarations.doc:
A morphism of locally constant sheaves of sets whose source is finite locally constant is, on
a covering of any object, obtained from a map of sets.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_cover_restrict_eq_constantSheaf_map
    (F G : Sheaf J (Type w)) (φ : F ⟶ G)
    [IsFiniteLocallyConstant J F] [IsLocallyConstant J G] (U : C) :
    ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (X : I → C) (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ U),
      Sieve.ofArrows X f ∈ J U ∧ ∀ i,
        ∃ (A B : Type w), Finite A ∧
          ∃ (g : A ⟶ B)
            (eF : (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) (Type w)).obj A ≅
              (J.overPullback (Type w) (X i)).obj F)
            (eG : (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) (Type w)).obj B ≅
              (J.overPullback (Type w) (X i)).obj G),
              (constantSheaf (J.over (X i)) (Type w)).map g ≫ eG.hom =
                eF.hom ≫ (J.overPullback (Type w) (X i)).map φ

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheafHomIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093T (1).** For a finitely presented `Λ`-module `M` and any
`Λ`-module `N`, the constant sheaf on `Hom_Λ(M, N)` is the internal hom of the constant sheaves
on `M` and on `N`:
`Hom_Λ(M, N)̲ ≅ SheafHom_{Λ̲}(M̲, N̲)`,
as sheaves of `Λ`-modules. The module `E` is any representative of `Hom_Λ(M, N)`, supplied with
the identification `e`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def constantSheafHomIso
    [Module.FinitePresentation Λ (M : Type (max u v x))] :
    (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj E ≅
      moduleSheafHom J Λ ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj M)
        ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj N)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheafHomIso_hom_app_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093T (1), the comparison is the canonical one.** The section of the
internal hom over `X` which the isomorphism assigns to the constant section determined by a
homomorphism `f : M ⟶ N` is the restriction to the slice site `C/X` of the morphism of constant
sheaves induced by `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantSheafHomIso_hom_app_apply
    [Module.FinitePresentation Λ (M : Type (max u v x))] (X : Cᵒᵖ) (f : M ⟶ N) :
    ((constantSheafHomIso J Λ M N E e).hom.hom.app X).hom
        (((constantUnit J Λ E).app X).hom (e (ModuleCat.homLinearEquiv (S := Λ) f))) =
      (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ) X.unop).map
        ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).map f)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheafHomIso_hom_app_id
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093T (1)**, applied to the identity: the comparison sends the constant
section given by `𝟙 M` to the identity on every slice.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantSheafHomIso_hom_app_id
    [Module.FinitePresentation Λ (M : Type (max u v x))] (E' : ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)
    (e' : ((M : Type (max u v x)) →ₗ[Λ] (M : Type (max u v x))) ≃ₗ[Λ] E') (X : Cᵒᵖ) :
    ((constantSheafHomIso J Λ M M E' e').hom.hom.app X).hom
        (((constantUnit J Λ E').app X).hom (e' (ModuleCat.homLinearEquiv (S := Λ) (𝟙 M)))) =
      𝟙 ((J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ) X.unop).obj
        ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj M))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheafHomIso_hom_app_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093T (1)**, applied to a composition: the comparison respects
composition of constant homomorphisms on every slice.
declarations.statement:
theorem constantSheafHomIso_hom_app_comp
    [Module.FinitePresentation Λ (M : Type (max u v x))]
    [Module.FinitePresentation Λ (N : Type (max u v x))] (P : ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)
    (E₁ E₂ : ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)
    (e₁ : ((N : Type (max u v x)) →ₗ[Λ] (P : Type (max u v x))) ≃ₗ[Λ] E₁)
    (e₂ : ((M : Type (max u v x)) →ₗ[Λ] (P : Type (max u v x))) ≃ₗ[Λ] E₂)
    (X : Cᵒᵖ) (f : M ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ P) :
    ((constantSheafHomIso J Λ M P E₂ e₂).hom.hom.app X).hom
        (((constantUnit J Λ E₂).app X).hom
          (e₂ (ModuleCat.homLinearEquiv (S := Λ) (f ≫ g)))) =
      ((constantSheafHomIso J Λ M N E e).hom.hom.app X).hom
          (((constantUnit J Λ E).app X).hom (e (ModuleCat.homLinearEquiv (S := Λ) f))) ≫
        ((constantSheafHomIso J Λ N P E₁ e₁).hom.hom.app X).hom
          (((constantUnit J Λ E₁).app X).hom
            (e₁ (ModuleCat.homLinearEquiv (S := Λ) g)))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheafHomIsoOfHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093T (1)**, with `Hom_Λ(M, N)` represented by the morphism type of the
category of `Λ`-modules rather than by an abstract representative.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def constantSheafHomIsoOfHom (M N : ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)
    [Module.FinitePresentation Λ (M : Type (max u v x))] :
    (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj (ModuleCat.of Λ (M ⟶ N)) ≅
      moduleSheafHom J Λ ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj M)
        ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj N)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheafIsomHom
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of Stacks Tag 093T (2)**,
`Isom_Λ(M, N)̲ ⟶ Isom_{Λ̲}(M̲, N̲)`:
the map which sends a linear equivalence to the isomorphism of constant sheaves it induces,
factored through the constant sheaf by the universal property of sheafification. That it is an
isomorphism, which is the content of part (2), is
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheafIsomIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def constantSheafIsomHom :
    (constantSheaf J (Type (max u v x))).obj
        ((M : Type (max u v x)) ≃ₗ[Λ] (N : Type (max u v x))) ⟶
      moduleSheafIsom J Λ ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj M)
        ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj N)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheafIsomIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093T (2).** `Isom_Λ(M, N)̲ ≅ Isom_{Λ̲}(M̲, N̲)` for finitely presented
`M` and `N`, as sheaves of sets. The comparison is the canonical one: it sends the constant section
given by a linear equivalence `e` to the restriction of the isomorphism of constant sheaves `e̲`,
which is `Stacks.ConstantSheaf.toSheafify_constantSheafIsomHom` together with
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantIsomNatTrans_app_apply`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def constantSheafIsomIso
    [Module.FinitePresentation Λ (M : Type (max u v x))]
    [Module.FinitePresentation Λ (N : Type (max u v x))] :
    (constantSheaf J (Type (max u v x))).obj
        ((M : Type (max u v x)) ≃ₗ[Λ] (N : Type (max u v x))) ≅
      moduleSheafIsom J Λ ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj M)
        ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)).obj N)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isLocallyConstant_moduleSheafIsom
declarations.doc:
If `F` and `G` are locally constant sheaves of `Λ`-modules of finite presentation, then
`Isom_{Λ̲}(F, G)` is a locally constant sheaf of sets. The assertion is local on `C`, so `F` and `G`
may be trivialized simultaneously; over a member of the resulting covering they are the constant
sheaves on finitely presented modules `M` and `N`, and then
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantSheafIsomIso` identifies `Isom_{Λ̲}(F, G)` with the constant sheaf on
`M ≃ₗ[Λ] N`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstant_moduleSheafIsom (F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ))
    (hF : IsFinitePresentationLocallyConstantModuleSheaf J Λ F)
    (hG : IsFinitePresentationLocallyConstantModuleSheaf J Λ G) :
    IsLocallyConstant J (moduleSheafIsom J Λ F G)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isLocallyConstant_moduleSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093T (3).** If `F` is a locally constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules of finite
presentation and `G` is a locally constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules, then the internal hom
`SheafHom_{Λ̲}(F, G)` is a locally constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstant_moduleSheafHom (F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ))
    (hF : IsFinitePresentationLocallyConstantModuleSheaf J Λ F) [IsLocallyConstant J G] :
    IsLocallyConstant J (moduleSheafHom J Λ F G)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.moduleSheafIsom
declarations.doc:
**The sheaf of isomorphisms of two sheaves of `Λ`-modules**, i.e. Stacks's
`Isom_{Λ̲}(F, G)`: the subsheaf of `Stacks.ConstantSheaf.moduleSheafHom` of those sections which
have an inverse in `Stacks.ConstantSheaf.moduleSheafHom` taken in the other order. The sections
of the internal hom of sheaves of `Λ`-modules over `X` are the morphisms `F|_X ⟶ G|_X` of sheaves
of `Λ`-modules, which are also the sections of `CategoryTheory.sheafHom`, so this is the
subobject Stacks describes.
declarations.statement:
def moduleSheafIsom (F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v x} Λ)) :
    Sheaf J (Type (max u v x))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isWeakSerreClass_isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 093U (3).** On a site, the finite type locally constant sheaves of modules over
a Noetherian ring form a weak Serre subcategory of the category of sheaves of modules.

The five conditions of Tag 0754 are: strict fullness
(`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf`),
containment of `0`
(`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.containsZero_isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf`), closure under
kernels and under cokernels
(`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isClosedUnderKernels_isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf` and
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isClosedUnderCokernels_isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf`), and
closure under extensions
(`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isClosedUnderExtensions_isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf`).
declarations.statement:
instance isWeakSerreClass_isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass
      (IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isWeakSerreClass_isFiniteLocallyConstantAbelianSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 093U (2).** On a site, the finite locally constant sheaves of abelian groups form
a weak Serre subcategory of the category of all abelian sheaves.

The clause proved here is part (2). It is not an instance of part (3),
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isWeakSerreClass_isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf`: there the
finiteness is finiteness of type over a Noetherian coefficient ring, here it is finiteness of the
local value itself. Part (3) over `ℤ` is however what the proof reduces to, together with the
local annihilation invariant `Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsLocallyAnnihilated`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakSerreClass_isFiniteLocallyConstantAbelianSheaf :
    (isFiniteLocallyConstantAbelianSheaf.{v, u, w} J).IsWeakSerreClass

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isClosedUnderFiniteLimits_and_finiteColimits_isFiniteLocallyConstantSetSheaf
declarations.doc:
On a site, the finite locally constant sheaves of sets are closed under finite limits and
under finite colimits inside the category of all sheaves of sets.

The clause of the tag proved here is part (1), about sheaves of *sets* whose local constant
values are finite sets. It is not an instance of part (3), which is
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isWeakSerreClass_isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf`: there the
finiteness is finiteness of type over a Noetherian coefficient ring, here it is finiteness of the
local value itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem isClosedUnderFiniteLimits_and_finiteColimits_isFiniteLocallyConstantSetSheaf :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderFiniteLimits
        (isFiniteLocallyConstantSetSheaf.{v, u, w} J) ∧
      ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderFiniteColimits
        (isFiniteLocallyConstantSetSheaf.{v, u, w} J)

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isLocallyConstant_tensor
declarations.doc:
The tensor product of two locally constant sheaves of `Λ`-modules on a site is a locally
constant sheaf of `Λ`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyConstant_tensor (F G : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ))
    [IsLocallyConstant J F] [IsLocallyConstant J G] : IsLocallyConstant J (F ⊗ G)

declarations.name: SheafOfModules.DifferentialGradedModule.shortExact_oneSubShift_piMap
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 093W for sheaf differential graded modules.** For a system `M₀ → M₁ → ⋯` of right
differential graded `A`-modules over a sheaf of differential graded algebras, the sequence

`0 → ⊕ₙ Mₙ --(1 - f)--> ⊕ₙ Mₙ --π--> colim Mₙ → 0`

is short exact, where `1 - f` is the morphism with `σₙ ≫ (1 - f) = σₙ - fₙ ≫ σₙ₊₁` on the `n`-th
coprojection and `π` is the morphism with `σₙ ≫ π = ιₙ`.

The general Lemma 093W applies verbatim: `Mod(A, d)` is abelian, it has colimits over `ℕ` and
countable direct sums, and those colimits over `ℕ` are exact by Tag 0FRJ.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_oneSubShift_piMap (F : ℕ ⥤ DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, max u v w} A) :
    ∃ hw : oneSubShift F ≫ piMap F = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk (oneSubShift F) (piMap F) hw).ShortExact

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.shortExact_oneSubShift_piMap
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 093W for differential graded modules.** For a system `M₀ → M₁ → ⋯` of right
differential graded `A`-modules the sequence
`0 → ⊕ₙ Mₙ --(1 - f)--> ⊕ₙ Mₙ --π--> colim Mₙ → 0` is short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_oneSubShift_piMap :
    ∃ w : oneSubShift F ≫ piMap F = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk (oneSubShift F) (piMap F) w).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.CountableCoproducts.hasColimitsOfShape_discrete_of_hasColimitsOfShape_nat
declarations.doc:
**Countable direct sums exist.** If colimits over `ℕ` exist in `A`, then every countable
family of objects has a coproduct, i.e. `A` has colimits of shape `Discrete ℕ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasColimitsOfShape_discrete_of_hasColimitsOfShape_nat
    [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ A] :
    HasColimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) A

declarations.name: Stacks.CountableCoproducts.preservesFiniteLimits_colim_discrete_of_hasColimitsOfShape_nat
declarations.doc:
**Countable direct sums are exact.** If colimits over `ℕ` exist and are exact in `A`, then the
countable-coproduct functor `colim : (Discrete ℕ ⥤ A) ⥤ A` preserves finite limits — which, for a
right-exact additive left adjoint, is exactness: it carries short exact sequences to short exact
sequences.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesFiniteLimits_colim_discrete_of_hasColimitsOfShape_nat
    [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ A] [HasColimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) A]
    (hexact : PreservesFiniteLimits (colim : (ℕ ⥤ A) ⥤ A)) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (colim : (Discrete ℕ ⥤ A) ⥤ A)

declarations.name: Stacks.CountableCoproducts.shortExact_oneSubShift_piMap
declarations.doc:
**The presentation of the colimit: Lemma 093W(2).** For every system over `ℕ` in an abelian
category with countable direct sums and colimits over `ℕ` that are exact, the sequence
`0 ⟶ ∐ₙ Aₙ --(1 - f)--> ∐ₙ Aₙ --π--> colim Aₙ ⟶ 0` is short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_oneSubShift_piMap
    [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ A] [HasColimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) A]
    (hexact : PreservesFiniteLimits (colim : (ℕ ⥤ A) ⥤ A))
    (F : SystemOverNat A) :
    ∃ w : oneSubShift F ≫ piMap F = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk (oneSubShift F) (piMap F) w).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.Injectives.injective_restriction_surjective
declarations.doc:
On a ringed site, restriction of an injective sheaf of modules over the
structure sheaf along a monomorphism of objects of the site is surjective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_restriction_surjective (X : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    {U' U : X.C} (a : U' ⟶ U)
    [Mono a]
    (I : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) [Injective I] :
    Function.Surjective (I.val.presheaf.map a.op)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.pushforwardModules_isKInjective_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 093Y.** Let `(f, f♯) : (Sh(C), O_C) ⟶ (Sh(D), O_D)` be a *flat* morphism of ringed
topoi — flat in the sense of Stacks 04JB, that the ring map `f♯ : f⁻¹O_D ⟶ O_C` is flat — and
let `I` be a K-injective complex of `O_C`-modules. Then the degreewise direct image `f_*I` is a
K-injective complex of `O_D`-modules.

The proof is the source's. The adjunction `f^* ⊣ f_*` of Stacks 03D7 identifies
`Hom_{K(O_D)}(F, f_*I)` with `Hom_{K(O_C)}(f^*F, I)`; flatness makes `f^*` exact (Stacks 04JC),
so it carries an acyclic `F` to an acyclic `f^*F`, on which K-injectivity of `I` makes every
morphism into `I` null-homotopic. That is Stacks 08BJ applied to this adjunction.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforwardModules_isKInjective_of_isFlat
    (f : RingedToposHom X Y) (hf : f.IsFlat)
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{w}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    CochainComplex.IsKInjective
      ((f.pushforwardModules.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.KInjectiveInternalHom.isKInjective_homSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 093Z.** Internal Hom from `O'` takes K-injective complexes of
`O`-modules to K-injective complexes of `O'`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKInjective_homSheaf (φ : O ⟶ O')
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} O) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] :
    letI := (RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.restrictScalarsHomAdjunction φ).right_adjoint_additive
    CochainComplex.IsKInjective
      (((RingedSpaceModuleAdjunction.homSheaf φ).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.exists_rightDerivedLimit_isDerivedLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project Tag 0941.** The value of the right derived functor of ordinary inverse limit
at `K` exists and is a derived limit of the tower of the derived evaluations `Kₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_rightDerivedLimit_isDerivedLimit
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{wG} A]
    [HasLimitsOfShape ℕᵒᵖ A]
    (K : DerivedCategory (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A)) :
    ∃ (h : HasProduct fun n : ℕ => (derivedEvaluationTower K).obj ⟨n⟩),
      ∃ c : Cocone
        (MorphismProperty.Under.forget
            (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) ⊤
            (DerivedCategory.Qh.objPreimage K) ⋙
          Under.forget (DerivedCategory.Qh.objPreimage K) ⋙
          ((lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Qh)),
      (((lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ⥤ A).mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙
          DerivedCategory.Qh).IsRightDerivedValueAt
        (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))
        (DerivedCategory.Qh.objPreimage K) c) ∧
      @IsDerivedLimit (DerivedCategory A) _ _ _ _ _ _
        (derivedEvaluationTower K) h c.pt

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.isUniformlyBoundedAbove_tensor_adicQuotientModule_of_isBoundedAbove
declarations.doc:
**If `K ⊗^L_O O/I` is bounded above then `K ⊗^L_O O/Iⁿ` is uniformly bounded above**: one
integer bounds the cohomology of every `K ⊗^L_O O/Iⁿ` from above. The graded pieces `Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹`
are killed by `I`, hence all bounded above by the bound of `K ⊗^L_O O/I` after tensoring with
`K`, and the tower `0 → Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹ → O/Iⁿ⁺¹ → O/Iⁿ → 0` carries that bound to every quotient.
declarations.statement:
theorem isUniformlyBoundedAbove_tensor_adicQuotientModule_of_isBoundedAbove
    (hQ : Stacks.DerivedCategory.IsBoundedAbove
      ((T.tensor.obj K).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (RingedSite.Modules.{u, u, u} X) 0).obj
          (adicQuotientModule I 1))))
    :
    Stacks.DerivedCategory.IsUniformlyBoundedAbove
      (fun n : ℕ => (T.tensor.obj K).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (RingedSite.Modules.{u, u, u} X) 0).obj
          (adicQuotientModule I n)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.hasTorAmplitude_adicQuotient_of_hasTorAmplitude_adicQuotientOne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0942 part (2).** If `K ⊗^L_O O/I` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` as an object of
`D(O/I)`, then `K ⊗^L_O O/Iⁿ` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` as an object of `D(O/Iⁿ)`, for
every `n`.

A sheaf `F` of `O/Iⁿ`-modules is tested by moving `(K ⊗^L_O O/Iⁿ) ⊗^L_{O/Iⁿ} F[0]` to `D(O)`:
restriction of scalars reflects a vanishing cohomology sheaf, and the projection formula at
`O ⟶ O/Iⁿ` identifies the restriction with `K ⊗^L_O F|_O`. There the filtration of `F|_O` by
the powers of `I` reaches zero, so the vanishing follows from the one at the sheaves of
`O`-modules killed by `I`, which is the hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_adicQuotient_of_hasTorAmplitude_adicQuotientOne
    (T : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u, u, u, _} X)
    (T₁ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u, u, u, _}
      (adicQuotientRingedSite X I 1))
    (n : ℕ)
    (Tₙ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u, u, u, _}
      (adicQuotientRingedSite X I n))
    (K : RingedSite.DerivedModules.{u, u, u, _} X) (a b : ℤ)
    (h : HasTorAmplitude T₁
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.derivedCoefficientChange (toAdicQuotient I 1)).obj K) a b) :
    HasTorAmplitude Tₙ
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.derivedCoefficientChange (toAdicQuotient I n)).obj K) a b
declarations.comment: tor amplitude modulo every power of the ideal

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ProjectionFormulaSection.projectionFormula
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of Section 21.50 of [Stacks, Tag 0943]**, as a morphism of bifunctors on
`D(𝒪_𝒞) × D(𝒪_𝒟)`:

`Rf_*E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_𝒟} K ⟶ Rf_*(E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_𝒞} Lf^*K)`,

natural in `E` and `K` together.  Its value at a pair is the map of [Stacks, Tag 0B56], the
adjoint for `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` of the comparison `Lf^*(Rf_*E ⊗^𝐋 K) ≅ Lf^*Rf_*E ⊗^𝐋 Lf^*K` of
[Stacks, Tag 07A4] followed by the counit `Lf^*Rf_*E ⟶ E` in the first factor.  There is no
hypothesis on `f`, `E` or `K`: the section stresses that the map exists for every morphism of
ringed topoi, and the joint naturality is the naturality of the adjoint-transpose construction
the map instantiates.
declarations.statement: def projectionFormula : pushforwardTensor f ⟶ tensorPullbackPushforward f
declarations.comment: the canonical map of Section 21.50, natural in the two complexes together

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ProjectionFormulaSection.isIso_projectionFormulaNatTransSource
declarations.doc:
**The lemma of Section 21.50 of [Stacks, Tag 0943]**, as an isomorphism of functors.  Let
`f : (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪_𝒞) ⟶ (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪_𝒟)` be a morphism of ringed topoi and let `K ∈ D(𝒪_𝒟)` be
perfect.  Then the canonical map of the section is invertible as a natural transformation of
functors of the complex on the source:

`Rf_*(-) ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_𝒟} K ≅ Rf_*(- ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_𝒞} Lf^*K)` on `D(𝒪_𝒞) ⥤ D(𝒪_𝒟)`.

A natural transformation is invertible as soon as each of its components is, and each component
is [Stacks, Tag 0944].
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_projectionFormulaNatTransSource
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)))
    (hK : RingedSite.IsPerfect Y.toRingedSite K) :
    IsIso (projectionFormulaNatTransSource f K)
declarations.comment: the lemma of Section 21.50: at a perfect complex the canonical map is invertible, here as an isomorphism of the two functors of the complex on the source

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ProjectionFormulaOfToposHom.isIso_projectionFormulaMap_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0944], the projection formula for a perfect complex.** Let
`f : (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪_𝒞) ⟶ (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪_𝒟)` be a morphism of ringed topoi, `E ∈ D(𝒪_𝒞)` and
`K ∈ D(𝒪_𝒟)`. If `K` is perfect, then the canonical map of [Stacks, Tag 0B56]
`Rf_*E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_𝒟} K ⟶ Rf_*(E ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪_𝒞} Lf^*K)` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_projectionFormulaMap_of_isPerfect {X Y : RingedTopos.{u, u, u}}
    (f : RingedToposHom X Y)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)))
    (hK : RingedSite.IsPerfect Y.toRingedSite K) :
    IsIso (projectionFormulaMap f E K)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyContractible.exact_sheafSections_of_isWeaklyContractible
declarations.doc:
Evaluation of abelian sheaves at a weakly contractible object is exact, with weak
contractibility tested in the value universe `w`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_sheafSections_of_isWeaklyContractible
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
    (U : C)
    (hU : ∀ (F G : Sheaf J (Type w)) (φ : F ⟶ G),
      Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective φ → Function.Surjective (φ.hom.app (op U))) :
    exactFunctor (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w}) AddCommGrpCat.{w}
      ((sheafSections J AddCommGrpCat.{w}).obj (op U))

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyContractible.subsingleton_cohomology_of_isWeaklyContractible
declarations.doc:
The positive-degree cohomology of an abelian sheaf over a weakly contractible object
vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_cohomology_of_isWeaklyContractible
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{v}]
    [HasExt.{w'} (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v})]
    (U : C) (hU : J.IsWeaklyContractible U)
    (F : Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{v}) (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p) :
    Subsingleton (Sheaf.H'.{w', v} F p U)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyContractible.nonempty_sections_of_isWeaklyContractible_of_isTorsor
declarations.doc: Every torsor has a section over a weakly contractible object.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_sections_of_isWeaklyContractible_of_isTorsor
    (U : C) (hU : J.IsWeaklyContractible U)
    (G : SheafOfGroups.{v, v, u} (C := C) J)
    (F : PseudoTorsor (C := C) G) (hF : F.IsTorsor) :
    Nonempty (F.presheaf.obj (op U))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.WeaklyContractible.hasExactLimitsOfShape_discrete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0947(4).** On a site every object of which has a covering by weakly contractible
objects, products of sheaves of modules are exact -- over an *arbitrary* index type `ι`, in an
arbitrary universe, subject only to the `t`-smallness that makes the product exist at all.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasExactLimitsOfShape_discrete (ι : Type u₀) [Small.{t} ι] (B : ObjectProperty C)
    (hB : J.HasEnoughObjects B)
    (hwc : ∀ ⦃U : C⦄, B U → ∀ (F G : Sheaf J (Type t)) (φ : F ⟶ G),
      Sheaf.IsLocallySurjective φ → Function.Surjective (φ.hom.app (op U))) :
    HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ι) (SheafOfModules.{t} R)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyContractible.isZero_homology_of_isDerivedLimit_single
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0947(6).** On a ringed site with a covering collection of weakly contractible
objects, the derived limit of a countable inverse system `(Fₙ)` of sheaves of modules has no
cohomology outside degrees `0` and `1`: `Rᵖ lim Fₙ = 0` for every `p ≠ 0, 1`, in particular for
every `p > 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_of_isDerivedLimit_single
    (S : WeaklyContractibleObjectsSituation.{w, v, u, t} C J)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O)]
    (G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ SheafOfModules.{t} S.O)
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O))
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit (G ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O) 0) L)
    (p : ℤ) (hp₀ : p ≠ 0) (hp₁ : p ≠ 1) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O) p).obj L)
declarations.comment: (6), vanishing of the higher derived limits

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyContractible.nonempty_cokernel_iso_homology_one_of_isDerivedLimit_single
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0947(6).** On a ringed site with a covering collection of weakly contractible
objects, the first derived limit of a countable inverse system `(Fₙ)` of sheaves of modules is
the cokernel of the difference map `(xₙ) ↦ (xₙ - fₙ₊₁(xₙ₊₁))` on the product `∏ₙ Fₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_cokernel_iso_homology_one_of_isDerivedLimit_single
    (S : WeaklyContractibleObjectsSituation.{w, v, u, t} C J)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O)]
    (G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ SheafOfModules.{t} S.O)
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O))
    (hL : IsDerivedLimit (G ⋙ DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O) 0) L) :
    Nonempty (cokernel (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ G.obj ⟨n⟩) n -
        Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ G.obj ⟨n⟩) (n + 1) ≫ G.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ≅
      (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O) 1).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyContractible.isLimit_productFanInDerivedCategory_of_weaklyContractibleObjectsSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0947(5).** On a ringed site with a covering collection of weakly contractible
objects, products in the derived category of sheaves of modules are computed by termwise
products of representing complexes: for every family `K` of cochain complexes of sheaves of
modules indexed by an *arbitrary* type `ι`, the fan whose apex is the image of the termwise
product complex `∏ᶜ K` and whose legs are the images of the projections `Pi.π K i` is a limit
fan.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimit_productFanInDerivedCategory_of_weaklyContractibleObjectsSituation
    (S : WeaklyContractibleObjectsSituation.{w, v, u, t} C J)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O)] (ι : Type u₀) [Small.{t} ι]
    (K : ι → CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O) ℤ) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit (Stacks.DerivedProducts.productFanInDerivedCategory K))

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyContractible.exact_iff_exact_sections_of_weaklyContractibleObjectsSituation
declarations.doc:
In a site covered by weakly contractible objects, a complex of sheaves of modules is
exact if and only if it is exact on sections over every chosen weakly contractible object.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_iff_exact_sections_of_weaklyContractibleObjectsSituation
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{t}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{t}]
    (h : WeaklyContractibleObjectsSituation.{w, v, u, t} C J)
    (S : ShortComplex (SheafOfModules.{t} h.O)) :
    S.Exact ↔ ∀ ⦃U : C⦄, h.B U →
      Function.Exact (S.f.val.app (op U)) (S.g.val.app (op U))

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyContractible.exists_milnor_shortExact_of_weaklyContractibleObjectsSituation
declarations.doc:
**Milnor sequences.** On a ringed site with a covering collection of weakly contractible
objects, an inverse system `K` in the derived category of sheaves of modules and a derived limit
`L` of it fit, in every degree `r`, into a short exact sequence

`0 ⟶ R¹lim Hʳ⁻¹(Kₙ) ⟶ Hʳ(L) ⟶ lim Hʳ(Kₙ) ⟶ 0`,

where `R¹lim` of an inverse system of sheaves of modules is the cokernel of the difference map
`1 - shift` on the product of its terms. The first map is induced by the connecting morphism of
the triangle `L ⟶ ∏ Kₙ ⟶ ∏ Kₙ ⟶ L[1]` through the comparison `Hʳ⁻¹(∏ Kₙ) ≅ ∏ Hʳ⁻¹(Kₙ)`, and the
second is the map whose components are `Hʳ` of the composites `L ⟶ ∏ Kₙ ⟶ Kₙ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_milnor_shortExact_of_weaklyContractibleObjectsSituation
    (S : WeaklyContractibleObjectsSituation.{w, v, u, t} C J)
    [HasDerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O)]
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O))
    (L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O)) (hL : IsDerivedLimit F L) :
    let X : ℕ → DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O) := fun n ↦ F.obj (Opposite.op n)
    let d : (∏ᶜ X) ⟶ ∏ᶜ X := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
      Pi.π X n - Pi.π X (n + 1) ≫ F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
    ∃ (a : L ⟶ ∏ᶜ X) (b : (∏ᶜ X) ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      let T := Triangle.mk a d b
      T ∈ distTriang (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O)) ∧
        ∀ r : ℤ,
          let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O) r
          let H₁ := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{t} S.O) (r - 1)
          let homologySystem : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ SheafOfModules.{t} S.O := F ⋙ H
          let shiftedHomologySystem : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ SheafOfModules.{t} S.O := F ⋙ H₁
          let P : SheafOfModules.{t} S.O :=
            ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (Opposite.op n)
          let δ : P ⟶ P := Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (Opposite.op n)) n -
              Pi.π (fun n : ℕ ↦ shiftedHomologySystem.obj (Opposite.op n)) (n + 1) ≫
                shiftedHomologySystem.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op
          ∃ (e : H₁.obj (∏ᶜ X) ≅ P)
            (i : cokernel δ ⟶ H.obj L) (q : H.obj L ⟶ limit homologySystem)
            (w : i ≫ q = 0),
            e.hom = piComparison H₁ X ∧
              cokernel.π δ ≫ i = e.inv ≫
                DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ T (r - 1) r ∧
              (∀ n : ℕ, q ≫ limit.π homologySystem (Opposite.op n) =
                H.map a ≫ H.map (Pi.π X n)) ∧
              (ShortComplex.mk i q w).ShortExact

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyContractible.epi_limit_π_zero_of_epi_map_succ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0947(3).** On a ringed site with a covering collection of weakly contractible
objects, let `G` be a countable inverse system of sheaves of modules whose transition maps
`Gₙ₊₁ ⟶ Gₙ` are all epimorphisms. Then the projection `lim G ⟶ G₀` from the inverse limit onto
the bottom term of the tower is an epimorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_limit_π_zero_of_epi_map_succ
    (S : WeaklyContractibleObjectsSituation.{w, v, u, t} C J)
    (G : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ SheafOfModules.{t} S.O)
    (hG : ∀ n : ℕ, Epi (G.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op)) :
    Epi (limit.π G ⟨0⟩)

declarations.name: Stacks.WeaklyContractible.exists_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_weaklyContractibleObjectsSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0947(2).** On a ringed site with a covering collection of weakly contractible
objects, every object `E` of the unbounded derived category of sheaves of modules *is* a derived
limit of the tower `n ↦ τ_{≥ -n} E` of its canonical truncations from below:
`E = R lim τ_{≥ -n} E`. The product of the tower exists because each of its stages is bounded
below, and is part of the conclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isDerivedLimit_truncGETower_of_weaklyContractibleObjectsSituation
    [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w t}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w t}]
    (S : WeaklyContractibleObjectsSituation.{w, v, u, max u v w t} C J)
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v w t} S.O)) :
    ∃ _ : HasProduct fun n : ℕ ↦
        (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{max u v w t} S.O) E).obj ⟨n⟩,
      IsDerivedLimit (Stacks.DerivedLimit.truncGETower (SheafOfModules.{max u v w t} S.O) E)
        E

declarations.name: DerivedCategory.isHomotopyColimit_Q_obj_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0949**. Let `A` be an abelian category in which colimits over `ℕ` exist and are
exact, and let `L : ℕ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ` be a system of complexes of `A`. Then the image
under `Q : CochainComplex A ℤ ⥤ D(A)` of the termwise colimit `colimit L` is a derived colimit
(homotopy colimit, Definition 090Z) of the system `L ⋙ Q` in `D(A)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem DerivedCategory.isHomotopyColimit_Q_obj_colimit {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A]
    [Abelian A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] [HasColimitsOfShape ℕ A]
    [HasExactColimitsOfShape ℕ A] (L : ℕ ⥤ CochainComplex A ℤ)
    [HasCoproduct (L ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q).obj] :
    IsHomotopyColimit (L ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (colimit L))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_iso_colimit_preadditiveCoyoneda_of_isHomotopyColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 094A**. Let `F : ℕ ⥤ D` be a system of objects `L n = F.obj n` of a pre-triangulated
category whose direct sum `∐ L n` exists, and let `K` be an object of `D` such that
`Hom(K, -) = preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (Opposite.op K)` commutes with countable direct sums, i.e.
for every countable family `E : ℕ → D` the canonical map `⨁ (K ⟶ E n) ⟶ (K ⟶ ∐ E)` is bijective.
If `L` is a derived colimit of the system with structure map `p : ∐ L n ⟶ L` (Definition 090Z),
then `Hom(K, L) = colim Hom(K, L n)`: there is an isomorphism of abelian groups
`e : colim Hom(K, L n) ≅ Hom(K, L)` such that for every `n` the `n`-th coprojection of the colimit
followed by `e` is composition with the coprojection `L n ⟶ L` of the derived colimit.

This is Lemma 0CRK for the homological functor `H = Hom(K, -)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_iso_colimit_preadditiveCoyoneda_of_isHomotopyColimit
    (F : ℕ ⥤ D) [HasCoproduct F.obj] (K : D)
    [PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (Opposite.op K))]
    {L : D} (p : ∐ F.obj ⟶ L) (q : L ⟶ (∐ F.obj)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hL : Triangle.mk (Limits.Sigma.desc fun n ↦ Limits.Sigma.ι F.obj n -
        F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)) ≫ Limits.Sigma.ι F.obj (n + 1)) p q ∈ distTriang D) :
    ∃ e : colimit (F ⋙ preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (Opposite.op K)) ≅
        (preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (Opposite.op K)).obj L, ∀ n : ℕ,
      colimit.ι (F ⋙ preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (Opposite.op K)) n ≫ e.hom =
        (preadditiveCoyoneda.obj (Opposite.op K)).map (Limits.Sigma.ι F.obj n ≫ p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CompactObjects.exists_retract_finiteComplex_of_isCompactObject
declarations.doc:
A compact derived object is a summand of a finite complex of finite sums
of compact generators of the abelian category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_retract_finiteComplex_of_isCompactObject
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{z} A]
    (S : Set A)
    (hS : ∀ X : A, ∃ (I : Type w) (E : I → A),
      (∀ i, E i ∈ S) ∧ ∃ f : (∐ E) ⟶ X, Epi f)
    (hcompact : ∀ E ∈ S, IsCompactObject.{w} E)
    (K : DerivedCategory A) [IsCompactObject.{w} K] :
    ∃ (L : CochainComplex A ℤ) (a b : ℤ),
      L.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ L.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, ∃ (n : ℕ) (E : Fin n → A),
        (∀ j, E j ∈ S) ∧ Nonempty (L.X i ≅ ∐ E)) ∧
      Nonempty (Retract K (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.exists_retract_finiteComplex_extensionByZero_of_isCompactObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 094C.** On a ringed site every object of which is covered by quasi-compact objects,
a compact object of the derived category of sheaves of modules is a direct summand of a bounded
complex whose terms are finite direct sums of the modules `j_{U!} O_U` for quasi-compact `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_retract_finiteComplex_extensionByZero_of_isCompactObject
    (hqc : ∀ U : X.C, ∃ 𝒰 : PreZeroHypercover.{max u v} U,
      𝒰.sieve₀ ∈ X.J U ∧ ∀ i, X.J.IsQuasiCompactObject (𝒰.X i))
    (K : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [IsCompactObject.{max u v w m} K] :
    ∃ (L : CochainComplex
        (SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
      (a b : ℤ),
      L.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ L.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → X.C),
        (∀ j, X.J.IsQuasiCompactObject (U j)) ∧
        Nonempty (L.X i ≅ ∐ fun j : Fin n ↦
          extensionByZeroUnit.{v, u, w, m} X.J
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) (U j))) ∧
      Nonempty (Retract K (DerivedCategory.Q.obj L))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CompactExtensionByZero.isCompactObject_singleFunctor_extensionByZeroUnit
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and `U` an object of `C`. If cohomology over
`U` has finite cohomological dimension and `H^p(U, -)` commutes with direct sums for every `p`,
then `j_{U!} O_U`, placed in degree zero, is a compact object of the unbounded derived category
of `O`-modules. Compactness is tested against families indexed by types in `Type w`, the
universe of the hypothesis on direct sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_singleFunctor_extensionByZeroUnit
    (hcd : ∃ d : ℤ, ∀ (p : ℕ) (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)),
      d < (p : ℤ) →
      IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        (op U)).rightDerived p).obj G))
    (hsums : ∀ (p : ℕ) (I : Type w), PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)
      ((SheafOfModules.evaluation (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        (op U)).rightDerived p)) :
    IsCompactObject.{w}
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (F := Over.forget U)
          (𝟙 ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CompactExtensionByZero.isCompactObject_singleFunctor_extensionByZeroUnit_of_isWeaklyContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 094E.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `U` be an object of `C` which is
quasi-compact and weakly contractible. Then `j_{U!} O_U`, placed in degree zero, is a compact
object of the unbounded derived category of `O`-modules.

The two hypotheses of Stacks 094D are discharged: weak contractibility makes `Γ(U, -)` exact, so
cohomology over `U` vanishes in positive degrees and in particular has finite cohomological
dimension, and together with quasi-compactness it makes every `R ᵖ Γ(U, -)` commute with direct
sums.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_singleFunctor_extensionByZeroUnit_of_isWeaklyContractible
    (hU : X.J.IsQuasiCompactObject U) (hU' : X.J.IsWeaklyContractible U) :
    IsCompactObject.{u}
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj
        ((SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (F := Over.forget U)
          (𝟙 ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))).obj
          (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_isRepresentedByLocallyConstantComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 094G, the case of at most one nonzero cohomology sheaf.** Let `K` be an object of
the derived category of sheaves of `Λ`-modules whose cohomology is concentrated in a single
degree `n` and whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant of finite type. Then every object
`U` of the site has a covering family `V i ⟶ U` such that the restriction of `K` to each slice
site `C/V i` is represented by a complex of locally constant sheaves of `Λ`-modules of finite
type, concentrated in degree `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover_isRepresentedByLocallyConstantComplex (n : ℤ) (U : C)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)))
    [K.IsGE n] [K.IsLE n]
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K)) :
    ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (V : I → C) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U),
      Sieve.ofArrows V f ∈ J U ∧ ∀ i : I,
        IsRepresentedByLocallyConstantComplex.{v, max u v, w} (J.over (V i)) Λ n n
          ((J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ) (V i)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
declarations.comment: the case of at most one nonzero cohomology sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_isRepresentedByLocallyConstantComplex_of_isGE_of_isLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 094G, the general case.** Let `K` be an object of the derived category of
sheaves of `Λ`-modules over a Noetherian ring whose cohomology is concentrated in the degrees
`[a, b]` and all of whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant of finite type. Then every
object `U` of the site has a covering family `V i ⟶ U` such that the restriction of `K` to each
slice site `C / V i` is represented by a complex of locally constant sheaves of `Λ`-modules of
finite type, concentrated in the degrees `[a, b]`.

This is the statement of the source for an arbitrary number of nonzero cohomology sheaves,
proved by the source's induction on `b - a`;
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_isRepresentedByLocallyConstantComplex` is the base case
`a = b` of that induction. The complex produced here is in fact degreewise *constant* on each
member of the covering family, which is more than the conclusion records.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_cover_isRepresentedByLocallyConstantComplex_of_isGE_of_isLE
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C)
    (Λ : Type w) [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    [∀ V : C, HasWeakSheafify (J.over V) (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)]
    (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b) (U : C)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)))
    [K.IsGE a] [K.IsLE b]
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K)) :
    ∃ (I : Type (max u v)) (V : I → C) (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U),
      Sieve.ofArrows V f ∈ J U ∧ ∀ i : I,
        IsRepresentedByLocallyConstantComplex.{v, max u v, w} (J.over (V i)) Λ a b
          ((J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ) (V i)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
declarations.comment: the general case: the induction on the number of nonzero cohomology sheaves

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantRingModules.isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_constantDerivedTensor
declarations.doc:
Let `(C, J)` be a small site, `Λ` a Noetherian commutative ring, and let `K` and `L` be
objects of `D^-` of the sheaves of `Λ`-modules whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant of
finite type. Then the cohomology sheaves of `K ⊗^L_Λ L` are locally constant of finite type, where
the derived tensor product is `Stacks.ConstantRingModules.constantDerivedTensor`, taken over the
constant sheaf of commutative rings on `Λ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_constantDerivedTensor
    (K L : DerivedCategory.Minus (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} Λ)))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K.obj))
    (hL : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj L.obj)) (i : ℤ) :
    IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
        (((constantDerivedTensor J Λ).obj K.obj).obj L.obj))
declarations.comment: the full statement for the derived tensor product over the constant sheaf of commutative rings on Λ: for K and L in D^- of the sheaves of Λ-modules whose cohomology sheaves are locally constant of finite type, so are those of K ⊗^L_Λ L. The site is small and every universe is one, which is the configuration in which the derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU is available; apart from that nothing is assumed, and in particular the bounded case of the tag is proved here and not supposed

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_mapBifunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 094H, the termwise conclusion.** Let `P` and `Q` be cochain complexes of
sheaves of `Λ`-modules, bounded strictly above, all of whose terms are locally constant of
finite type, and let `T` be a bifunctor on sheaves of `Λ`-modules, additive in each variable,
whose values on those terms are locally constant of finite type — for the sheafified tensor
product this is
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_tensor`. Then every term of the
total complex of `T` applied to `P` and `Q` is locally constant of finite type.

This is what the bounded case of Tag 094H consumes once Tag 094G and a finite free model have
produced the two complexes: the derived tensor product of two such complexes is the class of
their total tensor complex, so its cohomology sheaves are subquotients of these terms, and the
weak Serre property of Tag 093U finishes the argument.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_mapBifunctor
    (T : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ) ⥤ Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ) ⥤
      Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)) [T.Additive] [∀ X, (T.obj X).Additive]
    (P Q : CochainComplex (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)) ℤ)
    [HomologicalComplex.HasMapBifunctor P Q T (ComplexShape.up ℤ)] (a b : ℤ)
    [P.IsStrictlyLE a] [Q.IsStrictlyLE b]
    (hT : ∀ p q, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
      ((T.obj (P.X p)).obj (Q.X q))) (n : ℤ) :
    IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
      ((HomologicalComplex.mapBifunctor P Q T (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).X n)
declarations.comment: the termwise conclusion: every term of the total complex of an additive bifunctor applied to two bounded above complexes of locally constant sheaves of finite type is locally constant of finite type

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_of_bounded
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 094H, the reduction of the bounded above case to the bounded case.** Let `T` be
a bifunctor on the derived category of sheaves of `Λ`-modules which is exact in each variable
and carries objects in degrees `≤ a` and `≤ b` to objects in degrees `≤ a + b` — both are
properties of the derived tensor product of Tag 06YU. If the conclusion of Tag 094H holds for
bounded `K` and `L`, then it holds for `K` and `L` in `D^-`.

The proof is the first half of the source's: `H^i((T.obj K).obj L)` is computed by the bounded
truncations `τ^{> i-b-1}K` and `τ^{> i-a-1}L`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_of_bounded
    (T : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)))
    [∀ K, (T.obj K).CommShift ℤ] [∀ K, (T.obj K).IsTriangulated]
    [∀ L, (T.flip.obj L).CommShift ℤ] [∀ L, (T.flip.obj L).IsTriangulated]
    (hbound : ∀ (K L : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ))) (a b : ℤ),
      K.IsLE a → L.IsLE b → ((T.obj K).obj L).IsLE (a + b))
    (hbounded : ∀ (K L : DerivedCategory.Bounded (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ))),
      (∀ i, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K.obj)) →
      (∀ i, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj L.obj)) →
      ∀ i, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj ((T.obj K.obj).obj L.obj)))
    (K L : DerivedCategory.Minus (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)))
    (hK : ∀ i, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K.obj))
    (hL : ∀ i, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj L.obj)) (i : ℤ) :
    IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj ((T.obj K.obj).obj L.obj))
declarations.comment: the reduction of the bounded above case to the bounded case, for a bifunctor exact in each variable which carries bounds above to their sum; the bounded case is a hypothesis

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantRingModules.isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_constantDerivedTensor_quotientIdealPow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 094I.** Let `(C, J)` be a site, `Λ` a Noetherian commutative ring, `I ⊆ Λ` an
ideal and `K` an object of `D^-` of the sheaves of `Λ`-modules. If the cohomology sheaves of
`K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I` are locally constant of finite type, then so are those of `K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/Iⁿ` for every
`n ≥ 1`.

The derived tensor product is `Stacks.ConstantRingModules.constantDerivedTensor`, the derived
tensor product of Stacks 06YU over the constant sheaf of commutative rings on `Λ` read through
the identification of sheaves of modules over it with sheaves of `Λ`-modules. The proof is
`isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_tensor_quotientIdealPow_of_isLE`, in the
namespace `Stacks.ConstantSheaf`, whose bifunctor parameter is instantiated here and whose two
properties of it,
exactness in the second variable and the degree bound, are
`Stacks.ConstantRingModules.derivedTensor_isTriangulated` and
`Stacks.ConstantRingModules.isLE_constantDerivedTensor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_constantDerivedTensor_quotientIdealPow
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (I : Ideal Λ) (b : ℤ)
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} Λ))) [K.IsLE b]
    (hbase : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
        (derivedTensorConstant J Λ (constantDerivedTensor J Λ) K
          (ModuleCat.of Λ (Λ ⧸ I)))))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (i : ℤ) :
    IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
        (derivedTensorConstant J Λ (constantDerivedTensor J Λ) K
          (ModuleCat.of Λ (Λ ⧸ I ^ n))))
declarations.comment: for a site whose objects, morphisms and coefficient ring lie in one universe, which is where the library's derived tensor product over a sheaf of commutative rings is available; the derived tensor product is constructed, not a parameter. Beyond the source's own hypotheses the binders hold only `SmallCategory C`, `CommRing Λ` and `IsNoetherianRing Λ`: the sheafification conditions this file's construction uses — `HasSheafify`, `WEqualsLocallyBijective` and `HasSheafCompose` for the forgetful functor to abelian groups — are synthesized at such a site, not assumed

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_derivedTensorConstant_quotientIdealPow
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 094I.** Let `(C, J)` be a site, let `Λ` be a Noetherian commutative ring, let
`I ⊆ Λ` be an ideal and let `K` be an object of `D^-(C, Λ)`. If the cohomology sheaves of
`K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I` are locally constant sheaves of finite type, then so are those of
`K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/Iⁿ` for every `n ≥ 1`.

The derived tensor product is `Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantDerivedTensor`, the derived tensor
product of Tag 06YU for the constant ringed site read through the equivalence of Tag 03ET.
Nothing about it is assumed: its exactness in the second variable and its bound above are the
instances and the theorem of this file, and the mathematics of the tag is
`isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_tensor_quotientIdealPow_of_isLE`.

The hypothesis `K.IsLE b` is the source's `K ∈ D^-(C, Λ)`. Local constancy of finite type is
stated over `Λ` rather than over `Λ/Iⁿ`, which is equivalent: a `Λ`-module killed by `Iⁿ` is of
finite type over `Λ` exactly when it is over `Λ/Iⁿ`, by
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.module_finite_iff_finite_quotient`, and constant for one ring exactly when
constant for the other.

`HasSheafify J (ModuleCat.{u} Λ)` is deliberately **not** a binder here: the namespace is
reopened above with a `variable` line that does not carry it, so that the binder list is the
source's own hypotheses and nothing else. At these universes instance search finds it, through
Mathlib's sheafification instance for small sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_derivedTensorConstant_quotientIdealPow
    (I : Ideal Λ) (b : ℤ) (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} Λ))) [K.IsLE b]
    (hbase : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
        (derivedTensorConstant J Λ (constantDerivedTensor J Λ) K (ModuleCat.of Λ (Λ ⧸ I)))))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{u, u, u} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
        (derivedTensorConstant J Λ (constantDerivedTensor J Λ) K
          (ModuleCat.of Λ (Λ ⧸ I ^ n))))
declarations.comment: the derived tensor product is constructed, not assumed: it is Tag 06YU for the constant ringed site read through the equivalence Sheaf J (ModuleCat Λ) ≌ SheafOfModules Λ̲; the source's own hypotheses only

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_tensor_quotientIdealPow_of_isLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 094I.** Let `(C, J)` be a site, let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, let `I ⊆ Λ` be an
ideal and let `K` be an object of `D^-` of the sheaves of `Λ`-modules. Let `T` stand for the
derived tensor product over `Λ`: a bifunctor on that derived category which is exact in its
second variable and carries objects in degrees `≤ a` and `≤ b` to objects in degrees `≤ a + b`.
If the cohomology sheaves of `K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I` are locally constant of finite type, then so are
those of `K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/Iⁿ` for every `n ≥ 1`.

For the **constructed** derived tensor product `Stacks.ConstantSheaf.constantDerivedTensor` —
Tag 06YU for the constant ringed site, read through the equivalence of Tag 03ET — the bifunctor
`T`, its two exactness instances and `hbound` are discharged in
`isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_derivedTensorConstant_quotientIdealPow`, which
applies this theorem; the generality `Λ : Type (max u v w)` here is one the construction cannot
be given.

The proof is the source's induction on `n` along the distinguished triangles

`K ⊗^L_Λ Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹ ⟶ K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/Iⁿ⁺¹ ⟶ K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/Iⁿ ⟶ (K ⊗^L_Λ Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹)[1]`,

supplied by `Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_distTriang_derivedTensorConstant`, with the locally
constant sheaves of finite type absorbing the middle vertex because they form a weak Serre
subcategory (Tag 093U, through Tag 06UQ). Its remaining input, the local constancy of the graded
pieces `K ⊗^L_Λ Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹`, is
`isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_derivedTensorConstant_of_annihilated`:
`Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹` is a finitely generated `Λ`-module killed by `I`, hence has a resolution by finite
free `Λ/I`-modules, which computes each cohomology sheaf of `K ⊗^L_Λ Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹` out of finitely
many copies of `K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I`. That replaces the source's base change identification
`K ⊗^L_Λ Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹ = (K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I) ⊗^L_{Λ/I} Iⁿ/Iⁿ⁺¹` together with Tag 094H, and needs neither a
derived tensor product over `Λ/I` nor Tag 094H.

**The conclusion is stated over `Λ`, not over `Λ/Iⁿ`**: a `Λ`-module killed by `Iⁿ` is of
finite type over `Λ` exactly when it is over `Λ/Iⁿ`
(`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.module_finite_iff_finite_quotient`), and constant for one ring exactly
when constant for the other.

Besides the source's own hypotheses — `Λ` Noetherian, `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal, `K` in `D^-`, and the
local constancy of `K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/I` — the binders hold only the bifunctor `T` with the two
properties of a derived tensor product that the argument consumes: exactness in the second
variable, and the bound above.
declarations.statement:
theorem isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_tensor_quotientIdealPow_of_isLE
    (T : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ)))
    [∀ K, (T.obj K).CommShift ℤ] [∀ K, (T.obj K).IsTriangulated]
    (hbound : ∀ (K L : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ))) (a b : ℤ),
      K.IsLE a → L.IsLE b → ((T.obj K).obj L).IsLE (a + b))
    (b : ℤ) (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{max u v w} Λ))) [K.IsLE b]
    (hbase : ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
        (derivedTensorConstant J Λ T K (ModuleCat.of Λ (Λ ⧸ I)))))
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    ∀ i : ℤ, IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{v, u, w} J Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
        (derivedTensorConstant J Λ T K (ModuleCat.of Λ (Λ ⧸ I ^ n))))
declarations.comment: the induction on n from Λ/I to Λ/Iⁿ, with the source's distinguished triangles and its base change to Λ/I both proved rather than assumed. The derived tensor product enters as a bifunctor parameter, and two of its properties are hypotheses: exactness in the second variable, and that it takes objects in degrees ≤ a and ≤ b to objects in degrees ≤ a + b. The parameter is instantiated, and this tag registered with nothing assumed of the derived tensor product, on Stacks.ConstantRingModules.isFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf_homology_constantDerivedTensor_quotientIdealPow

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_finite_hypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 094K.** If a class `B` supplies finite coverings and every such
covering remains covering after adjoining one further arrow from an object of `B`, then every
object has a hypercovering whose family in every degree is finite and consists of objects of
`B`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_hypercovering
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasPullbacks C] (J : Pretopology C) (B : Set C)
    (exists_finite_cover : ∀ X : C,
      ∃ (I : Type w) (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X),
        Finite I ∧ (∀ i, B (U i)) ∧ Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J X)
    (cover_of_adjoin : ∀ {X : C} {I : Type w} (U : I → C) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X),
      Finite I → (∀ i, B (U i)) → Presieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J X →
      ∀ (V : C) (g : V ⟶ X), B V →
        Presieve.ofArrows
          (fun i : Sum I PUnit ↦ match i with | Sum.inl i => U i | Sum.inr _ => V)
          (fun i : Sum I PUnit ↦ match i with | Sum.inl i => f i | Sum.inr _ => g) ∈ J X) :
    ∀ X : C, ∃ K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)),
      IsHypercovering J K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, Finite (K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌)).I ∧
          ∀ i, B ((K.obj (Opposite.op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left

declarations.doc:
The underlying topological space of a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated scheme is a spectral space: it is sober and quasi-compact, the quasi-compact
opens form a basis, and any two of them meet in a quasi-compact open.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_quasiFinite_baseChange_of_quasiFinite_limitBaseChange
declarations.doc:
Let `c` be a limit cone of a cofiltered diagram `D` of schemes with affine transition
morphisms, and let `f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀` be a morphism locally of finite type of quasi-compact and
quasi-separated schemes over the quasi-compact and quasi-separated stage `D.obj i₀`. If the base
change of `f₀` to the limit is quasi-finite, then the base change of `f₀` to some later stage is
quasi-finite.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_quasiFinite_baseChange_of_quasiFinite_limitBaseChange
    {I : Type u} [Category.{u} I] [IsCofiltered I] (D : I ⥤ Scheme.{u})
    [∀ {i j : I} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)]
    (c : Cone D) (hc : IsLimit c) (i₀ : I)
    (X₀ Y₀ : Over (D.obj i₀)) (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀)
    [CompactSpace (D.obj i₀)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i₀)]
    [CompactSpace X₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X₀.left]
    [CompactSpace Y₀.left] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType f₀.left]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left]
    [QuasiCompact ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left]
    [LocallyQuasiFinite ((Over.pullback (c.π.app i₀)).map f₀).left] :
    ∃ (i : I) (g : i ⟶ i₀),
      (LocallyOfFiniteType ((Over.pullback (D.map g)).map f₀).left ∧
          QuasiCompact ((Over.pullback (D.map g)).map f₀).left) ∧
        LocallyQuasiFinite ((Over.pullback (D.map g)).map f₀).left

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weaklyEtale_iff_stalkMap_weaklyEtale
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is weakly étale if and only if all of its maps on local rings
are weakly étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyEtale_iff_stalkMap_weaklyEtale
    {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.WeaklyEtale f ↔
      ∀ x : X,
        letI := (f.stalkMap x).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.WeaklyEtale (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x)

If the diagonal of a scheme morphism is flat, every module flat over the

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weaklyEtale_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 094S.** For a morphism of schemes, weak étaleness is equivalent to
weak étaleness of every induced map on affine-open sections, to admitting compatible open
coverings on which the restricted morphisms are weakly étale, and to the analogous condition for
affine-open coverings and their induced maps on sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyEtale_tfae {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) :
    let weaklyEtaleOn := fun (V : S.Opens) (U : X.Opens) (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V) ↦
      @Algebra.WeaklyEtale Γ(S, V) Γ(X, U) _ _ (f.appLE V U e).hom.toAlgebra
    List.TFAE [
      WeaklyEtale f,
      ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U →
        ∀ (V : S.Opens), IsAffineOpen V →
          ∀ (e : U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V), weaklyEtaleOn V U e,
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ (V j)),
            ∀ i, WeaklyEtale
              (f.resLE (V j) (U i) ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le)),
      ∃ (J : Type u) (V : J → S.Opens),
        IsOpenCover V ∧
          (∀ j, IsAffineOpen (V j)) ∧
          ∀ j, ∃ (I : Type u) (U : I → X.Opens)
            (hU : (⨆ i, U i) = f ⁻¹ᵁ (V j)),
            (∀ i, IsAffineOpen (U i)) ∧
              ∀ i, weaklyEtaleOn (V j) (U i) ((le_iSup U i).trans hU.le)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weaklyEtale_iff_strictHenselizationMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
A morphism of schemes is weakly étale if and only if every map that it induces between
compatible strict henselizations of its local rings is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyEtale_iff_strictHenselizationMap_bijective
    {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.WeaklyEtale f ↔
      ∀ (x : X) (Ysh Xsh : Type u)
        [CommRing Ysh] [IsLocalRing Ysh]
        [CommRing Xsh] [IsLocalRing Xsh]
        [Algebra (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) Ysh]
        [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Ysh)]
        [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)))
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Ysh)]
        [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x))
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Ysh) Ysh]
        [Algebra (X.presheaf.stalk x) Xsh]
        [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x))
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Xsh)]
        [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.presheaf.stalk x))
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Xsh)]
        [IsLocalRing.IsHenselization (X.presheaf.stalk x)
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField Xsh) Xsh]
        (φ : IsLocalRing.ResidueField Ysh →+* IsLocalRing.ResidueField Xsh)
        (g : Ysh →+* Xsh),
        IsLocalHom g →
          g.comp (algebraMap (Y.presheaf.stalk (f x)) Ysh) =
            (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk x) Xsh).comp (f.stalkMap x).hom →
          (IsLocalRing.residue Xsh).comp g =
              φ.comp (IsLocalRing.residue Ysh) →
            Function.Bijective g

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.powerTorsionComplexInjectiveResolutionIso
declarations.doc:
**The `I`-power-torsion subcomplex of an injective resolution represents `RΓ_I(M)`.** Let `A`
be a commutative ring, `I ⊆ A` a finitely generated ideal and `M` an `A`-module, and let
`M → J^•` be a resolution of `M` by injective `A`-modules. Then the termwise `I`-power-torsion
subcomplex `⋃_n J^•[I^n]` represents derived `I`-power torsion `RΓ_I(M)` in `D(A)`.

This is the computation that [Stacks, Tag 0952] is cited for. No Noetherian hypothesis is
needed: a bounded-below complex of injectives is K-injective, and a right derived functor is
computed by a K-injective resolution.

The isomorphism is the composite of: the identification of the two spellings of the termwise
torsion subcomplex; the passage from the derived category to the homotopy category; the
comparison of `Γ_I` on the homotopy category with its derived-category avatar; the unit of the
total right derived functor `RΓ_I` at the K-injective complex `J^•`; the identification of
`Q(J^•)` with `M⟦0⟧`; and the comparison functor of [Stacks, Tag 0A6N]. Every factor is
invertible for formal reasons except the unit, which is invertible because `J^•` is
K-injective.
declarations.comment: RΓ_I(M) is the I-power-torsion subcomplex of an injective resolution

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.powerTorsionComplexComparison_comp_counit
declarations.doc:
**The comparison carries the structure map of `RΓ_I(M)` to the degreewise inclusion.**
Composing `Stacks.LocalCohomology.powerTorsionComplexComparison` with the structure map
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.derivedPowerTorsionObjCounit` of `RΓ_I(M)` gives the degreewise
inclusion `Γ_I(J^•) ⟶ J^•` of the termwise torsion subcomplex followed by the identification of
`Q(J^•)` with `M⟦0⟧`.

This is the normalization of the counit of [Stacks, Tag 0A6L] read on the K-injective complex
`J^•`.
declarations.statement:
lemma powerTorsionComplexComparison_comp_counit :
    powerTorsionComplexComparison A I hI M R ≫ derivedPowerTorsionObjCounit.{u, u} A I hI M =
      DerivedCategory.Q.map (powerTorsionComplexι A I R.cocomplex) ≫
        (injectiveResolutionIso A M R).hom
declarations.comment: the representation is compatible with the structure maps onto M

declarations.name: isIPowerTorsion_iff_support_subset
declarations.doc:
Let `R` be a commutative ring and let `I ⊆ R` be a finitely generated ideal. Then for every
`R`-module `M`, `M` is `I`-power torsion if and only if `Supp(M) ⊆ V(I)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIPowerTorsion_iff_support_subset
    (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    (I : Ideal R) (hI : I.FG) :
    IsIPowerTorsion R M I ↔
      Module.support R M ⊆ PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set R)

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.localCohomologyHomologyIsoColimitExt

from the quotients by powers of the ideal.

        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) q).obj (localCohomology R I K)) ≅
      colimit (extPowers R I K q)

declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0955, part (1).** Let `A` be a Noetherian ring and `I ⊆ A` a finitely generated
ideal. The counit `RΓ_I(K) ⟶ K` of [Stacks, Tag 0A6L] is an isomorphism at every object `K` of
`D(A)` whose cohomology modules are `I`-power torsion.

The object is represented by a K-injective complex with injective terms, where the counit is the
degreewise torsion inclusion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedPowerTorsionCounit_app
    (K : PowerTorsionDerivedCategory.{u, max u v} A I hI) :
    IsIso ((derivedPowerTorsionCounit.{u, v} A I hI).app K.obj)
