    Nonempty (indEtaleQuotientLift A I ⋙ indEtaleQuotientBaseChange A I ≅
      𝟭 (IndEtaleAlgebra (A ⧸ I)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.indEtaleQuotientLift_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc: The right-adjoint lift is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public theorem indEtaleQuotientLift_fullyFaithful
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) :
    Nonempty (indEtaleQuotientLift A I).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_faithfullyFlat_ind_etale_algebra_splitting_etale
declarations.doc:
There is a faithfully flat ind-étale `A`-algebra such that every faithfully flat étale
algebra over it has a retraction.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_faithfullyFlat_ind_etale_algebra_splitting_etale
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C),
      (algebraMap A C).FaithfullyFlat ∧
        ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
          (fun D : Under (CommRingCat.of A) ↦ D.hom.hom.Etale)
          (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A C))) ∧
        ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra C B],
          (algebraMap C B).FaithfullyFlat → Algebra.Etale C B →
            Nonempty (B →ₐ[C] C)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.mk_splittingAlgebra_le
declarations.doc:
The cardinality of `T(A)` is at most every infinite cardinal which bounds the cardinality
of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mk_splittingAlgebra_le (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (k : Cardinal.{u}) (hk : ℵ₀ ≤ k) (hA : Cardinal.mk A ≤ k) :
    Cardinal.mk (splittingAlgebra A) ≤ k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.mk_iteratedSplittingColimit_le
declarations.doc:
The colimit ring obtained by iterating `T` has the same cardinality bound as the ring it is
built from.
declarations.statement:
theorem mk_iteratedSplittingColimit_le (A : CommRingCat.{u})
    (k : Cardinal.{u}) (hk : ℵ₀ ≤ k) (hA : Cardinal.mk A ≤ k) :
    Cardinal.mk (iteratedSplittingColimit A) ≤ k
declarations.comment: the bound on the iterated construction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.iteratedSplittingColimit_splits_etale
declarations.doc:
The sequential colimit of the iterated splitting rings is a faithfully flat ind-étale
`A`-algebra over which every faithfully flat étale algebra admits a retraction. Its `A`-algebra
structure is induced by the first coprojection into the colimit.
declarations.statement:
theorem iteratedSplittingColimit_splits_etale (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    letI : Algebra A (iteratedSplittingColimit (CommRingCat.of A)) :=
      (colimit.ι (iteratedSplittingDiagram (CommRingCat.of A)) (0 : ℕ)).hom.toAlgebra
    (algebraMap A (iteratedSplittingColimit (CommRingCat.of A))).FaithfullyFlat ∧
      ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
        (fun D : Under (CommRingCat.of A) ↦ D.hom.hom.Etale)
        (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap A (iteratedSplittingColimit (CommRingCat.of A))))) ∧
      ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B]
        [Algebra (iteratedSplittingColimit (CommRingCat.of A)) B],
        (algebraMap (iteratedSplittingColimit (CommRingCat.of A)) B).FaithfullyFlat →
        Algebra.Etale (iteratedSplittingColimit (CommRingCat.of A)) B →
        Nonempty (B →ₐ[(iteratedSplittingColimit (CommRingCat.of A))]
          iteratedSplittingColimit (CommRingCat.of A))
declarations.comment: the properties of the iterated construction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_small_faithfullyFlat_ind_etale_algebra_splitting_etale
declarations.doc:
The faithfully flat ind-étale `A`-algebra splitting all faithfully flat étale covers can be
chosen of cardinality at most any infinite cardinal bounding the cardinality of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_faithfullyFlat_ind_etale_algebra_splitting_etale
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (k : Cardinal.{u})
    (hk : ℵ₀ ≤ k) (hA : Cardinal.mk A ≤ k) :
    ∃ (C : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C),
      Cardinal.mk C ≤ k ∧
        (algebraMap A C).FaithfullyFlat ∧
        ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
          (fun D : Under (CommRingCat.of A) ↦ D.hom.hom.Etale)
          (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A C))) ∧
        ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra C B],
          (algebraMap C B).FaithfullyFlat → Algebra.Etale C B →
            Nonempty (B →ₐ[C] C)
declarations.comment: the bounded form of the first construction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.etale_faithfullyFlat_retracts_quotient
declarations.doc:
If every faithfully flat étale `A`-algebra `B` admits an `A`-algebra map `B → A`, then for
every ideal `I` of `A`, every faithfully flat étale `A ⧸ I`-algebra admits an `A ⧸ I`-algebra map
to `A ⧸ I`.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_faithfullyFlat_retracts_quotient
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (h : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
      [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B], Nonempty (B →ₐ[A] A))
    (I : Ideal A) :
    ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra (A ⧸ I) B]
      [Algebra.Etale (A ⧸ I) B] [Module.FaithfullyFlat (A ⧸ I) B],
      Nonempty (B →ₐ[A ⧸ I] A ⧸ I)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.localizationAtPrime_strictlyHenselian_of_etale_faithfullyFlat_retracts
declarations.doc:
If every faithfully flat étale algebra over `A` has a retraction, then the localization
of `A` at any maximal ideal is strictly henselian.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationAtPrime_strictlyHenselian_of_etale_faithfullyFlat_retracts
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (h : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
      [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B], Nonempty (B →ₐ[A] A))
    (m : Ideal A) [m.IsMaximal] :
    StrictlyHenselianLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.etale_faithfullyFlat_retracts_localizationRing
declarations.doc:
The property that every faithfully flat étale algebra admits a retraction
passes to the canonical localization along any closed subscheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem etale_faithfullyFlat_retracts_localizationRing
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (h : ∀ (B : Type max u v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
      [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B], Nonempty (B →ₐ[A] A))
    (I : Ideal A) :
    ∀ (C : Type v) [CommRing C]
      [Algebra (localizationRing I (1 : A)) C]
      [Algebra.Etale (localizationRing I (1 : A)) C]
      [Module.FaithfullyFlat (localizationRing I (1 : A)) C],
      Nonempty (C →ₐ[localizationRing I (1 : A)]
        localizationRing I (1 : A))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_wLocal_faithfullyFlat_indEtale_extensions
declarations.doc:
A ring map inducing algebraic extensions on residue fields admits a commutative square of
faithfully flat ind-étale extensions with w-local spectra, compatible closed points, and strictly
henselian local rings at the closed points of the lower-right ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_wLocal_faithfullyFlat_indEtale_extensions
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (hres : let f : AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of B) ⟶ AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of A) :=
        Scheme.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A B)).op
      ∀ x,
        letI := (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra
        Algebra.IsAlgebraic
          ((AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of A)).residueField (f x))
          ((AlgebraicGeometry.Spec (.of B)).residueField x)) :
    ∃ (C D : Type u) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : CommRing D)
      (_ : Algebra A C) (_ : Algebra A D) (_ : Algebra B D) (_ : Algebra C D)
      (_ : IsScalarTower A B D) (_ : IsScalarTower A C D),
      (algebraMap A C).FaithfullyFlat ∧
      ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
        (fun E : Under (CommRingCat.of A) ↦ E.hom.hom.Etale)
        (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A C))) ∧
      (algebraMap B D).FaithfullyFlat ∧
      ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
        (fun E : Under (CommRingCat.of B) ↦ E.hom.hom.Etale)
        (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B D))) ∧
      WLocalSpace (PrimeSpectrum C) ∧
      WLocalSpace (PrimeSpectrum D) ∧
      IsWLocalMap (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap C D)) ∧
      closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum D) =
        (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap C D)) ⁻¹' closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum C) ∧
      (∀ x : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ y : PrimeSpectrum C,
        y ∈ closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum C) ∧
          PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A C) y = x) ∧
      (∀ x : PrimeSpectrum B, ∃ y : PrimeSpectrum D,
        y ∈ closedPoints (PrimeSpectrum D) ∧
          PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap B D) y = x) ∧
      ∀ (m : Ideal C) [m.IsMaximal],
        StrictlyHenselianLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_faithfullyFlat_indEtale_extension
declarations.doc:
A weakly étale ring map admits a faithfully flat ind-étale extension of its target after which
the composite is ind-étale.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_faithfullyFlat_indEtale_extension
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (f : A →+* B)
    (hf : letI := f.toAlgebra; Algebra.WeaklyEtale A B) :
    ∃ (B' : Type u) (_ : CommRing B') (g : B →+* B'),
      g.FaithfullyFlat ∧
        (ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
          (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of B) ↦ C.hom.hom.Etale)
          (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom g)) ∧
        ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
          (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of A) ↦ C.hom.hom.Etale)
          (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom (g.comp f))))

declarations.name: ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible
declarations.doc:
**Definition 4 (w-contractible ring; Stacks Tag `0981`).**
A ring `A` is *w-contractible* if every faithfully flat weakly etale ring map `A → B` has a
retraction.  We quantify over all `A`-algebra structures on all rings `B`; the universe of
`B` is the implicit universe parameter `w` of this definition, so the condition is not
restricted to a fixed universe.
declarations.statement: def IsWContractible.{w} (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.nonempty_algHom_of_ind_etale_of_isWContractible
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 0982, (1) ⇒ (2).** A w-contractible ring retracts every faithfully flat ind-étale
algebra over it, ind-étaleness being taken in the categorical form
`(CommAlgCat.etale A).ind (CommAlgCat.of A B)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_algHom_of_ind_etale_of_isWContractible (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (h : ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{u, u} A) (B : Type u) [CommRing B]
    [Algebra A B] (hff : Module.FaithfullyFlat A B)
    (hind : ObjectProperty.ind.{u} (fun C : CommAlgCat A ↦ Algebra.Etale A C)
      (CommAlgCat.of A B)) :
    Nonempty (B →ₐ[A] A)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.strictlyHenselian_atPrime_of_ind_etale_retraction
declarations.doc:
**Lemma 0982, the (3)(c) component of (2) ⇒ (3).** If every faithfully flat ind-étale
algebra over `A` has a retraction, then `A` localized at any maximal ideal is strictly
henselian. An étale algebra is ind-étale, so this is Lemma 097V.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictlyHenselian_atPrime_of_ind_etale_retraction (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (h : ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B], Module.FaithfullyFlat A B →
      ObjectProperty.ind.{u} (fun C : CommAlgCat A ↦ Algebra.Etale A C) (CommAlgCat.of A B) →
      Nonempty (B →ₐ[A] A))
    (m : Ideal A) [m.IsMaximal] :
    StrictlyHenselianLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.localizationAtPrime_strictlyHenselian_of_isWContractible
declarations.doc: The localization of a w-contractible ring at a maximal ideal is strictly henselian.
declarations.statement:
theorem localizationAtPrime_strictlyHenselian_of_isWContractible (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (h : ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{u, u} A) (m : Ideal A) [m.IsMaximal] :
    StrictlyHenselianLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.wContractible_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0982.** For a commutative ring `A` the following are equivalent: `A` is
w-contractible; every faithfully flat ind-étale `A`-algebra admits a retraction; `Spec A` is
w-local, `π₀(Spec A)` is extremally disconnected and the localization of `A` at every maximal
ideal is strictly henselian.
declarations.statement:
theorem wContractible_tfae (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    List.TFAE
      [ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{u, u} A,
        ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B], Module.FaithfullyFlat A B →
          StacksDraft.IndEtale A B → Nonempty (B →ₐ[A] A),
        WLocalSpace (PrimeSpectrum A) ∧
          ExtremallyDisconnected (ConnectedComponents (PrimeSpectrum A)) ∧
            ∀ (m : Ideal A) [m.IsMaximal],
              StrictlyHenselianLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_faithfullyFlat_ind_etale_wContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0983.** Every commutative ring has a faithfully flat ind-étale map to a
w-contractible ring.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_faithfullyFlat_ind_etale_wContractible (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    ∃ (D : Type u) (_ : CommRing D) (f : A →+* D),
      f.FaithfullyFlat ∧
        (ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
          (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of A) ↦ C.hom.hom.Etale)
          (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom f)) ∧
        ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{u, u} D)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_small_faithfullyFlat_ind_etale_wContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0984.** A ring of cardinality at most an infinite cardinal `κ` has a faithfully flat
ind-étale w-contractible extension of cardinality at most `κ ^ (2 ^ (2 ^ (2 ^ κ)))`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_small_faithfullyFlat_ind_etale_wContractible (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (κ : Cardinal.{u}) (hκ : ℵ₀ ≤ κ) (hA : Cardinal.mk A ≤ κ) :
    ∃ (D : Type u) (_ : CommRing D) (f : A →+* D),
      f.FaithfullyFlat ∧
        ObjectProperty.ind.{u}
          (fun C : Under (CommRingCat.of A) ↦ C.hom.hom.Etale)
          (Under.mk (CommRingCat.ofHom f)) ∧
        ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{u, u} D ∧
        Cardinal.mk D ≤
          κ ^ ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ ((2 : Cardinal.{u}) ^ κ)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.extremallyDisconnected_primeSpectrum_of_quasiFinite
declarations.doc:
The spectrum of a quasi-finite, finitely presented algebra over a ring with separably closed
residue fields and Hausdorff extremally disconnected spectrum is extremally disconnected.
declarations.statement:
theorem extremallyDisconnected_primeSpectrum_of_quasiFinite
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Algebra.QuasiFinite A B] [Algebra.FinitePresentation A B]
    (hres : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, IsSepClosed p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
    (hT2 : T2Space (PrimeSpectrum A))
    (hA : ExtremallyDisconnected (PrimeSpectrum A)) :
    ExtremallyDisconnected (PrimeSpectrum B)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isWContractible_of_finite_of_finitePresentation
declarations.doc: A finite, finitely presented algebra over a w-contractible ring is w-contractible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isWContractible_of_finite_of_finitePresentation
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [Module.Finite A B] [Algebra.FinitePresentation A B]
    (hA : ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{u, max u v} A) :
    ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{v, max u v} B

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isWContractible_localizationRing
declarations.doc:
The canonical localization along a finitely generated closed subset of the spectrum of
a w-contractible ring is w-contractible.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWContractible_localizationRing
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
    (hA : ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{u, max u v} A) :
    ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{u, max u v}
      (localizationRing I (1 : A))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_proetalePrecoverage_iff_weaklyEtale_and_mem_fpqcPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098A, conditions (1) and (2).** A family is a pro-étale covering if and only if
every member is weakly étale and the family is an fpqc covering.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_proetalePrecoverage_iff_affine_finite_support
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098A, conditions (1) and (3).** A family is a pro-étale covering if and only if
every member is weakly étale and every affine open of the target is the union of the images of
quasi-compact opens in the sources, all but finitely many of which are empty.
declarations.statement:
public lemma mem_proetalePrecoverage_iff_affine_finite_support :
    Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.proetalePrecoverage T ↔
      ((∀ i, WeaklyEtale (f i)) ∧
        (∀ U : T.Opens, IsAffineOpen U →
            ∃ V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens,
              ((∀ i, IsCompact (V i : Set (X i))) ∧
                ({i | V i ≠ ⊥} : Set I).Finite ∧
                ⋃ i, f i '' (V i : Set (X i)) = (U : Set T))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_proetalePrecoverage_iff_exists_affine_open_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098A, conditions (1) and (4).** A family is a pro-étale covering if and only if
its members are weakly étale and some affine open covering of the target is, member by member,
the union of images of finitely many quasi-compact opens in the sources.
declarations.statement:
public lemma mem_proetalePrecoverage_iff_exists_affine_open_cover :
    Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.proetalePrecoverage T ↔
      ((∀ i, WeaklyEtale (f i)) ∧
        ∃ (A : Type u) (U : A → T.Opens),
          ((∀ a, IsAffineOpen (U a)) ∧
            (⋃ a, (U a : Set T)) = Set.univ ∧
            ∀ a, ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n → I) (V : ∀ j, (X (i j)).Opens),
              ((∀ j, IsCompact (V j : Set (X (i j)))) ∧
                ⋃ j, f (i j) '' (V j : Set (X (i j))) = (U a : Set T))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.mem_proetalePrecoverage_iff_pointwise_compact_open_neighborhood
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098A, conditions (1) and (5).** If the target is quasi-separated, a family is a
pro-étale covering if and only if its members are weakly étale and every point has a
neighbourhood which is the union of the images of finitely many quasi-compact opens in the
sources. The neighbourhood itself is not required to be open.
declarations.statement:
public lemma mem_proetalePrecoverage_iff_pointwise_compact_open_neighborhood
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace T] :
    Presieve.ofArrows X f ∈ Scheme.proetalePrecoverage T ↔
      ((∀ i, WeaklyEtale (f i)) ∧
        ∀ t : T, ∃ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n → I) (V : ∀ j, (X (i j)).Opens),
          ((∀ j, IsCompact (V j : Set (X (i j)))) ∧
            (⋃ j, f (i j) '' (V j : Set (X (i j)))) ∈ nhds t))

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etalePrecoverage_le_proetalePrecoverage
registrations.comment: étale coverings

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.zariskiPrecoverage_le_propQCPrecoverage
registrations.comment: Zariski coverings (the case P = weakly étale)

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompactCover.exists_hom
registrations.comment: finite affine refinement by open immersions into the members

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompactCover.instCoverOfIsAffineOfFiniteI₀
registrations.comment: the refinement is quasi-compact, hence a pro-étale covering

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsStandardProEtaleCovering
declarations.doc:
A family of morphisms `f i : X i ⟶ T` is a *standard pro-étale covering* of `T` if `T` is
affine, the family is finite, each `X i` is affine, each `f i` is weakly étale, and the images of
the `f i` cover `T`.
declarations.statement:
structure IsStandardProEtaleCovering {T : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type v} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
    (f : ∀ i, X i ⟶ T) : Prop

registrations.name: ProetaleWContractible.everyProetaleCoverHasZariskiRefinement_of_wContractible
registrations.comment: w-contractible implies the covering-refinement condition

registrations.name: ProetaleWContractible.isWContractible_of_zariskiRefinement
registrations.comment: the covering-refinement condition implies w-contractibility

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleSite
declarations.doc:
A big pro-étale site, including the initial set-sized choices, the
size-bounded full category of schemes, and a set-sized choice of pro-étale coverings satisfying
the site axioms and representing every pro-étale covering.
declarations.statement: structure BigProetaleSite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isWContractible_globalSections_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098H.** For an affine object `T` of a chosen big pro-étale site the following are
equivalent: the ring of global sections of `T` is w-contractible; `T` is a weakly contractible
object of the site; every covering sieve of `T` is refined by a finite family of objects of the
site whose images form a disjoint clopen cover of `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWContractible_globalSections_tfae (B : BigProetaleSite.{u}) (T : B.Scheme)
    [IsAffine T.obj] :
    [IsWContractible.{u, u} Γ(T.obj, ⊤),
      B.topology.IsWeaklyContractible T,
      ∀ S : Sieve T, S ∈ B.topology T →
        ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → B.Scheme) (f : (i : Fin n) → U i ⟶ T),
          IsClopenDecompositionCover (fun i ↦ (U i).obj) (fun i ↦ B.inclusion.map (f i)) ∧
          ∀ i, S.arrows (f i)].TFAE

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleOver.hasEnoughObjects_isAffine_isWContractible
declarations.doc:
Every object of the big pro-étale site of `S` is covered by objects whose underlying schemes
are affine with w-contractible ring of global sections.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEnoughObjects_isAffine_isWContractible (T : BigProetaleOver B S hS) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (V : I → BigProetaleOver B S hS) (p : (i : I) → V i ⟶ T),
      Sieve.ofArrows V p ∈ topology B S hS T ∧
        ∀ i, IsAffine ((toScheme B S hS).obj (V i)) ∧
          IsWContractible.{u, u} Γ((toScheme B S hS).obj (V i), ⊤)
declarations.comment: in the big pro-étale site of a scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_covering_affine_wContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098I.** Every object `T` of a chosen big pro-étale site admits a chosen covering
family `{T_i → T}` of that site with each `T_i` affine and the spectrum of a w-contractible
ring; in particular each `T_i` is a weakly contractible object of the site.

The covering is the chosen representative of the composite of the chosen affine open cover of
the underlying scheme of `T` with the single affine w-contractible cover of each of its
members.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_covering_affine_wContractible :
    ∃ E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} T,
      B.covering ⟨T, E⟩ ∧
        ∀ i : E.I₀,
          IsAffine (E.X i).obj ∧
            IsWContractible.{u, u} Γ((E.X i).obj, ⊤) ∧
            B.topology.IsWeaklyContractible (E.X i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_covering_refining_proetaleCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098J.** Let `B` be a chosen big pro-étale site and `T` one of its objects. Let
`{Z i → T}_{i ∈ I}` be an *arbitrary* pro-étale covering of the underlying scheme of `T`: the
index type `I` is unrestricted and the members `Z i` are arbitrary schemes, so neither the
family nor its sources need belong to the chosen site. Then there is a covering family
`E` of `T` *in the site* — one of the chosen bounded pro-étale families — which refines
`{Z i → T}`: every member of `E` factors through some member of the given covering.

The family `E` is built by covering `T` inside the site by affine objects with w-contractible
global sections (Stacks 098I), refining the pullback of the given covering over each of them by
a finite disjoint clopen decomposition (Stacks 098F), and taking a chosen representative of the
composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_covering_refining_proetaleCovering (B : BigProetaleSite.{u}) (T : B.Scheme)
    {I : Type w} (Z : I → Scheme.{u}) (g : (i : I) → Z i ⟶ T.obj)
    (hcov : Presieve.ofArrows Z g ∈ Scheme.proetalePrecoverage.coverings T.obj) :
    ∃ E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} T, B.covering ⟨T, E⟩ ∧
      ∀ j : E.I₀, ∃ (i : I) (h : (E.X j).obj ⟶ Z i),
        h ≫ g i = B.inclusion.map (E.f j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.proetaleMorphismCompPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098U.** For composable morphisms `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : Y ⟶ Z` of a chosen big
pro-étale site we have `g_big ∘ f_big = (g ∘ f)_big` and `g_small ∘ f_small = (g ∘ f)_small`,
as canonical isomorphisms of the direct-image functors.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def proetaleMorphismCompPushforwardIso :
    (((bigProetaleMorphism B Y Z g).comp (bigProetaleMorphism B X Y f)).pushforward ≅
        (bigProetaleMorphism B X Z (f ≫ g)).pushforward) ×
      (((smallProetaleMorphism B Y Z g).comp (smallProetaleMorphism B X Y f)).pushforward ≅
        (smallProetaleMorphism B X Z (f ≫ g)).pushforward)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleSheafData
declarations.doc:
The data of a sheaf on the big pro-étale site over `S`, presented on the small sites: a
sheaf on the small pro-étale site of every `T / S`, transition maps between their inverse
images, subject to the cocycle condition and to invertibility along weakly étale maps.
See [Stacks Project, Tag 098V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/098V).
declarations.statement: public structure BigProetaleSheafData

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.characterizeSheafBigProetale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098V.** Sheaves on the big pro-étale site over `S` are the same thing as
compatible families of small pro-étale sheaves: there is an equivalence of categories whose
component at every object over `S` is restriction to its small pro-étale site, and which
carries the transition map of a sheaf to restriction along the projection out of the fibre
product.
declarations.statement:
public theorem characterizeSheafBigProetale :
    ∃ (e : Sheaf (BigProetaleOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max (u + 1) v)) ≌
        BigProetaleSheafData.{u, v} B S hS)
      (ι : ∀ T : BigProetaleOver B S hS,
        e.functor ⋙ BigProetaleSheafData.eval B S hS T ≅
          smallRestriction B S hS T),
      ∀ (F : Sheaf (BigProetaleOver.topology B S hS) (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
        {T T' : BigProetaleOver B S hS} (f : T' ⟶ T)
        (U : SmallProetale B T.left.obj T.left.property),
        (((smallProetalePullbackAdjunction B f.left).homEquiv _ _
          ((e.functor.obj F).pullback f)).hom.app (op U)) ≫
            ((ι T').hom.app F).hom.app
              (op ((smallProetaleBaseChange B T'.left T.left f.left).obj U)) =
          ((ι T).hom.app F).hom.app (op U) ≫
            F.obj.map (smallProetaleBaseChangeProjection B S hS f U).op

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleSite.IsContainedIn.fullyFaithfulSmallFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098Y**, hypothesis (c) of Stacks 00XU: the inclusion of the two small pro-étale
sites of `S` is fully faithful.

Both small sites are full subcategories of nested big pro-étale categories over `S`, and the
inclusion of those is fully faithful.
declarations.statement: def fullyFaithfulSmallFunctor : (h.smallFunctor S hS).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: hypothesis (c) of 00XU for the inclusion of the small sites: full faithfulness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleSite.IsContainedIn.smallFunctor_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098Y**, hypotheses (d) and (e) of Stacks 00XU: fibre products exist in the smaller
small pro-étale site and are preserved by the inclusion, which also carries the final object
`S/S` to the final object `S/S`.

Both small sites have fibre products and the final object `𝟙 S` (Stacks 098M), both computed in
the ambient big pro-étale category over `S`; the inclusion therefore preserves all finite
limits.
declarations.statement: theorem smallFunctor_preservesFiniteLimits : PreservesFiniteLimits (h.smallFunctor S hS)
declarations.comment:
hypotheses (d) and (e) of 00XU for the inclusion of the small sites: preservation of fibre
  products and of the final object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleSite.IsContainedIn.smallFunctor_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098Y**, hypothesis (a) of Stacks 00XU: the inclusion of the two small pro-étale
sites of `S` is cocontinuous.

A covering sieve of the larger small site at an object `X` of the smaller one contains a
covering family of the larger small site, whose image in the larger big pro-étale category is a
chosen covering family there, hence an arbitrary pro-étale covering of the scheme underlying
`X`. By Stacks 098J that covering is refined by a chosen covering family of the *smaller* big
site. The members of the refining family are weakly étale over `X`, being members of a pro-étale
covering, hence weakly étale over `S`, so the family is a covering family of the smaller small
site; and each of its members factors through a member of the given family, over `S` because the
factorization is compatible with the maps to `X`.
declarations.statement:
instance smallFunctor_isCocontinuous :
    (h.smallFunctor S hS).IsCocontinuous (SmallProetale.topology B S hS)
      (SmallProetale.topology B' S (h.contains hS))
declarations.comment: hypothesis (a) of 00XU for the inclusion of the small sites: cocontinuity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleSite.IsContainedIn.smallFunctor_isMorphismOfSites
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098Y**, hypothesis (b) of Stacks 00XU: the inclusion of the two small pro-étale
sites of `S` is continuous, and in fact defines a morphism of sites.

Continuity follows from cover-preservation because the inclusion is representably flat, being
left exact; the left adjoint of the pushforward on sheaves of sets is the sheafified left Kan
extension, which is left exact for the same reason.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallFunctor_isMorphismOfSites :
    _root_.IsMorphismOfSites.{u + 1} (h.smallFunctor S hS)
      (SmallProetale.topology B S hS) (SmallProetale.topology B' S (h.contains hS))
declarations.comment:
hypothesis (b) of 00XU for the inclusion of the small sites: continuity, in the form of
  being a morphism of sites

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleSite.IsContainedIn.smallToposRetraction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098Y**, the conclusion of Stacks 00XU for the two small pro-étale sites of `S`: the
morphisms of topoi `g : Sh(S_proetale) → Sh(S'_proetale)` and `f : Sh(S'_proetale) →
Sh(S_proetale)` induced by the inclusion, whose composite is isomorphic to the identity and
which satisfy `f_* = g^{-1}`.

The direct image of `g` is the cocontinuous pushforward and the direct image of `f` is the
continuous pushforward, which is also the inverse image of `g`; that is the identification
`f_* = g^{-1}`. The retraction is the counit of the adjunction `g^{-1} ⊣ g_*`, invertible
because the inclusion is fully faithful and cocontinuous.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallToposRetraction :
    letI : (h.smallFunctor S hS).IsCocontinuous (SmallProetale.topology B S hS)
        (SmallProetale.topology B' S (h.contains hS)) := h.smallFunctor_isCocontinuous S hS
    letI : (h.smallFunctor S hS).IsContinuous (SmallProetale.topology B S hS)
        (SmallProetale.topology B' S (h.contains hS)) :=
      (h.smallFunctor_isMorphismOfSites S hS).toIsContinuous
    ToposRetraction (SmallProetale B S hS) (SmallProetale B' S (h.contains hS))
      (SmallProetale.topology B S hS) (SmallProetale.topology B' S (h.contains hS))
      (h.smallFunctor S hS)
declarations.comment:
the two morphisms of topoi of the small sites, with `f ∘ g` isomorphic to the identity and
  `f_* = g^{-1}`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleSite.IsContainedIn.smallCohomologyRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098Y, part (1).** For an abelian sheaf `F'` on the larger small pro-étale site of
`S` and every degree `p`,

`H^p(S'_proetale, F') = H^p(S_proetale, g^{-1} F')`,

naturally in `F'`.

This is Stacks 03YU applied to the inclusion: restriction along it is exact and carries
injective abelian sheaves to injective abelian sheaves, because its left adjoint `g_!` is exact
(Stacks 04BH), and it matches the two final objects `S/S`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleSite.IsContainedIn.smallCohomologyPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098Y, part (2), first equality.** For an abelian sheaf `F` on the smaller small
pro-étale site of `S` and every degree `p`,

`H^p(S_proetale, F) = H^p(S'_proetale, g_* F)`,

naturally in `F`. This follows from part (1) because `g^{-1} g_* F = F`, the counit of
`g^{-1} ⊣ g_*` being invertible for a fully faithful cocontinuous functor.
declarations.comment: part (2), first equality: `H^p(S_proetale, F) = H^p(S'_proetale, g_* F)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleSite.IsContainedIn.smallCohomologyLowerShriekIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 098Y, part (2), second equality.** For an abelian sheaf `F` on the smaller small
pro-étale site of `S` and every degree `p`,

`H^p(S_proetale, F) = H^p(S'_proetale, f^{-1} F)`,

naturally in `F`. This follows from part (1) because `g^{-1} f^{-1} F = F`: the inverse image
`f^{-1} = g_!` is fully faithful (Stacks 00XU), so the unit of `g_! ⊣ g^{-1}` is invertible.
declarations.comment: part (2), second equality: `H^p(S_proetale, F) = H^p(S'_proetale, f^{-1} F)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.hasEnoughObjects_isAffine_isWeaklyContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0990 for the small pro-étale site of a scheme.** Every object of `X_proétale` is
covered by affine objects which are weakly contractible objects of the site.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEnoughObjects_isAffine_isWeaklyContractible (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (Scheme.ProEt.topology X).HasEnoughObjects
      (fun V : X.ProEt ↦ IsAffine V.left ∧
        (Scheme.ProEt.topology X).IsWeaklyContractible V)
declarations.comment: the small pro-etale site of a scheme, in the unrestricted form of AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt: every object is covered by affine weakly contractible ones

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.hasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects_proetale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0990, in the form the derived-completeness results consume.** The small pro-étale
site of a scheme has enough weakly contractible objects.

This is the theorem above with the affineness of the covering objects forgotten, which is the
shape `CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects` asks for — it
unfolds to `HasEnoughObjects J (IsWeaklyContractible J)`. It is what supplies the `hX` hypothesis
of the derived-completeness results for this site, among them Stacks 09BY in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.AdicCompletionCriterion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects_proetale (X : Scheme.{u}) :
    (Scheme.ProEt.topology X).HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects
declarations.comment: the small pro-etale site of a scheme has enough weakly contractible objects, the form HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects asks for

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.affineIndEtaleProetale_hasEnough_quasiCompact_weaklyContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0990, the affine ind-étale pro-étale site.** For an affine base, the affine
ind-étale pro-étale site has enough quasi-compact weakly contractible objects: every object is
covered by a single object which is quasi-compact and weakly contractible.
declarations.statement:
theorem affineIndEtaleProetale_hasEnough_quasiCompact_weaklyContractible [IsAffine S.obj] :
    (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B S).HasEnoughObjects
      (fun U : AffineIndEtaleProetale B S ↦
        (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B S).IsQuasiCompactObject U ∧
        (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B S).IsWeaklyContractible U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleOver.hasEnough_affine_quasiCompact_weaklyContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0990 for the big pro-étale site `(Sch/S)_proétale`.** Every object of the big
pro-étale site of `S` is covered by objects which are affine, quasi-compact objects of the site
and weakly contractible in it.

The covering is Stacks 098I, lifted to the slice by composing with the structure morphism; the
two properties of its members are
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleOver.isQuasiCompactObject_of_isWContractible` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigProetaleOver.isWeaklyContractible_of_isWContractible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem BigProetaleOver.hasEnough_affine_quasiCompact_weaklyContractible :
    (BigProetaleOver.topology B S hS).HasEnoughObjects
      (fun T : BigProetaleOver B S hS ↦
        IsAffine ((BigProetaleOver.toScheme B S hS).obj T) ∧
          (BigProetaleOver.topology B S hS).IsQuasiCompactObject T ∧
          (BigProetaleOver.topology B S hS).IsWeaklyContractible T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.SmallProetale.hasEnough_affine_quasiCompact_weaklyContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0990 for the small pro-étale site `S_proétale`.** Every object of the small
pro-étale site of `S` is covered by objects which are affine, quasi-compact objects of the site
and weakly contractible in it.

The covering is Stacks 098I in the small site,
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.SmallProetale.hasEnoughObjects_isWContractible`; the two properties
of its members are
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.SmallProetale.isQuasiCompactObject_of_isWContractible` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.SmallProetale.isWeaklyContractible_of_isWContractible`.
declarations.statement:
theorem SmallProetale.hasEnough_affine_quasiCompact_weaklyContractible :
    (SmallProetale.topology B S hS).HasEnoughObjects
      (fun U : SmallProetale B S hS ↦
        IsAffine ((SmallProetale.toScheme B S hS).obj U) ∧
          (SmallProetale.topology B S hS).IsQuasiCompactObject U ∧
          (SmallProetale.topology B S hS).IsWeaklyContractible U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.BigAffineProetale.hasEnough_affine_quasiCompact_weaklyContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0990 for the big affine pro-étale site `(Aff/S)_proétale`.** Every object of the
big affine pro-étale site of `S` is covered by objects which are affine, quasi-compact objects
of the site and weakly contractible in it.
declarations.statement:
theorem BigAffineProetale.hasEnough_affine_quasiCompact_weaklyContractible :
    (BigAffineProetale.topology B S hS).HasEnoughObjects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.SmallAffineProetale.hasEnough_affine_quasiCompact_weaklyContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0990 for the affine small pro-étale site `S_{affine, proétale}`.** Every object of
the affine small pro-étale site of `S` is covered by objects which are affine, quasi-compact
objects of the site and weakly contractible in it.
declarations.statement:
theorem SmallAffineProetale.hasEnough_affine_quasiCompact_weaklyContractible :
    (SmallAffineProetale.topology B S hS).HasEnoughObjects

declarations.comment: the affine small pro-étale site S_{affine, pro-étale}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.proetale_hasEnoughPoints
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 0992.** The pro-étale sites of schemes, the small pro-étale site of a scheme, the
big pro-étale site over it, the affine objects of the small site and the affine objects of the
big site all have enough points.
declarations.statement:
public theorem proetale_hasEnoughPoints
    (B : BigProetaleSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S) :
    GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily.{u + 1} B.topology ∧
      GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily.{u} (Scheme.ProEt.topology S) ∧
      GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily.{u + 1} (BigProetaleOver.topology B S hS) ∧
      GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily.{u} (AffineProetale.topology S) ∧
      GrothendieckTopology.HasConservativeFamily.{u + 1}
        (BigAffineProetale.topology B S hS)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.geometricPointToStrictHenselization_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0993.** The canonical lift of a geometric point to its strict
henselization lies over that geometric point, so the strict henselization is a pro-étale
neighbourhood of the point.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.weaklyEtale_strictHenselizationToBase
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0993.** The canonical morphism from the strict henselization of `S` at
a geometric point `s` is weakly étale, so the strict henselization is an object of the small
pro-étale site of `S`. It is the spectrum of an ind-étale ring map followed by the canonical
morphism from the local ring at the image of `s`.
declarations.statement:
theorem weaklyEtale_strictHenselizationToBase :
    WeaklyEtale (strictHenselizationToBase B S hS s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationSectionsEquivStalk
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0993.** Sections of a presheaf on the small pro-étale site over the
strict henselization at a geometric point are canonically the stalk of the presheaf at that
geometric point.
declarations.statement:
def strictHenselizationSectionsEquivStalk (F : (S.ProEt)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) v)) :
    F.obj (op (strictHenselizationProEt B S hS s)) ≃ proetaleStalk S s F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationSectionsEquivStalk_apply
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0993.** The comparison of sections over the strict henselization with
the stalk is the colimit insertion at the canonical pro-étale neighbourhood; this is what makes
it canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictHenselizationSectionsEquivStalk_apply
    (F : (S.ProEt)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) v))
    (x : F.obj (op (strictHenselizationProEt B S hS s))) :
    strictHenselizationSectionsEquivStalk B S hS s F x =
      colimit.ι ((Functor.Elements.π (proetalePointFiber S s)).op ⋙ F)
        (op ((proetalePointFiber S s).elementsMk (strictHenselizationProEt B S hS s)
        (strictHenselizationPoint B S hS s))) x

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.strictHenselizationSectionsEquivStalk_natural
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0993.** The comparison of sections over the strict henselization with
the stalk is functorial in the presheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictHenselizationSectionsEquivStalk_natural
    {F G : (S.ProEt)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max (u + 1) v)} (α : F ⟶ G)
    (x : F.obj (op (strictHenselizationProEt B S hS s))) :
    strictHenselizationSectionsEquivStalk B S hS s G
        (α.app (op (strictHenselizationProEt B S hS s)) x) =
      colim.map (Functor.whiskerLeft (Functor.Elements.π (proetalePointFiber S s)).op α)
        (strictHenselizationSectionsEquivStalk B S hS s F x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHom_awayCoextendScalars_idempotent
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let `f` be a global section of `𝒪` and let `K ∈ D(𝒪)`. Then

`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)) = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)`,

with `K` computed by a K-injective complex `I` of sheaves of `𝒪`-modules and
`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)` by the coextension of scalars of `I` along `𝒪 ⟶ 𝒪_f`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHom_awayCoextendScalars_idempotent (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    (h : Presheaf.globalSections (X.O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}))
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((coeffCoextendComplex X (awaySheaf h) (toAwaySheaf h)).obj I) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((coeffCoextendComplex X (awaySheaf h) (toAwaySheaf h)).obj
        ((coeffRestrictComplex X (awaySheaf h) (toAwaySheaf h)).obj
          ((coeffCoextendComplex X (awaySheaf h) (toAwaySheaf h)).obj I)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHom_awayMulCurryIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0996(3).** Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let `f` and `g` be global sections of
`𝒪` and let `K ∈ D(𝒪)`. Then

`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_g, K)) = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_{g f}, K)`.

Computing `K` by a K-injective complex `I` of sheaves of `𝒪`-modules, `SheafHom•_𝒪(𝒪_g, I)`
represents `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_g, K)` and is itself K-injective as a complex of sheaves of
`𝒪`-modules — `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isKInjective_sheafHomComplex_awayComplex` — so
`SheafHom•_𝒪(𝒪_f, SheafHom•_𝒪(𝒪_g, I))` represents the left-hand side; and
`SheafHom•_𝒪(𝒪_{g f}, I)` represents the right-hand side. Nothing is assumed of `f` or `g`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHom_awayMulCurryIso
    (I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj (sheafHomComplex X (awayComplex X f)
        (sheafHomComplex X (awayComplex X g) I).obj).obj ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (sheafHomComplex X (awayComplex X (mulGlobalSection X f g)) I).obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHom_coextendScalarsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 0996(2).** Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let `φ₀ : 𝒪 ⟶ 𝒪'` be a morphism of
sheaves of commutative rings — for instance the localization `𝒪 ⟶ 𝒪_f` at a global section —
let `K ∈ D(𝒪)` and `L ∈ D(𝒪')`. Then

`R SheafHom_𝒪(L, K) = R SheafHom_{𝒪'}(L, R SheafHom_𝒪(𝒪', K))`.

Computing `K` by a K-injective complex `I` of sheaves of `𝒪`-modules, the right-hand side is
the internal Hom complex over `𝒪'` of `L` and of `SheafHom_𝒪(𝒪', I)` = `coeffCoextendComplex`
applied to `I`, the latter representing `R SheafHom_𝒪(𝒪', K)`; the left-hand side is the
internal Hom complex over `𝒪` of the restriction of scalars of `L` and of `I`. The
identification is of complexes of sheaves of `𝒪`-modules.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSheafHom_coextendScalarsIso [I.IsKInjective] :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj (sheafHomComplex X ((coeffRestrictComplex X O' φ₀).obj L) I).obj ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((coeffRestrictComplex X O' φ₀).obj
        (sheafHomComplex (coeffSite X O') L ((coeffCoextendComplex X O' φ₀).obj I)).obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.coextHomComplexIso_hom_apply
declarations.doc:
**The comparison of Tag 0996(2) is the canonical one.** On a local section it evaluates each
local component of a cochain — a local morphism `𝒪'|_W ⟶ I|_W` — at the unit section, so it is
not merely some isomorphism between the two complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem coextHomComplexIso_hom_apply (U : X.C) (n p q : ℤ) (hpq : p + n = q)
    (t : ((coextSource X O' φ₀ L I).X n).val.obj (op U))
    {W : X.C} (g : W ⟶ U) (x : (L.X p).val.obj (op W)) :
    (((AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom
        (((sheafHomComplex X ((coeffRestrictComplex X O' φ₀).obj L) I).sectionsIso U).hom.f n)
        ((((coextHomComplexIso X O' φ₀ L I).hom.f n).val.app (op U)).hom t)).v
          p q hpq).val.app (op (Over.mk g))) x =
      invSecVal (coeffHom X O' φ₀).hom (I.X q).val (op W)
        ((((AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom
          (((sheafHomComplex (coeffSite X O') L
            ((coeffCoextendComplex X O' φ₀).obj I)).sectionsIso U).hom.f n) t).v
            p q hpq).val.app (op (Over.mk g))) x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHom_awayRestrictScalarsIso
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site and let `f` be a global section of `𝒪`. For
`L, N ∈ D(𝒪_f)` we have `R SheafHom_𝒪(L, N) = R SheafHom_{𝒪_f}(L, N)`: computing `N` by a
K-injective complex `I` of sheaves of `𝒪_f`-modules, the internal Hom complex over `𝒪` of the
restrictions of `L` and `I` is, as a complex of sheaves of `𝒪`-modules, the restriction of the
internal Hom complex over `𝒪_f` of `L` and `I`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedSheafHom_awayRestrictScalarsIso_canonical
declarations.doc:
The comparison `derivedSheafHom_awayRestrictScalarsIso` is induced by the isomorphism of
internal Hom complexes that leaves every local module homomorphism unchanged.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSheafHom_awayRestrictScalarsIso_canonical (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    (h : Presheaf.globalSections (X.O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}))
    (L I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose X.J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj (awaySheaf h))) ℤ)
    [I.IsKInjective] :
    let Xh : RingedSite.{u, u, u} := { C := X.C, J := X.J, O := awaySheaf h }
    let R := SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose X.J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map (toAwaySheaf h))
    let LR := (R.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj L
    let IR := (R.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I
    ∃ c : (sheafHomComplex X LR IR).obj ≅
        (R.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj (sheafHomComplex Xh L I).obj,
      (DerivedCategory.Q.mapIso c = derivedSheafHom_awayRestrictScalarsIso X h L I) ∧
      (∀ (U : X.C) (n p q : ℤ) (hpq : p + n = q)
          (s : ((sheafHomComplex X LR IR).obj.X n).val.obj (op U))
          {W : X.C} (g : W ⟶ U) (x : (L.X p).val.obj (op W)),
        (((AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom
            (((sheafHomComplex Xh L I).sectionsIso U).hom.f n)
            ((c.hom.f n).val.app (op U) s)).v p q hpq).val.app
              (op (Over.mk g))) x =
          (((AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom
            (((sheafHomComplex X LR IR).sectionsIso U).hom.f n) s).v p q hpq).val.app
              (op (Over.mk g))) x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.sheafHomComplex_awayLocalizedAction_agree
declarations.doc:
The two `𝒪_f`-structures on `R SheafHom_𝒪(L, N)` agree: acting by a local section of `𝒪_f`
on the source of a local Hom and acting by it on the target give the same section of the
internal Hom complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafHomComplex_awayLocalizedAction_agree (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u})
    (h : Presheaf.globalSections (X.O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}))
    (L I : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose X.J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj (awaySheaf h))) ℤ) :
    let _Xh : RingedSite.{u, u, u} := { C := X.C, J := X.J, O := awaySheaf h }
    let R := SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose X.J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map (toAwaySheaf h))
    let LR := (R.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj L
    let IR := (R.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I
    ∀ (U : X.C)
      (r : ((sheafCompose X.J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj
        (awaySheaf h)).obj.obj (op U))
      (n p q : ℤ) (hpq : p + n = q)
      (s : ((sheafHomComplex X LR IR).obj.X n).val.obj (op U))
      {W : X.C} (g : W ⟶ U) (x : (L.X p).val.obj (op W)),
      (((AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom
        (((sheafHomComplex X LR IR).sectionsIso U).hom.f n) s).v p q hpq).val.app
          (op (Over.mk g)))
            (((L.X p).val.obj (op W)).isModule.smul
              (((sheafCompose X.J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj
                (awaySheaf h)).obj.map g.op r) x) =
        ((I.X q).val.obj (op W)).isModule.smul
          (((sheafCompose X.J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj
            (awaySheaf h)).obj.map g.op r)
          (show (I.X q).val.obj (op W) from (((AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom
            (((sheafHomComplex X LR IR).sectionsIso U).hom.f n) s).v p q hpq).val.app
              (op (Over.mk g))) x)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isZero_derivedSheafHom_derivedAwayModule_of_forall
declarations.doc:
If `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(L, K)` vanishes for every object `L` of `D(𝒪_f)`, viewed as an object of
`D(𝒪)` by restriction of scalars, then `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)` vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_derivedSheafHom_derivedAwayModule_of_forall
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (H : ∀ L : DerivedCategory
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (awayRingedSite X h).O)),
      IsZero (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj
        (op ((awayRestrictScalarsDerived X h).obj L))).obj K)) :
    IsZero (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op (derivedAwayModule X h))).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isZero_derivedSheafHom_awayRestrictScalars_of_isZero
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site, let `f` be a global section of `𝒪` and let `K ∈ D(𝒪)`. If
`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)` vanishes, then `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(L, K)` vanishes for every object `L` of
`D(𝒪_f)`, viewed as an object of `D(𝒪)` by restriction of scalars.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_derivedSheafHom_awayRestrictScalars_of_isZero
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : IsZero (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op (derivedAwayModule X h))).obj K))
    (L : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (awayRingedSite X h).O))) :
    IsZero (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj
      (op ((awayRestrictScalarsDerived X h).obj L))).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isZero_derivedSheafHom_derivedAwayModule_iff_isDerivedCompleteAt
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0997], the equivalence of (1) and (3)**: the derived internal Hom
`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)` vanishes if and only if `T(K, f) = 0`.

Derived internal Hom into `K` carries the triangle of the telescope resolution of `𝒪_f` to a
distinguished triangle whose first vertex is `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)`, so that vertex vanishes
exactly when the second morphism of the triangle is invertible; under the identification
`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(∐ₙ 𝒪, K) ≅ ∏ₙ K` that morphism is the Milnor difference map `1 - f·shift`, whose
invertibility is `T(K, f) = 0` by definition.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_derivedSheafHom_derivedAwayModule_iff_isDerivedCompleteAt :
    IsZero (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op (derivedAwayModule X h))).obj K) ↔
      IsDerivedCompleteAt K (awaySmul X h)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.memVanishingIdeal_iff_isDerivedCompleteAt
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0997], the equivalence of conditions (1) and (3).** For a global section `f`
of `𝒪` and `K ∈ D(𝒪)`, the derived internal Hom `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)` vanishes exactly when
`T(K, f) = 0`, that is exactly when the Milnor difference map `1 - f·shift` is invertible on
`∏ₙ K`.

The proof is the source's: `𝒪_f` is the colimit of `𝒪 --f--> 𝒪 --f--> ⋯`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isColimitAwayModuleCocone`), so the mapping telescope resolves it
by countable direct sums of copies of `𝒪`
(`Stacks.MappingTelescope.telescope_shortExact_general`); derived internal Hom into `K` turns
that short exact sequence into a distinguished triangle
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_distinguished_derivedSheafHom`, the contravariant half of
[Stacks, Tag 08JC]) whose second and third vertices are `∏ₙ K` and whose first vertex is
`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)`; and the map between them is `1 - f·shift`, because derived internal Hom
is `𝒪`-linear in its contravariant variable. The first vertex of a distinguished triangle
vanishes exactly when the opposite map is invertible.
declarations.statement:
theorem memVanishingIdeal_iff_isDerivedCompleteAt :
    MemVanishingIdeal X K h ↔
      IsDerivedCompleteAt K
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.globalSectionToEnd (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
            (awayFamily X h))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.memVanishingIdeal_mulGlobalSection_of_memVanishingIdeal
declarations.doc:
**The vanishing locus is closed under multiplication, at the tag's own membership
condition.** If `f` lies in the vanishing locus of `K` then so does `gf`, for every global
section `g` of `𝒪`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightOrthogonalAway_mulGlobalSection` read through the
implication (1) ⇒ (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0997],
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isZero_derivedSheafHom_awayRestrictScalars_of_isZero`, which turns
membership into right orthogonality; the converse direction is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.MemVanishingIdeal.of_isRightOrthogonalAway`.

It is stated here rather than beside `isRightOrthogonalAway_mulGlobalSection` in
`VanishingIdeal.lean` because it is the one declaration of that file needing
`VanishingCriterionCoextension.lean`, and that import reaches `Completion.lean`, whose consumer
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.completionFunctor_obj_eq_derivedSheafHom_flip` of
`KoszulLimitFormula.lean` then fails to discharge its `omit` clause.
declarations.statement:
theorem memVanishingIdeal_mulGlobalSection_of_memVanishingIdeal
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (g h : Presheaf.globalSections (X.O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}))
    (H : MemVanishingIdeal X K h) :
    MemVanishingIdeal X K (mulGlobalSection X g h)
declarations.comment: closure under multiplication, at the membership condition

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.memVanishingIdeal_addGlobalSection
declarations.doc:
**The vanishing locus is closed under addition.** If `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_a, K)` and
`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_b, K)` vanish then so does `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_{a + b}, K)`.

Write `h = a + b`. Multiplicativity — `isRightOrthogonalAway_mulGlobalSection` together with the
implication (1) ⇒ (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0997], `isZero_derivedSheafHom_awayRestrictScalars_of_isZero`
— puts the three products `ha`, `hb` and `hab` in the locus, and the short exact sequence
`0 → 𝒪_h → 𝒪_{ha} ⊕ 𝒪_{hb} → 𝒪_{hab} → 0` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.shortExact_awayModuleAddComplex` then puts `h` there by the
dévissage `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isZero_derivedSheafHom_of_shortExact`, the middle term
being handled by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isZero_derivedSheafHom_biprod`.

Nothing is assumed of `K`, of `a` or of `b`.
declarations.statement:
theorem memVanishingIdeal_addGlobalSection
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (a b : Presheaf.globalSections (X.O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}))
    (Ha : MemVanishingIdeal X K a) (Hb : MemVanishingIdeal X K b) :
    MemVanishingIdeal X K (addGlobalSection X a b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.memVanishingIdeal_over_of_memVanishingIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0998], restriction stability of the vanishing locus.** If the global section
`f` of `𝒪` lies in the vanishing locus of `K`, then its restriction `f|_U` lies in the vanishing
locus of `K|_U` over the slice site `𝒞/U`.

Membership of `f|_U` in the locus of `K|_U` is the vanishing of `R𝑆heafHom_{𝒪_U}((𝒪_f)|_U, K|_U)`
by `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.memVanishingIdeal_over_iff_isZero_derivedSheafHom_overFunctor`,
whose input is the base change `(𝒪_f)|_U ≅ (𝒪_U)_{f|_U}`; and that object is the restriction of
`R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)` by [Stacks, Tag 08JB]. Restriction is additive, so it carries the
vanishing upstairs to the vanishing downstairs.
declarations.statement:
theorem memVanishingIdeal_over_of_memVanishingIdeal
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : MemVanishingIdeal X K h) :
    MemVanishingIdeal (X.over U)
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
      (globalSectionOver X U h)
declarations.comment: the vanishing locus is stable under restriction to a slice site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightOrthogonalAway_mulGlobalSection
declarations.doc:
**The vanishing locus is closed under multiplication.** If `K` is right orthogonal to
`D(𝒪_f)` and `g` is any global section of `𝒪`, then `K` is right orthogonal to `D(𝒪_{gf})`.
This is the first half of the proof of [Stacks, Tag 0998]: the source observes that `𝒪_{gf}` is
an `𝒪_f`-module, which here is the factorization of `𝒪 ⟶ 𝒪_{gf}` through `𝒪_f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRightOrthogonalAway_mulGlobalSection
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (g h : Presheaf.globalSections (X.O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat.{u}))
    (H : IsRightOrthogonalAway X K h) :
    IsRightOrthogonalAway X K (mulGlobalSection X g h)
declarations.comment: closure under multiplication, for the right-orthogonality condition of 0997

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.memVanishingIdeal_of_coversTop
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0998], the sheaf condition for the vanishing locus.** Let `V : ι → 𝒞` be a
family of objects covering the final object of the site. If the restriction `f|_{V i}` lies in
the vanishing locus of `K|_{V i}` for every `i`, then `f` lies in the vanishing locus of `K`.

This is the verification the source omits. Membership of `f|_{V i}` in the locus of `K|_{V i}` is
the vanishing of `R𝑆heafHom_{𝒪_{V i}}((𝒪_f)|_{V i}, K|_{V i})` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.memVanishingIdeal_over_iff_isZero_derivedSheafHom_overFunctor`, and
that object is the restriction of `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)` by [Stacks, Tag 08JB]. So the hypothesis
says that `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(𝒪_f, K)` vanishes on each member of the covering family, and
`isZero_of_coversTop_overFunctor_mapDerivedCategory` concludes that it vanishes.

Nothing is assumed of `K`, of `f` or of the site. The converse implication, at a single object
and with no covering, is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.memVanishingIdeal_over_of_memVanishingIdeal`.
declarations.statement:
theorem memVanishingIdeal_of_coversTop
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    {ι : Type*} {V : ι → X.C} (hV : X.J.CoversTop V)
    (hK : ∀ i, MemVanishingIdeal (X.over (V i))
      ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        (V i)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K)
      (globalSectionOver X (V i) h)) :
    MemVanishingIdeal X K h
declarations.comment:
the sheaf condition: membership in the vanishing locus is local on a family of
  objects covering the final object of the site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompleteIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0998]: the sections `f` of `𝒪` with `T(K|_U, f) = 0` form a sheaf of ideals
in `𝒪`.** For a ringed site `(𝒞, 𝒪)` and `K ∈ D(𝒪)`, the rule sending an object `U` of `𝒞` to
`{f ∈ 𝒪(U) | T(K|_U, f) = 0}` is a sheaf of ideals: the value at each object is an ideal
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompleteIdealAt`), the values are stable under
restriction (`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsDerivedCompleteAtSection.restrict`), and
membership is local (`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsDerivedCompleteAtSection.of_sieve`).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete
declarations.doc: Derived completeness of a complex of sheaves of modules along an ideal sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def IsDerivedComplete (X : RingedSite.{u, v, r})
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (K : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{max u v w} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_derivedSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 099A.** Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site and `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` a sheaf of ideals. For every
`K ∈ D(𝒪)` — arbitrary, with no finiteness or boundedness assumed — and every derived-complete
`L ∈ D(𝒪)`, the object `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(K, L)` is derived complete along the same `ℐ`.

Derived completeness is tested slice by slice. On the slice site over `U`, restriction commutes
with derived internal Hom by [Stacks, Tag 08JB], so the object to be tested is
`R𝑆heafHom_{𝒪_U}(K|_U, L|_U)`; and `L|_U` passes the test by hypothesis. That functor is
additive and takes multiplication by `f` to multiplication by `f`, both proved in
`StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/Sites/Cohomology/InternalHom/DerivedHomAdditive.lean`, and it
preserves the countable power of `L|_U` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.preservesLimit_derivedSheafHom`. Together these let it carry the
Milnor difference map, hence the test, from `L|_U` to its value.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_derivedSheafHom
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))))
    (hL : IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I L) :
    IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I
      (((derivedSheafHomBifunctor X).obj (op K)).obj L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_idealOfGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099F] for the ideal sheaf generated by finitely many global sections, with no
hypothesis left.** For a ringed site `(𝒞, 𝒪)` and global sections `f_1, …, f_r` of `𝒪`, the
inclusion of the objects of `D(𝒪)` derived complete along `ℐ = (f_1, …, f_r)` into `D(𝒪)` has a
left adjoint; the adjoint is the Čech completion functor `Φ K = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)` of
`Completion.lean`, and all three clauses its universal property was reduced to are now
discharged — clause 1 by `isDerivedComplete_completionFunctor`, clause 2 by
`isIso_completionUnit_app_of_isDerivedComplete` of `CompletionUnitIso.lean`, clause 3 by
`completionFunctor_map_completionUnit_app`.

The `@[stacks 099F]` attribute is *not* attached. The source states that proposition for an
arbitrary **finite type** sheaf of ideals, that is one which is only *locally* generated by
finitely many sections; an ideal sheaf generated by finitely many *global* sections is a special
case of that, and the general case is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete` of `FiniteTypeReflector.lean`.
What
*is* at the source's generality here is [Stacks, Tag 099B], whose hypothesis is exactly that
`ℐ` be generated by finitely many global sections; the attribute for that tag is attached, to
this statement and to `bijective_precomp_completionUnit_idealOfGlobalSections` below, which
carry its two halves.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_idealOfGlobalSections :
    (ObjectProperty.ι
      (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X (idealOfGlobalSections X f))).IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment:
the conclusion — for `ℐ` the ideal sheaf generated by the global sections
  `f_1, …, f_r`, the inclusion `D_comp(𝒪) ⥤ D(𝒪)` has a left adjoint. The tag's formula for
  that adjoint is `bijective_precomp_completionUnit_idealOfGlobalSections`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.bijective_precomp_completionUnit_idealOfGlobalSections
declarations.doc:
**The Čech complex computes the left adjoint of [Stacks, Tag 099B]**, which is the formula
the tag gives alongside the existence statement: for `ℐ = (f_1, …, f_r)`, every `K` and every
derived-complete `Z`, precomposition with the completion map `η_K : K ⟶ K^∧` is a bijection
`Hom_{D(𝒪)}(K^∧, Z) ⟶ Hom_{D(𝒪)}(K, Z)`, where
`K^∧ = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)` is `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.completionFunctor` and `η` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.completionUnit`, both of `Completion.lean`.

This is `Stacks.Algebraization.bijective_precomp_completionUnit` with its two hypotheses
discharged: `η_Z` is invertible on a derived-complete `Z` by clause 2
(`isIso_completionUnit_app_of_isDerivedComplete_idealOfGlobalSections`), and `Φ η_K` is
invertible with no hypothesis by `isIso_completionFunctor_map_completionUnit_app`. Clause 1 is
not used, so the bijection does not depend on `isDerivedComplete_completionFunctor`; what
clause 1 supplies is that `K^∧` is itself an object of `D_comp(𝒪)`, which is what turns the
bijection into an adjunction.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_precomp_completionUnit_idealOfGlobalSections
    {Z : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} X.O))}
    (hZ : IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X (idealOfGlobalSections X f) Z) :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun g : (completionFunctor X f).obj L ⟶ Z ↦ (completionUnit X f).app L ≫ g)
declarations.comment:
the tag's formula for the left adjoint: `K^∧ = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)`, with
  precomposition by `K ⟶ K^∧` bijective on morphisms into a derived-complete object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.bijective_precomp_completionUnit_generatedIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The universal property of the Čech completion**: for every `K` in `D(𝒪)` and every `E`
derived complete along `ℐ = (f_1, …, f_r)`, precomposition with the completion map `K ⟶ K^∧` is a
bijection

`Hom_{D(𝒪)}(K^∧, E) ⟶ Hom_{D(𝒪)}(K, E)`,

where `K^∧ = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)` is the Čech completion and the map `K ⟶ K^∧` is
`completionUnit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_precomp_completionUnit_generatedIdealSheaf
    (K E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hE : IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X (generatedIdealSheaf f) E) :
    Function.Bijective
      (fun g : (completionFunctor X f).obj K ⟶ E ↦ (completionUnit X f).app K ≫ g)
declarations.comment: the universal property of the Čech completion: precomposition with `K ⟶ K^∧` is bijective onto the morphisms into a derived-complete object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site and let `f_1, …, f_r` be global sections of `𝒪`. The inclusion
of the objects of `D(𝒪)` derived complete along `ℐ = (f_1, …, f_r)` into `D(𝒪)` has a left
adjoint, namely the Čech completion `K ↦ R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf :
    (ObjectProperty.ι
      (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X (generatedIdealSheaf f))).IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment: the existence of the left adjoint of the inclusion `D_comp(𝒪) ⥤ D(𝒪)`, at the ideal sheaf generated by the given global sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf_completionFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
**The `hΦ` hypothesis of [Stacks, Tag 099F], discharged**: every Čech completion
`K^∧ = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)` is derived complete along the ideal sheaf
`ℐ = (f_1, …, f_r)` generated by the sections the Čech complex is built from.

It is `memVanishingIdeal_completionFunctor_obj` — the vanishing at the generators — followed by
`isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf_of_forall_memVanishingIdeal`, which raises the vanishing
at the finitely many generators to the condition of [Stacks, Tag 0999] at every local section of
`ℐ`. Nothing is assumed of `K`, of the sections or of the site.

It is also the clause of [Stacks, Tag 099B] which asserts that the object `K^∧` the tag
constructs lies in `D_comp(𝒪)`; the universal property that makes it the left adjoint is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.bijective_precomp_completionUnit_generatedIdealSheaf` of
`GeneratedIdealAdjoint.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf_completionFunctor_obj
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X (generatedIdealSheaf f) ((completionFunctor X f).obj K)
declarations.comment: that the Čech completion `K^∧ = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)` lies in `D_comp(𝒪)`, at the ideal sheaf generated by the sections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_of_forall_isNilpotent
declarations.doc:
**The inclusion `D_comp(𝒪) ⥤ D(𝒪)` has a left adjoint when the local sections of `ℐ` are
nilpotent.** Every object is then derived complete, so the identity functor together with the
identity natural transformation is a derived completion functor.

This is the conclusion of [Stacks, Tag 099B], under a hypothesis that is not the source's. The
source asks that `ℐ` be the ideal sheaf generated by finitely many global sections
`f_1, …, f_r`; that generation relation is *not* assumed here, so in that direction the
statement is more general than the tag, and it is restricted in the other direction by the
nilpotence of the sections. The explicit formula the tag also gives for the left adjoint,
`K^∧ = R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)`, is constructed as
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.completionFunctor` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.completionUnit` in
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalGeometry/DerivedCompletionRinged/Completion.lean` and is
proved to be that left adjoint — *under* the tag's generation hypothesis — in
`CompletionIdempotent.lean`. Under the nilpotence hypothesis of this statement the left adjoint
is the identity, which is not that formula.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_of_forall_isNilpotent
    (hI : ∀ (U : X.C) (f : ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)).obj.obj (op U)),
      f ∈ I.toSubmodule.obj (op U) → IsNilpotent f) :
    (ObjectProperty.ι (IsDerivedComplete.{u, v, max u v, max u v} X I)).IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment:
the conclusion — the inclusion `D_comp(𝒪) ⥤ D(𝒪)` has a left adjoint — for a
  sheaf of ideals all of whose local sections are nilpotent, where that left adjoint is the
  identity. The source's hypothesis that `ℐ` be generated by finitely many global sections is
  not assumed; with that hypothesis the tag, including its Čech formula for the left adjoint,
  is carried by `CompletionIdempotent.lean`

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedRestrictScalars.isDerivedComplete_restrictScalars_of_extendIdeal
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099C], the inclusion `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ𝒪') ⊆` the inverse image of
`D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)`.** A complex of `𝒪'`-modules which is derived complete along the extension
`ℐ𝒪'` of a sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` restricts to a complex of `𝒪`-modules which is derived
complete along `ℐ`.

A local section `f` of `ℐ` has its image in `ℐ𝒪'` by `extendIdeal`, so the hypothesis gives
`T(E|_U, f) = 0` computed over `𝒪'`. Restriction of scalars commutes with restriction to the
slice site over `U`, and it carries multiplication by the image of `f` to multiplication by `f`,
so the two difference maps `1 - f·shift` correspond; since restriction of scalars commutes with
the countable products of the derived categories, invertibility transfers.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_restrictScalars_of_extendIdeal (α : O ⟶ O')
    (I : _root_.SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (ringedSite J O).O))))
    (E : DerivedCategory
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (ringedSite J O').O))))
    (h : RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} (ringedSite J O')
      (RingedSite.extendIdeal (ringSheafHom (O := O) (O' := O') α) I) E) :
    RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} (ringedSite J O) I
      ((_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
        (ringSheafHom (O := O) (O' := O') α)).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)
declarations.comment: the inclusion D_comp(𝒪', ℐ𝒪') ⊆ the inverse image of D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedRestrictScalars.isDerivedComplete_restrictScalars_iff
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099C].** For a homomorphism `𝒪 ⟶ 𝒪'` of sheaves of commutative rings on a
site and a sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪`, a complex of `𝒪'`-modules restricts to a complex of
`𝒪`-modules derived complete along `ℐ` if and only if it is derived complete along `ℐ𝒪'`. That
is, the inverse image of `D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)` under the restriction functor `D(𝒪') ⟶ D(𝒪)` is
`D_comp(𝒪', ℐ𝒪')`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_restrictScalars_iff (α : O ⟶ O')
    (I : _root_.SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (ringedSite J O).O))))
    (E : DerivedCategory
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (ringedSite J O').O)))) :
    RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} (ringedSite J O) I
        ((_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
          (ringSheafHom (O := O) (O' := O') α)).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) ↔
      RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} (ringedSite J O')
        (RingedSite.extendIdeal (ringSheafHom (O := O) (O' := O') α) I) E

declarations.name: Stacks.FunctorialCechFamily.exists_extendedCechObject_iso_over_augmentation
declarations.doc:
**Condition (d) of tag 099D, for the extended Čech complex of a chosen generating family.**
If `g₁, …, g_s` and `f₁, …, f_r` both generate the finitely generated ideal `I ⊆ A`, there is an
isomorphism in `D(A)` from the extended alternating Čech complex on `f₁, …, f_r` to the one on
`g₁, …, g_s`, carrying the augmentation of the former onto the augmentation of the latter.

This is the field `Stacks.LocalCohomology.FunctorialCechData.exists_cech_iso`, read at
`complex A I hI = extendedCechComplex g (ModuleCat.of A A)`. The isomorphism is
`Stacks.IdealCechComplex.canonicalIso`, which lives in `D(A)`; condition (d), being itself a
condition in `D(A)`, asks for nothing more.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_extendedCechObject_iso_over_augmentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {r s : ℕ}
    (f : Fin r → A) (g : Fin s → A) (I : Ideal A)
    (hf : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I) (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = I) :
    ∃ e : extendedCechObject f (ModuleCat.of A A) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (extendedCechComplex g (ModuleCat.of A A)),
      e.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (extendedCechAugmentation g (ModuleCat.of A A)) ≫
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctorIsoCompQ (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).app
            (ModuleCat.of A A)).inv =
        extendedCechAugmentationHom f (ModuleCat.of A A)
declarations.comment: condition (d) for a pair with a chosen finite generating family

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.nonempty_functorialCechData
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099D].** There is a way to construct, for every commutative ring `A` and
every finitely generated ideal `I ⊆ A`, a complex `K(A, I)` of `A`-modules, a map of complexes
of `A`-modules `K(A, I) → A`, and for every ring map `φ : A → B` a map of complexes of
`A`-modules `K(A, I) → K(B, IB)`, such that

* (a) for `A → B` and `I ⊆ A` finitely generated the square formed by the two augmentations,
  the map `K(A, I) → K(B, IB)` and `A → B` commutes;
* (b) for `A → B → C` and `I ⊆ A` finitely generated the composition of
  `K(A, I) → K(B, IB)` and `K(B, IB) → K(C, IC)` is the map `K(A, I) → K(C, IC)`;
* (c) for `A → B` and `I ⊆ A` finitely generated the induced map
  `K(A, I) ⊗^𝐋_A B → K(B, IB)` is an isomorphism in `D(B)`;
* (d) if `I = (f₁, …, f_r) ⊆ A` then the extended alternating Čech complex on `f₁, …, f_r` is
  isomorphic to `K(A, I)` in `D(A)` by an isomorphism commuting with the augmentations onto `A`.

These are exactly the data `complex`, `augmentation`, `map` and the conditions
`map_augmentation`, `map_map`, `isIso_derivedBaseChange`, `exists_cech_iso` of
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.FunctorialCechData`.
declarations.statement: theorem nonempty_functorialCechData : Nonempty FunctorialCechData.{u}
declarations.comment: for every ring A and finitely generated ideal I ⊆ A the complex K(A, I) of A-modules, its augmentation K(A, I) → A, and for every ring map A → B the map K(A, I) → K(B, IB), compatible with the augmentations and composing on the nose, with K(A, I) ⊗^𝐋_A B → K(B, IB) an isomorphism in D(B) and with K(A, I) identified in D(A) over A with the extended alternating Čech complex on any finite generating family of I

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.exists_pairCechComplex
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099D], with the three data and the four conditions written out.** This is
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.nonempty_functorialCechData` with the fields of
`Stacks.LocalCohomology.FunctorialCechData` unfolded into the statement, so that nothing about
the tag is hidden behind a structure.

The three quantified data are the tag's items (1), (2), (3):

* `K A I hI` is the complex of `A`-modules of item (1). It is a function of the pair `(A, I)`
  alone: no generating family of `I` occurs among its arguments, and `hI : I.FG` is a proof, so
  by proof irrelevance `K A I` is determined by `A` and `I`.
* `aug A I hI : K A I hI ⟶ A[0]` is the map of complexes of item (2).
* `mp A B φ I hI J hJ hφ : K A I hI ⟶ (K B J hJ)|_A` is the map of complexes of `A`-modules of
