  item (3), for `J = IB`. The ideal `IB` is passed as a separate `J` with the equation
  `hφ : J = Ideal.map φ I`, which is the same data and lets (b) be stated without transporting
  along `Ideal.map_map`.

The four conjuncts are the tag's conditions (a), (b), (c), (d), in order:

* (a) the square formed by `mp`, the two augmentations and `A → B` commutes;
* (b) `mp` for `A → C` is `mp` for `A → B` followed by `mp` for `B → C`;
* (c) the induced map `K(A, I) ⊗^𝐋_A B → K(B, IB)` is an isomorphism in `D(B)`;
* (d) for **every** finite family `f₁, …, f_r` generating `I` there is an isomorphism in `D(A)`
  from the extended alternating Čech complex on `f₁, …, f_r` to `K(A, I)` carrying its
  augmentation onto the augmentation of `K(A, I)`.

Conditions (a) and (b) are equalities of maps of complexes, not merely of their images in the
derived category, which is what makes `K` a functor on the category of pairs.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_pairCechComplex :
    ∃ (K : (A : Type u) → [CommRing A] → (I : Ideal A) → I.FG →
            CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
      (aug : (A : Type u) → [CommRing A] → (I : Ideal A) → (hI : I.FG) →
            (K A I hI ⟶
              (CochainComplex.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).obj (ModuleCat.of A A)))
      (mp : (A B : Type u) → [CommRing A] → [CommRing B] → (φ : A →+* B) → (I : Ideal A) →
            (hI : I.FG) → (J : Ideal B) → (hJ : J.FG) → J = I.map φ →
            (K A I hI ⟶ (CochainComplex.restrictScalars φ).obj (K B J hJ))),
      (∀ (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
          (J : Ideal B) (hJ : J.FG) (hφ : J = I.map φ),
          mp A B φ I hI J hJ hφ ≫ (CochainComplex.restrictScalars φ).map (aug B J hJ) =
            aug A I hI ≫ singleRingHom φ) ∧
      (∀ (A B C : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [CommRing C] (φ : A →+* B) (ψ : B →+* C)
          (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG) (J : Ideal B) (hJ : J.FG) (L : Ideal C) (hL : L.FG)
          (hφ : J = I.map φ) (hψ : L = J.map ψ),
          mp A C (ψ.comp φ) I hI L hL (by rw [hψ, hφ, Ideal.map_map]) =
            mp A B φ I hI J hJ hφ ≫
              (CochainComplex.restrictScalars φ).map (mp B C ψ J hJ L hL hψ) ≫
                (restrictScalarsCompComplexIso φ ψ).hom.app (K C L hL)) ∧
      (∀ (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG)
          (J : Ideal B) (hJ : J.FG) (hφ : J = I.map φ),
          IsIso (derivedBaseChange φ (mp A B φ I hI J hJ hφ))) ∧
      (∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → A) (I : Ideal A) (hI : I.FG),
          Ideal.span (Set.range f) = I →
          ∃ e : extendedCechObject f (ModuleCat.of A A) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (K A I hI),
            e.hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map (aug A I hI) ≫
                ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctorIsoCompQ (ModuleCat.{u} A) 0).app
                  (ModuleCat.of A A)).inv =
              extendedCechAugmentationHom f (ModuleCat.of A A))
declarations.comment: the complex K(A, I) of A-modules attached to the pair (A, I) alone, its augmentation K(A, I) → A, and for every ring map φ : A → B the map of complexes of A-modules K(A, I) → K(B, IB), with (a) the augmentation square commuting, (b) the maps composing on the nose, (c) K(A, I) ⊗^𝐋_A B → K(B, IB) an isomorphism in D(B), and (d) for every finite generating family f₁, …, f_r of I an isomorphism in D(A) over A from the extended alternating Čech complex on f₁, …, f_r to K(A, I); the data and the conditions written out in the statement

declarations.name: Stacks.CechRingBaseChange.cechModEmptyEquiv_modMap
declarations.doc:
**The augmentation square of tag 099D, condition (a).** In degree zero the change-of-rings
map is `φ` itself: the degree-zero localization inverts nothing, and the identification of it
with the ring carries the map onto `φ`.  The augmentations of the two Čech complexes are their
degree-zero identifications with the rings, so this is the commutativity of the square they form
with `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechModEmptyEquiv_modMap (φ : A →+* B) (f : Fin r → A)
    (x : Cech.cechMod f A (∅ : Finset (Fin r))) :
    Stacks.CechBaseChange.cechModEmptyEquiv (mapFamily φ f) B (modMap φ f ∅ x) =
      φ (Stacks.CechBaseChange.cechModEmptyEquiv f A x)
declarations.comment: condition (a) for a pair with a chosen finite generating family

declarations.name: Stacks.CechRingBaseChange.termMap_zero
declarations.doc:
**Condition (a) on the degree-zero term of the complex.**  The empty set is the only index
of cardinality zero, so the degree-zero term of the Čech complex is the summand it indexes, and
there the change-of-rings map is `φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem termMap_zero (φ : A →+* B) (f : Fin r → A) (a : A) :
    termMap φ f 0 (DirectSum.lof A {t : Finset (Fin r) // t.card = 0}
        (fun t => Cech.cechMod f A t.1) ⟨∅, Finset.card_empty⟩
        (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap (Cech.cechSub f (∅ : Finset (Fin r))) A a)) =
      DirectSum.lof B {t : Finset (Fin r) // t.card = 0}
        (fun t => Cech.cechMod (mapFamily φ f) B t.1) ⟨∅, Finset.card_empty⟩
        (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap
          (Cech.cechSub (mapFamily φ f) (∅ : Finset (Fin r))) B (φ a))
declarations.comment: condition (a) for a pair with a chosen finite generating family

declarations.name: Stacks.CechRingBaseChange.complexMap
declarations.doc:
**Change of rings for the extended alternating Čech complex, tag 099D items (1)–(3) for a
pair with a chosen finite generating family.** The complex is `C^•(f₁, …, f_r; A)`, the
augmentation onto `A` is its degree-zero projection, and this is the map of complexes of
`A`-modules onto `C^•(g₁, …, g_r; B)` for `g_i = φ(f_i)`.
declarations.statement:
def complexMap (φ : A →+* B) (f : Fin r → A) :
    Cech.cechComplex f A ⟶
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
        (Cech.cechComplex (mapFamily φ f) B)
declarations.comment: item (3) for a pair with a chosen finite generating family

declarations.name: Stacks.CechRingBaseChange.complexMap_comp
declarations.doc:
**Tag 099D, condition (b).** For `A → B → C` the composite of the change-of-rings maps for
`φ : A → B` and `ψ : B → C` is the change-of-rings map for `ψ ∘ φ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem complexMap_comp (φ : A →+* B) (ψ : B →+* C) (f : Fin r → A) :
    complexMap φ f ≫
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).map
          (complexMap ψ (mapFamily φ f)) =
      complexMap (ψ.comp φ) f
declarations.comment: condition (b) for a pair with a chosen finite generating family

declarations.name: Stacks.CechRingBaseChange.isIso_derivedBaseChange_extendedComplexMap
declarations.doc:
**The derived base change of the Čech complex is an isomorphism.** The map
`C^•(f₁, …, f_r; A) ⊗^L_A B → C^•(g₁, …, g_r; B)` induced by the change-of-rings map of item (3)
is an isomorphism in `D(B)`: the Čech complex of a ring is K-flat, so the derived base change is
computed by the degreewise one, which is an isomorphism because each
`B ⊗_A A_{f_{i_0} \cdots f_{i_{p-1}}} → B_{g_{i_0} \cdots g_{i_{p-1}}}` is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedBaseChange_extendedComplexMap (φ : A →+* B) (f : Fin r → A) :
    IsIso (Stacks.LocalCohomology.derivedBaseChange φ (extendedComplexMap φ f))
declarations.comment: condition (c) for a pair with a chosen finite generating family

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.extendedCechComplex
declarations.doc:
The extended alternating Čech complex `C^•(f₁, …, f_r; M)`, regarded as a cochain complex in
integer degrees.

Read at `M = A`, this is **item (1) of tag 099D** for a pair carrying a chosen finite generating
family: the complex of `A`-modules attached to the pair.
declarations.statement: abbrev extendedCechComplex : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max u v} R) ℤ
declarations.comment: item (1) for a pair with a chosen finite generating family

declarations.name: Stacks.LocalCohomology.extendedCechAugmentation
declarations.doc:
**The augmentation of the Čech complex.** It is the identity on `M` in degree zero and zero
elsewhere; the Stacks map `C^•(f₁, …, f_r; M) → M`.

Read at `M = A`, this is **item (2) of tag 099D** for a pair carrying a chosen finite generating
family: the map from the complex onto the ring.
declarations.comment: item (2) for a pair with a chosen finite generating family

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_isGlobalExtendedCech
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099E]**: for a sheaf of ideals `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪` on a ringed site there is a map
`K ⟶ 𝒪` such that for every object `U` and every finite family of sections over `U` generating
`ℐ|_U`, the extended alternating Čech complex of the family is isomorphic to `K|_U` in `D(𝒪_U)`,
compatibly with the maps to `𝒪_U`.

The source assumes `ℐ` of finite type; the construction does not use it — over an object on which
`ℐ` is not finitely generated the condition is empty — so it is not assumed here. The map is a map
of complexes, `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.finiteTypeCechAugmentation`, whose image in `D(𝒪)` is
the map of the tag.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isGlobalExtendedCech :
    ∃ (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ℤ)
      (a : K ⟶ structureSheafComplex X),
      IsGlobalExtendedCech X ℐ K a

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099F].** Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site and `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` a sheaf of ideals of
finite type. Then the inclusion `D_comp(𝒪, ℐ) ⥤ D(𝒪)` of the objects derived complete along `ℐ`
has a left adjoint.

As in the source, the left adjoint is `E ↦ R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(K, E)` for the map `K ⟶ 𝒪` of
[Stacks, Tag 099E], `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.finiteTypeCechAugmentation`: the three clauses
of the universal property are checked on the slices of a covering family over which `ℐ` is
generated by finitely many sections, in
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_of_isGlobalExtendedCech`; and
`derivedCompletionIsoFiniteTypeCech` below identifies the derived completion functor with that
formula.
declarations.statement:
instance isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete :
    (ObjectProperty.ι (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I)).IsRightAdjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, 𝒪)` be a ringed site and let `f_1, …, f_r` be global sections of `𝒪`. The inclusion
of the objects of `D(𝒪)` derived complete along `ℐ = (f_1, …, f_r)` into `D(𝒪)` has a left
adjoint, namely the Čech completion `K ↦ R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(Č(f), K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_generatedIdealSheaf :
    (ObjectProperty.ι
      (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X (generatedIdealSheaf f))).IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment: for the sheaf of ideals generated by finitely many global sections of the structure sheaf, with the Čech completion of 099B as the left adjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.completeDerivedSheafHom
declarations.doc:
**The derived internal Hom of derived-complete objects is derived complete**, so it is a
bifunctor `D_comp(𝒪)ᵒᵖ × D_comp(𝒪) ⥤ D_comp(𝒪)`. This is the last assertion of
[Stacks, Tag 099G], and it is [Stacks, Tag 099A] — which asks nothing of the source — applied
to a derived-complete target.
declarations.statement:
def completeDerivedSheafHom :
    (ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I))ᵒᵖ ⥤
      ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I) ⥤
        ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I)
declarations.comment:
the assertion `R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(L, M) ∈ D_comp(𝒪)` for `L, M ∈ D_comp(𝒪)`, which the
  tag records at the end and attributes to [Stacks, Tag 099A], as the induced bifunctor on the
  derived-complete objects; it holds for every sheaf of ideals

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.completedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**The completed tensor product of [Stacks, Tag 099G].** For `ℐ` of finite type and
derived-complete `K` and `L`, `K ⊗^∧_𝒪 L = (K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 L)^∧`, where `(-)^∧` is the derived
completion functor of [Stacks, Tag 099F]; the completion of any object is derived complete, so
this is a bifunctor on the derived-complete objects.
declarations.statement:
def completedTensorProduct :
    ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I) ⥤
      ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I) ⥤
        ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I)
declarations.comment:
the completed tensor product `K ⊗^∧_𝒪 L = (K ⊗^𝐋_𝒪 L)^∧` and its functoriality
  in each variable, as a bifunctor on `D_comp(𝒪)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.completedTensorProductProd
declarations.doc:
**The completed tensor product as a functor `D_comp(𝒪) × D_comp(𝒪) ⥤ D_comp(𝒪)`**, the
shape in which [Stacks, Tag 099G] states it, for `ℐ` of finite type.
declarations.statement:
def completedTensorProductProd :
    ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I) ×
        ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I) ⥤
      ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I)
declarations.comment: the completed tensor product as a functor `D_comp(𝒪) × D_comp(𝒪) → D_comp(𝒪)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.completedTensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**The adjunction of [Stacks, Tag 099G].** For `ℐ` of finite type and derived-complete `K`,
`L` and `M`,

`Hom_{D_comp(𝒪)}(K, R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(L, M)) = Hom_{D_comp(𝒪)}(K ⊗^∧_𝒪 L, M)`.

It is `completedTensorHomEquivOfIsRightAdjoint` at the derived completion functor of
[Stacks, Tag 099F]: in order, the full faithfulness of `D_comp(𝒪) ⥤ D(𝒪)`, the bijection of
[Stacks, Tag 08J8], and the inverse of the hom-set bijection of the adjunction of
[Stacks, Tag 099F] at the derived-complete `M`.
declarations.statement:
def completedTensorHomEquiv
    (K L M : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I)) :
    (K ⟶ ((completeDerivedSheafHom X I).obj (op L)).obj M) ≃
      (((completedTensorProduct X I).obj K).obj L ⟶ M)
declarations.comment:
the bijection
  `Hom_{D_comp(𝒪)}(K, R𝑆heafHom_𝒪(L, M)) = Hom_{D_comp(𝒪)}(K ⊗^∧_𝒪 L, M)` for
  `K, L, M ∈ D_comp(𝒪)`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.CechFlatNeighbourhood.quasiIso_complexMap_cechSystemBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 099H.**  Let `C` be a site, let `φ : O ⟶ O'` be a flat homomorphism
of sheaves of commutative rings on `C`, and let `f₁, …, f_r` be global sections of `O` such that
the canonical map `O/(f₁, …, f_r) ⟶ O'/(f₁, …, f_r)O'` of sheaves of `O`-modules
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedRestrictScalars.quotientMap`) is an isomorphism; here
`(f₁, …, f_r)` is the ideal sheaf generated by the `f_k`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.idealOfGlobalSections`) and `(f₁, …, f_r)O'` is the ideal sheaf of
`O'` it generates (`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.extendIdeal`), which is the ideal sheaf generated
by the images of the `f_k`
(`Stacks.Sheaves.CechFlatNeighbourhood.extendedIdeal_idealOfGlobalSections`). Then the map of
extended alternating Čech complexes

`O → ∏_{i₀} O_{f_{i₀}} → ∏_{i₀ < i₁} O_{f_{i₀}f_{i₁}} → ⋯ → O_{f₁⋯f_r}`
`  ⟶ O' → ∏_{i₀} O'_{f_{i₀}} → ∏_{i₀ < i₁} O'_{f_{i₀}f_{i₁}} → ⋯ → O'_{f₁⋯f_r}`

is a quasi-isomorphism.  The map is the one induced by the canonical maps
`O_{f_S} ⟶ O'_{f_S}` of sheaves of `O`-modules, `cechSystemBaseChangeMap`: they are compatible
with `O ⟶ O_{f_S}` and `O ⟶ O' ⟶ O'_{f_S}`
(`unitToAwayModule_comp_cechSystemBaseChangeMap_app`), and they are the only such family
(`eq_cechSystemBaseChangeMap`).  The lower complex is the extended alternating Čech complex of
the system `S ↦ O'_{f_S}` of sheaves of `O`-modules.

The proof is the source's: `quasiIso_extendedAlternatingCechBaseChangeMap`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_complexMap_cechSystemBaseChangeMap (hφ : IsFlatMap φ)
    (hiso : IsIso (Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedRestrictScalars.quotientMap φ
      (idealOfGlobalSections (ringedSite O) f))) :
    QuasiIso (AlternatingCech.complexMap (cechSystemBaseChangeMap O f φ))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedRestrictScalars.isEquivalence_derivedCompleteRestrictScalars
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099I].** Let `𝒞` be a site, `α : 𝒪 ⟶ 𝒪'` a homomorphism of sheaves of
commutative rings and `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` a sheaf of ideals of finite type. If `α` is flat and
`𝒪/ℐ ≅ 𝒪'/ℐ𝒪'`, then restriction of scalars `D(𝒪') ⥤ D(𝒪)` induces an equivalence
`D_comp(𝒪', ℐ𝒪') ⥤ D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)`: the functor `derivedCompleteRestrictScalars α ℐ` is an
equivalence.

Flatness is `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlatMap α` ([Stacks, Tag 03ER]): `𝒪'` is a flat
`𝒪`-module. The isomorphism `𝒪/ℐ ≅ 𝒪'/ℐ𝒪'` is the canonical map
`quotientMap α ℐ : 𝒪/ℐ ⟶ 𝒪'/ℐ𝒪'` induced by `α` being invertible, with `ℐ𝒪'` the ideal sheaf
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.extendIdeal` of `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ𝒪')`. Finite type is Mathlib's
`SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_derivedCompleteRestrictScalars
    (hflat : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsFlatMap α)
    (I : _root_.SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.unit
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf.{u, u, u} (ringedSite J O).O)))
    [I.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType]
    (hquot : IsIso (quotientMap α I)) :
    (derivedCompleteRestrictScalars α I).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.derivedPushforward_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099J].** Let `f : (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪_X) ⟶ (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪_Y)` be a morphism of ringed topoi
and let `ℐ' ⊂ 𝒪_X` and `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪_Y` be sheaves of ideals such that `f^♯` sends `f⁻¹ℐ` into `ℐ'`, that
is, such that the composite `f⁻¹ℐ ⟶ f⁻¹𝒪_Y ⟶ 𝒪_X` of the inverse image of the inclusion with the
structure map factors through `ℐ' ⊂ 𝒪_X`. Then `Rf_*` sends `D_comp(𝒪_X, ℐ')` into
`D_comp(𝒪_Y, ℐ)`.

The proof reduces to morphisms of ringed sites by [Stacks, Tag 03CR]; see the module
docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedPushforward_isDerivedComplete (f : RingedToposHom.{u, u, u, u, u, u} X Y)
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.toRingedSite.O))))
    (I' : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.toRingedSite.O))))
    (hI : ∃ φ : f.toToposHom.inverseImage.obj
        ((Sheaf.moduleSheafFunctor ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.toRingedSite.O))).obj
          I.toSheafOfModules) ⟶
        (Sheaf.moduleSheafFunctor ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.toRingedSite.O))).obj
          I'.toSheafOfModules,
      f.toToposHom.inverseImage.map
          ((Sheaf.moduleSheafFunctor
            ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.toRingedSite.O))).map I.ι) ≫
        X.forgetRing.map f.fSharpInverseImage =
      φ ≫ (Sheaf.moduleSheafFunctor
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.toRingedSite.O))).map I'.ι)
    (K : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (J := X.J)) X.O)))
    (hK : RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X.toRingedSite I' K) :
    RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} Y.toRingedSite I
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforward.derivedPushforward.{u, u, u, u, u, u} f).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isDerivedComplete_derivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099K], first statement.** Let `f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be a morphism
of ringed topoi and let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪`, `ℐ' ⊆ 𝒪'` be sheaves of ideals such that `f^♯` sends `f^{-1}ℐ`
into `ℐ'`. Then `Rf_*` sends `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ')` into `D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)`: if `K` is derived complete
along `ℐ'`, then `Rf_*K` is derived complete along `ℐ`.

The source asks `ℐ` and `ℐ'` to be of finite type; neither hypothesis is needed. This is
[Stacks, Tag 099J], `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.derivedPushforward_isDerivedComplete`,
read in the variables of Tag 099K, as the source's proof says.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_derivedPushforward (hI : IdealCompatible f I I')
    (K : DerivedCategory
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.toRingedSite.O))))
    (hK : RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X.toRingedSite I' K) :
    RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} Y.toRingedSite I
      ((DerivedPushforward.derivedPushforward (X := X) (Y := Y) f).obj K)
declarations.comment:
first statement: `Rf_*` sends `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ')` into `D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)`; the
  finite-type hypotheses on `ℐ` and `ℐ'` are not needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.derivedCompletePullbackPushforwardAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099K], second statement.** Let `f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be a
morphism of ringed topoi and let `ℐ ⊆ 𝒪`, `ℐ' ⊆ 𝒪'` be sheaves of ideals such that `f^♯` sends
`f^{-1}ℐ` into `ℐ'`, with `ℐ'` of finite type. Then `Rf_*` sends `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ')` into
`D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)` (`isDerivedComplete_derivedPushforward`, read as the functor
`derivedCompletePushforward`), and this functor has a left adjoint `Lf^*_comp`, which is `Lf^*`
followed by derived completion along `ℐ'` (`derivedCompletePullback`, and
`derivedCompletePullback_comp_ι`).

The derived completion functor is the left adjoint of the inclusion `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ') ⥤ D(𝒪')`
that [Stacks, Tag 099F] provides for `ℐ'` of finite type, the instance
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete`. The source also asks `ℐ` to be
of finite type; that is not needed, since [Stacks, Tag 099J] holds for an arbitrary `ℐ`. The two
ringed topoi are presented by sites small in the universe of the sections of their structure
sheaves, as in [Stacks, Tag 03CR], through which Tag 099J is proved.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCompletePullbackPushforwardAdjunction [I'.toSheafOfModules.IsFiniteType]
    (hI : IdealCompatible f I I') :
    derivedCompletePullback f I I' ⊣ derivedCompletePushforward f I I' hI
declarations.comment:
second statement: the left adjoint `Lf^*_comp` of `Rf_*` on the derived-complete
  objects, `Lf^*` followed by derived completion; the finite-type hypothesis on `ℐ` is not
  needed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletion_eq_rlim_constantAdicTower
declarations.doc:
Let `𝒞` be a site, let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring and let `I ⊂ Λ` be an ideal. The left adjoint
`K ↦ K^∧` of the inclusion of the objects of `D(𝒞, Λ)` derived complete along `IΛ̲`
([Stacks, Tag 099F]) sends `K` to `R lim (K ⊗^𝐋_Λ (Λ/Iⁿ)̲)`; and `K` is derived complete exactly
when `K = R lim (K ⊗^𝐋_Λ (Λ/Iⁿ)̲)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCompletion_eq_rlim_constantAdicTower
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constant J Λ).O))) :
    IsDerivedLimit (constantAdicTower J Λ I K)
        ((derivedCompletion (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I)).obj K) ∧
      (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I) K ↔
        IsDerivedLimit (constantAdicTower J Λ I K) K)

declarations.name: Stacks.ModuleSheaf.exists_leftAdjoint_isDerivedLimitWithProjections_derivedReductionTower
declarations.doc:
**The derived completion functor in the constant Noetherian case.** The inclusion of the
derived complete objects of `D(C, Λ)` has a left adjoint `K ↦ K^∧`, where `K^∧` is a derived limit
`R lim (K ⊗_Λ^L \underline{Λ/Iⁿ})` with projections natural in `K`, whose composites with the
unit `K → K^∧` are the reductions `K → K ⊗_Λ^L \underline{Λ/Iⁿ}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_leftAdjoint_isDerivedLimitWithProjections_derivedReductionTower :
    let P : ObjectProperty (DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ))) :=
      fun K ↦ IsDerivedComplete I K
    ∃ (Lf : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)) ⥤ P.FullSubcategory) (adj : Lf ⊣ P.ι)
      (π : ∀ n : ℕ, Lf ⋙ P.ι ⟶
        derivedReductionTowerFunctor J Λ I ⋙ (evaluation ℕᵒᵖ _).obj ⟨n⟩),
      (∀ K, IsDerivedLimitWithProjections (derivedReductionTower J Λ I K) ((Lf ⋙ P.ι).obj K)
        fun n ↦ (π n).app K) ∧
      ∀ K (n : ℕ), adj.unit.app K ≫ (π n).app K = (derivedReductionMap J Λ I K).app ⟨n⟩
declarations.comment: the left adjoint is `K ↦ R lim (K ⊗^L Λ/Iⁿ)`

declarations.name: Stacks.ModuleSheaf.isDerivedComplete_iff_isDerivedLimitWithProjections_derivedReductionTower
declarations.doc:
**`K` is derived complete if and only if `K = R lim (K ⊗_Λ^L \underline{Λ/Iⁿ})`**, i.e.
`K`, with the reductions `K → K ⊗_Λ^L \underline{Λ/Iⁿ}`, is a derived limit of the reductions.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_iff_isDerivedLimitWithProjections_derivedReductionTower
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ))) :
    IsDerivedComplete I K ↔ IsDerivedLimitWithProjections (derivedReductionTower J Λ I K) K
      fun n ↦ (derivedReductionMap J Λ I K).app ⟨n⟩
declarations.comment: in particular: `K` is complete iff `K = R lim (K ⊗^L Λ/Iⁿ)`

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isDerivedComplete_constantDerivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**`Rf_*` preserves derived completeness.** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊂ Λ` an ideal and
`f : Sh(𝒟) ⟶ Sh(𝒞)` a morphism of topoi. If `E` in `D(𝒟, Λ)` is derived complete along `IΛ̲`, so
is `Rf_*E` in `D(𝒞, Λ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_constantDerivedPushforward
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (RingedTopos.constant K Λ).O)))
    (hE : RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} (RingedSite.constant K Λ)
      (RingedSite.constantIdealSheaf K Λ I) E) :
    RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} (RingedSite.constant J Λ)
      (RingedSite.constantIdealSheaf J Λ I) ((constantDerivedPushforward Λ f).obj E)

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.constantDerivedCompletePullbackPushforwardAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099N], part (2).** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊂ Λ` an ideal and
`f : Sh(𝒟) ⟶ Sh(𝒞)` a morphism of topoi. The functor `Rf_* : D_comp(𝒟, Λ) ⥤ D_comp(𝒞, Λ)` has
a left adjoint `Lf^*_comp : D_comp(𝒞, Λ) ⥤ D_comp(𝒟, Λ)`, which is `Lf^*` followed by derived
completion (`MorphismOfTopoi.constantDerivedCompletePullback_comp_ι`).
declarations.statement:
def constantDerivedCompletePullbackPushforwardAdjunction :
    constantDerivedCompletePullback Λ I f ⊣ constantDerivedCompletePushforward Λ I f

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isIso_derivedCompletionComparison_constantDerivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099N], part (3).** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊂ Λ` an ideal and
`f : Sh(𝒟) ⟶ Sh(𝒞)` a morphism of topoi. `Rf_*` commutes with derived completion: the canonical
comparison `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)`, natural in `K` in `D(𝒟, Λ)`, is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionComparison_constantDerivedPushforward :
    IsIso (RingedSite.derivedCompletionComparison (RingedSite.constantIdealSheaf K Λ I)
      (RingedSite.constantIdealSheaf J Λ I) (constantDerivedPushforward Λ f)
      (fun E hE => isDerivedComplete_constantDerivedPushforward Λ f I E hE))

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isDerivedLimit_constantAdicTower_constantDerivedPushforward
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099N], part (4).** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊂ Λ` an ideal and
`f : Sh(𝒟) ⟶ Sh(𝒞)` a morphism of topoi. For `K` in `D_comp(𝒟, Λ)`,
`Rf_*K = R lim Rf_*(K ⊗^𝐋_Λ (Λ/Iⁿ)̲)`: `Rf_*K` is a derived limit of the tower
`n ↦ Rf_*(K ⊗^𝐋_Λ (Λ/Iⁿ)̲)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_constantAdicTower_constantDerivedPushforward
    (E : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (RingedTopos.constant K Λ).O)))
    (hE : RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} (RingedSite.constant K Λ)
      (RingedSite.constantIdealSheaf K Λ I) E) :
    IsDerivedLimit (RingedSite.constantAdicTower K Λ I E ⋙ constantDerivedPushforward Λ f)
      ((constantDerivedPushforward Λ f).obj E)

declarations.name: MorphismOfTopoi.isDerivedLimit_constantAdicTower_constantDerivedCompletePullback
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099N], part (5).** Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring, `I ⊂ Λ` an ideal and
`f : Sh(𝒟) ⟶ Sh(𝒞)` a morphism of topoi. For `M` in `D_comp(𝒞, Λ)`,
`Lf^*_comp M = R lim Lf^*(M ⊗^𝐋_Λ (Λ/Iⁿ)̲)`: `Lf^*_comp M` is a derived limit of the tower
`n ↦ Lf^*(M ⊗^𝐋_Λ (Λ/Iⁿ)̲)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_constantAdicTower_constantDerivedCompletePullback
    (M : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u}
      (RingedTopos.constant J Λ).toRingedSite (RingedSite.constantIdealSheaf J Λ I))) :
    IsDerivedLimit (RingedSite.constantAdicTower J Λ I M.1 ⋙ constantDerivedPullback Λ f)
      ((constantDerivedCompletePullback Λ I f).obj M).1

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_derivedPushforward_adicReductionTower_of_proIso
declarations.doc:
**Part (4) of [Stacks, Tag 099N], granted the pro-isomorphism of towers of
[Stacks, Tag 099M].** Let `f : (Sh(𝒟), 𝒪') ⟶ (Sh(𝒞), 𝒪)` be a morphism of ringed sites, let
`g_1, …, g_r` be global sections of `𝒪'` and let `ℐ' = (g_1, …, g_r)`. Suppose the tower
`n ↦ Kₙ^∨` of duals of the Koszul complexes on the powers of the `g_i` is isomorphic, as a
pro-object of `D(𝒪')`, to the tower `n ↦ 𝒪'/ℐ'ⁿ⁺¹`. Then for every `K` in `D(𝒪')` derived
complete along `ℐ'`,

`Rf_*K = R lim Rf_*(K ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪'} 𝒪'/ℐ'ⁿ⁺¹)`.

This is the source's proof: Tag 099M in criterion form,
`isDerivedComplete_iff_isDerivedLimit_adicReductionTower_of_proIso`, exhibits `K` itself as a
derived limit of the tower of its adic reductions, and [Stacks, Tag 0A07],
`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedPushforwardOnRingedTopoi.isDerivedLimit_map_derivedPushforward`,
carries a derived limit along `Rf_*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_derivedPushforward_adicReductionTower_of_proIso
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasCoproduct ((koszulPowerSystem X g ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q).obj)]
    (hK : IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X (idealOfGlobalSections X g) K)
    (a : InverseSequence.ProIso (koszulPowerDualSystem X g)
      (adicQuotientDerivedTower X (idealOfGlobalSections X g))) :
    IsDerivedLimit (adicReductionTower X (idealOfGlobalSections X g) K ⋙
        derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom)
      ((derivedPushforward.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj K)
declarations.comment:
part (4), for an arbitrary ringed site and `ℐ'` the ideal sheaf generated by
  finitely many global sections, in place of the source's constant Noetherian coefficients
  `(𝒞, Λ)`, and with the tower of adic quotients taken on the source site. ASSUMED: the
  pro-isomorphism `a` in `D(𝒪')` of the dual Koszul tower with the tower `n ↦ 𝒪'/ℐ'ⁿ⁺¹`, which
  is the one hypothesis of this library's form of [Stacks, Tag 099M] and which the source
  derives from [Stacks, Tag 0921] over a Noetherian coefficient ring; and, carried from
  [Stacks, Tag 0A0E], the instance `HasCoproduct` for the Koszul system, which is automatic in
  the source

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_adicReductionTower_derivedCompletePullback_of_proIso
declarations.doc:
**Part (5) of [Stacks, Tag 099N], granted the pro-isomorphism of towers of
[Stacks, Tag 099M].** In the situation of
`isDerivedLimit_derivedPushforward_adicReductionTower_of_proIso`, and for an arbitrary sheaf of
ideals `ℐ ⊂ 𝒪` on the base, the completed pullback `Lf^*_comp M` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletePullback` — that is `Lf^*` followed by derived
completion along `ℐ'` — of an object `M` of `D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)` satisfies

`Lf^*_comp M = R lim (Lf^*M ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪'} 𝒪'/ℐ'ⁿ⁺¹)`.

The source writes the tower as `n ↦ Lf^*(M ⊗^𝐋 Λ/Iⁿ)`, which with its constant coefficients is
the same system: `Lf^*` commutes with `⊗^𝐋` by [Stacks, Tag 07A4] and fixes the constant sheaf
`Λ/Iⁿ`. Here the reductions are formed on the source site to begin with, so what is proved is
Tag 099M in formula form,
`isDerivedLimit_adicReductionTower_completionFunctor_of_proIso`, at the object `Lf^*M`, whose
completion is `Lf^*_comp M` by definition. The completion there is named by the Čech functor of
[Stacks, Tag 099B] and here by the reflector of [Stacks, Tag 099F]; the two are identified by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_iso_derivedCompletion_completionFunctor`, and the derived
limit crosses that isomorphism by
`CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.IsDerivedLimit.of_objIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedLimit_adicReductionTower_derivedCompletePullback_of_proIso
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf Y.O)))
    [HasCoproduct ((koszulPowerSystem X g ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q).obj)]
    (M : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} Y I))
    (a : InverseSequence.ProIso (koszulPowerDualSystem X g)
      (adicQuotientDerivedTower X (idealOfGlobalSections X g))) :
    letI := isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete_idealOfGlobalSections X g
    IsDerivedLimit
      (adicReductionTower X (idealOfGlobalSections X g)
        ((derivedPullback.{u} f.toRingedToposSiteHom).obj M.1))
      ((derivedCompletePullback f I (idealOfGlobalSections X g)).obj M).1
declarations.comment:
part (5), at the generality of part (4) — an arbitrary ringed site, `ℐ'`
  generated by finitely many global sections, and the tower of adic quotients formed on the
  source site, where the source's `n ↦ Lf^*(M ⊗^𝐋 Λ/Iⁿ)` becomes
  `n ↦ Lf^*M ⊗^𝐋_{𝒪'} 𝒪'/ℐ'ⁿ⁺¹`. ASSUMED: exactly what part (4) assumes — the pro-isomorphism
  `a` and the `HasCoproduct` instance — and nothing else

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletePushforward
declarations.doc:
**The first statement of [Stacks, Tag 099K], for a morphism of ringed sites.** `Rf_*` as a
functor `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ') ⥤ D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)`: the derived direct image of a derived-complete object is
derived complete, by [Stacks, Tag 099J]. The tag is registered for a morphism of ringed topoi, on
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.isDerivedComplete_derivedPushforward`.

This is also part (1) of [Stacks, Tag 099N], stated for an arbitrary ringed site rather than for
the constant Noetherian coefficients `(𝒞, Λ)` of that tag. The identification of `D(𝒞, Λ)` with
`D(𝒪)` for the constant sheaf of rings `Λ` is not formalized in this library, so what is proved
is the statement at a generality containing the source's, not a composite with that
identification.
declarations.comment:
part (1), for an arbitrary ringed site in place of the source's constant
  Noetherian coefficients `(𝒞, Λ)`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletePullback
declarations.doc:
**The left adjoint of [Stacks, Tag 099K], for a reflective `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ')`.** `Lf^*_comp`,
that is `Lf^*` followed by derived completion, as a functor `D_comp(𝒪, ℐ) ⥤ D_comp(𝒪', ℐ')`.

The source reaches the derived completion functor from "`ℐ'` of finite type" through
[Stacks, Tag 099F]. What this construction consumes is that conclusion alone — that the
inclusion of the derived-complete objects has a left adjoint — so that is what the statement
asks for; for an `ℐ'` of finite type the instance of [Stacks, Tag 099F],
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isRightAdjoint_ι_isDerivedComplete`, supplies it. This is also
part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 099N], at the generality of part (1).
declarations.comment:
part (2), the functor `Lf^*_comp`, for an arbitrary ringed site in place of the
  source's constant Noetherian coefficients, and for every `ℐ'` whose derived-complete objects
  are reflective in `D(𝒪')` — which [Stacks, Tag 099F] gives for an ideal sheaf of finite
  type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCompletePullbackPushforwardAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**The adjunction of [Stacks, Tag 099K], for a reflective `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ')`.** On the
derived-complete objects, `Lf^*` followed by derived completion is left adjoint to `Rf_*`. This
is the source's chain `Hom(K, Rf_*M) = Hom(Lf^*K, M) = Hom(Lf^*_comp K, M)`: the composite of
the adjunction `Lf^* ⊣ Rf_*` of [Stacks, Tag 07A6] with the reflector adjunction of
[Stacks, Tag 099F], restricted along the fully faithful inclusion of `D_comp(𝒪, ℐ)` into
`D(𝒪)`.

The `@[stacks 099K]` registration of this second statement is on the statement for a morphism
of ringed topoi, `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedToposHom.derivedCompletePullbackPushforwardAdjunction`
of `PushforwardCompletionTopos.lean`.

This is also part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 099N]. Parts (4) and (5) of that tag, the formulas
`Rf_*K = R lim Rf_*(K ⊗^L Λ/Iⁿ)` and `Lf^*_comp M = R lim Lf^*(M ⊗^L Λ/Iⁿ)`, are proved in
`PushforwardAdicLimit.lean` of this directory, as
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_derivedPushforward_adicReductionTower_of_proIso`
and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedLimit_adicReductionTower_derivedCompletePullback_of_proIso`;
each carries the single hypothesis of this library's form of [Stacks, Tag 099M], a
pro-isomorphism of the dual Koszul tower with the tower of adic quotients.
declarations.statement:
def derivedCompletePullbackPushforwardAdjunction :
    derivedCompletePullback f I I' ⊣ derivedCompletePushforward f I I' hI
declarations.comment:
part (2), the adjunction, at the generality named on `derivedCompletePullback`;
  parts (4) and (5) are in `PushforwardAdicLimit.lean`

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 0A0G] at a derived-complete object.** For `K` in `D_comp(𝒪', ℐ')` the
canonical map `(Rf_*K)^∧ ⟶ Rf_*(K^∧)` is invertible, so `Rf_*(K^∧) = Rf_*K = (Rf_*K)^∧`: the
unit `K ⟶ K^∧` is invertible on a derived-complete `K`.

The general case of Tag 0A0G is not proved; see
`isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isIso_map_unit` for the criterion that is, and
the module documentation for the state of the four inputs of the source's proof. Three of them
([Stacks, Tags 0A0F, 0A0E, 0A07]) are now available; what is missing is the base case
`K = 𝒪[n]` of the projection formula [Stacks, Tag 0944] on a ringed topos — the dévissage from
it to a strictly perfect complex is available, and takes that case as a hypothesis — together
with the identification of `Lf^*` of a Koszul complex with a Koszul complex. That is also why
part (3) of [Stacks, Tag 099N] is registered here only for a derived-complete object.

This statement also carries [Stacks, Tag 0A0I], Equation 52.7.0.1 `Rf_*(ℱ^∧) = (Rf_*ℱ)^∧`,
which the source justifies by citing Tag 0A0G: what is proved is that ringed-site statement, at
a derived-complete object. The display's own setting — a proper morphism of schemes and a
coherent module, Section 52.7 — is not formalized here. It also carries part (3) of
[Stacks, Tag 099N], with the restrictions named on `derivedCompletePushforward`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison_of_isDerivedComplete
    {K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
    (hK : IsDerivedComplete.{u, u, u, u} X I' K) :
    IsIso ((derivedCompletionPushforwardComparison f I I' hI).app K)
declarations.comment: part (3), for a derived-complete object and an arbitrary ringed site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isLimit_adicQuotientSystem_iff_of_slicedObjectsSituation
declarations.doc: Ordinary completeness is derived completeness plus separatedness.

theorem isLimit_adicQuotientSystem_iff_of_slicedObjectsSituation
    (X : RingedSite.{u, v, max u v})
    [HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    (hX : Stacks.WeaklyContractible.SlicedObjectsSituation.{w, v, u, max u v} X.C X.J)
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hI : ∀ U : X.C, hX.B U →
      (I.toSubmodule.obj (op U)).FG)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) :

        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj F) ∧
        (⨅ n : ℕ, idealPowerProduct X I F n) = ⊥

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_limit_adicQuotientTower
declarations.doc:
**The completion `limₙ 𝒪/ℐⁿ` of the structure sheaf is derived complete along `ℐ`.** Every
term of the tower of adic quotients is derived complete, and an inverse limit of derived-complete
sheaves of modules is derived complete.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_limit_adicQuotientTower
    (X : RingedSite.{u, u, u}) [Small.{u} X.C] [HasSheafify X.J (Type u)]
    (hX : X.J.HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects)
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete X I
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj
        (limit (adicQuotientTower X I)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isWeakSerreClass_isDerivedComplete_constant
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099Q] (1).** On a site with enough weakly contractible objects, the derived
complete sheaves of `Λ`-modules form a weak Serre subcategory of `Mod(𝒞, Λ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakSerreClass_isDerivedComplete_constant (hJ : J.HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects)
    (I : Ideal Λ) :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass
      (fun F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constant J Λ).O) =>
        IsDerivedComplete (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I)
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_limit_constant
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099Q] (4).** On a site with enough weakly contractible objects, the limit of an
inverse system `… → ℱ₃ → ℱ₂ → ℱ₁` of derived complete sheaves of `Λ`-modules is derived
complete.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_limit_constant (hJ : J.HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects)
    (I : Ideal Λ)
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constant J Λ).O))
    (hF : ∀ n : ℕ, IsDerivedComplete (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I)
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (F.obj (op n)))) :
    IsDerivedComplete (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I)
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (limit F))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_iff_homology_constant
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099Q] (5).** On a site with enough weakly contractible objects, an object `K`
of `D(𝒞, Λ)` is derived complete if and only if each cohomology sheaf `Hᵖ(K)` is derived
complete.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_iff_homology_constant (hJ : J.HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects)
    (I : Ideal Λ)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constant J Λ).O))) :
    IsDerivedComplete (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I) K ↔
      ∀ p : ℤ, IsDerivedComplete (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I)
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ p).obj K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isLimit_adicQuotientSystem_iff_constant
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099Q] (2).** On a site with enough weakly contractible objects, a sheaf `ℱ` of
`Λ`-modules satisfies `ℱ = lim ℱ/Iⁿℱ` — the maps `ℱ ⟶ ℱ/Iⁿℱ` form a limit cone — if and only if
`ℱ` is derived complete and `⋂ Iⁿℱ = 0`. Only the finite generation of `I` is used of the
Noetherian hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLimit_adicQuotientSystem_iff_constant (hJ : J.HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects)
    {I : Ideal Λ} (hI : I.FG)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constant J Λ).O)) :
    Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk F
      (adicQuotientSystem (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I) F).quotientMap)) ↔
      IsDerivedComplete (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I)
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F) ∧
        (⨅ n : ℕ, idealPowerProduct (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I) F n) = ⊥

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_constantCompletion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099Q] (3).** On a site with enough weakly contractible objects, the sheaf
`Λ̲^∧ = lim (Λ/Iⁿ)̲` is derived complete. Only the finite generation of `I` is used of the
Noetherian hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedComplete_constantCompletion (hJ : J.HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects)
    {I : Ideal Λ} (hI : I.FG) :
    IsDerivedComplete (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I)
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
        (limit (Stacks.ConstantSheaf.adicQuotientSystem I ⋙ constantModuleFunctor J Λ)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isBoundedAbove_iff_constant
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099Q] (6).** On a site with enough weakly contractible objects, a derived
complete object `K` of `D(𝒞, Λ)` is bounded above if and only if `K ⊗^𝐋_Λ (Λ/I)̲` is bounded
above.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBoundedAbove_iff_constant [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    (hJ : J.HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects) (I : Ideal Λ)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constant J Λ).O)))
    (hK : IsDerivedComplete (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I) K) :
    Stacks.DerivedCategory.IsBoundedAbove K ↔
      Stacks.DerivedCategory.IsBoundedAbove
        (((Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensorProductFunctor (constant J Λ)).obj K).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
            ((constantModuleFunctor J Λ).obj (ModuleCat.of Λ (Λ ⧸ I)))))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isBounded_of_hasFiniteTorDimension_constant
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 099Q] (7).** On a site with enough weakly contractible objects, a derived
complete object `K` of `D(𝒞, Λ)` is bounded if `K ⊗^𝐋_Λ Λ/I`, as an object of `D(𝒞, Λ/I)`, has
finite Tor dimension, for any derived tensor product `T₁` on `D(𝒞, Λ/I)` against which Tor
dimension is measured.
declarations.statement:
theorem isBounded_of_hasFiniteTorDimension_constant [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    (hJ : J.HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects) (I : Ideal Λ)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constant J Λ).O)))
    (hK : IsDerivedComplete (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I) K)
    (T₁ : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u, u, u, u + 1}
      (Stacks.Sites.adicQuotientRingedSite (constant J Λ) (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I) 1))
    (h : HasFiniteTorDimension.{u, u, u, u + 1} T₁
      ((Stacks.Cohomology.derivedCoefficientChange
        (Stacks.Sites.toAdicQuotient (constantIdealSheaf J Λ I) 1)).obj K)) :
    ∃ a b : ℤ, K.IsGE a ∧ K.IsLE b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isDerivedComplete_limit_of_slicedObjectsSituation
declarations.doc:
**The inverse limit of a countable system of derived-complete sheaves of modules is derived
complete**, on a ringed site equipped with a covering collection of objects which test
surjectivity of sheaves of sets valued in the module universe, on the site and on each of its
slices.

The weakly contractible objects enter only through that collection, so the statement reaches a
site whose objects outnumber its morphisms — the small pro-étale site of a scheme among them —
where weak contractibility cannot be tested at the morphism universe at all.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDerivedComplete_limit_of_slicedObjectsSituation
    (X : RingedSite.{u, v, max u v})
    [HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proetaleInverseImage_exists_map_eq_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 099S, the injectivity half.** Let `Y = lim Y_i` be the limit of an inverse system of
quasi-compact objects of `X_proétale` with affine transition morphisms, and let `ℱ` be a sheaf on
`X_étale`.  Two sections of `ε⁻¹ℱ` over a stage `Y_i` with the same restriction to `Y` already
have the same restriction to some later stage `Y_j`; equivalently, the canonical map
`colim ε⁻¹ℱ(Y_i) → ε⁻¹ℱ(Y)` is injective.

The sections are computed by the formula of Stacks 0GLZ through
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proetaleInverseImageIsoEtaleSectionsSheaf`, which turns this into
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleSectionsSheaf_exists_map_eq_of_isLimit`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Scheme.proetaleInverseImage_exists_map_eq_of_isLimit
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsCofiltered I] (X : Scheme.{u}) (Y : I ⥤ X.ProEt)
    (c : Cone Y) (hc : IsLimit ((Scheme.ProEt.forget X ⋙ Over.forget X).mapCone c))
    (haffine : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (Y.map f).left)
    (hqc : ∀ i : I, CompactSpace (Y.obj i).left)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (max (u + 1) v))) (i : I)
    (s t : ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback X.etaleToProetale
      (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology
      (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj F).obj.obj (op (Y.obj i)))
    (hst : ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback X.etaleToProetale
        (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology
        (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj F).obj.map (c.π.app i).op s =
      ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback X.etaleToProetale
        (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology
        (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj F).obj.map (c.π.app i).op t) :
    ∃ (j : I) (f : j ⟶ i),
      ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback X.etaleToProetale
          (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology
          (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj F).obj.map (Y.map f).op s =
        ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback X.etaleToProetale
          (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology
          (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj F).obj.map (Y.map f).op t
declarations.comment: the injectivity half of ε⁻¹ℱ(Y) = colim ε⁻¹ℱ(Y_i), proved: two sections over a stage that agree over the limit agree over a later stage. The surjectivity half, hence the formula itself, is not proved here. `Y = lim Y_i` is the scheme-theoretic limit, as in the source; the index category is small in the universe of the schemes

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.injective_desc_proetaleInverseImage_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 099S, the injectivity half, for the comparison map out of the colimit.** The
canonical map `colim ε⁻¹ℱ(Y_i) → ε⁻¹ℱ(Y)` induced by the limit cone is injective, for any cocone
exhibiting the colimit of the sections at the stages.

Elements of a filtered colimit come from a stage and the comparison map restricts on a stage to
restriction along the cone leg, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proetaleInverseImage_exists_map_eq_of_isLimit` at a stage below both.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Scheme.injective_desc_proetaleInverseImage_of_isLimit
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsCofiltered I] (X : Scheme.{u}) (Y : I ⥤ X.ProEt)
    (c : Cone Y) (hc : IsLimit ((Scheme.ProEt.forget X ⋙ Over.forget X).mapCone c))
    (haffine : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (Y.map f).left)
    (hqc : ∀ i : I, CompactSpace (Y.obj i).left)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (max (u + 1) v)))
    (E : Cocone (Y.op ⋙ ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback X.etaleToProetale
      (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj F).obj))
    (hE : IsColimit E) :
    Function.Injective (hE.desc (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback
      X.etaleToProetale (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology
      (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj F).obj.mapCocone c.op))
declarations.comment: proved: the comparison map colim ε⁻¹ℱ(Y_i) → ε⁻¹ℱ(Y) of the displayed formula is INJECTIVE, for every colimit cocone of the sections at the stages. Its surjectivity is not proved, so the formula itself is not

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.etaleSections_exists_map_eq_of_isLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 099S for étale stages, the injectivity half.** If the stages `Y_i` are objects of
`X_étale`, two sections of `ℱ` over a stage whose images in `ε⁻¹ℱ(Y)` under the unit
`ℱ ⟶ ε_*ε⁻¹ℱ` agree already agree over some later stage; equivalently, the canonical map
`colim ℱ(Y_i) → ε⁻¹ℱ(Y)` is injective.

The unit is an isomorphism by Stacks 099T, naturally in the étale object, which reduces this to
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proetaleInverseImage_exists_map_eq_of_isLimit`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Scheme.etaleSections_exists_map_eq_of_isLimit
    {I : Type u} [SmallCategory I] [IsCofiltered I] (X : Scheme.{u}) (Y : I ⥤ X.Etale)
    (c : Cone (Y ⋙ X.etaleToProetale))
    (hc : IsLimit ((Scheme.ProEt.forget X ⋙ Over.forget X).mapCone c))
    (haffine : ∀ {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (Y.map f).left)
    (hqc : ∀ i : I, CompactSpace (Y.obj i).left)
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (max (u + 1) v))) (i : I)
    (s t : F.obj.obj (op (Y.obj i)))
    (hst : ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback X.etaleToProetale
          (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology
          (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj F).obj.map (c.π.app i).op
        (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous X.etaleToProetale
          (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology
          (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).unit.app F).hom.app (op (Y.obj i)) s) =
      ((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback X.etaleToProetale
          (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology
          (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).obj F).obj.map (c.π.app i).op
        (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous X.etaleToProetale
          (Type (max (u + 1) v)) X.smallEtaleTopology
          (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).unit.app F).hom.app (op (Y.obj i)) t)) :
    ∃ (j : I) (f : j ⟶ i), F.obj.map (Y.map f).op s = F.obj.map (Y.map f).op t
declarations.comment: the final statement ε⁻¹ℱ(Y) = colim ℱ(Y_i) for étale stages, injectivity half proved: two sections of ℱ over a stage with the same image in ε⁻¹ℱ(Y) agree over a later stage. Surjectivity is not proved, so the formula itself is not
