declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_singleton_affine_weaklyContractible_hypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09A1 (2).** Every quasi-compact quasi-separated object `U` of a chosen
big pro-étale site admits a hypercovering each of whose terms is a one-element family on an
affine weakly contractible object of the site covering `U`.

The construction of Stacks 09A1 is run in the quasi-compact quasi-separated pro-étale site, where
the one-element coverings by affine weakly contractible objects of Stacks 0F4P are available, and
the hypercovering obtained there is transported to the big site by Stacks 0DAZ along the
inclusion, which is continuous and preserves fibre products.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_singleton_affine_weaklyContractible_hypercovering (U : B.Scheme)
    [CompactSpace U.obj] [QuasiSeparatedSpace U.obj] :
    ∃ K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{u + 1} (Over U)),
      IsHypercovering B.topology.toPretopology K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ i : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I,
          (∀ j : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I, j = i) ∧
            IsAffine ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left.obj ∧
            B.topology.IsWeaklyContractible ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left ∧
            Presieve.singleton ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).hom ∈
              B.topology.toPretopology U
declarations.comment: (2), at the library's big pro-etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_singleton_weaklyContractible_hypercovering_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09A1 (1).** Every object `U` of a chosen big pro-étale site admits a
hypercovering each of whose terms is a one-element family on a weakly contractible object of the
site covering `U`.

The one-element coverings by weakly contractible objects are those of Stacks 0F4P, supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_weaklyContractible_singleton_covering`. The two hypotheses on
disjoint unions are discharged here: that taking finite disjoint unions preserves coverings
because the summands of a finite disjoint union cover it, and that a finite disjoint union of
weakly contractible objects is weakly contractible.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_singleton_weaklyContractible_hypercovering_unconditional (U : B.Scheme) :
    ∃ K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{u + 1} (Over U)),
      IsHypercovering B.topology.toPretopology K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ i : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I,
          (∀ j : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I, j = i) ∧
            B.topology.IsWeaklyContractible ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left ∧
            Presieve.singleton ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).hom ∈
              B.topology.toPretopology U
declarations.comment: (1), at the library's big pro-etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_singleton_weaklyContractible_hypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09A1 (1).** Every object `U` of a chosen big pro-étale site admits a
hypercovering each of whose terms is a one-element family on a weakly contractible object of the
site covering `U`.

The one-element coverings by weakly contractible objects are those of Stacks 0F4P, supplied by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_weaklyContractible_singleton_covering`; the hypotheses on
disjoint unions are those of Stacks 0DB2, together with the weak contractibility of a finite
disjoint union of weakly contractible objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_singleton_weaklyContractible_hypercovering (U : B.Scheme)
    [HasFiniteCoproducts (Over U)]
    [ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderFiniteLimits
      (fun A : FormalCoproduct.{u + 1} (Over U) ↦ HasCoproduct A.obj)]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits (takeUnions.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (C := Over U))]
    (hunions : TakeUnionsFinPreservesCoverings.{u + 1} B.topology U)
    (sum_weaklyContractible :
      SumMemFin.{u + 1} {V : B.Scheme | B.topology.IsWeaklyContractible V} U) :
    ∃ K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{u + 1} (Over U)),
      IsHypercovering B.topology.toPretopology K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ i : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I,
          (∀ j : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I, j = i) ∧
            B.topology.IsWeaklyContractible ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left ∧
            Presieve.singleton ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).hom ∈
              B.topology.toPretopology U
declarations.comment: (1), at the library's big pro-etale site. The one-element weakly contractible covering is Tag 0F4P, discharged here; hunions and the two instance hypotheses are Tag 0DB2's own hypotheses, propagated

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.SmallProetale.exists_weaklyContractible_hypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09A1 (1).** Let `S` be a scheme in a chosen big pro-étale site. Every
object `U` of the small pro-étale site `S_proétale` admits a hypercovering `K` of `U` in
`S_proétale` such that each term `K_n` consists of a single weakly contractible object of
`S_proétale` covering `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_weaklyContractible_hypercovering (U : SmallProetale B S hS) :
    ∃ K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over U)),
      IsHypercovering (topology B S hS).toPretopology K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ i : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I,
          (∀ j : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I, j = i) ∧
            (topology B S hS).IsWeaklyContractible ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left ∧
            Presieve.singleton ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).hom ∈
              (topology B S hS).toPretopology U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.SmallProetale.exists_affine_weaklyContractible_hypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09A1 (2).** Let `S` be a scheme in a chosen big pro-étale site. Every
quasi-compact and quasi-separated object `U` of the small pro-étale site `S_proétale` admits a
hypercovering `K` of `U` in `S_proétale` such that each term `K_n` consists of a single affine
and weakly contractible object of `S_proétale` covering `U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_weaklyContractible_hypercovering (U : SmallProetale B S hS)
    [CompactSpace ((toScheme B S hS).obj U)] [QuasiSeparatedSpace ((toScheme B S hS).obj U)] :
    ∃ K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over U)),
      IsHypercovering (topology B S hS).toPretopology K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ i : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I,
          (∀ j : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I, j = i) ∧
            IsAffine ((toScheme B S hS).obj ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left) ∧
            (topology B S hS).IsWeaklyContractible ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left ∧
            Presieve.singleton ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).hom ∈
              (topology B S hS).toPretopology U

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_singleton_weaklyContractible_hypercovering_finiteDisjointUnions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09A1 (1).** On a site with fibre products in which every object has a
one-element covering by a weakly contractible object, every object `X` admits a hypercovering
each of whose terms is a single weakly contractible object covering `X`.

The disjoint unions taken degreewise are governed by the hypotheses of Tag 0DB2 and by the fact
that a finite disjoint union of weakly contractible objects is weakly contractible.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_singleton_weaklyContractible_hypercovering_finiteDisjointUnions
    (hunions : TakeUnionsFinPreservesCoverings.{w} T X)
    (sum_weaklyContractible : SumMemFin.{w} {V : C | T.IsWeaklyContractible V} X)
    (exists_singleton_cover : ∀ Y : C, ∃ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ Y),
      T.IsWeaklyContractible V ∧ Presieve.singleton f ∈ T.toPretopology Y) :
    ∃ K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)),
      IsHypercovering T.toPretopology K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ i : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I,
          (∀ j : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I, j = i) ∧
            T.IsWeaklyContractible ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left ∧
            Presieve.singleton ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).hom ∈ T.toPretopology X
declarations.comment: (1), for a general site: the one-element weakly contractible covering is the hypothesis exists_singleton_cover (Tag 0F4P), and hunions is the remaining hypothesis of the library's Tag 0DB2, propagated

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_singleton_weaklyContractible_hypercovering_of_prop_finiteDisjointUnions
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09A1 (2).** The same construction run with a further property `P` of
objects stable under the disjoint unions taken, such as affineness on the site of quasi-compact
and quasi-separated objects: every object `X` admits a hypercovering each of whose terms is a
single object satisfying `P`, weakly contractible, and covering `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_singleton_weaklyContractible_hypercovering_of_prop_finiteDisjointUnions (P : Set C)
    (hunions : TakeUnionsFinPreservesCoverings.{w} T X)
    (sum_mem : SumMemFin.{w} {V : C | V ∈ P ∧ T.IsWeaklyContractible V} X)
    (exists_singleton_cover : ∀ Y : C, ∃ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ Y),
      V ∈ P ∧ T.IsWeaklyContractible V ∧ Presieve.singleton f ∈ T.toPretopology Y) :
    ∃ K : SimplicialObject (FormalCoproduct.{w} (Over X)),
      IsHypercovering T.toPretopology K ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ i : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I,
          (∀ j : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I, j = i) ∧
            ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left ∈ P ∧
            T.IsWeaklyContractible ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left ∧
            Presieve.singleton ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).hom ∈ T.toPretopology X
declarations.comment: (2), with the object property P as a parameter: the source states it for affineness on the quasi-compact quasi-separated pro-etale site, which is constructed in StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/ProEtale/Site/Qcqs.lean, and (2) itself is proved at a chosen big pro-etale site as AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_singleton_affine_weaklyContractible_hypercovering. That instantiation runs exists_singleton_hypercovering_objects_in_finiteDisjointUnions rather than this lemma, because the weak contractibility carried here is that of the site being worked in, while the source's — and the library statement's — is that of the ambient pro-etale site. Instantiating this lemma at the big site with P := affine would be vacuous, since a non-quasi-compact object has no one-element affine cover. Same carried hypotheses as (1)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.derivedSectionsIsoHypercoverTotalComplex
declarations.doc:
A hypercovering by weakly contractible objects computes the derived
sections of any bounded-below complex of abelian sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def derivedSectionsIsoHypercoverTotalComplex
    [Small.{v} C]
    [HasSheafify J.toGrothendieck (Type v)]
    [HasSheafify J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}]
    [J.toGrothendieck.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}]
    [EnoughInjectives (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w})]
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K)
    (hweak : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ i : (K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).I,
      J.toGrothendieck.IsWeaklyContractible ((K.obj (op ⦋n⦌)).obj i).left)
    (E : CochainComplex.Plus (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w})) :
    DerivedCategory.Plus.ι.obj
      ((sheafSectionsFunctor J U).rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.Q.obj E)) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (hypercoverTotalComplex J U K E)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_derivedSectionsPlus
declarations.doc:
Derived sections over `U` commute with direct sums: every colimit cocone on a family of
objects of `D⁺(Sh(J, Ab))` is carried by `RΓ(U, -) : D⁺(Sh(J, Ab)) ⥤ D(Ab)` to a colimit cocone
in `D(Ab)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_derivedSectionsPlus
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K) (hcov : IsSingletonExactQuasiCompact J U K) (ι : Type u) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete ι)
      ((sheafSectionsFunctor J U).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.ι)
declarations.comment: direct sums, as preservation of colimit cocones indexed by a discrete category; same hypotheses as the cofan form below

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isColimit_mapCofan_derivedSectionsPlus
declarations.doc:
Let `U` be an object of a site admitting a hypercovering each of whose terms is a one-element
family on a quasi-compact object over which taking sections of abelian sheaves is exact. Then
`RΓ(U, -) : D⁺(Sh(J, Ab)) ⥤ D(Ab)` commutes with direct sums: if `S`, together with maps
`E i ⟶ S`, is the direct sum of a family `E` of bounded below objects, then `RΓ(U, S)` with the
images of those maps is the direct sum of the `RΓ(U, E i)` in `D(Ab)`.
declarations.comment: direct sums, at an object of a general site admitting a hypercovering by one-element families on quasi-compact objects with exact sections --- which is what Tag 09A1 provides for the pro-etale site of a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, modulo the hypotheses that Tag 09A1 itself carries in this library

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.isHomotopyColimit_derivedSectionsPlus
declarations.doc:
Derived sections over `U` carry a homotopy colimit of a system of bounded below complexes of
abelian sheaves to a homotopy colimit in `D(Ab)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isHomotopyColimit_derivedSectionsPlus
    (hK : IsHypercovering J K) (hcov : IsSingletonExactQuasiCompact J U K)
    (F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{u}))
    [HasCoproduct F.obj]
    {X : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{u})}
    [HasCoproduct (F ⋙ (sheafSectionsFunctor J U).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Plus.ι).obj]
    (h : Pretriangulated.IsHomotopyColimit F X) :
    Pretriangulated.IsHomotopyColimit
      (F ⋙ (sheafSectionsFunctor J U).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.ι)
      (((sheafSectionsFunctor J U).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.ι).obj X)
declarations.comment: homotopy colimits, under the same hypotheses on the hypercovering as the direct sums half

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.derivedGlobalSections_preservesCoproducts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09A3, direct sums.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Then

> `RΓ(X, -) : D⁺(X_pro-étale) ⥤ D(Ab)`

commutes with direct sums: every colimit cocone on a family of objects of `D⁺(X_pro-étale)`
indexed by a discrete category is carried to a colimit cocone in `D(Ab)`.

The statement quantifies over colimit cocones rather than preserving a coproduct functor: an
arbitrary direct sum of bounded below objects need not be bounded below, so `D⁺(X_pro-étale)`
has no coproducts, and the source itself conditions on `⊕ E i` being an object of `D⁺`.

The index type is arbitrary. The family is reduced to its nonzero members, which form a set
small in the universe at which the sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian, and there
`preservesColimit_derivedGlobalSections_of_isGE` applies, the common lower bound coming from
the direct sum itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedGlobalSections_preservesCoproducts (I : Type i₀) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)
      ((Sheaf.Γ (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
        AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.ι)
declarations.comment: direct sums, for the derived global sections of the small pro-etale site of a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, as preservation of colimit cocones indexed by a discrete category with an arbitrary index type

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.derivedGlobalSections_preservesHomotopyColimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09A3, homotopy colimits.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Then `RΓ(X, -) : D⁺(X_pro-étale) ⥤ D(Ab)` carries a homotopy colimit of a system of objects of
`D⁺(X_pro-étale)` to a homotopy colimit in `D(Ab)`.

This follows formally from the direct sums half: the functor is triangulated, and a homotopy
colimit is defined by a distinguished triangle whose first vertex is a direct sum.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedGlobalSections_preservesHomotopyColimits
    (F : ℕ ⥤ DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}))
    {K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})}
    [HasCoproduct F.obj]
    [HasCoproduct (F ⋙ (Sheaf.Γ (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
      DerivedCategory.Plus.ι).obj]
    (hK : Pretriangulated.IsHomotopyColimit F K) :
    Pretriangulated.IsHomotopyColimit
      (F ⋙ (Sheaf.Γ (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
        AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.ι)
      (((Sheaf.Γ (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
        AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.ι).obj K)
declarations.comment: homotopy colimits, for the derived global sections of the small pro-etale site of a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.proetaleDirectImageEtaleInverseImageIso
registrations.comment: part (1), naturally in the sheaf of sets

registrations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.proetaleDirectImageRightDerivedEpsilonInverseImageIso
registrations.comment: part (2), for complexes bounded below: `R f_{proétale,*} ∘ ε⁻¹ ≅ ε⁻¹ ∘ R f_{étale,*}` on `D⁺`, with `ε⁻¹` applied termwise

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exact_smallProetalePushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09A8.** For a finite morphism of schemes which is locally of finite presentation,
direct image of abelian sheaves along the induced morphism of small pro-étale sites is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_smallProetalePushforward
    [IsFinite (B.inclusion.map f)] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation (B.inclusion.map f)] :
    exactFunctor
      (Sheaf (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      (Sheaf (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      ((smallProetaleBaseChange B Z X f).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
        (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleMorphism_counit_isIso_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AA (3).** For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of objects of a chosen big pro-étale
site, the counit `i⁻¹ i_* ⟶ id` of the direct-image adjunction on small pro-étale sheaves of sets
is an isomorphism.

The assertion is Zariski local on `X` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleMorphism_counit_isIso_of_affineCounit`, which reduces it
to the affine objects of the small pro-étale site of `X`; over such an object the base change of
`i` is a closed immersion of affine objects, where the assertion is Stacks 09BL.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallProetaleMorphism_counit_isIso_of_isClosedImmersion
    [IsClosedImmersion (B.inclusion.map i)] :
    IsIso (smallProetaleMorphism B Z X i).adj.counit
declarations.comment: (3), the counit i^{-1} i_* -> id of the morphism of topoi of a closed immersion of objects of a chosen big pro-etale site is an isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleMorphism_pushforward_fullyFaithful_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AA (2).** For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of objects of a chosen big pro-étale
site, the direct image `i_*` on small pro-étale sheaves of sets is fully faithful.

This is assertion (3) together with the equivalence of Sites 04D6: the right adjoint of an
adjunction whose counit is invertible is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
def smallProetaleMorphism_pushforward_fullyFaithful_of_isClosedImmersion :
    (smallProetaleMorphism B Z X i).pushforward.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: (2), the direct image i_* of the morphism of topoi of a closed immersion of objects of a chosen big pro-etale site is fully faithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleMorphism_inverseImage_preservesLimits_of_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AA (1).** For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of objects of a chosen big pro-étale
site, the inverse image `i⁻¹` on small pro-étale sheaves of sets commutes with limits.

The base changes along `i` of the affine objects of the small pro-étale site of `X` cover the
final object of the small pro-étale site of `Z`, so the canonical comparison map from `i⁻¹` of a
limit to the limit of `i⁻¹` is invertible as soon as it is bijective on the sections over the
objects lying over one of them, and that is invertibility of its restriction to such a member.
Restriction commutes with limits, being a right adjoint, and exchanges with `i⁻¹` across the
base-change square by Beck–Chevalley, so the restricted comparison map is the comparison map for
the base-changed closed immersion of affine objects, whose inverse image commutes with limits by
Stacks 09BL (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem smallProetaleMorphism_inverseImage_preservesLimits_of_isClosedImmersion :
    PreservesLimits (smallProetaleMorphism B Z X i).inverseImage
declarations.comment: (1), the inverse image i^{-1} of the morphism of topoi of a closed immersion of objects of a chosen big pro-etale site commutes with limits

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleMorphismPushforwardFullyFaithfulOfAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AA (2) given the adjoint of Stacks 09BK.** If small pro-étale base change along
`f` admits a fully faithful left adjoint, the direct image `f_*` on small pro-étale sheaves of
sets is fully faithful.

The direct image is restriction along base change, which is fully faithful on presheaves because
restriction along the left adjoint is a left adjoint of it with invertible counit.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallProetaleMorphismPushforwardFullyFaithfulOfAdjoint
    [v.Full] [v.Faithful] :
    (smallProetaleMorphism B T S f).pushforward.FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: (2), the direct image is fully faithful, given that pro-etale base change admits a fully faithful left adjoint -- the adjoint that Tag 09BK supplies for a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleMorphism_isIso_counit_of_adjoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AA (3) given the adjoint of Stacks 09BK.** If small pro-étale base change along
`f` admits a fully faithful left adjoint, the counit `f⁻¹f_*F ⟶ F` of the morphism of topoi is an
isomorphism, so `f⁻¹f_*` is the identity on small pro-étale sheaves of sets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallProetaleMorphism_isIso_counit_of_adjoint [v.Full] [v.Faithful] :
    IsIso (smallProetaleMorphism B T S f).adj.counit
declarations.comment: (3), the counit of the morphism of topoi is an isomorphism, given that pro-etale base change admits a fully faithful left adjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleMorphism_inverseImage_preservesLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AA (1) given the left adjoint of Stacks 09BL (3).** If the inverse image `f⁻¹` on
small pro-étale sheaves of sets admits a left adjoint, it commutes with limits.
declarations.statement:
public theorem smallProetaleMorphism_inverseImage_preservesLimits
    [(smallProetaleMorphism B T S f).inverseImage.IsRightAdjoint] :
    PreservesLimits (smallProetaleMorphism B T S f).inverseImage
declarations.comment: (1), the inverse image commutes with limits, given that it admits a left adjoint -- which is clause (3) of Tag 09BL

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetalePushforward_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Topological invariance of the small pro-étale topos, direct image.** For an integral,
universally injective and surjective morphism `f : T ⟶ S` in a chosen big pro-étale site, the
direct image of the induced morphism of small pro-étale topoi is an equivalence.

This is the direct-image half of Stacks Project, Tag 09AB, with the two inputs that this library
does not have carried as explicit hypotheses: essential surjectivity of base change on small
étale sites, which is the remaining content of Stacks Project, Tag 04DZ, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.IntegralHasFinitePresentationLimit`, which is Stacks Project, Tag 09YZ over a
quasi-compact quasi-separated base and is what Stacks Project, Tag 05YU still needs.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallProetalePushforward_isEquivalence
    (hIntegral : IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map f))
    (hInjective : UniversallyInjective (B.inclusion.map f))
    (hSurjective : Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)) :
    (smallProetaleMorphism B T S f).pushforward.IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
direct image, assuming essential surjectivity of etale pullback (the content of
Stacks 04DZ) and Stacks 09YZ over a qcqs base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleInverseImage_isEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Topological invariance of the small pro-étale topos, inverse image.** For an integral,
universally injective and surjective morphism `f : T ⟶ S` in a chosen big pro-étale site, the
inverse image of the induced morphism of small pro-étale topoi is an equivalence.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetalePushforward_isEquivalence` and
`CategoryTheory.Adjunction.toEquivalence` of the adjunction `f⁻¹ ⊣ f_*`, this is Stacks Project,
Tag 09AB; its two hypotheses are those of the direct-image half.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallProetaleInverseImage_isEquivalence
    (hIntegral : IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map f))
    (hInjective : UniversallyInjective (B.inclusion.map f))
    (hSurjective : Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)) :
    (smallProetaleMorphism B T S f).inverseImage.IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
inverse image, assuming essential surjectivity of etale pullback (the content of
Stacks 04DZ) and Stacks 09YZ over a qcqs base

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleMorphism_isIso_unit_and_counit
declarations.doc:
**Topological invariance of the small pro-étale topos.** Let `f : T ⟶ S` be an integral,
universally injective and surjective morphism of schemes. Then the direct image `f_*` and the
inverse image `f⁻¹` of the induced morphism of small pro-étale topoi are quasi-inverse
equivalences: the unit and the counit of the adjunction `f⁻¹ ⊣ f_*` are isomorphisms.

The only hypotheses are `f` and the three conditions on it. The proof supplies Stacks 04DZ, by
`Stacks.Etale.etalePullback_isEquivalence`, and Stacks 09YZ, by
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag0817PartTwo.nonempty_integralLimitPresentation`, to the base's
conditional `AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetalePushforward_isEquivalence`, so it has no
further hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallProetaleMorphism_isIso_unit_and_counit
    (hIntegral : IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map f))
    (hInjective : UniversallyInjective (B.inclusion.map f))
    (hSurjective : Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)) :
    IsIso (smallProetaleMorphism B T S f).adj.unit ∧
      IsIso (smallProetaleMorphism B T S f).adj.counit
declarations.comment:
unit and counit of f^{-1} -| f_* are isomorphisms; unconditional: only f
integral, universally injective, surjective; 04DZ and 09YZ are proved and supplied, not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetalePushforward_isEquivalence_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Topological invariance of the small pro-étale topos, direct image, unconditionally.** Let
`f : T ⟶ S` be an integral, universally injective and surjective morphism of schemes. Then the
direct image `f_*` of the induced morphism of small pro-étale topoi is an equivalence.

The only hypotheses are `f` and the three conditions integral, universally injective and
surjective. The base's `AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetalePushforward_isEquivalence` is the
same statement taking in addition topological invariance of the étale site (Stacks 04DZ) and
integral morphisms as limits of finite ones (Stacks 09YZ) as section hypotheses; this theorem is
that one with both supplied, by `Stacks.Etale.etalePullback_isEquivalence` and
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag0817PartTwo.nonempty_integralLimitPresentation`, so it has no
further hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallProetalePushforward_isEquivalence_of_isIntegralHom
    [IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map f)] [UniversallyInjective (B.inclusion.map f)]
    [Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)] :
    (smallProetaleMorphism B T S f).pushforward.IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
direct image f_* is an equivalence; unconditional: only f integral, universally
injective, surjective; 04DZ and 09YZ are proved and supplied, not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleInverseImage_isEquivalence_of_isIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Topological invariance of the small pro-étale topos, inverse image, unconditionally.** Let
`f : T ⟶ S` be an integral, universally injective and surjective morphism of schemes. Then the
inverse image `f⁻¹` of the induced morphism of small pro-étale topoi is an equivalence.

The only hypotheses are `f` and the three conditions integral, universally injective and
surjective. The base's `AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleInverseImage_isEquivalence` is the
same statement taking in addition Stacks 04DZ and Stacks 09YZ as section hypotheses; this theorem
is that one with both supplied, by `Stacks.Etale.etalePullback_isEquivalence` and
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag0817PartTwo.nonempty_integralLimitPresentation`, so it has no
further hypotheses.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallProetaleInverseImage_isEquivalence_of_isIntegralHom
    [IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map f)] [UniversallyInjective (B.inclusion.map f)]
    [Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)] :
    (smallProetaleMorphism B T S f).inverseImage.IsEquivalence
declarations.comment:
inverse image f^{-1} is an equivalence; unconditional: only f integral,
universally injective, surjective; 04DZ and 09YZ are proved and supplied, not assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**The small pro-étale topoi along an integral universal homeomorphism are equivalent.** For
`f : T ⟶ S` integral, universally injective and surjective, the equivalence between the small
pro-étale topos of `S` and that of `T` whose functor is the inverse image `f⁻¹` and whose inverse
is the direct image `f_*`, with unit and counit those of the adjunction `f⁻¹ ⊣ f_*`: these two
functors are quasi-inverse equivalences.

The only hypotheses are `f` and the three conditions on it; Stacks 04DZ and Stacks 09YZ, which
the base's conditional statements take as section hypotheses, are supplied by
`Stacks.Etale.etalePullback_isEquivalence` and
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.Tag0817PartTwo.nonempty_integralLimitPresentation`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def smallProetaleEquivalence
    (hIntegral : IsIntegralHom (B.inclusion.map f))
    (hInjective : UniversallyInjective (B.inclusion.map f))
    (hSurjective : Surjective (B.inclusion.map f)) :
    Sheaf (SmallProetale.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1)) ≌
      Sheaf (SmallProetale.topology B T.obj T.property) (Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment:
f^{-1} and f_* as quasi-inverse equivalences of the small pro-etale topoi;
unconditional: only f integral, universally injective, surjective

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.abelianProetaleInverseImage_sections_iso_closedFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AC.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of objects of a chosen big pro-étale
site and let `U` be an object of the small pro-étale site of `X` such that

1. `U` is affine and weakly contractible, and
2. every point of `U` specializes to a point of `U ×_X Z`.

Then `i^{-1}F(U ×_X Z) = F(U)` for every abelian sheaf `F` on the small pro-étale site of `X`,
naturally in `F`.

Weak contractibility of `U` is taken in the chosen big pro-étale site; for an affine object it
is equivalent to w-contractibility of its ring of global sections by Stacks 098H, and it implies
weak contractibility of `U` as an object of the small pro-étale site of `X`.
declarations.statement:
def abelianProetaleInverseImage_sections_iso_closedFibre [IsAffine U.obj.left.obj]
    (hU : B.topology.IsWeaklyContractible U.obj.left)
    (hspec : ∀ x : U.obj.left.obj, ∃ w : (pullback U.obj.hom i).obj,
      x ⤳ (B.inclusion.map (pullback.fst U.obj.hom i)).base w) :
    Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback (smallProetaleBaseChange B Z X i)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) ⋙
      sheafToPresheaf (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
      (evaluation _ _).obj (op ((smallProetaleBaseChange B Z X i).obj U)) ≅
    sheafToPresheaf (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
      (evaluation _ _).obj (op U)
declarations.comment: i^{-1}F(U x_X Z) = F(U) for every abelian sheaf F on X_proetale, naturally in F, for an ARBITRARY closed immersion i : Z -> X and U affine and weakly contractible (in the chosen big pro-etale site, Tag 098H) all of whose points specialize into U x_X Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.existsUnique_algHom_comp_quotientMk_eq
declarations.doc:
**The ring-theoretic content of Stacks 09AC.** Let `A` be a w-contractible ring and `I ⊆ A`
an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of `A`. Every `A`-algebra map from an ind-étale
`A`-algebra `B` to `A ⧸ I` factors through the quotient map `A → A ⧸ I` by a unique `A`-algebra
map `B → A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_algHom_comp_quotientMk_eq (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (hA : ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{u, u} A) (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : I ≤ Ring.jacobson A) (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
    (hB : StacksDraft.IndEtale A B) (φ : B →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I) :
    ∃! σ : B →ₐ[A] A, (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A I).comp σ = φ
declarations.comment: the ring-theoretic statement the lemma reduces to: for A w-contractible and I in the Jacobson radical, a factorization A -> B -> A/I with A -> B ind-etale has a unique retraction B -> A compatible with the maps to A/I; the source's B/IB = A/I x R splitting is not used, see the module docstring

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleLiftBaseChangeObjIsoOfIsWContractible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AC.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of affine schemes and let `U` be an
object of `X_app` which is affine and weakly contractible and every point of which specializes
to a point of `U ×_X Z`. Then `U` is the lift of its closed fibre: `v(U ×_X Z) ≅ U`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def appProetaleLiftBaseChangeObjIsoOfIsWContractible (U : AppSmallProetale X)
    (hU : ProetaleWContractible.IsWContractible.{u, u} (appAlg U).obj.right)
    (hjac : (appTopKer i).map (appAlg U).obj.hom.hom ≤ Ring.jacobson (appAlg U).obj.right) :
    (appProetaleLift i).obj ((appProetaleBaseChange i).obj U) ≅ U
declarations.comment: the identification v(U x_X Z) = U, to which Stacks 09BL (1) reduces the lemma; hypothesis (1) is w-contractibility of Gamma(U, O_U) and hypothesis (2) is containment of the ideal of the closed fibre in its Jacobson radical

      Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v},
        F ⊣ proetaleRestriction j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.epsilonInverseImageExtensionByZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09AF.** For an étale morphism `j : U ⟶ X`, pulling back along the comparison
morphism `ε` of the small pro-étale and small étale sites commutes with extension by zero:
`ε^{-1} j_! ≅ j_! ε^{-1}` on abelian sheaves.  Both sides are left adjoint to
`ε_* j^{-1} = j^{-1} ε_*`.
declarations.comment: the natural isomorphism eps^{-1} j_! = j_! eps^{-1}

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.epsilonInverseImageExtensionByZeroObjIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09AF**, evaluated at an abelian sheaf `G` on `U_étale`:
`ε^{-1} j_! G = j_! ε^{-1} G` as abelian sheaves on `X_proétale`.  This is the form in which the
source states the lemma.
declarations.statement:
def epsilonInverseImageExtensionByZeroObjIso
    (G : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    (epsilonInverseImage.{u, v} X).obj
        ((Stacks.EtaleCohomology.extensionByZero.{u, v} j).obj G) ≅
      (Abelian.extensionByZero.{u, v} j).obj ((epsilonInverseImage.{u, v} U).obj G)
declarations.comment: at an abelian sheaf G on U_etale: eps^{-1} j_! G = j_! eps^{-1} G

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isZero_extensionByZero_sections_of_specializes_to_closed
declarations.doc:
Extension by zero vanishes on an affine pro-étale object whose points
specialize to a closed fibre disjoint from the weakly étale source.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_extensionByZero_sections_of_specializes_to_closed
    {U X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [WeaklyEtale j]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hdisjoint : IsEmpty (pullback j i : Scheme.{u}))
    (V : X.ProEt) [IsAffine V.left]
    (hV : ∀ x : V.left, ∃ z : (pullback V.hom i : Scheme.{u}),
      Specializes x ((pullback.fst V.hom i).base z))
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology U) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    IsZero (((Abelian.extensionByZero j).obj F).obj.obj (op V))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.hasEnoughObjects_openPart_or_closedFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AH, the geometric reduction.** For a closed immersion `i` and its complementary
quasi-compact open immersion `j`, every object of `X_proétale` is covered by objects which are
either pulled back from `U_proétale`, or affine, weakly contractible and with all their points
specializing into the closed fibre.

Quasi-compactness of `j` is what makes the closed fibre of an affine object cut out by finitely
many equations, and hence what produces the ind-Zariski localization of Stacks 096V along it.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasEnoughObjects_openPart_or_closedFibre {Z U X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (hij : Set.range j.base = (Set.range i.base)ᶜ) :
    (Scheme.ProEt.topology X).HasEnoughObjects (fun V : X.ProEt ↦
      (∃ W : U.ProEt, Nonempty (V ≅ (proetalePostcompose j).obj W)) ∨
      (IsAffine V.left ∧ (Scheme.ProEt.topology X).IsWeaklyContractible V ∧
        ∀ x : V.left, ∃ z : (pullback V.hom i : Scheme.{u}),
          Specializes x ((pullback.fst V.hom i).base z)))
declarations.comment: the geometric reduction of the source's proof: quasi-compactness of j splits every affine weakly contractible object of X_proetale into a part lying over U and the ind-Zariski localization along its closed fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.openClosedShortComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AH.** The canonical short complex `j_! j^{-1} F ⟶ F ⟶ i_* i^{-1} F` on the small
pro-étale site of `X`, for a closed subscheme `i : Z ⟶ X` and the inclusion `j : U ⟶ X` of its
complement. Its two maps are the counit of `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}` and the unit of `i^{-1} ⊣ i_*`.

The tag states in addition that this short complex is short exact when `j` is quasi-compact. That
is not proved here: `shortExact_openClosedShortComplex_of_isIso_unit_app` below reduces it to the
single input described in the header of this file.
declarations.statement:
def openClosedShortComplex
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    ShortComplex (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
declarations.comment: the two canonical maps j_! j^{-1} F -> F -> i_* i^{-1} F and the fact that they compose to zero, i.e. the short complex of the tag; its short exactness is NOT proved here, see shortExact_openClosedShortComplex_of_isIso_unit_app

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.shortExact_map_proetaleRestriction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AH, over the open part.** Restricted to `U`, the short complex of the tag is
short exact, and indeed split: its third term vanishes over `U` and its first map becomes
invertible there.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_map_proetaleRestriction [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    ((openClosedShortComplex.{u, v} i j hij F).map
      (Abelian.proetaleRestriction.{u, v} j)).ShortExact
declarations.comment: exactness over the open part only: the restriction to U of the canonical short complex is short exact, unconditionally. Short exactness of the sequence on X_proetale itself is NOT proved in this file: shortExact_openClosedShortComplex_of_isIso_unit_app proves it at the source's hypotheses but assumes Tag 09AC for the site of AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ProEt, namely that the unit F -> i_* i^{-1} F is invertible on sections over every affine weakly contractible object all of whose points specialize into its closed fibre

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.shortExact_openClosedShortComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AH.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion and let `j : U ⟶ X` be an open
immersion onto the complement of its image, and assume `j` quasi-compact. For every abelian sheaf
`F` on the small pro-étale site of `X` the canonical sequence
`0 → j_! j^{-1} F → F → i_* i^{-1} F → 0`,
whose maps are the counit of `j_! ⊣ j^{-1}` and the unit of `i^{-1} ⊣ i_*`, is short exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem shortExact_openClosedShortComplex {Z U X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j]
    (hij : Set.range j.base = (Set.range i.base)ᶜ)
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}) :
    (openClosedShortComplex.{u, v} i j hij F).ShortExact

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsConstructibleModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AJ.** A sheaf of `Λ`-modules on the small pro-étale site of `X`, with `Λ`
Noetherian, is *constructible* if every affine open of `X` has a finite partition into
constructible locally closed subschemes on each of which the inverse image of the sheaf is
locally constant of finite type.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsConstructibleModuleSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) (Λ : Type v) [CommRing Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u}, HasWeakSheafify (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)]
    [∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (V : Y.ProEt),
      HasWeakSheafify ((Scheme.ProEt.topology Y).over V) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)]
    [∀ {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ Y),
      ((Scheme.proetaleBaseChange f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        (ModuleCat.{w} Λ) (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
        (Scheme.ProEt.topology Z)).IsRightAdjoint]
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsConstructibleModuleSheaf'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AJ.** A sheaf of `Λ`-modules on the small pro-étale site of `X` is
*constructible* when every affine open `U` of `X` admits a finite decomposition into
constructible locally closed subschemes on each of which the inverse image of the sheaf is
locally constant of finite type.

This is reducible, so a client can use the witnesses of the stratification directly.

The primed name records the weaker hypotheses: pinning the sections universe to
`max (u + 1) v w` makes sheafification and the left Kan extensions exist unconditionally, so
this form needs none of the `HasWeakSheafify` and `IsRightAdjoint` assumptions that
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsConstructibleModuleSheaf` of
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.Constructible.Defs` carries, at the cost of leaving
that universe no longer free. The two are stated with different local-constancy predicates —
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf` here against
`Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant` there — and identifying them is not done.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsConstructibleModuleSheaf' (X : Scheme.{u}) (Λ : Type v) [CommRing Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) v w} Λ)) : Prop

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_identifiesLocalRings_not_indEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AP.** A ring map can identify local rings without being ind-étale or
ind-Zariski.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_identifiesLocalRings_not_indEtale :
    ∃ (A : Type u) (_ : CommRing A) (B : Type v) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B),
      Algebra.IdentifiesLocalRings A B ∧
        ¬ StacksDraft.IndEtale A B ∧
        ¬ AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsIndZariski.{u, v, w} A B

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.exists_boundedAbove_projective_lift_representing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AR.** Let `I` be a nilpotent ideal of a commutative ring `R` and let `K` be an
object of `D(R)`. A bounded above complex `E` of projective `R ⧸ I`-modules representing
`K ⊗ᴸ[R] R ⧸ I` lifts to a bounded above complex `P` of projective `R`-modules representing `K`,
with `P ⊗[R] R ⧸ I` isomorphic to `E`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_boundedAbove_projective_lift_representing
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} (R ⧸ I)) ℤ)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max v u} R))
    (hEbdd : ∃ b : ℤ, E.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (hEprojective : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) (E.X i))
    (hErep : Nonempty
      ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj E ≅
        (totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).functor.obj K))
    (hI : IsNilpotent I) :
    ∃ P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v u} R) ℤ,
      (∃ b : ℤ, P.IsStrictlyLE b) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective R (P.X i)) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.Q).obj P ≅ K) ∧
      Nonempty
        (((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u, u, max v u} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P ≅ E)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_derivedReduction_mul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AS.** Let `I` and `J` be ideals of a commutative ring `R` and let `K` be an object
of the derived category of `R`-modules. If the derived reductions of `K` modulo `I` and modulo `J`
are both perfect, then so is the derived reduction of `K` modulo `I * J`.

Perfectness modulo `I ∩ J` follows from `isPerfect_of_isPerfect_reductions`, applied over the ring
`R/(I ∩ J)` where the images of `I` and of `J` meet in zero; and `R/(I * J) → R/(I ∩ J)` is
surjective with nilpotent kernel, so perfectness descends along it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedReduction_mul (I J : Ideal R)
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} R))
    (hI : IsPerfect
      ((totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v} (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).functor.obj K))
    (hJ : IsPerfect
      ((totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v} (Ideal.Quotient.mk J)).functor.obj K)) :
    IsPerfect
      ((totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v} (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I * J))).functor.obj K)

declarations.name: PrincipalAdicPresentation.isDerivedCompleteModule_iff_exists_shortExact_isAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AT.** Let `f` be a nonzerodivisor in a commutative ring `A`. An `A`-module `M` is
derived complete with respect to `(f)` if and only if it occurs as the cokernel in a short exact
sequence `0 ⟶ K ⟶ L ⟶ M ⟶ 0`, where `K` and `L` are `f`-adically complete and multiplication by
`f` is injective on both.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDerivedCompleteModule_iff_exists_shortExact_isAdicComplete
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (f : A)
    (hf : Function.Injective (LinearMap.lsmul A A f)) (M : ModuleCat.{u} A) :
    letI : HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (ModuleCat.{u} A) :=
      moduleCat_hasExactLimitsOfShape_discrete.{u} A ℕ
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    IsDerivedCompleteModule (Ideal.span {f}) M ↔
      ∃ (K L : ModuleCat.{u} A) (i : K ⟶ L) (p : L ⟶ M) (w : i ≫ p = 0),
        (ShortComplex.mk i p w).ShortExact ∧
          IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) K ∧
          IsAdicComplete (Ideal.span {f}) L ∧
          Function.Injective (LinearMap.lsmul A K f) ∧
          Function.Injective (LinearMap.lsmul A L f)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedLimit.AdicSystem.isDerivedComplete_and_reduction_isIso_of_isDerivedLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AU.** Let `A` be Noetherian and `I` an ideal. Suppose that `F` is an inverse
system in `D(A)` whose `n`-th member is the restriction of an object `Kq n` of
`D(A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1))`. If `Kq 0` is bounded above and every transition induces an isomorphism
after derived reduction to the preceding quotient, then a derived limit `K` is bounded above
and derived `I`-complete. Moreover, the canonical map from the derived reduction of `K` to
`Kq n` is an isomorphism for every `n`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isDerivedComplete_and_reduction_isIso_of_isDerivedLimit
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (F : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
    (Kq : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1))))
    (e : ∀ n : ℕ, F.obj (.op n) ≅
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v} (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)))).mapDerivedCategory.obj
        (Kq n))
    (adj : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (CochainComplex.DerivedExtensionScalars.totalDerivedExtensionScalars.{u, u, v}
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)))).functor ⊣
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v}
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)))).mapDerivedCategory)
    (hbounded : DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.minus (Kq 0))
    (t : ∀ n : ℕ, Kq (n + 1) ⟶
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v} (quotientTransition I n)).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Kq n))
    (htransition : ∀ n : ℕ,
      F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op ≫ (e n).hom =
        (e (n + 1)).hom ≫
          (ModuleCat.restrictScalars.{max u v}
            (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 2)))).mapDerivedCategory.map
            (t n) ≫ (restrictScalarsTransitionIso I n).hom.app (Kq n))
    (hcompat : ∀ n : ℕ,
      IsIso (StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedBaseChangeComparison.{u, v, u}
        (quotientTransition I n) (t n))) :
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
      (p : K ⟶ ∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => F.obj (.op n))
      (δ : (∏ᶜ fun n : ℕ => F.obj (.op n)) ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk p
          (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ => Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => F.obj (.op n)) n -
            Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => F.obj (.op n)) (n + 1) ≫
              F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) δ ∈
            distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) →
        DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.minus K ∧
          _root_.IsDerivedComplete I K ∧
          ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (((adj n).homEquiv _ _).symm
            (p ≫ Pi.π (fun n : ℕ => F.obj (.op n)) n ≫ (e n).hom))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedLimit_isPseudoCoherent_isDerivedComplete_and_baseChange_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09AV.** Let `A` be `I`-adically complete and let `Kₙ n` be a derived object over
`A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)`. Suppose `Kₙ 0` is pseudo-coherent and every transition map becomes an
isomorphism after derived base change. Then a derived inverse limit `K` over `A` is
pseudo-coherent and derived complete, and its canonical derived base-change map to every
`Kₙ n` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedLimit_isPseudoCoherent_isDerivedComplete_and_baseChange_iso
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (Kₙ : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1))))
    (φ : ∀ n : ℕ, Kₙ (n + 1) ⟶
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars
        (Ideal.Quotient.factorPow I (Nat.le_succ (n + 1)))).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Kₙ n))
    (hPseudoCoherent : PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent (Kₙ 0))
    (hBaseChange : ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (derivedBaseChangeComparison
      (Ideal.Quotient.factorPow I (Nat.le_succ (n + 1))) (φ n))) :
    letI : HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) :=
      moduleCat_hasExactLimitsOfShape_discrete A ℕ
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    let q : ∀ n : ℕ, A ⧸ I ^ (n + 2) →+* A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1) := fun n ↦
      Ideal.Quotient.factorPow I (Nat.le_succ (n + 1))
    let a : ∀ n : ℕ, A →+* A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1) := fun n ↦
      Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1))
    let X : ℕ → DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) := fun n ↦
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (a n)).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Kₙ n)
    let t : ∀ n : ℕ, X (n + 1) ⟶ X n := fun n ↦
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (a (n + 1))).mapDerivedCategory.map (φ n) ≫
        (derivedRestrictScalarsComp (a (n + 1)) (q n) (a n)
          (by ext x; rfl)).hom.app (Kₙ n)
    ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
      (p : K ⟶ ∏ᶜ X) (δ : ∏ᶜ X ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦ Pi.π X n - Pi.π X (n + 1) ≫ t n) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) →
        PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K ∧ _root_.IsDerivedComplete I K ∧
          ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (derivedBaseChangeComparison
            (a n) (p ≫ Pi.π X n))

declarations.name: StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedLimit_isPerfect_isDerivedComplete_and_baseChange_iso
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be `I`-adically complete and let `Kₙ n` be a derived object over
`A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1)`. Suppose `Kₙ 0` is perfect and every transition map becomes an isomorphism
after derived base change. Then a derived inverse limit `K` over `A` is perfect and derived
complete, and its canonical derived base-change map to every `Kₙ n` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedLimit_isPerfect_isDerivedComplete_and_baseChange_iso
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A]
    (Kₙ : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1))))
    (φ : ∀ n : ℕ, Kₙ (n + 1) ⟶
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars
        (Ideal.Quotient.factorPow I (Nat.le_succ (n + 1)))).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Kₙ n))
    (hPerfect : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect (Kₙ 0))
    (hBaseChange : ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedBaseChangeComparison
      (Ideal.Quotient.factorPow I (Nat.le_succ (n + 1))) (φ n))) :
    letI : HasExactLimitsOfShape (Discrete ℕ) (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) :=
      moduleCat_hasExactLimitsOfShape_discrete.{max u v} A ℕ
    letI : HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) :=
      Stacks.DerivedProducts.hasProductsOfShape_derivedCategory
    let q : ∀ n : ℕ, A ⧸ I ^ (n + 2) →+* A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1) := fun n ↦
      Ideal.Quotient.factorPow I (Nat.le_succ (n + 1))
    let a : ∀ n : ℕ, A →+* A ⧸ I ^ (n + 1) := fun n ↦
      Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1))
    let X : ℕ → DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A) := fun n ↦
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (a n)).mapDerivedCategory.obj (Kₙ n)
    let t : ∀ n : ℕ, X (n + 1) ⟶ X n := fun n ↦
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (a (n + 1))).mapDerivedCategory.map (φ n) ≫
        (StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedRestrictScalarsComp (a (n + 1)) (q n) (a n)
          (by ext x; rfl)).hom.app (Kₙ n)
    ∀ (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A))
      (p : K ⟶ ∏ᶜ X) (δ : ∏ᶜ X ⟶ K⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk p (Pi.lift fun n : ℕ ↦ Pi.π X n - Pi.π X (n + 1) ≫ t n) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} A)) →
        StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K ∧ _root_.IsDerivedComplete I K ∧
          ∀ n : ℕ, IsIso (StacksDraft.DerivedInverseLimit.derivedBaseChangeComparison
            (a n) (p ≫ Pi.π X n))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleZariskiSheafHAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
Let `S` be a scheme all of whose local rings are strictly henselian. Then
for every abelian sheaf `F` on the small étale site of `S` and every degree `p`, étale cohomology
`H^p(S_étale, F)` agrees with Zariski cohomology `H^p(S_Zariski, ε_* F)` of its restriction to
the open subschemes of `S`.
declarations.statement:
public def etaleZariskiSheafHAddEquiv
    (hlocal : ∀ x : S, StrictlyHenselianLocalRing ↥(S.presheaf.stalk x))
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.smallEtaleTopology S) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (p : ℕ) :
    Sheaf.H.{w, u + 1} F p ≃+ Sheaf.H.{w, u + 1} ((zariskiPushforward S).obj F) p

    [(Scheme.smallEtaleTopology S).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.wLocal_extremallyDisconnected_tfae
declarations.doc:
For a commutative ring `A` the following are equivalent: every faithfully
flat `A`-algebra identifying local rings admits a retraction; every faithfully flat ind-Zariski
`A`-algebra admits a retraction; `Spec A` is w-local and `π₀(Spec A)` is extremally
disconnected.
declarations.statement:
theorem wLocal_extremallyDisconnected_tfae (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    List.TFAE
      [∀ (B : Type (max u v)) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B],
          Module.FaithfullyFlat A B → Algebra.IdentifiesLocalRings A B → Nonempty (B →ₐ[A] A),
        ∀ (B : Type (max u v)) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B],
          Module.FaithfullyFlat A B →
            IsIndZariski.{u, max u v, max u v} A B → Nonempty (B →ₐ[A] A),
        WLocalSpace (PrimeSpectrum A) ∧
          ExtremallyDisconnected (ConnectedComponents (PrimeSpectrum A))]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_faithfullyFlat_indZariski_wLocal_extremallyDisconnected
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09B0.** Every ring has a faithfully flat ind-Zariski extension whose spectrum is
w-local and whose space of connected components is extremally disconnected.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_faithfullyFlat_indZariski_wLocal_extremallyDisconnected (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra A B),
      (algebraMap A B).FaithfullyFlat ∧
        IsIndZariski.{u, u, u} A B ∧
          WLocalSpace (PrimeSpectrum B) ∧
            ExtremallyDisconnected (ConnectedComponents (PrimeSpectrum B))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.essImage_mapDerivedCategory_and_hasTorAmplitude_derivedExtendScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09B2.** Let `X` be a scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal and `K` an
object of `D(X_proétale, Λ)`. Set `Kₙ = K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ`, the derived extension of scalars of `K`
along `Λ → Λ/Iⁿ`. If `K₁` is in the essential image of `ε⁻¹ : D(X_étale, Λ/I) ⥤
D(X_proétale, Λ/I)` and has Tor amplitude in `[a, ∞)`, then, for every `n`, `Kₙ` is in the
essential image of `ε⁻¹ : D(X_étale, Λ/Iⁿ) ⥤ D(X_proétale, Λ/Iⁿ)` and has Tor amplitude in
`[a, ∞)`.

Here `ε⁻¹` on derived categories is `ε⁻¹` applied termwise, and Tor amplitude in `[a, ∞)` is
`Stacks.ModuleSheaf.HasTorAmplitude` for `Set.Ici a`: `Hⁱ(L ⊗^L F) = 0` for `i < a` and every
sheaf of modules `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem essImage_mapDerivedCategory_and_hasTorAmplitude_derivedExtendScalars
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ)))
    (a : ℤ)
    (h₁ : (Scheme.etaleInverseImage.{u, w} X (Λ ⧸ I)).mapDerivedCategory.essImage
      ((derivedExtendScalars _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj K))
    (h₂ : HasTorAmplitude (J := Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      ((derivedExtendScalars _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj K) (Set.Ici a))
    (n : ℕ) :
    (Scheme.etaleInverseImage.{u, w} X (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)).mapDerivedCategory.essImage
        ((derivedExtendScalars _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n))).obj K) ∧
      HasTorAmplitude (J := Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
        ((derivedExtendScalars _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n))).obj K)
        (Set.Ici a)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GaloisSheaf.profiniteSheaf
declarations.doc:
The canonical pro-étale sheaf `M^∧` attached to a profinite abelian group `M` with continuous
action of the absolute Galois group of a field: the inverse limit of the pro-étale pullbacks of the
locally constant étale sheaves of the discrete quotients `M/N` by the open Galois-stable subgroups
`N`.
declarations.statement:
def profiniteSheaf (K : Type u) [Field K] (M : Type w) [AddCommGroup M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    [IsTopologicalAddGroup M] [CompactSpace M] [T2Space M] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace M]
    (ρ : Representation ℤ (galoisGroup K) M)
    (_hρ : Continuous fun p : galoisGroup K × M ↦ ρ p.1 p.2) :
    Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology (base K)) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} ℤ)
declarations.comment: case (1): the canonical sheaf of a profinite abelian group

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GaloisSheaf.adicSheaf
declarations.doc:
The canonical pro-étale sheaf `M^∧` attached to an `I`-adically complete module `M` over a
Noetherian ring, with continuous action of the absolute Galois group of a field for the `I`-adic
topology: the inverse limit of the pro-étale pullbacks of the locally constant étale sheaves of
the discrete quotients `M/IⁿM`.
declarations.statement:
def adicSheaf (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (I : Ideal Λ) (M : Type w)
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module Λ M] [IsAdicComplete I M]
    (ρ : Representation Λ (galoisGroup K) M)
    (_hρ : letI : TopologicalSpace M := I.adicModuleTopology M
      Continuous fun p : galoisGroup K × M ↦ ρ p.1 p.2) :
    Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology (base K)) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r w} Λ)
declarations.comment: case (2): the canonical sheaf of an adically complete module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GaloisSheaf.rightDerivedAdicSheafIso
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a field with absolute Galois group `G`, let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring with an ideal
`I`, and let `M` be an `I`-adically complete `Λ`-module with a continuous action of `G` for the
`I`-adic topology. Then the pro-étale cohomology of `Spec K` with coefficients in the completed
sheaf `M^∧ = limₙ ε⁻¹(M/IⁿM)` is the continuous cohomology of `G` with coefficients in `M`:

  `Hⁱ(Spec(K)_proét, M^∧) ≅ Hⁱ_cont(G, M)`.

Here `Λ` and `M` carry their `I`-adic topologies, pro-étale cohomology is the `i`-th right
derived functor of global sections of the underlying abelian sheaf, and the identification is of
abelian groups, the right hand side being lifted to the coefficient universe of the site.
declarations.statement:
def rightDerivedAdicSheafIso
    (ρ : Representation Λ (galoisGroup K) M)
    (hρ : letI := I.adicModuleTopology M
      Continuous fun p : galoisGroup K × M ↦ ρ p.1 p.2) (i : ℕ) :
    letI : TopologicalSpace Λ := I.adicTopology
    letI := I.adicModuleTopology M
    letI := hasSheafify_galois.{u, r, w} K
    letI := enoughInjectives_galois.{u, r, w} K
    letI := Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalSections.additive_Γ.{max r w, u, u + 1}
      (Scheme.ProEt.topology (base K))
    ((Sheaf.Γ (Scheme.ProEt.topology (base K)) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) r w}).rightDerived i).obj
      ((sheafCompose _ (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r w} Λ) AddCommGrpCat)).obj
        (adicSheaf Λ K I M ρ hρ)) ≅
      (underlyingAb.{u, r, w} Λ).obj (continuousCohomology i (uliftRep.{u} ρ hρ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GaloisSheaf.rightDerivedProfiniteSheafIso
declarations.doc:
Let `K` be a field with absolute Galois group `G` and let `M` be a profinite abelian group
with a continuous action of `G`. Then the pro-étale cohomology of `Spec K` with coefficients in
the completed sheaf `M^∧ = lim_N ε⁻¹(M/N)`, the limit over the open `G`-stable subgroups `N`, is
the continuous cohomology of `G` with coefficients in `M`:

  `Hⁱ(Spec(K)_proét, M^∧) ≅ Hⁱ_cont(G, M)`.

Pro-étale cohomology is the `i`-th right derived functor of global sections of the underlying
abelian sheaf, and the identification is of abelian groups, the right hand side being lifted to
the coefficient universe of the site.
declarations.statement:
def rightDerivedProfiniteSheafIso (i : ℕ) :
    letI := hasSheafify_galois.{u, 0, w} K
    letI := enoughInjectives_galois.{u, 0, w} K
    letI := Stacks.Cohomology.GlobalSections.additive_Γ.{max 0 w, u, u + 1}
      (Scheme.ProEt.topology (base K))
    ((Sheaf.Γ (Scheme.ProEt.topology (base K)) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) w}).rightDerived i).obj
      ((sheafCompose _ (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} ℤ) AddCommGrpCat)).obj
        (profiniteSheaf K M ρ hρ)) ≅
      (underlyingAb.{u, 0, w} ℤ).obj (continuousCohomology i (uliftRep.{u} ρ hρ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.GaloisSheaf.rightDerivedAdicSheafLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09B4, case (2), as `Λ`-modules.** In the situation of
`rightDerivedAdicSheafIso`, the pro-étale cohomology `Hⁱ(Spec(K)_proét, M^∧)`, a `Λ`-module
through the action of `Λ` on `M^∧`, is isomorphic as a `Λ`-module to the continuous cohomology
`Hⁱ_cont(G, M)`, by the identification `rightDerivedAdicSheafIso`.
declarations.statement:
def rightDerivedAdicSheafLinearEquiv
    (ρ : Representation Λ (galoisGroup K) M)
    (hρ : letI := I.adicModuleTopology M
      Continuous fun p : galoisGroup K × M ↦ ρ p.1 p.2) (i : ℕ) :
    letI : TopologicalSpace Λ := I.adicTopology
    letI := I.adicModuleTopology M
    rightDerivedAdicSheafModule K Λ I M ρ hρ i ≃ₗ[Λ]
      ULift.{max (u + 1) r} (continuousCohomology i (uliftRep.{u} ρ hρ))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isWeakSerreClass_isConstructibleModuleSheaf'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09B5.** For `Λ` a Noetherian ring, the constructible sheaves of `Λ`-modules on the
small pro-étale site of a scheme `X` form a weak Serre subcategory of all sheaves of
`Λ`-modules on that site. There is no hypothesis on `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isWeakSerreClass_isConstructibleModuleSheaf' :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass
      (fun F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) v w} Λ) =>
        IsConstructibleModuleSheaf'.{u, v, w} X Λ F)

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicCompletion.InverseLimit.InverseSystem.quotientEquiv
declarations.doc:
Identification of the quotients: the map `M / Iⁿ M → M n` induced by the limit projection
`p n` is an isomorphism of `A`-modules.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicCompletion.InverseLimit.InverseSystem.isAdicComplete
declarations.doc:
The limit `M = lim_n M n` is `I`-adically complete: the canonical map `M → lim_k M / Iᵏ M`
is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement: theorem isAdicComplete (hI : I.FG) : IsAdicComplete I S.limit

declarations.name: subsingleton_of_isDerivedCompleteModule_of_quotient_smul
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09B9.** A derived complete module with zero reduction modulo a finitely generated
ideal is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem subsingleton_of_isDerivedCompleteModule_of_quotient_smul
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [HasProductsOfShape ℕ (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} A))]
    (I : Ideal A) (M : ModuleCat.{v} A) (hI : I.FG)
    (hM : IsDerivedCompleteModule I M)
    (hMI : Subsingleton (M ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule A M))) : Subsingleton M

declarations.name: FiniteDerivedComplete.exists_finite_adicCompletionModule_of_isDerivedCompleteModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BA.** A derived-complete module over a Noetherian ring whose reduction modulo
`I` is finite is canonically its `I`-adic completion and is finite over the completed ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_adicCompletionModule_of_isDerivedCompleteModule
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (M : ModuleCat.{v} A)
    (hM : IsDerivedCompleteModule I M)
    (hfin : Module.Finite (A ⧸ I) (M ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule A M))) :
    ∃ moduleM : Module (AdicCompletion I A) M,
      letI := moduleM
      IsScalarTower A (AdicCompletion I A) M ∧
        Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I A) M ∧
        ∃ e : M ≃ₗ[AdicCompletion I A] AdicCompletion I M,
          ∀ m, e m = AdicCompletion.of I M m

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.HomComparison.hom_isom_quotient_systems_mittagLeffler_and_completion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BB.** Homomorphisms and isomorphisms between the adic quotients of two
finite modules form Mittag--Leffler systems.  The canonical comparison from the adic
quotients of `Hom` has uniformly bounded kernel and cokernel, and passage to the inverse
limit identifies both homomorphisms and isomorphisms with those between the completed
modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hom_isom_quotient_systems_mittagLeffler_and_completion
    {A : Type u} {M : Type v} {N : Type w} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module.Finite A N]
    (I : Ideal A) :
    let Mq : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => M ⧸ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M)
    let Nq : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => N ⧸ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A N)
    let H : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => Mq n →ₗ[A] Nq n
    let E : ℕ → Type _ := fun n => Mq n ≃ₗ[A] Nq n
    ∃ (homTransition : ∀ n, H (n + 1) →ₗ[A] H n)
      (isoTransition : ∀ n, E (n + 1) → E n)
      (comparison : ∀ n,
        ((M →ₗ[A] N) ⧸ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A (M →ₗ[A] N))) →ₗ[A] H n),
      (∀ n (f : H (n + 1)) (m : M),
        homTransition n f (Submodule.Quotient.mk m) =
          AdicCompletion.transitionMap I N (Nat.le_succ n)
            (f (Submodule.Quotient.mk m))) ∧
      (∀ n (e : E (n + 1)) (m : M),
        isoTransition n e (Submodule.Quotient.mk m) =
          AdicCompletion.transitionMap I N (Nat.le_succ n)
            (e (Submodule.Quotient.mk m))) ∧
      (∀ n (f : M →ₗ[A] N) (m : M),
        comparison n (Submodule.Quotient.mk f) (Submodule.Quotient.mk m) =
          Submodule.Quotient.mk (f m)) ∧
      let HomSys : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat A :=
        Functor.ofOpSequence (X := fun n => ModuleCat.of A (H n))
          (fun n => ModuleCat.ofHom (homTransition n))
      let IsoSys : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max v w) :=
        Functor.ofOpSequence (X := E) (fun n => TypeCat.ofHom (isoTransition n))
      (HomSys ⋙ forget (ModuleCat A)).IsMittagLeffler ∧
      IsoSys.IsMittagLeffler ∧
      (∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n,
        I ^ c ≤ Module.annihilator A (LinearMap.ker (comparison n)) ∧
        I ^ c ≤ Module.annihilator A
          (H n ⧸ LinearMap.range (comparison n))) ∧
      (∃ homLimitIso :
          limit HomSys ≅ ModuleCat.of A (AdicCompletion I (M →ₗ[A] N)),
        ∀ (f : ↥(limit HomSys)) n,
          comparison n
              (AdicCompletion.eval I (M →ₗ[A] N) n (homLimitIso.hom.hom f)) =
            (limit.π HomSys (op n)).hom f) ∧
      (∃ completedHomEquiv :
          AdicCompletion I (M →ₗ[A] N) ≃ₗ[AdicCompletion I A]
            (AdicCompletion I M →ₗ[AdicCompletion I A] AdicCompletion I N),
        ∀ (f : M →ₗ[A] N) (m : M),
          completedHomEquiv (AdicCompletion.of I (M →ₗ[A] N) f)
              (AdicCompletion.of I M m) =
            AdicCompletion.of I N (f m)) ∧
      ∃ isoLimitEquiv :
          { e : ∀ n, E n // ∀ n, isoTransition n (e (n + 1)) = e n } ≃
            (AdicCompletion I M ≃ₗ[AdicCompletion I A] AdicCompletion I N),
        ∀ (e : { e : ∀ n, E n // ∀ n, isoTransition n (e (n + 1)) = e n })
          (n : ℕ) (m : M),
          e.1 n (Submodule.Quotient.mk m) =
            AdicCompletion.eval I N n
              (isoLimitEquiv e (AdicCompletion.of I M m))

declarations.name: Stacks.AdicSystem.CompletionIsomorphism.adicCompletion_linearEquiv_of_quotient_linearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BC.** If all quotients of two finite modules by powers of an ideal
are linearly equivalent, then their adic completions are linearly equivalent over
the completed ring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem adicCompletion_linearEquiv_of_quotient_linearEquiv
    {A : Type u} {M : Type v} {N : Type w} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module.Finite A N]
    (I : Ideal A)
    (h : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Nonempty ((M ⧸ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A M)) ≃ₗ[A]
        (N ⧸ I ^ n • (⊤ : Submodule A N)))) :
    Nonempty (AdicCompletion I M ≃ₗ[AdicCompletion I A] AdicCompletion I N)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coveringSieve_complexMap_constant
declarations.doc:
**Maps out of the complex of constant sheaves of modules.** Let `Λ` be a commutative ring, let
`K^•` be a bounded complex of finite projective `Λ`-modules, and let `L^•` be a complex of sheaves
of modules over the restriction to `U` of the structure sheaf `Λ̲` of the constant ringed site.
Any morphism `K̲^• ⟶ L^•` of `D(Λ̲|_U)` is, after restriction along the arrows of a covering sieve
of `U`, the image under the localisation functor of a morphism of complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringSieve_complexMap_constant
    [∀ W : C, HasSheafify (J.over W) AddCommGrpCat.{0}]
    [∀ W : C, (J.over W).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{0}]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d}
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{0}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constantRingedSite J Λ).O).over U))]
    {P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{0} Λ) ℤ} (a b : ℤ)
    [P.IsStrictlyGE a] [P.IsStrictlyLE b]
    (hfin : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite Λ (P.X i)) (hproj : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective Λ (P.X i))
    {F : CochainComplex
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.{0}
        ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constantRingedSite J Λ).O).over U)) ℤ}
    (α : DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((constantFunctorOver J Λ U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ J U ∧
      ∀ {V : C} (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
        let H := _root_.SheafOfModules.overMap
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constantRingedSite J Λ).O) f
        ∃ (hsheaf : HasSheafify (J.over V) AddCommGrpCat)
          (hlocal : (J.over V).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat),
          letI := hsheaf
          letI := hlocal
          letI : HasDerivedCategory
              (_root_.SheafOfModules
                ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constantRingedSite J Λ).O).over V)) :=
            HasDerivedCategory.standard _
          ∃ (hadd : H.Additive)
            (hlim : PreservesFiniteLimits H)
            (hcolim : PreservesFiniteColimits H),
            letI := hadd
            letI := hlim
            letI := hcolim
            ∃ β : (H.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
                (((constantFunctorOver J Λ U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ⟶
                (H.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj F,
              H.mapDerivedCategory.map α ≫ H.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app F =
                H.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
                    (((constantFunctorOver J Λ U).mapHomologicalComplex
                      (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
                  DerivedCategory.Q.map β

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Constant.isStrictlyPerfect_constantModuleSheafFunctor

The complex of constant sheaves of modules on a bounded complex of finite projective

theorem isStrictlyPerfect_constantModuleSheafFunctor
    {P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{w} Λ) ℤ} (a b : ℤ)
