declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.exists_coveringSieve_complexMap_of_finite_projective
declarations.doc:
Let `Φ` be an additive right exact functor from `Λ`-modules to sheaves of `O|_U`-modules
taking `Λ` to the unit object. Let `K^•` be a bounded complex of finite projective `Λ`-modules
and `L^•` a complex of sheaves of `O|_U`-modules. Any morphism `Φ(K^•) ⟶ L^•` of `D(O|_U)` is,
after restriction along the arrows of a covering sieve of `U`, the image under the localisation
functor of a morphism of complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coveringSieve_complexMap_of_finite_projective
    {Λ : Type} [Ring Λ]
    (Φ : ModuleCat.{0} Λ ⥤ SheafOfModules.{0} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))
    [Φ.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteColimits Φ]
    (e : Φ.obj (ModuleCat.of Λ Λ) ≅
      SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U))
    {P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{0} Λ) ℤ} (a b : ℤ)
    [P.IsStrictlyGE a] [P.IsStrictlyLE b]
    (hfin : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite Λ (P.X i)) (hproj : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Projective Λ (P.X i))
    {F : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{0} ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over U)) ℤ}
    (α : DerivedCategory.Q.obj ((Φ.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ⟶
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ X.J U ∧
      ∀ {V : X.C} (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
        let H := SheafOfModules.overMap (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) f
        ∃ (hsheaf : HasSheafify (X.J.over V) AddCommGrpCat)
          (hlocal : (X.J.over V).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat),
          letI := hsheaf
          letI := hlocal
          letI : HasDerivedCategory
              (SheafOfModules ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over V)) :=
            HasDerivedCategory.standard _
          ∃ (hadd : H.Additive)
            (hlim : PreservesFiniteLimits H)
            (hcolim : PreservesFiniteColimits H),
            letI := hadd
            letI := hlim
            letI := hcolim
            ∃ β : (H.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
                ((Φ.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ⟶
                (H.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj F,
              H.mapDerivedCategory.map α ≫ H.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app F =
                H.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
                    ((Φ.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ≫
                  DerivedCategory.Q.map β

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantSheaf.exists_cover_overPullback_eq_constantSheaf_mapHomologicalComplex
declarations.doc:
**The local constancy of a map of complexes of constant sheaves of modules.** Let `P` be a
complex of finite projective `Λ`-modules which is nonzero in only finitely many degrees, let `T`
be any complex of `Λ`-modules, and write `P̲`, `T̲` for the associated complexes of constant
sheaves of `Λ`-modules. A map of complexes `β : P̲|_U ⟶ T̲|_U` on a slice site is, after
restriction along the arrows of a covering sieve of `U`, the image of an honest map of complexes
`P ⟶ T` of `Λ`-modules.

This is the content Stacks 09BE adds to Stacks 09BD at the level of complexes, i.e. the
application of Stacks 093S (3) made in the source's proof.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover_overPullback_eq_constantSheaf_mapHomologicalComplex
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)]
    [∀ V : C, HasWeakSheafify (J.over V) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)]
    [∀ V : C, (J.over V).WEqualsLocallyBijective (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)]
    (P T : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{w} Λ) ℤ)
    (hs : {n : ℤ | ¬ IsZero (P.X n)}.Finite)
    (hfin : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite Λ (P.X n))
    (hproj : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Projective Λ (P.X n)) (U : C)
    (β : ((J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{w} Λ) U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        (((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj P) ⟶
      ((J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{w} Λ) U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
        (((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj T)) :
    ∃ S : Sieve U, S ∈ J U ∧ ∀ {V : C} (f : V ⟶ U), S f →
      ∃ g : P ⟶ T, ∀ n,
        (J.overMapPullback (ModuleCat.{w} Λ) f).map (β.f n) =
          (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{w} Λ) V).map
            ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)).map (g.f n))

declarations.name: Stacks.ConstantDerivedMap.exists_cover_overPullback_map_eq_overConstantSheaf_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BE.** Let `(C, J)` be a site, `X` an object of `C` (in the source, its final
object), `Λ` a ring, and `K`, `L` objects of `D(Λ)` with `K` perfect. Let `φ : K̲ ⟶ L̲` be a
map in `D(C, Λ)`. There exists a covering `{U_i ⟶ X}` such that `φ|_{U_i}` is equal to
`α̲_i` for some map `α_i : K ⟶ L` in `D(Λ)`.

Here `φ|_{U_i}` is the image of `φ` under the functor `D(C, Λ) ⥤ D(C/U_i, Λ)` induced by
restriction, and `α̲_i` is the map `K̲ ⟶ L̲` of `D(C/U_i, Λ)` induced by the constant sheaf
functor of the slice site `C/U_i`; the two objects `(K̲)|_{U_i}` and `K̲` of `D(C/U_i, Λ)` are
identified by the canonical isomorphism
`Stacks.ConstantDerivedMap.overConstantSheafMapDerivedCategoryIso` (and likewise for `L`), which
is the first conjunct. The second conjunct records the equivalent form `φ|_{U_i} = (α̲_i)|_{U_i}`,
with `α̲_i` the constant map on `C`.

The derived categories `D(Λ)`, `D(C, Λ)` and `D(C/V, Λ)` are taken with arbitrary models
(`HasDerivedCategory` instances, which always exist: `HasDerivedCategory.standard`). The site is
small and the modules live in its universe `u`, the library's standard one-universe convention
for sheaves of modules on a site; the ring is commutative, as are all rings of the Stacks
Project; and the final object `X` of the source is generalized to an arbitrary object.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover_overPullback_map_eq_overConstantSheaf_map
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (ModuleCat.{u} Λ)]
    (X : C) {K L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Λ)} (hK : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect K)
    (φ : (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} Λ)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ⟶
      (constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} Λ)).mapDerivedCategory.obj L) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (U : ι → C) (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X), Sieve.ofArrows U f ∈ J X ∧
      ∀ i, ∃ α : K ⟶ L,
        (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{u} Λ) (U i)).mapDerivedCategory.map φ =
          (overConstantSheafMapDerivedCategoryIso J Λ (U i)).inv.app K ≫
            (constantSheaf (J.over (U i)) (ModuleCat.{u} Λ)).mapDerivedCategory.map α ≫
              (overConstantSheafMapDerivedCategoryIso J Λ (U i)).hom.app L ∧
        (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{u} Λ) (U i)).mapDerivedCategory.map φ =
          (J.overPullback (ModuleCat.{u} Λ) (U i)).mapDerivedCategory.map
            ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{u} Λ)).mapDerivedCategory.map α)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleCover_constant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BF.** On a connected scheme, a locally constant sheaf of modules becomes the
constant sheaf associated to one fixed module after an étale covering.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_etaleCover_constant
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace X]
    (Λ : Type v) [Ring Λ]
    [HasWeakSheafify X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{v} Λ)]
    [∀ U : X.Etale, HasWeakSheafify (X.smallEtaleTopology.over U) (ModuleCat.{v} Λ)]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{v} Λ))
    [Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsLocallyConstant X.smallEtaleTopology F] :
    ∃ (M : ModuleCat.{v} Λ) (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → X.Etale),
      ((⋃ i, Set.range (fun x : (U i).left =>
        (((U i).hom : (U i).left ⟶ X) x))) : Set X) = Set.univ ∧
        ∀ i, Nonempty
          ((X.smallEtaleTopology.overPullback (ModuleCat.{v} Λ) (U i)).obj F ≅
            (X.smallEtaleTopology.overPullback (ModuleCat.{v} Λ) (U i)).obj
              ((constantSheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{v} Λ)).obj M))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleSetSheaf_of_mono_of_epi_and_isSerreClass_abelian_and_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BH.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme and let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring.

1. Any sub or quotient sheaf of a constructible sheaf of sets on the small étale site of `X` is
   constructible.
2. The constructible abelian sheaves on that site form a (strong) Serre subcategory of all
   abelian sheaves on it; in particular every subsheaf and quotient sheaf of a constructible
   abelian sheaf is constructible.
3. The constructible sheaves of `Λ`-modules on that site form a (strong) Serre subcategory of all
   sheaves of `Λ`-modules on it; in particular every submodule and quotient module of a
   constructible sheaf of `Λ`-modules is constructible.

`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass` is containing zero and closure under subobjects,
quotients and extensions, which is a Serre subcategory by Stacks 02MP.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleSetSheaf_of_mono_of_epi_and_isSerreClass_abelian_and_module
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme) [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    (Λ : Type r) [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ] [Small.{u + 1} Λ] :
    ((∀ (F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1))) (i : G ⟶ F),
        Mono i → IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X F → IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X G) ∧
      (∀ (F Q : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1))) (p : F ⟶ Q),
        Epi p → IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X F → IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X Q)) ∧
      ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass
        (fun F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} =>
          IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf B X F) ∧
      ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass
        (fun F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) =>
          IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X Λ F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_mono'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BH, part (3), subsheaves, for a coefficient ring in any universe.** A subsheaf of
a constructible sheaf of `R`-modules on the small étale site of a Noetherian scheme is
constructible.

`AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_mono` proves this for a ring in `Type (u + 1)`.
Here `R` need only be small in that universe: the statement is read at `Shrink.{u + 1} R`, a
Noetherian ring in `Type (u + 1)`, and transported back. The equivalence of sheaf categories
preserves monomorphisms, so the subsheaf upstairs is one.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_mono' [IsNoetherian X.obj] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {G F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R)}
    (i : G ⟶ F) [Mono i] (hF : IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X R F) :
    IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X R G
declarations.comment: part (3), subsheaf, for a Noetherian coefficient ring in any universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_epi'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BH, part (3), quotient sheaves, for a coefficient ring in any universe.** A
quotient of a constructible sheaf of `R`-modules on the small étale site of a Noetherian scheme
is constructible. This is `AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_epi` transported along
the same equivalence, which preserves epimorphisms.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_epi' [IsNoetherian X.obj] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {G Q : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.1 X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R)}
    (p : G ⟶ Q) [Epi p] (hG : IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X R G) :
    IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X R Q
declarations.comment: part (3), quotient sheaf, for a Noetherian coefficient ring in any universe

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleAbelianSheaf_of_mono
declarations.doc:
A subsheaf of a constructible sheaf of abelian groups on the small étale site of a Noetherian
scheme is constructible. It assumes `hunderlying : SmallEtaleUnderlyingSetCommutes B X`,
`hrep : RepresentableIsConstructibleSetSheaf B X` and `hcover : HasFiniteRepresentableCover B X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleAbelianSheaf_of_mono [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    (hunderlying : SmallEtaleUnderlyingSetCommutes B X)
    (hrep : RepresentableIsConstructibleSetSheaf B X)
    (hcover : HasFiniteRepresentableCover B X)
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}}
    (i : G ⟶ F) [Mono i] (hF : IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf B X F) :
    IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf B X G
declarations.comment: part (2), subsheaf, with Stacks 00YT as hunderlying, Stacks 03S8 as hrep and the surjection half of Stacks 09Y9 as hcover

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleAbelianSheaf_of_epi
declarations.doc:
A quotient of a constructible sheaf of abelian groups on the small étale site of a Noetherian
scheme is constructible. It assumes `hunderlying : SmallEtaleUnderlyingSetCommutes B X`,
`hrep : RepresentableIsConstructibleSetSheaf B X` and `hcover : HasFiniteRepresentableCover B X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleAbelianSheaf_of_epi [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    (hunderlying : SmallEtaleUnderlyingSetCommutes B X)
    (hrep : RepresentableIsConstructibleSetSheaf B X)
    (hcover : HasFiniteRepresentableCover B X)
    {F Q : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}}
    (p : F ⟶ Q) [Epi p] (hF : IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf B X F) :
    IsConstructibleAbelianSheaf B X Q
declarations.comment: part (2), quotient sheaf, with Stacks 00YT as hunderlying, Stacks 03S8 as hrep and the surjection half of Stacks 09Y9 as hcover

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSerreClass_isConstructibleAbelianSheaf
declarations.doc:
The constructible sheaves of abelian groups on the small étale site of a Noetherian scheme form
a *strong* Serre subcategory of all abelian sheaves on that site: they contain zero and are closed
under subobjects, quotients and extensions. It assumes
`hunderlying : SmallEtaleUnderlyingSetCommutes B X`,
`hrep : RepresentableIsConstructibleSetSheaf B X` and `hcover : HasFiniteRepresentableCover B X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSerreClass_isConstructibleAbelianSheaf [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    (hunderlying : SmallEtaleUnderlyingSetCommutes B X)
    (hrep : RepresentableIsConstructibleSetSheaf B X)
    (hcover : HasFiniteRepresentableCover B X) :
    (isConstructibleAbelianSheafProperty B X :
      ObjectProperty (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})).IsSerreClass
declarations.comment: part (2), the strong Serre property, with Stacks 00YT as hunderlying, Stacks 03S8 as hrep and the surjection half of Stacks 09Y9 as hcover

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BH, part (3), subsheaves.** A subsheaf of a constructible sheaf of `Λ`-modules on
the small étale site of a Noetherian scheme is constructible.

By Stacks 095E the ambient sheaf is locally constant of finite type on the strata of a single
stratification of `X`. Inverse image to a stratum is left exact, so the subsheaf restricts to a
subsheaf there, and the geometric step of the source's proof,
`AlgebraicGeometry.finiteTypeLocallyConstantSubsheavesAreConstructible`, makes that restriction
constructible on the stratum. The strata are immersed with constructible images and they cover
`X`, so Stacks 09YR carries constructibility back to `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_mono [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    {G F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)}
    (i : G ⟶ F) [Mono i] (hF : IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X Λ F) :
    IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X Λ G
declarations.comment: part (3), subsheaf; Stacks 095E, Stacks 09YR, Stacks 03RZ (3) and the geometric step of the source's proof are all discharged from the library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BH, part (3), quotient sheaves.** A quotient of a constructible sheaf of
`Λ`-modules on the small étale site of a Noetherian scheme is constructible.

An epimorphism of sheaves of modules is the cokernel of its kernel; the kernel is a subobject, so
it is constructible by `AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_mono`, and the weak Serre
property of Stacks 03RZ (3) then puts the target in the class.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_epi [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    {G Q : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)}
    (p : G ⟶ Q) [Epi p] (hG : IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X Λ G) :
    IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X Λ Q
declarations.comment: part (3), quotient sheaf; Stacks 095E, Stacks 09YR, Stacks 03RZ (3) and the geometric step of the source's proof are all discharged from the library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isSerreClass_isConstructibleModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BH, part (3).** The constructible sheaves of `Λ`-modules on the small étale site
of a Noetherian scheme form a *strong* Serre subcategory of all sheaves of `Λ`-modules on that
site: `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass` is closure under subobjects, quotients and
extensions together with containing zero, which is the characterisation of a Serre subcategory in
Stacks 02MP.

Closure under extensions and the zero object are the weak Serre property of Stacks 03RZ (3),
which is unconditional; closure under subobjects is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_mono`, and it implies closure under quotients
because an epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isSerreClass_isConstructibleModuleSheaf [IsNoetherian X.obj] :
    ObjectProperty.IsSerreClass
      (fun F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) =>
        IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X Λ F)
declarations.comment: part (3), the strong Serre property; Stacks 095E, Stacks 09YR, Stacks 03RZ (3) and the geometric step of the source's proof are all discharged from the library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleSetSheaf_of_mono
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BH, part (1), subsheaves.** A subsheaf of a constructible sheaf of sets on the
small étale site of a Noetherian scheme is constructible.

`hrep` is Stacks 03S8 and `hcover` is the surjection half of Stacks 09Y9; neither mentions
subobjects. Given a surjection onto `F` from a finite coproduct of quasi-compact representables,
sub-closure for the coproduct and for its square descends to `F`, and sub-closure for a
quasi-compact representable is `isConstructibleSetSheaf_of_mono_representable`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleSetSheaf_of_mono (B : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    (X : B.Scheme) [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    (hrep : RepresentableIsConstructibleSetSheaf B X)
    (hcover : HasFiniteRepresentableCover B X)
    {F G : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1))}
    (i : G ⟶ F) [Mono i] (hF : IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X F) :
    IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X G
declarations.comment: part (1), subsheaf, with Stacks 03S8 as hrep and the surjection half of Stacks 09Y9 as hcover

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleSetSheaf_of_epi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BH, part (1), quotient sheaves.** A quotient sheaf of a constructible sheaf of sets
on the small étale site of a Noetherian scheme is constructible.

This is the source's argument: the kernel pair `ℱ ×_𝒬 ℱ` is a subsheaf of `ℱ × ℱ`, hence
constructible by the subsheaf case and Stacks 03RZ (1), and `𝒬` is the coequalizer of that kernel
pair, hence constructible by Stacks 03RZ (1) again.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleSetSheaf_of_epi (B : BigEtaleSite.{u})
    (X : B.Scheme) [IsNoetherian X.obj]
    (hrep : RepresentableIsConstructibleSetSheaf B X)
    (hcover : HasFiniteRepresentableCover B X)
    {F Q : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1))}
    (p : F ⟶ Q) [Epi p] (hF : IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X F) :
    IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X Q
declarations.comment: part (1), quotient sheaf, with Stacks 03S8 as hrep and the surjection half of Stacks 09Y9 as hcover

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.FiniteLevelSheaf.isConstructible_of_mono
declarations.doc: A subsheaf of a constructible finite-level sheaf is constructible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructible_of_mono (n : ℕ)
    {G F : FiniteLevelSheaf.{u, u + 1} B X ℓ n} (i : G ⟶ F) [Mono i]
    (hF : IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1))) F) :
    IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1))) G
declarations.comment: part (3), subsheaf, at the coefficients Z/l^{n+1}Z of a finite level of an l-adic sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.FiniteLevelSheaf.isConstructible_of_epi
declarations.doc: A quotient of a constructible finite-level sheaf is constructible.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructible_of_epi (n : ℕ)
    {G Q : FiniteLevelSheaf.{u, u + 1} B X ℓ n} (p : G ⟶ Q) [Epi p]
    (hG : IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1))) G) :
    IsConstructibleModuleSheaf B X (ZMod (ℓ ^ (n + 1))) Q
declarations.comment: part (3), quotient sheaf, at the coefficients Z/l^{n+1}Z of a finite level of an l-adic sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.EtaleCohomology.LAdicSheaf.isConstructible_stableKernelLevel
declarations.doc: Each level of the kernel of a morphism of ℓ-adic sheaves is a constructible sheaf.
declarations.comment: part (3), subsheaf, applied to the intersection of the images of the levelwise kernels inside a levelwise kernel

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_etaleCover_constantFiniteProjectiveComplex
declarations.doc:
**Tag 09BI, with its finite-Tor-dimension input named at the points of the site.**

Let `X` be a connected scheme in a big étale site and `Λ` a Noetherian ring. Let `K` be a bounded
object of the derived category of sheaves of `Λ`-modules on the small étale site of `X` whose
cohomology sheaves are locally constant of finite type, and suppose that at every point `q` of
the site lifting to an object `V` the derived fibre of the restriction to the slice over `V` of a
representative of `K` has a bounded flat representative over `Λ` — the finite-Tor-dimension half
of membership in `D_{ctf}(X_{étale}, Λ)`. Then there is a single finite complex `E` of finite
projective `Λ`-modules and an étale covering of `X` over every member of which `K` becomes the
constant complex attached to `E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleCover_constantFiniteProjectiveComplex
    (K : DerivedCategory.Bounded
      (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)))
    (hK : ∀ n : ℤ, Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstantModuleSheaf.{u, u + 1, u, u}
      (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) n).obj K.obj))
    (hflat : ∀ (T : CochainComplex
        (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) ℤ)
      (V : SmallEtale B X.obj X.property)
      (q : (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property).Point.{u + 1}) (z : q.fiber.obj V),
      (K.obj ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj T) →
      ∃ c d : ℤ, StacksDraft.Perfect.HasFlatRepresentative.{u, u + 1}
        (((q.over z).sheafFiber (A := ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).mapDerivedCategory.obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            ((((SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property).overPullback
              (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) V).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj T))) c d) :
    ∃ (E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) ℤ) (a b : ℤ)
      (T : CochainComplex
        (Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) ℤ)
      (_e : K.obj ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj T),
      E.IsStrictlyGE a ∧ E.IsStrictlyLE b ∧
      (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Finite Λ (E.X n)) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Projective Λ (E.X n)) ∧
      ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → SmallEtale B X.obj X.property)
        (f : ∀ i, U i ⟶ SmallEtale.final B X.obj X.property),
        Sieve.ofArrows U f ∈ SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property
          (SmallEtale.final B X.obj X.property) ∧
        ∀ i, Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            ((((SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property).overPullback
              (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) (U i)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj T) ≅
          DerivedCategory.Q.obj
            (((constantSheaf ((SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property).over (U i))
              (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj E))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isIndZariski_locallyConstant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09BJ.** Locally constant functions on a profinite space form an
ind-Zariski algebra over a field.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIndZariski_locallyConstant
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (T : Type v) [TopologicalSpace T]
    (hT : IsProfiniteStacks T) :
    IsIndZariski.{u, max u v, max u v} k (LocallyConstant T k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.primeSpectrum_locallyConstant_homeomorph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09BJ.** The spectrum of the ring of locally constant functions on a
profinite space is homeomorphic to that space.
declarations.statement:
theorem primeSpectrum_locallyConstant_homeomorph
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (T : Type v) [TopologicalSpace T]
    (hT : IsProfiniteStacks T) :
    Nonempty (PrimeSpectrum (LocallyConstant T k) ≃ₜ T)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isColimit_functionRingCocone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09BJ.** For any presentation of a space as a limit of finite discrete
spaces, its ring of locally constant functions is the colimit of the finite-stage function
rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isColimit_functionRingCocone
    (k : Type u) [Field k] {J : Type w} [SmallCategory J] [IsCofiltered J]
    (F : J ⥤ TopCat.{v}) (c : Cone F)
    (hc : IsLimit c)
    (hfinite : ∀ j, Finite (F.obj j) ∧ DiscreteTopology (F.obj j)) :
    Nonempty (IsColimit (functionRingCocone k c))
declarations.comment: filtered colimit of finite-stage function rings

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appBaseChange
declarations.doc:
The functor `u`: pro-étale base change along a morphism of affine schemes `i : Z ⟶ X`, as a
functor `X_app ⥤ Z_app` between the affine ind-étale sites. On underlying schemes it is
`U ↦ U ×_X Z`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def appBaseChange {Z X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Z]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) : AppProetale X ⥤ AppProetale Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**The base change functor.** For a morphism `i : Z ⟶ X` of affine schemes,
pulling back along `i` carries an affine object of the small pro-étale site of `X` with
ind-étale ring of global sections to one over `Z`, giving a functor `X_app ⥤ Z_app`,
`U ↦ U ×_X Z`.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def appProetaleBaseChange : AppSmallProetale X ⥤ AppSmallProetale Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isClosedImmersion_pullback_fst
declarations.doc:
**The closed immersion `V → v(V)`.** The first projection of the fibre product
`U ×_X Z` is a closed immersion, being the base change of `i`; combined with the identification
of `V` with `v(V) ×_X Z` this exhibits `V → v(V)` as a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isClosedImmersion_pullback_fst (U : AppSmallProetale X) :
    IsClosedImmersion (pullback.fst U.obj.hom i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleLift
declarations.doc:
**The left adjoint `v` of base change.** For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of affine
schemes, the lift of an object of `Z_app` to `X_app`: it is the right-adjoint lift of
Stacks 097P on ind-étale algebras, read through the identification of each site with the
opposite of a category of ind-étale algebras.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def appProetaleLift : AppSmallProetale Z ⥤ AppSmallProetale X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleBaseChange_hasLeftAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**The adjunction.** The base change functor `U ↦ U ×_X Z` along a closed
immersion of affine schemes has a left adjoint.
declarations.statement:
public theorem appProetaleBaseChange_hasLeftAdjoint :
    Nonempty (appProetaleLift i ⊣ appProetaleBaseChange i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleLift_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc: **Full faithfulness of the left adjoint.**
declarations.statement:
public theorem appProetaleLift_fullyFaithful :
    Nonempty (appProetaleLift i).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: full faithfulness of the left adjoint

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleLift_baseChangeIso
declarations.doc:
**The identification of `V` with `u(v(V))`.** For `V` in `Z_app` the unit of
the adjunction identifies `V` with the fibre product `v(V) ×_X Z`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem appProetaleLift_baseChangeIso :
    Nonempty (𝟭 (AppSmallProetale Z) ≅ appProetaleLift i ⋙ appProetaleBaseChange i)
declarations.comment: the identification of V with u(v(V))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleBaseChange_isCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BK, continuity of the base change functor: coverings.** For a morphism
`i : Z ⟶ X` of affine schemes, the base change functor `U ↦ U ×_X Z` from `X_app` to `Z_app`
carries a standard pro-étale covering family to a standard pro-étale covering family.
declarations.statement:
public theorem appProetaleBaseChange_isCovering {X Z : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Z]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) {U : AppSmallProetale X} (E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} U)
    (hE : AppSmallProetale.IsCovering X ⟨U, E⟩) :
    AppSmallProetale.IsCovering Z
      ⟨(appProetaleBaseChange i).obj U, E.map (appProetaleBaseChange i)⟩
declarations.comment: the base change functor is continuous

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleLift_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BK, cocontinuity of the left adjoint.** For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of
affine schemes the left adjoint `v : Z_app ⥤ X_app` of the base change functor is cocontinuous:
it pulls covering sieves back to covering sieves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem appProetaleLift_isCocontinuous {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Z] :
    (appProetaleLift i).IsCocontinuous (AppSmallProetale.topology Z)
      (AppSmallProetale.topology X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleBaseChange_preservesPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BK, continuity of the base change functor: fibre products.** For a morphism
`i : Z ⟶ X` of affine schemes the functor `U ↦ U ×_X Z` from `X_app` to `Z_app` preserves fibre
products, which is the second half of continuity in the sense of the Stacks Project.
declarations.comment: the base change functor is continuous

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.indEtaleQuotientLift_exists_specializes
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BK, specialization to a point of `V`.** Let `A` be a ring, `I ⊆ A` an ideal and
`V` an ind-étale `A ⧸ I`-algebra. Writing `C` for the lift of `V` to an ind-étale `A`-algebra,
so that `v(V) = Spec C` and `V = Spec (C ⧸ I C)` is the closed subscheme of `v(V)` cut out by
the ideal generated by the image of `I`, every point of `v(V)` specializes to a point of `V`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem indEtaleQuotientLift_exists_specializes (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (V : IndEtaleAlgebra (A ⧸ I))
    (p : PrimeSpectrum ((indEtaleQuotientLift A I).obj V).obj.right) :
    ∃ q : PrimeSpectrum ((indEtaleQuotientLift A I).obj V).obj.right, p ⤳ q ∧
      I.map ((indEtaleQuotientLift A I).obj V).obj.hom.hom ≤ q.asIdeal
declarations.comment: every point of v(V) specialises to a point of V

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.affineIndEtaleBaseChange
declarations.doc: Pullback along a morphism of the base, on affine ind-étale pro-étale sites.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.affineIndEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous
declarations.doc: Base change on the affine ind-étale sites is continuous.
declarations.statement:
public instance affineIndEtaleBaseChange_isContinuous (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsAffine X.obj] [IsAffine Z.obj] :
    (affineIndEtaleBaseChange B i).IsContinuous (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B X)
      (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B Z)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.affineIndEtaleBaseChange_comp_forget
declarations.doc: On underlying schemes, affine ind-étale base change is ordinary fibre product.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineIndEtaleBaseChange_comp_forget :
    Nonempty ((affineIndEtaleBaseChange B i ⋙ AffineIndEtaleProetale.inclusion B Z ⋙
      SmallProetale.inclusion B Z.obj Z.property) ≅
      (AffineIndEtaleProetale.inclusion B X ⋙ SmallProetale.inclusion B X.obj X.property ⋙
        Over.pullback i))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.affineIndEtaleLift_adj_baseChange
declarations.doc: The lift is left adjoint to base change.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineIndEtaleLift_adj_baseChange :
    Nonempty (affineIndEtaleLift B i ⊣ affineIndEtaleBaseChange B i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.closedFiberInclusion_isPullback
declarations.doc: The natural inclusion identifies an object with the closed fibre of its lift.
declarations.statement:
public theorem closedFiberInclusion_isPullback
    (V : AffineIndEtaleProetale B Z) :
    IsPullback ((closedFiberInclusion B i).app V) (B.inclusion.map V.obj.obj.hom)
      (B.inclusion.map ((affineIndEtaleLift B i).obj V).obj.obj.hom) (B.inclusion.map i)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.affineIndEtaleLift_baseChangeIso
declarations.doc: Base change of the lift is canonically the original object, naturally in that object.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.affineIndEtaleLift_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc: The left-adjoint lift is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineIndEtaleLift_fullyFaithful :
    Nonempty (affineIndEtaleLift B i).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.closedFiberInclusion_isClosedImmersion
declarations.doc: The natural map from an object to its lift is a closed immersion.
declarations.statement:
public instance closedFiberInclusion_isClosedImmersion
    (V : AffineIndEtaleProetale B Z) :
    IsClosedImmersion ((closedFiberInclusion B i).app V)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_specialization_closedFiber
declarations.doc: Every point of the lift specializes to a point of its closed fibre.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_specialization_closedFiber
    (V : AffineIndEtaleProetale B Z)
    (x : ((affineIndEtaleLift B i).obj V).obj.obj.left.obj) :
    ∃ z : V.obj.obj.left.obj,
      x ⤳ ((closedFiberInclusion B i).app V).base z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.affineIndEtaleLift_isCocontinuous
declarations.doc: The lift is cocontinuous for the affine ind-étale topologies.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.affineIndEtaleLift_isCovering
declarations.doc: The lift takes finite standard pro-étale coverings to such coverings.
declarations.statement:
public theorem affineIndEtaleLift_isCovering
    (E : Covering (AffineIndEtaleProetale B Z))
    (hE : AffineIndEtaleProetale.IsCovering B Z E) :
    AffineIndEtaleProetale.IsCovering B X
      ⟨(affineIndEtaleLift B i).obj E.1, E.2.map (affineIndEtaleLift B i)⟩

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.abelianSmallProetalePushforward_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (6) for the direct image on abelian sheaves.** For a closed immersion of
affine schemes the direct image `i_*` on abelian sheaves on the small pro-étale sites is fully
faithful.
declarations.comment: (6), full faithfulness of the direct image i_* on abelian sheaves, for the small pro-etale sites of a closed immersion of affine objects of a chosen big pro-etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.abelianSmallProetale_isIso_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (5) for the direct image on abelian sheaves.** For a closed immersion of
affine schemes the counit `i^{-1} i_* ⟶ id` on abelian sheaves on the small pro-étale sites is
an isomorphism, its right adjoint `i_*` being fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianSmallProetale_isIso_counit :
    IsIso (Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
      (smallProetaleBaseChange B Z X i) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
      (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property)
      (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)).counit
declarations.comment: (5), the map i^{-1} i_* -> id is an isomorphism on abelian sheaves, for the small pro-etale sites of a closed immersion of affine objects of a chosen big pro-etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isRightAdjoint_abelianSmallProetaleSheafPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (4).** The inverse image `i^{-1}` on abelian sheaves on the small pro-étale
sites of a closed immersion of affine schemes has a left adjoint `i_!`.
declarations.statement:
instance isRightAdjoint_abelianSmallProetaleSheafPullback :
    (Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback (smallProetaleBaseChange B Z X i)
      AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property)
      (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)).IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment: (4), the inverse image i^{-1} : Ab(X_proetale) -> Ab(Z_proetale) of a closed immersion of affine objects of a chosen big pro-etale site has a left adjoint i_!

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.abelianSmallProetaleLowerShriek_unit_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (5), the unit of lower shriek on abelian sheaves.** For a closed immersion of
affine schemes the unit `id ⟶ i^{-1} i_!` of the adjunction `i_! ⊣ i^{-1}` on abelian sheaves on
the small pro-étale sites is an isomorphism.

In the adjoint triple `i_! ⊣ i^{-1} ⊣ i_*` the unit of the left adjunction is invertible exactly
when the counit of the right one is, and the latter is
`abelianSmallProetale_isIso_counit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianSmallProetaleLowerShriek_unit_isIso :
    IsIso (abelianSmallProetaleLowerShriekAdjunction B i).unit
declarations.comment: (5), the map id -> i^{-1} i_! is an isomorphism, for abelian sheaves on the small pro-etale sites of a closed immersion of affine objects of a chosen big pro-etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.abelianSmallProetaleLowerShriek_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (6) for lower shriek on abelian sheaves.** For a closed immersion of affine
schemes the left adjoint `i_!` of the inverse image on abelian sheaves on the small pro-étale
sites is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
def abelianSmallProetaleLowerShriek_fullyFaithful :
    (abelianSmallProetaleLowerShriek B i).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: (6), full faithfulness of i_!, for abelian sheaves on the small pro-etale sites of a closed immersion of affine objects of a chosen big pro-etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.affineIndEtalePushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL.** The direct image of the small pro-étale morphism of a closed immersion of
affine schemes, read through the restriction equivalences to the affine ind-étale sites, is the
direct image attached to the cocontinuous lift.
declarations.statement:
def affineIndEtalePushforwardIso :
    (smallProetaleMorphism B Z X i).pushforward ⋙
      (AffineIndEtaleProetale.inclusion B X).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B X) (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property) ≅
    (AffineIndEtaleProetale.inclusion B Z).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B Z) (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) ⋙
      (affineIndEtaleLift B i).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type (u + 1))
        (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B Z) (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B X)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleMorphism_counit_isIso_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL.** For a closed immersion of affine schemes, the counit
`i^{-1} i_* → id` of the small pro-étale adjunction is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallProetaleMorphism_counit_isIso_of_isAffine :
    IsIso (smallProetaleMorphism B Z X i).adj.counit

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.proetaleInverseImage_sheafify_affineIndEtaleLift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL.** For a closed immersion of affine schemes, the inverse image of a small
pro-étale sheaf, restricted to the affine ind-étale site of `Z`, is the sheafification of the
presheaf of its values on the lift, naturally in the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def proetaleInverseImage_sheafify_affineIndEtaleLift :
    (smallProetaleMorphism B Z X i).inverseImage ⋙
        (AffineIndEtaleProetale.inclusion B Z).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type (u + 1))
          (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B Z) (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) ≅
      sheafToPresheaf (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙
        (Functor.whiskeringLeft (AffineIndEtaleProetale B Z)ᵒᵖ
          (SmallProetale B X.obj X.property)ᵒᵖ (Type (u + 1))).obj
            (affineIndEtaleLift B i ⋙ AffineIndEtaleProetale.inclusion B X).op ⋙
        presheafToSheaf (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B Z) (Type (u + 1))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isRightAdjoint_smallProetaleMorphism_inverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (3).** The inverse image `i^{-1}` on small pro-étale sheaves of sets of a
closed immersion of affine schemes has a left adjoint `i^{Sh}_!`.
declarations.statement:
instance isRightAdjoint_smallProetaleMorphism_inverseImage :
    (smallProetaleMorphism B Z X i).inverseImage.IsRightAdjoint
declarations.comment: (3), the inverse image i^{-1} : Sh(X_proetale) -> Sh(Z_proetale) of a closed immersion of affine objects of a chosen big pro-etale site has a left adjoint i^{Sh}_!

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleLowerShriek_unit_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (5), the unit of lower shriek.** For a closed immersion of affine schemes the
unit `id ⟶ i^{-1} i^{Sh}_!` of the adjunction `i^{Sh}_! ⊣ i^{-1}` on small pro-étale sheaves of
sets is an isomorphism.

In an adjoint triple `i^{Sh}_! ⊣ i^{-1} ⊣ i_*` the unit of the left adjunction is invertible
exactly when the counit of the right one is, and the latter is Stacks 09BL (5) for `i^{-1}i_*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem smallProetaleLowerShriek_unit_isIso :
    IsIso (smallProetaleLowerShriekAdjunction B i).unit
declarations.comment: (5), the map id -> i^{-1} i^{Sh}_! is an isomorphism, for sheaves of sets on the small pro-etale sites of a closed immersion of affine objects of a chosen big pro-etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.smallProetaleLowerShriek_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (6) for lower shriek.** For a closed immersion of affine schemes the left
adjoint `i^{Sh}_!` of the inverse image on small pro-étale sheaves of sets is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
def smallProetaleLowerShriek_fullyFaithful :
    (smallProetaleLowerShriek B i).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: (6), full faithfulness of i^{Sh}_!, for sheaves of sets on the small pro-etale sites of a closed immersion of affine objects of a chosen big pro-etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.proetaleInverseImage_sections_iso_affineIndEtaleLift
declarations.doc:
At a weakly contractible affine ind-étale object of the closed fibre, inverse image is
evaluation at its lift, naturally in the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def proetaleInverseImage_sections_iso_affineIndEtaleLift (V : AffineIndEtaleProetale B Z)
    (hV : (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B Z).IsWeaklyContractible V) :
    Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback (smallProetaleBaseChange B Z X i)
        (Type (max (u + 1) v)) (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) ⋙
      sheafToPresheaf (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)
        (Type (max (u + 1) v)) ⋙
      (evaluation _ _).obj (Opposite.op ((AffineIndEtaleProetale.inclusion B Z).obj V)) ≅
    sheafToPresheaf (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        (Type (max (u + 1) v)) ⋙
      (evaluation _ _).obj
        (Opposite.op ((AffineIndEtaleProetale.inclusion B X).obj
          ((affineIndEtaleLift B i).obj V)))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.proetaleInverseImage_sections_iso_affineIndEtaleLiftAddCommGrp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (2) for abelian sheaves.** At a weakly contractible affine ind-étale object of
the closed fibre, the inverse image of an abelian pro-étale sheaf is evaluation at the lift of
that object, naturally in the sheaf.
declarations.statement:
def proetaleInverseImage_sections_iso_affineIndEtaleLiftAddCommGrp
    (V : AffineIndEtaleProetale B Z)
    (hV : (AffineIndEtaleProetale.topology B Z).IsWeaklyContractible V) :
    Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafPullback (smallProetaleBaseChange B Z X i)
        AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) ⋙
      sheafToPresheaf (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
      (evaluation _ _).obj (Opposite.op ((AffineIndEtaleProetale.inclusion B Z).obj V)) ≅
    sheafToPresheaf (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} ⋙
      (evaluation _ _).obj
        (Opposite.op ((AffineIndEtaleProetale.inclusion B X).obj
          ((affineIndEtaleLift B i).obj V)))
declarations.comment: (2) for abelian sheaves: at a weakly contractible object V of Z_app the inverse image of an abelian sheaf is F(v(V)), for the morphism of topoi of a closed immersion of affine objects of a chosen big pro-etale site

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleInverseImage_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (1), the formula.** The inverse image of the morphism of topoi induced by `v`
is the sheafification of the presheaf `V ↦ F(v(V))` on `Z_app`: it is restriction along `v.op`
sandwiched between the inclusion of sheaves into presheaves and sheafification.
declarations.statement:
public theorem appProetaleInverseImage_eq :
    appProetaleInverseImage i =
      sheafToPresheaf (AppSmallProetale.topology X) (Type (u + 1)) ⋙
        (Functor.whiskeringLeft (AppSmallProetale Z)ᵒᵖ (AppSmallProetale X)ᵒᵖ
            (Type (u + 1))).obj (appProetaleLift i).op ⋙
          presheafToSheaf (AppSmallProetale.topology Z) (Type (u + 1))
declarations.comment: (1), the inverse image is the sheafification of the presheaf V -> F(v(V)), for the morphism of topoi induced by the fully faithful cocontinuous functor v of Tag 09BK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetaleInverseImageAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (1), that this is the inverse image.** The sheafification of `V ↦ F(v(V))` is
left adjoint to the direct image, so it is the inverse image of the morphism of topoi induced
by `v`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def appProetaleInverseImageAdjunction :
    appProetaleInverseImage i ⊣ appProetalePushforward i
declarations.comment: (1), the sheafification of V -> F(v(V)) is the inverse image, being left adjoint to the direct image of the morphism of topoi induced by the cocontinuous functor v of Tag 09BK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetalePushforwardFullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (6) for the direct image.** The direct image `i_*` of the morphism of topoi
induced by `v` is fully faithful.

On underlying presheaves `i_*` is restriction along the base change functor `u`, whose left
adjoint is restriction along `v`; the composite of the two is restriction along `v ⋙ u`, which
is the identity because `v` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def appProetalePushforwardFullyFaithful :
    (appProetalePushforward i).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: (6), full faithfulness of the direct image i_*, for the morphism of topoi induced by the fully faithful cocontinuous functor v of Tag 09BK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.appProetale_isIso_counit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BL (5) for the direct image.** The counit `i^{-1}i_* ⟶ id` of the morphism of
topoi induced by `v` is an isomorphism, because its right adjoint `i_*` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
public theorem appProetale_isIso_counit :
    IsIso (appProetaleInverseImageAdjunction i).counit
declarations.comment: (5), the map i^{-1} i_* -> id is an isomorphism, for the morphism of topoi induced by the fully faithful cocontinuous functor v of Tag 09BK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exact_smallProetalePushforward_of_isRetrocompact_compl_range
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BM.** Let `i : Z → X` be a closed immersion of schemes whose open complement is
retrocompact. Then direct image of abelian sheaves along the induced morphism of small pro-étale
sites is exact.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_smallProetalePushforward_of_isRetrocompact_compl_range
    (B : BigProetaleSite.{u}) {Z X : B.Scheme} (i : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion (B.inclusion.map i)]
    (hi : IsRetrocompact ((Set.range (B.inclusion.map i).base)ᶜ)) :
    exactFunctor
      (Sheaf (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      (Sheaf (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property) AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
      ((smallProetaleBaseChange B Z X i).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
        (SmallProetale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        (SmallProetale.topology B Z.obj Z.property))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.preservesLimits_extensionByZero_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BP.** For a quasi-compact open immersion `j : U ⟶ X` of schemes, extension by
zero `j_! : Ab(U_proétale) ⥤ Ab(X_proétale)` of abelian sheaves on the small pro-étale sites
commutes with limits.

Nothing is assumed: `j_! j^{-1}` commutes with limits by
`preservesLimits_proetaleRestriction_comp_extensionByZero_of_quasiCompact`, whose proof computes
the sections of `j_! j^{-1}` on the covering family that quasi-compactness of `j` produces; and
`j_!` is isomorphic to `j_! j^{-1} j_*` because the counit of `j^{-1} ⊣ j_*` is invertible for
an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesLimits_extensionByZero_unconditional [IsOpenImmersion j] [QuasiCompact j] :
    PreservesLimits (Abelian.extensionByZero.{u, v} j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.minus_tensor_and_isConstructibleModuleSheaf'_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BQ.** Let `X` be a scheme and `Λ` a Noetherian ring. If `K` and `L` are bounded
above objects of `D(X_proét, Λ)` whose cohomology sheaves are constructible, then their derived
tensor product `K ⊗_Λ^L L` is bounded above and has constructible cohomology sheaves: it lies in
`D_c^-(X_proét, Λ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem minus_tensor_and_isConstructibleModuleSheaf'_homology
    (K L : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ)))
    (hK : DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.minus K) (hL : DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.minus L)
    (hKc : ∀ i, IsConstructibleModuleSheaf'.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K))
    (hLc : ∀ i, IsConstructibleModuleSheaf'.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj L)) :
    DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.minus (K ⊗ L) ∧
      ∀ i, IsConstructibleModuleSheaf'.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj (K ⊗ L))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.minus_and_isConstructibleModuleSheaf'_homology_derivedExtendScalars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BR.** Let `X` be a scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal and `K` an
object of `D(X_proét, Λ)`. Set `Kₙ = K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ`, the derived extension of scalars of `K` along
`Λ → Λ/Iⁿ`. If `K₁` lies in `D_c^-(X_proét, Λ/I)`, that is, it is bounded above and its
cohomology sheaves are constructible, then `Kₙ` lies in `D_c^-(X_proét, Λ/Iⁿ)` for all `n`.
declarations.statement:
theorem minus_and_isConstructibleModuleSheaf'_homology_derivedExtendScalars
    (K : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ)))
    (hK : DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.minus
        ((derivedExtendScalars _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj K) ∧
      ∀ i, IsConstructibleModuleSheaf'.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X (Λ ⧸ I)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
          ((derivedExtendScalars _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)).obj K)))
    (n : ℕ) :
    DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.minus
        ((derivedExtendScalars _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n))).obj K) ∧
      ∀ i, IsConstructibleModuleSheaf'.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
          ((derivedExtendScalars _ (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ n))).obj K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsConstructibleAdicSheaf
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of `Λ`-modules on the small pro-étale site is a *constructible `Λ`-sheaf* if it is
the limit of its quotients by the powers of `I` and each of those quotients is, as a sheaf of
`Λ ⧸ Iⁿ`-modules, constructible.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsConstructibleAdicSheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) (Λ : Type v) [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    [UnivLE.{u + 1, w}] (I : Ideal Λ)
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (Y : Scheme.{u}),
      HasWeakSheafify (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) (ModuleCat.{w} (Λ ⧸ I ^ n))]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (Y : Scheme.{u}) (V : Y.ProEt),
      HasWeakSheafify ((Scheme.ProEt.topology Y).over V) (ModuleCat.{w} (Λ ⧸ I ^ n))]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ Y),
      ((Scheme.proetaleBaseChange f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        (ModuleCat.{w} (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)) (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
        (Scheme.ProEt.topology Z)).IsRightAdjoint]
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsLisse
declarations.doc:
A constructible `Λ`-sheaf is *lisse* if each of its quotients by a power of `I` is a locally
constant sheaf of `Λ ⧸ Iⁿ`-modules.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsLisse (X : Scheme.{u}) (Λ : Type v) [CommRing Λ] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    [UnivLE.{u + 1, w}] (I : Ideal Λ)
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (Y : Scheme.{u}),
      HasWeakSheafify (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) (ModuleCat.{w} (Λ ⧸ I ^ n))]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) (Y : Scheme.{u}) (V : Y.ProEt),
      HasWeakSheafify ((Scheme.ProEt.topology Y).over V) (ModuleCat.{w} (Λ ⧸ I ^ n))]
    [∀ (n : ℕ) {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ Y),
      ((Scheme.proetaleBaseChange f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        (ModuleCat.{w} (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)) (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
        (Scheme.ProEt.topology Z)).IsRightAdjoint]
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsAdicConstructible
declarations.doc:
A sheaf of `Λ`-modules on the small pro-étale site of `X` is *adic constructible* if every
affine open of `X` decomposes into constructible locally closed subschemes on each of which the
inverse image of the sheaf is adic lisse.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsAdicConstructible (X : Scheme.{u}) (Λ : Type v) [CommRing Λ] (I : Ideal Λ)
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u}, HasWeakSheafify (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)]
    [∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (V : Y.ProEt),
      HasWeakSheafify ((Scheme.ProEt.topology Y).over V) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)]
    [∀ {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Z ⟶ Y),
      ((Scheme.proetaleBaseChange f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        (ModuleCat.{w} Λ) (Scheme.ProEt.topology Y)
        (Scheme.ProEt.topology Z)).IsRightAdjoint]
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_iso_completedConstantSheaf_of_isConstant
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a scheme whose pro-étale topos is not empty, let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring and
`I ⊆ Λ` an ideal, and let `F` be a sheaf of `Λ`-modules on the small pro-étale site of `X` such
that

1. `F` is the limit of its adic reductions `F / IⁿF`,
2. every `F / IⁿF` is a constant sheaf, and
3. `F / IF` is the constant sheaf of a finite module.

Then `F ≅ M̲^∧` for an `I`-adically complete `Λ`-module `M` which is finite over `Λ^∧`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_iso_completedConstantSheaf_of_isConstant
    (hne : ∃ U : X.ProEt, (⊥ : Sieve U) ∉ Scheme.ProEt.topology X U)
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ))
    (Q : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ))
    (q : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj F ⟶ Q)
    (hq : ∀ n : ℕ, IsQuotientBy X Λ (I ^ n) F (Q.obj (op n)) (q.app (op n)))
    (hlim : IsLimit (Limits.Cone.mk F q))
    (hconst : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ N : ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ,
      Nonempty ((constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
        (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ)).obj N ≅ Q.obj (op n)))
    (hfin : ∃ N : ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ,
      Module.Finite Λ (N : Type (max (u + 1) w)) ∧
      Nonempty ((constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
        (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ)).obj N ≅ Q.obj (op 1))) :
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} Λ,
      IsAdicComplete I (M : Type (max (u + 1) w)) ∧
      Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I Λ) (AdicCompletion I (M : Type (max (u + 1) w))) ∧
      Nonempty (F ≅ completedConstantSheaf X Λ I M)
declarations.comment: the sheaf is the completed constant sheaf of a finite complete module

declarations.name: Stacks.ModuleSheaf.exists_finite_isAdicComplete_constantSheaf_iso_of_isConstant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BV, the coefficient module, on a site with a terminal object.** Let `Λ` be
Noetherian, `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal and `F` a sheaf of `Λ`-modules on a site with a terminal object whose
topos is not empty, whose reductions `F / IⁿF` are constant sheaves and whose first reduction is
the constant sheaf of a finite module. Then there is an `I`-adically complete `Λ`-module `M`,
finite over `Λ^∧` and with every reduction `M / IⁿM` finite over `Λ`, whose tower of constant
reductions is termwise isomorphic to the adic quotient tower of `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_isAdicComplete_constantSheaf_iso_of_isConstant (I : Ideal Λ)
    (hne : ∃ U : C, (⊥ : Sieve U) ∉ J U)
    (F : Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ))
    (Q : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ))
    (q : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj F ⟶ Q)
    (hq : ∀ n : ℕ, IsQuotientBy J Λ (I ^ n) F (Q.obj (op n)) (q.app (op n)))
    (hconst : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ N : ModuleCat.{w} Λ,
      Nonempty ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)).obj N ≅
        Q.obj (op n)))
    (hfin : ∃ N : ModuleCat.{w} Λ, Module.Finite Λ (N : Type w) ∧
      Nonempty ((constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)).obj N ≅
        Q.obj (op 1))) :
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{w} Λ, IsAdicComplete I (M : Type w) ∧
      Module.Finite Λ ((M : Type w) ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule Λ (M : Type w))) ∧
      Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I Λ) (AdicCompletion I (M : Type w)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, Module.Finite Λ ((M : Type w) ⧸ (I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule Λ (M : Type w)))) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty ((adicQuotientModuleSystem Λ I M ⋙
        constantSheaf J (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)).obj (op n) ≅
          Q.obj (op n))
declarations.comment: the coefficient module, on any site with a terminal object

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_finite_isAdicComplete_constantSheaf_iso_of_isConstant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BV, the coefficient module.** Let `Λ` be Noetherian, `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal and `F` a
sheaf of `Λ`-modules on the small pro-étale site whose reductions `F / IⁿF` are constant sheaves
and whose first reduction is of finite type. Then there is an `I`-adically complete `Λ`-module
`M`, finite over `Λ^∧` and with every reduction `M / IⁿM` finite over `Λ`, whose tower of constant
reductions is termwise isomorphic to the adic quotient tower of `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_isAdicComplete_constantSheaf_iso_of_isConstant (I : Ideal Λ)
    (hne : ∃ U : X.ProEt, (⊥ : Sieve U) ∉ Scheme.ProEt.topology X U)
    (F : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ))
    (Q : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ))
    (q : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj F ⟶ Q)
    (hq : ∀ n : ℕ, IsQuotientBy X Λ (I ^ n) F (Q.obj (op n)) (q.app (op n)))
    (hconst : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ N : ModuleCat.{w} Λ,
      Nonempty ((constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)).obj N ≅
        Q.obj (op n)))
    (hfin : ∃ N : ModuleCat.{w} Λ, Module.Finite Λ (N : Type w) ∧
      Nonempty ((constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)).obj N ≅
        Q.obj (op 1))) :
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{w} Λ, IsAdicComplete I (M : Type w) ∧
      Module.Finite Λ ((M : Type w) ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule Λ (M : Type w))) ∧
      Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I Λ) (AdicCompletion I (M : Type w)) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, Module.Finite Λ ((M : Type w) ⧸ (I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule Λ (M : Type w)))) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, Nonempty ((adicQuotientModuleSystem Λ I M ⋙
        constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{w} Λ)).obj (op n) ≅
          Q.obj (op n))
declarations.comment: the finite complete coefficient module and its termwise constant reductions

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isAdicLisse_of_isLisseAdicModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BW.** Let `X` be a connected scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring and `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal.
A lisse constructible `Λ`-sheaf on the small pro-étale site of `X` is adic lisse.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isAdicConstructibleModuleSheaf_of_isConstructibleAdicModuleSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BX.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring and `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal.
A constructible `Λ`-sheaf on the small pro-étale site of `X` is adic constructible: it is lisse on

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isZero_of_isDerivedComplete_of_idealProduct_eq_top_of_slicedObjectsSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BY.** A sheaf of modules on a ringed site with enough weakly contractible
objects which is derived complete along a sheaf of ideals and satisfies `IF = F`, that is
whose adic quotient `F/IF` vanishes, is zero. The sheaf of ideals is assumed finitely
generated on sections over the weakly contractible objects.

This generalizes the content of the tag, whose site is `X_proétale` and whose coefficients are a
constant ring `Λ` with a finitely generated ideal `I`: the site here is any ringed site with
enough weakly contractible objects, `I` is any sheaf of ideals, and the finite-generation
requirement is *weaker* than the source's, being asked only on sections over weakly contractible
objects.

The weakly contractible objects enter only through the bundle `hX`, whose members test
surjectivity of sheaves of sets valued in the *module* universe `max u v`, on the site and on
each of its slice sites. That is what makes the statement readable at a site whose objects
outnumber its morphisms. The small pro-étale site of a scheme is such a site: it is a
`RingedSite.{u + 1, u, _}` — for instance
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.constantCoefficientRingedSite`, which is `X_proétale` ringed by the
constant sheaf `Λ̲` — and its weak contractibility cannot be tested at the morphism universe `u`
at all, since `Small.{u} X.ProEt` is false: the objects of `X.ProEt` lie in `Type (u + 1)` and
the site is small, and essentially small, only at `u + 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_of_isDerivedComplete_of_idealProduct_eq_top_of_slicedObjectsSituation
    (X : RingedSite.{u, v, max u v})
    [HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    (hX : Stacks.WeaklyContractible.SlicedObjectsSituation.{w, v, u, max u v} X.C X.J)
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hI : ∀ U : X.C, hX.B U →
      (I.toSubmodule.obj (op U)).FG)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete X I
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj F))
    (hIF : idealPowerProduct X I F 1 = ⊤) :
    IsZero F
declarations.comment: generalized to a ringed site with a covering collection of objects testing surjectivity of sheaves of sets in the module universe, on the site and on its slices, and to an arbitrary sheaf of ideals; the Small and HasSheafify hypotheses that used to exclude the pro-etale site are gone, but the sliced bundle is not yet constructed for that site, so the pro-etale site is still NOT an instance of this statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isZero_of_isDerivedComplete_of_idealProduct_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BY.** A sheaf of modules on a ringed site with enough weakly contractible
objects which is derived complete along a sheaf of ideals and satisfies `IF = F`, that is
whose adic quotient `F/IF` vanishes, is zero. The sheaf of ideals is assumed finitely
generated on sections over the weakly contractible objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_of_isDerivedComplete_of_idealProduct_eq_top
    (X : RingedSite.{u, v, max u v}) [Small.{v} X.C]
    [HasSheafify X.J (Type v)]
    [HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}]
    (hX : X.J.HasEnoughWeaklyContractibleObjects)
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hI : ∀ U : X.C, X.J.IsWeaklyContractible U →
      (I.toSubmodule.obj (op U)).FG)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete X I
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{max u v} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj F))
    (hIF : idealPowerProduct X I F 1 = ⊤) :
    IsZero F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isZero_of_isDerivedComplete_of_idealProduct_eq_top_of_sliceTestingFamily
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09BY.** A sheaf of modules on a ringed site with enough weakly contractible
objects which is derived complete along a sheaf of ideals and satisfies `IF = F`, that is
whose adic quotient `F/IF` vanishes, is zero. The sheaf of ideals is assumed finitely
generated on sections over the weakly contractible objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_of_isDerivedComplete_of_idealProduct_eq_top_of_sliceTestingFamily
    (X : RingedSite.{u, v, max u v w})
    [HasSheafify X.J AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}]
    [X.J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u v w}]
    (B : Stacks.WeaklyContractible.SliceTestingFamily.{max u v w} X.C X.J)
    (I : SheafOfModules.Submodule
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hI : ∀ U : X.C, B.B U →
      (I.toSubmodule.obj (op U)).FG)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{max u v w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))
    (hF : AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u, v, max u v w, max u v w} X I
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{max u v w} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj F))
    (hIF : idealPowerProductOfSize X I F 1 = ⊤) :
    IsZero F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isZero_of_isDerivedComplete_constantCoefficients
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09BY].** Let `X` be a scheme, let `Λ` be a ring with a finitely generated
ideal `I ⊂ Λ`, and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `X_proétale` — a sheaf of modules over
the constant coefficient ring sheaf `Λ̲`. If `ℱ` is derived complete along the ideal sheaf `IΛ̲`
cut out by `I`, and `ℱ/Iℱ = 0`, then `ℱ = 0`.

This is the tag's own statement at the tag's own objects. It is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isZero_of_isDerivedComplete_proetale` — the chapter's lemma at the
small pro-étale site for an arbitrary sheaf of rings and an arbitrary sheaf of ideals — read at
`𝒪 = Λ̲` and `ℐ = AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.constantCoefficientIdealSheaf`, with that
statement's finite-generation hypothesis discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.fg_constantCoefficientIdealSheaf_obj`. The two ringed sites agree
on the nose, so no transport is needed at this step.

`Λ` is an arbitrary commutative ring: `I.FG` is the only hypothesis on the coefficients, as in
the source. The hypothesis `hIF` says the first ideal power product is everything, which is the
vanishing of the adic quotient `ℱ/Iℱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_of_isDerivedComplete_constantCoefficients (X : Scheme.{u}) (Λ : Type u)
    [CommRing Λ] (I : Ideal Λ) (hI : I.FG)
    (F : SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, u, u} X Λ).O))
    (hF : RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, u, u} X Λ)
      (constantCoefficientIdealSheaf.{u, u, u} X Λ I)
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u + 1}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf
            (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, u, u} X Λ).O)) 0).obj F))
    (hIF : RingedSite.idealPowerProduct (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, u, u} X Λ)
      (constantCoefficientIdealSheaf.{u, u, u} X Λ I) F 1 = ⊤) :
    IsZero F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_epi_biproduct_completedConstantCoefficientSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Derived complete sheaves are quotients of finite sums of `\underline{Λ}^∧`.** Let `X` be a
weakly contractible affine scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring and `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal. Let `F` be a
derived complete sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `X_proét` with `F/IF` of finite type, for instance
locally constant of finite type. Then there are an integer `t` and a surjection
`(\underline{Λ}^∧)^{⊕ t} → F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_biproduct_completedConstantCoefficientSheaf [IsAffine X]
    (hX : IsWeaklyContractibleObj X)
    (F : RingedSite.Modules.{u + 1, u, max (u + 1) w}
      (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ))
    (hF : RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u + 1, u, max (u + 1) w, w}
      (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ)
      (constantCoefficientIdealSheaf.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ I)
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))
    (hFI : (cokernel (RingedSite.idealPowerProductOfSize.{u + 1, u, w} _
      (constantCoefficientIdealSheaf.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ I) F 1).ι).IsFiniteType) :
    ∃ (t : ℕ) (α : (⨁ fun _ : Fin t =>
        (completedConstantCoefficientSheafFunctor.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ I).obj
          (Functor.unitModule Λ)) ⟶ F), Epi α
declarations.comment: `F/IF` is only assumed of finite type, which a locally constant sheaf of finite type is

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_epi_sigma_completedConstantSheaf_of_isDerivedComplete
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09BZ].** Let `X` be a weakly contractible affine scheme, let `Λ` be a
Noetherian ring and let `I ⊂ Λ` be an ideal. Let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `Λ`-modules on `X_proétale`
which is derived complete, and such that `ℱ/Iℱ` is a locally constant sheaf of `Λ/I`-modules of
finite type. Then there is an integer `t` and a surjection `(Λ̲^∧)^{⊕t} ⟶ ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_epi_sigma_completedConstantSheaf_of_isDerivedComplete
    [IsAffine X] (hX : ProetaleWContractible.IsWeaklyContractibleObj X)
    (F : RingedSite.Modules.{u + 1, u, u + 1} (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, u + 1, u} X Λ))
    (hF : RingedSite.IsDerivedComplete.{u + 1, u, u + 1, u + 1}
      (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, u + 1, u} X Λ)
      (constantCoefficientIdealSheaf.{u, u + 1, u} X Λ I)
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj F))
    (hFI : ∃ G : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (Λ ⧸ I)),
      Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsFiniteTypeLocallyConstant (Λ ⧸ I) (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) G ∧
      Nonempty ((toCoefficientModuleSheaf.{u, u + 1, u} X Λ).obj
          (cokernel (RingedSite.idealPowerProduct (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, u + 1, u} X Λ)
            (constantCoefficientIdealSheaf.{u, u + 1, u} X Λ I) F 1).ι) ≅
        (restrictQuotientScalars.{u + 1, u + 1, u} X Λ I).obj G)) :
    ∃ t : ℕ, ∃ α : (∐ fun _ : Fin t =>
        (moduleSheafOverConstantCoefficientsFunctor.{u, u + 1, u} X Λ).obj
          (Stacks.ConstantSheaf.completedConstantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) I)) ⟶ F,
      Epi α

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsConstructibleDerivedSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C1.** An object `K` of `D(X_proét, Λ)` is *constructible* with respect to the
ideal `I` of the Noetherian coefficient ring `Λ` when it is derived complete along the ideal
sheaf cut out by `I`, and its derived reduction `K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/I`, formed with the derived base
change `T`, has constructible cohomology sheaves and locally has finite Tor dimension measured
against the derived tensor products `D` on the slices.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsConstructibleDerivedSheaf
    (T : DerivedReduction.{u, r, w} X Λ I)
    (D : ∀ U : (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, r, w} X (Λ ⧸ I)).C,
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, max (u + 1) r w,
          max (u + 1) r w + 1}
        ((constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, r, w} X (Λ ⧸ I)).over U))
    (K : DerivedSheaves.{u, r, w} X Λ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsConstructibleViaDerivedReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C1.** An object `K` of `D(X_proét, Λ)` is *constructible* with respect to the
ideal `I` of the Noetherian coefficient ring `Λ` when it is derived complete along the ideal
sheaf cut out by `I`, and its derived reduction `K ⊗_Λ^L \underline{Λ/I}` has constructible
cohomology sheaves and locally has finite Tor dimension.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsConstructibleViaDerivedReduction (K : DerivedSheaves.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.constructibleDerivedSheavesViaDerivedReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C1.** The full subcategory `D_cons(X, Λ)` of `D(X_proét, Λ)` on the
constructible objects.
declarations.statement: abbrev constructibleDerivedSheavesViaDerivedReduction

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.hasConstructibleCohomology_derivedReduction_pow
declarations.doc:
**The reductions of a constructible complex have constructible cohomology sheaves.** If `X`
is quasi-compact and `K` lies in `D_cons(X, Λ)`, every reduction
`Kₙ = K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ` has constructible cohomology sheaves.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasConstructibleCohomology_derivedReduction_pow [CompactSpace X]
    {K : DerivedSheaves.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ}
    (hK : IsConstructibleViaDerivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ I K)
    (n : ℕ) :
    HasConstructibleModuleSheafCohomology.{u, w} X (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)
      ((derivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ (I ^ n)).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_isDerivedLimit_derivedReductionTower_and_hasTorAmplitude
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be quasi-compact and `K` an object of `D_cons(X, Λ)`, and set
`Kₙ = K ⊗_Λ^L \underline{Λ/Iⁿ}`. There are integers `a` and `b` such that

1. `K = R lim Kₙ`, with the reduction maps `K ⟶ Kₙ` as projections, and `Hⁱ(K) = 0` for
   `i ∉ [a, b]`;
2. every `Kₙ` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]`.

In (1) the tower `Kₙ` is read in the derived category of sheaves of `Λ`-modules, as the derived
tensor product of `K` with the constant sheaves `\underline{Λ/Iⁿ}`; in (2) `Kₙ` is the derived
reduction of `K`, an object of `D(X_proét, Λ/Iⁿ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isDerivedLimit_derivedReductionTower_and_hasTorAmplitude [CompactSpace X]
    {K : DerivedSheaves.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ}
    (hK : IsConstructibleViaDerivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ I K) :
    ∃ a b : ℤ,
      (NoetherianAdicCompletion.IsDerivedLimitWithProjections
          (derivedReductionTower.{u, w} X Λ I
            ((derivedModuleEquiv.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ).inverse.obj K))
          ((derivedModuleEquiv.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ).inverse.obj K)
          (fun n ↦ (Stacks.ModuleSheaf.derivedReductionMap (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Λ I
            ((derivedModuleEquiv.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ).inverse.obj K)).app ⟨n⟩) ∧
        ∀ i : ℤ, i ∉ Set.Icc a b →
          IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj K)) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, Stacks.ModuleSheaf.HasTorAmplitude (J := Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
        ((derivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ (I ^ n)).obj K) (Set.Icc a b)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_etaleInverseImage_iso_derivedReduction_pow
declarations.doc:
**The reductions of a constructible complex come from the étale site.** If `X` is
quasi-compact and `K` lies in `D_cons(X, Λ)`, every reduction
`Kₙ = K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ` is `ε⁻¹ Lₙ` for an object `Lₙ` of `D(X_étale, Λ/Iⁿ)` with constructible
cohomology sheaves and finite Tor dimension.

Here `ε⁻¹` on derived categories is `ε⁻¹` applied termwise.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_etaleInverseImage_iso_derivedReduction_pow [CompactSpace X]
    {K : DerivedSheaves.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ}
    (hK : IsConstructibleViaDerivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ I K)
    (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ L : DerivedCategory (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} (Λ ⧸ I ^ n))),
      (∀ i : ℤ, Scheme.IsConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj L)) ∧
      Stacks.ModuleSheaf.HasFiniteTorDimension (J := X.smallEtaleTopology) L ∧
      Nonempty ((Scheme.etaleInverseImage.{u, w} X (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)).mapDerivedCategory.obj L ≅
        (derivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ (I ^ n)).obj K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.hasFiniteDisjointCompletedConstantModel_of_isLocallyConstant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C3.** Let `X` be a weakly contractible affine scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring,
`I ⊆ Λ` an ideal and `K` an object of `D_cons(X, Λ)` such that the cohomology sheaves of
`K ⊗_Λ^L \underline{Λ/I}` are locally constant. Then there are a finite disjoint open covering
`X = ∐ U_i` and, for each `i`, finite projective `Λ^∧`-modules `M^a, …, M^b` such that `K|_{U_i}`
is represented in `D(U_{i, proét}, Λ)` by a complex
`(\underline{M^a})^∧ → ⋯ → (\underline{M^b})^∧` for some maps of sheaves of `Λ`-modules between
consecutive terms.

The covering, the restrictions and the models are those of
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.HasFiniteDisjointCompletedConstantModel`; weak contractibility of `X`
is that of Stacks 090L.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasFiniteDisjointCompletedConstantModel_of_isLocallyConstant [IsAffine X]
    (hX : ProetaleWContractible.IsWeaklyContractibleObj X)
    (K : DerivedSheaves.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ)
    (hK : IsConstructibleViaDerivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ I K)
    (hloc : ∀ i : ℤ, Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsLocallyConstant (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj ((derivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ I).obj K))) :
    HasFiniteDisjointCompletedConstantModel.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ I K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsAdicConstructibleViaDerivedInverseImage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C4, part (2).** An object `K` of `D(X_proét, Λ)` is *adic constructible* if every
affine open `U` of `X` admits a decomposition `U = ∐ U_i` into constructible locally closed
subschemes such that every restriction `K|_{U_i}` is adic lisse.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdicConstructibleViaDerivedInverseImage (K : DerivedSheaves.{u, r, w} X Λ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsAdicLisseDerivedSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C4, part (1).** An object `K` of `D(X_proét, Λ)` is *adic lisse* if there is a
finite complex `M^•` of finite projective `Λ^∧`-modules such that `K` is pro-étale locally
isomorphic to the complex `\underline{M^a}^∧ → ⋯ → \underline{M^b}^∧` of completed constant
sheaves, whose differentials are those induced by the differentials of `M^•`.
