declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdicLisseDerivedSheaf (K : DerivedSheaves.{u, r, w} X Λ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsAdicConstructibleDerivedSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C4, part (2).** An object `K` of `D(X_proét, Λ)` is *adic constructible* if every
affine open of `X` admits a decomposition into constructible locally closed subschemes on which
the restriction of `K` is adic lisse.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdicConstructibleDerivedSheaf (K : DerivedSheaves.{u, r, w} X Λ) : Prop

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isMittagLefflerCategorical_derivedReductionSectionsSystem_of_isConstructibleViaDerivedReduction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C5.** Let `X` be a weakly contractible affine scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring,
`I ⊆ Λ` an ideal and `K` an object of `D_cons(X, Λ)` such that every reduction
`K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ` is isomorphic, in `D(X_proét, Λ/Iⁿ)`, to a complex of constant sheaves of
`Λ/Iⁿ`-modules. Then the inverse system `n ↦ H⁰(X, K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ)` of `Λ`-modules satisfies the
Mittag-Leffler condition.

The conclusion is the Mittag-Leffler condition of Stacks Tag 02N0 for the system
`derivedReductionSectionsSystem X Λ I K'`, `K'` being `K` read in the derived category of sheaves
of `Λ`-modules; its terms are the sections modules `H⁰(X, K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ)` and its transition maps
are induced by the reductions `Λ/Iⁿ⁺¹ → Λ/Iⁿ`. Constructibility is
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.IsConstructibleViaDerivedReduction`, and the reductions are
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.derivedReduction`.

The proof: for a K-flat representative `P` of `K`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.exists_isBoundedAboveFiniteFree_reduction_iso` gives a bounded
above complex `F` of finite free `Λ^∧`-modules whose constant complex has, levelwise, the
reductions of `P`; the sections system of the reductions of `\underline{F}` is
`j ↦ Γ(X, \underline{H⁰(F/IʲF)})`, which is Mittag-Leffler by the Artin–Rees lemma
(`AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isMittagLefflerCategorical_constantComplexReductionSections`), and
`Stacks.ModuleSheaf.isMittagLefflerCategorical_reductionSections_of_adicModel` transports the
condition. Over the empty scheme every term of the system vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem
    isMittagLefflerCategorical_derivedReductionSectionsSystem_of_isConstructibleViaDerivedReduction
    [IsAffine X] (hX : ProetaleWContractible.IsWeaklyContractibleObj X)
    (K : DerivedSheaves.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ)
    (hK : IsConstructibleViaDerivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ I K)
    (hconstant : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)),
      Nonempty ((derivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ (I ^ n)).obj K ≅
        (constantSheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
          (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} (Λ ⧸ I ^ n))).mapDerivedCategory.obj E)) :
    IsMittagLefflerCategorical (derivedReductionSectionsSystem X Λ I
      ((derivedModuleEquiv.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ).inverse.obj K))
declarations.comment: the Mittag-Leffler condition for the inverse system n ↦ H^0(X, K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/I^n) of sections modules, with its canonical transition maps; the hypothesis that each reduction is a complex of constant sheaves is read, as in the source's proof, as K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/I^n ≅ \underline{E_n} for an object E_n of D(Λ/I^n)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isMittagLefflerCategorical_derivedReductionSectionsSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C5.** Let `X` be a weakly contractible affine scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring,
`I ⊆ Λ` an ideal and `K` an object of `D_cons(X, Λ)` such that for every `n ≥ 1` the reduction
`K ⊗_Λ^L \underline{Λ/Iⁿ}` is isomorphic in `D(X_proét, Λ/Iⁿ)` to a complex of constant sheaves
of `Λ/Iⁿ`-modules. Then the inverse system `n ↦ H⁰(X, K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ)` of `Λ`-modules satisfies the
Mittag-Leffler condition.

The reductions in the hypothesis are taken with derived base changes `Tn n` along
`Λ → Λ/Iⁿ` (any two of which are canonically isomorphic), and a complex of constant sheaves is
the constant sheaf functor applied to a complex `E` of `Λ/Iⁿ`-modules. The inverse system of the
conclusion is `AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.derivedReductionSectionsSystem`: degree-zero cohomology
and sections over `X` of the derived tensor products of `K` with the constant sheaves
`\underline{Λ/Iⁿ}`, whose transition maps are induced by the reductions `Λ/Iⁿ⁺¹ → Λ/Iⁿ`; here `K`
is read in the derived category of sheaves of `Λ`-modules, where the derived tensor product is
constructed, through the constant coefficients equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLefflerCategorical_derivedReductionSectionsSystem [IsAffine X]
    (hX : ProetaleWContractible.IsWeaklyContractibleObj X)
    (T : DerivedReduction.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ I)
    (D : ∀ U : (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X (Λ ⧸ I)).C,
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, max (u + 1) w,
          max (u + 1) w + 1}
        ((constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X (Λ ⧸ I)).over U))
    (K : DerivedSheaves.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ)
    (hK : IsConstructibleDerivedSheaf.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ I T D K)
    (Tn : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedReduction.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ (I ^ n))
    (hconstant : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
      ∃ E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) w} (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)) ℤ,
        Nonempty ((Tn n).baseChange.obj K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((constantSheafOverCoefficients.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj E))) :
    IsMittagLefflerCategorical (derivedReductionSectionsSystem X Λ I
      ((derivedCoefficientModuleSheafEquivalence.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ).functor.obj K))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isMittagLefflerCategorical_reductionSectionsSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C5**, for the inverse system over `n`, from the pro-domination data that the
source's steps (1)–(6) supply.

Let `X` be a weakly contractible affine scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring, `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal and `K`
a constructible object of `D(X_proét, Λ)` such that every reduction `K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ` is
isomorphic, in `D(X_proét, Λ/Iⁿ)`, to a complex of constant sheaves of `Λ/Iⁿ`-modules. Then the
inverse system `n ↦ H⁰(X, K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ)` of `Λ`-modules satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition.

The conclusion is the Mittag-Leffler condition of Stacks Tag 02N0 for the system indexed by
`n`, not a statement about any single `n`, and it is stated about the concrete system
`reductionSectionsSystem X Λ I Tn K t` whose terms are the sections modules
`H⁰(X, K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/Iⁿ)` themselves.

The setting hypotheses `_hX`, `_hK` and `_hconstant` are not used in the proof: pro-domination
of the sections system by an adic quotient system already forces the Mittag-Leffler condition,
without weak contractibility of `X` and without constructibility of `K`. They are retained,
underscore-prefixed, so that the statement reads as the source's; the result is therefore more
general than the source, which this charter permits.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMittagLefflerCategorical_reductionSectionsSystem [IsAffine X]
    (_hX : ProetaleWContractible.IsWeaklyContractibleObj X)
    (T : DerivedReduction.{u, r, w} X Λ I)
    (D : ∀ U : (constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, r, w} X (Λ ⧸ I)).C,
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.{u + 1, u, max (u + 1) r w,
          max (u + 1) r w + 1}
        ((constantCoefficientRingedSite.{u, r, w} X (Λ ⧸ I)).over U))
    (K : DerivedSheaves.{u, r, w} X Λ)
    (_hK : IsConstructibleDerivedSheaf.{u, r, w} X Λ I T D K)
    (Tn : ∀ n : ℕ, DerivedReduction.{u, r, w} X Λ (I ^ n))
    (_hconstant : ∀ n : ℕ, IsConstantSheafComplexModel.{u, r, w} X (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)
      ((Tn n).baseChange.obj K))
    (t : ∀ n : ℕ, reductionSectionsObj.{u, r, w} X Λ I Tn K (n + 1) ⟶
      reductionSectionsObj.{u, r, w} X Λ I Tn K n)
    (N : ModuleCat.{max (u + 1) r w} Λ) (c : ℕ)
    (β : ∀ n : ℕ, (adicQuotientModuleSystem Λ I N).obj (op (n + c)) ⟶
      (reductionSectionsSystem.{u, r, w} X Λ I Tn K t).obj (op n))
    (hβ : ∀ (i j : ℕ) (h : i ≤ j),
      (adicQuotientModuleSystem Λ I N).map (homOfLE (Nat.add_le_add_right h c)).op ≫ β i =
        β j ≫ (reductionSectionsSystem.{u, r, w} X Λ I Tn K t).map (homOfLE h).op)
    (α : ∀ n : ℕ, (reductionSectionsSystem.{u, r, w} X Λ I Tn K t).obj (op (n + c)) ⟶
      (adicQuotientModuleSystem Λ I N).obj (op n))
    (hαβ : ∀ n : ℕ, α (n + c) ≫ β n =
      (reductionSectionsSystem.{u, r, w} X Λ I Tn K t).map
        (homOfLE (show n ≤ n + c + c by omega)).op) :
    IsMittagLefflerCategorical (reductionSectionsSystem.{u, r, w} X Λ I Tn K t)
declarations.comment: the Mittag-Leffler conclusion for the INVERSE SYSTEM over n, stated about the concrete system of sections modules H^0(X, K ⊗_Λ^L Λ/I^n) and proved from the pro-domination of that system by the adic quotient system n ↦ N/I^nN of a Λ-module N. Two things are assumed rather than proved. First, the transition maps of the system are taken as a datum t: the source's are those induced by Λ/I^(n+1) → Λ/I^n, and the comparison of the derived base changes along Λ → Λ/I^(n+1) → Λ/I^n and along Λ → Λ/I^n is not constructed in the library, so the statement is proved for every family t. Second, the pro-domination itself is the output of the source's steps (1)-(6): steps (1)-(5) rest on 09C3 (the local adic model, also not formalized), 0658 (perfectness of the reduction E_1), 09BE (local constancy of a map of complexes of constant sheaves) and 09AW (the complex M^• of finite projective Λ^∧-modules with M^•/I^nM^• ≅ E_n), and step (6) on the Tor spectral sequence together with 0911 (strict pro-vanishing of Tor); that chain is not assembled. What is proved outright is the Mittag-Leffler condition for the sections system from that data, including the surjectivity of the transition maps of the adic quotient system. The source's weak contractibility of X and constructibility of K are not needed for this implication and are carried unused

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isAdicLisseDerivedSheaf_of_isLocallyConstant
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a connected scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring and `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal. If `K` is in
`D_cons(X, Λ)` and `K ⊗_Λ^L \underline{Λ/I}` has locally constant cohomology sheaves, then `K` is
adic lisse.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdicLisseDerivedSheaf_of_isLocallyConstant [ConnectedSpace X] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    {K : DerivedSheaves.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ}
    (hK : IsConstructibleViaDerivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ I K)
    (hloc : ∀ i : ℤ, Stacks.ConstantSheaf.IsLocallyConstant (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj ((derivedReduction.{u, w} X Λ I).obj K))) :
    IsAdicLisseDerivedSheaf.{u, max (u + 1) w, w} X Λ I K
declarations.comment: a constructible complex over a connected scheme whose reduction modulo I has locally constant cohomology sheaves is adic lisse

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isAdicConstructibleDerivedSheaf_of_isConstructibleDerivedSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C7.** Let `X` be a Noetherian scheme, `Λ` a Noetherian ring and `I ⊆ Λ` an
ideal. Every object `K` of `D_cons(X, Λ)` is adic constructible.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.isIso_proetaleCompletedBaseChangeMap_of_isProper
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09C9 (proper base change for derived complete complexes).** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a
proper morphism of schemes and `g : Y' ⟶ Y` a morphism, with base change square
`sq : IsPullback g' f' f g`. Let `Λ` be a Noetherian ring and `I ⊆ Λ` an ideal such that `Λ/I` is
torsion. Let `K` be an object of `D(X_proétale, Λ)` such that
1. `K` is derived complete,
2. `K ⊗^L_Λ Λ/Iⁿ` is bounded below with cohomology sheaves coming from `X_étale`, and
3. `Λ/Iⁿ` is a perfect `Λ`-module,
for every `n ≥ 1`. Then the base change map `Lg^*_comp Rf_* K ⟶ Rf'_* L(g')^*_comp K` is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_proetaleCompletedBaseChangeMap_of_isProper [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (I : Ideal Λ)
    (hI : AddMonoid.IsTorsion (Λ ⧸ I))
    {X Y X' Y' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsProper f] (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (g' : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ Y')
    (sq : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (K : ProetaleDerivedCategory Λ X) (hK : IsDerivedComplete I K)
    (hbdd : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ a : ℤ, ((proetaleDerivedReduction Λ I X n).obj K).IsGE a)
    (het : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∀ q : ℤ, (Scheme.etaleInverseImage.{u, 0, u + 1} X Λ).essImage
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ q).obj ((proetaleDerivedReduction Λ I X n).obj K)))
    (hperf : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfectModule (R := Λ) (Λ ⧸ I ^ n)) :
    IsIso (proetaleCompletedBaseChangeMap Λ I f g f' g' sq.w.symm K)

declarations.name: Ideal.hilbertPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CA.** The *Hilbert polynomial* of an `R`-module `M` relative to an ideal `I ⊆ R`:
the polynomial `P ∈ ℚ[t]` such that `P(n) = φ_{I,M}(n) = length_R (I ^ n M / I ^ (n + 1) M)` for
all `n ≫ 0`. At most one polynomial has this property, so this is a definition of that element;
the value is `0` in the case that none has it. For `R` Noetherian local, `M` finite and `I` an
ideal of definition — in particular for `I = m`, the Hilbert polynomial of `M` over `R` — such a
`P` exists by Proposition 00K8.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def Ideal.hilbertPolynomial {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R)
    (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] : ℚ[X]
declarations.comment:
Stated relative to an ideal `I ⊆ R`, as the rest of the section is (Tags 00K8, 00K9,
00KA); the Hilbert polynomial of Definition 09CA is the case `I = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R`, for
`R` Noetherian local and `M` finite, where Proposition 00K8 makes the characterising property
satisfiable. The property is what the definition consumes, and it determines the polynomial
uniquely; the value is `0` where nothing has it.

declarations.name: AlgCat.face_eq_lift_and_degeneracy_eq_lift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CB**.
Let `A` be a ring and let `X` be an `A`-algebra. In the tower `Xₙ = A[A[⋯[X]⋯]]` (`n + 1` brackets)
of the standard resolution of `X` for the free/forget adjunction, each stage being the free algebra
on the previous one, the faces `dⁿⱼ` and degeneracies `sⁿⱼ` are described on the variables by:
`dⁿ₀` substitutes for the variable `[z]` the element `z`, so it is `FreeAlgebra.lift A id` and
`d⁰₀ : A[X] ⟶ X` is the augmentation; `sⁿ₀` sends `[z]` to `[[z]]`; and `dⁿ⁺¹ⱼ₊₁`, `sⁿ⁺¹ⱼ₊₁` send
`[z]` to `[dⁿⱼ(z)]`, resp. `[sⁿⱼ(z)]`. In degree `1`, for
`x = ∑ a_k [b_{k,1}] ⋯ [b_{k,n_k}] ∈ A[X]`, this is `d₀([x]) = x`,
`d₁([x]) = [∑ a_k b_{k,1} ⋯ b_{k,n_k}]`, `s₀([x]) = [[x]]` and
`s₁([x]) = [∑ a_k [[b_{k,1}]] ⋯ [[b_{k,n_k}]]]`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem face_eq_lift_and_degeneracy_eq_lift {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (X : AlgCat.{u} A)
    (n : ℕ) :
    ((Godement.face (adj (R := A)).toComonad.ε n 0).app X).hom = FreeAlgebra.lift A id ∧
      (∀ j : Fin (n + 1), ((Godement.face (adj (R := A)).toComonad.ε (n + 1) j.succ).app X).hom =
        FreeAlgebra.lift A (FreeAlgebra.ι A ∘
          ((Godement.face (adj (R := A)).toComonad.ε n j).app X).hom)) ∧
      ((Godement.degeneracy (adj (R := A)).toComonad.δ n 0).app X).hom =
        FreeAlgebra.lift A (fun z => FreeAlgebra.ι A (FreeAlgebra.ι A z)) ∧
      (∀ j : Fin (n + 1),
        ((Godement.degeneracy (adj (R := A)).toComonad.δ (n + 1) j.succ).app X).hom =
          FreeAlgebra.lift A (FreeAlgebra.ι A ∘
            ((Godement.degeneracy (adj (R := A)).toComonad.δ n j).app X).hom))

declarations.name: Koszul.regular_koszulRegular_h1Regular_quasiRegular_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CC.** Let `M` be a nonzero finite module over a local Noetherian ring `R`, and
let `f` be a finite sequence in the maximal ideal. Being `M`-regular, `M`-Koszul-regular,
`M`-`H₁`-regular, and `M`-quasi-regular are equivalent. In particular, the corresponding
four notions for the sequence in `R` are equivalent.
declarations.statement:
public theorem regular_koszulRegular_h1Regular_quasiRegular_tfae
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Nontrivial M] [Module.Finite R M]
    {r : ℕ} (f : Fin r → R) (hf : ∀ i, f i ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) :
    List.TFAE
        [RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular M (List.ofFn f),
          Koszul.IsKoszulRegularOn f M,
          Koszul.IsH1RegularOn f M,
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular M (List.ofFn f)] ∧
      List.TFAE
        [RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R (List.ofFn f),
          Koszul.IsKoszulRegular f,
          Koszul.IsH1Regular f,
          RingTheory.Sequence.IsQuasiRegular R (List.ofFn f)]

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.lichtenbaumSchlessingerComplex
declarations.doc:
The Lichtenbaum–Schlessinger complex associated to a polynomial presentation and chosen
generators of its defining ideal.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lichtenbaumSchlessingerComplex
    (P : Algebra.Presentation A B X T) : LichtenbaumSchlessingerComplex P

declarations.name: Biderivation
declarations.doc:
An `A`-biderivation from an `A`-algebra `B` to a `(B, B)`-bimodule `M` is
an `A`-linear map satisfying the Leibniz rule for the left and right actions.
declarations.statement:
structure Biderivation (A : Type u) (B : Type v) (M : Type w)
    [CommSemiring A] [Semiring B] [AddCommMonoid M] [Algebra A B]
    [Module A M] [Module B M] [Module Bᵐᵒᵖ M]
    [IsScalarTower A B M] [IsScalarTower A Bᵐᵒᵖ M]
    [SMulCommClass B Bᵐᵒᵖ M]
    extends B →ₗ[A] M

declarations.name: Biderivation.IsCompatibleOnVars
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CF.** The equations that commutativity of the polynomial variables forces on the
values of a biderivation of `A[S]`: the Leibniz rule applied to the two readings of
`X s * X t = X t * X s`. For a bimodule whose two actions agree they hold automatically.

The source imposes no such condition; that omission is a Stacks erratum, and these equations
really can fail, as
`Biderivation.not_isCompatibleOnVars_erratumValues` shows for the counterexample of
`StacksFrontier.Cotangent.BiderivationErratum`.
declarations.statement:
def IsCompatibleOnVars (A : Type u) {S : Type v} {M : Type w} [CommSemiring A]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module (MvPolynomial S A) M] [Module (MvPolynomial S A)ᵐᵒᵖ M]
    (m : S → M) : Prop
declarations.comment: the compatibility equations the values on the variables must satisfy

declarations.name: Biderivation.existsUnique_mvPolynomial
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CF.** Let `P = A[S]` be a polynomial ring over `A` and let `M` be a `(P, P)`
bimodule over `A`. Given `m s ∈ M` for `s ∈ S` satisfying the compatibility equations that
commutativity of the variables forces, there is a unique `A`-biderivation `P → M` sending
`X s` to `m s`.

This is the corrected form of the tag. The source prescribes the values `m s` with no condition
at all, and the existence half of that unrestricted claim is false: it is a Stacks erratum,
refuted by `Biderivation.not_exists_biderivation_erratum` in
`StacksFrontier.Cotangent.BiderivationErratum`, which exhibits `k[x, y]` acting on `k` by
evaluation at `(1, 0)` on the left and at `(0, 0)` on the right and prescribed values `0` and
`1` admitting no biderivation. Uniqueness is unaffected, and by
`Biderivation.existsUnique_mvPolynomial_iff` the compatibility hypothesis below is not merely
sufficient but exactly the obstruction.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_mvPolynomial (m : S → M) (hcomm : IsCompatibleOnVars A m) :
    ∃! D : Biderivation A (MvPolynomial S A) M, ∀ s, D (X s) = m s
declarations.comment: existence and uniqueness of the biderivation with prescribed values

declarations.name: Biderivation.existsUnique_mvPolynomial_of_op_smul_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CF**, in the case the source applies it: when the two actions of the polynomial
ring on `M` agree, the compatibility equations hold for every family of prescribed values, and
the source's unrestricted assertion is recovered.

This hypothesis cannot be dropped: stated for an arbitrary bimodule the source's assertion is a
Stacks erratum, refuted by
`Biderivation.not_forall_existsUnique_mvPolynomial_erratumModule` in
`StacksFrontier.Cotangent.BiderivationErratum`, whose bimodule is a copy of `k` carrying the two
different actions evaluation at `(1, 0)` and evaluation at `(0, 0)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_mvPolynomial_of_op_smul_eq
    (h : ∀ (q : MvPolynomial S A) (x : M), MulOpposite.op q • x = q • x) (m : S → M) :
    ∃! D : Biderivation A (MvPolynomial S A) M, ∀ s, D (X s) = m s
declarations.comment: the unrestricted assertion of the source, for a bimodule whose two actions agree

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.cotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CG.** The canonical map `L_{B/A} → L` in `D(B)` attached to a chain-level
comparison: its image under the localization functor.
declarations.comment:
the canonical map L_{B/A} → L in D(B), attached to a chain-level comparison
carried as the explicit datum Algebra.Presentation.LichtenbaumSchlessingerComparison

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.truncGECotangentIsoLichtenbaumSchlessinger
declarations.doc: **Stacks 09CG.** The isomorphism `τ_{≥ -2} L_{B/A} ≅ L` induced by the canonical map.
declarations.statement:
public def truncGECotangentIsoLichtenbaumSchlessinger
    (c : LichtenbaumSchlessingerComparison P) :
    (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (-2)).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplexULift.{u, v, w} A B)) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (lichtenbaumSchlessingerComplex P).complex
declarations.comment: the induced map τ_{≥ -2} L_{B/A} → L is an isomorphism in D(B)

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.truncGECotangentIsoLichtenbaumSchlessinger_fac
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CG.** The isomorphism `τ_{≥ -2} L_{B/A} ≅ L` is the one induced by the canonical
map `L_{B/A} → L`: composing it with the projection to the truncation returns that map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem truncGECotangentIsoLichtenbaumSchlessinger_fac
    (c : LichtenbaumSchlessingerComparison P) :
    (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-2)).app
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplexULift.{u, v, w} A B)) ≫
      (truncGECotangentIsoLichtenbaumSchlessinger c).hom =
        cotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger c
declarations.comment: the isomorphism τ_{≥ -2} L_{B/A} → L is induced by the canonical map L_{B/A} → L

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.LichtenbaumSchlessingerComparison.canonical
declarations.doc:
The chain-level comparison of a presentation constructed in the source: the map of complexes
`Algebra.Presentation.lsChainMap`, which is `dψ ⊗ 1`, `λ̄` and `q` in degrees `0`, `-1` and `-2`,
together with its isomorphisms on `H⁰`, `H^{-1}` and `H^{-2}`.
declarations.statement: public def LichtenbaumSchlessingerComparison.canonical : LichtenbaumSchlessingerComparison P
declarations.comment:
the map of complexes L_{B/A} → L built from the choices ψ and λ of the source,
with its isomorphisms on H^0 (Remark 08UP, Lemma 08RB), H^{-1} (idem) and H^{-2} (Remark 09D6)

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `L_{B/A} → L` in `D(B)`: the image under the localization functor of the
map of complexes `Algebra.Presentation.lsChainMap`. It does not depend on the choices `ψ` and
`λ`: `Algebra.Presentation.Q_map_eq_canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger`.
declarations.comment:
the canonical map L_{B/A} → L in D(B), the class of the map of complexes
dψ ⊗ 1, λ̄, q built from the choices ψ : P₀ → P and the biderivation λ of the source

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.isIso_descTruncGE_canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger
declarations.doc:
The canonical map `L_{B/A} → L` factors through the truncation `τ_{≥ -2} L_{B/A}`, and the
factorization is an isomorphism.
declarations.comment:
the canonical map L_{B/A} → L induces an isomorphism τ_{≥ -2} L_{B/A} → L in
D(B)

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.canonicalTruncGECotangentIsoLichtenbaumSchlessinger
declarations.doc: The isomorphism `τ_{≥ -2} L_{B/A} ≅ L` induced by the canonical map.
declarations.statement:
public def canonicalTruncGECotangentIsoLichtenbaumSchlessinger :
    (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE (-2)).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplexULift.{u, v, w} A B)) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj (lichtenbaumSchlessingerComplex P).complex
declarations.comment: the induced map τ_{≥ -2} L_{B/A} → L is an isomorphism in D(B)

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.canonicalTruncGECotangentIsoLichtenbaumSchlessinger_fac
declarations.doc:
The isomorphism `τ_{≥ -2} L_{B/A} ≅ L` is the one induced by the canonical map
`L_{B/A} → L`: composing it with the projection to the truncation returns that map.
declarations.statement:
public theorem canonicalTruncGECotangentIsoLichtenbaumSchlessinger_fac :
    (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGEπ (-2)).app
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplexULift.{u, v, w} A B)) ≫
      (canonicalTruncGECotangentIsoLichtenbaumSchlessinger P).hom =
        canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger P
declarations.comment: the isomorphism τ_{≥ -2} L_{B/A} → L is induced by the canonical map L_{B/A} → L

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.Q_map_eq_canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger
declarations.doc:
**Independence of the choices.** Every map of complexes `L_{B/A} → L` given by the formulas
`dψ ⊗ 1`, `λ̄`, `q` of the source, for any permissible choice of `ψ : P₀ → P` and of the
biderivation `λ : P₁ → F/TrivRel`, represents the canonical map
`Algebra.Presentation.canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger` in `D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem Q_map_eq_canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger (c : LichtenbaumSchlessingerChoice P)
    (f : cotangentComplexULift.{u, v, w} A B ⟶ (lichtenbaumSchlessingerComplex P).complex)
    (hf : IsLichtenbaumSchlessingerComparison P c f) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.map f = canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger P
declarations.comment:
the formulas dψ ⊗ 1, λ̄, q specify the comparison for every permissible choice of
ψ and λ, and changing these choices gives the same morphism in D(B)

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `M` and `N` be `S`-modules, and let `k : ℕ`.
`D.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S k` says that the `R`-linear map `D : M → N` is a
*differential operator of order at most `k`* relative to `R → S`. By induction on `k`: order at
most `0` means `S`-linear, and order at most `k + 1` means that for every `g : S` the commutator
`m ↦ D (g • m) - g • D m` is a differential operator of order at most `k`.
declarations.statement:
public def IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE (S : Type*) [Semiring S] [Algebra R S] [Module S M]
    [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N] : ℕ → (M →ₗ[R] N) → Prop
declarations.comment:
The source's `k` bounds the order: `Diff⁰ ⊆ Diff¹ ⊆ …`, whence `LE` in the name.
The commutator `m ↦ D (g • m) - g • D m` is the difference of the two composites of `D` with
`Algebra.lsmul R R _ g`, multiplication by `g`. The `S`-module `Diffᵏ_{S/R}(M, N)` of the
paragraph following the definition is a separate statement. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: isDiffOpOfOrder_comp
declarations.doc:
The composition of a differential operator of order `k` with one of order `k'` is a
differential operator of order `k + k'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDiffOpOfOrder_comp
    {L : Type*} [AddCommGroup L] [Module S L] [Module R L] [IsScalarTower R S L]
    (k k' : ℕ) (D : L →ₗ[R] M) (D' : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (hD : IsDiffOpOfOrder S k D) (hD' : IsDiffOpOfOrder S k' D') :
    IsDiffOpOfOrder S (k + k') (D'.comp D)

declarations.name: LinearMap.exists_universal_isDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CK.** Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `M` be an `S`-module and let `k : ℕ`. There
exist an `S`-module `P` and a differential operator `D_univ : M → P` of order at most `k`
relative to `R → S` such that, for every `S`-module `N`, precomposition with `D_univ` is a
bijection from the `S`-linear maps `P → N` onto the differential operators `M → N` of order at
most `k`. Thus `P = Pᵏ_{S/R}(M)` represents `Diffᵏ_{S/R}(M, -)`, functorially in `N`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_universal_isDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE (k : ℕ) :
    ∃ (P : Type (max v w)) (_ : AddCommGroup P) (_ : Module R P) (_ : Module S P)
      (_ : IsScalarTower R S P) (Duniv : M →ₗ[R] P),
      Duniv.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S k ∧
        ∀ (N : Type x) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N] [IsScalarTower R S N],
          Function.Injective (fun α : P →ₗ[S] N => α.restrictScalars R ∘ₗ Duniv) ∧
            Set.range (fun α : P →ₗ[S] N => α.restrictScalars R ∘ₗ Duniv) =
              {D : M →ₗ[R] N | D.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S k}
declarations.comment:
Stated in the universal-object form of the paragraph following the lemma: the
isomorphism `Diffᵏ_{S/R}(M, N) = Hom_S(Pᵏ_{S/R}(M), N)` is the map `α ↦ α ∘ D_univ`, so the
universal operator is pinned and functoriality in `N` is automatic. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE
declarations.doc:
Let `R → S` be a ring map, let `M` be an `S`-module and let `k : ℕ`. For an
`R`-linear map `D : M → P` into an `S`-module `P`, the property
`D.IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S k` says that `D` is a differential operator of order
at most `k` relative to `R → S` and that every differential operator `E : M → N` of order at most
`k` into an `S`-module factors as `E = α ∘ D` for a unique `S`-linear map `α : P → N`. Equivalently
`α ↦ α ∘ D` is the canonical isomorphism `Hom_S(P, N) = Diffᵏ_{S/R}(M, N)` of Lemma 09CK: that is,
`P` is a *module of principal parts of order `k`* of `M`, written `Pᵏ_{S/R}(M)`, and `D` is its
universal differential operator. Such a pair is unique up to unique isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
public def IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE (S : Type v) [Semiring S] [Algebra R S]
    [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M] [Module S P] [IsScalarTower R S P] (k : ℕ)
    (D : M →ₗ[R] P) : Prop
declarations.comment:
The source names the module `Pᵏ_{S/R}(M)` it has just constructed; defined here is
the property of a pair `(P, D)` of being one, which determines it up to unique isomorphism and so
applies to every construction. Existence of such a pair is Lemma 09CK. See the module docstring.

declarations.name: diff1EquivDerProd
declarations.doc:
The `S`-module isomorphism `Diff¹(S, N) ≃ₗ[S] Der_R(S, N) × N` given by `D ↦ (σ_D, D 1)`, where
`σ_D g = D g - g · D 1`, with inverse `(σ, x) ↦ σ + λ_x`.
declarations.statement: def diff1EquivDerProd : Diff1 R S N ≃ₗ[S] (Derivation R S N × N)

declarations.name: LinearMap.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE.exists_shortExact_principalParts
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CN.** Let `R → S` be a ring map and let `M` be an `S`-module. Let `D : M → P` be a
universal differential operator of order at most `1` on `M`, i.e. `D` has order at most `1` and
every order-`≤ 1` operator out of `M` factors uniquely through `D` by an `S`-linear map, so that
`P` is a module of principal parts `P¹_{S/R}(M)`. Then there is a short exact sequence
`0 → Ω[S⁄R] ⊗[S] M → P → M → 0`, the *sequence of principal parts*, whose first map sends
`d b ⊗ₜ m` to `D (b • m) - b • D m` and whose second map is the retraction of `D`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_shortExact_principalParts {R : Type*} {S : Type u} {M : Type v} {P : Type w}
    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module S M] [IsScalarTower R S M]
    [AddCommGroup P] [Module R P] [Module S P] [IsScalarTower R S P]
    (D : M →ₗ[R] P) (hD : D.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S 1)
    (huniv : ∀ (N : Type (max u v w)) [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module S N]
      [IsScalarTower R S N] (E : M →ₗ[R] N), E.IsDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE S 1 →
      ∃! α : P →ₗ[S] N, ∀ m : M, α (D m) = E m) :
    ∃ (ι : Ω[S⁄R] ⊗[S] M →ₗ[S] P) (π : P →ₗ[S] M),
      (∀ (b : S) (m : M), ι (KaehlerDifferential.D R S b ⊗ₜ[S] m) = D (b • m) - b • D m) ∧
      (∀ m : M, π (D m) = m) ∧
      Function.Injective ι ∧ Function.Exact ι π ∧ Function.Surjective π
declarations.comment:
Stated for an arbitrary universal order-≤ 1 differential operator `D : M → P` rather
than for a chosen construction of `P¹_{S/R}(M)`, whose existence is Lemma 09CK; both maps of the
sequence are pinned by equations, from which functoriality in `M` is formal. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: DiffOp.isGlobalDiffOpOfOrder_comp
declarations.doc:
The composition of a differential operator of order `k` with a differential operator
of order `k'` is a differential operator of order `k + k'`.

The argument: `IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder` is `∀ U, IsDiffOpOfOrder` on `restrict`; by
`GlobalOp.restrict_comp` the restriction of the composite is the raw composite of the
restrictions; then apply the raw composition lemma `isDiffOpOfOrder_comp_raw`
(strong induction on `k + k'` via the commutator-of-composition identity).
declarations.statement:
theorem isGlobalDiffOpOfOrder_comp (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    {E F G : SheafOfModules O₂} {k k' : ℕ}
    (D : GlobalOp E F) (D' : GlobalOp F G)
    (hD : IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder φ k D) (hD' : IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder φ k' D') :
    IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder φ (k + k') (D'.comp D)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.existsUnique_descDiffOp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CT**, in unique-factorization form: every differential operator of order at
most `k` out of `F` factors through the universal one by a unique morphism of sheaves of
modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsUnique_descDiffOp
    (F G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} O₂) (k : ℕ)
    (D : DiffOp.GlobalOp F G) (hD : DiffOp.IsGlobalDiffOpOfOrder phi k D) :
    ∃! f : moduleOfPrincipalParts.{v, u, w, m} phi F k ⟶ G,
      postcomp (universalDiffOp.{v, u, w, m} phi F k) f = D

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.differentialOperatorsFunctor_isCorepresentable
declarations.doc:
Differential operators of order at most `k` out of a fixed module sheaf are
represented by a sheaf of modules (the sheaf of principal parts).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance differentialOperatorsFunctor_isCorepresentable (phi : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} O₂) (k : ℕ) :
    (differentialOperatorsFunctor.{v, u, w, m} phi F k).IsCorepresentable

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.moduleOfPrincipalParts
declarations.doc:
The sheaf of principal parts `Pᵏ_{O₂/O₁}(F)`: the sheaf of modules corepresenting the
functor of differential operators of order at most `k` out of `F`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev moduleOfPrincipalParts
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} O₂) (k : ℕ) :
    _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} O₂
declarations.comment: the module of principal parts of order k

declarations.name: Stacks.Sheaves.PrincipalParts.principalPartsSheafification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 0G3U**, which read as a statement about the sheaf of principal parts
is **Tag 09CV**. Let `φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂` be a morphism of presheaves of
commutative rings on a site and let `F` be a presheaf of `O₂`-modules. Then the sheaf of
principal parts of order `k` of `F^#` relative to `O₂^# / O₁^#` is the sheaf associated to
the presheaf `X ↦ Pᵏ_{O₂(X)/O₁(X)}(F X)` of sectionwise modules of principal parts, and the
sectionwise universal operators are compatible with restriction.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def principalPartsSheafification [HasWeakSheafify J CommRingCat.{u}]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective CommRingCat.{u}]
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})]
    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max u u₁ v₁ v}]
    [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max u u₁ v₁ v}] {O₁ O₂ : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}}
    (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂)
    (F : PresheafOfModules.{max u u₁ v₁ v} (O₂ ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}))
    (k : ℕ) :
    Σ' P : PresheafOfModules.{max u u₁ v₁ v}
        (O₂ ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u}),
      Σ' D : F.presheaf ⟶ P.presheaf,
        Σ' _e : (AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.differentialOperatorsFunctor.{v₁, u₁, u,
            max u u₁ v₁ v}
            ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map
              (associatedCommRingSheafMap J φ))
            ((PresheafOfModules.sheafification (toAssociatedRingSheaf J O₂)).obj F)
            k).coreprX (hF :=
              AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.differentialOperatorsFunctor_isCorepresentable
                ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map
                  (associatedCommRingSheafMap J φ))
                ((PresheafOfModules.sheafification (toAssociatedRingSheaf J O₂)).obj F) k) ≅
          (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (toAssociatedRingSheaf J O₂)).obj P,
        ∀ X : Cᵒᵖ,
          letI : Algebra (O₁.obj X) (O₂.obj X) := (φ.app X).hom.toAlgebra
          letI : Module (O₁.obj X) (F.obj X) :=
            Module.compHom (F.obj X) (φ.app X).hom
          letI : Module (O₁.obj X) (P.obj X) :=
            Module.compHom (P.obj X) (φ.app X).hom
          letI : IsScalarTower (O₁.obj X) (O₂.obj X) (F.obj X) :=
            IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ ↦ rfl
          letI : IsScalarTower (O₁.obj X) (O₂.obj X) (P.obj X) :=
            IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ ↦ rfl
          ∃ d : F.obj X →ₗ[O₁.obj X] P.obj X,
            (∀ x, d x = (D.app X).hom x) ∧
              d.IsUniversalDifferentialOperatorOfOrderLE (O₂.obj X) k

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.exists_shortExact_principalPartsSequence'
declarations.doc: **The sequence of principal parts is a short exact sequence.**
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_principalPartsSequence' :
    ∃ h : (principalPartsInclusion.{v, u, w, m} φ).app F ≫
        (principalPartsProjection.{v, u, w, m}
          (underlyingRingSheafMapOfSite φ) 1).app F = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk ((principalPartsInclusion.{v, u, w, m} φ).app F)
        ((principalPartsProjection.{v, u, w, m}
          (underlyingRingSheafMapOfSite φ) 1).app F) h).ShortExact
declarations.comment: field 8 ALONE: the short exact sequence of the principal-parts sequence, now

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.principalPartsSequence_nonempty
declarations.doc: The functorial short exact sequence of first principal parts exists.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalPartsSequence_nonempty (O₁ O₂ : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
    (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂) : Nonempty (PrincipalPartsSequence.{v, u, w, m} O₁ O₂ φ)
declarations.comment: the tag's OWN assertion: a functorial first-principal-parts sequence exists, i.e. the eight-field record is inhabited. The individual clauses of field 8 are carried separately in `PrincipalPartsJet.lean` and `PrincipalPartsSequence.lean`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.principalPartsMapOfSquare
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CX.** The map on order-`k` principal parts induced by a commutative square of
sheaves of rings together with a compatible linear map of module sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def principalPartsMapOfSquare
    (φ : A ⟶ B) (φ' : A' ⟶ B') (α : A ⟶ A') (β : B ⟶ B')
    (h : φ ≫ β = α ≫ φ')
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} B)
    (F' : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} B')
    (uF : F ⟶ (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m} β).obj F')
    (k : ℕ) :
    moduleOfPrincipalParts.{v, u, w, m} φ F k ⟶
      (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m} β).obj
        (moduleOfPrincipalParts.{v, u, w, m} φ' F' k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.principalPartsMapOfSquare_universalOperator
declarations.doc:
The induced map sends each universal local generator to the generator associated to its
image under the module map.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalPartsMapOfSquare_universalOperator (k : ℕ) (X : Cᵒᵖ) (s : F.val.obj X) :
    ((principalPartsMapOfSquare φ φ' α β h F F' uF k).val.app X).hom
      ((differentialOperatorsFunctor.{v, u, w, m} φ F k).coreprx.1 X s) =
      (differentialOperatorsFunctor.{v, u, w, m} φ' F' k).coreprx.1 X
        ((uF.val.app X).hom s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.principalPartsMapOfSquare_comp_orderReduction
declarations.doc: The induced maps commute with the canonical maps reducing the order from `k + 1` to `k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalPartsMapOfSquare_comp_orderReduction (k : ℕ) :
    principalPartsOrderReduction.{v, u, w, m} φ F k ≫
        principalPartsMapOfSquare φ φ' α β h F F' uF k =
      principalPartsMapOfSquare φ φ' α β h F F' uF (k + 1) ≫
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m} β).map
          (principalPartsOrderReduction.{v, u, w, m} φ' F' k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.principalPartsMapOfSquare_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CX.** The map on principal parts associated to two successive compatible squares
is the composite of their maps on principal parts.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalPartsMapOfSquare_comp
    (φ : A ⟶ B) (φ' : A' ⟶ B') (φ'' : A'' ⟶ B'')
    (α : A ⟶ A') (β : B ⟶ B')
    (α' : A' ⟶ A'') (β' : B' ⟶ B'')
    (h : φ ≫ β = α ≫ φ') (h' : φ' ≫ β' = α' ≫ φ'')
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} B)
    (F' : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} B')
    (F'' : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} B'')
    (uF : F ⟶ (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m} β).obj F')
    (uF' : F' ⟶ (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m} β').obj F'')
    (k : ℕ) :
    principalPartsMapOfSquare.{v, u, w, m} φ φ'' (α ≫ α') (β ≫ β')
        (by rw [← Category.assoc, h, Category.assoc, h', ← Category.assoc])
        F F'' (uF ≫ (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m} β).map uF') k =
      principalPartsMapOfSquare.{v, u, w, m} φ φ' α β h F F' uF k ≫
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m} β).map
          (principalPartsMapOfSquare.{v, u, w, m} φ' φ'' α' β' h' F' F'' uF' k)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.principalPartsSequence_naturality_projection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CX.** The change-of-rings maps on first principal parts are compatible with the
projections of the short exact sequences of Tag 09CW: the right-hand square of the naturality
diagram commutes, the comparison of its two right-hand terms being `uF`.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalPartsSequence_naturality_projection
    (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂) (φ' : O₁' ⟶ O₂') (α : O₁ ⟶ O₁') (β : O₂ ⟶ O₂')
    (hsq : φ ≫ β = α ≫ φ')
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O₂))
    (F' : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O₂'))
    (uF : F ⟶ (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m}
      (underlyingRingSheafMapOfSite β)).obj F') :
    principalPartsSquareMap.{v, u, w, m} φ φ' α β hsq F F' uF ≫
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m}
          (underlyingRingSheafMapOfSite β)).map
          ((principalPartsProjection.{v, u, w, m}
            (underlyingRingSheafMapOfSite φ') 1).app F') =
      (principalPartsProjection.{v, u, w, m}
        (underlyingRingSheafMapOfSite φ) 1).app F ≫ uF

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.principalPartsSequence_naturality_inclusion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CX.** The change-of-rings maps on first principal parts are compatible with the
inclusions of the short exact sequences of Tag 09CW: the left-hand square of the naturality
diagram commutes, with the tensor product of `uF` and the map on differentials on the left.
declarations.statement:
theorem principalPartsSequence_naturality_inclusion
    (φ : O₁ ⟶ O₂) (φ' : O₁' ⟶ O₂') (α : O₁ ⟶ O₁') (β : O₂ ⟶ O₂') (hsq : φ ≫ β = α ≫ φ')
    (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O₂))
    (F' : _root_.SheafOfModules.{max u v w m} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O₂'))
    (uF : F ⟶ (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m}
      (underlyingRingSheafMapOfSite β)).obj F') :
    (principalPartsInclusion.{v, u, w, m} φ).app F ≫
        principalPartsSquareMap.{v, u, w, m} φ φ' α β hsq F F' uF =
      differentialsTensorMap.{v, u, w, m} φ φ' α β hsq F F' uF ≫
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{max u v w m}
          (underlyingRingSheafMapOfSite β)).map
          ((principalPartsInclusion.{v, u, w, m} φ').app F')

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FibredCategory.FibredCategorySituation.toMorphismSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CY, the reduction.** The standing data of Stacks 08PA obtained from that of
Stacks 08P8: the same ringed base site, the target fibred category taken to be the base itself
fibred over itself by the identity functor, the source fibred category taken to be `C`, and the
1-morphism taken to be the structure functor `p`.
declarations.statement: def toMorphismSituation : MorphismSituation.{uD, uD, uC, vD, vD, vC, w}
declarations.comment: the reduction of Situation 08P8 to Situation 08PA, by `C = D` and `u = p`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FibredCategory.FibredCategorySituation.abelianInverseImage_toMorphismSituation
declarations.doc:
`g^{-1}` of the reduced situation is `π^{-1}`: both are restriction of abelian sheaves along
`p` between the same two sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianInverseImage_toMorphismSituation :
    HEq s.toMorphismSituation.abelianInverseImage s.abelianInverseImage
declarations.comment: the reduced situation's `g^{-1}` is the `π^{-1}` of Situation 08P8

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FibredCategory.FibredCategorySituation.abelianLowerShriek_toMorphismSituation
declarations.doc:
`g_!^{Ab}` of the reduced situation is `π_!^{Ab}`: both are the chosen left adjoint of
restriction of abelian sheaves along `p` between the same two sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem abelianLowerShriek_toMorphismSituation :
    HEq (@MorphismSituation.abelianLowerShriek.{uD, uD, uC, vD, vD, vC, w} s.toMorphismSituation
        s.hasWeakSheafifyToMorphismSituationTotalTopology) s.abelianLowerShriek
declarations.comment: the reduced situation's `g_!^{Ab}` is the `π_!^{Ab}` of Situation 08P8

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FibredCategory.FibredCategorySituation.derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunctionUnconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CY, the derived abelian `Lπ_!^{Ab}` of Situation 08P8.** Remark 09CY reduces
Situation 08P8 to Situation 08PA and reads off from Lemma 08PC the four functors `π_!`,
`π_!^{Ab}`, `Lπ_!` and `Lπ_!^{Ab}`. This is the third of them: `Lπ_!^{Ab} : D(Ab(C)) ⥤ D(Ab(D))`
is left adjoint to derived `π^{-1}`, which is part (3) of Stacks 08PC on abelian sheaves.

It is stated here rather than transported along the reduction because the acyclicity statement
of Stacks 07AC, which is what part (3) rests on, is discharged for `π` in this file, as
`abelianLowerShriekAcyclic`; the conditional form `derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunction` takes it
as an argument, and this is that argument supplied, so the adjunction holds under the hypotheses
of Situation 08P8 alone.
declarations.statement:
def derivedAbelianLowerShriekAdjunctionUnconditional :
    s.derivedAbelianLowerShriek ⊣ s.derivedAbelianInverseImage
declarations.comment: the derived abelian `Lπ_!^{Ab}` of Situation 08P8 and its adjunction `Lπ_!^{Ab} ⊣ π^{-1}`, with the acyclicity statement of Stacks 07AC discharged

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FibredCategory.FibredCategorySituation.derivedModuleLowerShriekAdjunctionAtBaseModuleRing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CY, the derived `Lπ_!` on sheaves of modules.** The unbounded left derived functor
`Lπ_! : D(O_C) ⥤ D(O_D)` of the lower-shriek functor on sheaves of modules exists and is left
adjoint to `π^* : D(O_D) ⥤ D(O_C)`. This is Stacks 08PC part (3) for modules in the situation of
the remark; the acyclicity statement of Stacks 07AC it rests on is `moduleLowerShriekAcyclic`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedModuleLowerShriekAdjunctionAtBaseModuleRing :
    s.derivedModuleLowerShriekAtBaseModuleRing ⊣ s.derivedModuleRestriction
declarations.comment: the derived `Lπ_!` of Situation 08P8 on sheaves of modules and its adjunction `Lπ_! ⊣ π^*`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FibredCategory.FibredCategorySituation.isIso_derivedModuleLowerShriekForgetComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CY, `forget ∘ Lπ_! = Lπ_!^{Ab} ∘ forget`.** The canonical comparison
`Lπ_!^{Ab} ∘ forget ⟶ forget ∘ Lπ_!` of Stacks 07AE is an isomorphism. This is Stacks 08PC
part (4) in the situation of the remark.
declarations.statement:
instance isIso_derivedModuleLowerShriekForgetComparison :
    IsIso s.derivedModuleLowerShriekForgetComparison
declarations.comment: `forget ∘ Lπ_! = Lπ_!^{Ab} ∘ forget`: the canonical comparison of Stacks 07AE is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FibredCategory.FibredCategorySituation.moduleLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CY, the module-level `π_!`.** The lower-shriek functor `π_!` on sheaves of modules
is left adjoint to `π^* = π⁻¹`, restriction of sheaves of modules along `p`.
declarations.statement: def moduleLowerShriekAdjunction : s.moduleLowerShriek ⊣ s.sheafModuleRestriction
declarations.comment: the module-level `π_!` of Situation 08P8 and its adjunction `π_! ⊣ π^*`

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.FibredCategory.FibredCategorySituation.isIso_moduleLowerShriekForgetComparison
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CY, `forget ∘ π_! = π_!^{Ab} ∘ forget`.** The canonical comparison
`π_!^{Ab} ∘ forget ⟶ forget ∘ π_!` of Stacks 0798 between lower shriek of abelian sheaves and
lower shriek of sheaves of modules, for the projection of a fibred category, is an isomorphism.

By the criterion of Stacks 0798 this reduces to the canonical maps
`(π_U)_!^{Ab} O_U ⟶ O_{p(U)}`, which are isomorphisms by
`isIso_localizedStructureSheafComparison_baseModuleRing`. This is Stacks 08PC part (2) in the
situation of the remark.
declarations.statement:
instance isIso_moduleLowerShriekForgetComparison :
    IsIso s.moduleLowerShriekForgetComparison
declarations.comment: `forget ∘ π_! = π_!^{Ab} ∘ forget`: the canonical comparison of Stacks 0798 is an isomorphism

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficients
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CZ.** For a map `φ : O ⟶ B̲` from a sheaf of rings on a chaotic site to the
constant sheaf of rings of a ring `B`, derived lower shriek with coefficients in `O` is the
functor `Lπ_! : D(O) ⟶ D(B)` obtained by composing derived extension of scalars
`- ⊗^L_O B̲` with derived lower shriek `D(B̲) ⟶ D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedColimitWithCoefficients :
    DerivedCategory (PresheafOfModules.{u} O) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B)

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficients_commShift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CZ**: derived lower shriek with coefficients commutes with the shift, being a
left adjoint of a functor that does.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedColimitWithCoefficients_commShift :
    (derivedColimitWithCoefficients B O φ).CommShift ℤ

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficients_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CZ**: derived lower shriek with coefficients is an exact functor of triangulated
categories `D(O) ⟶ D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedColimitWithCoefficients_isTriangulated :
    (derivedColimitWithCoefficients B O φ).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficientsForgetNatIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09CZ: the `B`-module structure on `Lπ_!(K)`.** Let `C` and `B` be as in Example
08PF, let `U_•` be a cosimplicial object of `C` which is a point resolution (Lemma 08Q9), and let
`φ : O ⟶ B̲` be a map to the constant sheaf of rings which induces an isomorphism
`Lπ_!O ⟶ Lπ_!B̲`. Then derived lower shriek with coefficients in `O` on underlying abelian
sheaves is derived lower shriek with coefficients in `B`, read on underlying abelian groups:

`Lπ^{Ab}_!(K) ≅ Lπ_!(K)` in `D(Ab)`, naturally in `K ∈ D(Mod(O))`,

where the right-hand side is `Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficients`, the functor
`D(O) ⟶ D(B)` of the tag. This is the remark's closing assertion, that `Lπ_!(K)` carries a
`B`-module structure "coming from the (canonical, functorial) identification of `Lπ_!(K)` with
`Lπ_!(K ⊗_O^L B̲)` of the lemma".

The remark is covered by this declaration together with the three that state the functor and
its exactness: `Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficients` (the functor
`Lπ_! : D(O) ⟶ D(B)`, defined as `- ⊗^L_O B̲` followed by `Lπ_! : D(B̲) ⟶ D(B)`),
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficients_commShift` and
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficients_isTriangulated` (it is an exact functor of
triangulated categories), all in
`StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/Sites/Cohomology/ChaoticSite/DerivedLowerShriek.lean`. Those exist
for every `φ`; the hypotheses of the remark enter only here, through Stacks 08RX
(`Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitTensorNatIso`), and they are what makes the functor a lift of
`Lπ^{Ab}_!`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedColimitWithCoefficientsForgetNatIso (U : CosimplicialObject C)
    (hU : IsPointResolution U)
    (ha : IsIso ((totalDerivedColimit C AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{u}) 0).map
        (Functor.whiskerRight φ (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u}))))) :
    abelianDerivedColimitOfModules O ≅
      derivedColimitWithCoefficients B O φ ⋙
        (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} B) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapDerivedCategory
declarations.comment: the B-module structure on `Lpi_!(K)`: the identification of `Lpi^{Ab}_!(K)` with the underlying object of `D(Ab)` of `Lpi_!(K)` read in `D(B)`, for a cosimplicial point resolution and a coefficient map `O -> B` inducing an isomorphism `Lpi_!O -> Lpi_!B`. The functor `Lpi_! : D(O) -> D(B)` and its exactness, which need no hypothesis on the coefficient map, are `Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficients`, `Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficients_commShift` and `Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficients_isTriangulated`

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.derivedProjectionLowerShriekIsoMooreComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D0.** Let `(C, J)` be a small site and let `Δ × C` carry the topology inherited
from `(C, J)` along the projection `π : Δ × C ⥤ C`. For every sheaf of abelian groups `ℱ` on
`Δ × C`, the abelian derived lower shriek of Remark 09CY carries `ℱ` to the associated chain
complex of the simplicial abelian sheaf `ℱ_•` that `ℱ` is:

`Lπ_!(ℱ[0]) ≅ s(ℱ_•)` in `D(Ab(C))`,

where `s(ℱ_•)` is the alternating-face-map complex of `ℱ_• = fibrewise ℱ`, read as a cochain
complex over `ℤ` in non-positive degrees.

This is the source's own argument: a resolution of `ℱ` by direct sums of the free abelian
sheaves `j_{W!}ℤ_W` (Stacks 06XX) computes `Lπ_!` because `π_!` is acyclic on those
(`Stacks.SimplicialModules.abelianLowerShriekAcyclic_projection`, which is Lemma 21.40.2), and
the degreewise colimit over `Δᵒᵖ` of such a resolution is the Moore complex
(`Stacks.ChaoticSite.GeneralValued.mooreCochainQIsoColimOfResolution`, which is Lemma
21.39.7).
declarations.statement:
def derivedProjectionLowerShriekIsoMooreComplex
    (F : Sheaf (projectionTopology C J) AddCommGrpCat.{w}) :
    (derivedAbelianLowerShriek.{w} (projectionTopology C J) J (projection C)).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((HomologicalComplex.single (Sheaf (projectionTopology C J) AddCommGrpCat.{w})
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj F)) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((Stacks.ChaoticSite.GeneralValued.mooreCochainComplex (𝟭 SimplexCategory)
          (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{w})).obj ((fibrewise J AddCommGrpCat.{w}).obj F))
declarations.comment: Lπ_!(ℱ_•) is represented by the alternating-face-map complex s(ℱ_•) of the simplicial abelian sheaf ℱ_•, for every abelian sheaf on Δ × C — in particular for the underlying abelian sheaf of a simplicial A_•-module over any simplicial sheaf of rings A_•, the Lπ_! of the section being the abelian one of Remark 09CY. Proved from Stacks 08PJ's two inputs as the source directs: the acyclicity of π_! and the Moore computation over Δ

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.derivedProjectionLowerShriekIsoMooreComplexModules
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D0 at module coefficients.** Let `(C, J)` be a small site, let `O` be a sheaf of
rings on it and let `Δ × C` carry the topology inherited from `(C, J)` along the projection
`π : Δ × C ⥤ C`. For every sheaf of `π^{-1}O`-modules `ℱ` on `Δ × C`, the derived lower shriek of
Remark 09CY carries `ℱ` to the associated chain complex of the simplicial sheaf of `O`-modules
`ℱ_•` that `ℱ` is:

`Lπ_!(ℱ[0]) ≅ s(ℱ_•)` in `D(O)`,

where `s(ℱ_•)` is the alternating-face-map complex of `ℱ_• = fibrewiseMod ℱ`, read as a cochain
complex over `ℤ` in non-positive degrees.

This is the source's own argument, run at module coefficients: a resolution of `ℱ` by direct sums
of the `j_{W!}(π^{-1}O)_W` (Stacks 06XX) computes `Lπ_!` because `π_!` is acyclic on those
(`Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedLowerShriek.lowerShriekAcyclic_of_preservesCoveringPullbacks`, which
is Lemma 21.40.2), and the degreewise colimit over `Δᵒᵖ` of such a resolution is the Moore
complex (`Stacks.ChaoticSite.GeneralValued.mooreCochainQIsoColimOfResolution`, which is Lemma
21.39.7).
declarations.statement:
def derivedProjectionLowerShriekIsoMooreComplexModules
    (F : SheafOfModules.{w} (projectionRing C J O)) :
    (derivedProjectionLowerShriek C J O).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((HomologicalComplex.single (SheafOfModules.{w} (projectionRing C J O))
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj F)) ≅
      DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((Stacks.ChaoticSite.GeneralValued.mooreCochainComplex (𝟭 SimplexCategory)
          (SheafOfModules.{w} O)).obj ((fibrewiseMod C J O).obj F))
declarations.comment: the MODULE-coefficient representation: for a simplicial sheaf of O-modules ℱ_•, equivalently a sheaf of π^{-1}O-modules on Δ × C, Lπ_!(ℱ_•) is represented by the associated chain complex s(ℱ_•) in D(O). This is the form in which the untagged paragraph of Section 09D0 is used by Tag 09DH, whose triangle lives in D(ℬ); the abelian registration beside it, derivedProjectionLowerShriekIsoMooreComplex, cannot reach it because derived lower shriek does not commute with forgetting the module structure

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.simplicialSheafEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D0.** A sheaf on `Δ × C` *is* a simplicial sheaf on `C`: levelwise restriction to
the fibres and uncurrying are an equivalence of categories.
declarations.comment: a simplicial sheaf on C is the same thing as a sheaf on Δ × C for the topology inherited along π

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.SimplicialModule
declarations.doc:
A simplicial module over a simplicial sheaf of rings `A` is a presheaf of modules over the
associated ring presheaf on `Δ × C` whose underlying abelian-group presheaf is a sheaf for the
topology inherited from `C`.
declarations.statement: abbrev SimplicialModule (A : SimplicialObject (Sheaf J RingCat.{r}))

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.ringSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D1.** The sheaf of rings on `Δ × C` associated to a simplicial sheaf of rings.
The sheaf condition is `isSheaf_associatedRingPresheaf`.
declarations.statement:
def ringSheaf :
    Sheaf ((CategoryTheory.Prod.snd SimplexCategory C).inheritedTopology J) RingCat.{r}
declarations.comment: the sheaf of rings on Δ × C associated to A_•

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.isIso_derivedBaseChangeComparison
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a site and `A_• ⟶ B_•` a homomorphism of simplicial sheaves of (commutative) rings
on `C`. If `Lπ_!A_• ⟶ Lπ_!B_•` is an isomorphism in `D(C)`, then the canonical map
`Lπ_!(K) ⟶ Lπ_!(K ⊗^L_{A_•} B_•)` is an isomorphism for every `K` in `D(A_•)`.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_derivedBaseChangeComparison : IsIso (derivedBaseChangeComparison J φ)

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.isIso_derivedLowerShriekHomology_map_of_fibrewise
declarations.doc:
**The reduction of Stacks 09D2 to the fibre categories.** Let `C` be a site and let
`π : Δ × C ⥤ C` be the projection. A morphism `a` of abelian sheaves on `Δ × C` which induces an
isomorphism on the degree `n` homology of the fibre over every object of `C` is inverted by
`L_nπ_!`.

This is the step of the proof of Stacks 09D2 which, both sides of the asserted identity being
sheaves, computes their cohomology sheaves by the procedure of Stacks 08PI and so reduces the
lemma to the restriction of the coefficients to the fibre categories `Δ × U`, where the source
appeals to Stacks 08RX. It is not the lemma: the derived tensor product, the flat resolution and
Stacks 08RX itself do not appear. See the scope paragraph of the module docstring.

The two acyclicity statements of Stacks 08PJ are taken as arguments here;
`isIso_derivedLowerShriekHomology_map_of_fibrewise_unconditional` is the same reduction with
both discharged.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedLowerShriekHomology_map_of_fibrewise
    (h : (simplicialSituation B).AbelianLowerShriekAcyclic)
    (hcov : (simplicialSituation B).UliftFreeCoverLowerShriekAcyclic) (n : ℕ)
    {F G : Sheaf (simplicialSituation B).topology AddCommGrpCat.{max w u}} (a : F ⟶ G)
    (ha : ∀ U : B.Cᵒᵖ, IsIso (((fiberHomologyPresheafFunctor (simplicialSituation B) n).map
      ((sheafToPresheaf (simplicialSituation B).topology
        AddCommGrpCat.{max w u}).map a)).app U)) :
    IsIso (((simplicialSituation B).derivedAbelianLowerShriekHomology n).map a)
declarations.comment: the reduction to the fibre categories Δ × U

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.isIso_derivedLowerShriekHomology_map_of_fibrewise_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**The reduction of Stacks 09D2 to the fibre categories**, with no hypothesis. Let `C` be a
site and let `π : Δ × C ⥤ C` be the projection. A morphism `a` of abelian sheaves on `Δ × C`
which induces an isomorphism on the degree `n` homology of the fibre over every object of `C` is
inverted by `L_nπ_!`.

Both acyclicity statements of Stacks 08PJ are discharged rather than carried:
`StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/Sites/Cohomology/FibredCategory/ProjectionLowerShriekAcyclic.lean` proves Stacks 0D6X along the projection of a fibred category,
hence `FibredCategorySituation.abelianLowerShriekAcyclic` and the instance giving `Lπ_!`, and
`StacksFrontier/CategoryTheory/Sites/Cohomology/FibredCategory/UliftFreeCoverGenerators.lean` proves
`FibredCategorySituation.abelianLowerShriekGeneratorsAcyclic`, from which the acyclicity of the
sheafified canonical presentation follows by
`uliftFreeCoverLowerShriekAcyclic_of_generatorsAcyclic`.

It is still not the lemma, for the reasons in the scope paragraph of the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedLowerShriekHomology_map_of_fibrewise_unconditional (n : ℕ)
    {F G : Sheaf (simplicialSituation B).topology AddCommGrpCat.{max w u}} (a : F ⟶ G)
    (ha : ∀ U : B.Cᵒᵖ, IsIso (((fiberHomologyPresheafFunctor (simplicialSituation B) n).map
      ((sheafToPresheaf (simplicialSituation B).topology
        AddCommGrpCat.{max w u}).map a)).app U)) :
    IsIso (((simplicialSituation B).derivedAbelianLowerShriekHomology n).map a)
declarations.comment: the reduction to the fibre categories Δ × U

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.augmentedDerivedLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**Remark 09D3, the functor.** For an augmentation `ε : A_• ⟶ O` of a simplicial sheaf of rings
by a sheaf of rings, `Lπ_! : D(A_•) ⥤ D(O)` is the composite of derived base change
`- ⊗^L_{A_•} O : D(A_•) ⥤ D(Δ × C, π^{-1}O)` with the functor
`Lπ_! : D(Δ × C, π^{-1}O) ⥤ D(O)` of Remark 09CY.
declarations.comment: the functor `Lπ_! : D(A_•) ⟶ D(O)`, the composition of `- ⊗^L_{A_•} O` with the functor `Lπ_! : D(Δ × C, π^{-1}O) ⟶ D(O)` of Remark 09CY

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.augmentedDerivedLowerShriek_commShift
declarations.doc: **Remark 09D3, exactness: the functor commutes with the shift.**
declarations.statement:
instance augmentedDerivedLowerShriek_commShift (ε : CommAugmentation J A O) :
    (augmentedDerivedLowerShriek J ε).CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: `Lπ_! : D(A_•) ⟶ D(O)` is a functor of triangulated categories: it commutes with the shift

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.augmentedDerivedLowerShriek_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Remark 09D3, exactness: `Lπ_! : D(A_•) ⥤ D(O)` is an exact functor of triangulated
categories**, as a composite of two exact functors.
declarations.statement:
instance augmentedDerivedLowerShriek_isTriangulated (ε : CommAugmentation J A O) :
    (augmentedDerivedLowerShriek J ε).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: `Lπ_! : D(A_•) ⟶ D(O)` is an exact functor of triangulated categories

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.augmentedDerivedLowerShriekForgetIso
declarations.doc:
**Remark 09D3, the `O`-module structure on `Lπ_!(K)`.** Let `ε : A_• ⟶ O` be an augmentation
inducing a quasi-isomorphism `s(A_•) ⟶ O`. For `K` in `D(A_•)`, `Lπ_!(K)` is canonically and
functorially identified with `Lπ_!(K ⊗^L_{A_•} O)` by Lemma 09D2, and the latter is, by
Remark 09CY, the underlying complex of abelian sheaves of the object `Lπ_!(K)` of `D(O)` of
`augmentedDerivedLowerShriek`. So, naturally in `K`, forgetting the `O`-module structure of the
functor of the source gives back `Lπ_!(K)`.
declarations.statement:
def augmentedDerivedLowerShriekForgetIso (ε : CommAugmentation J A O)
    (hε : InducesQuasiIso J ε) :
    augmentedDerivedLowerShriek J ε ⋙
        (SheafOfModules.toSheaf (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf O)).mapDerivedCategory ≅
      moduleDerivedLowerShriek J A
declarations.comment: the `O`-module structure on `Lπ_!(K)`: under the hypothesis that `ε` induces a quasi-isomorphism `s(A_•) ⟶ O`, the canonical, functorial identification of `Lπ_!(K)` with `Lπ_!(K ⊗^L_{A_•} O)` of Lemma 09D2, read as the underlying complex of abelian sheaves of the object `Lπ_!(K)` of `D(O)`

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.augmentedLowerShriek
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D3.** Derived lower shriek along an augmented simplicial sheaf of rings:
`Lπ_! : D(A_•) ⟶ D(O)`, the composite of derived extension of scalars along the augmentation
with derived lower shriek on modules over `π^{-1}O`.
declarations.statement:
def augmentedLowerShriek (_ε : Augmentation J A O)
    (base : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{w, v, u, r} J A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)))
    (proj : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory D) :
    DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{w, v, u, r} J A) ⥤ DerivedCategory D
declarations.comment: the functor Lπ_! : D(A_•) ⟶ D(O). Two inputs of the source are carried as explicit parameters, the library not yet having them: `base` is derived extension of scalars `- ⊗^L_{A_•} O`, introduced in the untagged prose before Lemma 09D2, and `proj` is the functor Lπ_! : D(π^{-1}O) ⟶ D(O) of Tag 09CY, which is Tag 08PC part (3) for modules and is reduced in this library to the acyclicity statement of Tag 0794 at the class of direct sums of the j_{U!} O_U; see the implementation notes for what that still owes

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.augmentedLowerShriek_commShift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D3.** Derived lower shriek along an augmented simplicial sheaf of rings commutes
with the shift.
declarations.statement:
instance augmentedLowerShriek_commShift (ε : Augmentation J A O)
    (base : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{w, v, u, r} J A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)))
    (proj : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory D) [base.CommShift ℤ] [proj.CommShift ℤ] :
    (augmentedLowerShriek J ε base proj).CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: the functor commutes with the shift

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.augmentedLowerShriek_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D3.** Derived lower shriek along an augmented simplicial sheaf of rings is an
exact functor of triangulated categories.
declarations.statement:
instance augmentedLowerShriek_isTriangulated (ε : Augmentation J A O)
    (base : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{w, v, u, r} J A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)))
    (proj : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory D) [base.CommShift ℤ] [proj.CommShift ℤ]
    [base.IsTriangulated] [proj.IsTriangulated] :
    (augmentedLowerShriek J ε base proj).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.augmentedLowerShriek_derivedTarget
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D3.** Derived lower shriek along an augmented simplicial sheaf of rings,
`Lπ_! : D(A_•) ⟶ D(O)` with `D(O)` the derived category of the sheaves of `O`-modules on `C`,
which is the `D(O)` of the source.

Nothing is assumed about either category of simplicial modules: the abelian structure is
`Stacks.SimplicialModules.abelian` and the derived category is `HasDerivedCategory.standard`,
both seated as local instances. That abelian structure is supplied at sections universe
`max u v r w`, which is why the module sections are taken there.
declarations.statement:
def augmentedLowerShriek_derivedTarget (_ε : Augmentation J A O)
    (base : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{max u v r w, v, u, r} J A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{max u v r w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)))
    (proj : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{max u v r w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O)) :
    DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{max u v r w, v, u, r} J A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O)
declarations.comment: the functor Lπ_! : D(A_•) ⟶ D(O), at the target D(O) the source names and with the abelian structure and the derived category of both categories of simplicial modules discharged rather than assumed. Two inputs of the source are carried as explicit parameters, the library not yet having them: `base` is derived extension of scalars `- ⊗^L_{A_•} O`, introduced in the untagged prose before Lemma 09D2, and `proj` is the functor Lπ_! : D(π^{-1}O) ⟶ D(O) of Tag 09CY, whose underived half is `Stacks.SimplicialModules.moduleLowerShriek` and whose total left derived functor is part (3) of Tag 08PC, open here

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.augmentedLowerShriek_derivedTarget_commShift
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D3.** Derived lower shriek along an augmented simplicial sheaf of rings commutes
with the shift, at the target `D(O)`.
declarations.statement:
instance augmentedLowerShriek_derivedTarget_commShift (ε : Augmentation J A O)
    (base : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{max u v r w, v, u, r} J A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{max u v r w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)))
    (proj : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{max u v r w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O))
    [base.CommShift ℤ] [proj.CommShift ℤ] :
    (augmentedLowerShriek_derivedTarget.{w} J ε base proj).CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: the functor commutes with the shift, at the target D(O) the source names

declarations.name: Stacks.SimplicialModules.augmentedLowerShriek_derivedTarget_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D3.** Derived lower shriek along an augmented simplicial sheaf of rings is an
exact functor of triangulated categories, at the target `D(O)`.
declarations.statement:
instance augmentedLowerShriek_derivedTarget_isTriangulated (ε : Augmentation J A O)
    (base : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{max u v r w, v, u, r} J A) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{max u v r w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)))
    (proj : DerivedCategory (SimplicialModule.{max u v r w, v, u, r} J (constantRing J O)) ⥤
      DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max u v r w} O))
    [base.CommShift ℤ] [proj.CommShift ℤ]
    [base.IsTriangulated] [proj.IsTriangulated] :
    (augmentedLowerShriek_derivedTarget.{w} J ε base proj).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the functor is exact, at the target D(O) the source names

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.Degeneracies.degeneracyZero
declarations.doc: The first degeneracy fixes `uᵢ` and sends `xₜ` to `yₜ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def degeneracyZero :
    DegreeOne.P1 p →ₐ[p.A] DegreeTwo.P2 p

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.Degeneracies.degeneracyOne
declarations.doc: The second degeneracy fixes `uᵢ` and sends `xₜ` to `zₜ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def degeneracyOne :
    DegreeOne.P1 p →ₐ[p.A] DegreeTwo.P2 p

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.Degeneracies.degeneracyZero_unique
declarations.doc:
The first degeneracy is the unique algebra map with the displayed
values on the old and relation variables.
declarations.statement:
theorem degeneracyZero_unique
    (f : DegreeOne.P1 p →ₐ[p.A] DegreeTwo.P2 p)
    (hu : ∀ i : p.variableIndex,
      f (MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl i)) =
        MvPolynomial.X (DegreeTwo.DegreeTwoVariable.base i))
    (hx : ∀ t : p.relationIndex,
      f (MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inr t)) =
        MvPolynomial.X (DegreeTwo.DegreeTwoVariable.y t)) :
    f = degeneracyZero p

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.Degeneracies.degeneracyOne_unique
declarations.doc:
The second degeneracy is the unique algebra map with the displayed
values on the old and relation variables.
declarations.statement:
theorem degeneracyOne_unique
    (f : DegreeOne.P1 p →ₐ[p.A] DegreeTwo.P2 p)
    (hu : ∀ i : p.variableIndex,
      f (MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl i)) =
        MvPolynomial.X (DegreeTwo.DegreeTwoVariable.base i))
    (hx : ∀ t : p.relationIndex,
      f (MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inr t)) =
        MvPolynomial.X (DegreeTwo.DegreeTwoVariable.z t)) :
    f = degeneracyOne p

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.Degeneracies.degeneracyZero_lifts
declarations.doc:
The displayed first degeneracy lifts the first degeneracy of the
one-coskeleton.
declarations.statement:
theorem degeneracyZero_lifts :
    AlgCat.ofHom (degeneracyZeroLift p) ≫
        DegreeTwo.degreeTwoToCoskeleton p =
        (DegreeOne.degreeOneCoskeleton p).oneIso.inv ≫
        (DegreeOne.degreeOneCoskeleton p).simplicial.σ (0 : Fin 2)

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.Degeneracies.degeneracyOne_lifts
declarations.doc:
The displayed second degeneracy lifts the second degeneracy of the
one-coskeleton.
declarations.statement:
theorem degeneracyOne_lifts :
    AlgCat.ofHom (degeneracyOneLift p) ≫
        DegreeTwo.degreeTwoToCoskeleton p =
      (DegreeOne.degreeOneCoskeleton p).oneIso.inv ≫
        (DegreeOne.degreeOneCoskeleton p).simplicial.σ (1 : Fin 2)

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.Degeneracies.explicitResolution
declarations.doc:
The displayed first three degrees extend to a polynomial simplicial
resolution of `B` over `A`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def explicitResolution : ExplicitResolution p

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.DegreeOne.degreeOneCoskeleton
declarations.doc: The coskeleton of the explicit one-truncated polynomial simplicial algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def degreeOneCoskeleton : DegreeOneCoskeleton p

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.DegreeOne.range_faceZero_sub_faceOne
declarations.doc: Exactness at `P₀` of `P₁ → P₀ → B`.

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.DegreeOne.facePair_surjective
declarations.doc: Every compatible pair of degree-zero simplices lifts to degree one.
declarations.statement:
theorem facePair_surjective :
    ∀ a b : p.P0,
      augmentationZero p a = augmentationZero p b →
        ∃ z : P1 p, faceZero p z = a ∧ faceOne p z = b

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.DegreeOne.coskeleton_trivialKanFibration
declarations.doc: The augmentation of this degree-one coskeleton is a trivial Kan fibration.
declarations.statement:
theorem coskeleton_trivialKanFibration :
    SSet.trivialKanFibrations
      (Functor.whiskerRight (degreeOneCoskeleton p).augmentation
        (forget (AlgCat.{max u v w x} p.A)))

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.DegreeTwo.faces_matching
declarations.doc: The three displayed face maps define a map to the degree-two matching object.
declarations.statement:
theorem faces_matching (q : P2 p) :
    MatchingTriple p (faceZero p q) (faceOne p q) (faceTwo p q)

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.DegreeTwo.matchingEquiv
declarations.doc:
The actual second degree of the one-coskeleton is canonically the algebra
of compatible triples of degree-one elements.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def matchingEquiv :
    ((DegreeOne.degreeOneCoskeleton p).simplicial _⦋2⦌) ≃
      {g : (DegreeOne.P1 p ×
          DegreeOne.P1 p × DegreeOne.P1 p) //
        MatchingTriple p g.1 g.2.1 g.2.2}

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.DegreeTwo.matchingEquiv_faces
declarations.doc:
The canonical matching equivalence records exactly the three actual faces
of a degree-two simplex.
declarations.statement:
theorem matchingEquiv_faces
    (a : (DegreeOne.degreeOneCoskeleton p).simplicial _⦋2⦌) :
    (matchingEquiv p a).val =
      (coskeletonFace p 0 a, coskeletonFace p 1 a, coskeletonFace p 2 a)

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.DegreeTwo.degreeTwoToCoskeleton
declarations.doc:
The algebra map from the displayed polynomial degree two to the actual
degree-two object of the one-coskeleton.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def degreeTwoToCoskeleton :
    algP2 p ⟶ (DegreeOne.degreeOneCoskeleton p).simplicial _⦋2⦌

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.DegreeTwo.matchingEquiv_degreeTwoToCoskeleton
declarations.doc:
Under the canonical matching equivalence, the algebra map has the three
displayed face maps as its components.
declarations.statement:
theorem matchingEquiv_degreeTwoToCoskeleton (q : P2 p) :
    matchingEquiv p (degreeTwoToCoskeleton p (ULift.up q)) =
      ⟨(faceZero p q, faceOne p q, faceTwo p q), faces_matching p q⟩

declarations.name: Algebra.PolynomialPresentationWithKernelGenerators.DegreeTwo.degreeTwoToCoskeleton_surjective
declarations.doc:
The displayed algebra map onto the actual second coskeleton degree is
surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem degreeTwoToCoskeleton_surjective :
    Function.Surjective (degreeTwoToCoskeleton p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.isIso_conormalTorOneDifferential
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D5: the differential `H₂(C_{B/A}, 𝒥/𝒥²) → H₀(C_{B/A}, Tor₁^𝒪(𝒥, B̲))` of the
spectral sequence of Remark 08R7 is an isomorphism.** The differential is the composite of the two
connecting maps, which is `d₂` of that spectral sequence (see the module docstring); each is an
isomorphism because `H₁` and `H₂` of `𝒥`, and `H₀` and `H₁` of `𝒥 ⊗_𝒪 𝒥`, vanish.
declarations.statement: theorem isIso_conormalTorOneDifferential : IsIso (conormalTorOneDifferential.{u, v} A B)
declarations.comment: the differential H₂(C_{B/A}, 𝒥/𝒥²) → H₀(C_{B/A}, Tor₁^𝒪(𝒥, B̲)) of the spectral sequence of Remark 08R7 is an isomorphism, read on the standard resolution

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.cotangentComplexHomologyTwoLinearIsoTorOne
