declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D5: `H₂(L_{B/A}) = H₀(C_{B/A}, Tor₁^𝒪(𝒥, B̲))`, as `B`-modules.** `H₂(L_{B/A})`
is the homology in cohomological degree `-2` of the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN, and the
right-hand side is `H₀` of the Moore complex of the simplicial `B`-module
`n ↦ Tor₁^{Pₙ}(Jₙ, B)` on the standard resolution. The isomorphism is
`H₂(L_{B/A}) ≅ H₂(C_{B/A}, 𝒥/𝒥²)` followed by the differential, made `B`-linear by
`Stacks.Cotangent.isoOfRestrictScalarsIso`.
declarations.statement:
def cotangentComplexHomologyTwoLinearIsoTorOne :
    (cotangentComplex A B).homology (-2) ≅ (torOneMooreComplexB.{u, v} A B).homology 0
declarations.comment: H₂(L_{B/A}) = H₀(C_{B/A}, Tor₁^𝒪(𝒥, B̲)), an isomorphism of B-modules

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.isZero_homology_kernel_conormalToCotangentMoore
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D5**, the kernel of `d` has no higher homology on `C_{B/A}`. By Tag 08PS the
homology of a sheaf on `C_{B/A}` is the homology of the simplicial module it gives on the
standard resolution, and `Ker(d)` is there the *constant* simplicial module on
`Algebra.H1Cotangent A B` (`Stacks.Cotangent.kernelConormalToCotangentMooreIso`, which is the
constancy of `Stacks.Cotangent.outerTerms_constant` combined with the exactness of
`Stacks.Cotangent.surjectivePresentation_exact`); the Moore complex of a constant simplicial
module has no homology in positive degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_kernel_conormalToCotangentMoore (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsZero ((kernel (conormalToCotangentMoore A B)).homology n)
declarations.comment: Ker(d) has vanishing higher homology on C_{B/A}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.isZero_homology_cokernel_conormalToCotangentMoore
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D5**, the cokernel of `d` has no higher homology on `C_{B/A}`: on the standard
resolution `Coker(d)` is the *constant* simplicial module on `Ω[B⁄A]`
(`Stacks.Cotangent.cokernelConormalToCotangentMooreIso`), and the Moore complex of a constant
simplicial module has no homology in positive degrees.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_cokernel_conormalToCotangentMoore (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    IsZero ((cokernel (conormalToCotangentMoore A B)).homology n)
declarations.comment: Coker(d) has vanishing higher homology on C_{B/A}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.isIso_homologyMap_conormalToCotangentComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D5**, the map `H_n(C_{B/A}, 𝒥/𝒥²) → H_n(L_{B/A})` is an isomorphism for every
`n ≥ 2`, stated at the cotangent complex `CommAlgCat.cotangentComplex` of Tag 08PN, whose
homology in cohomological degree `-n` is `H_n(L_{B/A})`. This is
`Stacks.Cotangent.isIso_homologyMap_conormalToCotangentMoore` transported along the reindexing,
which changes no homology.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_homologyMap_conormalToCotangentComplex (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
    IsIso (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (conormalToCotangentComplex A B) (-(n : ℤ)))
declarations.comment: H_n(C_{B/A}, 𝒥/𝒥²) → H_n(L_{B/A}) is an isomorphism for n ≥ 2, at the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.surjectivePresentation_exact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D5**, the exact sequence of sheaves on `C'_{B/A}`, read at an object: for a
surjection `α : P → B` with `P` a polynomial algebra over `A` and `J = ker α`, the sequence

```
0 ⟶ H₁(L_{B/A}) ⟶ J/J² --d--> Ω_{P/A} ⊗_P B ⟶ Ω[B⁄A] ⟶ 0
```

is exact. The source writes the right-hand term as `H₂(L_{B/A})`, which is a slip for
`H₀(L_{B/A})`; that term is `Ω[B⁄A]`, and
`Stacks.Cotangent.cokerCotangentComplexIsoHomologyZero` identifies it with the degree-zero
homology of the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjectivePresentation_exact (P : Algebra.Extension.{w} A B)
    (hP : Algebra.IsPolynomialAlgebra A P.Ring) :
    Function.Injective (h1CotangentIncl P) ∧
      Function.Exact (h1CotangentIncl P) P.cotangentComplex ∧
        Function.Exact P.cotangentComplex P.toKaehler ∧
          Function.Surjective P.toKaehler
declarations.comment: the exact sequence 0 → H₁(L_{B/A}) → J/J² → Ω → Ω_{B/A} → 0 at an object of C'_{B/A}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.outerTerms_constant
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D5**, the outer terms of the sequence are the constant sheaves on `C'_{B/A}`:
for any morphism `f : P ⟶ P'` of extensions of `B` over `A`, the left-hand map
`H₁(L_{B/A}) ⟶ J/J²` is carried to the one of `P'` by `f`, and the right-hand map
`Ω_{P/A} ⊗_P B ⟶ Ω[B⁄A]` is the composite of `f` with the one of `P'`. Hence the identifications
`Ker(d) = H₁(L_{B/A})` and `Coker(d) = Ω[B⁄A]` of
`Stacks.Cotangent.surjectivePresentation_exact` do not depend on the object.
declarations.statement:
theorem outerTerms_constant {P P' : Algebra.Extension.{w} A B} (f : P.Hom P') :
    Algebra.Extension.Cotangent.map f ∘ₗ h1CotangentIncl P = h1CotangentIncl P' ∧
      P'.toKaehler ∘ₗ Algebra.Extension.CotangentSpace.map f = P.toKaehler
declarations.comment: Ker(d) and Coker(d) are the constant sheaves on C'_{B/A}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.cokerCotangentComplexIsoHomologyZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D5**, the right-hand term of the sequence is `H₀(L_{B/A})`: at an object
`α : P → B` of `C'_{B/A}` the cokernel of `d : J/J² → Ω_{P/A} ⊗_P B` is the degree-zero homology
of the cotangent complex of Tag 08PN, by Tag 08QF.
declarations.statement:
def cokerCotangentComplexIsoHomologyZero (P : Algebra.Extension.{max u v} A B) :
    ModuleCat.of (B : Type (max u v))
        (P.CotangentSpace ⧸ LinearMap.range P.cotangentComplex) ≅
      (CommAlgCat.cotangentComplex A B).homology 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.cotangentHomologyTwoIsoTorTwoCoker
declarations.doc:
`H₂(L_{B/A}) = Coker(Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B) → Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B))` for an arbitrary resolution `P_•`
of `B` over `A`, as `B`-modules, where `Tor₂^{P_n}(B, B) = Ker(J_n ⊗_{P_n} J_n → J_n²)` and the
map is `d₀ - d₁`. The isomorphism is Remark 09D5's `H₂(L_{B/A}) = H₀(C_{B/A}, Tor₁^𝒪(𝒥, B̲))`,
followed by `H₀ = Coker(d₀ - d₁)` on the standard resolution and the canonical comparison of the
cokernels of two resolutions.
declarations.statement:
def cotangentHomologyTwoIsoTorTwoCoker (hP : CommAlgCat.IsResolution A B P ε) :
    (cotangentComplex A B).homology (-2) ≅ torTwoCoker hP
declarations.comment: H₂(L_{B/A}) is canonically Coker(Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B) → Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B)), the map being d₀ - d₁, for an arbitrary resolution P_• of B over A (Remark 08QI), as B-modules, with Tor₂^{P_n}(B, B) read as Ker(J_n ⊗_{P_n} J_n → J_n²); obtained from Remark 09D5, Stacks.Cotangent.cotangentComplexHomologyTwoLinearIsoTorOne, as the source obtains it

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.toHomologyTwo_surjective
declarations.doc: The map `Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A})` is surjective.
declarations.statement: theorem toHomologyTwo_surjective : Function.Surjective (toHomologyTwo p)
declarations.comment: the exact sequence ∧²_B(J₀/J₀²) → Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A}) → 0 for the resolution of Example 09D4: the last map is surjective

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.exact_wedgeAntisymm_toHomologyTwo
declarations.doc:
The exact sequence `∧²_B(J₀/J₀²) → Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A}) → 0` for the resolution
of Example 09D4: exactness at `Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B)`, the first map being `ā ∧ b̄ ↦ a ⊗ b - b ⊗ a`; the
second map is surjective by `toHomologyTwo_surjective`. Both maps are `B`-linear.
declarations.statement:
theorem exact_wedgeAntisymm_toHomologyTwo :
    Function.Exact (wedgeAntisymm (φ := aug p 0)) (toHomologyTwo p)
declarations.comment: the exact sequence ∧²_B(J₀/J₀²) → Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B) → H^{-2}(L_{B/A}) → 0 for the resolution of Example 09D4: exactness at Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B), the first map being ā ∧ b̄ ↦ a ⊗ b - b ⊗ a

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.Explicit.decomposition
declarations.doc:
**The decomposition of `Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B)` for the explicit resolution**:

`Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B) = ∧²_B(⨁_{t ∈ T} B) ⊕ ⨁_{t ∈ T} J₀/J₀² ⊕ Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B)`

as `B`-modules, `Tor₂` read in the tensor-kernel model. The correspondences are
`decomposition_wedge`, `decomposition_mixed` and `decomposition_degen`.
declarations.statement:
def decomposition :
    (⋀[target p]^2 (p.relationIndex →₀ target p) ×
        (p.relationIndex →₀ (RingHom.ker (aug p 0)).Cotangent) × mulKernel (aug p 0)) ≃ₗ[target p]
      mulKernel (aug p 1)
declarations.comment: the decomposition Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B) = ∧²(⨁_{t ∈ T} B) ⊕ ⨁_{t ∈ T} J₀/J₀² ⊕ Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B) for the resolution P_• of Example 09D4, as B-modules, with Tor₂^{P_n}(B, B) read as Ker(J_n ⊗_{P_n} J_n → J_n²) (the remark's own identification, Stacks.Cotangent.torTwoSelfIsoMulKernel); the correspondences are decomposition_wedge, decomposition_mixed and decomposition_degen

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.Explicit.decomposition_wedge
declarations.doc:
The basis element `x_t ∧ x_{t'}` of `∧²(⨁_T B)` corresponds to
`x_t ⊗ x_{t'} - x_{t'} ⊗ x_t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem decomposition_wedge (t t' : p.relationIndex) :
    decomposition p (wedgeBilin (Finsupp.single t 1) (Finsupp.single t' 1), 0, 0) =
      antisymm (xJ p t) (xJ p t')
declarations.comment: the basis element x_t ∧ x_{t'} of the first summand corresponds to x_t ⊗ x_{t'} - x_{t'} ⊗ x_t in J₁ ⊗_{P₁} J₁

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.Explicit.decomposition_mixed
declarations.doc:
For `f ∈ J₀`, the element `x_t ⊗ f̄` of `⨁_T J₀/J₀²` corresponds to
`x_t ⊗ s₀(f) - s₀(f) ⊗ x_t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem decomposition_mixed (t : p.relationIndex) (f : RingHom.ker (aug p 0)) :
    decomposition p (0, Finsupp.single t ((RingHom.ker (aug p 0)).toCotangent f), 0) =
      antisymm (xJ p t) (degenJ p f)
declarations.comment: for f ∈ J₀ the element x_t ⊗ f̄ of the second summand corresponds to x_t ⊗ s₀(f) - s₀(f) ⊗ x_t in J₁ ⊗_{P₁} J₁

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.Explicit.decomposition_degen
declarations.doc: The map `Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B) → Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B)` onto the last summand is given by `s₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem decomposition_degen (k : mulKernel (aug p 0)) :
    decomposition p (0, 0, k) = mulKernelMap (degenMap p) (aug_comp_degenMap p) k
declarations.comment: the map Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B) → Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B) onto the last summand is given by s₀

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.Explicit.face_degen
declarations.doc: `d₀ - d₁` vanishes on the summand `Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem face_degen (k : mulKernel (aug p 0)) :
    face p (mulKernelMap (degenMap p) (aug_comp_degenMap p) k) = 0
declarations.comment: d₀ - d₁ : Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B) → Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B) is zero on the last summand

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.Explicit.face_mixed
declarations.doc: `d₀ - d₁` sends `x_t ⊗ f̄` to `f ⊗ f_t - f_t ⊗ f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem face_mixed (t : p.relationIndex) (f : RingHom.ker (aug p 0)) :
    face p (antisymm (xJ p t) (degenJ p f)) = antisymm f (relJ p t)
declarations.comment: d₀ - d₁ maps x_t ⊗ f̄ to f ⊗ f_t - f_t ⊗ f

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.Explicit.face_wedge
declarations.doc: `d₀ - d₁` sends `x_t ∧ x_{t'}` to `f_{t'} ⊗ f_t - f_t ⊗ f_{t'}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem face_wedge (t t' : p.relationIndex) :
    face p (antisymm (xJ p t) (xJ p t')) = antisymm (relJ p t') (relJ p t)
declarations.comment: d₀ - d₁ maps x_t ∧ x_{t'} to f_{t'} ⊗ f_t - f_t ⊗ f_{t'}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.TorTwo.Explicit.torTwoDecomposition
declarations.doc:
**The decomposition of `Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B)`, on Mathlib's `Tor'`**: for the
`P₁`-algebra `B` (through the augmentation),

`Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B) ≅ ∧²_B(⨁_T B) ⊕ ⨁_T J₀/J₀² ⊕ Tor₂^{P₀}(B, B)`,

an additive isomorphism which is `P₁`-linear for `P₁` acting on the right through `P₁ → B`
(`torTwoDecomposition_smul`). It is `Stacks.Cotangent.torTwoSelfIsoMulKernel` followed by the
inverse of `decomposition`.
declarations.statement:
def torTwoDecomposition :
    letI : Algebra (term p 1) (target p) := (aug p 1).toAlgebra
    ((CategoryTheory.Tor' (ModuleCat.{max u v w x} (term p 1)) 2).obj
        (ModuleCat.of (term p 1) (target p))).obj (ModuleCat.of (term p 1) (target p)) ≃+
      (⋀[target p]^2 (p.relationIndex →₀ target p) ×
        (p.relationIndex →₀ (RingHom.ker (aug p 0)).Cotangent) × mulKernel (aug p 0))
declarations.comment: the decomposition of Tor₂^{P₁}(B, B) read on Mathlib's Tor' itself

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.torTwoSelfIsoTorOneIdeal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D6**, first identification. For a surjection `P → B` with kernel `J`, the
connecting homomorphism of `0 → J → P → B → 0` for the functor `- ⊗ B` is an isomorphism
`Tor₂^P(B, B) ≅ Tor₁^P(J, B)`: the two flanking terms are `Tor_i^P(P, B)` for `i = 1, 2`, which
vanish because `P` is projective over itself.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def torTwoSelfIsoTorOneIdeal (hf : Function.Surjective (algebraMap P B)) :
    ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} P) 2).obj (ModuleCat.of P B)).obj (ModuleCat.of P B) ≅
      ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} P) 1).obj
          (ModuleCat.of P (RingHom.ker (algebraMap P B)))).obj (ModuleCat.of P B)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.torOneIdealIsoMulKernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D6**, second identification. For a surjection `P → B` with kernel `J`, the
connecting homomorphism of `0 → J → P → B → 0` for the functor `J ⊗ -` identifies
`Tor₁^P(J, B)` with the kernel of the multiplication map `J ⊗_P J → J²`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def torOneIdealIsoMulKernel (hf : Function.Surjective (algebraMap P B)) :
    ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} P) 1).obj
          (ModuleCat.of P (RingHom.ker (algebraMap P B)))).obj (ModuleCat.of P B) ≅
      ModuleCat.of P ↥(LinearMap.ker (Submodule.mulMap' (RingHom.ker (algebraMap P B))
        (RingHom.ker (algebraMap P B))))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cotangent.torTwoSelfIsoMulKernel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D6**, the composite identification
`Tor₂^P(B, B) = Ker(J ⊗_P J → J²)` for a surjection `P → B` with kernel `J`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def torTwoSelfIsoMulKernel (hf : Function.Surjective (algebraMap P B)) :
    ((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} P) 2).obj (ModuleCat.of P B)).obj (ModuleCat.of P B) ≅
      ModuleCat.of P ↥(LinearMap.ker (Submodule.mulMap' (RingHom.ker (algebraMap P B))
        (RingHom.ker (algebraMap P B))))
declarations.comment: Tor₂^P(B, B) = Tor₁^P(J, B) = Ker(J ⊗_P J → J²)

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.LichtenbaumSchlessingerHom.canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger_naturality
declarations.doc:
For a commutative square of rings `A → A'`, `B → B'` and compatible presentations `P → P'`
with `f'_t` the image of `f_t`, the canonical maps `L_{B/A} → L` and `L_{B'/A'} → L'` commute in
`D(B)` with the map `L_{B/A} → L_{B'/A'}` of cotangent complexes and the map `L → L'` of
Lichtenbaum–Schlessinger complexes, the objects over `B'` being read over `B` along `B → B'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger_naturality :
    DerivedCategory.Q.map (cotangentComplexULiftSquareMap.{u, u', v, w} A A' B B') ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap B B')).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv.app
          (cotangentComplexULift.{u', max u v, w} A' B') ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap B B')).mapDerivedCategory.map
          (canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger.{u', max u v, w} P') ≫
        (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap B B')).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app
          (lichtenbaumSchlessingerComplex P').complex =
      canonicalCotangentToLichtenbaumSchlessinger.{u, max u' v, w} P ≫
        DerivedCategory.Q.map f.complexMap
declarations.comment:
the second commutative diagram: L_{B/A} → L, L → L' equals
L_{B/A} → L_{B'/A'}, L_{B'/A'} → L' in D(B)

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.LichtenbaumSchlessingerHom.relationQuotientMap
declarations.doc: The map `Rel/TrivRel → Rel'/TrivRel'` induced by `Rel → Rel'`, in degree `-2`.
declarations.statement: def relationQuotientMap : relationQuotient P →ₛₗ[f.ringHom] relationQuotient P'
declarations.comment: the vertical arrow Rel/TrivRel → Rel'/TrivRel' of the displayed diagram

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.LichtenbaumSchlessingerHom.freeTensorMap
declarations.doc: **Stacks 09D7.** The arrow `F ⊗_P B → F' ⊗_{P'} B'` of the diagram, in degree `-1`.
declarations.statement:
def freeTensorMap :
    (B ⊗[P.Ring] (T →₀ P.Ring)) →ₗ[B] B' ⊗[P'.Ring] ((T ⊕ S) →₀ P'.Ring)
declarations.comment: the vertical arrow F ⊗_P B → F' ⊗_{P'} B' of the displayed diagram

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.LichtenbaumSchlessingerHom.differentialTensorMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D7.** The arrow `Ω_{P/A} ⊗_P B → Ω_{P'/A'} ⊗_{P'} B'` of the diagram, in degree
`0`.
declarations.statement:
def differentialTensorMap :
    (B ⊗[P.Ring] Ω[P.Ring⁄A]) →ₗ[B] B' ⊗[P'.Ring] Ω[P'.Ring⁄A']
declarations.comment: the vertical arrow Ω_{P/A} ⊗_P B → Ω_{P'/A'} ⊗_{P'} B' of the displayed diagram

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.LichtenbaumSchlessingerHom.freeTensorMap_relationBoundaryR
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D7.** The left-hand square of the displayed diagram commutes: the arrow
`Rel/TrivRel → F ⊗_P B` followed by the vertical arrow in degree `-1` agrees with the vertical
arrow in degree `-2` followed by `Rel'/TrivRel' → F' ⊗_{P'} B'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma freeTensorMap_relationBoundaryR (q : relationQuotient P) :
    f.freeTensorMap (relationBoundaryR P q) =
      relationBoundaryR P' (f.relationQuotientMap q)
declarations.comment: commutativity of the left-hand square of the displayed diagram

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.LichtenbaumSchlessingerHom.differentialTensorMap_relationDifferentialB
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D7.** The right-hand square of the displayed diagram commutes: the arrow
`F ⊗_P B → Ω_{P/A} ⊗_P B` followed by the vertical arrow in degree `0` agrees with the vertical
arrow in degree `-1` followed by `F' ⊗_{P'} B' → Ω_{P'/A'} ⊗_{P'} B'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma differentialTensorMap_relationDifferentialB (z : B ⊗[P.Ring] (T →₀ P.Ring)) :
    f.differentialTensorMap (relationDifferentialB P z) =
      relationDifferentialB P' (f.freeTensorMap z)
declarations.comment: commutativity of the right-hand square of the displayed diagram

declarations.name: Algebra.Presentation.LichtenbaumSchlessingerHom.complexMap
declarations.doc:
The canonical map of Lichtenbaum–Schlessinger complexes `L → L'` attached to compatible
presentations of a commutative square of rings: the arrows `Rel/TrivRel → Rel'/TrivRel'`,
`F ⊗_P B → F' ⊗_{P'} B'`, `Ω_{P/A} ⊗_P B → Ω_{P'/A'} ⊗_{P'} B'` (tensored up to `B'`), which
commute with the differentials. It is `B`-linear, `L'` being read over `B` along `B → B'`.
declarations.statement:
def complexMap : (lichtenbaumSchlessingerComplex P).complex ⟶
    ((𝓡).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
      (lichtenbaumSchlessingerComplex P').complex
declarations.comment:
the first commutative diagram: the canonical map of Lichtenbaum–Schlessinger
complexes L → L' with vertical arrows Rel/TrivRel → Rel'/TrivRel', F ⊗_P B → F' ⊗_{P'} B',
Ω_{P/A} ⊗_P B → Ω_{P'/A'} ⊗_{P'} B'

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exists_tensorProduct_nine_diagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D9**, Equation 92.15.0.1. Let `A` and `B` be algebras over a ring `R`. Given the
fundamental triangle `L_{A/R} ⊗^L_A (A ⊗_R B) ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/R} ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/A}` of
`R → A → A ⊗_R B` and the fundamental triangle
`L_{B/R} ⊗^L_B (A ⊗_R B) ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/R} ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/B}` of `R → B → A ⊗_R B`, there is an
object `E` of `D(A ⊗_R B)` fitting into the upper right corner of the diagram

```
L_{A/R} ⊗^L_A (A ⊗_R B) ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/B}      ⟶ E
            ‖                     ↑                ↑
L_{A/R} ⊗^L_A (A ⊗_R B) ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/R}      ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/A}
                                  ↑                ↑
                      L_{B/R} ⊗^L_B (A ⊗_R B) ═ L_{B/R} ⊗^L_B (A ⊗_R B)
```

whose top row and right column are distinguished triangles and whose squares commute.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_tensorProduct_nine_diagram
    {u : cotangentComplexDerivedBaseChange R (CommAlgCat.of R A) (A ⊗[R] B) ⟶
      cotangentComplexDerived R (CommAlgCat.of R (A ⊗[R] B))}
    {p : cotangentComplexDerived R (CommAlgCat.of R (A ⊗[R] B)) ⟶
      cotangentComplexDerived A (CommAlgCat.of A (A ⊗[R] B))}
    {d₁ : cotangentComplexDerived A (CommAlgCat.of A (A ⊗[R] B)) ⟶
      (cotangentComplexDerivedBaseChange R (CommAlgCat.of R A) (A ⊗[R] B))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧}
    (h₁ : Triangle.mk u p d₁ ∈ distTriang _)
    {v : cotangentComplexDerivedBaseChange R (CommAlgCat.of R B) (A ⊗[R] B) ⟶
      cotangentComplexDerived R (CommAlgCat.of R (A ⊗[R] B))}
    {q : cotangentComplexDerived R (CommAlgCat.of R (A ⊗[R] B)) ⟶
      cotangentComplexDerived B (CommAlgCat.of B (A ⊗[R] B))}
    {d₂ : cotangentComplexDerived B (CommAlgCat.of B (A ⊗[R] B)) ⟶
      (cotangentComplexDerivedBaseChange R (CommAlgCat.of R B) (A ⊗[R] B))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧}
    (h₂ : Triangle.mk v q d₂ ∈ distTriang _) :
    ∃ (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{max u v} (A ⊗[R] B)))
      (a : cotangentComplexDerived B (CommAlgCat.of B (A ⊗[R] B)) ⟶ E)
      (b : cotangentComplexDerived A (CommAlgCat.of A (A ⊗[R] B)) ⟶ E)
      (e₁ : E ⟶ (cotangentComplexDerivedBaseChange R (CommAlgCat.of R A) (A ⊗[R] B))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (e₂ : E ⟶ (cotangentComplexDerivedBaseChange R (CommAlgCat.of R B) (A ⊗[R] B))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk (u ≫ q) a e₁ ∈ distTriang _ ∧
      Triangle.mk (v ≫ p) b e₂ ∈ distTriang _ ∧
      q ≫ a = p ≫ b ∧ b ≫ e₁ = d₁ ∧ a ≫ e₂ = d₂

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exists_canonical_tensorProduct_nine_diagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09D9**, Equation 92.15.0.1, on the canonical maps. Let `A` and `B` be algebras over
a ring `R`. In `D(A ⊗_R B)` consider

```
L_{A/R} ⊗^L_A (A ⊗_R B) ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/B}      ⟶ E
            ‖                     ↑                ↑
L_{A/R} ⊗^L_A (A ⊗_R B) ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/R}      ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/A}
                                  ↑                ↑
                      L_{B/R} ⊗^L_B (A ⊗_R B) ═ L_{B/R} ⊗^L_B (A ⊗_R B)
```

The middle row is the fundamental triangle of `R → A → A ⊗_R B` and the middle column is the
fundamental triangle of `R → B → A ⊗_R B`. Both are distinguished, with the functoriality maps of
Tag 08PN (`CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₁`, `CommAlgCat.fundamentalMor₂`) and the connecting maps
`CommAlgCat.productFundamentalMor₃`. The first map of the top row is the canonical map
`CommAlgCat.cotangentTensorProductBaseChangeMap`, and the first map of the right column is
`CommAlgCat.cotangentTensorProductBaseChangeMapRight`. The left and the lower squares commute.
There is an object `E` in the upper right corner that makes the top row and the right column
distinguished triangles, makes the upper right square commute, and has connecting maps that
recover those of the middle row and the middle column.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_canonical_tensorProduct_nine_diagram :
    Triangle.mk (fundamentalMor₁ R A (A ⊗[R] B)) (fundamentalMor₂ R A (A ⊗[R] B))
        (productFundamentalMor₃ R A (A ⊗[R] B)) ∈ distTriang _ ∧
    Triangle.mk (fundamentalMor₁ R B (A ⊗[R] B)) (fundamentalMor₂ R B (A ⊗[R] B))
        (productFundamentalMor₃ R B (A ⊗[R] B)) ∈ distTriang _ ∧
    fundamentalMor₁ R A (A ⊗[R] B) ≫ fundamentalMor₂ R B (A ⊗[R] B) =
      cotangentTensorProductBaseChangeMap R A B ∧
    fundamentalMor₁ R B (A ⊗[R] B) ≫ fundamentalMor₂ R A (A ⊗[R] B) =
      cotangentTensorProductBaseChangeMapRight R A B ∧
    ∃ (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B)))
      (a : cotangentComplexDerived B (CommAlgCat.of B (A ⊗[R] B)) ⟶ E)
      (b : cotangentComplexDerived A (CommAlgCat.of A (A ⊗[R] B)) ⟶ E)
      (e₁ : E ⟶ (cotangentComplexDerivedBaseChange R (CommAlgCat.of R A) (A ⊗[R] B))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (e₂ : E ⟶ (cotangentComplexDerivedBaseChange R (CommAlgCat.of R B) (A ⊗[R] B))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
      Triangle.mk (cotangentTensorProductBaseChangeMap R A B) a e₁ ∈ distTriang _ ∧
      Triangle.mk (cotangentTensorProductBaseChangeMapRight R A B) b e₂ ∈ distTriang _ ∧
      fundamentalMor₂ R B (A ⊗[R] B) ≫ a = fundamentalMor₂ R A (A ⊗[R] B) ≫ b ∧
      b ≫ e₁ = productFundamentalMor₃ R A (A ⊗[R] B) ∧
      a ≫ e₂ = productFundamentalMor₃ R B (A ⊗[R] B)
declarations.comment: the diagram 92.15.0.1 on the canonical maps, with nothing assumed: the middle row and column are the fundamental triangles of Proposition 08QX for R → A → A ⊗_R B and R → B → A ⊗_R B, with the functoriality maps of Tag 08PN and their own connecting maps; the top-row and right-column first maps are the 08PN maps of the squares (R → B, A → A ⊗_R B) and (R → A, B → A ⊗_R B); the left and lower squares commute; and an object E makes the top row and the right column distinguished, with the upper right square commuting

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.cotangentComplex_tensorProduct_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
If `A` and `B` are Tor independent `R`-algebras, then the object `E` of Equation 92.15.0.1 —
the cone of the map of complexes
`L_{A/R} ⊗_R B ⊕ L_{B/R} ⊗_R A ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/R}` given by the functoriality maps — is zero;
the canonical map
`L_{A/R} ⊗^L_A (A ⊗_R B) ⊕ L_{B/R} ⊗^L_B (A ⊗_R B) ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/R}` is an isomorphism in
`D(A ⊗_R B)`; and this is represented by the complex `L_{A/R} ⊗_R B ⊕ L_{B/R} ⊗_R A` of
`A ⊗_R B`-modules, the map of complexes being a quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem cotangentComplex_tensorProduct_of_torIndependent
    (hTor : RingTheory.TorIndependence.TorIndependent R A B) :
    IsZero (tensorProductCotangentCone R A B) ∧
      IsIso (biprod.desc (cotangentTensorProductLeftMap R A B)
        (cotangentTensorProductRightMap R A B)) ∧
      QuasiIso (cotangentTensorProductComplexMap R A B)

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.isZero_homology_of_tensorProduct_nine_diagram
declarations.doc:
The cohomology of the object `E` of the nine diagram of Tag 09D9 vanishes in degrees `≥ 1`.

Only the middle column `L_{B/R} ⊗^L_B (A ⊗_R B) ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/R} ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/B}` and the right
column `L_{B/R} ⊗^L_B (A ⊗_R B) ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/A} ⟶ E` of the diagram are used, together with the
vanishing of the cohomology of a cotangent complex in positive degrees.

This is weaker than Tag 09DB, which asserts the vanishing in all degrees `≥ -1`; see the module
documentation for why the extra two degrees are not available from the nine diagram alone.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_homology_of_tensorProduct_nine_diagram
    (h₂ : Triangle.mk v q d₂ ∈ distTriang _)
    (hE₂ : Triangle.mk (v ≫ p) b e₂ ∈ distTriang _) (i : ℤ) (hi : 1 ≤ i) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{max u v} (A ⊗[R] B)) i).obj E)
declarations.comment: the vanishing in degrees i ≥ 1 only, which is the exact ceiling of what the nine diagram of Tag 09D9 determines in this library. The source asserts it for i ≥ -1 and identifies H^{-2}(E) with Tor_1^R(A, B); neither is a consequence of the 09D9 conclusion as formalized here, because exists_tensorProduct_nine_diagram leaves the morphisms of the two fundamental triangles arbitrary -- its host file sits upstream of the proof of Tag 08QX and so cannot name the display's own map L_{A ⊗ B/R} ⟶ L_{A ⊗ B/A} -- and two distinguished triangles on the given objects do not pin those maps down to anything that fixes their homology. At i = 0 the long exact sequence leaves coker H^0(v ≫ p), which the abstract data does not force to vanish

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.tensorProduct_rightColumn_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DB**, for every cone `E` of the canonical map
`L_{B/R} ⊗^L_B (A ⊗_R B) ⟶ L_{A ⊗_R B/A}` of the right column of Equation 92.15.0.1:
`H^i(E) = 0` for `i ≥ -1` and `H^{-2}(E) ≅ Tor_1^R(A, B)` as `A ⊗_R B`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorProduct_rightColumn_homology
    (hE : Triangle.mk (cotangentTensorProductBaseChangeMapRight R A B) b e ∈ distTriang _) :
    (∀ i : ℤ, -1 ≤ i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B)) i).obj E)) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B)) (-2)).obj E ≅
        torOneTensorProductModule R A B)
declarations.comment: for every object E in a distinguished triangle on the canonical map L_{B/R} ⊗^L_B (A ⊗_R B) → L_{A ⊗_R B/A} of the right column of Equation 92.15.0.1, which is how the source's proof describes E: H^i(E) = 0 for i ≥ -1 and H^{-2}(E) ≅ Tor_1^R(A, B) as A ⊗_R B-modules, Tor_1 with its canonical module structure

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.canonicalTensorProductNineDiagram_upperRight_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DB.** Let `R` be a ring and let `A`, `B` be `R`-algebras. The object `E` of
Equation 92.15.0.1 satisfies `H^i(E) = 0` for `i ≥ -1` and `H^{-2}(E) = Tor_1^R(A, B)`, the
latter as an isomorphism of `A ⊗_R B`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalTensorProductNineDiagram_upperRight_homology :
    (∀ i : ℤ, -1 ≤ i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B)) i).obj
        (canonicalTensorProductNineDiagram R A B).upperRight)) ∧
      Nonempty ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B)) (-2)).obj
          (canonicalTensorProductNineDiagram R A B).upperRight ≅
        torOneTensorProductModule R A B)
declarations.comment: the object E of the nine diagram of Tag 09D9, CommAlgCat.canonicalTensorProductNineDiagram: H^i(E) = 0 for i ≥ -1 and H^{-2}(E) ≅ Tor_1^R(A, B) as A ⊗_R B-modules, Tor_1 with its canonical module structure (CommAlgCat.torOneTensorProductModule); the isomorphism itself is CommAlgCat.homologyNegTwoCanonicalUpperRightIsoTorOne

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAtiyahTriangle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DD.** The Atiyah triangle of a `B`-module `M`: the image under
`Lπ_! : D(𝒪) ⟶ D(B)` of the sequence of first principal parts of `M` on `C_{B/A}`.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialAtiyahTriangle :
    Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u))))

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAtiyahTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc: **Stacks 09DD.** The Atiyah triangle is distinguished.
declarations.statement:
theorem polynomialAtiyahTriangle_distinguished :
    polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M ∈ distinguishedTriangles

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAtiyahClass
declarations.doc: **Stacks 09DD.** The Atiyah class of `M`: the last arrow of the Atiyah triangle.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialAtiyahClass :
    (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).obj₃ ⟶ (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).obj₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧
declarations.comment: the Atiyah class, the last arrow of the triangle

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAtiyahTriangle_distinguished_of_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DD.** The Atiyah triangle written with its first and third terms replaced by
objects identified with them: for `L` identified with `Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 M)` and `N` identified
with `Lπ_!(M)`, the sequence `L ⟶ Lπ_!(P¹_{𝒪/A}(M)) ⟶ N ⟶ L[1]` is a distinguished triangle,
whose last arrow is the Atiyah class of `M`.
declarations.statement:
theorem polynomialAtiyahTriangle_distinguished_of_iso
    (L N : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u))))
    (e₁ : (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).obj₁ ≅ L)
    (e₃ : (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).obj₃ ≅ N) :
    Triangle.mk (e₁.inv ≫ (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).mor₁)
        ((polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).mor₂ ≫ e₃.hom)
        (e₃.inv ≫ (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).mor₃ ≫
          (shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u))))
            (1 : ℤ)).map e₁.hom) ∈
      distinguishedTriangles

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exists_atiyahDisplayedTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DD, the displayed triangle.** For a ring map `A → B` and a `B`-module `M` there is
an identification `e₁` of the first term of the Atiyah triangle on the site `C_{B/A}` with
`L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B M` for which

`L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B M ⟶ Lπ_!(P¹_{𝒪/A}(M)) ⟶ M ⟶ (L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B M)[1]`

is a distinguished triangle, the third term being identified with `M` by the canonical
`CommAlgCat.polynomialAtiyahTriangleObj₃Iso`.

Nothing is assumed: the first identification is
`CommAlgCat.nonempty_atiyahFirstVertexDerivedTensorIso`, the chain of [Stacks, Tag 08PT] and
[Tag 08PU] together with the universe-lift comparison of the sections of `B̲ ⊗_𝒪 Ω_{𝒪/A}`, and
the third is [Tag 08QE] through
`Stacks.ChaoticSite.derivedColimitWithCoefficientsRestrictScalarsIso`. It is `e₁` that is
existentially quantified rather than named, because the K-flat resolution computing the derived
tensor product is chosen and not canonical.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_atiyahDisplayedTriangle_distinguished :
    ∃ e₁ : (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).obj₁ ≅ atiyahDisplayedObj₁ A B M,
      Triangle.mk (e₁.inv ≫ (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).mor₁)
          ((polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).mor₂ ≫
            (polynomialAtiyahTriangleObj₃Iso A B M).hom)
          ((polynomialAtiyahTriangleObj₃Iso A B M).inv ≫
            (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).mor₃ ≫
              (shiftFunctor
                (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u))))
                (1 : ℤ)).map e₁.hom) ∈
        distinguishedTriangles
declarations.comment: the displayed triangle `L_{B/A} ⊗^L_B M → Lπ_!(P¹(M)) → M → [1]` at the site C_{B/A} itself, with both endpoint identifications proved rather than assumed

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.polynomialAtiyahClassOfIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DE.** The *Atiyah class* of `M`, in the form displayed by the source. For `L`
identified with `Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 M)` and `N` identified with `Lπ_!(M)` this is the last arrow
`N ⟶ L[1]` of the distinguished triangle of Tag 09DD. Under the source's identifications
`L = L_{B/A} ⊗_B^𝐋 M` and `N = M` it is the Atiyah class `M ⟶ L_{B/A} ⊗_B^𝐋 M[1]`. That it is
the last arrow of the displayed triangle is
`CommAlgCat.polynomialAtiyahClassOfIso_mem_distinguished`.
declarations.statement:
def polynomialAtiyahClassOfIso
    (L N : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u))))
    (e₁ : (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).obj₁ ≅ L)
    (e₃ : (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).obj₃ ≅ N) : N ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧
declarations.comment:
the Atiyah class; the source's identifications
Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 M) = L_{B/A} ⊗_B^L M (Tag 08PT) and Lπ_!(M) = M (Tag 08QE) are not available
here, so they are carried as the extra hypotheses `e₁` and `e₃`, which the source does not have

declarations.name: CommAlgCat.exists_atiyahDisplayedClass_mem_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DE, the Atiyah class of a module.** For a ring map `A → B` and a `B`-module `M`
there is an identification `e₁` of the first term of the Atiyah triangle on the site `C_{B/A}`
with `L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B M` for which the *Atiyah class* of `M`,

`M ⟶ (L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B M)[1]`,

is the last arrow of the distinguished triangle displayed by [Stacks, Tag 09DD]:

`L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B M ⟶ Lπ_!(P¹_{𝒪/A}(M)) ⟶ M ⟶ (L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B M)[1]`.

The class itself is `CommAlgCat.polynomialAtiyahClassOfIso`, the last arrow
`Lπ_!(M̲) ⟶ Lπ_!(Ω_{𝒪/A} ⊗_𝒪 M̲)[1]` of the Atiyah triangle read through identifications of the
endpoints, instantiated at the displayed endpoints: the third by the canonical
`CommAlgCat.polynomialAtiyahTriangleObj₃Iso`, [Stacks, Tag 08QE] at this site, and the first by
`e₁`. Nothing is assumed — `e₁` is produced inside the proof from
`CommAlgCat.nonempty_atiyahFirstVertexDerivedTensorIso`, the chain of [Tag 08PT] and [Tag 08PU]
at this site — and this is the whole of the definition: the arrow, its source `M`, its target
`(L_{B/A} ⊗^𝐋_B M)[1]`, and its being the last arrow of the triangle of (92.17.0.1).

`e₁` is existentially quantified rather than named because the K-flat resolution computing the
derived tensor product is chosen and not canonical, so there is no canonical identification of
the first term to name. That costs nothing: by
`CommAlgCat.polynomialAtiyahClassOfIso_mem_distinguished` the conclusion holds for *every* such
identification, so the existential asserts only that one exists. The module documentation records
why naming one by `Classical.choice` instead would fix a non-canonical choice.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_atiyahDisplayedClass_mem_distinguished :
    ∃ e₁ : (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).obj₁ ≅ atiyahDisplayedObj₁ A B M,
      Triangle.mk (e₁.inv ≫ (polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).mor₁)
          ((polynomialAtiyahTriangle A B M).mor₂ ≫
            (polynomialAtiyahTriangleObj₃Iso A B M).hom)
          (polynomialAtiyahClassOfIso A B M (atiyahDisplayedObj₁ A B M)
            ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
              (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} (B : Type u))) 0).obj M) e₁
            (polynomialAtiyahTriangleObj₃Iso A B M)) ∈
        distinguishedTriangles
declarations.comment: the Atiyah class M → (L_{B/A} ⊗^L_B M)[1] at the site C_{B/A} itself, as the last arrow of the displayed distinguished triangle of (92.17.0.1); both endpoint identifications are proved rather than assumed

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.exists_shortExact_principalPartsSequence'
declarations.doc: **The sequence of principal parts is a short exact sequence.**
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_shortExact_principalPartsSequence' :
    ∃ h : (principalPartsInclusion.{v, u, w, m} φ).app F ≫
        (principalPartsProjection.{v, u, w, m}
          (underlyingRingSheafMapOfSite φ) 1).app F = 0,
      (ShortComplex.mk ((principalPartsInclusion.{v, u, w, m} φ).app F)
        ((principalPartsProjection.{v, u, w, m}
          (underlyingRingSheafMapOfSite φ) 1).app F) h).ShortExact
declarations.comment: the sequence for a term of the standard resolution

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.resolutionPrincipalPartsShortComplex_shortExact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DG.** The extension of principal parts of a term of the standard resolution is
short exact: `0 ⟶ Ω_{P_n/A} ⊗_{P_n} F ⟶ P¹_{P_n/A}(F) ⟶ F ⟶ 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem resolutionPrincipalPartsShortComplex_shortExact (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ)
    (F : targetModules J B) :
    (resolutionPrincipalPartsShortComplex J f n F).ShortExact

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.atiyahTriangle_distinguished_of_iso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DH.** The Atiyah triangle of a sheaf of `B`-modules, written with its first and
third terms replaced by objects identified with them: for `L` identified with
`Lπ_!(Ω_{P_•/A} ⊗_{P_•} F)` and `N` identified with `Lπ_!(F)`, the sequence
`L ⟶ Lπ_!(P¹_{P_•/A}(F)) ⟶ N ⟶ L[1]` is a distinguished triangle in `D(B)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem atiyahTriangle_distinguished_of_iso
    (G : DerivedCategory M ⥤ DerivedCategory (targetModules J B))
    [G.CommShift ℤ] [G.IsTriangulated] {S : ShortComplex M} (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (L N : DerivedCategory (targetModules J B))
    (e₁ : (atiyahTriangle J G hS).obj₁ ≅ L) (e₃ : (atiyahTriangle J G hS).obj₃ ≅ N) :
    Triangle.mk (e₁.inv ≫ (atiyahTriangle J G hS).mor₁)
        ((atiyahTriangle J G hS).mor₂ ≫ e₃.hom)
        (e₃.inv ≫ (atiyahTriangle J G hS).mor₃ ≫
          (shiftFunctor (DerivedCategory (targetModules J B)) (1 : ℤ)).map e₁.hom) ∈
      distinguishedTriangles
declarations.comment: the distinguished triangle; `M`, `G`, `hS`, `e₁` and `e₃` carry the inputs the library does not yet have — the category of simplicial `P_•`-modules known to be abelian, the functor Lπ_! of Tag 09D3, the simplicial short exact sequence of Tag 09DG, and the identifications of Tags 08PU and 08QE. See the implementation notes

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.sheafAtiyahTriangle_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09DH], Equation 92.19.0.2.** For a homomorphism `f : 𝒜 ⟶ ℬ` of sheaves of
commutative rings on a site and a sheaf of `ℬ`-modules `ℱ`,

`L_{ℬ/𝒜} ⊗^𝐋_ℬ ℱ ⟶ Lπ_!(P¹_{𝒫/π^{-1}𝒜}(ℱ)) ⟶ ℱ ⟶ (L_{ℬ/𝒜} ⊗^𝐋_ℬ ℱ)[1]`

is a distinguished triangle in `D(ℬ)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheafAtiyahTriangle_distinguished (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (targetRing J (B := B))) :
    sheafAtiyahTriangle J f F ∈ distinguishedTriangles

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.atiyahClass
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DI.** The *Atiyah class* of a sheaf of `B`-modules: the map
`F ⟶ L_{B/A} ⊗_B^L F[1]`, realised as the last arrow `N ⟶ L[1]` of the Atiyah triangle of
Tag 09DH, read through the identifications of its first and third terms.
declarations.statement:
def atiyahClass (G : DerivedCategory M ⥤ DerivedCategory (targetModules J B))
    [G.CommShift ℤ] [G.IsTriangulated] {S : ShortComplex M} (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (L N : DerivedCategory (targetModules J B))
    (e₁ : (atiyahTriangle J G hS).obj₁ ≅ L) (e₃ : (atiyahTriangle J G hS).obj₃ ≅ N) :
    N ⟶ L⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧
declarations.comment: the Atiyah class, as the last arrow of the triangle of Tag 09DH; `M`, `G`, `hS`, `e₁` and `e₃` carry the same five inputs the library does not yet have that `atiyahTriangle_distinguished_of_iso` carries, so `N` stands for `F` and `L` for `L_{B/A} ⊗_B^L F`. See the implementation notes

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sheaf.sheafAtiyahClass
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09DI], Definition 92.19.1: the Atiyah class of a sheaf of modules.** For a
homomorphism `f : 𝒜 ⟶ ℬ` of sheaves of commutative rings on a site and a sheaf of `ℬ`-modules `ℱ`,
the *Atiyah class* of `ℱ` is the morphism

`ℱ ⟶ (L_{ℬ/𝒜} ⊗^𝐋_ℬ ℱ)[1]`

of `D(ℬ)` which is the last arrow of the triangle (92.19.0.2) of [Stacks, Tag 09DH]: the image
under the `Lπ_!` of Remark 09D3 of the short exact sequence of first principal parts of the
standard resolution (Tag 09DG), read through the identifications
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.atiyahTriangleFirstTermIso` and
`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.atiyahTriangleThirdTermIso` of its outer terms.
declarations.statement:
def sheafAtiyahClass (F : SheafOfModules.{u} (targetRing J (B := B))) :
    DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        ((HomologicalComplex.single (SheafOfModules.{u} (targetRing J (B := B)))
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj F) ⟶
      (((derivedTensorProductFunctor B).obj
          (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (cotangentComplex.{u, u, u} J f))).obj
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          ((HomologicalComplex.single (Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.Modules B)
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).obj F)))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.nonempty_upperRightCorner
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DK.** Two distinguished triangles sharing their middle vertex have an upper right
corner: an object `E` turning both the top row `A₁ ⟶ C₂ ⟶ E` and the right column
`A₂ ⟶ C₁ ⟶ E` of the diagram into distinguished triangles, with the remaining square
commutative.

This is the nine diagram of Tag 05R0 applied to the lower left square of the diagram, whose
left column and bottom row are the contractible triangles `0 ⟶ A₁ ⟶ A₁` and `0 ⟶ A₂ ⟶ A₂`;
the square commutes because both of its composites leave a zero object. The identity second
arrow of each contractible triangle is what identifies the first arrow of the third row with
`α₁ ≫ β₂` and the first arrow of the third column with `α₂ ≫ β₁`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_upperRightCorner (h₁ : Triangle.mk α₁ β₁ γ₁ ∈ distTriang D)
    (h₂ : Triangle.mk α₂ β₂ γ₂ ∈ distTriang D) :
    Nonempty (UpperRightCorner α₁ β₁ α₂ β₂)
declarations.comment: existence of the upper right corner, in a triangulated category

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Triangulated.UpperRightCorner.ofBiprodCone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DK.** Any cone of the map `A₁ ⊞ A₂ ⟶ M` out of the direct sum, with components
the first arrows `α₁` and `α₂` of the two given triangles, is an upper right corner.

The two arrows into the cone come from the octahedron axiom for the two factorizations of
`biprod.desc α₁ α₂` through the biproduct inclusions: factoring through `biprod.inr` has
`A₁` as the cone of the first map and `C₂` as the cone of the composite, so the octahedron is
the top row, and factoring through `biprod.inl` has `A₂` and `C₁`, so the octahedron is the
right column. In each case the first arrow of the octahedron becomes the required composite
after precomposition with the complementary inclusion.
declarations.comment: the cone of the direct sum as an upper right corner, in a triangulated category

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fibreProductCotangentCorner
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DK.** Let `p : W ⟶ X` and `q : W ⟶ Y` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`
with `p ≫ f = q ≫ g` for morphisms `f : X ⟶ Z` and `g : Y ⟶ Z`, for instance the two projections
of `W = X ×_Z Y`. In `D(𝒪_W)` the diagram

```
Lp^*L_{X/Z} ──────▶ L_{W/Y} ──────▶ E
     ‖                ▲             ▲
Lp^*L_{X/Z} ──────▶ L_{W/Z} ──────▶ L_{W/X}
                      ▲             ▲
                Lq^*L_{Y/Z} ═════ Lq^*L_{Y/Z}
```

exists: its middle row is the transitivity triangle of Stacks 08V1 for `W ⟶ X ⟶ Z`, its middle
column the one for `W ⟶ Y ⟶ Z`, and the object `E` of the upper right corner, with its two
incoming and two outgoing arrows, turns the top row and the right column into distinguished
triangles and makes the remaining square commute. The value of the definition is that upper
right corner, together with the distinguishedness of the two middle triangles and the triangle
`Lp^*L_{X/Z} ⊕ Lq^*L_{Y/Z} ⟶ L_{W/Z} ⟶ E ⟶`, which exhibits `E` as the cone of the map out of
the direct sum.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fibreProductCotangentCorner (h : p ≫ f = q ≫ g) :
    { E : Triangulated.UpperRightCorner (transitivityUnit p f) (transitivityCounit p f)
          (fibreProductColumnUnit h) (fibreProductColumnCounit h) //
      (∃ δ : cotangentComplexDerived B S hS p ⟶
          ((derivedPullbackULift p).obj (cotangentComplexDerived B S hS f))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
        Triangle.mk (transitivityUnit p f) (transitivityCounit p f) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (smallEtaleModulesULift B S hS W))) ∧
      (∃ δ : cotangentComplexDerived B S hS q ⟶
          ((derivedPullbackULift q).obj (cotangentComplexDerived B S hS g))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧,
        Triangle.mk (fibreProductColumnUnit h) (fibreProductColumnCounit h) δ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (smallEtaleModulesULift B S hS W))) ∧
      ∃ (ε : cotangentComplexDerived B S hS (p ≫ f) ⟶ E.obj)
        (ζ : E.obj ⟶ ((derivedPullbackULift p).obj (cotangentComplexDerived B S hS f) ⊞
          (derivedPullbackULift q).obj (cotangentComplexDerived B S hS g))⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
        Triangle.mk (fibreProductBiprodMap h) ε ζ ∈
          distTriang (DerivedCategory (smallEtaleModulesULift B S hS W)) }
declarations.comment: the diagram for a commutative square, in particular for the two projections of a fibre product; `E` is the cone of the map out of the direct sum

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fiberProductCotangentCorner
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DK**, for the fibre product `X ×_Z Y` of algebraic spaces (Stacks 02X2) with its
projections `p` and `q`: the diagram of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fibreProductCotangentCorner` in `D(𝒪_{X ×_Z Y})`, built on the
transitivity triangles of `X ×_Z Y ⟶ X ⟶ Z` and `X ×_Z Y ⟶ Y ⟶ Z`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def fiberProductCotangentCorner
declarations.comment: the diagram for the fibre product `X ×_Z Y` and its two projections

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fiberProduct_cotangentComplex_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DL.** Let `X ⟶ Z` and `Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, and let
`W = X ×_Z Y` with projections `p` and `q`. If `X` and `Y` are Tor independent over `Z`, then the
object `E` of Stacks 09DK, i.e. any object fitting into the upper right corner of its diagram, is
zero, and the canonical map `Lp^*L_{X/Z} ⊕ Lq^*L_{Y/Z} ⟶ L_{W/Z}` is an isomorphism, so that
`L_{X ×_Z Y/Z} ≅ Lp^*L_{X/Z} ⊕ Lq^*L_{Y/Z}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiberProduct_cotangentComplex_of_torIndependent (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    (hTor : TorIndependent X.2 Y.2 Z.2 f.hom g.hom) :
    (∀ E : Triangulated.UpperRightCorner (transitivityUnit (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst
        f.hom g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ X) f) (transitivityCounit
            (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS
                f g) ⟶ X) f)
      (fibreProductColumnUnit (AlgebraicSpaces.isPullback_fiberProduct B S hS f g).w)
      (fibreProductColumnCounit (AlgebraicSpaces.isPullback_fiberProduct B S hS f g).w),
      IsZero E.obj) ∧
    IsIso (fibreProductBiprodMap (AlgebraicSpaces.isPullback_fiberProduct B S hS f g).w)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.upperRightCorner_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DM, for a cartesian square.** Let `p : W ⟶ X`, `q : W ⟶ Y`, `f : X ⟶ Z`,
`g : Y ⟶ Z` be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces over `S` and let `E` be an object fitting
into the upper right corner of the diagram of Stacks 09DK. Then `H^0(E) = H^{-1}(E) = 0`, and at
every geometric point `w̄` of `W`, with `R = 𝒪_{Z, f(p(w̄))}`, `A = 𝒪_{X, p(w̄)}`,
`B = 𝒪_{Y, q(w̄)}` and `C = 𝒪_{W, w̄}` the étale local rings and the canonical maps between them,
`H^{-2}(E)_{w̄} ≅ Tor_1^R(A, B) ⊗_{A ⊗_R B} C` as `C`-modules, `χ : A ⊗_R B → C` being the map
induced by the canonical maps `A → C` and `B → C`. The stalk `H^{-2}(E)_{w̄}` is a module over the
stalk of the structure sheaf, which is identified with `C` by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.smallEtaleStructureSheafULiftStalkEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
theorem upperRightCorner_homology (hpb : IsPullback p q f g)
    (E : Triangulated.UpperRightCorner (transitivityUnit p f) (transitivityCounit p f)
      (fibreProductColumnUnit hpb.w) (fibreProductColumnCounit hpb.w)) :
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (smallEtaleModulesULift B S hS W) 0).obj E.obj) ∧
    IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (smallEtaleModulesULift B S hS W) (-1)).obj E.obj) ∧
    ∀ w : GeometricPoint B S hS W.1,
    letI : Algebra (etaleLocalRing B S hS Z.1 (geometricPointMap f.hom (geometricPointMap p.hom w)))
        (etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 (geometricPointMap p.hom w)) :=
      (etaleLocalRingMap X.2 f.hom (geometricPointMap p.hom w)).toAlgebra
    letI : Algebra (etaleLocalRing B S hS Z.1 (geometricPointMap f.hom (geometricPointMap p.hom w)))
        (etaleLocalRing B S hS Y.1 (geometricPointMap q.hom w)) :=
      ((eqToHom (congrArg (etaleLocalRing B S hS Z.1)
          (congrArg (fun k : W ⟶ Z => geometricPointMap k.hom w) hpb.w)) ≫
        CommRingCat.ofHom (etaleLocalRingMap Y.2 g.hom (geometricPointMap q.hom w))).hom).toAlgebra
    ∃ χ : etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 (geometricPointMap p.hom w) ⊗[etaleLocalRing B S hS Z.1
        (geometricPointMap f.hom (geometricPointMap p.hom w))]
        etaleLocalRing B S hS Y.1 (geometricPointMap q.hom w) →+* etaleLocalRing B S hS W.1 w,
      χ.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom = etaleLocalRingMap W.2 p.hom w ∧
      χ.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom = etaleLocalRingMap W.2 q.hom w ∧
      Nonempty ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
          (smallEtaleStructureSheafULiftStalkEquiv B S hS W w).toRingHom).obj
          ((Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing (geometricSitePoint B S hS W w)
            (smallEtaleStructureSheafULift B S hS W)).obj
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (smallEtaleModulesULift B S hS W) (-2)).obj E.obj)) ≅
        (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1} χ).obj
          (CommAlgCat.torOneTensorProductModule _ _ _))
declarations.comment: for every cartesian square of algebraic spaces, in particular for the fibre product with its two projections (`fiberProduct_upperRightCorner_homology`), and every object E fitting into the upper right corner of the diagram of 09DK

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.fiberProduct_upperRightCorner_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DM.** Let `X ⟶ Z` and `Y ⟶ Z` be morphisms of algebraic spaces over `S`, let
`W = X ×_Z Y` with projections `p` and `q`, and let `E` be the object of Stacks 09DK, i.e. any
object fitting into the upper right corner of its diagram. Then `H^0(E) = H^{-1}(E) = 0`, and
for a geometric point `w̄` of `W`,
`H^{-2}(E)_{w̄} ≅ Tor_1^R(A, B) ⊗_{A ⊗_R B} C` as `C`-modules, where `R = 𝒪_{Z, f(p(w̄))}`,
`A = 𝒪_{X, p(w̄)}`, `B = 𝒪_{Y, q(w̄)}` and `C = 𝒪_{W, w̄}` are the étale local rings,
`Tor_1^R(A, B)` carries its canonical `A ⊗_R B`-module structure, and `χ : A ⊗_R B → C` is the map
induced by the canonical maps of étale local rings.
declarations.statement:
theorem fiberProduct_upperRightCorner_homology (f : X ⟶ Z) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    ∀ E : Triangulated.UpperRightCorner (transitivityUnit (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom
        g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ X) f) (transitivityCounit
            (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS
                f g) ⟶ X) f)
      (fibreProductColumnUnit (AlgebraicSpaces.isPullback_fiberProduct B S hS f g).w)
      (fibreProductColumnCounit (AlgebraicSpaces.isPullback_fiberProduct B S hS f g).w),
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (smallEtaleModulesULift B S hS
          (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g)) 0).obj E.obj) ∧
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (smallEtaleModulesULift B S hS
          (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g)) (-1)).obj E.obj) ∧
      ∀ w : GeometricPoint B S hS (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g).1,
      letI : Algebra (etaleLocalRing B S hS Z.1 (geometricPointMap f.hom (geometricPointMap
          (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f
              g) ⟶ X).hom w)))
          (etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom
              g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ X).hom w)) :=
        (etaleLocalRingMap X.2 f.hom (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom
            g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ X).hom w)).toAlgebra
      letI : Algebra (etaleLocalRing B S hS Z.1 (geometricPointMap f.hom (geometricPointMap
          (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f
              g) ⟶ X).hom w)))
          (etaleLocalRing B S hS Y.1 (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd f.hom
              g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ Y).hom w)) :=
        ((eqToHom (congrArg (etaleLocalRing B S hS Z.1)
            (congrArg (fun k : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ Z => geometricPointMap
                k.hom w) (AlgebraicSpaces.isPullback_fiberProduct B S hS f g).w)) ≫
          CommRingCat.ofHom (etaleLocalRingMap Y.2 g.hom (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk
              (pullback.snd f.hom g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ Y).hom
                  w))).hom).toAlgebra
      ∃ χ : etaleLocalRing B S hS X.1 (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom
          g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ X).hom w) ⊗[etaleLocalRing B S hS Z.1
          (geometricPointMap f.hom (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom
              g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ X).hom w))]
          etaleLocalRing B S hS Y.1 (geometricPointMap (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd f.hom
              g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ Y).hom w) →+* etaleLocalRing B S
                  hS (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g).1 w,
        χ.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeftRingHom = etaleLocalRingMap
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g).2 (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.fst f.hom
                g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ X).hom w ∧
        χ.comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight.toRingHom = etaleLocalRingMap
            (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g).2 (ObjectProperty.homMk (pullback.snd f.hom
                g.hom) : (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) ⟶ Y).hom w ∧
        Nonempty ((ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1}
            (smallEtaleStructureSheafULiftStalkEquiv B S hS (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f
                g) w).toRingHom).obj
            ((Stacks.sheafModuleFiberOfCommRing (geometricSitePoint B S hS
                (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g) w)
              (smallEtaleStructureSheafULift B S hS (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g))).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (smallEtaleModulesULift B S hS
                  (AlgebraicSpaces.fiberProduct B S hS f g)) (-2)).obj E.obj)) ≅
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars.{u + 1, u + 1, u + 1} χ).obj
            (CommAlgCat.torOneTensorProductModule _ _ _))
declarations.comment: for the fibre product X ×_Z Y with its two projections and every object E fitting into the upper right corner of the diagram of 09DK: H^0(E) = H^{-1}(E) = 0, and H^{-2}(E)_w ≅ Tor_1^R(A, B) ⊗_{A ⊗_R B} C as C-modules for the etale local rings R, A, B, C

declarations.name: IsGalois.exists_artinSchreier_of_finrank_eq_char
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09DY**.
Let `F` be a field of characteristic `p > 0` and let `K/F` be a Galois extension of degree `p`.
Then `K = F(b)` for some `b ∈ K` whose Artin–Schreier expression `b^p - b` lies in `F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsGalois.exists_artinSchreier_of_finrank_eq_char
    {F K : Type*} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [FiniteDimensional F K] [IsGalois F K]
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] [CharP F p] (hp : Module.finrank F K = p) :
    ∃ b : K, F⟮b⟯ = ⊤ ∧ b ^ p - b ∈ Set.range (algebraMap F K)

declarations.name: IsLocalRing.exists_finiteEtale_directed_residueField_algEquiv
declarations.doc:
**A separable algebraic residue field extension is realized by a colimit of finite étale
extensions** (Stacks 09E0). Let `(R, 𝔪, k)` be a local ring and let `K` be a separable algebraic
extension of `k`. Then there are a local ring `R'`, a local ring map `R → R'`, and a directed
family `𝒮` of `R`-subalgebras of `R'` whose union is `R'`, each a local ring finite étale over
`R`, such that the residue field of `R'` is isomorphic to `K` as an extension of `k`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsLocalRing.exists_finiteEtale_directed_residueField_algEquiv (R : Type u)
    [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (K : Type v) [Field K] [Algebra (ResidueField R) K]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable (ResidueField R) K] :
    ∃ (R' : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : Algebra R R') (_ : IsLocalRing R')
      (_ : IsLocalHom (algebraMap R R')) (𝒮 : Set (Subalgebra R R')),
      DirectedOn (· ≤ ·) 𝒮 ∧
      (∀ x : R', ∃ S ∈ 𝒮, x ∈ S) ∧
      (∀ S ∈ 𝒮, Module.Finite R S ∧ Algebra.Etale R S ∧ IsLocalRing S) ∧
      Nonempty (ResidueField R' ≃ₐ[ResidueField R] K)
declarations.comment:
The source's directed set `I` and system of finite étale extensions `R ⊂ R_i` with
`R' = colim R_i` appear as a directed family `𝒮` of finite étale local `R`-subalgebras of `R'`
covering `R'`, which is equivalent since the transition maps of such a system are injective. `K`
is allowed to live in a universe of its own, the source's case being `v = u`. See the module
docstring.

declarations.name: IsNagataRing.exists_pow_eq_iff_exists_pow_eq_adicCompletion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09E2.** Let `(A, 𝔪)` be a local domain which is a Nagata ring and has
characteristic `p ≠ 0`, and let `A^ = lim_n A ⧸ 𝔪ⁿ` be its completion. An element `a : A` has a
`p`-th root in `A` if and only if it has one in `A^`.

The source also assumes `A` Noetherian, which is the first conjunct of `IsNagataRing A`, and
assumes `p` prime, which follows from `p ≠ 0` because `A` is a domain. The source's
characteristic assumption is on the fraction field of `A`; that is the same condition as
`CharP A p`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem IsNagataRing.exists_pow_eq_iff_exists_pow_eq_adicCompletion {A : Type*}
    [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsDomain A] (hA : IsNagataRing A) {p : ℕ} [CharP A p]
    (hp : p ≠ 0) (a : A) :
    (∃ b : A, b ^ p = a) ↔
      ∃ α : AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A,
        α ^ p = algebraMap A (AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A) a
declarations.comment: Stated as a biconditional, the reverse implication being `map_pow` on the completion map. Noetherian is absorbed into `IsNagataRing` (Definition 032R(2)), primality of `p` into `p ≠ 0` over a domain (`CharP.char_is_prime_or_zero`), and the characteristic of `Frac A` is read off `A`. The completion is `AdicCompletion (maximalIdeal A) A` as in Tag 032X.

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsExtension
declarations.doc: An extension of discrete valuation rings is an injective local algebra map.
declarations.statement:
class IsExtension (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain B]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [Algebra A B] : Prop extends
    FaithfulSMul A B, IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.ramificationIndex
declarations.doc: The ramification index of an extension of discrete valuation rings.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev ramificationIndex (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain B]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsExtension A B] : ℕ

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsWeaklyUnramified
declarations.doc: An extension of DVRs is weakly unramified when its ramification index is one.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsWeaklyUnramified (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain B]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsExtension A B] : Prop

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.residueDegree
declarations.doc: The residue degree of an extension of discrete valuation rings.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev residueDegree (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain B]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsExtension A B] : ℕ

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.ramificationIndex_characterization
declarations.doc:
The ramification index is positive, is the unique positive exponent expressing the extended
maximal ideal as a power of the maximal ideal upstairs, and is the exponent relating any choices
of uniformizers up to a unit.
declarations.statement:
theorem ramificationIndex_characterization (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [IsExtension A B] :
    1 ≤ ramificationIndex A B ∧
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A B) =
        IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ ramificationIndex A B ∧
      (∀ e : ℕ, 1 ≤ e →
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A).map (algebraMap A B) =
          IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B ^ e →
        e = ramificationIndex A B) ∧
      ∀ πA : A, Irreducible πA → ∀ πB : B, Irreducible πB →
        ∃ u : Bˣ, algebraMap A B πA = (u : B) * πB ^ ramificationIndex A B

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.residueField_finite_and_ramificationIdx_mul_residueDegree_le_finrank
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be an injective local map of discrete valuation rings, with compatible fraction
fields `K → L`. If `L / K` is finite, then the residue-field extension is finite and its degree,
multiplied by the ramification index of `B / A`, is at most `[L : K]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem residueField_finite_and_ramificationIdx_mul_residueDegree_le_finrank
    (A B K L : Type*)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [FaithfulSMul A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)]
    [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    [Field L] [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing B L]
    [Algebra A L] [Algebra K L]
    [IsScalarTower A B L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    [Module.Finite K L] :
    Module.Finite (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) ∧
      (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B).ramificationIdx A *
          Module.finrank (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) ≤
        Module.finrank K L

declarations.name: Stacks.DiscreteValuationRing.Ramification.ramificationIdx_eq_prime_pow_of_purelyInseparable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09E6**.
Let `A ⊂ B` be an extension of discrete valuation rings inducing the field extension `K ⊂ L`. If
`K` has characteristic `p` with `p` prime and `L / K` is purely inseparable, then the ramification
index `e` of `B` over `A` is a power of `p`: there is `m ≥ 0` with `e = p ^ m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem ramificationIdx_eq_prime_pow_of_purelyInseparable (A B : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A]
    [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B] [Algebra A B]
    [FaithfulSMul A B] [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] (K L : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K]
    [IsFractionRing A K] [Field L] [Algebra B L] [IsFractionRing B L] [Algebra A L] [Algebra K L]
    [IsScalarTower A B L] [IsScalarTower A K L] (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) [CharP K p]
    [IsPurelyInseparable K L] : ∃ m : ℕ, ramificationIdx A B = p ^ m

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.formallySmooth_iff_weaklyUnramified_and_isSeparableExtension
declarations.doc:
An extension of discrete valuation rings is formally smooth for the maximal-ideal-adic
topology if and only if it is weakly unramified and its possibly nonalgebraic residue-field
extension is separable.
declarations.statement:
theorem formallySmooth_iff_weaklyUnramified_and_isSeparableExtension
    (A : Type u) (B : Type v)
    [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsDiscreteValuationRing B]
    [Algebra A B] [IsExtension A B] :
    RingHom.FormallySmoothNAdic.{max u v} (algebraMap A B)
        (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal B) ↔
      IsWeaklyUnramified A B ∧
        Algebra.IsSeparableExtension (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
          (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B)

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.integralClosure_finite_dedekind_and_degree_eq_sum_ramification_inertia
declarations.doc:
Let `A` be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field `K`, and let `L / K` be a finite
separable extension. The integral closure `B` of `A` in `L` is finite and Noetherian over `A`,
has dimension one, and is Dedekind. Its maximal ideals `m i` are precisely the primes over the
maximal ideal of `A`; every `B_(m i)` is a discrete valuation ring, and
`[L : K] = ∑ i, e(m i / m_A) * f(m i / m_A)`. If `A` is henselian—or, in particular,
maximal-ideal-adically complete—there is exactly one such maximal ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem integralClosure_finite_dedekind_and_degree_eq_sum_ramification_inertia
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    Module.Finite A B ∧
      IsNoetherianRing B ∧
      ringKrullDim B = 1 ∧
      IsDedekindDomain B ∧
      ∃ (n : ℕ) (m : Fin n → Ideal B),
        ∃ hmax : ∀ i, (m i).IsMaximal,
          (∀ q : Ideal B, q.IsMaximal ↔ ∃! i, m i = q) ∧
          (∀ i, (m i).LiesOver (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A)) ∧
          (∀ i, letI : (m i).IsPrime := (hmax i).isPrime
            IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime (m i))) ∧
          Module.finrank K L = ∑ i, (m i).ramificationIdx A * (m i).inertiaDeg A ∧
          (HenselianLocalRing A → n = 1) ∧
          (IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) A → n = 1)

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsUnramifiedWithRespectTo
declarations.doc:
An extension is unramified with respect to a discrete valuation ring `A` if, at every
maximal ideal of the integral closure lying over the maximal ideal of `A`, the ramification index
is one and the induced residue field extension is separable.
declarations.statement:
def IsUnramifiedWithRespectTo
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L] : Prop

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsTamelyRamifiedWithRespectTo
declarations.doc:
An extension is tamely ramified with respect to `A` if every induced residue field extension
is separable and, in positive residue characteristic, every ramification index is relatively
prime to that characteristic. This is `Stacks.KummerExtension.IsTamelyRamified`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsTamelyRamifiedWithRespectTo
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L] : Prop

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.IsTotallyRamifiedWithRespectTo
declarations.doc:
An extension is totally ramified with respect to `A` if its integral closure has a unique
maximal ideal above that of `A` and its induced residue field extension is trivial. This is
`Stacks.KummerExtension.IsTotallyRamified`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev IsTotallyRamifiedWithRespectTo
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [Algebra.IsSeparable K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L] : Prop

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.galAction_transitive_on_maximalIdeals_integralClosure
declarations.doc:
For a finite Galois extension `L / K`, the canonical action of `Gal(L/K)` on the integral
closure of a discrete valuation ring `A` in `L` is transitive on its maximal ideals.
declarations.statement:
theorem galAction_transitive_on_maximalIdeals_integralClosure
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsGalois K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    ∀ P Q : Ideal B, P.IsMaximal → Q.IsMaximal →
      ∃ σ : Gal(L/K), σ • P = Q

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_uniform_ramificationIdx_inertiaDeg_and_finrank_eq
declarations.doc:
In a finite Galois extension of the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring, all primes
of the integral closure over the maximal ideal have the same positive ramification index and
inertia degree. The field degree is the number of these primes times the two common values.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_uniform_ramificationIdx_inertiaDeg_and_finrank_eq
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsGalois K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    let p := IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A
    ∃ e f : ℕ,
      1 ≤ e ∧
      1 ≤ f ∧
      (∀ P : p.primesOver B, P.1.ramificationIdx A = e ∧ P.1.inertiaDeg A = f) ∧
      (p.primesOver B).ncard * e * f = Module.finrank K L

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.under_eq_maximalIdeal_and_ker_stabilizerHom_eq_inertia
declarations.doc:
The decomposition and the inertia group at a maximal ideal `P` of the integral closure `B`
of a discrete valuation ring `A` in a field extension `L / K`.

The decomposition group is the stabilizer `{σ ∈ Gal(L/K) | σ P = P}`, and the ideal of `A` below
`P` is the maximal ideal, so the residue extension the decomposition group acts on really is
`κ(P) / κ_A`. The inertia group is the kernel of that action: it is `Ideal.inertia`, sitting
inside the decomposition group, and an element of the decomposition group lies in it exactly when
it acts trivially on `κ(P)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem under_eq_maximalIdeal_and_ker_stabilizerHom_eq_inertia
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (P : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [P.IsMaximal] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    let D := MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) P
    let I := P.inertia Gal(L/K)
    (∀ σ : Gal(L/K), σ ∈ D ↔ σ • P = P) ∧
      P.under A = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ∧
      I ≤ D ∧
      (Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom P (P.under A) Gal(L/K)).ker = I.subgroupOf D ∧
      (∀ σ : D, σ ∈ (Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom P (P.under A) Gal(L/K)).ker ↔
        ∀ b : B, Ideal.Quotient.mk P ((σ : Gal(L/K)) • b) = Ideal.Quotient.mk P b)
declarations.comment:
The decomposition group is `MulAction.stabilizer` and the inertia group is
`Ideal.inertia`, both of which Mathlib already has for an arbitrary action; what is recorded here
is that they are the source's two groups, the ideal below `P` being the maximal ideal of `A` so
that the extension acted on is `κ(P)/κ_A`. Stated without the fraction-field, finiteness and
Galois hypotheses, which the comparison does not use, so the source's setting is a special
case.

registrations.name: MulAction.stabilizer
registrations.comment: (1), the decomposition group

registrations.name: Ideal.inertia
registrations.comment: (2), the inertia group

registrations.name: Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom
registrations.comment: The action of the decomposition group on the residue algebra

registrations.name: Ideal.Quotient.ker_stabilizerHom
registrations.comment: The inertia group as the kernel of the residue-algebra action

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.residueField_normal_and_stabilizerHom_surjective_of_isGalois
declarations.doc:
In a finite Galois extension of the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring, every
residue extension at a maximal ideal of the integral closure is normal, and its decomposition
group surjects onto the relative automorphism group. Separability of one such residue extension is
equivalent to separability of all of them; when this holds, the fixed residue extension is Galois
and the same canonical map is surjective onto its Galois group.
declarations.statement:
theorem residueField_normal_and_stabilizerHom_surjective_of_isGalois
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsGalois K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (P : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [P.IsMaximal] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    let p := P.under A
    letI : Field (A ⧸ p) := Ideal.Quotient.field p
    letI : Field (B ⧸ P) := Ideal.Quotient.field P
    Normal (A ⧸ p) (B ⧸ P) ∧
      Function.Surjective (Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom P p Gal(L/K)) ∧
      ((∃ (Q : Ideal B) (_hQ : Q.IsMaximal),
          let q := Q.under A
          letI : Field (A ⧸ q) := Ideal.Quotient.field q
          letI : Field (B ⧸ Q) := Ideal.Quotient.field Q
          Algebra.IsSeparable (A ⧸ q) (B ⧸ Q)) ↔
        (∀ (Q : Ideal B) (_hQ : Q.IsMaximal),
          let q := Q.under A
          letI : Field (A ⧸ q) := Ideal.Quotient.field q
          letI : Field (B ⧸ Q) := Ideal.Quotient.field Q
          Algebra.IsSeparable (A ⧸ q) (B ⧸ Q))) ∧
      ((∃ (Q : Ideal B) (_hQ : Q.IsMaximal),
          let q := Q.under A
          letI : Field (A ⧸ q) := Ideal.Quotient.field q
          letI : Field (B ⧸ Q) := Ideal.Quotient.field Q
          Algebra.IsSeparable (A ⧸ q) (B ⧸ Q)) →
        IsGalois (A ⧸ p) (B ⧸ P) ∧
          Function.Surjective (Ideal.Quotient.stabilizerHom P p Gal(L/K)))

declarations.name: IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_wildInertia_exact_and_tameInertia_equiv_rootsOfUnity
declarations.doc:
The inertia group at a maximal ideal of the integral closure in a finite Galois extension
has a canonical wild–tame exact sequence. Wild inertia consists precisely of the elements of
inertia acting trivially on the maximal ideal modulo its square; it is normal in the decomposition
group and is a `p`-group in positive residue characteristic (and trivial in characteristic zero).
The tame quotient is cyclic of prime-to-`p` order and is canonically isomorphic to the
corresponding roots of unity in the residue field. If the residue extension is separable, wild
inertia is also the kernel of the action on `B / P²`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_wildInertia_exact_and_tameInertia_equiv_rootsOfUnity
    (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A]
    (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
    (L : Type*) [Field L] [Algebra K L] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsGalois K L] [Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
    (P : Ideal (integralClosure A L)) [P.IsMaximal] :
    let B := integralClosure A L
    letI := IsIntegralClosure.MulSemiringAction A K L B
    let D := MulAction.stabilizer Gal(L/K) P
    let I := P.inertia Gal(L/K)
    let inclusion : I →* D := I.subtype.codRestrict D
      (fun σ ↦ Ideal.inertia_le_stabilizer (M := Gal(L/K)) P σ.property)
    let e := P.ramificationIdx A
    let p := ringChar (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
    ∃ W : Subgroup I, ∃ _hW : W.Normal,
      (W.map inclusion).Normal ∧
      (∀ σ : I, σ ∈ W ↔ ∀ b : B, b ∈ P → (σ : Gal(L/K)) • b - b ∈ P ^ 2) ∧
      (∀ σ : D, σ ∈ W.map inclusion ↔
        (σ : Gal(L/K)) ∈ I ∧ ∀ b : B, b ∈ P → σ • b - b ∈ P ^ 2) ∧
      (0 < p → IsPGroup p W) ∧
      (p = 0 → W = ⊥) ∧
      (letI : Field (A ⧸ P.under A) := Ideal.Quotient.field (P.under A)
       Algebra.IsSeparable (A ⧸ P.under A) (B ⧸ P) →
         ∀ σ : D, σ ∈ W.map inclusion ↔ ∀ b : B, σ • b - b ∈ P ^ 2) ∧
      ∃ θ : I →* rootsOfUnity e (B ⧸ P),
        Function.Injective W.subtype ∧
        Function.MulExact W.subtype θ ∧
        Function.Surjective θ ∧
        IsCyclic (rootsOfUnity e (B ⧸ P)) ∧
        Nat.card (rootsOfUnity e (B ⧸ P)) = e / p ^ e.factorization p ∧
        (∀ (σ : I) (x a : B), x ∈ P → x ∉ P ^ 2 →
            Ideal.Quotient.mk P a = (θ σ).1.1 →
            (σ : Gal(L/K)) • x - a * x ∈ P ^ 2) ∧
        ∀ θ' : I →* rootsOfUnity e (B ⧸ P),
          (∀ (σ : I) (x a : B), x ∈ P → x ∉ P ^ 2 →
            Ideal.Quotient.mk P a = (θ' σ).1.1 →
            (σ : Gal(L/K)) • x - a * x ∈ P ^ 2) →
          θ' = θ

declarations.name: PrimeSpectrum.isHomeomorph_comap_and_isPurelyInseparable_and_baseChange_of_adjoin_eq_top
declarations.doc:
Let `φ : R → S` be a ring map whose kernel is locally nilpotent and such that `S` is generated
as an `R`-algebra by elements `x` for which there are an `n > 0` and a polynomial `P(T) ∈ R[T]`
whose image in `S[T]` is `(T - x) ^ n`. Then `Spec(S) → Spec(R)` is a homeomorphism, the induced
residue field extensions `κ(p) → κ(q)` are purely inseparable, and both hypotheses hold again for
every base change `R' → S'` of `R → S` along an arbitrary ring map `R → R'`, i.e. for every pushout
square of `R`-algebras completing `R`, `S` by `R'`, `S'`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isHomeomorph_comap_and_isPurelyInseparable_and_baseChange_of_adjoin_eq_top
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (hker : RingHom.ker (algebraMap R S) ≤ nilradical R)
    (hgen : Algebra.adjoin R
      {x : S | ∃ n > 0, ((X : S[X]) - C x) ^ n ∈ lifts (algebraMap R S)} = ⊤) :
    IsHomeomorph (comap (algebraMap R S)) ∧
      (∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] (q : Ideal S) [q.IsPrime]
        (hpq : p = q.comap (algebraMap R S)),
        (Ideal.ResidueField.map p q (algebraMap R S) hpq).IsPurelyInseparable) ∧
      ∀ (R' : Type u') (S' : Type v') [CommRing R'] [CommRing S'] [Algebra R R'] [Algebra S S']
        [Algebra R' S'] [Algebra R S'] [IsScalarTower R R' S'] [IsScalarTower R S S']
        [Algebra.IsPushout R S R' S'],
        RingHom.ker (algebraMap R' S') ≤ nilradical R' ∧
          Algebra.adjoin R'
