declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09IL (the reduced fibre theorem).**  Let `A` be a Nagata Dedekind
domain with fraction field `K` and let `f : X ⟶ Spec A` be flat, quasi-compact and locally of
finite type.  Then there is a finite extension `L / K` such that, with `B` the integral closure
of `A` in `L`, the normalization `Y` of `X ×_{Spec A} Spec B` is smooth over `Spec B` at every
generic point of every one of the fibres of `Y ⟶ Spec B`.

`X` is assumed neither reduced nor normal nor affine, and `A` is not assumed excellent; the
smoothness is at *all* generic points of *all* fibres.

The fraction field is allowed its own universe: the statement is the one in the scheme's universe
transported along the `A`-algebra isomorphism `K ≃ₐ[A] FractionRing A`, which carries the
`K`-algebra structure of the extension and its finite dimensionality while leaving the extension,
the integral closure and the whole conclusion where they are.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteExtension_smoothAt_genericPoints_fiber_normalization_pullback
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsDedekindDomain A] (K : Type v) [Field K]
    [Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K] (hA : IsNagataRing A) {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of A)) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra K L) (_ : FiniteDimensional K L)
      (_ : Algebra A L) (_ : IsScalarTower A K L),
      ∃ hW : ∀ U : (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L)))) : Scheme.{u}).Opens,
        IsCompact (U : Set (pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L)))) : Scheme.{u})) →
        (irreducibleComponents U).Finite,
      ∀ b : Spec (.of ↥(integralClosure A L)),
      ∀ y : (Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
        (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L))))).fiber b,
      y ∈ genericPoints ↥((Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L))))).fiber b) →
      InfinitesimalLifting.SmoothAt (Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫ pullback.snd f
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L)))))
        ((Scheme.normalization _ hW ≫ pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
          (algebraMap A ↥(integralClosure A L))))).fiberι b y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.LiftingComplexes.exists_isPerfect_lift
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IM].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, `U ⊆ X` a
quasi-compact open, `T ⊆ X` a closed subset whose complement is retrocompact in `X`, and `E` an
object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. Every map `α : P ⟶ E|_U` out of a perfect object `P` of `D(𝒪_U)` whose
cohomology is supported on `T ∩ U` comes from a map `β : R ⟶ E` out of a perfect object `R` of
`D(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology is supported on `T`, with `P` a direct summand of `R|_U` by an inclusion
`i` satisfying `i ≫ β|_U = α`.

Quasi-compactness of `X` gives a finite cover of `X` by affine opens; the statement then follows
from `Stacks.Perfect.LiftingComplexes.exists_isPerfect_lift_of_list` by the induction over that
cover, whose single step glues the object already built over a smaller open to the one the affine
case produces over the next affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_lift {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hTc : ∀ W : X.Opens, IsCompact (W : Set X) → IsCompact ((W : Set X) ∩ Tᶜ))
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : Stacks.DerivedQCoh.IsDQCoh (R := X.ringCatSheaf) E)
    (P : DerivedCategory U.toScheme.Modules) (hP : IsPerfect (X := ringedSpace U.toScheme) P)
    (hPT : CohomologySupportedOn U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf (⇑U.ι.base ⁻¹' T) P)
    (α : P ⟶ (derivedRestrict U.ι).obj E) :
    ∃ (R : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (β : R ⟶ E),
      IsPerfect (X := ringedSpace X) R ∧
      CohomologySupportedOn X.ringCatSheaf T R ∧
      ∃ (i : P ⟶ (derivedRestrict U.ι).obj R) (p : (derivedRestrict U.ι).obj R ⟶ P),
        i ≫ p = 𝟙 P ∧ i ≫ (derivedRestrict U.ι).map β = α

declarations.name: Stacks.Perfect.SupportedLiftDegree.exists_isPerfect_supported_hom_biprod_sumShifts_isZero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IN].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, `U ⊆ X` a
quasi-compact open, `T ⊆ X` closed with `X ∖ T` retrocompact, and `E` an object of `D(𝒪_X)` with
quasi-coherent cohomology. Let `P` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_U)` supported on `T ∩ U` and
`α : P ⟶ E|_U`. Then for every degree `n` there are a perfect object `R` of `D(𝒪_X)` supported on
`T`, a map `β : R ⟶ E`, an object `Q` of `D(𝒪_U)` and an isomorphism `R|_U ≅ P ⊞ Q` through which
`β|_U` is the projection onto `P` followed by `α`, with `Q` a finite biproduct of positive shifts
of `P` and `Hⁱ(Q) = 0` for every `i ≥ n`.

The two clauses are the remark's two sentences: the shape
`R|_U = P ⊕ P^{⊕n_1}[1] ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ P^{⊕n_m}[m]`, recorded as
`Stacks.SumOfPositiveShifts.IsSumOfPositiveShifts`, and the agreement of the cohomology sheaves
of `R|_U` and of `P` above the given degree, which for a splitting is the vanishing of the
complement there. The degree is fixed first: the other reading, one `R` serving every `n`, is
false, because a perfect object is bounded, so agreement in every degree would make `P ⟶ R|_U`
an isomorphism and extend `P` to a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.

The statement proved here is stronger than the remark in one further respect, and that
strengthening is what makes the iteration possible: `β|_U` is the projection `R|_U ⟶ P` followed
by `α`, not merely a map restricting to `α` on the summand.

**Where the formalisation departs from the source's recipe.** The remark says to repeat the
construction "for the map `P^{⊕n_1}[1] ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ P^{⊕n_m}[m] ⟶ R|_U`", that is, with ambient object
`R` and then to take cones. A map out of `cone(ρ)` extends a map out of `R` only when its
composite with `ρ` vanishes, and with ambient object `R` nothing makes `ρ ≫ β` vanish, so that
route loses the map to `E` at the first cone. The route taken instead carries, at each stage `k`,
the fibre `F_k` of `β_k : R_k ⟶ E` — the first vertex of a distinguished triangle
`F_k ⟶ R_k ⟶ E ⟶ F_k⟦1⟧` — and applies [Stacks, Tag 09IM] with ambient object `F_k`; the cone is
then formed on `ρ := β'' ≫ u` with `u : F_k ⟶ R_k`, and `ρ ≫ β_k = β'' ≫ (u ≫ β_k) = 0` because
`u` and `β_k` are consecutive maps of a distinguished triangle. The octahedral axiom returns both
the new map to `E` and the new fibre at once. The device is
`Stacks.SplitLiftTower.exists_biprod_iso_lift_of_fibre_octahedron` and the iteration is
`DerivedCategory.exists_hom_biprod_iso_of_fibreOracle`.

[Stacks, Tag 09IM] itself is registered on another declaration and is used here
through
`Stacks.Perfect.SupportedLiftGeneral.exists_isPerfect_supported_hom_biprod_sumShifts`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_supported_hom_biprod_sumShifts_isZero (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact ((U : X.Opens) : Set X))
    (T : Set X) (hT : IsClosed T) (hTc : IsRetrocompact (Tᶜ : Set X))
    (E : DerivedModules X.toRingedSpace) (hE : HasQuasicoherentHomology X E)
    (P : DerivedModules (X.toRingedSpace.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))
    (hP : IsPerfect.{u, u, u + 1} (X := X.toRingedSpace.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding) P)
    (hPT : AlgebraicGeometry.CohomologySupportedOn
      (structureSheafRing (X.toRingedSpace.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))
      (Subtype.val ⁻¹' T) P)
    (α : P ⟶ (derivedRestrict (openInclusion X U)).obj E) :
    ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ (R : DerivedModules X.toRingedSpace) (β : R ⟶ E),
      (IsPerfect.{u, u, u + 1} (X := X.toRingedSpace) R ∧
          AlgebraicGeometry.CohomologySupportedOn (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace) T R) ∧
        ∃ (Q : DerivedModules (X.toRingedSpace.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))
          (e : (derivedRestrict (openInclusion X U)).obj R ≅ P ⊞ Q),
          IsSumOfPositiveShifts P Q ∧
            (∀ i : ℤ, n ≤ i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (SheafOfModules.{u}
              (structureSheafRing (X.toRingedSpace.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding))) i).obj Q)) ∧
              e.inv ≫ (derivedRestrict (openInclusion X U)).map β = biprod.fst ≫ α
declarations.comment:
The complement of `P` in `R|_U` is a finite biproduct of positive shifts of `P`,
and for every degree `n` the construction can be iterated so that the complement has vanishing
cohomology in all degrees `≥ n`, which is the agreement of the cohomology sheaves of `R|_U` and
of `P` above `n`.

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.AnyModel.exists_isPerfect_retract_derivedRestrict
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IQ].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and `U ⊆ X` a
quasi-compact open. Every perfect object `P` of `D(𝒪_U)` is a direct summand -- a retract -- of
the restriction to `U` of a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.

This is [Stacks, Tag 09IM] with `T` the whole space and the zero object, transported from the
model that tag is proved at to the locally small one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_retract_derivedRestrict {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X))
    (P : DerivedCategory U.toScheme.Modules)
    (hP : IsPerfect (X := ringedSpace U.toScheme) P) :
    ∃ R : DerivedCategory X.Modules, IsPerfect (X := ringedSpace X) R ∧
      ∃ (i : P ⟶ (Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.derivedRestrict U.ι).obj R)
        (p : (Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.derivedRestrict U.ι).obj R ⟶ P), i ≫ p = 𝟙 P

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.OpenLift.exists_isPerfectComplex_retract_of_isPerfect_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IQ].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and `U ⊆ X` a
quasi-compact open. Every perfect object `P` of `D(𝒪_U)` is a direct summand -- a retract -- of
the restriction to `U` of a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, here exhibited by a perfect complex `M` of
`𝒪_X`-modules: `P` is a retract of the class of `M|_U`.

The derived category of `𝒪_U` is an arbitrary model, and none is needed on `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfectComplex_retract_of_isPerfect_of_qcqs (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X))
    [hd : HasDerivedCategory.{d₁} U.toScheme.Modules] (P : DerivedCategory U.toScheme.Modules)
    (hP : @IsPerfect U.toScheme.toRingedSpace hd P) :
    ∃ M : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ, IsPerfectComplex (X := X.toRingedSpace) M ∧
      Nonempty (Retract P (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
          M)))
declarations.comment: the perfect object on X exhibited by a perfect complex; any model of D(O_U)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.OpenLift.exists_isPerfect_retract_derivedRestrict
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IQ], in `D(𝒪_X)`.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme
and `U ⊆ X` a quasi-compact open. Every perfect object `P` of `D(𝒪_U)` is a retract of the
restriction to `U` of a perfect object `R` of `D(𝒪_X)`, at any models of the two derived
categories, in independent universes; restriction is `j^*` for the open immersion `j : U ⟶ X`,
which `Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.derivedRestrict` names when the two universes agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_retract_derivedRestrict (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X))
    [hU' : HasDerivedCategory.{d₁} U.toScheme.Modules] [hX : HasDerivedCategory.{d₂} X.Modules]
    (P : DerivedCategory U.toScheme.Modules) (hP : @IsPerfect U.toScheme.toRingedSpace hU' P) :
    ∃ R : DerivedCategory X.Modules, @IsPerfect X.toRingedSpace hX R ∧
      Nonempty (Retract P ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj R))
declarations.comment: in D(O_X), at any models of the two derived categories

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.OpenLift.exists_isPerfectComplex_retract_restrict_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IQ] for `X` affine.** Let `X` be an affine scheme and `U ⊆ X` a
quasi-compact open. Every perfect object `P` of `D(𝒪_U)` is a direct summand -- a retract -- of
the restriction to `U` of a perfect complex of `𝒪_X`-modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfectComplex_retract_restrict_of_isPerfect
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X))
    (P : DerivedCategory U.toScheme.Modules)
    (hP : IsPerfect (X := U.toScheme.toRingedSpace) P) :
    ∃ M : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u, u} X.toRingedSpace) ℤ,
      IsPerfectComplex M ∧
      Nonempty (Retract P (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.restrictModules.{u, u} X.toRingedSpace
          U).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj M)))
declarations.comment:
for X affine; the quasi-compact quasi-separated case is deduced in the source
from 09IM, whose induction over an affine cover needs 08EK and 08EH, neither of which this
library has

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.exists_isPerfect_retract_derivedRestrict
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IQ].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and `U ⊆ X` a
quasi-compact open. Every perfect object `P` of `D(𝒪_U)` is a direct summand -- a retract -- of
the restriction to `U` of a perfect object `R` of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_retract_derivedRestrict (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]

    (P : DerivedCategory U.toScheme.Modules)
    (hP : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := U.toScheme.toRingedSpace) P) :

      Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) R ∧

declarations.name: Stacks.Koszul.Truncation.hom_koszulObject_eq_zero_of_isIso_unit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IR], the implication "(1) implies (2)".** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 08CZ],
if the canonical map `E ⟶ Rj_*(E|_U)` is invertible then `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K[n], E) = 0` for every
`n ∈ ℤ`, where `K` is the sheafified Koszul complex on `f₁, …, f_r`.

There is nothing to assume. The Koszul object restricts to zero on `U = ⋃ᵢ D(f_i)` by
`Stacks.Koszul.OpenComplement.isZero_derivedRestrict_koszulObject`, so a morphism `K⟦n⟧ ⟶ Rj_* Z`
is adjoint to a morphism out of `(j^* K)⟦n⟧ = 0` and hence zero; and `E` is isomorphic to
`Rj_*(E|_U)` through the unit, while the condition is closed under isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_koszulObject_eq_zero_of_isIso_unit
    (E : DerivedCategory (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Modules)
    (h : IsIso ((derivedRestrictPushforwardAdjunction (openComplement f).ι).unit.app E)) :
    ∀ (n : ℤ) (g : (koszulObject f)⟦n⟧ ⟶ E), g = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.Koszul.Truncation.isIso_unit_of_hom_koszulObject_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IR], the implication "(2) implies (1)".** In Situation [Stacks, Tag 08CZ],
let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, that is one whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent.
If `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K[n], E) = 0` for every `n ∈ ℤ` then the canonical map `E ⟶ Rj_*(E|_U)` is
invertible.

Take a distinguished triangle `E ⟶ Rj_*(E|_U) ⟶ M ⟶ E⟦1⟧`; the claim is that `M = 0`. Three
things are known about `M`.

* `M|_U = 0`, because `j^*` of the unit at `E` is a section of the counit at `E|_U`, which is
  invertible — `Rj_*` is fully faithful along an open immersion.
* `Hom(K⟦n⟧, M) = 0` for every `n`, because right orthogonality to the shifts of `K` is a
  triangulated subcategory and both `E` and `Rj_*(E|_U)` lie in it, the latter for the formal
  reason that `j^* K = 0`.
* The cohomology sheaves of `M` are quasi-coherent, because those of `E` are and `Rj_*` preserves
  quasi-coherent cohomology along a quasi-compact open immersion ([Stacks, Tag 08D5]).

Those three force `M = 0` by `Stacks.Koszul.Truncation.isZero_of_forall_hom_koszulObject_eq_zero`,
which is the source's argument: pass to `D(A)` along the affine comparison of [Stacks, Tag 06Z0]
and apply the Koszul detection statement over the ring. A distinguished triangle whose third
vertex vanishes has invertible first morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_unit_of_hom_koszulObject_eq_zero
    (E : DerivedCategory (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Modules)
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).Modules)
      (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).ringCatSheaf) E)
    (h : ∀ (n : ℤ) (g : (koszulObject f)⟦n⟧ ⟶ E), g = 0) :
    IsIso ((derivedRestrictPushforwardAdjunction (openComplement f).ι).unit.app E)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.AnyModel.hasPerfectGenerator_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IS], the theorem of Bondal and Van den Bergh**, in the form that
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is weakly generated by a single perfect object: on a quasi-compact quasi-separated
scheme the property `Stacks.DerivedQCoh.AnyModel.HasPerfectGenerator` holds.

This is the induction principle [Stacks, Tag 08DR] — in the clause `induction_top` for the whole
space — applied to `Stacks.DerivedQCoh.AnyModel.HasPerfectGeneratorOn`, whose two clauses are
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.AnyModel.hasPerfectGeneratorOn_of_isAffineOpen` and
`Stacks.DerivedQCoh.AnyModel.hasPerfectGeneratorOn_sup`; the conclusion is read at the identity
of `X`, an open immersion whose image is all of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPerfectGenerator_of_qcqs (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] :
    HasPerfectGenerator X

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.AnyModel.exists_isPerfect_isZero_iff_forall_hom_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IS], the theorem of Bondal and Van den Bergh, in the source's own words.**
Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme. There is a perfect object `P` of `D(𝒪_X)` such
that for every object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` the following are equivalent: `E = 0`, and
`Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(P⟦n⟧, E) = 0` for all `n : ℤ`.

This is `Stacks.DerivedQCoh.AnyModel.hasPerfectGenerator_of_qcqs` read in the ambient derived
category by `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_singleton_iff`; the
converse implication holds for any object, a morphism into a zero object being zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_isZero_iff_forall_hom_eq_zero (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] :
    ∃ P : DerivedCategory X.Modules, IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) P ∧
      ∀ E : DerivedCategory X.Modules, DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := X.Modules)
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf) E →
          (IsZero E ↔ ∀ (n : ℤ) (g : P⟦n⟧ ⟶ E), g = 0)

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.AffineGeneration.exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IS] for an affine scheme.** `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is generated by a single compact
object: there is an object `P` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` which is compact and such that an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` receiving only zero morphisms from the shifts of `P` is zero.

The object produced is the image under
`Stacks.Duality.AffineGeneration.affineComparison` of the regular module in degree zero, which is
the structure sheaf in degree zero — the source's own generator for an affine scheme. See the
implementation notes for why it is exhibited as compact rather than as perfect, and for what
separates this from the tag's quasi-compact quasi-separated statement.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsAffine X] :
    ∃ P : (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory,
      IsCompactObject.{u} P ∧ (ObjectProperty.singleton P).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.comment: FOR AN AFFINE SCHEME ONLY, and with the generator exhibited as a COMPACT rather than a perfect object. The source's induction over the quasi-compact opens, Tag 08DR, is available and so is its generation step, but two of its inputs are not: Tag 09IQ at a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme (the library has only the affine case, Stacks.DerivedQCoh.OpenLift.exists_isPerfectComplex_retract_restrict_of_isPerfect; the source deduces the rest from Tag 09IM, needing Tags 08EK and 08EH, none of the three being present), and the implication perfect implies compact of Tag 09M1, which the source draws from the Hom formula of Tag 08DQ, absent. The generator here is the image of the regular module in degree zero under the comparison of Tag 06Z0, that is the structure sheaf in degree zero, which is the source's generator for an affine scheme; that it is perfect as well as compact is Tag 07LT carried across Tag 06Z0, which is not done here because the library's statement of the affine case of Tag 09M1, AlgebraicGeometry.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect_spec, is pinned to CategoryTheory.HasDerivedCategory.standard and so speaks of a different derived category. Compactness is what the consumers of the tag ask for

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.AffineGeneration.isCompactlyGenerated_derivedQuasiCoherent_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IS] for an affine scheme, in the form [Stacks, Tag 09SQ] defines and Brown
representability consumes.** `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is compactly generated: the one-element family
consisting of the generator of
`Stacks.Duality.AffineGeneration.exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_isAffine`
is a family of compact objects which jointly generate.

The category is spelled over `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf`, which is the
spelling the hypothesis of [Stacks, Tag 0CR0] uses.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactlyGenerated_derivedQuasiCoherent_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    IsCompactlyGenerated.{u}
      (DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB
        (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory
declarations.comment: FOR AN AFFINE SCHEME ONLY, in the IsCompactlyGenerated form of Tag 09SQ and with the generator exhibited as compact rather than perfect; see Stacks.Duality.AffineGeneration.exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_isAffine for the full caveat

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.AffineGeneration.isCompactlyGenerated_quasiCoherentDerivedCategory_of_isAffine
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IS] for an affine scheme**, at the spelling of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` over
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules X` — the one the statement of [Stacks, Tag 0A9E] uses. The two
spellings are the same type with separately declared `HasDerivedCategory` instances; see the
implementation notes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactlyGenerated_quasiCoherentDerivedCategory_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsAffine X] :
    IsCompactlyGenerated.{u} (Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
declarations.comment: FOR AN AFFINE SCHEME ONLY, in the IsCompactlyGenerated form of Tag 09SQ at the Scheme.Modules spelling of the category, which is the one Tag 0A9E's statement uses; see Stacks.Duality.AffineGeneration.exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_isAffine for the full caveat

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.QuasiAffineGeneration.exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_isQuasiAffine
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IS] for a quasi-affine scheme.** `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is generated by a single
compact object.

A quasi-affine scheme is quasi-compact and `X ⟶ Spec Γ(X, ⊤)` is an open immersion
([Stacks, Tag 01P6], Mathlib's `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IsQuasiAffine`), so this is the affine
case `AffineGeneration.exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_isAffine`
restricted along that immersion by
`OpenImmersion.exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_isOpenImmersion`.
The generator is therefore the restriction to `X` of the structure sheaf of `Spec Γ(X, ⊤)` in
degree zero, which is `𝒪_X` in degree zero — the source's own generator.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_isQuasiAffine (X : Scheme.{u})
    [X.IsQuasiAffine] :
    ∃ P : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X,
      IsCompactObject.{u} P ∧ (ObjectProperty.singleton P).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.comment: FOR A QUASI-AFFINE SCHEME, and with the generator exhibited as a COMPACT rather than a perfect object. This weakens the affine hypothesis of Stacks.Duality.AffineGeneration.exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_isAffine but does NOT reach the tag's quasi-compact quasi-separated statement. The route is the reverse of the source's: compact generation passes DOWN from a scheme to a quasi-compact open of it, by Stacks.Duality.OpenImmersion.isCompactlyGenerated_quasiCoherentDerivedCategory_of_isOpenImmersion, so from the affine case it reaches exactly the schemes with a quasi-compact open immersion into an affine scheme, the quasi-affine ones. The source's own induction over the quasi-compact opens, Tag 08DR, goes the other way and still needs Tag 09IQ at a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and the implication perfect implies compact of Tag 09M1, neither of which is in the library; see the implementation notes of StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Duality/CompactGeneration/AffineQuasiCoherent.lean. Nothing here needs either: the generator is compact by construction and compactness is what the consumers of the tag ask for

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isPerfect_generator
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09IS].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. Then
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` has a perfect generator: there is a perfect object `G` of `D(𝒪_X)` such that every
object `K` of `D(𝒪_X)` with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves which receives no nonzero morphism
from any shift `G⟦n⟧` is zero.

This is `Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_isPerfect_generator_modules` read in the spelling
`StructureSheafModules X.sheaf` with perfectness for the ringed site of opens, the spelling of the
generator hypotheses of Stacks 0GEN in `DetectingBoundedAboveGenerator`; the two notions of
perfectness agree by `Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.isPerfect_ringedSite_of_isPerfect`.

The proof is the source's: induction over a finite affine cover produces finitely many compact
generators of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` (`Stacks.Duality.QcqsGeneration.exists_finite_compact_generators`),
compact objects of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` are perfect
(`Stacks.Duality.QcqsPerfect.isPerfect_of_isCompactObject_of_qcqs`), and their direct sum is a
single perfect generator.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_generator {X : Scheme.{u}}
    [HasSheafify (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toPresheafedSpace.carrier) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [(Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toPresheafedSpace.carrier).WEqualsLocallyBijective
      AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    (hqc : CompactSpace X) (hqs : QuasiSeparatedSpace X) :
    ∃ G : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf), (ringedSite X.sheaf).IsPerfect G ∧
      ∀ K : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf),
        (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf) i).obj
          K).IsQuasicoherent) →
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (f : G⟦n⟧ ⟶ K), f = 0) → IsZero K

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.qcqs_induction_on_enlargement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09IT.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space and let
`W ⊆ X` be a quasi-compact open subspace. A property `P` of the quasi-compact open subspaces
of `X` which holds for `W`, and which for every elementary distinguished square
`(W₁ ⊆ W₂, f : V ⟶ W₂)` with `W₁`, `W₂` quasi-compact open subspaces of `X` containing `W`
and `V` affine passes from `W₁` to `W₂`, holds for `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem qcqs_induction_on_enlargement
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (W : Subfunctor X.1) (hWopen : IsOpenSubspace B S hS W)
    (hWqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS W.toFunctor)
    (P : Subfunctor X.1 → Prop) (hPW : P W)
    (hstep : ∀ (W₁ W₂ : Subfunctor X.1) (hW₁ : IsOpenSubspace B S hS W₁)
      (hW₂ : IsOpenSubspace B S hS W₂),
      IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS W₁.toFunctor →
      IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS W₂.toFunctor →
      ∀ hle : W₁ ≤ W₂, W ≤ W₁ →
      ∀ {V : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : V ⟶ W₂.toFunctor),
        IsAffineSpace B S hS V →
        IsElementaryDistinguishedSquare B S hS hW₂.1
          (Subfunctor.range (Subfunctor.homOfLe hle)) f →
        P W₁ → P W₂) :
    P (⊤ : Subfunctor X.1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPerfect_retract_restrict_of_supported
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09IV.** Let `S` be a scheme, `X` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space
over `S`, `W ⊆ X` a quasi-compact open subspace and `T ⊆ |X|` a closed subset such that
`X \ T ⟶ X` is quasi-compact. Let `E` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `α : P ⟶ E|_W` a map
where `P` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_W)` supported on `T ∩ W`. Then there exists a map
`β : R ⟶ E` where `R` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` supported on `T` such that `P` is a
direct summand of `R|_W` in `D(𝒪_W)` compatibly with `α` and `β|_W`: there are
`s : P ⟶ R|_W` and `r : R|_W ⟶ P` with `s ≫ r = 𝟙 P` and `s ≫ β|_W = α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_retract_restrict_of_supported
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1) (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1)
    (W : Subfunctor X.1) (hW : IsOpenSubspace B S hS W)
    (hWqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS W.toFunctor) (T : Set (points B S hS X.1))
    (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hTqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS
      ((openSubspacesOrderIso B S hS X.1 X.2).symm ⟨Tᶜ, hT.isOpen_compl⟩).1.ι)
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)
    (P : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2))
    (hP : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2).IsPerfect P)
    (hPT : CohomologySupportedOn B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2 (pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor W.ι ⁻¹' T) P)
    (α : P ⟶ (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
      (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.obj E.obj) :
    ∃ (R : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)) (β : R ⟶ E.obj),
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect R ∧
      CohomologySupportedOn B S hS X.1 X.2 T R ∧
      ∃ (s : P ⟶ (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
          (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.obj R)
        (r : (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
          (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.obj R ⟶ P),
        s ≫ r = 𝟙 P ∧
        s ≫ (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
          (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.map β = α

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPerfect_restrict_iso_biprod_isIso_homologyFunctor_map_inl
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09IW, first two assertions.** Let `S` be a scheme, `X` a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, `W ⊆ X` a quasi-compact open subspace, `T ⊆ |X|` a
closed subset such that `X \ T ⟶ X` is quasi-compact, `E` an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and
`α : P ⟶ E|_W` a morphism from a perfect object `P` of `D(𝒪_W)` supported on `T ∩ W`. The
construction of Stacks 09IV gives `β : R ⟶ E`, with `R` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` supported
on `T`, such that

1. `R|_W ≅ P ⊕ C` with `C ≅ P^{⊕ n₁}[1] ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ P^{⊕ nₘ}[m]` for some `m ≥ 0` and `n_j ≥ 0`
   (`CategoryTheory.IsFiniteSumOfPositiveShifts`), `β|_W` being `α` on `P` and zero on `C`;
2. the highest degree cohomology sheaf of `R|_W` is that of `P`: whenever `Hⁱ(P) = 0` for all
   `i > d`, the inclusion of the summand `P` induces `Hⁱ(P) ≅ Hⁱ(R|_W)` for every `i ≥ d`.

Both derived categories are taken at arbitrary models; "supported on" is the condition of
Stacks 08GF on every cohomology sheaf, and `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is the condition of Stacks 071X.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_restrict_iso_biprod_isIso_homologyFunctor_map_inl
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (W : Subfunctor X.1) (hW : IsOpenSubspace B S hS W)
    (hWqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS W.toFunctor) (T : Set (points B S hS X.1))
    (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hTqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS
      ((openSubspacesOrderIso B S hS X.1 X.2).symm ⟨Tᶜ, hT.isOpen_compl⟩).1.ι)
    [hDX : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)]
    [hDW : HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O)) E)
    (P : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2))
    (hP : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2).IsPerfect P)
    (hPT : ∀ i : ℤ, supportOfSheaf B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} _).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
          (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2) i).obj P)) ⊆
        pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor W.ι ⁻¹' T)
    (α : P ⟶ (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
      (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) :
    ∃ (R : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)) (β : R ⟶ E),
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect R ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} _).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) i).obj R)) ⊆ T) ∧
      ∃ (C : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
          (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2))
        (e : (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
          (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.obj R ≅ P ⊞ C),
        IsFiniteSumOfPositiveShifts P C ∧
        (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
          (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.map β =
          e.hom ≫ biprod.fst ≫ α ∧
        ∀ d : ℤ, (∀ i : ℤ, d < i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS
            (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
          (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2) i).obj P)) →
          ∀ i : ℤ, d ≤ i → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS
              (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
          (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2) i).map (biprod.inl ≫ e.inv))
declarations.comment: first and second assertions: the shape of the restriction, and its top cohomology

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPerfect_retract_restrict_isIso_homologyFunctor_map
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09IW, third assertion.** In the situation of Stacks 09IV — `S` a scheme, `X` a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, `W ⊆ X` a quasi-compact open subspace,
`T ⊆ |X|` closed with `X \ T ⟶ X` quasi-compact, `E` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` and `α : P ⟶ E|_W` with
`P` perfect in `D(𝒪_W)` supported on `T ∩ W` — one can achieve equality of the cohomology sheaves
of `R|_W` and `P` above any given degree: for every integer `N` there is `β : R ⟶ E` with `R`
perfect in `D(𝒪_X)` and supported on `T`, and `P` a direct summand of `R|_W` compatibly with `α`
and `β|_W` — `s : P ⟶ R|_W` and `r : R|_W ⟶ P` with `s ≫ r = 𝟙 P` and `s ≫ β|_W = α`, indeed
`β|_W = r ≫ α` — such that `Hⁱ(s) : Hⁱ(P) ⟶ Hⁱ(R|_W)` is an isomorphism for every `i ≥ N`.

Both derived categories are taken at arbitrary models.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_retract_restrict_isIso_homologyFunctor_map
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (W : Subfunctor X.1) (hW : IsOpenSubspace B S hS W)
    (hWqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS W.toFunctor) (T : Set (points B S hS X.1))
    (hT : IsClosed T)
    (hTqc : IsQuasiCompact B S hS
      ((openSubspacesOrderIso B S hS X.1 X.2).symm ⟨Tᶜ, hT.isOpen_compl⟩).1.ι)
    [hDX : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)]
    [hDW : HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2)]
    (E : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2))
    (hE : DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherentOnSite.{u + 1, u, u, u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).O)) E)
    (P : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2))
    (hP : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2).IsPerfect P)
    (hPT : ∀ i : ℤ, supportOfSheaf B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} _).obj ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
          (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2) i).obj P)) ⊆
        pointsMap B S hS W.toFunctor W.ι ⁻¹' T)
    (α : P ⟶ (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
      (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) (N : ℤ) :
    ∃ (R : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)) (β : R ⟶ E),
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect R ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, supportOfSheaf B S hS X.1
        ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf.{u} _).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) i).obj R)) ⊆ T) ∧
      ∃ (s : P ⟶ (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
          (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.obj R)
        (r : (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
          (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.obj R ⟶ P),
        s ≫ r = 𝟙 P ∧
        s ≫ (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
          (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.map β = α ∧
        (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
          (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.map β = r ≫ α ∧
        ∀ i : ℤ, N ≤ i → IsIso ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS
            (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
          (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2) i).map s)
declarations.comment: third assertion: equality of cohomology sheaves above any given degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPerfect_retract_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09IX.** Let `S` be a scheme, `X` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space
over `S`, `W` a quasi-compact open subspace of `X` and `P` a perfect object of `D(𝒪_W)`. Then `P`
is a direct summand of the restriction `Q|_W` of a perfect object `Q` of `D(𝒪_X)`: there are
`s : P ⟶ Q|_W` and `r : Q|_W ⟶ P` with `s ≫ r = 𝟙`.

The induction of Stacks 09IT on the quasi-compact opens containing `W`, with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSummandOfPerfectRestriction_step` as the inductive step.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_retract_restrict (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1) (W : Subfunctor X.1)
    (hW : IsOpenSubspace B S hS W) (hWqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS W.toFunctor)
    (P : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2))
    (hP : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2).IsPerfect P) :
    ∃ Q : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2),
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect Q ∧
      ∃ (s : P ⟶ (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS
          (ObjectProperty.homMk W.ι : openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW ⟶ X)
          (isEtale_of_isOpenImmersion B S hS hW.2)).mapDerivedCategory.obj Q)
        (r : (etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS
          (ObjectProperty.homMk W.ι : openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW ⟶ X)
          (isEtale_of_isOpenImmersion B S hS hW.2)).mapDerivedCategory.obj Q ⟶ P),
        s ≫ r = 𝟙 P

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPerfect_restrict_iso_biprod_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09IX.** Let `S` be a scheme, `X` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space
over `S` and `W ⊆ X` a quasi-compact open subspace. Let `P` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_W)`.
Then `P` is a direct summand of the restriction of a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`: there are a
perfect `R` in `D(𝒪_X)` and an object `C` of `D(𝒪_W)` with `R|_W ≅ P ⊕ C`. Both derived
categories are taken at arbitrary models; quasi-separation is absolute, over the final object of
the base category of schemes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_restrict_iso_biprod_of_isPerfect
    (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (W : Subfunctor X.1) (hW : IsOpenSubspace B S hS W)
    (hWqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS W.toFunctor)
    [hDX : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2)]
    [hDW : HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2)]
    (P : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2))
    (hP : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
      (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2).IsPerfect P) :
    ∃ R : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2),
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect R ∧
      ∃ C : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).1
          (openSubspaceSpace B S hS W hW).2),
        Nonempty ((etaleModulePullback.{u, u} B S hS (openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)
          (isEtale_openSubspaceHom B S hS W hW)).mapDerivedCategory.obj R ≅ P ⊞ C)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPerfect_generator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09IY.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`.
There is a perfect object `P` of `D(𝒪_X)` such that an object `E` of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is zero if and
only if `Hom(P[n], E) = 0` for all `n ∈ ℤ`.

The compact weak generator of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isCompactObject_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_of_qcqs` is perfect by
Stacks 09M8.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_generator (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1) :
    ∃ P : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2),
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect P ∧
        ∀ E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2,
          IsZero E.obj ↔ ∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (P⟦n⟧ ⟶ E.obj)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isPerfect_isZero_iff_forall_hom_shift_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09IY.** Let `S` be a scheme and `X` a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic
space over `S`. The category `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is generated by a single perfect object: there is a
perfect object `P` of `D(𝒪_X)` such that for `E` in `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` the following are equivalent:
(1) `E = 0`, (2) `Hom(P[n], E) = 0` for all `n ∈ ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_isZero_iff_forall_hom_shift_eq_zero (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1) (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X.1) :
    ∃ P : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2),
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect P ∧
      ∀ E, qcohDerivedProp B S hS X E → (IsZero E ↔ ∀ (n : ℤ) (g : P⟦n⟧ ⟶ E), g = 0)

declarations.name: quasiIso_of_goodResolution
declarations.doc:
A good resolution `A → M` yields a chain map `A.total shZ ⟶ M` whose
per-degree components agree with `canonicalMapF`, and this chain map is a
quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_of_goodResolution
    (M : HomologicalComplex Ab shZ)
    (A : HomologicalComplex₂ Ab shZ shZ)
    [A.HasTotal shZ]
    (f : A.X 0 ⟶ M)
    (_h : GoodResolution M A f) :
    ∃ φ : A.total shZ ⟶ M,
      (∀ n : ℤ, φ.f n = canonicalMapF M A f n) ∧ QuasiIso φ

declarations.name: HomologicalComplex₂.quasiIso_toProductTotal
declarations.doc:
Let `0 → M^• → A_0^• → A_1^• → ⋯` be an exact complex of complexes of abelian groups such
that for every `p` the induced complex `0 → Coker(d_M^p) → Coker(d_{A_0}^p) → ⋯` is exact. Then
the map `M^• → Tot_π(A^{•, •})` induced by `M^• → A_0^•` is a quasi-isomorphism. Here `K` is the
double complex `A^{p, q} = A_p^q`, `ε` is the map `M^• → A_0^•`, the exact complex of complexes
is the augmentation of `K` by `ε`, and `Coker(d^p)` is the object of opcycles in degree `p + 1`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIso_toProductTotal (ε : M ⟶ K.X 0) (w : ε ≫ K.d 0 1 = 0)
    (hA : (CochainComplex.augment K ε w).Acyclic)
    (hC : ∀ q : ℤ, (((HomologicalComplex.opcyclesFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{u} (ComplexShape.up ℤ)
      q).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj (CochainComplex.augment K ε w)).Acyclic) :
    QuasiIso (toProductTotal ε w)

declarations.name: isEquivalence_of_fullyFaithful_of_adjunction_of_ker_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Let `F : D ⥤ D'` and `G : D' ⥤ D` be exact functors of pretriangulated categories with
`F ⊣ G`. If `F` is fully faithful and every `X : D'` with `G X` a zero object is itself a zero
object, then `F` is an equivalence of categories.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_of_fullyFaithful_of_adjunction_of_ker_eq_zero
    [F.IsTriangulated] [G.IsTriangulated] [F.Full] [F.Faithful]
    (adj : F ⊣ G)
    (hker : ∀ X : D', IsZero (G.obj X) → IsZero X) :
    F.IsEquivalence

declarations.name: strictlyPerfect_tensorObj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09J2 (Lemma 20.46.3).** If `E` and `F` are strictly perfect complexes, then the
total complex `HomologicalComplex.tensorObj E F` of their tensor product, whose degree `n` term is
`⨁_{p+q=n} E^p ⊗ F^q` with the Koszul-sign differential, is strictly perfect.

The hypothesis `[E.HasTensor F]` asserts that the total complex exists; for bounded complexes
(such as strictly perfect ones) it is automatically satisfied since each total degree only
involves finitely many summands.
declarations.statement:
theorem strictlyPerfect_tensorObj
    (E F : CochainComplex C ℤ) [E.HasTensor F]
    (hE : StrictlyPerfect E) (hF : StrictlyPerfect F) :
    StrictlyPerfect (HomologicalComplex.tensorObj E F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Tag 09J3, part (1).**  Let `(X, 𝒪_X)` be a ringed space and let `K`, `L` be objects of
`D(𝒪_X)`.  If `K` is `n`-pseudo-coherent with `H^i(K) = 0` for `i > a`, and `L` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent with `H^j(L) = 0` for `j > b`, then `K ⊗_{𝒪_X}^{𝐋} L` is
`t`-pseudo-coherent for `t = max (m + a, n + b)`.

If `a < n` then `t > a + b`, so the conclusion follows from right t-exactness of the derived
tensor product alone; that is
`Stacks.Cohomology.PseudoCoherentTensor.isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedTensorProduct_of_lt`.
Otherwise `n ≤ a`.  Both factors are replaced by K-flat representatives `𝒜`, `ℬ` with no terms
above their own bounds (Tag 06YQ through Tag 05T7); on those the derived tensor product is
`Tot(𝒜 ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℬ)` by the comparison of Tag 06YU, so that complex represents
`K ⊗^{𝐋} L` and is the one fed to Tag 08CC part (1).  Pseudo-coherence passes to `𝒜` and `ℬ` by
Tag 08CC part (2), and `AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.localApproximationData` produces the
required local approximations in degree `t`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedTensorProduct
    (T : Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.DerivedTensorProduct X.sheaf)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules X)) (n m a b : ℤ)
    (hK : IsPseudoCoherentFrom (X := X) K n)
    (hKa : ∀ i : ℤ, a < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules X) i).obj K))
    (hL : IsPseudoCoherentFrom (X := X) L m)
    (hLb : ∀ j : ℤ, b < j →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules X) j).obj L)) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom (X := X) ((T.tensor.obj K).obj L) (max (m + a) (n + b))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherent_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Tag 09J3, part (2).**  The derived tensor product of two pseudo-coherent objects of
`D(𝒪_X)` is pseudo-coherent.

Neither factor is assumed bounded above, so the representatives come from the unrestricted
K-flat resolutions of Tag 06YS rather than from a bounded one; `Tot(𝒜 ⊗_{𝒪_X} ℬ)` is then a
representative of `K ⊗^{𝐋} L`, and it suffices to see that it is `q`-pseudo-coherent as a
complex for every `q`.  By Tag 08CC that is `q`-pseudo-coherence of `K ⊗^{𝐋} L`, which
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.localApproximationData_of_isPseudoCoherentComplex` supplies: the
cohomological bounds that part (1) needs are produced on an open covering, which is the source's
reduction to a covering on which both factors are bounded above.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_derivedTensorProduct
    (T : Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.DerivedTensorProduct X.sheaf)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (KFlatDerivedPullback.Modules X))
    (hK : IsPseudoCoherent (X := X) K) (hL : IsPseudoCoherent (X := X) L) :
    IsPseudoCoherent (X := X) ((T.tensor.obj K).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.Tensor.hasTorAmplitude_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
If `K` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` and `L` has Tor amplitude in `[c, d]`, then
`K ⊗^L_{O_X} L` has Tor amplitude in `[a + c, b + d]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_derivedTensor (K L : DerivedCategory (Modules X)) (a b c d : ℤ)
    (hK : HasTorAmplitude X K a b)
    (hL : HasTorAmplitude X L c d) :
    HasTorAmplitude X
      (((derTensor X).tensor.obj K).obj L) (a + c) (b + d)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPerfect_derivedTensor
declarations.doc:
On a ringed space the derived tensor product `Stacks.SheafOfModules.derivedTensor` takes a
pair of perfect objects of `D(O_X)` to a perfect object.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedTensor
    (K L : DerivedCategory (StructureSheafModules X.sheaf))
    (hK : IsPerfect (X := X) K)
    (hL : IsPerfect (X := X) L) :
    IsPerfect (X := X)
      (((derivedTensor X.sheaf).obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment: at the derived tensor product of the internal Hom development

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPerfect_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**The derived tensor product of two perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)` is perfect.**

Represent the objects by perfect complexes `E` and `F`, and replace `F` by a K-flat resolution
`B`, which is perfect as well.  The derived tensor product is then the class of the total tensor
complex `Tot(E ⊗_{𝒪_X} B)`, which is perfect by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPerfectComplex_tensorComplex`.

Stated for an arbitrary derived tensor product, since only its `comparisonRight` field is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedTensorProduct
    (T : Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.DerivedTensorProduct X.sheaf)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (hK : IsPerfect K) (hL : IsPerfect L) :
    IsPerfect ((T.tensor.obj K).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RingedSpaceCompact.isCompactObject_of_isPerfect_of_finiteCohomDim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09J7 (b).** Let `X` be a ringed space whose underlying topological
space is quasi-compact, has a basis of quasi-compact opens, and has quasi-compact intersections
of quasi-compact opens — hypotheses (1), (2) and (3) of the tag. Let `K` be a perfect object of
`D(O_X)` and suppose `X` has finite cohomological dimension, that is `Hᵖ(X, F) = 0` for every
`O_X`-module `F` and every `p` beyond a fixed bound `d`. Then `K` is a compact object of
`D(O_X)`.

The reduction the source performs first — by Stacks 08DQ morphisms out of
`K` are morphisms out of `j_{X!}O_X` after applying `K^∨ ⊗^L_{O_X} -`, a functor commuting with
direct sums — is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualHomEquivOfIsoStructureSheaf` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedTensorFlip`, and it is applied at
the final object `⊤` of the site of opens. The three topological conditions enter through
Stacks 01FF: they make the cohomology functors `F ↦ Hᵖ(X, F)` commute
with arbitrary direct sums, which with the dimension bound is what Stacks 094D consumes.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_of_isPerfect_of_finiteCohomDim [CompactSpace X.carrier]
    (hBasis : PrespectralSpace X.carrier)
    (hInter : QuasiSeparatedSpace X.carrier)
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (RingedSpace.ringedSite X).O)))
    (hK : (RingedSpace.ringedSite X).IsPerfect K)
    (hcd : ∃ d : ℤ, ∀ (p : ℕ) (F : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (RingedSpace.ringedSite X).O)),
      d < (p : ℤ) → IsZero (Hgroup
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (RingedSpace.ringedSite X).O) ⊤ p F)) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} K
declarations.comment: (b): on a ringed space satisfying (1), (2) and (3) and of finite cohomological dimension, a perfect object is a compact object of D(O_X)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.RingedSpaceCompact.hom_coproduct_bijective_of_isPerfect_of_compactSpace
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09J7 (a).** Let `X` be a ringed space whose underlying topological
space is quasi-compact, has a basis of quasi-compact opens, and has quasi-compact intersections
of quasi-compact opens — hypotheses (1), (2) and (3) of the tag. Let `K` be a perfect object of
`D(O_X)` and let `M : I → D(O_X)` be a family whose coproduct is bounded below. Then
`Hom(K, ⨁ Mᵢ) = ⨁ Hom(K, Mᵢ)`: the canonical map from the direct sum of the `Hom(K, Mᵢ)` is
bijective.

The proof applies `hom_coproduct_bijective_of_isPerfect_of_hasFiniteTorDimension`; the finite
Tor dimension of `K^∨` is the global form of Stacks 08G8,
`Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.hasFiniteTorDimension_of_ringedSite_isPerfect`, applied to the
dual `K^∨`, which is perfect by Stacks 08JJ
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPerfect_derivedDual`): perfectness gives the Tor amplitude of
`K^∨` only locally, quasi-compactness makes the local intervals one interval, and the bridge
`Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.hasTorAmplitude_iff_derivedTensorProduct` reads that interval
against the derived tensor product datum the reduction measures Tor dimension by.

The index type lies in the universe of the space, as for clause (b).
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_coproduct_bijective_of_isPerfect_of_compactSpace [CompactSpace X.carrier]
    (hBasis : PrespectralSpace X.carrier)
    (hInter : QuasiSeparatedSpace X.carrier)
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (RingedSpace.ringedSite X).O)))
    (hK : (RingedSpace.ringedSite X).IsPerfect K)
    {I : Type u} [DecidableEq I]
    (M : I → DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf (RingedSpace.ringedSite X).O))) [HasCoproduct M]
    (hplus : DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow (∐ M)) :
    Function.Bijective
      (DirectSum.toAddMonoid fun j => Preadditive.rightComp K (Limits.Sigma.ι M j))
declarations.comment: (a): on a ringed space satisfying (1), (2) and (3), a perfect object K satisfies Hom(K, ⨁ M_i) = ⨁ Hom(K, M_i) whenever ⨁ M_i is bounded below

declarations.name: Stacks.StrictlyPerfect.Modules.isStrictlyPerfect_tensor
declarations.doc:
If `E` and `F` are strictly perfect complexes of `R`-modules, then so is their tensor product
`E ⊗ F`, the total complex of the tensor product double complex.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrictlyPerfect_tensor
    (E F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ)
    (hE : IsStrictlyPerfect E) (hF : IsStrictlyPerfect F) :
    IsStrictlyPerfect (E ⊗ F)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.isStrictlyPerfect_tensorComplex
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09J8.** The total tensor complex `Tot(K ⊗_O L)` of two strictly perfect complexes
of `O`-modules on a ringed site is strictly perfect.

Each degree of `Tot(K ⊗_O L)` is the coproduct of the `K^t ⊗_O L^r` with `t + r` that degree.
Such a summand vanishes unless both `K^t` and `L^r` are nonzero, which happens for finitely
many pairs only, so the degree vanishes outside the sum of the two ranges of nonvanishing; and
each surviving summand is a direct summand of a finite free `O`-module because both of its
factors are.
declarations.statement:
theorem isStrictlyPerfect_tensorComplex
    (K L : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{w} (ringSheaf R)) ℤ)
    (hK : IsStrictlyPerfect (ringSheaf R) K) (hL : IsStrictlyPerfect (ringSheaf R) L) :
    IsStrictlyPerfect (ringSheaf R) (((tensorComplex R).obj K).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09J9, part (1).** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and let `K`, `L` be objects of
`D(O)`. If `K` is `n`-pseudo-coherent with `H^i(K) = 0` for `i > a`, and `L` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent with `H^j(L) = 0` for `j > b`, then `K ⊗^{𝐋}_O L` is `t`-pseudo-coherent
for `t = max (m + a) (n + b)`. Here `⊗^{𝐋}_O` is the derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU,
`Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedTensorProduct
    (K L : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (n m a b : ℤ)
    (hK : X.IsPseudoCoherentFrom K n)
    (hKa : ∀ i : ℤ, a < i →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) i).obj K))
    (hL : X.IsPseudoCoherentFrom L m)
    (hLb : ∀ j : ℤ, b < j →
      IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (_root_.SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) j).obj L)) :
    X.IsPseudoCoherentFrom
      ((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.O |>.obj K).obj L)
      (max (m + a) (n + b))

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.isPseudoCoherent_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09J9, part (2).** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site. If `K` and `L` are pseudo-coherent
objects of `D(O)`, then `K ⊗^{𝐋}_O L` is pseudo-coherent. Here `⊗^{𝐋}_O` is the derived tensor
product of Stacks 06YU, `Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherent_derivedTensorProduct
    (K L : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPseudoCoherent K) (hL : X.IsPseudoCoherent L) :
    X.IsPseudoCoherent
      ((Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.derivedTensorProductFunctor X.O |>.obj K).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.hasTorAmplitude_tensor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09JA.** If `K` has Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` and `L` has Tor amplitude in
`[c, d]`, then `K ⊗^L_O L` has Tor amplitude in `[a + c, b + d]`.

A degenerate interval is replaced by a one-point interval chosen below the degree under
consideration, which is a weaker hypothesis, and `hasTorAmplitude_tensor_of_le` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasTorAmplitude_tensor (a b c d : ℤ)
    (hK : HasTorAmplitude T K a b) (hL : HasTorAmplitude T L c d) :
    HasTorAmplitude T ((T.tensor.obj K).obj L) (a + c) (b + d)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPerfect_derivedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09JB.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site.  If `K` and `L` are perfect objects of
`D(O)`, then so is `K ⊗^{𝐋}_O L`.

Representatives of the two objects are replaced by resolutions `A` and `B` which are K-flat on
the site and on every slice of it, so that `K ⊗^{𝐋} L` is the class of `Tot(A ⊗_O B)`.  Above
an object of the site lying under a member of the covering that the perfectness of the first
factor supplies and a member of the one the second supplies, both factors have strictly perfect
models; the total tensor complex of those models is strictly perfect and is a local model of
`Tot(A ⊗_O B)`.  Stacks 08G6 (1) turns that family of local models into perfectness.

Stated for an arbitrary derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU, since only its `comparison`
field is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_derivedTensorProduct
    (T : Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.DerivedTensorProduct X.O)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{0} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) (hL : X.IsPerfect L) :
    X.IsPerfect ((T.tensor.obj K).obj L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isPerfect_tensor_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09JB.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site whose objects, morphisms and sections lie in
one universe.  If `K` and `L` are perfect objects of `D(O)`, then so is `K ⊗^{𝐋}_O L`.

Representatives of the two objects are replaced by resolutions `A` and `B` which are K-flat on
the site and on every slice of it, so that `K ⊗^{𝐋} L` is the class of `Tot(A ⊗_O B)`.  Above
an object of the site lying under a member of the covering that the perfectness of the first
factor supplies and a member of the one the second supplies, both factors have strictly perfect
models; the total tensor complex of those models is strictly perfect and is a local model of
`Tot(A ⊗_O B)`.  Stacks 08G6 (1) turns that family of local models into perfectness.

Stated for an arbitrary derived tensor product of Stacks 06YU, since only its `comparison`
field is used.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_tensor_of_isPerfect
    (T : Stacks.DerivedTensor.RingedSite.DerivedTensorProduct X.O)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K) (hL : X.IsPerfect L) :
    X.IsPerfect ((T.tensor.obj K).obj L)
declarations.comment: if K, L are perfect objects of D(O), then so is K ⊗^L_O L, on any ringed site RingedSite.{u,u,u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.hom_coproduct_bijective_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09JC (a).** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site, let `B` be a collection of objects of `C`
with a cofinal system of finite coverings whose fibre products again lie in `B` — hypotheses (1),
(2) and (3) of the tag, with `B` the quasi-compact objects — and let `X₀` be a member of `B`, the
quasi-compact final object of the tag. Let `K` be a perfect object of `D(O)`. If `M : I → D(O)`
has a bounded-below coproduct, then morphisms from `K` into that coproduct are finite sums,
`Hom(K, ⨁ M_i) = ⨁ Hom(K, M_i)`: the object `K` is compact relative to `D⁺(O)`.

The hypothesis `hreduce` is the reduction the source performs, and is what perfectness of `K` is
used for: by Stacks 08JJ the dual `K^∨` satisfies
`Hom_{D(O)}(K, N) = H⁰(X₀, K^∨ ⊗^L_O N)` naturally in `N`, the functor `T = K^∨ ⊗^L_O -`
commutes with direct sums, and `T` keeps a bounded-below coproduct bounded below. None of those
three facts is available in this library — see "What this file assumes" in the module
documentation — so the reduction is assumed; granted it, this is Stacks 0G22 at `U = X₀`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_coproduct_bijective_of_isPerfect
    (B : Set X.C) (Cov : ∀ U : X.C, Set (PreZeroHypercover.{c} U))
    (hCov : ∀ (U : X.C) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{c} U), Cov U F → F.sieve₀ ∈ X.J U)
    (hfinite : ∀ (U : X.C) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{c} U), Cov U F → HasIntersectionsIn B F)
    (hcofinal : ∀ (U : X.C), B U → ∀ S ∈ X.J U,
      ∃ F : PreZeroHypercover.{c} U, Cov U F ∧ F.sieve₀ ≤ S)
    (X₀ : X.C) (hX₀ : B X₀)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K)
    {I : Type i} [DecidableEq I]
    (M : I → DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    [HasCoproduct M]
    (hreduce : X.IsPerfect K →
      ∃ T : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)),
        ∃ _ : PreservesColimit (Discrete.functor M) T,
          (DerivedCategory.TStructure.t
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))).plus
              (T.obj (∐ M)) ∧
          ∃ e : ∀ N : DerivedCategory
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)), (K ⟶ N) ≃+
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
                  (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj
                (extensionByZeroUnit.{u, u, u, u} X.J
                  (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) X₀) ⟶ T.obj N),
            ∀ {N N' : DerivedCategory
                (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
              (f : K ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ N'), e N' (f ≫ g) = e N f ≫ T.map g) :
    Function.Bijective
      (DirectSum.toAddMonoid fun j => Preadditive.rightComp K (Limits.Sigma.ι M j))
declarations.comment: (a) bounded-below compactness; assumes the 08JJ reduction, not formalized

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.isCompactObject_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09JC (b).** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site, let `X₀` be an object of `C` — the
quasi-compact final object of the tag — and let `K` be a perfect object of `D(O)`. If cohomology
over `X₀` has finite cohomological dimension, that is `(C, O)` has finite cohomological
dimension, and if the functors `F ↦ H^p(X₀, F)` commute with direct sums, then `K` is a compact
object of `D(O)`.

The hypothesis `hreduce` is the reduction the source performs, and is what perfectness of `K` is
used for: by Stacks 08JJ the dual `K^∨` satisfies
`Hom_{D(O)}(K, N) = H⁰(X₀, K^∨ ⊗^L_O N)` naturally in `N`, and `T = K^∨ ⊗^L_O -` commutes with
direct sums. Neither fact is available in this library — see "What this file assumes" in the
module documentation — so the reduction is assumed; granted it, this is Stacks 094D at `U = X₀`.
The hypothesis `hsums` is what hypotheses (2) and (3) of the tag supply through Stacks 0739.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_of_isPerfect (X₀ : X.C)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K)
    (hcd : ∃ d : ℤ, ∀ (p : ℕ)
      (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)), d < (p : ℤ) →
        IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
          (op X₀)).rightDerived p).obj G))
    (hsums : ∀ (p : ℕ) (I : Type w), PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)
      ((SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        (op X₀)).rightDerived p))
    (hreduce : X.IsPerfect K →
      ∃ T : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)),
        ∃ _ : ∀ I : Type w, PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I) T,
          ∃ e : ∀ N : DerivedCategory
              (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)), (K ⟶ N) ≃+
              ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
                  (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)) 0).obj
                ((SheafOfModules.pullback.{u} (F := Over.forget X₀)
                  (𝟙 ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over X₀))).obj
                    (SheafOfModules.unit ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O).over X₀))) ⟶
                T.obj N),
            ∀ {N N' : DerivedCategory
                (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))}
              (f : K ⟶ N) (g : N ⟶ N'), e N' (f ≫ g) = e N f ≫ T.map g) :
    IsCompactObject.{w} K
declarations.comment: (b) unbounded compactness; assumes the 08JJ reduction, 0739 sums; not formalized

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.isCompactObject_of_isPerfect_of_isTerminal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09JC (b).** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site with a final object `X₀` and let `K` be a
perfect object of `D(O)`. If `(C, O)` has finite cohomological dimension, that is
`H^p(X₀, F) = 0` for every `O`-module `F` and every `p` beyond a fixed bound, and if the
functors `F ↦ H^p(X₀, F)` commute with direct sums, then `K` is a compact object of `D(O)`.

Unlike `Stacks.Cohomology.isCompactObject_of_isPerfect` this carries no hypothesis standing in
for the reduction of Stacks 08JJ: the functor is `- ⊗^L_O K^∨` for the canonical derived tensor
product of Stacks 06YU, it commutes with direct sums by
`preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedTensorFlip`, and the natural bijection is
`derivedDualHomEquivOfIsoStructureSheaf` at the identification
`derivedExtensionByZeroUnitIsoStructureSheaf` of `j_{X₀!}O_{X₀}[0]` with `O[0]`. Perfectness of
`K` is used exactly where the source uses it, to produce that bijection. What is still a
hypothesis, as in the conditional form, is the commutation `hsums` of the higher cohomology
functors with direct sums, which the source supplies from Stacks 0739.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_of_isPerfect_of_isTerminal (X₀ : X.C) (hX₀ : IsTerminal X₀)
    (K : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)))
    (hK : X.IsPerfect K)
    (hcd : ∃ d : ℤ, ∀ (p : ℕ)
      (G : SheafOfModules.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)), d < (p : ℤ) →
      IsZero (((SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        (op X₀)).rightDerived p).obj G))
    (hsums : ∀ (p : ℕ) (I : Type u), PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete I)
      ((SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u} (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)
        (op X₀)).rightDerived p)) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} K
declarations.comment: (b) unbounded compactness of a perfect object, with the 08JJ reduction DISCHARGED rather than assumed; the 0739 commutation of the cohomology functors with direct sums is still a hypothesis here, and is discharged from hypotheses (2) and (3) of the tag in Stacks.Cohomology.QuasiCompactSite.hom_coproduct_bijective_and_isCompactObject_of_isPerfect, which states both clauses

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.QuasiCompactSite.hom_coproduct_bijective_and_isCompactObject_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09JC.** Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site and assume `C` has the three properties of the
tag: a quasi-compact final object `X₀`, a cofinal system of finite coverings by quasi-compact
objects for every quasi-compact object, and quasi-compact fibre products inside such a covering.
Let `K` be a perfect object of `D(O)`. Then

* **(a)** `K` is a compact object of `D⁺(O)` in the sense of the tag: if `M : I → D(O)` is a
  family whose coproduct `⨁ M_i` is bounded below, then the canonical map
  `⨁ Hom(K, M_i) → Hom(K, ⨁ M_i)` is bijective; and
* **(b)** if `(C, O)` has finite cohomological dimension, that is if there is a `d` with
  `H^p(X₀, F) = 0` for `p > d` and every `O`-module `F`, then `K` is a compact object of `D(O)`.

Hypothesis (1) of the tag is `hterm`, `hqc` and `hX₀`; hypotheses (2) and (3) are the covering
data `B`, `Cov`, `hCov`, `hcofinal` and `hfinite`, `Stacks.Cohomology.HasIntersectionsIn`
carrying the finiteness clause of (2) together with the whole of (3). See "How the hypotheses of
the tag are read" in the module documentation.

Both clauses rest on the source's reduction to `j_{X₀!}O_{X₀}`, which is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedDualHomEquivOfIsoStructureSheaf` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.preservesColimitsOfShape_derivedTensorFlip`. Clause (a) then needs
the global Tor amplitude of `K^∨`, which is
`hasFiniteTorDimension_derivedDual_of_isPerfect` from (1); clause (b) needs the commutation of
the cohomology functors over `X₀` with direct sums, which is
`preservesCoproducts_rightDerived_evaluation_of_covers` from (2) and (3).
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_coproduct_bijective_and_isCompactObject_of_isPerfect
    (B : Set X.C) (Cov : ∀ U : X.C, Set (PreZeroHypercover.{c} U))
    (hCov : ∀ (U : X.C) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{c} U), Cov U F → F.sieve₀ ∈ X.J U)
    (hfinite : ∀ (U : X.C) (F : PreZeroHypercover.{c} U), Cov U F →
      Stacks.Cohomology.HasIntersectionsIn B F)
    (hcofinal : ∀ (U : X.C), B U → ∀ S ∈ X.J U,
      ∃ F : PreZeroHypercover.{c} U, Cov U F ∧ F.sieve₀ ≤ S)
    (X₀ : X.C) (hterm : IsTerminal X₀) (hqc : X.J.IsQuasiCompactObject X₀) (hX₀ : B X₀)
    (K : DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
      (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) (hK : X.IsPerfect K) :
    (∀ {I : Type u} [DecidableEq I]
        (M : I → DerivedCategory (_root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
          (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O))) [HasCoproduct M],
        DerivedCategoryB.IsBoundedBelow (∐ M) →
        Function.Bijective
          (DirectSum.toAddMonoid fun j => Preadditive.rightComp K (Limits.Sigma.ι M j))) ∧
      ((∃ d : ℤ, ∀ (p : ℕ) (G : _root_.SheafOfModules.{u}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O)), d < (p : ℤ) →
          IsZero (((_root_.SheafOfModules.evaluation.{u}
            (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.ringSheaf X.O) (op X₀)).rightDerived p).obj G)) →
        IsCompactObject.{u} K)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedAlgebra.opposite
declarations.doc:
The opposite differential graded algebra. Its underlying graded module and differential are
canonically identified with those of `A`, and its multiplication on homogeneous elements is
`a ⋅ᵒᵖᵖ b = (-1)^(deg a * deg b) • (b * a)`.
declarations.statement: public noncomputable def opposite : Opposite R A

A short exact sequence of differential graded modules remains short exact after forgetting
to cochain complexes of modules over the base ring.

The cohomology of a short exact sequence of differential graded modules forms a long exact

    (hS : S.ShortExact) (n m : ℤ) (hnm : (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel n m) :

The `k`-shifted differential graded module `M[k]`: degree `n` is the old degree `n + k`,
the differential is multiplied by `(-1)^k`, and the right algebra action is unchanged.

    DifferentialGradedModule A

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.Homotopy.exists_comp
declarations.doc:
Composing a homotopy with homomorphisms of differential graded modules on either side gives
a homotopy whose underlying map is the corresponding composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem Homotopy.exists_comp {K L : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A} (f g : Hom L M)
    (a : Hom K L) (c : Hom M N) (h : Homotopy f g) :
    ∃ k : Homotopy (c.comp (f.comp a)) (c.comp (g.comp a)),
      ∀ x : K.M, k.toLinearMap x = c.toFun (h.toLinearMap (a.toFun x))
