declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.preservesCoproducts_toHomotopyCategory
declarations.doc: The quotient functor preserves direct sums indexed by a type in the ambient universe.
declarations.statement:
instance preservesCoproducts_toHomotopyCategory (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R)
    (ι : Type u) :
    PreservesColimitsOfShape (Discrete ι) (toHomotopyCategory A)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.hasProducts_homotopyCategory
declarations.doc:
The homotopy category of differential graded modules over a differential graded algebra has
all products.
declarations.statement:
instance hasProducts_homotopyCategory (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, v} R) :
    HasProducts.{w} (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.hasCoproducts_homotopyCategory
declarations.doc: The homotopy category of differential graded modules has direct sums.
declarations.statement:
instance hasCoproducts_homotopyCategory (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, v} R) :
    HasCoproducts.{w} (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.IsAdmissibleMono
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism of differential graded modules is an admissible monomorphism if it has a
retraction by a map of graded right modules.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdmissibleMono {K L : DifferentialGradedModule A} (f : Hom K L) : Prop

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.IsAdmissibleEpi
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism of differential graded modules is an admissible epimorphism if it has a
section by a map of graded right modules.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdmissibleEpi {L M : DifferentialGradedModule A} (g : Hom L M) : Prop

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.IsAdmissibleShortExact
declarations.doc:
A short exact sequence of differential graded modules that splits as a sequence of graded
modules.
declarations.statement:
structure IsAdmissibleShortExact {K L M : DifferentialGradedModule A}
    (f : Hom K L) (g : Hom L M) : Prop

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.isAdmissibleShortExact_gradedSplit
declarations.doc:
**The two closed arrows of a graded-split short exact sequence are an admissible short exact
sequence.** Injectivity, surjectivity and exactness are all consequences of the four identities
of the graded splitting, and the splitting itself witnesses admissibility of the two arrows.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdmissibleShortExact_gradedSplit :
    IsAdmissibleShortExact (homOfCocycle A E.a) (homOfCocycle A E.b)
declarations.comment: a graded splitting is an admissible short exact sequence

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.IsAdmissibleMono
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism of left differential graded modules is an admissible monomorphism if it has a
retraction by a map of graded left modules.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdmissibleMono {K L : LeftModule A} (f : Hom K L) : Prop

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.IsAdmissibleEpi
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism of left differential graded modules is an admissible epimorphism if it has a
section by a map of graded left modules.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsAdmissibleEpi {L M : LeftModule A} (g : Hom L M) : Prop

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.IsAdmissibleShortExact
declarations.doc:
A short exact sequence of left differential graded modules that splits as a sequence of
graded modules.
declarations.statement: structure IsAdmissibleShortExact {K L M : LeftModule A} (f : Hom K L) (g : Hom L M) : Prop

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.connectingHom
declarations.doc:
The connecting homomorphism `M ⟶ K[1]` associated to graded splittings of an admissible short
exact sequence of differential graded modules, bundled with the formula `δ x = π (d_L (s x))`.

This is the first half of Stacks 09JU: the family `π ∘ d_L ∘ s` is a morphism of
`Mod_{(A,d)}`, i.e. it is `A`-linear, of degree `0` as a map into the shift, and commutes with
the differentials.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def connectingHom (f : Hom K L) (g : Hom L M)
    (hfg : IsAdmissibleShortExact f g) (s : GradedHom M L) (π : GradedHom L K)
    (hs : ∀ x : M.M, g.toFun (s.toFun x) = x)
    (hπ : ∀ x : K.M, π.toFun (f.toFun x) = x)
    (hker : LinearMap.ker π.toFun = LinearMap.range s.toFun) :
    {δ : Hom M (shift K 1) // ∀ x : M.M, δ.toFun x = π.toFun (L.d (s.toFun x))}
declarations.comment: clause (i): δ = π ∘ d_L ∘ s is a morphism M ⟶ K[1] of differential graded A-modules

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homologyMap_connectingHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09JU**, second clause: the connecting homomorphism `δ = π ∘ d_L ∘ s : M ⟶ K[1]` of
an admissible short exact sequence of differential graded modules induces the boundary maps of
the long exact cohomology sequence of 09JK.

The boundary map is the `δ` of the short exact sequence of underlying cochain complexes, i.e. the
one appearing in `DifferentialGradedModule.longExactCohomology`; the cohomology of `K[1]` in
degree `n` is identified with that of `K` in degree `n + 1` by the shift isomorphism of
`HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor`, as in 011H.

The proof transports 011K, the same statement for a degreewise split short exact sequence of
cochain complexes, along `forgetToCochainComplex`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homologyMap_connectingHom (hS : S.ShortExact)
    (hfg : IsAdmissibleShortExact S.f S.g)
    (sec : GradedHom S.X₃ S.X₂) (ret : GradedHom S.X₂ S.X₁)
    (hs : ∀ x : S.X₃.M, S.g.toFun (sec.toFun x) = x)
    (hret : ∀ x : S.X₁.M, ret.toFun (S.f.toFun x) = x)
    (hker : LinearMap.ker ret.toFun = LinearMap.range sec.toFun)
    (n m : ℤ) (hnm : (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel n m) (hm : 1 + n = m) :
    HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
        ((forgetToCochainComplex A).map
            (connectingHom S.f S.g hfg sec ret hs hret hker).val ≫
          (shiftToCochainComplexIso S.X₁).hom) n ≫
        ((HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} R) (ComplexShape.up ℤ) 0).shiftIso
          1 n m hm).hom.app S.X₁.toCochainComplex =
      (shortExact_forgetToCochainComplex A S hS).δ n m hnm
declarations.comment: clause (ii): δ induces the boundary maps of the long exact cohomology sequence

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.AdmissibleSquare.statement1
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1** (Stacks Tag 09JV).  Consider a square of homomorphisms of
differential graded `𝒜`-modules
```
K --f--> L
|a       |b
v        v
M --g--> N
```
that commutes up to homotopy, i.e. `b ∘ f` is homotopic to `g ∘ a`.  If `f` is an
admissible monomorphism, then `b` is homotopic to a homomorphism `b' : L → N`
that makes the diagram commute strictly: `b' ∘ f = g ∘ a`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement1 {K L M N : DGModule 𝒜}
    (f : Hom K L) (a : Hom K M) (b : Hom L N) (g : Hom M N)
    (hf : IsAdmissibleMono f)
    (hcomm : Homotopic (b.comp f) (g.comp a)) :
    ∃ b' : Hom L N, Homotopic b b' ∧
      ∀ x, b'.toLinearMap (f.toLinearMap x) = g.toLinearMap (a.toLinearMap x)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.AdmissibleSquare.statement2
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2** (Stacks Tag 09JV).  With the same setup as Statement 1, if
`g` is an admissible epimorphism, then `a` is homotopic to a homomorphism
`a' : K → M` that makes the diagram commute strictly: `g ∘ a' = b ∘ f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement2 {K L M N : DGModule 𝒜}
    (f : Hom K L) (a : Hom K M) (b : Hom L N) (g : Hom M N)
    (hg : IsAdmissibleEpi g)
    (hcomm : Homotopic (b.comp f) (g.comp a)) :
    ∃ a' : Hom K M, Homotopic a a' ∧
      ∀ x, g.toLinearMap (a'.toLinearMap x) = b.toLinearMap (f.toLinearMap x)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_factorization_isAdmissibleMono
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism of differential graded modules factors through an admissible monomorphism,
followed by a homomorphism which is split and a homotopy equivalence.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorization_isAdmissibleMono (α : K ⟶ L) :
    ∃ (L' : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A) (α' : K ⟶ L')
      (π : L' ⟶ L) (s : L ⟶ L'),
      α' ≫ π = α ∧ IsAdmissibleMono α' ∧
        s ≫ π = 𝟙 L ∧ Homotopic (π ≫ s) (𝟙 L')

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_admissibleMono_sequence
declarations.doc:
Replace a finite sequence of differential graded modules by one whose arrows are admissible
monomorphisms, compatibly with homotopy equivalences to the original sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_admissibleMono_sequence (n : ℕ)
    (L : Fin (n + 1) → DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A)
    (f : ∀ i : Fin n, Hom (L i.castSucc) (L i.succ)) :
    ∃ (M : Fin (n + 1) → DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A)
      (g : ∀ i : Fin n, Hom (M i.castSucc) (M i.succ))
      (p : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), Hom (M i) (L i)),
      (∀ i, IsAdmissibleMono (g i)) ∧
      (∀ i, IsHomotopyEquivalence (p i)) ∧
      (∀ i : Fin n, Hom.comp (p i.succ) (g i) = Hom.comp (f i) (p i.castSucc))

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.comp_homotopic_zero_of_isAdmissibleShortExact
declarations.doc:
A map which becomes null-homotopic after projection onto the quotient, followed by a map
which is null-homotopic on the sub-object, has null-homotopic composite.
declarations.statement:
theorem comp_homotopic_zero_of_isAdmissibleShortExact
    (f₂ : Hom K₂ L₂) (g₂ : Hom L₂ M₂) (h₂ : IsAdmissibleShortExact f₂ g₂)
    (b : Hom L₁ L₂) (b' : Hom L₂ L₃)
    (hright₁ : Homotopic (Hom.comp g₂ b) 0)
    (hleft₂ : Homotopic (Hom.comp b' f₂) 0) :
    Homotopic (Hom.comp b' b) 0

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGraded.DGModule.isAdmissibleEpi_of_surjective_of_isProjectiveAsGradedModule
declarations.doc:
A surjective homomorphism of lawful differential graded modules whose target is
projective as a graded module is an admissible epimorphism.

The lawfulness of `A` and of `P` is part of the setting of the statement but is not
needed to produce the splitting.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAdmissibleEpi_of_surjective_of_isProjectiveAsGradedModule
    (_hA : A.IsLawful) {M : DGModule.{u, w', v} A} {P : DGModule.{u, w, v} A}
    (hM : M.IsLawful) (_hP : P.IsLawful) (f : DGModule.Hom M P)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f.toFun)
    (hPProjective : IsProjectiveAsGradedModule.{u, v, w, w'} P) :
    DGModule.IsAdmissibleEpi f

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGraded.HomComplex.DGModule.hom_shift_equiv_cocycles
declarations.doc:
**Statement 1.**  Evaluation at the generator `1` gives a natural
`R`-linear isomorphism
`Hom_{Mod_{(A,d)}}(A[k], M) ≃ₗ[R] ker(d_M : M^{-k} → M^{-k+1}) = Z^{-k}(M)`,
sending `f` to `f(1)`.  The first conjunct records that the underlying map is
`f ↦ f(1)`; the second records naturality in `M`: for any morphism
`g : M → N`, the square with `cocyclesMap g` commutes.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_shift_equiv_cocycles (M : DGModule A) (k : ℤ) :
    ∃ e : Hom ((A.toDGModule).shift k) M ≃ₗ[R] ↥(M.cocyclesM (-k)),
      (∀ f : Hom ((A.toDGModule).shift k) M, ((e f : M.carrier)) = f.toFun (1 : A.carrier))
      ∧ (∀ (N : DGModule A) (g : Hom M N)
          (eN : Hom ((A.toDGModule).shift k) N ≃ₗ[R] ↥(N.cocyclesM (-k)))
          (_ : ∀ f', ((eN f' : N.carrier)) = f'.toFun (1 : A.carrier))
          (f : Hom ((A.toDGModule).shift k) M),
          eN (g.comp f) = cocyclesMap g (-k) (e f))

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGraded.HomComplex.DGModule.homotopyClasses_shift_equiv_cohomology
declarations.doc:
**Statement 2.**  Passing to homotopy classes, the isomorphism of
Statement 1 descends to a natural `R`-linear isomorphism
`Hom_{K(Mod_{(A,d)})}(A[k], M) ≃ₗ[R] H^{-k}(M)`, sending the homotopy class
`[f]` to the cohomology class of `f(1)`.  Here `hf` is the membership
`f(1) ∈ Z^{-k}(M)` provided by Statement 1.  The second conjunct records
naturality in `M`: for any morphism `g : M → N`, the square with the induced
map `cohomologyMap g` commutes (where the action on homotopy classes is
`[f] ↦ [g ∘ f]`).
declarations.statement:
theorem homotopyClasses_shift_equiv_cohomology (M : DGModule A) (k : ℤ) :
    ∃ e : HomotopyClass ((A.toDGModule).shift k) M ≃ₗ[R] M.cohomology (-k),
      (∀ (f : Hom ((A.toDGModule).shift k) M) (hf : f.toFun (1 : A.carrier) ∈ M.cocyclesM (-k)),
        e (Submodule.Quotient.mk f)
          = Submodule.Quotient.mk (⟨f.toFun (1 : A.carrier), hf⟩ : ↥(M.cocyclesM (-k))))
      ∧ (∀ (N : DGModule A) (g : Hom M N)
          (eN : HomotopyClass ((A.toDGModule).shift k) N ≃ₗ[R] N.cohomology (-k))
          (_ : ∀ (f' : Hom ((A.toDGModule).shift k) N)
                (hf' : f'.toFun (1 : A.carrier) ∈ N.cocyclesM (-k)),
              eN (Submodule.Quotient.mk f')
                = Submodule.Quotient.mk (⟨f'.toFun (1 : A.carrier), hf'⟩ : ↥(N.cocyclesM (-k))))
          (f : Hom ((A.toDGModule).shift k) M),
          eN (Submodule.Quotient.mk (g.comp f))
            = cohomologyMap g (-k) (e (Submodule.Quotient.mk f)))

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.isZero_hom_toHomotopyCategory_shift_regularModule
declarations.doc:
Every morphism of the homotopy category from the image of a shift of the regular module to
an acyclic object is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_hom_toHomotopyCategory_shift_regularModule (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R)
    (k : ℤ) {N : HomotopyCategory A} (hN : acyclic' A N) :
    ∀ f : (toHomotopyCategory A).obj (shift (regularModule A) k) ⟶ N, f = 0

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.leftOrthogonal_acyclic_toHomotopyCategory_shift_regularModule
declarations.doc:
The image of a shift of the regular module lies in the left orthogonal of the acyclic
objects of the homotopy category.
declarations.statement:
theorem leftOrthogonal_acyclic_toHomotopyCategory_shift_regularModule
    (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R) (k : ℤ) :
    (acyclic' A).leftOrthogonal ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj (shift (regularModule A) k))
declarations.comment: left orthogonality of the shifted regular module

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.isZero_hom_shift_regularModule
declarations.doc:
Every morphism of the homotopy category from the `k`-th shift, taken in `K(A, d)`, of the
regular module to an acyclic object is zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_hom_shift_regularModule (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R) (k : ℤ)
    {N : HomotopyCategory A} (hN : acyclic' A N) :
    ∀ f : ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj (regularModule A))⟦k⟧ ⟶ N, f = 0

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.leftOrthogonal_shift_regularModule
declarations.doc:
The `k`-th shift, taken in `K(A, d)`, of the regular module lies in the left orthogonal of
the acyclic objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem leftOrthogonal_shift_regularModule (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R) (k : ℤ) :
    (acyclic' A).leftOrthogonal (((toHomotopyCategory A).obj (regularModule A))⟦k⟧)
declarations.comment: left orthogonality, with the shift taken in the homotopy category

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.AdmissibleMono.admissibleMono_of_gradedInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks, Tag 09K2 / Lemma 22.19.1.** Let `f : I -> M` be an injective
homomorphism of differential graded `A`-modules. If `I` is graded injective
(Definition 3), then `f` is an admissible monomorphism (Definition 4): there is a
graded `A`-module map `pi : M -> I` with `pi . f = id_I`.

Because the structures `DGAlgebra`, `GradedModule`, `DGModule` bundle all their
axioms, `A`, `I`, `M` are genuine objects and no extra hypotheses are needed.
declarations.statement:
theorem admissibleMono_of_gradedInjective {A : DGAlgebra R}
    {I M : DGModule A} (f : DGModule.Hom I M)
    (hf : f.Injective) (hI : I.GradedInjective) :
    DGModule.AdmissibleMono f

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.tensorCharacterBilinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09K3, second equality.** For a right differential graded `A`-module `N` and a left
differential graded `A`-module `M`, maps of complexes of abelian groups `N ⊗_A M → ℚ/ℤ` are
exactly the differential graded `A`-bilinear pairings `N × M → ℚ/ℤ`.

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.homTensorCharacterEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09K3, first equality.** For a right differential graded `A`-module `N` and a left
differential graded `A`-module `M`, homomorphisms of right differential graded `A`-modules
`N → M^∨` into the character dual are exactly the maps of complexes of abelian groups
`N ⊗_A M → ℚ/ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
def homTensorCharacterEquiv :
    DifferentialGradedModule.Hom N (LeftModule.dual M) ≃
      ((CochainComplex.forget₂AddCommGrpCat R).obj (tensorComplex N M) ⟶
        characterTarget.{u})

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedDual.DGAlgebra.statement_one
declarations.doc:
There is an isomorphism of abelian groups
`Hom_{Mod_(A,d)}(M, A^vee[k]) ~= Z^k(M^vee)`, natural in `M`: it is compatible with
precomposition by an arbitrary morphism `phi : M' -> M` on the left and the induced
map `phi^vee` of dual complexes on the right.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement_one (k : ℤ) :
    ∃ Φ : ∀ M : RightModule A,
        RightModuleHom M ((dualModule A).shift k) ≃+ M.cocycles k,
      ∀ {M' M : RightModule A} (φ : RightModuleHom M' M)
        (f : RightModuleHom M ((dualModule A).shift k)),
        Φ M' (precomp φ ((dualModule A).shift k) f)
          = cocyclesMap φ k (Φ M f)

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedDual.DGAlgebra.statement_two
declarations.doc:
There is an isomorphism of abelian groups `Hom_{K(Mod_(A,d))}(M, A^vee[k]) ~= H^k(M^vee)`,
natural in `M` over the homotopy category: there is a family of group isomorphisms `Ψ M` such
that, for every morphism `phi : M' -> M`, the precomposition map `homotopyPrecomp phi` on
homotopy-category Hom groups corresponds under `Ψ` to the map `cohomologyMap phi k` induced on
cohomology by the dual chain map `dualMap phi`; moreover `cohomologyMap phi k` depends only on
the homotopy class of `phi`.
declarations.statement:
theorem statement_two (k : ℤ) :
    ∃ Ψ : ∀ M : RightModule A, homotopyHom M ((dualModule A).shift k) ≃+ M.cohomology k,
      (∀ {M' M : RightModule A} (φ : RightModuleHom M' M)
          (ξ : homotopyHom M ((dualModule A).shift k)),
          Ψ M' (homotopyPrecomp φ ((dualModule A).shift k) ξ)
            = cohomologyMap φ k (Ψ M ξ))
      ∧ (∀ {M' M : RightModule A} {φ ψ : RightModuleHom M' M},
          Homotopic φ ψ → cohomologyMap φ k = cohomologyMap ψ k)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.AdmissibleTriangle.DGModule.associatedTriangle_iso_of_compatibleSplittings
declarations.doc:
The triangle associated to an admissible short exact sequence is, up to canonical
isomorphism in the homotopy category `K(Mod_{(A,d)})`, independent of the choice of
compatible splittings: for any two pairs of compatible splittings `(s, π)` and `(s', π')`,
the identity morphisms on `K`, `L`, `M` form an isomorphism of the associated triangles
`T : K → L → M → K[1]` and `T' : K → L → M → K[1]` in `K(Mod_{(A,d)})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedTriangle_iso_of_compatibleSplittings
    {K L M : DGModule A} (E : AdmissibleSES K L M)
    (P P' : E.CompatibleSplittings) :
    Nonempty (TriangleHtpyIso P.associatedTriangle P'.associatedTriangle)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.nonempty_compatibleSplittings
declarations.doc: Admissibility supplies graded splittings compatible with one another.

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.associatedTriangle
declarations.doc: The triangle of an admissible short exact sequence in the homotopy category.

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.associatedTriangleOfSplittings_eq
declarations.doc:
The associated triangle is independent of the compatible graded splittings used to compute
its connecting arrow.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedTriangleOfSplittings_eq {K L M : DifferentialGradedModule A}
    (f : Hom K L) (g : Hom L M) (hfg : IsAdmissibleShortExact f g)
    (c : CompatibleSplittings A f g) :
    associatedTriangleOfSplittings A f g hfg c = associatedTriangle A f g hfg

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.IsDistinguishedTriangle
declarations.doc:
A triangle of the homotopy category is distinguished precisely when it is isomorphic to the
triangle of an admissible short exact sequence.
declarations.statement: def IsDistinguishedTriangle (T : Pretriangulated.Triangle (HomotopyCategory A)) : Prop

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.isDistinguishedTriangle_gradedSplit
declarations.doc:
**The triangle of a graded-split short exact sequence is distinguished.** The third arrow may
be presented by any homomorphism `Z ⟶ X[1]` whose underlying linear map is the connecting
morphism `π d(s)` of the splitting; a homomorphism of differential graded modules is determined
by that map.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDistinguishedTriangle_gradedSplit (δ : Hom Z (shift X 1))
    (hδ : ∀ z : Z.M, δ.toFun z = (DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.connectingHom E).1 z) :
    IsDistinguishedTriangle A (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk
      ((toHomotopyCategory A).map (homOfCocycle A E.a))
      ((toHomotopyCategory A).map (homOfCocycle A E.b))
      ((toHomotopyCategory A).map δ ≫
        eqToHom (CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor_obj_shift (homotopyRel A) ℤ X 1).symm))
declarations.comment: the triangle of a graded splitting is distinguished

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.cone
declarations.doc: The mapping cone, with its direct-sum coordinates and canonical maps.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def cone (f : K ⟶ L) : Cone f

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.mappingCone_isAdmissibleShortExact
declarations.doc:
The cone sequence `L ⟶ C(f) ⟶ K[1]` of a homomorphism of differential graded modules is an
admissible short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem mappingCone_isAdmissibleShortExact (f : K ⟶ L) :
    IsAdmissibleShortExact (coneInclusion f) (coneProjection f)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.associatedTriangle_mappingCone_eq
declarations.doc:
The triangle of the cone sequence of `f` is the displayed triangle `L → C(f) → K[1]` whose
connecting arrow is the shift `f[1]` of `f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedTriangle_mappingCone_eq (f : K ⟶ L)
    (h : IsAdmissibleShortExact (coneInclusion f) (coneProjection f)) :
    Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk
      ((toHomotopyCategory A).map (coneInclusion f))
      ((toHomotopyCategory A).map (coneProjection f))
      ((toHomotopyCategory A).map (shiftMap f 1) ≫
        eqToHom (CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor_obj_shift (homotopyRel A) ℤ L 1).symm) =
      associatedTriangle A (coneInclusion f) (coneProjection f) h

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.rotatedAssociatedTriangle_iso_connectingConeTriangle
declarations.doc:
The rotated admissible-sequence triangle is isomorphic to the cone triangle of its
desuspended connecting homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem rotatedAssociatedTriangle_iso_connectingConeTriangle (f : K ⟶ L) (g : L ⟶ M)
    (hfg : IsAdmissibleShortExact f g) :
    Nonempty (rotatedAssociatedTriangle f g hfg ≅ connectingConeTriangle f g hfg)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.inverseRotatedAssociatedTriangle_iso_mappingConeTriangle
declarations.doc:
The standard inverse rotation of an admissible-sequence triangle is the standard cone
triangle of the negative desuspended connecting map.
declarations.statement:
theorem inverseRotatedAssociatedTriangle_iso_mappingConeTriangle (f : K ⟶ L) (g : L ⟶ M)
    (hfg : IsAdmissibleShortExact f g) :
    Nonempty (inverseRotatedAssociatedTriangle f g hfg ≅
      mappingConeTriangle (-desuspendedConnectingHom f g hfg))

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_mappingConeMap_of_homotopic_square
declarations.doc:
A square of homomorphisms of differential graded modules commuting up to homotopy extends to
their mapping cones. The inclusion square and the shifted-projection square commute already
before passing to homotopy classes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mappingConeMap_of_homotopic_square
    (f₁ : K₁ ⟶ L₁) (f₂ : K₂ ⟶ L₂)
    (a : K₁ ⟶ K₂) (b : L₁ ⟶ L₂)
    (h : Homotopic (f₁ ≫ b) (a ≫ f₂)) :
    ∃ c : coneModule f₁ ⟶ coneModule f₂,
      coneInclusion f₁ ≫ c = b ≫ coneInclusion f₂ ∧
      c ≫ coneProjection f₂ = coneProjection f₁ ≫ shiftMap a 1

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.isIso_mappingConeMap_of_isIso
declarations.doc:
In a morphism of cone triangles, if the maps on the source and the target of the two
original arrows are homotopy equivalences, then so is the induced map on the cones.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_mappingConeMap_of_isIso
    (f₁ : K₁ ⟶ L₁) (f₂ : K₂ ⟶ L₂)
    (a : K₁ ⟶ K₂) (b : L₁ ⟶ L₂)
    (c : coneModule f₁ ⟶ coneModule f₂)
    (h₁ : Homotopic (a ≫ f₂) (f₁ ≫ b))
    (h₂ : Homotopic (b ≫ coneInclusion f₂) (coneInclusion f₁ ≫ c))
    (h₃ : Homotopic (c ≫ coneProjection f₂)
      (coneProjection f₁ ≫ shiftMap a 1))
    [IsIso ((toHomotopyCategory A).map a)]
    [IsIso ((toHomotopyCategory A).map b)] :
    IsIso ((toHomotopyCategory A).map c)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.mem_distinguishedConeTriangles_iff_isDistinguishedTriangle_negMor₃
declarations.doc:
A triangle of the homotopy category is isomorphic to a cone triangle exactly when negating
its third arrow gives the triangle of an admissible short exact sequence: the two classes are the
two sign conventions for the third arrow of the triangle of a homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_distinguishedConeTriangles_iff_isDistinguishedTriangle_negMor₃
    (T : Triangle (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)) :
    T ∈ distinguishedConeTriangles.{u, v, w} (A := A) ↔
      IsDistinguishedTriangle A (Triangle.mk T.mor₁ T.mor₂ (-T.mor₃))
declarations.comment: the two cone sign conventions against the admissible-sequence class

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.mem_distinguishedTriangles_admissible_iff
declarations.doc:
**The sign comparison of the two pretriangulated structures on `K(Mod_(A, d))`.** A triangle
is distinguished for the admissible-sequence structure
`DifferentialGradedModule.instPretriangulatedHomotopyCategory'` exactly when negating its third
arrow gives a triangle distinguished for the default cone-triangle structure
`DifferentialGradedModule.instPretriangulatedHomotopyCategory`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_distinguishedTriangles_admissible_iff
    (T : Triangle (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)) :
    T ∈ (instPretriangulatedHomotopyCategory' A).distinguishedTriangles ↔
      Triangle.mk T.mor₁ T.mor₂ (-T.mor₃) ∈
        (instPretriangulatedHomotopyCategory (A := A)).distinguishedTriangles
declarations.comment: the admissible-sequence pretriangulated structure against the cone-triangle one

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.mem_distinguishedTriangles_cone_iff
declarations.doc:
**The sign comparison, from the side of the default structure.** A triangle is distinguished
for the cone-triangle structure `DifferentialGradedModule.instPretriangulatedHomotopyCategory`
exactly when negating its third arrow gives a triangle distinguished for the admissible-sequence
structure `DifferentialGradedModule.instPretriangulatedHomotopyCategory'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_distinguishedTriangles_cone_iff
    (T : Triangle (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)) :
    T ∈ (instPretriangulatedHomotopyCategory (A := A)).distinguishedTriangles ↔
      Triangle.mk T.mor₁ T.mor₂ (-T.mor₃) ∈
        (instPretriangulatedHomotopyCategory' A).distinguishedTriangles
declarations.comment: the cone-triangle pretriangulated structure against the admissible-sequence one

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_mappingConeTriangle_iso_associatedTriangle
declarations.doc:
For an admissible short exact sequence, the projection of the cone onto the third term is a
homotopy equivalence and completes the identity maps on `K` and `L` to an isomorphism from the
cone triangle to the triangle of the sequence.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_mappingConeTriangle_iso_associatedTriangle (f : K ⟶ L) (g : L ⟶ M)
    (hfg : IsAdmissibleShortExact f g) :
    ∃ (q : coneModule f ⟶ M),
      (∀ x : (coneModule f).M,
        q.toFun x = g.toFun ((cone f).coordinates x).1) ∧
      ∃ e : mappingConeTriangle f ≅ associatedTriangle A f g hfg,
        e.hom.hom₁ = 𝟙 _ ∧ e.hom.hom₂ = 𝟙 _ ∧
          e.hom.hom₃ = (toHomotopyCategory A).map q

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_associatedTriangle_iso_mappingConeTriangle
declarations.doc:
Every cone triangle is isomorphic to the triangle of an admissible short exact sequence, by
the identity on the first vertex and a comparison to the original second vertex compatible with
the given homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_associatedTriangle_iso_mappingConeTriangle (f : K ⟶ L) :
    ∃ (L' M' : DifferentialGradedModule A) (f' : K ⟶ L') (g' : L' ⟶ M')
      (hfg : IsAdmissibleShortExact f' g') (b : L' ⟶ L),
      f' ≫ b = f ∧
        ∃ e : associatedTriangle A f' g' hfg ≅ mappingConeTriangle f,
          e.hom.hom₁ = 𝟙 _ ∧ e.hom.hom₂ = (toHomotopyCategory A).map b

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexToDerivedCategory_negMor₃_distinguished
declarations.doc:
The image in `D(O)` of a triangle isomorphic to a cone triangle of `K(Mod_(E, d))` is
distinguished once its third arrow is negated: that negation turns a cone triangle into the
triangle of an admissible short exact sequence, which tensoring with `K` keeps distinguished.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorWithComplexToDerivedCategory_negMor₃_distinguished
    (T : Triangle (DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.{0, max u v w t s, max u v w t s}
      (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).algebra))
    (hT : T ∈ distinguishedConeTriangles.{0, max u v w t s, max u v w t s}
      (A := (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).algebra)) :
    (tensorWithComplexToDerivedCategory.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).mapTriangle.obj
        (Triangle.mk T.mor₁ T.mor₂ (-T.mor₃)) ∈
      distTriang (DerivedCategory (TensorModO.{u, v, w, t, s} X))
declarations.comment: the sign that relates the two classes of triangles

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.mem_distinguishedConeTriangles_iff_isDistinguishedTriangle_signTwist_mapTriangle
declarations.doc:
**The two pretriangulated structures on `K(Mod_(A, d))` are exchanged by the sign-twisted
identity.** A triangle lies in the cone class exactly when its image under `signTwist A` is the
triangle of an admissible short exact sequence, and symmetrically. The two structures are
therefore equivalent as pretriangulated categories, by an equivalence which is the identity on
objects and on morphisms and twists only the comparison with the shift; they are *not* the same
structure, the two classes of triangles being the two sign conventions for the third arrow.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_distinguishedConeTriangles_iff_isDistinguishedTriangle_signTwist_mapTriangle
    (T : Triangle (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)) :
    T ∈ distinguishedConeTriangles.{u, v, w} (A := A) ↔
      IsDistinguishedTriangle A ((signTwist.{u, v, w} A).mapTriangle.obj T)
declarations.comment:
the cone-triangle structure against the admissible-sequence structure: the two
are exchanged by the sign-twisted identity of the homotopy category

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_pretriangulated_structure
declarations.doc:
There is a pretriangulated structure on the homotopy category of differential
graded modules whose distinguished triangles are precisely those arising from
admissible short exact sequences.

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.octahedron_of_admissible_monos
declarations.doc:
**Tag 09KI.** Two composable admissible monomorphisms of differential graded modules have
distinguished triangles completing them to an octahedron: there are distinguished triangles
`(K, L, Q₁)`, `(K, M, Q₂)` and `(L, M, Q₃)` on `α`, on `β ∘ α` and on `β`, together with maps
`a : Q₁ ⟶ Q₂` and `b : Q₂ ⟶ Q₃` satisfying the four commutations of (TR 4), for which the
triangle `(Q₁, Q₂, Q₃)` is itself distinguished.
declarations.statement:
theorem octahedron_of_admissible_monos (α : K ⟶ L) (β : L ⟶ M)
    (_hα : IsAdmissibleMono α) (_hβ : IsAdmissibleMono β) :
    letI q := toHomotopyCategory A
    ∃ (Q₁ Q₂ Q₃ : HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)
      (p₁ : q.obj L ⟶ Q₁) (d₁ : Q₁ ⟶ (q.obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (p₂ : q.obj M ⟶ Q₂) (d₂ : Q₂ ⟶ (q.obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (p₃ : q.obj M ⟶ Q₃) (d₃ : Q₃ ⟶ (q.obj L)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (a : Q₁ ⟶ Q₂) (b : Q₂ ⟶ Q₃),
      Triangle.mk (q.map α) p₁ d₁ ∈ distTriang (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A) ∧
      Triangle.mk (q.map α ≫ q.map β) p₂ d₂ ∈ distTriang (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A) ∧
      Triangle.mk (q.map β) p₃ d₃ ∈ distTriang (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A) ∧
      (p₁ ≫ a = q.map β ≫ p₂) ∧
      (a ≫ d₂ = d₁) ∧
      (p₂ ≫ b = p₃) ∧
      (d₂ ≫ (q.map α)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = b ≫ d₃) ∧
      Triangle.mk a b (d₃ ≫ p₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧') ∈ distTriang (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.octahedron_of_isAdmissibleMono
declarations.doc:
Two composable homomorphisms of differential graded modules have distinguished triangles
forming an octahedron.
declarations.statement:
theorem octahedron_of_isAdmissibleMono {K L M : DifferentialGradedModule A}
    (α : Hom K L) (β : Hom L M) (_hα : IsAdmissibleMono α) (_hβ : IsAdmissibleMono β) :
    let q := toHomotopyCategory A
    ∃ (Q₁ Q₂ Q₃ : HomotopyCategory A)
      (p₁ : q.obj L ⟶ Q₁) (d₁ : Q₁ ⟶ (q.obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (p₂ : q.obj M ⟶ Q₂) (d₂ : Q₂ ⟶ (q.obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (p₃ : q.obj M ⟶ Q₃) (d₃ : Q₃ ⟶ (q.obj L)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
      (a : Q₁ ⟶ Q₂) (b : Q₂ ⟶ Q₃),
      IsDistinguishedTriangle A (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk (q.map α) p₁ d₁) ∧
      IsDistinguishedTriangle A
        (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk (q.map α ≫ q.map β) p₂ d₂) ∧
      IsDistinguishedTriangle A (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk (q.map β) p₃ d₃) ∧
      (p₁ ≫ a = q.map β ≫ p₂) ∧
      (a ≫ d₂ = d₁) ∧
      (p₂ ≫ b = p₃) ∧
      (d₂ ≫ (q.map α)⟦1⟧' = b ≫ d₃) ∧
      IsDistinguishedTriangle A
        (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk a b (d₃ ≫ p₁⟦1⟧'))

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.instIsTriangulatedHomotopyCategory'
declarations.doc:
The homotopy category of differential graded modules is triangulated: the pretriangulated
structure of Tag 09KH satisfies the octahedron axiom.

Stated against `DifferentialGradedModule.instPretriangulatedHomotopyCategory'`, whose
distinguished triangles are those of an admissible short exact sequence. The homonymous
instance in `StacksFrontier/Algebra/DGA/Octahedron.lean` is the same axiom for the *other*
pretriangulated structure, `DifferentialGradedModule.instPretriangulatedHomotopyCategory`,
whose distinguished triangles are the cone triangles; the two are distinct statements and
carry distinct names.
declarations.statement:
instance instIsTriangulatedHomotopyCategory' (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, v} R) :
    IsTriangulated (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)

registrations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.instIsTriangulatedHomotopyCategory
registrations.comment: the homotopy category is triangulated

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.PropertyPFiltration
declarations.doc:
A *property-(P) filtration* of a differential graded `A`-module `P` (Tag 09KK): an
exhaustive increasing filtration `0 = F_{-1} ⊆ F_0 ⊆ F_1 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ P` by differential graded
submodules whose inclusions are admissible monomorphisms and whose successive quotients are
direct sums of shifts of `A`.

The stages are presented by injective homomorphisms `ι i : F i ⟶ P` rather than as submodules,
and the graded pieces by surjective homomorphisms onto direct sums of shifts with the prescribed
kernel; the implicit stage `F_{-1} = 0` is encoded by the requirement that `F 0` itself be
isomorphic to a direct sum of shifts.
declarations.statement: structure PropertyPFiltration (P : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A)
declarations.comment: a filtration as in property (P): exhaustive, admissible inclusions, graded pieces direct sums of shifts A[k]; bundled encoding

registrations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGraded.DGModule.PropertyPFiltration
registrations.comment: a filtration as in property (P); unbundled encoding

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGraded.DGModule.admissible_ses_of_propertyP
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09KL (Lemma 22.20.1).**
Let `(A, d)` be a *lawful* differential graded algebra, `P` a lawful differential graded
`A`-module, and `F_*` a filtration as in property (P) (Definition 3, with all its
gradedness/lawfulness/quotient conditions bundled into `PropertyPFiltration`).  Then the
telescope object `⨁_{i ≥ 0} F_i P` is itself a lawful differential graded `A`-module, and
there exist DG homomorphisms `α` and `β` whose underlying linear maps are the explicit
telescoping maps `telescopeAlphaFun F` and `telescopeBetaFun F`, fitting into an admissible
short exact sequence of differential graded `A`-modules
`0 → ⨁_{i ≥ 0} F_i P →[α] ⨁_{i ≥ 0} F_i P →[β] P → 0`.

In particular this asserts items (1)–(5) of the Main Statement: the source/target object
lives in the category `Mod_(A,d)` (it is lawful), `α, β` are DG homomorphisms with the
prescribed underlying maps, `α` is injective, `β` is surjective, `range α = ker β`, and the
sequence is admissible.

Proof: assemble the eight sub-lemmas above.  Lawfulness is `telescopeObj_isLawful`; obtain
`α, β` from `exists_telescopeAlpha`/`exists_telescopeBeta` with `α.toFun = telescopeAlphaFun F`
and `β.toFun = telescopeBetaFun F`; the `AdmissibleSES` fields are then
`telescopeAlphaFun_injective`,
`telescopeBetaFun_surjective`, `telescope_exact`, `telescopeAlpha_admissibleMono`, and
`telescopeBeta_admissibleEpi`, with the underlying-map equalities `hα`, `hβ` used to rewrite
`α.toFun`/`β.toFun` to the explicit telescope maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem admissible_ses_of_propertyP
    {P : DGModule A} (hP : P.IsLawful)
    (F : PropertyPFiltration P) :
    (telescopeObj F).IsLawful ∧
    ∃ (α : Hom (telescopeObj F) (telescopeObj F)) (β : Hom (telescopeObj F) P),
      α.toFun = telescopeAlphaFun F ∧
      β.toFun = telescopeBetaFun F ∧
      AdmissibleSES α β

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.leftOrthogonal_acyclic_of_propertyP
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09KM.** *"Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra. Let `P` be a
differential graded `A`-module with property (P). Then `Hom_{K(Mod_(A,d))}(P, N) = 0` for all
acyclic differential graded `A`-modules `N`."*

Here the vanishing of all those hom-sets is phrased as membership of `P` in the left orthogonal
of the acyclic objects of the homotopy category, which says that every morphism out of `P` into
an object satisfying `acyclic'` is zero; since every object of `HomotopyCategory A` is the image
of a differential graded module, the two readings agree.

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.exists_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09KN for left differential graded modules.** Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded
algebra over a commutative ring `R` and let `N` be a *left* differential graded `A`-module. Then
there are a family of degrees `k : ι → ℤ`, a family of cell kinds `b : ι → Bool` and a
homomorphism `f : ⨁ᵢ Q_{kᵢ} ⟶ N` such that

1. `f` is surjective;
2. a homogeneous cocycle of `N` of degree `m` is the image of a cocycle of degree `m`, and
   consequently `Ker(d) → Ker(d_N)` is surjective — part (2) of the source lemma; and
3. `⨁ᵢ Q_{kᵢ}` sits in an admissible short exact sequence
   `0 → ⨁ᵢ A[-kᵢ-1] → ⨁ᵢ Q_{kᵢ} → ⨁ᵢ A[-kᵢ] → 0`

whose two ends are direct sums of shifts of `A`.

The cover is indexed by the homogeneous elements of `N`, which give two-cells and supply (1),
together with the homogeneous *cocycles* of `N`, which give bare cells and supply (2): the
generator `xᵢ` of a bare cell is itself a cocycle, homogeneous of degree `kᵢ`, and it maps to
the cocycle it indexes. A general cocycle of `N` is the finite sum of its homogeneous
components, which are cocycles by `induction_cocycle`.

The degreewise form of (2) is recorded as well as the plain one because that is what the proof
of Stacks 09KT needs: the differential of a graded dual is precomposition with the *signed*
differential, and the sign is only known on a homogeneous element.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R) (N : LeftModule A) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : DecidableEq ι) (k : ι → ℤ) (b : ι → Bool)
      (f : twoCellSum A k b ⟶ N),
      Function.Surjective f.toFun ∧
      (∀ (m : ℤ) (z : N.M), z ∈ N.grading m → N.d z = 0 →
        ∃ q : (twoCellSum A k b).M, q ∈ (twoCellSum A k b).grading m ∧
          (twoCellSum A k b).d q = 0 ∧ f.toFun q = z) ∧
      (∀ z : N.M, N.d z = 0 →
        ∃ q : (twoCellSum A k b).M, (twoCellSum A k b).d q = 0 ∧ f.toFun q = z) ∧
      ∃ (i : directSumShifts A (fun c => -k c - 1) ⟶ twoCellSum A k b)
        (p : twoCellSum A k b ⟶ directSumShifts A (fun c => -k c)),
        IsAdmissibleShortExact i p

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_cover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09KN** in the bundled encoding. Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra over
a commutative ring `R` and let `M` be a right differential graded `A`-module. Then there is a
right differential graded `A`-module `P` and a homomorphism `f : P ⟶ M` such that

1. `f` is surjective;
2. `f` is surjective on cocycles in every degree: every degree-`n` cocycle of `M` is the image
   of a degree-`n` cocycle of `P`; and
3. `P` is an extension of a direct sum of shifts of `A` by a direct sum of shifts of `A`, by an
   admissible short exact sequence `P' ⟶ P ⟶ P''` whose two ends `P'` and `P''` admit bijective
   homomorphisms onto `directSumShifts A k'` and `directSumShifts A k''` respectively.

This is `DifferentialGraded.NativeCover.exists_native_cover` transported to the bundled
encoding.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R) (M : DifferentialGradedModule A) :
    ∃ (P : DifferentialGradedModule A) (f : P ⟶ M),
      Function.Surjective f.toFun ∧
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (y : M.M), y ∈ M.grading n → M.d y = 0 →
        ∃ x : P.M, x ∈ P.grading n ∧ P.d x = 0 ∧ f.toFun x = y) ∧
      ∃ (P' P'' : DifferentialGradedModule A) (i : P' ⟶ P) (p : P ⟶ P'')
        (ι' ι'' : Type u) (dec' : DecidableEq ι') (dec'' : DecidableEq ι'')
        (k' : ι' → ℤ) (k'' : ι'' → ℤ)
        (e' : P' ⟶ @directSumShifts _ _ A ι' dec' k')
        (e'' : P'' ⟶ @directSumShifts _ _ A ι'' dec'' k''),
        Function.Bijective e'.toFun ∧ Function.Bijective e''.toFun ∧
        IsAdmissibleShortExact i p

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.NativeCover.exists_dgModule_surjective_cover
declarations.doc:
**Theorem (Stacks Project, Tag 09KN, Lemma 22.20.3).**

Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra over `R` and `M` a differential
graded `A`-module.  Then there exists a differential graded `A`-module `P` and a
homomorphism `φ : P → M` of differential graded `A`-modules such that:
1. `φ` is surjective;
2. the induced map on cocycles `Ker(d_P) → Ker(d_M)` is graded surjective, i.e.
   every degree-`n` cocycle of `M` is the image of a degree-`n` cocycle of `P`;
   and
3. `P` sits in an admissible short exact sequence `0 → P' → P → P'' → 0` of
   differential graded `A`-modules where both `P'` and `P''` are isomorphic to
   direct sums of shifts of `A`.

All objects live in a common universe `Type u`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dgModule_surjective_cover
    {R : Type u} {A : Type u} [CommRing R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A]
    {𝒜 : ℤ → Submodule R A} [GradedAlgebra 𝒜] (dA : DGAlgebra R A 𝒜)
    {M : Type u} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (PM : DGModule R A 𝒜 dA M) :
    ∃ (P : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup P) (_ : Module R P)
      (PP : DGModule R A 𝒜 dA P) (φ : DGModule.Hom PP PM),
      -- (1) φ is surjective
      φ.Surjective ∧
      -- (2) the induced map on cocycles is graded surjective
      φ.GradedSurjectiveOnCocycles ∧
      -- (3) P sits in an admissible SES with both ends direct sums of shifts of A
      (∃ (P' : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup P') (_ : Module R P')
        (PP' : DGModule R A 𝒜 dA P')
        (P'' : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup P'') (_ : Module R P'')
        (PP'' : DGModule R A 𝒜 dA P''),
        -- the shift index types live in `Type u` as well, which is what the
        -- single-universe reading of Tag 09KN asserts
        IsDirectSumOfShifts.{u, u, u, u} PP' ∧ IsDirectSumOfShifts.{u, u, u, u} PP'' ∧
        Nonempty (AdmissibleSES PP' PP PP''))

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_propertyP_resolution
declarations.doc:
**Property-(P) resolutions exist** (Tag 09KP). Every right differential graded module `M`
over a differential graded algebra `(A, d)` receives a quasi-isomorphism from a differential
graded `A`-module `P` carrying a property-(P) filtration: an exhaustive increasing filtration by
differential graded submodules with admissible inclusions whose successive quotients are direct
sums of shifts of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_propertyP_resolution (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R)
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A) :
    ∃ (P : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A) (f : P ⟶ M),
      QuasiIso ((forgetToCochainComplex A).map f) ∧ Nonempty (PropertyPFiltration P)

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGraded.DGModule.exists_propertyP_resolution
declarations.doc:
**Property-(P) resolutions exist.** Every lawful differential graded module `M` over a lawful
differential graded algebra `A` receives a quasi-isomorphism from a lawful differential graded
`A`-module `P` carrying a property-(P) filtration: an exhaustive increasing filtration by
differential graded submodules with admissible inclusions whose graded pieces are direct sums of
shifts of `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_propertyP_resolution (A : DGAlgebra.{u, v} R) (hA : A.IsLawful)
    (M : DGModule.{u, w, v} A) (hM : M.IsLawful) :
    ∃ (P : DGModule.{u, max v w, v} A) (_hP : P.IsLawful) (f : DGModule.Hom P M),
      IsQuasiIsomorphism f ∧
        Nonempty (DGModule.PropertyPFiltration.{u, v, max v w, max v w, max v w, max v w} P)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_isAdmissibleShortExact_uliftProduct
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09KR.** *"Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra. Let `I` be a differential
graded `A`-module. If `F_•` is a filtration as in property (I), then we obtain an admissible
short exact sequence `0 → I → ∏ I/F_iI → ∏ I/F_iI → 0` of differential graded `A`-modules."*

The filtration enters only through the tower of quotients `Q i = I/F_iI` it determines, together
with conditions (1) and (2) of property (I): the quotient maps `p i : I ⟶ Q i` are compatible
with the transitions `t i : Q (i + 1) ⟶ Q i` (`hp`), the transitions are admissible
epimorphisms (`hadm`, condition (2)), and `I = lim Q i`, which is injectivity of
`I → lim Q i` (`hsep`) together with its surjectivity in each degree (`hcomplete`, the limit
being formed in differential graded modules and hence degreewise).

The product is `DifferentialGradedModule.uliftProduct Q`, the first map is the family of
quotient maps and the second is the identity minus the map induced by the transitions; each is
pinned down by what it does on the projections.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAdmissibleShortExact_uliftProduct {I : DifferentialGradedModule A}
    (Q : ℕ → DifferentialGradedModule A) (p : ∀ i, I ⟶ Q i) (t : ∀ i, Q (i + 1) ⟶ Q i)
    (hp : ∀ (i : ℕ) (x : I.M), (t i).toFun ((p (i + 1)).toFun x) = (p i).toFun x)
    (hadm : ∀ i, IsAdmissibleEpi (t i))
    (hsep : ∀ x : I.M, (∀ i, (p i).toFun x = 0) → x = 0)
    (hcomplete : ∀ (n : ℤ) (q : ∀ i, (Q i).M), (∀ i, q i ∈ (Q i).grading n) →
      (∀ i, (t i).toFun (q (i + 1)) = q i) → ∃ y ∈ I.grading n, ∀ i, (p i).toFun y = q i) :
    ∃ (α : I ⟶ uliftProduct Q) (β : uliftProduct Q ⟶ uliftProduct Q),
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (x : I.M), (uliftProduct.π Q i).toFun (α.toFun x) = (p i).toFun x) ∧
      (∀ (i : ℕ) (y : (uliftProduct Q).M), (uliftProduct.π Q i).toFun (β.toFun y)
        = (uliftProduct.π Q i).toFun y - (t i).toFun ((uliftProduct.π Q (i + 1)).toFun y)) ∧
      IsAdmissibleShortExact α β

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.rightOrthogonal_acyclic_of_propertyI
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09KS.** A right differential graded module with property (I) is orthogonal on the
right to the acyclic objects of the homotopy category: every morphism of `K(A, d)` from an
acyclic differential graded module into it vanishes.

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_dual_injection
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09KT.** Every right differential graded `A`-module `M` admits an injection `φ` into
the graded dual `I` of a direct sum of cells of left modules, such that
`Coker(d_M) → Coker(d_I)` is injective, and `I` sits in an admissible short exact sequence whose
two ends are the products of shifts of `A^∨`

`∏ᵢ A^∨[kᵢ]` and `∏ᵢ A^∨[kᵢ + 1]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dual_injection (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R)
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule A) :
    ∃ (ι : Type u) (_ : DecidableEq ι) (k : ι → ℤ) (b : ι → Bool)
      (φ : M ⟶ Ldual (DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.twoCellSum A k b)),
      Function.Injective φ.toFun ∧
      (∀ x : M.M,
        (∃ w : (Ldual (DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.twoCellSum A k b)).M,
          (Ldual (DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.twoCellSum A k b)).d w = φ.toFun x) →
        ∃ y : M.M, M.d y = x) ∧
      ∃ (i : productDualShifts A k ⟶ Ldual (DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.twoCellSum A k b))
        (p : Ldual (DifferentialGraded.LeftModule.twoCellSum A k b) ⟶
          productDualShifts A (fun c => k c + 1)),
        IsAdmissibleShortExact i p

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_propertyI_resolution
declarations.doc:
**Property-(I) resolutions exist** (Tag 09KU). Every right differential graded module `M`
over a differential graded algebra `(A, d)` admits a quasi-isomorphism into a differential
graded `A`-module `I` carrying a property-(I) filtration: an exhaustive decreasing filtration by
differential graded submodules with admissible inclusions whose successive quotients are
products of shifts of the graded dual `A^∨`.

The resolution is the one of the Stacks proof: `I` is the totalization
`∏_{j ≥ 0} Iⱼ[-j]` of the tower `I₀ → I₁ → ⋯` built from Stacks 09KT, and the map is its
augmentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_propertyI_resolution (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R)
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule A) :
    ∃ (I : DifferentialGradedModule A) (f : M ⟶ I),
      QuasiIso ((forgetToCochainComplex A).map f) ∧ Nonempty (PropertyIFiltration I)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic
declarations.doc:
The acyclic differential graded modules, as a class of objects of the
homotopy category of right differential graded `A`-modules.
declarations.statement: def acyclic : ObjectProperty (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.quasiIsomorphisms
declarations.doc:
The quasi-isomorphisms in the homotopy category of right differential graded
`A`-modules: those morphisms all of whose representing homomorphisms are
quasi-isomorphisms of the underlying cochain complexes.
declarations.statement: def quasiIsomorphisms : MorphismProperty (HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.quasiIsomorphisms_map_iff
declarations.doc:
A homomorphism of differential graded modules induces a quasi-isomorphism in the
homotopy category exactly when it is a quasi-isomorphism of the underlying cochain
complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIsomorphisms_map_iff {M N : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A} (g : M ⟶ N) :
    quasiIsomorphisms A ((toHomotopyCategory A).map g) ↔
      QuasiIso ((forgetToCochainComplex A).map g)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.doc:
Acyclicity is invariant under isomorphism in the homotopy category: an isomorphism there
is represented by a homotopy equivalence of the underlying cochain complexes, so it induces
isomorphisms on all homology.
declarations.statement:
instance acyclic_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms :
    (acyclic.{u, v, w} A).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroCohomologyDescent
declarations.doc:
Degree-zero cohomology of differential graded modules factors through the homotopy
category, and the resulting functor factors in turn through the localization at the
quasi-isomorphisms.  Both factorizations are the universal ones: the first is the lift along
the quotient by homotopy, available because homotopic homomorphisms agree on cohomology, and
the second is the lift along the localization functor, available because a quasi-isomorphism
becomes invertible on cohomology.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def degreeZeroCohomologyDescent :
    DegreeZeroCohomologyDescent.{u, v, w} A

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
Acyclic differential graded modules form a triangulated subcategory of the homotopy category:
they are the objects killed by degree-zero cohomology in every shift, and degree-zero cohomology
is a homological functor.
declarations.statement: instance acyclic_isTriangulated : (acyclic.{u, v, w} A).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
The triangulated subcategory of acyclic differential graded modules is saturated: the kernel of
a homological functor is stable under retracts, and a direct summand is a retract.
declarations.statement: instance acyclic_isSaturated : (acyclic.{u, v, w} A).IsSaturated

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic_trW_eq_quasiIsomorphisms
declarations.doc:
The morphisms of the homotopy category whose cone is acyclic are exactly the
quasi-isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem acyclic_trW_eq_quasiIsomorphisms :
    (acyclic.{u, v, w} A).trW = quasiIsomorphisms.{u, v, w} A

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.quasiIsomorphisms_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
The quasi-isomorphisms of the homotopy category of right differential graded `A`-modules form
a saturated multiplicative system: they are the morphisms whose cone lies in the kernel of
degree-zero cohomology, and the multiplicative system attached to the kernel of a homological
functor on a triangulated category is saturated.
declarations.statement: theorem quasiIsomorphisms_isSaturated : (quasiIsomorphisms.{u, v, w} A).IsSaturated

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.localization_kernel_eq_acyclic
declarations.doc:
The objects of the homotopy category annihilated by the localization at the
quasi-isomorphisms are exactly the acyclic differential graded modules: the acyclic modules are a
strictly full saturated triangulated subcategory, and such a subcategory is the kernel of the
localization at the multiplicative system it determines.
declarations.statement:
theorem localization_kernel_eq_acyclic :
    ((quasiIsomorphisms.{u, v, w} A).Q).kernel = acyclic.{u, v, w} A

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.quasiIsomorphisms_iff_forall_isIso_degreeZeroCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Cohomology detects quasi-isomorphisms on the homotopy category.** A morphism of `K(A, d)` is
a quasi-isomorphism exactly when degree-zero cohomology of each of its shifts is an isomorphism.
No representability is assumed of the morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIsomorphisms_iff_forall_isIso_degreeZeroCohomology {X Y : HomotopyCategory A}
    (g : X ⟶ Y) :
    quasiIsomorphisms' A g ↔
      ∀ n : ℤ, IsIso ((degreeZeroCohomologyOnHomotopy' A).map (g⟦n⟧'))

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic'
declarations.doc: The acyclic differential graded modules, as objects of the homotopy category.
declarations.statement: def acyclic' : ObjectProperty (HomotopyCategory.{u, u, u} A)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.quasiIsomorphisms'
declarations.doc: The quasi-isomorphisms in the homotopy category of differential graded modules.
declarations.statement:
def quasiIsomorphisms' :
    MorphismProperty (HomotopyCategory.{u, u, u} A)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroCohomologyDescent'
declarations.doc: The canonical descent data for degree-zero cohomology.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def degreeZeroCohomologyDescent' :
    DegreeZeroCohomologyDescent' A

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.quasiIsomorphisms_map_iff'
declarations.doc:
A DG-module map induces a quasi-isomorphism in the homotopy category
exactly when it is a quasi-isomorphism of the underlying cochain complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIsomorphisms_map_iff'
    {M N : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A} (g : M ⟶ N) :
    quasiIsomorphisms' A ((toHomotopyCategory.{u, u, u} A).map g) ↔
      QuasiIso ((forgetToCochainComplex A).map g)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms'
declarations.doc: Acyclicity is invariant under isomorphism in the homotopy category.
declarations.statement:
instance acyclic_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms' :
    (acyclic' A).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic_isTriangulated'
declarations.doc: Acyclic differential graded modules form a triangulated subcategory.
declarations.statement: instance acyclic_isTriangulated' : (acyclic' A).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic_isSaturated'
declarations.doc: The triangulated subcategory of acyclic modules is saturated.
declarations.statement: instance acyclic_isSaturated' : (acyclic' A).IsSaturated

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic_trW_eq_quasiIsomorphisms'
declarations.doc: The morphisms whose cones are acyclic are exactly the quasi-isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
theorem acyclic_trW_eq_quasiIsomorphisms' :
    (acyclic' A).trW = quasiIsomorphisms' A

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.quasiIsomorphisms_isSaturated'
declarations.doc: Quasi-isomorphisms form a saturated multiplicative system.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIsomorphisms_isSaturated' :
    (quasiIsomorphisms' A).IsSaturated

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.localization_kernel_eq_acyclic'
declarations.doc:
The objects annihilated by localization at quasi-isomorphisms are exactly
the acyclic differential graded modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem localization_kernel_eq_acyclic' :
    ((quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).kernel = acyclic' A

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory
declarations.doc:
The derived category of a differential graded algebra `A`: the localization of the homotopy
category of right differential graded `A`-modules at the quasi-isomorphisms.
declarations.statement: abbrev derivedCategory : Type _

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory_eq_verdierQuotient
declarations.doc:
The derived category is the Verdier quotient of the homotopy category by the full
triangulated subcategory of acyclic modules: the two descriptions are localizations of the
homotopy category at the same class of morphisms, by
`DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic_trW_eq_quasiIsomorphisms`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategory_eq_verdierQuotient :
    derivedCategory.{u, v, w} A = (acyclic.{u, v, w} A).verdierQuotient

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroCohomology_unique
declarations.doc:
Degree-zero cohomology on the derived category is the unique descent of degree-zero
cohomology on the homotopy category: any functor on the derived category whose composite with the
localization functor is degree-zero cohomology on the homotopy category is uniquely isomorphic to
`DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalization`, by an isomorphism compatible with
the given identification.
declarations.statement:
theorem degreeZeroCohomology_unique
    (G : derivedCategory.{u, v, w} A ⥤ ModuleCat.{w} R)
    (α : (quasiIsomorphisms A).Q ⋙ G ≅ degreeZeroCohomologyOnHomotopy A) :
    ∃! e : G ≅ degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalization A,
      Functor.whiskerLeft (quasiIsomorphisms A).Q e.hom ≫
        (degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalizationIso A).hom = α.hom

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory'
declarations.doc:
The derived category `D(A, d)` of right differential graded `A`-modules: the localization
of the homotopy category `K(A, d)` at the quasi-isomorphisms.
declarations.statement: abbrev derivedCategory' : Type (u + 1)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory_eq_verdierQuotient'
declarations.doc:
The derived category is the Verdier quotient of the homotopy category by the triangulated
subcategory of acyclic differential graded modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategory_eq_verdierQuotient' :
    derivedCategory' A = (acyclic' A).verdierQuotient

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroCohomology_unique'
declarations.doc:
Degree-zero cohomology on the derived category is the unique descent of degree-zero
cohomology on the homotopy category: a functor `G` on `D(A, d)` together with an identification
`α` of its restriction along the quotient functor with
`DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroCohomologyOnHomotopy'` agrees with
`DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalization'` by a unique natural isomorphism
compatible with `α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem degreeZeroCohomology_unique' (G : derivedCategory' A ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} R)
    (α : (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q ⋙ G ≅ degreeZeroCohomologyOnHomotopy' A) :
    ∃! e : G ≅ degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalization' A,
      Functor.whiskerLeft (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q e.hom ≫
        (degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalizationIso' A).hom = α.hom

registrations.comment: degree-zero cohomology

registrations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalizationIso
registrations.comment: cohomology factorization

registrations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalization'
registrations.comment: degree-zero cohomology on the derived category

registrations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroCohomologyOnLocalizationIso'
registrations.comment: factorization of degree-zero cohomology through the derived category

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_homEquiv_of_propertyPResolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09KY(1).** *"Let `P → M` be a P-resolution as in Lemma 09KP. Then
`Hom_{D(A,d)}(M, N) = Hom_{K(Mod_{(A,d)})}(P, N)`."*

The identification sends a morphism `g : M ⟶ N` of the derived category to the unique morphism
`P ⟶ N` of the homotopy category whose image in `D(A, d)` is the resolution map followed by
`g`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homEquiv_of_propertyPResolution {P M : DifferentialGradedModule A} (f : P ⟶ M)
    (hf : QuasiIso ((forgetToCochainComplex A).map f))
    (hP : Nonempty (PropertyPFiltration P)) (N : DifferentialGradedModule A) :
    ∃ e : ((quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj M) ⟶
            (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj N)) ≃
          ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj P ⟶ (toHomotopyCategory A).obj N),
      ∀ g, (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q.map (e g) =
        (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q.map ((toHomotopyCategory A).map f) ≫ g

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_homEquiv_of_propertyIResolution
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09KY(2).** *"Let `N → I` be an I-resolution as in Lemma 09KU. Then
`Hom_{D(A,d)}(M, N) = Hom_{K(Mod_{(A,d)})}(M, I)`."*

The identification sends a morphism `g : M ⟶ N` of the derived category to the unique morphism
`M ⟶ I` of the homotopy category whose image in `D(A, d)` is `g` followed by the resolution
map.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_homEquiv_of_propertyIResolution {N I : DifferentialGradedModule A} (f : N ⟶ I)
    (hf : QuasiIso ((forgetToCochainComplex A).map f))
    (hI : Nonempty (PropertyIFiltration I)) (M : DifferentialGradedModule A) :
    ∃ e : ((quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj M) ⟶
            (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj N)) ≃
          ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj M ⟶ (toHomotopyCategory A).obj I),
      ∀ g, (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q.map (e g) =
        g ≫ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q.map ((toHomotopyCategory A).map f)

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.DeltaFunctor.exists_deltaFunctorStructure_δ_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09L0.** The canonical functor from differential graded modules to
their derived category is a `δ`-functor, with connecting arrow the third arrow of the cone
triangle read after inverting the cone-to-quotient quasi-isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_deltaFunctorStructure_δ_eq :
    ∃ h : (canonicalFunctor.{u, v, w} A).DeltaFunctorStructure
        (DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A) (derivedCategory.{u, v, w} A),
      ∀ (S : ShortComplex (DifferentialGradedModule.{u, v, w} A)) (hS : S.ShortExact),
        ∃ q : coneModule S.f ⟶ S.X₃,
          (∀ x : (coneModule S.f).M,
            q.toFun x = S.g.toFun ((cone S.f).coordinates x).1) ∧
          (coneInclusion S.f ≫ q = S.g) ∧
          quasiIsomorphisms A ((toHomotopyCategory A).map q) ∧
          ∃ _ : IsIso ((canonicalFunctor A).map q),
            h.δ hS =
              inv ((canonicalFunctor A).map q) ≫
                (quasiIsomorphisms A).Q.map (coneTriangle S.f).mor₃ ≫
                  ((quasiIsomorphisms A).Q.commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app
                    ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj S.X₁)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.canonicalDeltaFunctorStructure
declarations.doc:
*"Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra. The functor `Mod_{(A, d)} → D(A, d)` has the
natural structure of a `δ`-functor."* The connecting morphism is
`DifferentialGradedModule.shortExactδ`, identified with `- p ∘ q⁻¹` in
`DifferentialGradedModule.canonicalDeltaFunctorStructure_δ_eq`.

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.canonicalDeltaFunctorStructure_δ_eq
declarations.doc:
The formula for the connecting morphism of the canonical `δ`-functor structure:
*"`δ_{K → L → M} = - p ∘ q⁻¹` with `p` and `q` as explained above"*. Here `q` is the comparison
`C(f) ⟶ M`, which on the underlying module `L × K` is `(l, k) ↦ g l` and restricts along the
inclusion of `L` to `g`, and which is invertible in `D(A, d)`; and `- p` is the third morphism of
the cone triangle, the *signed* cone projection `C(f) ⟶ K[1]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem canonicalDeltaFunctorStructure_δ_eq
    {S : ShortComplex (DifferentialGradedModule A)} (hS : S.ShortExact) :
    (∀ x : (coneObject S.f).M, (coneDescShortComplex S).toFun x = S.g.toFun x.1) ∧
      coneIncl S.f ≫ coneDescShortComplex S = S.g ∧
      ∃ _ : IsIso ((toDerivedCategory A).map (coneDescShortComplex S)),
        (canonicalDeltaFunctorStructure A).δ hS =
          inv ((toDerivedCategory A).map (coneDescShortComplex S)) ≫
            (quasiIsomorphisms A).Q.map (coneTriangle S.f).mor₃ ≫
              ((quasiIsomorphisms A).Q.commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app
                ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj S.X₁)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GradedCategory
declarations.doc:
A category graded over a ring `R`: every morphism module is the direct sum of its
integer-indexed homogeneous pieces, identities are homogeneous of degree zero, and composition
of morphisms of degrees `m` and `n` has degree `m + n`.
declarations.statement:
class GradedCategory (R : Type w) [Ring R] (C : Type u) [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C]
    extends Linear R C

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Graded
declarations.doc:
A functor between categories graded over `R` is graded if its maps on morphisms are
`R`-linear and preserve each homogeneous degree.
declarations.statement:
class Functor.Graded (R : Type w) [Ring R] {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] [Preadditive C]
    [GradedCategory R C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] [Preadditive D] [GradedCategory R D]
    (F : C ⥤ D) : Prop extends F.Additive, F.Linear R

declarations.name: DGCategory
declarations.doc:
**Definition 1 (Tag 09L5).**  A *differential graded category over a
commutative ring `R`*.  For each pair of objects `x, y` the family
`Hom x y n` (degree-`n` morphisms) is a graded `R`-module; the differential `d`
raises the degree by one and squares to zero; composition `comp` is graded and
`R`-bilinear, obeys the Leibniz rule, is associative and unital, and the
identities are closed of degree `0`.

To avoid casting along the (non-definitional) arithmetic identities of the
grading group `ℤ`, the graded operations carry an explicit equality of degrees
(e.g. composition of a degree-`m` and a degree-`n` morphism lands in any
prescribed degree `k` together with a proof `m + n = k`).
declarations.statement: structure DGCategory (R : Type*) [CommRing R]

declarations.name: DGCategory.DGFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Definition 2 (Tag 09L6).**  A *functor of differential graded categories
over `R`*: a map on objects together with degree-preserving `R`-linear maps on
Hom-modules that commute with the differential and preserve composition and
identities.
declarations.statement: structure DGFunctor {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (A B : DGCategory R)

declarations.name: DGCategory.dgFunctor_induces_functors
declarations.doc:
**Tag 09L8.**  A DG-functor `F : A → B` induces ordinary functors
`Comp F : Comp A ⥤ Comp B` (here `F.onComp`) and `K F : K A ⥤ K B` (here
`F.onK`), characterised by:

1. (objects) both agree with `F` on objects;
2. (morphisms of `Comp`) `Comp F` sends a closed degree-`0` morphism `f` to the
   (again closed) morphism `F.map f`;
3. (morphisms of `K`) `K F` sends the homotopy class `[f]` to `[F.map f]`;
4. (compatibility) the canonical functors `Comp → K` intertwine `Comp F` and
   `K F`, i.e. `compToK A ⋙ K F = Comp F ⋙ compToK B`.

These are the genuine functoriality content of the lemma; `F.onComp` and
`F.onK` are honest `CategoryTheory.Functor`s, so identity- and
composition-preservation (part (4) of the informal statement) is built into
their types.
declarations.statement:
theorem dgFunctor_induces_functors (F : DGFunctor A B) :
    (∀ x : A.Comp, F.onComp.obj x = F.obj x) ∧
      (∀ {x y : A.Comp} (f : x ⟶ y), (F.onComp.map f).1 = F.map f.1) ∧
      (∀ x : A.K, F.onK.obj x = F.obj x) ∧
      (∀ {x y : A.Obj} (f : A.Cocycle x y),
        F.onK.map (Quotient.mk _ f : A.HomotopyClass x y)
          = Quotient.mk _ (F.mapCocycle f)) ∧
      (compToK A ⋙ F.onK = F.onComp ⋙ compToK B)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homotopicToZero_iff_eq_d
declarations.doc:
A closed homogeneous morphism is a boundary if and only if the associated morphism to the
shifted target is homotopic to zero.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopicToZero_iff_eq_d {A C : CochainComplex B ℤ} {n : ℤ}
    (f : Cocycle A C n) :
    Nonempty (Homotopy (Cocycle.equivHomShift.symm f) 0) ↔
      ∃ (m : ℤ) (hm : m + 1 = n) (g : (dgCategory B).Hom A C m),
        hm ▸ (dgCategory B).d g = f.1

declarations.name: CochainComplex.complexesCategoryEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The canonical equivalence from the category of complexes of `CochainComplex.dgCategory B`
to the ordinary category of cochain complexes in `B`. It fixes objects and acts on morphisms by
taking the component of a cochain in each degree.

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homotopyCategoryHomologyAddEquiv
declarations.doc:
The canonical identification of homotopy classes of maps of complexes with
degree-zero cohomology of the differential graded Hom.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def homotopyCategoryHomologyAddEquiv
    (A C : CochainComplex B ℤ) :
    (((HomotopyCategory.quotient B (.up ℤ)).obj A) ⟶
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient B (.up ℤ)).obj C)) ≃+
      (CochainComplex.HomComplex A C).homology 0

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homotopyCategoryHomologyAddEquiv_map
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison carries a chain map to the cohomology class of its
degree-zero cochain.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopyCategoryHomologyAddEquiv_map
    {A C : CochainComplex B ℤ} (f : A ⟶ C) :
    homotopyCategoryHomologyAddEquiv B A C
        ((HomotopyCategory.quotient B (.up ℤ)).map f) =
      (homologyAddEquiv A C 0).symm (CohomologyClass.mk (Cocycle.ofHom f))

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homotopyCategoryEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The homotopy category of the differential graded category of complexes is
equivalent to the usual homotopy category of complexes.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def homotopyCategoryEquivalence :
    HomotopyCategory B (.up ℤ) ≌ (dgCategory B).K

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homotopyCategoryEquivalence_obj
declarations.doc: The comparison equivalence is the identity on complexes.

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homotopyCategoryEquivalence_map
declarations.doc:
On morphisms, the comparison sends the homotopy class of a chain map to
the corresponding degree-zero cocycle modulo boundaries.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopyCategoryEquivalence_map {A C : CochainComplex B ℤ}
    (f : A ⟶ C) :
    HEq ((homotopyCategoryEquivalence B).functor.map
      ((HomotopyCategory.quotient B (.up ℤ)).map f))
      (Quotient.mk _
        (show (dgCategory B).Cocycle A C from
          ⟨Cochain.ofHom f, by
            change δ 0 1 (Cochain.ofHom f) = 0
            simp⟩) :
        (dgCategory B).HomotopyClass A C)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homotopyCategoryEquivalence_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**The comparison of the two homotopy categories is an equivalence of triangulated
categories.** This is [Stacks, Tag 09L9] read as a statement about triangulated categories: the
two pretriangulated structures, Mathlib's on `K(B)` and
`CochainComplex.dgCategoryKPretriangulated` on `K(Comp^dg(B))`, correspond under it.
declarations.statement:
instance homotopyCategoryEquivalence_isTriangulated :
    (homotopyCategoryEquivalence B).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the comparison of the homotopy category of the differential graded category of complexes with the ordinary homotopy category is an equivalence of TRIANGULATED categories

declarations.name: CochainComplex.dgCategory
declarations.doc:
The differential graded category of cochain complexes in a preadditive category `B`. Its
degree-`n` morphisms `A ⟶ C` are the families `A.X i ⟶ C.X (i + n)`, the differential is
`(d f) i = f i ≫ d - (-1)^n • (d ≫ f (i + 1))`, and composition and identities are the
componentwise ones.
declarations.statement: public def dgCategory : DGCategory ℤ

declarations.name: CochainComplex.additiveFunctorDG
declarations.doc:
Applying an additive functor to each component of a cochain defines a differential graded
functor on complexes.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def additiveFunctorDG (F : B ⥤ B') [F.Additive] :
    DGFunctor (dgCategory B) (dgCategory B')

declarations.name: CochainComplex.additiveFunctorDG_obj
declarations.doc: The differential graded functor applies `F` degreewise to objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem additiveFunctorDG_obj (A : CochainComplex B ℤ) :
    (additiveFunctorDG F).obj A = (F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj A

declarations.name: CochainComplex.additiveFunctorDG_map
declarations.doc: The differential graded functor applies `F` to every component of a homogeneous map.

declarations.name: CochainComplex.additiveFunctorDG_onComp
declarations.doc:
On closed degree-zero maps, the differential graded functor is the usual functor on
cochain complexes, through the canonical comparisons.
declarations.statement:
theorem additiveFunctorDG_onComp :
    (additiveFunctorDG F).onComp ⋙ (complexesCategoryEquivalence B').1.functor =
      (complexesCategoryEquivalence B).1.functor ⋙ F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.additiveFunctorDG_onK
declarations.doc:
On homotopy classes, the differential graded functor is the usual functor on homotopy
categories, through the canonical comparisons.
declarations.statement:
theorem additiveFunctorDG_onK :
    letI : Category (dgCategory B).K :=
      (dgCategory B).instCategoryK
    letI : Category (dgCategory B').K :=
      (dgCategory B').instCategoryK
    F.mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙ (homotopyCategoryEquivalence B').functor =
      (homotopyCategoryEquivalence B).functor ⋙ (additiveFunctorDG F).onK

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homologyCoyonedaNatIso
declarations.doc:
**`H^n(Hom^•(K, -)) ≅ Hom_{K(B)}(K, (-)[n])` as functors.** The degree-`n` cohomology of the
`D(Ab)`-valued differential graded Hom functor `Hom(K, -)` that Tag 09LK right derives, read as a
functor to sets, is the functor corepresented by the homotopy class of `K` composed with the
`n`-th translation of the homotopy category of complexes in `B`.
declarations.statement:
def homologyCoyonedaNatIso (n : ℤ) :
    homToDerivedCategoryForget B K ⋙ DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) n ⋙
        forget (ModuleCat.{0} ℤ) ≅
      CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (HomotopyCategory B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) n ⋙
        coyoneda.obj (Opposite.op ((HomotopyCategory.quotient B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K))
declarations.comment: the cohomology of the differential graded Hom module Hom(K, -) of 09LE, in every degree, as the functor corepresented by K composed with the translation

declarations.doc: A homogeneous right `A`-linear map of degree `n` between differential graded modules.

declarations.doc: The differential graded category of right differential graded modules over `A`.
