declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homogeneousMapDifferential_eq_zero_iff_exists_hom_shift
declarations.doc:
A homogeneous map is closed for the Hom differential if and only if it is a homomorphism
into the shifted target, with the same underlying linear map.
declarations.statement:
theorem homogeneousMapDifferential_eq_zero_iff_exists_hom_shift
    (L M : DifferentialGradedModule A) (n : ℤ) (f : HomogeneousMap A L M n) :
    homogeneousMapDifferential A f = 0 ↔
      ∃ g : Hom L (shift M n), g.toFun = f.1

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homotopic_zero_iff_exists_homogeneousMapDifferential
declarations.doc:
A closed homogeneous map is a boundary exactly when the corresponding homomorphism into the
shifted target is homotopic to zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem homotopic_zero_iff_exists_homogeneousMapDifferential
    {L M : DifferentialGradedModule A} {n : ℤ}
    (f : HomogeneousMap A L M n) (F : Hom L (shift M n)) (hF : F.toFun = f.1) :
    Homotopic F 0 ↔
      ∃ g : HomogeneousMap A L M (n - 1), (homogeneousMapDifferential A g).1 = f.1

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.dgCategoryCompEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The category of complexes of the differential graded category of differential graded modules
is canonically equivalent to the category of differential graded modules: the equivalence is the
identity on objects and does not change the underlying linear map of a morphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dgCategoryCompEquivalence :
    { E : (dgCategoryData A).category.Comp ≌ DifferentialGradedModule A //
      (∀ M : (dgCategoryData A).category.Comp, E.functor.obj M = M) ∧
      (∀ (L M : (dgCategoryData A).category.Comp) (f : L ⟶ M),
        HEq (E.functor.map f).toFun f.1.1) }

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homotopyCategoryHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
Homotopy classes of homomorphisms of differential graded modules are canonically the
degree-zero cohomology classes of their differential graded Hom module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homotopyCategoryHomEquiv (L M : DifferentialGradedModule A) :
    ((((toHomotopyCategory A).obj L) ⟶ ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj M)) ≃
      (dgCategory A).HomotopyClass L M)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homotopyCategoryHomEquiv_map
declarations.doc:
The canonical bijection sends a homomorphism to the cohomology class of the closed
homogeneous map with the same underlying linear map.
declarations.statement:
theorem homotopyCategoryHomEquiv_map (L M : DifferentialGradedModule A) (f : Hom L M) :
    ∃ c : (dgCategory A).Cocycle L M, c.1.1 = f.toFun ∧
      homotopyCategoryHomEquiv A L M ((toHomotopyCategory A).map f) = Quotient.mk _ c

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homotopyCategoryEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The homotopy category of the differential graded category of differential graded modules is
canonically equivalent to the homotopy category of differential graded modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def homotopyCategoryEquivalence :
    HomotopyCategory A ≌ (dgCategory A).K

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homotopyCategoryEquivalence_obj
declarations.doc:
The canonical equivalence of homotopy categories is the identity on differential graded
modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem homotopyCategoryEquivalence_obj (L : DifferentialGradedModule A) :
    (homotopyCategoryEquivalence A).functor.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj L) = L

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homotopyCategoryEquivalence_map
declarations.doc:
The functor of the canonical equivalence acts on every morphism by the canonical
identification with degree-zero Hom cohomology.
declarations.statement:
theorem homotopyCategoryEquivalence_map (L M : DifferentialGradedModule A)
    (f : ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj L) ⟶ ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj M)) :
    HEq ((homotopyCategoryEquivalence A).functor.map f) (homotopyCategoryHomEquiv A L M f)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homologyAddEquiv_homologyMap_mk
declarations.doc:
**Tag 09LC is natural under a differential graded functor**, on cohomology classes. The
degree-`n` cohomology of the map of Hom complexes induced by `F` sends the class of a closed
degree-`n` homogeneous morphism `f : M ⟶ N` to the class of the cocycle `F f`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homologyAddEquiv_homologyMap_mk
    (f : ↥(AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom (General.homSc A M N n).g).ker) :
    CochainComplex.HomComplex.homologyAddEquiv ((dgFunctorToComplexes F).obj M)
        ((dgFunctorToComplexes F).obj N) n
        (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (dgFunctorHomComplexMap F M N) n
          ((General.homScHomologyEquiv A M N n).symm (QuotientAddGroup.mk f))) =
      CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass.mk
        (dgFunctorCocycle F (General.scX₂ A M N n f.1)
          ((General.homSc_g_eq_zero_iff A M N n f.1).mp f.2))
declarations.comment: naturality of the cohomology of the Hom complex under a differential graded functor, on cohomology classes

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homAddEquiv_homologyAddEquiv_homologyMap
declarations.doc:
**Tag 09LC is natural under a differential graded functor**, read on homotopy classes. The
degree-`n` cohomology class of the Hom complex `Hom^•_{(A, d)}(M, N)` attached to a closed
degree-`n` homogeneous morphism `f` is the homotopy class of `f : M ⟶ N[n]`
(`DifferentialGradedModule.General.closedToHomotopy`); its image under the degree-`n` cohomology
of the map of Hom complexes induced by `F` is the homotopy class attached to the cocycle `F f`,
and that class is the image of `f : M ⟶ N[n]` under the functor `F` induces on homotopy
categories, followed by the comparison `F(N[n]) ≅ F(N)[n]` of
`DifferentialGradedModule.dgFunctorToComplexesShiftIso`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homAddEquiv_homologyAddEquiv_homologyMap
    (f : ↥(AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom (General.homSc A M N n).g).ker) :
    CochainComplex.HomComplex.CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv
        (CochainComplex.HomComplex.homologyAddEquiv ((dgFunctorToComplexes F).obj M)
          ((dgFunctorToComplexes F).obj N) n
          (HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (dgFunctorHomComplexMap F M N) n
            ((General.homScHomologyEquiv A M N n).symm (QuotientAddGroup.mk f)))) =
      (dgFunctorToHomotopyCategory F).map (General.closedToHomotopy A M N n f) ≫
        (HomotopyCategory.quotient B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map
          (dgFunctorToComplexesShiftIso F N n).hom
declarations.comment: naturality of the cohomology of the Hom complex under a differential graded functor

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.General.homComplexHomologyEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Tag 09LC in every degree, at independent universes.** The degree-`n` cohomology of the
differential graded Hom complex `Hom^•_{(A, d)}(L, M)` is the group of morphisms `L ⟶ M[n]` of the
homotopy category of right differential graded `A`-modules.

A degree-`n` cohomology class is a closed degree-`n` homogeneous map modulo coboundaries, a closed
degree-`n` homogeneous map is a homomorphism `L ⟶ M[n]`, and a coboundary is a null-homotopic
one.
declarations.comment: the cohomology of the Hom complex in every degree, at independent universes

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.homCohomologyZeroNatIso
declarations.doc:
**`H^0(Hom^•_B(N, -)) ≅ Hom_{K(B,d)}(N, -)` on the homotopy category.** Degree-zero
cohomology of the internal hom out of a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule, as a functor on
`K(B, d)`, is the module of morphisms out of `N` in `K(B, d)`.

This is Tag 09LC read functorially: the left-hand side is the internal hom functor of Tag 0FQQ
followed by the degree-zero cohomology functor of Tag 09KW.
declarations.statement:
def homCohomologyZeroNatIso :
    homHomotopyCategoryFunctor A B N L ⋙ degreeZeroCohomologyOnHomotopy' A ≅
      (linearCoyoneda R (HomotopyCategory B)).obj
        (Opposite.op ((toHomotopyCategory B).obj N))
declarations.comment: degree-zero cohomology of the internal hom, functorially

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homShiftIso
declarations.doc:
**The shift comparison for `Hom(K, -)`.** For a cochain complex `K` in a preadditive
category, the identification of a degree `k + n` cochain `K ⟶ X` with a degree `k` cochain
`K ⟶ X[n]` is an isomorphism `Hom(K, X[n]) ≅ Hom(K, X)[n]` of differential graded modules over

      (DGCategory.representableModule (dgCategory B) K X).shift n

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedHomData
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LI.** *The right derived functor of `F` exists; we denote it
`RHom(N, -) : D(B, d) ⥤ D(A, d)`.* Here `F` is internal Hom out of the differential graded
`(A, B)`-bimodule `N` read on homotopy categories and followed by localization
(`DifferentialGradedModule.homToDerivedCategory`), and a right derived functor of it, with its
comparison map and the everywhere-definedness of Tag 05SV, is exactly a
`DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData`; so the source's assertion that the derived functor
exists is the construction of one such datum, which this is.

It is `DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.ofPropertyIResolutions` — the Stacks proof, Tag
06XN applied to the modules with property (I), whose orthogonality to the acyclic modules is
Tag 09KS — fed the existence of the resolutions, Tag 09KU
(`DifferentialGradedModule.exists_propertyI_resolution`). Nothing is assumed.

The functor is determined by this up to the canonical isomorphism
`DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.functorIso`, so a consumer that only needs *some*
`RHom(N, -)` should take an arbitrary datum rather than this one.
declarations.statement:
def derivedHomData (A B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R) (N : DifferentialGradedModule B)
    (L : BimoduleStructure A B N) : DerivedHomData A B N L

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homComplexesFunctorCommShift
declarations.doc:
**`Hom(K, -)` commutes with the translation.** The shift comparisons
`Hom(K, X[n]) ≅ Hom(K, X)[n]` of Tag 09LE are natural in `X` and compatible with
`CategoryTheory.shiftFunctorZero` and `CategoryTheory.shiftFunctorAdd`, so they make
`Hom(K, -) : CochainComplex B ℤ ⥤ Mod_{(E, d)}` a functor commuting with the shift by `ℤ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance homComplexesFunctorCommShift :
    (homComplexesFunctor B K).CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: the functor Hom(K, -) being derived commutes with the translation: the shift comparisons Hom(K, X[n]) = Hom(K, X)[n] are natural in X and compatible with shiftFunctorZero and shiftFunctorAdd, which is the coherence Functor.mapTriangle is formed with

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedForgetData
declarations.doc:
**The forgetful functor datum of Tag 09LK exists**, with no hypothesis beyond a differential
graded algebra over a commutative ring and a chosen derived category of complexes of modules
over that ring.

The functor is `DifferentialGradedModule.derivedForget`, the underlying-complex functor descended
through the quotient by homotopy and then through the localization at the quasi-isomorphisms, and
the identification is the composite of those two descents,
`DifferentialGradedModule.derivedForgetFactorization` and
`DifferentialGradedModule.forgetHomotopyToDerivedCategoryIso`.
declarations.statement: def derivedForgetData : DerivedForgetData A
declarations.comment: the forgetful functor D(E, d) ⥤ D(Ab) of the conclusion, together with the identification of its value on an ordinary differential graded module with the underlying complex of that module, which is the phrase `on taking associated complexes`

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homHomotopyFunctor_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LK, the exactness of `Hom(K, -)` on the homotopy categories.** The differential
graded Hom functor `Hom(K, -) : K(B) ⥤ K(E, d)` of Tag 09LE is exact as a functor of triangulated
categories: it commutes with the translation, which is
`CochainComplex.homHomotopyFunctorCommShift`, and it carries distinguished triangles to
distinguished triangles.

This is the exactness asserted by Tag 09LK of the functor being derived, read on the homotopy
categories. It is obtained from the exactness of the descent of `Hom(K, -)` along the quotient by
homotopy, transported along `CochainComplex.homHomotopyFunctorLiftIso`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance homHomotopyFunctor_isTriangulated :
    (homHomotopyFunctor B K).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the differential graded Hom functor Hom(K, -) : K(B) ⥤ K(E, d) is exact as a functor of triangulated categories -- it commutes with the translation and carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles, which is the exactness of the functor being derived read on the homotopy categories

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homToDerivedCategory_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LK, the exactness of the functor being right derived.** The functor
`Hom(K, -) : K(B) ⥤ D(E, d)` of Tag 09LK — the differential graded Hom functor followed by the
localization of the differential graded `E`-modules at the quasi-isomorphisms — is exact as a
functor of triangulated categories, the localization functor being exact.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance homToDerivedCategory_isTriangulated :
    (homToDerivedCategory B K).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the functor Hom(K, -) : K(B) ⥤ D(E, d) being right derived is exact as a functor of triangulated categories

declarations.name: CochainComplex.derivedHomReflectorFunctor
declarations.doc:
**The functor `R Hom(K, -) : D(A) ⥤ D(E, d)` of [Stacks, Tag 09LK]**, for
`E = C(K, K)` the endomorphism differential graded category of `K` in `Comp^dg(A)`: the
reflector-and-descend functor `DGCategory.phiReflector` of steps 1 and 2, taken at the chosen
witnesses `CochainComplex.derivedHomReflectorL` and `CochainComplex.derivedHomReflector_isZero`.

Deliberately an `abbrev`: the exactness and shift compatibility of `DGCategory.phiReflector`
(`DGCategory.phiReflectorCommShift`, `DGCategory.phiReflector_isTriangulated`) and the
identification `(*)` and step 3 at an arbitrary reflector all apply to it after reduction, so
nothing has to be re-registered or restated at the chosen witnesses — and in particular no second
`CommShift` term competes with the canonical one.
declarations.statement:
abbrev derivedHomReflectorFunctor : DerivedCategory A ⥤
    DGCategory.RightModule.derivedCategory
      (DGCategory.endDGCategory (CochainComplex.dgCategory A) K)
declarations.comment: the functor itself: R Hom(K, -) : D(A) ⥤ D(E, d), for E the endomorphism differential graded category of K

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homHomotopyFunctorCommShift
declarations.doc: **`Hom(K, -) : K(B) ⥤ K(E, d)` commutes with the translation.**
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance homHomotopyFunctorCommShift :
    (homHomotopyFunctor B K).CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: the differential graded Hom functor Hom(K, -) : K(B) ⥤ K(E, d) commutes with the translation, the shift comparisons of 09LE descending along the quotient by homotopy

declarations.name: CochainComplex.homToDerivedCategoryCommShift
declarations.doc: **The functor being right derived in Tag 09LK commutes with the translation.**
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance homToDerivedCategoryCommShift :
    (homToDerivedCategory B K).CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: the functor Hom(K, -) : K(B) ⥤ D(E, d) being right derived commutes with the translation

declarations.name: CochainComplex.isDistinguishedTriangle_homComplexesFunctor_triangleOfDegreewiseSplit
declarations.doc:
**`Hom(K, -)` carries the triangle of a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes to
a distinguished triangle of `K(E, d)`.** This is the triangle half of the exactness clause of Tag
09LK for the functor being derived.
declarations.statement:
theorem isDistinguishedTriangle_homComplexesFunctor_triangleOfDegreewiseSplit :
    IsDistinguishedTriangle (DGCategory.endAlgebra (dgCategory B) K)
      (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk
        ((toHomotopyCategory _).map ((homComplexesFunctor B K).map S.f))
        ((toHomotopyCategory _).map ((homComplexesFunctor B K).map S.g))
        ((toHomotopyCategory _).map (homComplexesConnecting B K S σ) ≫
          eqToHom (CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor_obj_shift
            (homotopyRel (DGCategory.endAlgebra (dgCategory B) K)) ℤ
            (DGCategory.representableModule (dgCategory B) K S.X₁) 1).symm))
declarations.comment: the functor Hom(K, -) carries the triangle of a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes to a distinguished triangle of K(E, d) -- preservation of distinguished triangles for the functor being derived

declarations.name: CochainComplex.exists_isDistinguishedTriangle_homComplexesFunctor
declarations.doc:
**`Hom(K, -)` preserves distinguished triangles.** Every distinguished triangle of `K(B)` is
isomorphic to the triangle of a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes, and the
image of that triangle under `Hom(K, -)` — with its third arrow corrected by the shift
comparison `Hom(K, X[1]) ≅ Hom(K, X)[1]` — is a distinguished triangle of `K(E, d)`.

This is the preservation of distinguished triangles asserted by Tag 09LK of the functor being
derived. It is stated for a presentation of the triangle by a degreewise split sequence rather
than as `CategoryTheory.Functor.IsTriangulated`; the `CategoryTheory.Functor.CommShift ℤ` that
the latter also requires is `CochainComplex.homComplexesFunctorCommShift`, whose degree-one
component is the comparison appearing here.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isDistinguishedTriangle_homComplexesFunctor [HasZeroObject B]
    [HasBinaryBiproducts B]
    (T : Pretriangulated.Triangle (HomotopyCategory B (ComplexShape.up ℤ)))
    (hT : T ∈ Pretriangulated.distinguishedTriangles
      (C := HomotopyCategory B (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) :
    ∃ (S : ShortComplex (CochainComplex B ℤ))
      (σ : ∀ n, (S.map (eval B (ComplexShape.up ℤ) n)).Splitting),
      Nonempty (T ≅ trianglehOfDegreewiseSplit S σ) ∧
        IsDistinguishedTriangle (DGCategory.endAlgebra (dgCategory B) K)
          (Pretriangulated.Triangle.mk
            ((toHomotopyCategory _).map ((homComplexesFunctor B K).map S.f))
            ((toHomotopyCategory _).map ((homComplexesFunctor B K).map S.g))
            ((toHomotopyCategory _).map (homComplexesConnecting B K S σ) ≫
              eqToHom (CategoryTheory.Quotient.functor_obj_shift
                (homotopyRel (DGCategory.endAlgebra (dgCategory B) K)) ℤ
                (DGCategory.representableModule (dgCategory B) K S.X₁) 1).symm))
declarations.comment: the functor Hom(K, -) being derived preserves distinguished triangles: every distinguished triangle of K(B) is the triangle of a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes, and its image, with the third arrow read through the shift comparison Hom(K, X[1]) = Hom(K, X)[1], is a distinguished triangle of K(E, d)

declarations.name: DGCategory.derivedHomForgetPhiReflectorBetaIso
declarations.doc: **`R Hom(K, -) ≅ R̃ ⋙ U`, with nothing owed.**
declarations.statement:
def derivedHomForgetPhiReflectorBetaIso :
    CochainComplex.derivedHomForgetFunctor A K h ≅ phiReflectorForget A K L hΦ
declarations.comment: the reduction clause: the functor REDUCES TO THE USUAL R Hom(K, -) on taking associated complexes of abelian groups, under the source's own hypothesis h and the reflector data of steps 1 and 2

declarations.name: DGCategory.phiReflectorCommShift
declarations.doc:
**`R̃ : D(A) ⥤ D(E)` commutes with the translations.** The comparison isomorphisms are
those of the composite `J ⋙ ev_K`: on the first factor they come from
`CategoryTheory.Functor.commShiftOfLocalization` at the localization
`DGCategory.phiComparisonLocalization`, on the second from the derived evaluation functor.

This names the term global instance search already produces for this goal; it is deliberately
not itself registered as an instance, since `CategoryTheory.Functor.CommShift` is data and a
second registration would be a diamond.
declarations.statement: def phiReflectorCommShift : (phiReflector A K L hΦ).CommShift ℤ
declarations.comment: half of exactness as a functor of TRIANGULATED categories: the translation compatibility of R Hom(K, -) : D(A) ⥤ D(E, d), relative to which the exactness below is stated

declarations.name: DGCategory.phiReflector_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**`R̃ : D(A) ⥤ D(E)` is exact.** It is the composite of the descent `J` of step 1 through
the localization `q` of `K(Comp^dg(A))` at the complexes `Φ⁻¹ N`, which is exact by
`DGCategory.isTriangulated_derivedReflectorDescent`, with evaluation at `K` on the derived
categories; both factors are exact, hence so is `R̃`.
declarations.statement: instance phiReflector_isTriangulated : (phiReflector A K L hΦ).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the other half: R Hom(K, -) : D(A) ⥤ D(E, d) is EXACT -- it carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles, for the translation compatibility above

declarations.name: StacksDraft.BalancedTensorProduct
declarations.doc:
The tensor product `M ⊗_A N` of a right `A`-module `M` and a left `A`-module `N`: the quotient
of `M ⊗_R N` by the balancing relations `x a ⊗ y - x ⊗ a y`.
declarations.statement: def BalancedTensorProduct : Type (max w w')

declarations.name: StacksDraft.BalancedTensorProduct.tmul
declarations.doc: The universal `A`-balanced bilinear map `(x, y) ↦ x ⊗ y` of `M ⊗_A N`.
declarations.statement: def tmul : M →ₗ[R] N →ₗ[R] BalancedTensorProduct R A M N

declarations.name: StacksDraft.BalancedTensorProduct.tmul_balanced
declarations.doc:
The universal map is `A`-balanced: `x a ⊗ y = x ⊗ a y`. This is the balancing relation the
tensor product is defined by.
declarations.statement: theorem tmul_balanced : IsBalancedBilinear A (tmul R A M N)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.BalancedTensorProduct.span_tmul_eq_top
declarations.doc: As an `R`-module, `M ⊗_A N` is generated by the symbols `x ⊗ y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem span_tmul_eq_top :
    Submodule.span R (Set.range fun p : M × N => tmul R A M N p.1 p.2) = ⊤
declarations.comment: generated by the symbols x ⊗ y

declarations.name: StacksDraft.BalancedTensorProduct.liftEquiv
declarations.doc:
The identification `Bilinear_A(M × N, Q) = Hom_R(M ⊗_A N, Q)`: composing with the universal
map `(x, y) ↦ x ⊗ y` is an `R`-linear bijection from the `R`-linear maps out of `M ⊗_A N` onto the
`A`-balanced `R`-bilinear maps `M × N → Q`.
declarations.statement:
def liftEquiv (Q : Type t) [AddCommGroup Q] [Module R Q] :
    balancedBilinearMaps R A M N Q ≃ₗ[R] (BalancedTensorProduct R A M N →ₗ[R] Q)
declarations.comment: Bilinear_A(M × N, Q) = Hom_R(M ⊗_A N, Q)

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.preservesColimits_balancedTensorFunctor_obj
declarations.doc:
Balanced tensoring with a fixed right `Λ`-module commutes with arbitrary colimits; in
particular it is right exact. This is because it is a left adjoint, its right adjoint being
`Q ↦ Hom_ℤ(N, Q)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem preservesColimits_balancedTensorFunctor_obj (N : ModuleCat.{v} (MulOpposite Λ)) :
    PreservesColimits ((balancedTensorFunctor Λ).obj N)
declarations.comment: right exactness and commutation with colimits

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorDGFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LM.** Tensoring with a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule is a functor of
differential graded categories.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def tensorDGFunctor (N : Bimodule A B) : TensorDGFunctorData N

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorCompFunctor
declarations.doc: **Stacks 09LM.** The induced functor on the categories of differential graded modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev tensorCompFunctor (N : Bimodule A B) :
    DifferentialGradedModule A ⥤ DifferentialGradedModule B

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorHomotopyFunctor
declarations.doc: **Stacks 09LM.** The induced functor on the homotopy categories.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorHomotopyFunctor (N : Bimodule A B) :
    HomotopyCategory A ⥤ HomotopyCategory B

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorCompFunctor_quotient
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LM.** Passing the ordinary tensor functor to homotopy classes yields the tensor
functor on the homotopy categories.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorCompFunctor_quotient (N : Bimodule A B) :
    (tensorCompFunctor N ⋙ toHomotopyCategory B) ≅
      (toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ tensorHomotopyFunctor N)

declarations.name: Bimod.tensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LN, ordinary tensor--hom.**  For a right `A`-module `M`, an `(A,B)`-bimodule
`N`, and a right `B`-module `P`, `B`-linear maps from `M ⊗_A N` to `P` are canonically the
same as `A`-balanced maps from `M` into the `B`-linear maps from `N` to `P`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def tensorHomEquiv {A B : Mon (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
    (M : Bimod (𝟙_ (Mon (ModuleCat.{u} R))) A) (N : Bimod A B)
    (P : Bimod (𝟙_ (Mon (ModuleCat.{u} R))) B) :
    rightLinearMaps (M.tensorBimod N) P ≃ₗ[R] balancedRightLinearMaps M N P

declarations.name: Bimod.tensorHomEquiv_apply
declarations.doc: The forward tensor-hom correspondence is evaluation on pure tensors.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tensorHomEquiv_apply {A B : Mon (ModuleCat.{u} R)}
    (M : Bimod (𝟙_ (Mon (ModuleCat.{u} R))) A) (N : Bimod A B)
    (P : Bimod (𝟙_ (Mon (ModuleCat.{u} R))) B)
    (f : rightLinearMaps (M.tensorBimod N) P) (m : M.X) (n : N.X) :
    (tensorHomEquiv M N P f).1 m n =
      f.1 (CategoryTheory.Limits.coequalizer.π
        (M.actRight ▷ N.X) ((α_ M.X A.X N.X).hom ≫ (M.X ◁ N.actLeft)) |>.hom
        (m ⊗ₜ[R] n))

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorCompFunctor_adj_homModuleFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LN, the differential graded case.** Tensoring with a differential graded
`(A, B)`-bimodule `N` is left adjoint to the internal hom out of `N`, as functors between the
categories of differential graded modules:
`Hom_{Mod^{dg}_{(B,d)}}(M ⊗_A N, P) = Hom_{Mod^{dg}_{(A,d)}}(M, Hom^•_B(N, P))`,
naturally in `M` and `P`.

This is the degree-zero part of the source's isomorphism of Hom complexes — the bijection of the
morphism groups of the two categories of differential graded modules — which is why the tag is
part-qualified.
declarations.statement:
def tensorCompFunctor_adj_homModuleFunctor (N : Bimodule A B) :
    tensorCompFunctor N ⊣ homModuleFunctor A B N.rightModule N.leftAction
declarations.comment: the differential graded case in degree zero

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorHomEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LN, the differential graded case**, as the bijection of morphism groups
`Hom_{Mod^{dg}_{(B,d)}}(M ⊗_A N, P) = Hom_{Mod^{dg}_{(A,d)}}(M, Hom^•_B(N, P))`. It is natural
in `M` and `P`, being the hom-set bijection of
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorCompFunctor_adj_homModuleFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
def tensorHomEquiv (N : Bimodule A B) (M : DifferentialGradedModule A)
    (P : DifferentialGradedModule B) :
    ((tensorCompFunctor N).obj M ⟶ P) ≃
      (M ⟶ (homModuleFunctor A B N.rightModule N.leftAction).obj P)
declarations.comment: the differential graded case in degree zero, as a bijection

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorHomotopyFunctor_adj_homHomotopyCategoryFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LN for differential graded modules, on the homotopy categories.** Tensoring with a
differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N` is left adjoint to the internal hom out of `N` as
functors `K(A, d) ⥤ K(B, d)` and `K(B, d) ⥤ K(A, d)`.

This is the adjunction on the categories of differential graded modules, descended along the
passage to homotopy classes: both functors are compatible with it, by Tag 09LM
(`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorCompFunctor_quotient`) and Tag 0FQQ
(`DifferentialGradedModule.homHomotopyDescent`), and an adjunction descends to a quotient
category by `CategoryTheory.Quotient.adjunctionOfSquares`.
declarations.statement:
def tensorHomotopyFunctor_adj_homHomotopyCategoryFunctor (N : Bimodule A B) :
    tensorHomotopyFunctor N ⊣ homHomotopyCategoryFunctor A B N.rightModule N.leftAction
declarations.comment: the differential graded case in degree zero, on the homotopy categories

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.exists_tensorHomComplexIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LN, in every degree.** For a right differential graded `A`-module `M`, a
differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N` and a right differential graded `B`-module `P` the two
Hom complexes

`Hom^•_{Mod^{dg}_{(B, d)}}(M ⊗_A N, P)`  and  `Hom^•_{Mod^{dg}_{(A, d)}}(M, Hom^•_B(N, P))`

are isomorphic as complexes of `R`-modules: in each degree `n` the homogeneous right-`B`-linear
maps `M ⊗_A N → P` of degree `n` correspond `R`-linearly to the homogeneous right-`A`-linear maps
`M → Hom^•_B(N, P)` of degree `n`, by restriction to the pure tensors, and the correspondence
commutes with the differentials of the two Hom complexes.

The correspondence is pinned by its value on pure tensors, which is what the first displayed
property says: the homogeneous map that the image of `ψ` at a homogeneous `x` presents sends `y`
to `ψ (x ⊗ y)`. That property determines it, since the pure tensors generate `M ⊗_A N`.

The degree-zero part is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorHomEquiv`, which is the bijection of
morphism groups of the two categories of differential graded modules; the statement here is the
isomorphism of Hom complexes that the source asserts, of which that bijection is the part given
by the closed elements of degree zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_tensorHomComplexIso (N : Bimodule A B) (M : DifferentialGradedModule A)
    (P : DifferentialGradedModule B) :
    ∃ e : ∀ n : ℤ, HomogeneousMap B (tensorObj N M) P n ≃ₗ[R]
        HomogeneousMap A M (homPresentation N P).module n,
      (∀ (n p : ℤ) (ψ : HomogeneousMap B (tensorObj N M) P n) (x : M.M)
          (hx : x ∈ M.grading p) (y : N.rightModule.M),
        ((homPresentation N P).homogeneousEquiv (p + n)
            ⟨(e n ψ).1 x, (e n ψ).2.1 p x hx⟩).1 y =
          ψ.1 (((tensorDGFunctor N).pure M).toLinearMap x y)) ∧
        ∀ (n : ℤ) (ψ : HomogeneousMap B (tensorObj N M) P n),
          e (n + 1) (homogeneousMapDifferential B ψ) =
            homogeneousMapDifferential A (e n ψ)
declarations.comment: the differential graded case in every degree, as an isomorphism of Hom complexes

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorCompFunctor
declarations.doc: **Stacks 09LM.** The induced functor on the categories of differential graded modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev tensorCompFunctor (N : Bimodule A B) :
    DifferentialGradedModule A ⥤ DifferentialGradedModule B
declarations.comment: the functor Mod_(A,d) -> Mod_(B,d), M |-> M (x)_A N

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorHomotopyFunctor_isTriangulated'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LR.** Tensoring with a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule is an exact functor
from the homotopy category of differential graded `A`-modules to that of differential graded
`B`-modules: it commutes with translation and carries distinguished triangles to distinguished
triangles.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorHomotopyFunctor_isTriangulated' (N : Bimodule A B) :
    ∃ h : (tensorHomotopyFunctor N).CommShift ℤ,
      letI := h
      (tensorHomotopyFunctor N).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorFunctorToDerivedCategory_isLeftDerivable
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09LS**, in the source's own sense. Tensoring with the bimodule `N`, followed by
localization of the target, is left derivable with respect to the quasi-isomorphisms: its left
derived functor is defined at every object of `K(A, d)`, meaning that the pro-object
`Qis(A)/X ⥤ D(B, d)` is essentially constant (Tag 05SV).
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorFunctorToDerivedCategory_isLeftDerivable (N : Bimodule A B) :
    (tensorFunctorToDerivedCategory N).IsLeftDerivable (quasiIsomorphisms' A)

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorFunctorToDerivedCategory_hasLeftDerivedFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09LS**, in Mathlib's Kan extension sense. Tensoring with the bimodule `N`,
followed by localization of the target, has a total left derived functor: a right Kan extension
along the localization of `K(A, d)` at the quasi-isomorphisms. This is what names
`- ⊗_A^𝐋 N` as a functor on `D(A, d)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorFunctorToDerivedCategory_hasLeftDerivedFunctor (N : Bimodule A B) :
    (tensorFunctorToDerivedCategory N).HasLeftDerivedFunctor (quasiIsomorphisms' A)
declarations.comment: existence of the total left derived functor

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor
declarations.doc:
The derived tensor product `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` of **Stacks Tag 09LS**: the total
left derived functor of tensoring with `N` followed by localization.
declarations.statement: def derivedTensorFunctor (N : Bimodule A B) : derivedCategory' A ⥤ derivedCategory' B

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_isLeftDerivedFunctor
declarations.doc:
The universal property of **Stacks Tag 09LS**: the comparison
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctorCounit` exhibits `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N` as the left derived
functor of tensoring with `N` followed by localization, with respect to the
quasi-isomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedTensorFunctor_isLeftDerivedFunctor (N : Bimodule A B) :
    (derivedTensorFunctor N).IsLeftDerivedFunctor
      (derivedTensorFunctorCounit N) (quasiIsomorphisms' A)

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedHomFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LT.** The derived tensor product `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` of Tag 09LS is a
left adjoint to derived Hom `RHom(N, -) : D(B, d) ⥤ D(A, d)` of Tag 09LI, for a differential
graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N`. Nothing is assumed.

This is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedHom` with both of its
hypotheses supplied: Tag 09LN by
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.tensorHomotopyFunctor_adj_homHomotopyCategoryFunctor`, and Tag 09KU
by `DifferentialGradedModule.exists_propertyI_resolution`, which also pins the derived Hom
functor to that of `DifferentialGradedModule.derivedHomData`.

*The degree-zero scope of the Tag 09LN input does not limit this.* What is proved of Tag 09LN
for differential graded modules is the bijection of the morphism groups of the two categories,
not the isomorphism of Hom *complexes* in all degrees that the source also states there. But
Tag 09LT asserts an adjunction of functors between the derived categories — a bijection of
morphism groups, natural in both variables — and it is deduced from an adjunction of functors
between the homotopy categories, which is again a bijection of morphism groups. The all-degrees
half of Tag 09LN is neither used nor needed, so this is Tag 09LT in full and the tag is bare.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedHomFunctor (N : Bimodule A B) :
    derivedTensorFunctor N ⊣ (derivedHomData A B N.rightModule N.leftAction).functor

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedHomFunctor_homEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LT**, as the bifunctorial identification of morphism groups
`Hom_{D(B,d)}(M ⊗_A^𝐋 N, P) ≃ Hom_{D(A,d)}(M, RHom(N, P))` that Stacks 0BYX, Example 22.33.2
uses. Nothing is assumed: it is the hom-set bijection of
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedHomFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedHomFunctor_homEquiv (N : Bimodule A B)
    (M : derivedCategory' A) (P : derivedCategory' B) :
    ((derivedTensorFunctor N).obj M ⟶ P) ≃
      (M ⟶ (derivedHomData A B N.rightModule N.leftAction).functor.obj P)
declarations.comment: as a bijection of morphism groups

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexToDerivedCategory_negMor₃_distinguished
declarations.doc:
The image in `D(O)` of a triangle isomorphic to a cone triangle of `K(Mod_(E, d))` is
distinguished once its third arrow is negated: that negation turns a cone triangle into the
triangle of an admissible short exact sequence, which tensoring with `K` keeps distinguished.
declarations.statement:
theorem tensorWithComplexToDerivedCategory_negMor₃_distinguished
    (T : Triangle (DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.{0, max u v w t s, max u v w t s}

`- ⊗_E^𝐋 K^• : D(E, d) ⥤ D(O)` of Tag 09LX is left adjoint to derived Hom

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerived_fullyFaithful_of_ext
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09LZ.** *"Let `(C, O)` be a ringed site. Let `K` be a complex of `O`-modules.
Assume (1) `K` represents a compact object of `D(O)`, and (2)
`E = Hom_{Comp^dg(O)}(K, K)` computes the ext groups of `K` in `D(O)`. Then the functor
`- ⊗_E^𝐋 K : D(E, d) ⥤ D(O)` of Lemma 09LX is fully faithful."*

The functor is the one Tag 09LX constructs,
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerived`, and the right adjoint through which the
source's proof runs is the derived Hom `RHom(K, -)` of Tag 09LK, the adjunction between them
being the unconditional
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerived_adj_derivedHomWithComplex` of Tag 09LY.

The source's two hypotheses are its two hypotheses here: `hcompact` is (1), that `K` represents a
compact object of `D(O)`, and `hExt` is (2), read as the bijectivity of the functor on the
morphism groups `Hom_{D(E, d)}(E, E[n])`. The source's proof uses (1) only through the
commutation of the right adjoint with direct sums, and that commutation is derived here rather
than assumed: the regular module `E` is a compact weak generator of `D(E, d)` and
`- ⊗_E^𝐋 K` sends it to `K`, so
`CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.preservesCoproducts_of_isCompactObject_map` applies.

Exactness of neither functor is assumed. The exactness of `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K` in the pretriangulated
structure in force on `D(E, d)` is false, by a sign; what holds, unconditionally, is the
exactness of its composite with the sign-twisted identity of `D(O)`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerived_signTwist_isTriangulated`), and the
adjunction read between the twisted composites carries that to the right adjoint. Since
`CategoryTheory.signTwist` is the identity on objects and on morphisms, the full faithfulness
obtained is full faithfulness of `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K` itself. See the module's implementation notes.

Everything else that
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerived_fullyFaithful` takes as an argument is
supplied here — the adjunction of Tag 09LY and its commutation
with the translation, the dévissage of Tag 0FQE, the direct sums of `D(E, d)` and the weak
generation of `D(E, d)` by the regular module. See the module's implementation notes.

Full faithfulness is data, a chosen inverse to the action on morphism groups, so this is a
definition.
declarations.statement:
def tensorWithComplexDerived_fullyFaithful_of_ext
    (hcompact : IsCompactObject.{max u v w t s}
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (liftComplex.{u, v, w, t, s} X K)))
    (hExt : ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Bijective
      (fun f : repRegularDerived.{u, v, w, t, s} X K ⟶
          (repRegularDerived.{u, v, w, t, s} X K)⟦n⟧ =>
        (tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).map f)) :
    (tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).FullyFaithful
declarations.comment: exactly the source's two hypotheses and nothing else: (1) is compactness of K in D(O), stated as such, and (2) is bijectivity of the functor on Hom(E, E[n]). The adjunction of Tag 09LY, the dévissage of Tag 0FQE, the direct sums and the weak generation of D(E, d), the commutation of RHom(K, -) with direct sums and the exactness of both functors (Tag 09LW, read through the sign-twisted identity of D(O)) are supplied by carriers of this library

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09M1].** On a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme `X`, an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is compact if and only if it is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`, in any model of
`D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem _root_.Stacks.Duality.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [h : HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules]
    (K : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} K ↔ @Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect X.toRingedSpace h K.obj

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.isCompactObject_eq_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09M1].** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. An object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is compact if and only if it is perfect: the compact objects of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` are
exactly those whose underlying object of `D(𝒪_X)` is perfect, in any model of `D(𝒪_X)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_eq_isPerfect (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    [h : HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.Modules] :
    (IsCompactObject.{u} : ObjectProperty (quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)) =
      fun K => @Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect X.toRingedSpace h K.obj

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.PerfectCompact.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme. An object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is compact
if and only if it is perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (K : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} K ↔ RingedSpace.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect_spec
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09M1 on an affine scheme.** Let `R` be a ring and let `L` be an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`. Then `L` is a compact object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})` if and only if it is a
perfect object of `D(𝒪_{Spec R})`.

Writing `L = M̃` for an object `M` of `D(R)`, compactness of `L` is compactness of `M` because
`M ↦ M̃` is an equivalence ([Stacks, Tag 06Z0], here
`AlgebraicGeometry.affineTildeQuasicoherent_isEquivalence`), compactness of `M` is perfectness of
`M` by [Stacks, Tag 07LT], and perfectness of `M` is perfectness of `M̃` by
[Stacks, Tag 08EB].
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect_spec (R : CommRingCat.{u})
    (L : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory (Spec R)) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} L ↔
      Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := (Spec R).toRingedSpace) L.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfect_of_isCompactObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09M1, the implication from compactness to perfectness.** Let `X` be a scheme and let
`K` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. Suppose every point of `X` has an open neighbourhood `U` on
which `K` is the image, under a functor preserving perfectness, of a compact object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})` for some ring `R`. Then `K` is a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.

Compactness of `K` itself enters only through the local models: on a quasi-compact
quasi-separated scheme the restriction of a compact object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` to an affine open is
compact there, by [Stacks, Tag 08DZ] and adjunction. The affine case makes the local models
perfect, and perfectness is local on the space by [Stacks, Tag 08CN].
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_of_isCompactObject (X : Scheme.{u}) (K : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (hloc : ∀ x : X.toRingedSpace.carrier,
      ∃ (U : Opens X.toRingedSpace.carrier) (_ : x ∈ U) (R : CommRingCat.{u})
        (Φ : DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{u} (Spec R).ringCatSheaf) ⥤
          DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u, u}
            (X.toRingedSpace.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding)))
        (L : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory (Spec R)),
        IsCompactObject.{u} L ∧
          (∀ N, Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect
              (X := (Spec R).toRingedSpace) N →
            Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect
              (X := X.toRingedSpace.restrict U.isOpenEmbedding) (Φ.obj N)) ∧
          Nonempty (Φ.obj L.obj ≅
            (RingedSpace.restrictModules X.toRingedSpace U).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj)) :
    Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K.obj
declarations.comment:
compact implies perfect; the affine-local datum, which the source draws from Tag
08DZ (derived direct image along a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism commutes with direct
sums) together with Tag 06Z0, is a hypothesis: that deduction is not carried out here. Tag 08DZ
is proved in this repository, as
Stacks.Duality.DerivedPushforward.preservesColimitsOfShape_discrete_qcqsQuasiCoherentDerivedPushforward,
but only at HasDerivedCategory.standard

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect_spec_of_model
declarations.doc:
**The affine case of [Stacks, Tag 09M1], at an arbitrary chosen derived category.** Let `R` be
a ring and let `K` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`, for any chosen model of `D(R)` and any
chosen model of `D(𝒪_{Spec R})`. Then `K` is a compact object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_{Spec R})`, with the
direct sums tested over index types in `Type u`, if and only if `K` is a perfect object of
`D(𝒪_{Spec R})`.

Writing `K = M̃` for an object `M` of `D(R)`, which is possible because `M ↦ M̃` is an equivalence
([Stacks, Tag 06Z0]), compactness of `K` is compactness of `M` because compactness at a fixed
index universe crosses an additive equivalence, compactness of `M` is perfectness of `M` by
[Stacks, Tag 07LT], and perfectness of `M` is perfectness of `M̃` by [Stacks, Tag 08EB].

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect_spec` with the pin on the standard model
removed; see the implementation notes for why it cannot be added beside it.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect_spec_of_model
    (K : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory (Spec R)) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} K ↔
      @Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (Spec R).toRingedSpace hS K.obj
declarations.comment: the affine case, both directions, at an arbitrary chosen derived category -- in particular at the locally small AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hasDerivedCategory, at which the companion AlgebraicGeometry.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect_spec says nothing. The global case is not covered here

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.QcqsPerfect.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09M1].** On a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme `X`, an object of
`D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is compact if and only if it is perfect, at the locally small derived category.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (K : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} K ↔
      Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K.obj
declarations.comment: both directions, on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, at the locally small AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hasDerivedCategory

declarations.name: Stacks.Duality.QcqsPerfect.isCompactObject_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and let `K` be an object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`
which is perfect as an object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Then `K` is a compact object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`, with
the direct sums tested over index types in the universe of `X`, at the locally small derived
category `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hasDerivedCategory`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_of_isPerfect (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (K : Stacks.Duality.quasiCoherentDerivedCategory X)
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K.obj) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} K
declarations.comment: perfect implies compact, on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, at the locally small AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.hasDerivedCategory. The opposite implication is not covered here; for it on a general scheme see AlgebraicGeometry.isPerfect_of_isCompactObject, and for both on an affine scheme see AlgebraicGeometry.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect_spec_of_model

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCategoryB_tensorWithComplexDerived_obj_scheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09M3.** *"Let `X` be a scheme, `K` a complex of `O_X`-modules with quasi-coherent
cohomology sheaves, `(E, d) = Hom(K, K)`. Then `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K : D(E, d) ⟶ D(O_X)` of Tag 09LX has
image contained in `D_QCoh(O_X)`."* The scheme is read as the ringed site of its opens.
declarations.comment: for the site of opens of the scheme

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCategoryB_isQuasicoherent_tensorWithComplexDerived_obj_scheme
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09M3.** Every cohomology sheaf of `M ⊗_E^𝐋 K` is a quasi-coherent `O_Y`-module, for
`Y` a scheme and `K` a complex of `O_Y`-modules with quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves.

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.exists_window_subsingleton_hom_of_isPerfect_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09M4], part (1).** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and
let `K` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`. Then there are integers `a ≤ b` such that every
`L ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology sheaves vanish in the degrees `a, …, b` admits no nonzero
morphism `K ⟶ L`.

This is `Stacks.DerivedQCoh.exists_window_subsingleton_hom_of_isPerfect_general` at the derived
global sections `Stacks.DerivedQCoh.schemeDerivedSections X`, which exist for every scheme; the
statement mentions no derived global sections functor and carries no hypothesis beyond the
source's.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_window_subsingleton_hom_of_isPerfect_qcqs (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K) :
    ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧
      ∀ L : DerivedCategory X.Modules,
        (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj L).IsQuasicoherent) →
        (∀ i : ℤ, a ≤ i → i ≤ b → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj L)) →
        Subsingleton (K ⟶ L)

declarations.name: Stacks.DerivedQCoh.finite_setOf_not_subsingleton_hom_shift_of_isPerfect_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09M4], part (2).** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, let
`K` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `L` be a bounded object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`. Then
`Ext^n_{D(𝒪_X)}(K, L) = Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K, L⟦n⟧)` vanishes for all but finitely many `n`.

This is `Stacks.DerivedQCoh.finite_setOf_not_subsingleton_hom_shift_of_isPerfect_general` at the
derived global sections `Stacks.DerivedQCoh.schemeDerivedSections X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_setOf_not_subsingleton_hom_shift_of_isPerfect_qcqs (K : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hK : Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect (X := X.toRingedSpace) K)
    (L : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hLqc : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj L).IsQuasicoherent)
    (c d : ℤ) (hLGE : L.IsGE c) (hLLE : L.IsLE d) :
    {n : ℤ | ¬ Subsingleton (K ⟶ L⟦n⟧)}.Finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_differentialGradedAlgebra_quasiCoherentDerivedCategory_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09M5** (Bondal–van den Bergh). *Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated
scheme. Then there exist a differential graded algebra `(E, d)` with only a finite number of
nonzero cohomology groups `H^i(E)` such that `D_QCoh(O_X)` is equivalent to `D(E, d)`.*

`D_QCoh(O_X)` is the full subcategory of the derived category of `O_X`-modules — at an arbitrary
chosen model — of the objects all of whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent, and `D(E, d)` is
the derived category of differential graded `E`-modules. The algebra is an algebra over `ℤ`, the
endomorphism algebra `Hom_{Comp^dg(O_X)}(K^•, K^•)` of a K-injective perfect generator `K^•` of
`D_QCoh(O_X)`; the equivalence is the derived tensor product `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K^•` of Tag 09LX, see
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isKInjective_tensorWithComplexDerived_lift_isEquivalence`, followed by
the comparison of the standard model with the chosen one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_differentialGradedAlgebra_quasiCoherentDerivedCategory_equivalence
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [HasDerivedCategory X.Modules] :
    ∃ E : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{0, u} ℤ,
      {i : ℤ | Nontrivial (E.Cohomology i)}.Finite ∧
        Nonempty ((DerivedCategoryB.derivedCategoryB (A := X.Modules)
          (SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent X.ringCatSheaf)).FullSubcategory ≌
            DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory.{0, u, u} E)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09M8.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`. An
object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is compact if and only if it is perfect.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_iff_isPerfect (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1)
    (E : QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} E ↔ (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X.1 X.2).IsPerfect E.obj

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCategoryB_tensorWithComplexDerived_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09MA**, and with it the content of section **09M9** that this file delivers. *"Let
`S` be a scheme, `X` an algebraic space over `S`. Let `K` be a complex of `O_X`-modules whose
cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent. Let `(E, d) = Hom(K, K)` be the endomorphism differential
graded algebra. Then the functor `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K : D(E, d) ⟶ D(O_X)` of Tag 09LX has image contained
in `D_QCoh(O_X)`."*

The dévissage is the source's: a differential graded `E`-module with property (P) is the
homotopy colimit of the stages of its filtration, each stage carries a finite filtration whose
graded pieces are direct sums of shifts of `E`, and `E[k] ⊗_E K` is `K[k]`. Tag 0FQE packages
exactly that reduction, so what has to be checked is that lying in `D_QCoh(O)` holds at every
shift of the free rank-one module — which is the staged computation
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCategoryB_tensorWithComplexDerived_obj_regular` together
with the stability of `D_QCoh(O)` under the translation — is inherited by direct sums, and is
inherited by the third vertex of a distinguished triangle from the other two, the last because
`- ⊗_E^𝐋 K` is exact and `D_QCoh(O)` is a triangulated subcategory of `D(O)`.

Three assumptions are upstream inputs, not pieces of the conclusion: that quasi-coherence is a
weak Serre class and that `hqcsum`, a direct sum of quasi-coherent `O`-modules is quasi-coherent
(the two clauses of Tag 03M1, the first as a typeclass assumption so that instance search
supplies it where this repository has it); and `htensorSum`, that tensoring with `K` carries a
direct sum of differential graded `E`-modules to a direct sum in `D(O)` (the differential graded
half of which is Tag 09LV, formalized as
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDG_preservesCoproducts`). The hypothesis
`hK` is the source's own, that the cohomology sheaves of `K` be quasi-coherent, stated for the
complex `liftComplex X K` that the functor tensors with.

Exactness of `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K`, which the two-out-of-three step needs, is **not assumed**. As a
hypothesis `hexact`, Tag 09LW read against the pretriangulated structure that is not the one in
force here, it would be unsatisfiable and this statement vacuous. What discharges it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerived_signTwist_isTriangulated`, the
unconditional exactness of `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K` composed with the sign-twisted identity of `D(O)`: that
composite has the same action on objects and on morphisms, so its image of a distinguished
triangle has the same three vertices, which is all this step uses of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryB_tensorWithComplexDerived_obj
    [ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass (tensorModOQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, t, s} X)]
    (hqcsum : ∀ {ι : Type (max u v w t s)} (Mf : ι → TensorModO.{u, v, w, t, s} X)
      (c : Cofan Mf), IsColimit c →
      (∀ i, tensorModOQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, t, s} X (Mf i)) →
      tensorModOQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, t, s} X c.pt)
    (htensorSum : ∀ {ι : Type (max u v w t s)} [DecidableEq ι]
      (N : ι → DifferentialGradedModule.{0, max u v w t s, max u v w t s}
        (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).algebra),
      IsColimit ((toHomotopyCategory (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).algebra ⋙
        tensorWithComplexToDerivedCategory.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).mapCocone
          (Cofan.mk (General.directSumObj N) (General.directSumInj N))))
    (hK : tensorModOQuasicoherentDerived.{u, v, w, t, s} X
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (liftComplex.{u, v, w, t, s} X K)))
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory.{0, max u v w t s, max u v w t s}
      (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).algebra) :
    tensorModOQuasicoherentDerived.{u, v, w, t, s} X
      ((tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).obj M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.derivedCategoryB_tensorWithComplexDerived_obj_smallEtale
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09MA.**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `F` be an algebraic space over `S`, let `K` be a
complex of `𝒪_F`-modules whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent and let `(E, d) = Hom(K, K)`
be the endomorphism differential graded algebra.  Then the functor
`- ⊗_E^𝐋 K : D(E, d) ⟶ D(𝒪_F)` of Stacks 09LX has image contained in `D_QCoh(𝒪_F)`.

The hypothesis `hK` is the source's, that the cohomology sheaves of `K` be quasi-coherent, stated
for the complex `liftComplex F K` that the functor tensors with.  Nothing else is assumed: the
weak Serre class that the dévissage
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCategoryB_tensorWithComplexDerived_obj_of_hqcsum` uses comes
from `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.quasicoherentSheaves_isWeakSerreClass` together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderKernels`,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderCokernels` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderExtensions` at the module universe in which the tensor
products are formed, and its `hqcsum` is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isClosedUnderDirectSumsQuasicoherent`; the exactness of the functor and
its preservation of direct sums are instances of this development.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCategoryB_tensorWithComplexDerived_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09MA**, and with it the content of section **09M9** that this file delivers. *"Let
`S` be a scheme, `X` an algebraic space over `S`. Let `K` be a complex of `O_X`-modules whose
cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent. Let `(E, d) = Hom(K, K)` be the endomorphism differential
graded algebra. Then the functor `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K : D(E, d) ⟶ D(O_X)` of Tag 09LX has image contained
in `D_QCoh(O_X)`."*

The dévissage is the source's: a differential graded `E`-module with property (P) is the
homotopy colimit of the stages of its filtration, each stage carries a finite filtration whose
graded pieces are direct sums of shifts of `E`, and `E[k] ⊗_E K` is `K[k]`. Tag 0FQE packages
exactly that reduction, so what has to be checked is that lying in `D_QCoh(O)` holds at every
shift of the free rank-one module — which is the staged computation
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.derivedCategoryB_tensorWithComplexDerived_obj_regular` together
with the stability of `D_QCoh(O)` under the translation — is inherited by direct sums, and is
inherited by the third vertex of a distinguished triangle from the other two, the last because
`- ⊗_E^𝐋 K` is exact and `D_QCoh(O)` is a triangulated subcategory of `D(O)`.

Three assumptions are upstream inputs, not pieces of the conclusion: that quasi-coherence is a
weak Serre class and that `hqcsum`, a direct sum of quasi-coherent `O`-modules is quasi-coherent
(the two clauses of Tag 03M1, the first as a typeclass assumption so that instance search
supplies it where this repository has it); and `htensorSum`, that tensoring with `K` carries a
direct sum of differential graded `E`-modules to a direct sum in `D(O)` (the differential graded
half of which is Tag 09LV, formalized as
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDG_preservesCoproducts`). The hypothesis
`hK` is the source's own, that the cohomology sheaves of `K` be quasi-coherent, stated for the
complex `liftComplex X K` that the functor tensors with.

Exactness of `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K`, which the two-out-of-three step needs, is **not assumed**. As a
hypothesis `hexact`, Tag 09LW read against the pretriangulated structure that is not the one in
force here, it would be unsatisfiable and this statement vacuous. What discharges it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSite.tensorWithComplexDerived_signTwist_isTriangulated`, the
unconditional exactness of `- ⊗_E^𝐋 K` composed with the sign-twisted identity of `D(O)`: that
composite has the same action on objects and on morphisms, so its image of a distinguished
triangle has the same three vertices, which is all this step uses of it.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedCategoryB_tensorWithComplexDerived_obj
    [ObjectProperty.IsWeakSerreClass (tensorModOQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, t, s} X)]
    (hqcsum : ∀ {ι : Type (max u v w t s)} (Mf : ι → TensorModO.{u, v, w, t, s} X)
      (c : Cofan Mf), IsColimit c →
      (∀ i, tensorModOQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, t, s} X (Mf i)) →
      tensorModOQuasicoherent.{u, v, w, t, s} X c.pt)
    (htensorSum : ∀ {ι : Type (max u v w t s)} [DecidableEq ι]
      (N : ι → DifferentialGradedModule.{0, max u v w t s, max u v w t s}
        (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).algebra),
      IsColimit ((toHomotopyCategory (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).algebra ⋙
        tensorWithComplexToDerivedCategory.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).mapCocone
          (Cofan.mk (General.directSumObj N) (General.directSumInj N))))
    (hK : tensorModOQuasicoherentDerived.{u, v, w, t, s} X
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (liftComplex.{u, v, w, t, s} X K)))
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory.{0, max u v w t s, max u v w t s}
      (Rep.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).algebra) :
    tensorModOQuasicoherentDerived.{u, v, w, t, s} X
      ((tensorWithComplexDerived.{u, v, w, t, s, 0} X ℤ K).obj M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_window_subsingleton_hom_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09MB, part (1).**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S` and let `K` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)`.  Then there
are integers `a ≤ b` such that `Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K, L) = 0` for every `L ∈ D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` with
`Hⁱ(L) = 0` for `i ∈ [a, b]`.

The model of the derived category is arbitrary.  The window is the one produced at the standard
model by the induction `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasHomWindow_of_isPerfect_of_affine`, whose affine
case is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.hasHomWindow_of_isAffineSpace`, carried across the comparison of
the two models.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_window_subsingleton_hom_of_isPerfect
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    [hD : HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX))
    (hK : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X hX).IsPerfect K) :
    ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ ∀ L : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX),
      (∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) i).obj
        L).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) →
      (∀ i : ℤ, a ≤ i → i ≤ b →
        IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) i).obj L)) →
      Subsingleton (K ⟶ L)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.finite_setOf_not_subsingleton_hom_shift_of_isPerfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09MB, part (2).**  Let `S` be a scheme, let `X` be a quasi-compact and
quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`, let `K` be a perfect object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `L` be a
bounded object of `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)`.  Then `Extⁿ_{D(𝒪_X)}(K, L) = Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(K, L⟦n⟧)` is zero for
all but finitely many `n`.

Outside a bounded range of `n` the shift `L⟦n⟧` has no cohomology at all in the window of part
(1), because `L` is bounded.
declarations.statement:
theorem finite_setOf_not_subsingleton_hom_shift_of_isPerfect
    (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX)]
    (K : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX))
    (hK : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS X hX).IsPerfect K)
    (L : DerivedCategory (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX))
    (hLqc : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (Modules.{u, u} B S hS X hX) i).obj
      L).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (c d : ℤ) (hLGE : L.IsGE c) (hLLE : L.IsLE d) :
    {n : ℤ | ¬ Subsingleton (K ⟶ L⟦n⟧)}.Finite

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_differentialGradedAlgebra_equivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09MC.** *Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over `S`.
Then there exists a differential graded algebra `(E, d)` with only a finite number of nonzero
cohomology groups `H^i(E)` such that `D_QCoh(𝒪_X)` is equivalent to `D(E, d)`.*
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_differentialGradedAlgebra_equivalence (hqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X.1)
    (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X.1) :
    ∃ E : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{0, u} ℤ, {i : ℤ | Nontrivial (E.Cohomology i)}.Finite ∧
      Nonempty (QuasicoherentDerivedCategory.{u, u} B S hS X.1 X.2 ≌
        DifferentialGradedModule.derivedCategory.{0, u, u} E)

declarations.name: Ideal.invertible_of_mul_eq_span_singleton
declarations.doc:
**A factor of a principal ideal generated by a nonzerodivisor is invertible.** Let `A` be a
commutative ring and let `I` and `J` be ideals of `A` with `I * J = (f)` for a nonzerodivisor
`f ∈ A`. Then `I` is an invertible `A`-module, that is, finite locally free of rank `1`; in
particular `I` is a finitely generated ideal. Applying this to `J * I = (f)` gives the same
conclusions for `J`.
declarations.comment:
Stated as `Module.Invertible A ↥I` for one factor: the hypotheses are symmetric in
`I` and `J`, and finite generation and local freeness of rank `1` follow from invertibility. The
source's `I ≠ 0` and `J ≠ 0` are consequences of the hypothesis on `f` and are omitted. See
the module docstring.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.GradedObject.degreeZeroEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Degree-zero homogeneous maps of graded objects are precisely the componentwise maps: the
degree-zero category of the graded category of graded objects is canonically equivalent to the
ordinary category of graded objects.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def degreeZeroEquivalence :
    { E : @CategoryTheory.Equivalence
        (GradedCategory.DegreeZero ℤ (GradedObject ℤ B)) (GradedObject ℤ B)
        (degreeZeroCategory B) (GradedObject.categoryOfGradedObjects ℤ) //
      let F := @CategoryTheory.Equivalence.functor
        (GradedCategory.DegreeZero ℤ (GradedObject ℤ B)) (GradedObject ℤ B)
        (degreeZeroCategory B) (GradedObject.categoryOfGradedObjects ℤ) E
      (∀ X : GradedCategory.DegreeZero ℤ (GradedObject ℤ B),
        @CategoryTheory.Functor.obj _ (degreeZeroCategory B) _
          (GradedObject.categoryOfGradedObjects ℤ) F X = X) ∧
      (∀ (X Y : GradedCategory.DegreeZero ℤ (GradedObject ℤ B))
          (f : @Quiver.Hom _ (degreeZeroCategory B).toQuiver X Y) (i : ℤ),
        HEq ((@CategoryTheory.Functor.map _ (degreeZeroCategory B) _
          (GradedObject.categoryOfGradedObjects ℤ) F X Y f) i)
          (((DirectSum.component ℤ ℤ
            (fun n ↦ Cochain
              (zeroDifferentialComplex B X)
              (zeroDifferentialComplex B Y) n) 0)
            ((gradedCategoryData B).homEquiv X Y f.1)).v
              i i (add_zero i))) }

declarations.doc: The canonical identification of degree-zero morphisms with graded right-module maps.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def degreeZeroHomEquiv (𝒜 : ExternallyGradedAlgebra.{u, v} R)
    (M N : RightModuleCat.{u, v, w} 𝒜) :
    { e : GradedCategory.DegreeZero.Hom R (RightModuleCat 𝒜) M N ≃ HomogeneousMap M N 0 //
      ∀ f, (e f).1 = toLinearMap M N f.1 }

declarations.name: ExternallyGraded.RightModuleCat.degreeZeroHomEquiv_id
declarations.doc: Under the canonical identification, the identity is the identity homogeneous map.
declarations.statement:
theorem degreeZeroHomEquiv_id (𝒜 : ExternallyGradedAlgebra.{u, v} R)
    (M : RightModuleCat.{u, v, w} 𝒜) :
    ((degreeZeroHomEquiv 𝒜 M M).1
      (GradedCategory.DegreeZero.identity R (RightModuleCat 𝒜) M)) =
      HomogeneousMap.id M

declarations.name: ExternallyGraded.RightModuleCat.degreeZeroHomEquiv_comp
declarations.doc: Under the canonical identification, composition is composition of homogeneous maps.
declarations.statement:
theorem degreeZeroHomEquiv_comp (𝒜 : ExternallyGradedAlgebra.{u, v} R)
    {M N P : RightModuleCat.{u, v, w} 𝒜}
    (f : GradedCategory.DegreeZero.Hom R (RightModuleCat 𝒜) M N)
    (g : GradedCategory.DegreeZero.Hom R (RightModuleCat 𝒜) N P) :
    (degreeZeroHomEquiv 𝒜 M P).1
      (GradedCategory.DegreeZero.comp R (RightModuleCat 𝒜) f g) =
      HomogeneousMap.comp ((degreeZeroHomEquiv 𝒜 M N).1 f)
        ((degreeZeroHomEquiv 𝒜 N P).1 g)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.TwistedLocalizationMap.bijective_canonicalMap_of_le_nonvanishingOpen
declarations.doc:
**The comparison map is bijective on an open contained in the nonvanishing open of `s`.** Let
`X` be a scheme, `ℒ` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module, `s` a global section of `ℒ`, `ℱ` an arbitrary
`𝒪_X`-module, `p` a cohomological degree and `U ⊆ X_s` an open contained in the nonvanishing
locus of `s`. Then the canonical map

`H^p_*(U, ℒ, ℱ)₍s₎ ⟶ H^p(U ∩ X_s, ℱ)`,  `ξ / sⁿ ↦ s^{-n} ξ`

of `Stacks.Cohomology.TwistedLocalizationMap.canonicalMap` is **bijective**.

Neither quasi-compactness nor quasi-separatedness of `U`, nor quasi-coherence of `ℱ`, nor
positivity of `p` is assumed, and this is **not** a both-sides-vanish statement: taking
`U = X_s` it reads `H^p_*(X_s, ℒ, ℱ)₍s₎ ≅ H^p(X_s, ℱ)` on an arbitrary scheme, with neither side
forced to be zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_canonicalMap_of_le_nonvanishingOpen (hU : U ≤ nonvanishingOpen L s) :
    Function.Bijective (canonicalMap X L s F p U)
declarations.comment: for an open U inside the nonvanishing locus X_s: the canonical map H^p_*(U,L,F)_(s) to H^p(U ∩ X_s,F), xi/s^n to s^(-n) xi, is bijective, on an arbitrary scheme, for an arbitrary module and in every degree. The quasi-compact quasi-separated case of the tag is bijective_canonicalMap_of_isCompact, and neither case subsumes the other.

`H^p_*(S, ℒ, ℱ)₍s₎ ⟶ H^p(S ∩ X_s, ℱ)`,  `ξ / sⁿ ↦ s^{-n} ξ`

is bijective.
declarations.statement:
theorem bijective_canonicalMap_of_isCompact [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (S : X.Opens) (hS : IsCompact (S : Set X)) (p : ℕ) :
    Function.Bijective (canonicalMap X L s F p S)
