declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleSurjectiveThickening.isAmple_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**`L` ample `⟹` `i^* L` ample.** For a closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of Noetherian schemes
inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces, ampleness of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L` gives
ampleness of `i^* L` ([Stacks, Tag 0892]). The proof is
`Stacks.AmpleClosedImmersion.isAmple_modulePullback_of_surjective_isClosedImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_modulePullback [IsClosedImmersion i] [Surjective i] [IsNoetherian X]
    (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    IsAmple Z ((modulePullback i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleSurjectiveThickening.isAmple_modulePullback_iff_isAmple_of_isHomeomorph
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09MS].** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of Noetherian schemes inducing a
homeomorphism of underlying topological spaces, and let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. Then
`i^* L` is ample on `Z` if and only if `L` is ample on `X`. Noetherianness of `Z` follows from that
of `X`, since `i` is a closed immersion, and is not assumed.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_modulePullback_iff_isAmple_of_isHomeomorph [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsNoetherian X]
    (hi : IsHomeomorph i.base) :
    IsAmple Z ((modulePullback i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj L) ↔ IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AmpleLimit.exists_isAmple_pullback_map_of_isLimit_of_qcqs
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 09MT].**  Let `c` be a limit cone on a cofiltered diagram `D` of
quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transition morphisms and let `M` be an
invertible module on the stage `D.obj j`.  If the pullback of `M` to `c.pt` is ample, then the
pullback of `M` to some stage over `j` is ample.

This is `exists_isAmple_pullback_map_of_isLimit` with its hypothesis `hdesc` discharged by
`nonvanishingLocusDescent_of_isLimit`, which derives it from [Stacks Project, Tag 01ZR] (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_pullback_map_of_isLimit_of_qcqs (hc : IsLimit c) (j : I)
    (M : (D.obj j).Modules)
    [_root_.AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (D.obj j).toRingedSpace.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing (D.obj j).toRingedSpace).property M]
    (hample : Scheme.Modules.IsAmple c.pt ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (c.π.app j)).obj M)) :
    ∃ (j' : I) (g : j' ⟶ j),
      Scheme.Modules.IsAmple (D.obj j') ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (D.map g)).obj M)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isLimit_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09MV.** A quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme over a
quasi-separated base is a directed inverse limit of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes of
finite presentation over that base, with affine transition morphisms over the base.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_finitePresentation
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] :
    ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I)
      (_ : IsDirectedOrder I) (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u})
      (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj S)
      (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D) (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p)),
      p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f ∧
        (∀ i, FinitePresentation (t.app i)) ∧
        (∀ i, CompactSpace (D.obj i) ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)) ∧
        ∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom (D.map g)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleThickeningAscent.isAmple_modulePullback_iff
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09MW].** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of schemes inducing a
homeomorphism of underlying topological spaces, and `𝓛` an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. Then `i^* 𝓛`
is ample on `Z` if and only if `𝓛` is ample on `X`. No Noetherian hypothesis.

The implication `𝓛` ample `⟹` `i^* 𝓛` ample is
`Stacks.AmpleThickeningLimit.isAmple_modulePullback`; the converse is
`Stacks.AmpleThickeningAscent.isAmple_of_isAmple_pullback_of_isThickening`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_modulePullback_iff {Z X : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hi : IsHomeomorph i.base) (L : X.Modules) [IsInvertibleModule X L] :
    IsAmple Z ((modulePullback i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj L) ↔ IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleThickeningLimit.isAmple_modulePullback
declarations.doc:
**The implication `L` ample `⟹` `i^* L` ample of [Stacks, Tag 09MW].** For a closed immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` inducing a homeomorphism of underlying spaces and an invertible `𝒪_X`-module `L`,
ampleness of `L` gives ampleness of `i^* L`. No Noetherian hypothesis.

The homeomorphism hypothesis is **not used** — hence its binder is named `_hi`: the proof needs
only that `i` is an affine morphism. It is carried so that this is literally one half of the
source statement rather than a
more general lemma wearing the tag of [Stacks, Tag 09MW]. Neither is this half of the source any
harder than part (2) of [Stacks, Tag 0892] for a quasi-affine morphism, which
`Stacks.SectionRatioNoAmple.isAmple_modulePullback_of_isQuasiAffineHom` proves with no premise; a
closed immersion is affine, and an affine morphism is quasi-affine because the inverse image of an
affine open is affine.

This is `Stacks.AmpleSurjectiveThickening.isAmple_modulePullback` — the same half of
[Stacks, Tag 09MS] — with its `[Surjective i]` and `[IsNoetherian X]` hypotheses dropped, which is
exactly the difference between the two tags on this side of the biconditional.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_modulePullback [IsClosedImmersion i] (_hi : IsHomeomorph i.base)
    (hL : IsAmple X L) :
    IsAmple Z ((modulePullback i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj L)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleThickeningLimit.isAmple_modulePullback_iff_of_isHomeomorph
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09MW].** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a closed immersion of schemes inducing a
homeomorphism of underlying topological spaces, and let `L` be an invertible `𝒪_X`-module. Then
`i^* L` is ample on `Z` if and only if `L` is ample on `X`.

No hypothesis beyond the source's: neither Noetherianness nor separatedness nor
quasi-compactness of either scheme is assumed. The `mpr` half is
`Stacks.AmpleThickeningLimit.isAmple_modulePullback`; the `mp` half is
`Stacks.AmpleThickeningLimit.isAmple_of_isAmple_modulePullback_of_isHomeomorph`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAmple_modulePullback_iff_of_isHomeomorph [IsClosedImmersion i]
    (hi : IsHomeomorph i.base) :
    IsAmple Z ((modulePullback i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj L) ↔ IsAmple X L

declarations.name: Ring.GluingSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09MY.** The standing data for glueing two rings along a common
fraction field: a field `K` together with two subrings `A` and `B` of `K`, each of which has
`K` as its fraction field. These fit into a commutative square whose fourth corner is the
ring `R = A ×_K B = A ∩ B`.
declarations.statement: public structure GluingSituation

declarations.name: Ring.GluingSituation.R
declarations.doc:
The fourth corner `R = A ×_K B` of the commutative square, realized as the intersection
of `A` and `B` in `K`.
declarations.statement: public def R (S : GluingSituation) : Subring S.K
declarations.comment: the fourth corner of the square

declarations.name: Ring.GluingSituation.coe_R
declarations.doc: The fourth corner of the square is the intersection `A ∩ B` inside the common field.
declarations.statement: public lemma coe_R (S : GluingSituation) : (S.R : Set S.K) = (S.A : Set S.K) ∩ S.B

declarations.name: Ring.GluingSituation.subtype_comp_algebraMap_eq
declarations.doc: The square commutes: the two composites `R → A → K` and `R → B → K` agree.
declarations.statement:
public lemma subtype_comp_algebraMap_eq (S : GluingSituation) :
    S.A.subtype.comp (algebraMap S.R S.A) = S.B.subtype.comp (algebraMap S.R S.B)

declarations.name: Ring.GluingSituation.equivPullback
declarations.doc:
The fourth corner of the square is the fibre product `A ×_K B`: the intersection of `A`
and `B` in `K` is canonically isomorphic to the subring of `A × B` of pairs having the same
image in `K`.
declarations.statement:
public def equivPullback (S : GluingSituation) :
    S.R ≃+* RingHom.pullback S.A.subtype S.B.subtype

declarations.name: Subring.not_surjective_tensorProduct_iff_exists_isDiscreteValuationRing
declarations.doc:
For two subrings of a field that is the fraction field of the first, with
the first Noetherian and one-dimensional, the multiplication map from their
tensor product is not surjective if and only if they are contained in a common
discrete valuation subring.
declarations.statement:
public theorem not_surjective_tensorProduct_iff_exists_isDiscreteValuationRing
    {K : Type u} [Field K] (A B : Subring K)
    [IsFractionRing A K] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (h_dim : ringKrullDim A = 1) :
    (¬ Function.Surjective
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (B := B) A.subtype.toIntAlgHom
        B.subtype.toIntAlgHom (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _))) ↔
      ∃ O : Subring K, IsDiscreteValuationRing O ∧ A ≤ O ∧ B ≤ O

declarations.name: Ring.SemilocalDVRGluingSituation.exists_maximalIdeal_localization_le_of_units_mem_inf
declarations.doc:
If every unit of `A` belongs to `A ∩ B`, then the DVR `B` dominates the
localization of `A` at some maximal ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_maximalIdeal_localization_le_of_units_mem_inf
    (h_units : ∀ u : S.Aˣ, (((u : S.A) : S.K) ∈ S.R)) :
    ∃ p : MaximalSpectrum S.A,
      LocalSubring.ofPrime S.A p.asIdeal ≤
        ({ toSubring := S.B } : LocalSubring S.K)

declarations.name: Ring.SemilocalDVRGluingSituation.not_surjective_tensorProduct_of_units_mem_inf
declarations.doc:
If every unit of `A` belongs to `A ∩ B`, then the canonical
multiplication map `A ⊗[ℤ] B → K` is not surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_surjective_tensorProduct_of_units_mem_inf
    (h_units : ∀ u : S.Aˣ, (((u : S.A) : S.K) ∈ S.R)) :
    ¬ Function.Surjective
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (B := S.B) S.A.subtype.toIntAlgHom
        S.B.subtype.toIntAlgHom (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _))

declarations.name: Ring.SemilocalDVRGluingSituation.isOpenImmersion_specMap_R_A_of_unit_not_mem_R
declarations.doc:
If a unit of `A` lies outside `R`, the map from `Spec A` to `Spec R` is an open
immersion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenImmersion_specMap_R_A_of_unit_not_mem_R
    (h : ¬ ∀ a : S.Aˣ, (((a : S.A) : S.K) ∈ S.R)) :
    IsOpenImmersion
      (Scheme.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom ((S.A ⊓ S.B : Subring S.K).inclusion inf_le_left)).op)

declarations.name: Ring.SemilocalDVRGluingSituation.isOpenImmersion_specMap_R_B_of_unit_not_mem_R
declarations.doc:
If a unit of `A` lies outside `R`, the map from `Spec B` to `Spec R` is an open
immersion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenImmersion_specMap_R_B_of_unit_not_mem_R
    (h : ¬ ∀ a : S.Aˣ, (((a : S.A) : S.K) ∈ S.R)) :
    IsOpenImmersion
      (Scheme.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom ((S.A ⊓ S.B : Subring S.K).inclusion inf_le_right)).op)

declarations.name: Ring.SemilocalDVRGluingSituation.range_specMap_R_A_union_R_B_of_unit_not_mem_R
declarations.doc: If a unit of `A` lies outside `R`, the images of `Spec A` and `Spec B` cover `Spec R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem range_specMap_R_A_union_R_B_of_unit_not_mem_R
    (h : ¬ ∀ a : S.Aˣ, (((a : S.A) : S.K) ∈ S.R)) :
    Set.range
        (Scheme.Spec.map
          (CommRingCat.ofHom ((S.A ⊓ S.B : Subring S.K).inclusion inf_le_left)).op).base ∪
      Set.range
        (Scheme.Spec.map
          (CommRingCat.ofHom ((S.A ⊓ S.B : Subring S.K).inclusion inf_le_right)).op).base =
      Set.univ

declarations.name: Ring.SemilocalDVRGluingSituation.tensorProductTo_bijective_of_unit_not_mem_R
declarations.doc:
If a unit of `A` lies outside `R`, multiplication identifies `A ⊗[R] B` with the
common fraction field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem tensorProductTo_bijective_of_unit_not_mem_R
    (h : ¬ ∀ a : S.Aˣ, (((a : S.A) : S.K) ∈ S.R)) :
    Function.Bijective (tensorProductTo S)

declarations.name: IsIntegralClosure.finite_maximalSpectrum
declarations.doc:
The integral closure of a semilocal Noetherian domain of dimension at most one in its
fraction field is semilocal.
declarations.statement:
public lemma finite_maximalSpectrum (B : Type u) (K : Type v) (C : Type w)
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Ring.DimensionLEOne B] [Finite (MaximalSpectrum B)] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [IsFractionRing B K] [CommRing C] [Algebra B C] [Algebra C K] [IsScalarTower B C K]
    [IsIntegralClosure C B K] :
    Finite (MaximalSpectrum C)

declarations.name: IsIntegralClosure.exists_pow_mul_mem_range
declarations.doc:
A nonzero element of the Jacobson radical of the integral closure eventually carries every
element of the integral closure into the original domain.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_pow_mul_mem_range (B : Type u) (K : Type v) (C : Type w)
    [CommRing B] [IsDomain B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
    [Ring.DimensionLEOne B] [Finite (MaximalSpectrum B)] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
    [IsFractionRing B K] [CommRing C] [Algebra B C] [Algebra C K] [IsScalarTower B C K]
    [IsIntegralClosure C B K]
    (x : C) (hx : x ≠ 0) (hxj : x ∈ Ring.jacobson C) (y : C) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, x ^ n * y ∈ RingHom.range (algebraMap B C)

registrations.name: IsIntegralClosure.isDedekindDomain_and_comap_surjective_and_quasiFinite
registrations.comment: the Dedekind-domain assertion

declarations.name: Subring.isOpenImmersion_specMap_inf_left
declarations.doc: The left-hand subring gives an open immersion into the spectrum of the intersection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenImmersion_specMap_inf_left
    (hA : ringKrullDim A = 1) (hB : ringKrullDim B = 1)
    (h_surj : Function.Surjective
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (B := B) A.subtype.toIntAlgHom
        B.subtype.toIntAlgHom (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _))) :
    IsOpenImmersion
      (Scheme.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom ((A ⊓ B : Subring K).inclusion inf_le_left)).op)

declarations.name: Subring.isOpenImmersion_specMap_inf_right
declarations.doc: The right-hand subring gives an open immersion into the spectrum of the intersection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenImmersion_specMap_inf_right
    (hA : ringKrullDim A = 1) (hB : ringKrullDim B = 1)
    (h_surj : Function.Surjective
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (B := B) A.subtype.toIntAlgHom
        B.subtype.toIntAlgHom (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _))) :
    IsOpenImmersion
      (Scheme.Spec.map
        (CommRingCat.ofHom ((A ⊓ B : Subring K).inclusion inf_le_right)).op)

declarations.name: Subring.range_specMap_inf_left_union_right
declarations.doc: The images of the two spectra cover the spectrum of the intersection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem range_specMap_inf_left_union_right
    (hA : ringKrullDim A = 1) (hB : ringKrullDim B = 1)
    (h_surj : Function.Surjective
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (B := B) A.subtype.toIntAlgHom
        B.subtype.toIntAlgHom (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _))) :
    Set.range
        (Scheme.Spec.map
          (CommRingCat.ofHom ((A ⊓ B : Subring K).inclusion inf_le_left)).op).base ∪
      Set.range
        (Scheme.Spec.map
          (CommRingCat.ofHom ((A ⊓ B : Subring K).inclusion inf_le_right)).op).base =
      Set.univ

declarations.name: Subring.intersectionTensorProductTo_bijective
declarations.doc:
Multiplication identifies the tensor product over the intersection with the common fraction
field.
declarations.statement:
public theorem intersectionTensorProductTo_bijective
    (hA : ringKrullDim A = 1) (hB : ringKrullDim B = 1)
    (h_surj : Function.Surjective
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (B := B) A.subtype.toIntAlgHom
        B.subtype.toIntAlgHom (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _))) :
    Function.Bijective (intersectionTensorProductTo A B)

declarations.name: Subring.isNoetherianRing_gluedSubring
declarations.doc: The intersection is Noetherian.
declarations.statement: lemma isNoetherianRing_gluedSubring : IsNoetherianRing (gluedSubring B)

declarations.name: Subring.finite_maximalSpectrum_gluedSubring
declarations.doc: The intersection is semilocal.
declarations.statement: lemma finite_maximalSpectrum_gluedSubring : Finite (MaximalSpectrum (gluedSubring B))

declarations.name: Subring.ringKrullDim_gluedSubring
declarations.doc: The intersection has Krull dimension one.
declarations.statement: lemma ringKrullDim_gluedSubring : ringKrullDim (gluedSubring B) = 1

declarations.name: Subring.isOpenImmersion_specMap_gluedSubringInclusion
declarations.doc:
The map on affine spectra induced by inclusion of the intersection into each member is an
open immersion.
declarations.statement:
lemma isOpenImmersion_specMap_gluedSubringInclusion (i : ι) :
    AlgebraicGeometry.IsOpenImmersion
      (AlgebraicGeometry.Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (gluedSubringInclusion B i)))

declarations.name: Subring.iUnion_range_comap_gluedSubringInclusion
declarations.doc: The images of the spectra of the members cover the spectrum of the intersection.
declarations.statement:
lemma iUnion_range_comap_gluedSubringInclusion :
    (⋃ i, Set.range (PrimeSpectrum.comap (gluedSubringInclusion B i))) = Set.univ

declarations.name: Subring.existsUnique_range_comap_gluedSubringInclusion
declarations.doc:
Every closed point of the spectrum of the intersection is in the image of exactly one
member of the family.
declarations.statement:
lemma existsUnique_range_comap_gluedSubringInclusion
    (x : MaximalSpectrum (gluedSubring B)) :
    ∃! i, x.toPrimeSpectrum ∈ Set.range
      (PrimeSpectrum.comap (gluedSubringInclusion B i))

declarations.name: Ring.exists_ne_zero_inverse_mem_jacobson_of_tensorProduct_surjective
declarations.doc:
For finitely many Noetherian one-dimensional semilocal subrings of a common
fraction field, surjectivity of the corresponding multiplication maps produces
a nonzero element whose reciprocal belongs to all their Jacobson radicals.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_ne_zero_inverse_mem_jacobson_of_tensorProduct_surjective
    {K : Type u} [Field K] {ι : Type v} [Finite ι]
    (A : Subring K) (B : ι → Subring K)
    [IsFractionRing A K] [∀ i, IsFractionRing (B i) K]
    [∀ i, IsNoetherianRing (B i)] [∀ i, Finite (MaximalSpectrum (B i))]
    (h_dim : ∀ i, ringKrullDim (B i) = 1)
    (h_surj : ∀ i, Function.Surjective
      (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift (B := B i) A.subtype.toIntAlgHom
        (B i).subtype.toIntAlgHom (fun _ _ ↦ Commute.all _ _))) :
    ∃ x : A, x ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ i, ∃ y : B i,
      (y : K) = (x : K)⁻¹ ∧ y ∈ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal (B i))

declarations.name: Ideal.primeFamilyCompl
declarations.doc: The elements outside every prime ideal in a finite family.
declarations.statement: public abbrev primeFamilyCompl (s : Finset {p : Ideal A // p.IsPrime}) : Submonoid A

declarations.name: Ideal.finite_maximalSpectrum_localization_primeFamilyCompl
declarations.doc: Localization outside finitely many prime ideals is semilocal.
declarations.statement:
public theorem finite_maximalSpectrum_localization_primeFamilyCompl
    (s : Finset {p : Ideal A // p.IsPrime})
    {B : Type*} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalization (primeFamilyCompl s) B] :
    Finite (MaximalSpectrum B)

declarations.name: Ideal.bijOn_under_maximalSpectrum_localization_primeFamilyCompl
declarations.doc:
Contraction identifies the maximal ideals of the localization with the maximal members of
the finite family of prime ideals.
declarations.statement:
public theorem bijOn_under_maximalSpectrum_localization_primeFamilyCompl
    (s : Finset {p : Ideal A // p.IsPrime})
    {B : Type*} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [IsLocalization (primeFamilyCompl s) B] :
    Set.BijOn (fun m : MaximalSpectrum B => m.asIdeal.under A) Set.univ
      {p : Ideal A | (∃ q ∈ s, p = q.1) ∧
        ∀ q ∈ s, p ≤ q.1 → p = q.1}

declarations.name: Stacks.RetrocompactOneDimensional.isZero_rightDerived_pushforward_of_isRetrocompact
declarations.doc:
The positive higher direct images of a quasi-coherent module along the inclusion of a
retrocompact open subscheme of a scheme whose local rings are Noetherian of dimension at most one
vanish.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_rightDerived_pushforward_of_isRetrocompact
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : IsRetrocompact (U : Set X))
    (h_noetherian : ∀ x : X, IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (h_dimension : ∀ x : X, Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (F : U.toScheme.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasicoherent)
    (p : ℕ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (((Scheme.Modules.pushforward U.ι).rightDerived p).obj F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineOpen_of_isCompact_of_krullDimLE_one
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09N9].** Let `X` be an affine scheme all of whose local rings are Noetherian of
dimension at most one. Then every quasi-compact open `V ⊆ X` is affine.

The sections of `𝒪_X` over `V` whose basic open is affine span `Γ(X, V)` by
`span_eq_top_of_isCompact`, and they cover `V` by `iSup_basicOpen_isAffineOpen_eq`, so
[Stacks, Tag 01QF] applies. The dimension hypothesis enters only through
`AlgebraicGeometry.isAffineOpen_of_krullDimLE_one`, which makes every open of the spectrum of a
local ring of `X` affine.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineOpen_of_isCompact_of_krullDimLE_one {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X]
    (hN : ∀ x : X, IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hD : ∀ x : X, Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (V : X.Opens) (hV : IsCompact (V : Set X)) : IsAffineOpen V

declarations.name: Stacks.RetrocompactOneDimensional.isAffineOpen_of_isCompact
declarations.doc:
A quasi-compact open subset of an affine scheme is affine when every local ring is Noetherian
and has Krull dimension at most one.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffineOpen_of_isCompact (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X]
    (h_noetherian : ∀ x : X, IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (h_dim : ∀ x : X, Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsCompact (U : Set X)) : IsAffineOpen U

declarations.name: Stacks.PicSurjectiveOpen.exists_isInvertible_modulePullback_iso_of_isRetrocompact
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of Stacks Tag 09NA.** For a retrocompact open `U` of a scheme `X` whose
complement is discrete and along which the local rings of `X` are Noetherian of Krull dimension
at most one, every invertible `𝒪_U`-module is the pullback of an invertible `𝒪_X`-module; that
is, `Pic(X) → Pic(U)` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvertible_modulePullback_iso_of_isRetrocompact
    (hU : IsRetrocompact (U : Set X)) [DiscreteTopology (Uᶜ : Set X)]
    (h_noetherian : ∀ x : X, x ∈ (U : Set X)ᶜ → IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (h_dimension : ∀ x : X, x ∈ (U : Set X)ᶜ → Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (N : U.toScheme.Modules)
    [IsInvertible U.toScheme.presheaf
      (structureSheafRing U.toScheme.toRingedSpace).property N] :
    ∃ (L : X.Modules)
      (_ : IsInvertible X.presheaf (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L),
      Nonempty ((modulePullback U.ι.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj L ≅ N)
declarations.comment: surjectivity of the restriction Pic(X) -> Pic(U)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isInvertible_nonvanishingOpen_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09NA.** A retrocompact open with discrete complement along which the
local rings are Noetherian of Krull dimension at most one is the nonvanishing open of a global
section of an invertible module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvertible_nonvanishingOpen_eq
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)
    (hU : IsRetrocompact (U : Set X))
    [DiscreteTopology (Uᶜ : Set X)]
    (h_noetherian : ∀ x : X, x ∈ (U : Set X)ᶜ →
      IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (h_dimension : ∀ x : X, x ∈ (U : Set X)ᶜ →
      Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (X.presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ (L : X.Modules)
      (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property
          L)
      (s : L.sections),
      U = (letI := hL
           Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonvanishingOpen (X := X.toRingedSpace) L s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isInvertible_generatingSections_nonvanishingOpen_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09NB.** On an integral separated scheme, a nonempty affine open with
finite complement along which the local rings are Noetherian of dimension one is the
nonvanishing open of a global section of a globally generated invertible module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isInvertible_generatingSections_nonvanishingOpen_eq
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [X.IsSeparated]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hU_nonempty : U ≠ ⊥)
    (hfinite : ((U : Set X)ᶜ).Finite)
    (hnoetherian : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (hdim : ∀ x : X, x ∉ U → ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 1) :
    ∃ (L : X.Modules)
      (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property
          L)
      (s : L.sections),
      Nonempty L.GeneratingSections ∧
        U = (letI := hL
             Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonvanishingOpen (X := X.toRingedSpace) L s)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_isAmple_of_globallyGenerated_affine_nonvanishing
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09NC.** A quasi-compact scheme every point of which lies in an affine
nonvanishing locus of a global section of some globally generated invertible sheaf carries an
ample invertible sheaf.

The proof is the Stacks Project's. Quasi-compactness gives finitely many pairs `(L i, t i)` with
`X = ⋃ X_{t i}` and each `X_{t i}` affine; put `B = L 0 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ L n`. For a point `x`, pick an
index `j` with `x ∈ X_{t j}` and take `σ = s 0 ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ s n` where `s j = t j` and, for `i ≠ j`,
`s i` is a member of the generating family of `L i` not vanishing at `x`
(`Stacks.SheafOfModules.exists_generatingSection_nonvanishing`). Then `X_σ = ⋂ X_{s i}` contains
`x` and is contained in `X_{t j}`, so Tag 01PV applied `n + 1` times makes it affine. Ampleness
is read at exponent `1` through `Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.tensorPowerOneIso`.

**Two invertibility predicates.** The hypothesis is spelled with
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible`, which is the one `Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonvanishingOpen`
is defined for, and the conclusion with `AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible`, which is
the one `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple` is defined for. Both are `Prop`s, so the
choice of witness does not affect what either statement says, and
`Stacks.SheafOfModules.isInvertible_iff_algebraicGeometry` crosses between them.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isAmple_of_globallyGenerated_affine_nonvanishing (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (hcpt : CompactSpace Y)
    (hcover : ∀ y : Y, ∃ (M : Y.Modules)
      (hM : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf.obj
        (structureSheaf Y.toRingedSpace.sheaf).property M),
      Nonempty M.GeneratingSections ∧
        ∃ t : M.sections,
          y ∈ @Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonvanishingOpen
              Y.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace _ M hM t ∧
            IsAffineOpen (@Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonvanishingOpen
              Y.toLocallyRingedSpace.toRingedSpace _ M hM t)) :
    ∃ (M : Y.Modules)
      (hM : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.toRingedSpace.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing Y.toRingedSpace).property M),
      @AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple Y M hM

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_isAmple_of_topologicalKrullDim_one
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09ND.** A Noetherian integral separated scheme of topological Krull
dimension one has an ample invertible sheaf.

It is `Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.AmpleDimensionOne.exists_ample_invertible_of_09NC` applied to
`exists_isAmple_of_globallyGenerated_affine_nonvanishing`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isAmple_of_topologicalKrullDim_one (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsIntegral X] [X.IsSeparated]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) :
    ∃ (L : X.Modules)
      (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.toRingedSpace.presheaf
        (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace).property L),
      @AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L hL

declarations.name: StacksTag09NE.exists_invertible_of_closed_cover_discrete_intersections
declarations.doc:
Invertible sheaves on a finite closed cover of a reduced scheme extend when
pairwise intersections are discrete.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_invertible_of_closed_cover_discrete_intersections
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (Z : ι → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ X)
    [∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (f i)]
    (hcover : ∀ x : X, ∃ i z, f i z = x)
    (hdiscrete : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → DiscreteTopology
      (↥(Set.range (f i) ∩ Set.range (f j) : Set X)))
    (L : ∀ i, (Z i).Modules)
    [∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (Z i).presheaf (Z i).ringCatSheaf.2 (L i)] :
    ∃ (M : X.Modules)
      (_ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 M),
      ∀ i, Nonempty ((modulePullback (f i).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj M ≅ L i)

declarations.name: StacksTag09NE.exists_invertible_with_sections_of_closed_cover_discrete_intersections
declarations.doc:
Sections nonvanishing along the pairwise intersections can be glued along
with the invertible sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_invertible_with_sections_of_closed_cover_discrete_intersections
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (Z : ι → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ X)
    [∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (f i)]
    (hcover : ∀ x : X, ∃ i z, f i z = x)
    (hdiscrete : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → DiscreteTopology
      (↥(Set.range (f i) ∩ Set.range (f j) : Set X)))
    (L : ∀ i, (Z i).Modules)
    [∀ i, AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible (Z i).presheaf (Z i).ringCatSheaf.2 (L i)]
    (s : ∀ i, (L i).sections)
    (hs : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ z : Z i,
      (f i) z ∈ Set.range (f j) →
        z ∈ Stacks.SheafOfModules.nonvanishingLocus (X := (Z i).toRingedSpace) (L i) (s i)) :
    ∃ (M : X.Modules)
      (_ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 M)
      (t : M.sections),
      ∀ i, ∃ e : (modulePullback (f i).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj M ≅ L i,
        e.hom.val.app (op ⊤)
          (((modulePullbackPushforwardAdjunction (f i).toLRSHom.toShHom).unit.app M).val.app
            (op ⊤) (t.eval (op ⊤))) = (s i).eval (op ⊤)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_invertible_of_closed_cover_discrete_intersections
declarations.doc:
Invertible sheaves on a finite closed cover of a reduced scheme extend when
pairwise intersections are discrete.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_invertible_with_sections_of_closed_cover_discrete_intersections
declarations.doc:
Sections nonvanishing along the pairwise intersections can be glued along
with the invertible sheaves.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_invertible_with_sections_of_closed_cover_discrete_intersections
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsReduced X]
    (Z : ι → Scheme.{u}) (f : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ X)
    [∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (f i)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_of_openCover_source_of_separated_of_genericPoints_injOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09NG.** A separated morphism that is locally an open immersion on
the source and injective on generic points of irreducible components is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenImmersion_of_openCover_source_of_separated_of_genericPoints_injOn
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsSeparated f] (𝒰 : X.OpenCover)
    (h𝒰 : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (𝒰.f i ≫ f))
    (hinj : Set.InjOn f (genericPoints X)) :
    IsOpenImmersion f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isOpenImmersion_res_of_isIso_stalkMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09NH.** If the local-ring map of a locally finite-type morphism
is an isomorphism at `x`, and the target is reduced with finitely many irreducible
components, then the morphism is an open immersion near `x`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isOpenImmersion_res_of_isIso_stalkMap
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (x : X)
    [IsReduced S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hcomponents : (irreducibleComponents S).Finite)
    (hstalk : IsIso (f.stalkMap x)) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsOpenImmersion (U.ι ≫ f)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_containing_image_of_genericPoints_injOn
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09NI].** Let `f : T ⟶ X` be a morphism of schemes with `T` affine and `X`
quasi-separated with finitely many generic points. If `f` carries the generic points of the
irreducible components of `T` into those of `X` and does so injectively, and if the canonical
map of local rings at each member of a finite family of points of `T` is an isomorphism, then
the images of that family lie in a common affine open of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isAffineOpen_containing_image_of_genericPoints_injOn
    {T X : Scheme.{u}} (f : T ⟶ X) [IsAffine T] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (hX : (genericPoints X).Finite)
    (hgeneric : Set.MapsTo f (genericPoints T) (genericPoints X))
    (hinj : Set.InjOn f (genericPoints T))
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (t : ι → T)
    (hstalk : ∀ i, IsIso (f.stalkMap (t i))) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∀ i, f (t i) ∈ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_containing_of_stalk_krullDimLE_one
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09NJ]** A finite family of points on an integral separated scheme,
whose local rings are Noetherian of Krull dimension at most one, lies in a common affine open.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineOpen_containing_of_stalk_krullDimLE_one
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [X.IsSeparated]
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (x : ι → X)
    (h_noetherian : ∀ i, IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk (x i)))
    (h_dimension : ∀ i, Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (X.presheaf.stalk (x i))) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∀ i, x i ∈ U

declarations.name: Ideal.exists_lift_avoiding_primes
declarations.doc:
If an ideal is contained in none of a finite family of prime ideals, every
class modulo that ideal has a representative outside all of the primes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_lift_avoiding_primes
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) {r : ℕ} (p : Fin r → Ideal A)
    (hp : ∀ i, (p i).IsPrime) (hI : ∀ i, ¬ I ≤ p i) (fbar : A ⧸ I) :
    ∃ f : A, (∀ i, f ∉ p i) ∧ Ideal.Quotient.mk I f = fbar

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineClosedUnion.isAffine_of_isClosedImmersion_iUnion_of_surjective_appTop
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09NL], granted that global functions lift to the ambient scheme.** A scheme
which is set theoretically the union of finitely many affine closed subschemes is affine,
provided every global function on its reduced induced closed subscheme is the restriction of a
global function on it.

The hypothesis `hlift` is the only thing assumed, it concerns the single morphism
`X.nilradical.subschemeι`, and it is the cohomological content of [Stacks, Tag 06AD] for that
thickening: see the module docstring. Everything else — that the reduced induced closed
subscheme is affine — is
`Stacks.AffineClosedUnion.isAffine_nilradical_subscheme_of_isClosedImmersion_iUnion`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_isClosedImmersion_iUnion_of_surjective_appTop {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    {Z : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ X) [∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (f i)]
    [∀ i, IsAffine (Z i)] (hcov : ⋃ i, Set.range (f i).base = Set.univ)
    (hlift : Function.Surjective X.nilradical.subschemeι.appTop.hom) : IsAffine X

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineClosedUnion.isAffine_of_surjective_sigmaDesc_of_surjective_appTop
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09NL] in the tag's own vocabulary, granted that global functions lift to the
ambient scheme.** The covering hypothesis is surjectivity of the morphism from the coproduct, as
in the tag; it is the same hypothesis by
`Stacks.AffineClosedUnion.surjective_sigmaDesc_iff`.

The hypothesis `hlift` is as in
`Stacks.AffineClosedUnion.isAffine_of_isClosedImmersion_iUnion_of_surjective_appTop`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_surjective_sigmaDesc_of_surjective_appTop {ι : Type v} [Finite ι]
    {Z : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ X) [∀ i, IsAffine (Z i)]
    [∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (f i)] [hsurj : Surjective (Sigma.desc f)]
    (hlift : Function.Surjective X.nilradical.subschemeι.appTop.hom) : IsAffine X

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineClosedUnion.isAffine_of_isClosedImmersion_iUnion_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09NL].** A scheme which is set theoretically the union of finitely many
affine closed subschemes is affine. Nothing is assumed about the ambient scheme.

Its reduced induced closed subscheme is affine by
`Stacks.AffineClosedUnion.isAffine_nilradical_subscheme_of_isClosedImmersion_iUnion`, and `X` is
a thickening of that subscheme by
`Stacks.AffineClosedUnion.isThickening_subschemeι_nilradical`, so [Stacks, Tag 06AD] in the form
`Stacks.Thickenings.isAffine_of_isThickening` gives affineness of `X` itself.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_isClosedImmersion_iUnion_unconditional {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    {Z : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ X) [∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (f i)]
    [∀ i, IsAffine (Z i)] (hcov : ⋃ i, Set.range (f i).base = Set.univ) : IsAffine X

declarations.name: Stacks.AffineClosedUnion.isAffine_of_surjective_sigmaDesc_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09NL] in the tag's own vocabulary.** The covering is surjectivity of the
morphism from the coproduct of the affine closed subschemes, as the tag states it; it is the
same hypothesis as a union of ranges by
`Stacks.AffineClosedUnion.surjective_sigmaDesc_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isAffine_of_surjective_sigmaDesc_unconditional {ι : Type v} [Finite ι]
    {Z : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, Z i ⟶ X) [∀ i, IsAffine (Z i)]
    [∀ i, IsClosedImmersion (f i)] [hsurj : Surjective (Sigma.desc f)] : IsAffine X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_containing_of_components
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09NM].** Let `X` be a scheme with finitely many irreducible components and
`T ⊆ X` a finite set of points. If for every irreducible component `Z` the set `T ∩ Z` is
contained in an affine open of the reduced induced closed subscheme on `Z`, then `T` is
contained in an affine open subscheme of `X`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isAffineOpen_containing_of_components
    (X : Scheme.{u}) {T : Set X} (hT : T.Finite)
    (hcomponents : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite)
    (hlocal : ∀ Z : Closeds X, (Z : Set X) ∈ irreducibleComponents X →
      ∃ U : (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal Z).subscheme.Opens,
        IsAffineOpen U ∧
          T ∩ (Z : Set X) ⊆
            Set.range (U.ι ≫ (Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal Z).subschemeι)) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ T ⊆ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isAffineOpen_containing_of_stalk_krullDimLE_one_of_finite_components
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09NN]** Let `X` be a separated scheme such that every quasi-compact open of
`X` has finitely many irreducible components. A finite family of points of `X` whose local rings
are Noetherian of Krull dimension at most one is contained in an affine open subscheme of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAffineOpen_containing_of_stalk_krullDimLE_one_of_finite_components
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.IsSeparated]
    (hX : ∀ U : X.Opens, IsCompact (U : Set X) → (irreducibleComponents U).Finite)
    {ι : Type v} [Finite ι] (x : ι → X)
    (h_noetherian : ∀ i, IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk (x i)))
    (h_dimension : ∀ i, Ring.KrullDimLE 1 (X.presheaf.stalk (x i))) :
    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∀ i, x i ∈ U

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.universallyInjective_of_flat_of_separated_of_genericPoints_injOn
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09NP.** A flat separated morphism with isomorphic residue fields
at, and distinct images of, the generic points of its source is universally injective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem universallyInjective_of_flat_of_separated_of_genericPoints_injOn
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Flat f] [IsSeparated f]
    (hres : ∀ ξ ∈ genericPoints X, IsIso (f.residueFieldMap ξ))
    (hinj : Set.InjOn f (genericPoints X)) :
    UniversallyInjective f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isOpenImmersion_of_etale_of_separated_of_genericPoints_injOn
declarations.doc:
An étale separated morphism with isomorphic residue fields at, and distinct images of, the
generic points of its source is an open immersion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isOpenImmersion_of_etale_of_separated_of_genericPoints_injOn
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [Etale f] [IsSeparated f]
    (hres : ∀ ξ ∈ genericPoints X, IsIso (f.residueFieldMap ξ))
    (hinj : Set.InjOn f (genericPoints X)) :
    IsOpenImmersion f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.exists_isLimit_finitePresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09NS.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism of algebraic spaces over a scheme `S`, with `X`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated and `Y` quasi-separated. Then `X` is the limit of a directed
inverse system of algebraic spaces `Xᵢ` of finite presentation over `Y`, with affine transition
morphisms over `Y`: an inverse system `D` of algebraic spaces over `S` with morphisms
`tᵢ : Xᵢ ⟶ Y` of finite presentation compatible with the affine transition morphisms, and a
limit cone `X ⟶ Xᵢ` over `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isLimit_finitePresentation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    {X Y : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ Y) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (_ : Preorder I) (_ : Nonempty I) (_ : IsDirectedOrder I)
      (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ ((BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u))
      (t : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj Y) (p : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D)
      (_ : IsLimit (Cone.mk X p)),
      (p ≫ t = (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).map f) ∧
        (∀ i, IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS (D.obj i)) ∧
        (∀ i, IsFinitePresentation B S hS (t.app i)) ∧
        (∀ {i j : Iᵒᵖ} (g : i ⟶ j), IsAffineHom B S hS (D.map g))

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Generators.generatorTorsorOfInvertible
declarations.doc:
The sections of an invertible module `L` that trivialize it form a sheaf of sets on which
the sheaf of units acts simply transitively: the *generator torsor* of `L`.  The identification
of its sections with the trivializing sections of `L`, and the compatibility of that
identification with restriction and with the action of units, are part of the data.
declarations.statement:
def generatorTorsorOfInvertible (X : RingedSpace.{u, u})
    [∀ x : X, IsLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)]
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf X.sheaf))
    (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L) :
    GeneratorTorsor X L

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Generators.h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup
declarations.doc:
For a ringed space all of whose stalks are local rings, the first cohomology of the sheaf of
units is canonically isomorphic, as an abelian group, to the Picard group.
declarations.statement:
def h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup :
    Stacks.Cohomology.SheafTorsor.sheafCohomologyOne X (unitsSheaf X) ≃+
      Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.PicardGroup X.sheaf.obj
        (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.Generators.h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup_symm_classOf
declarations.doc:
The inverse of the canonical isomorphism `H^1(X, 𝒪_X^*) ≅ Pic(X)` sends the class of an
invertible module to the first-cohomology class of its torsor of generators.
declarations.statement:
theorem h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup_symm_classOf
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheaf X.sheaf))
    (hL : Stacks.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.sheaf.obj
      (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L) :
    (h1UnitsAddEquivPicardGroup X).symm (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Picard.classOf X.sheaf.obj
        (structureSheaf X.sheaf).property L hL) =
      Stacks.Cohomology.SheafTorsor.torsorClassEquivSheafCohomologyOne X (unitsSheaf X)
        (Quotient.mk _ (generatorTorsorOfInvertible X L hL).toTorsor)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleFiniteAffineNonvanishing.exists_affine_nonvanishingOpen_containing_finite_sections
declarations.doc:
Let `L` be an ample invertible `𝒪_X`-module on a scheme `X`. A finite subset `E` of an open
`W` of `X` lies in an affine ringed-space nonvanishing locus of a section of a positive tensor
power of `L`, with that locus contained in `W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_affine_nonvanishingOpen_containing_finite_sections (hL : IsAmple X L) {E : Set X}
    (hE : E.Finite) (W : X.Opens) (hEW : E ⊆ (W : Set X)) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n ∧
      ∃ s : (toSheafOfModules X (tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ))).sections,
        IsAffineOpen (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X.toRingedSpace
            (toSheafOfModules X (tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ))) s) ∧
          E ⊆ (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X.toRingedSpace
            (toSheafOfModules X (tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ))) s : Set X) ∧
            (Stacks.NonvanishingTrivialize.nonvanishingOpen X.toRingedSpace
              (toSheafOfModules X (tensorPowModule X L (n : ℤ))) s : Set X) ⊆ (W : Set X)

declarations.name: Stacks.SheafOfModules.Invertible.exists_sections_finite_subset_nonvanishingOpen_le_of_isAmple
declarations.doc:
Let `L` be an ample invertible module on a scheme `Y`, and let `E ⊆ W ⊆ Y` with `E` finite
and `W` open. Then there are an `n ≥ 1` and a global section `s` of `L^{⊗ n}` whose nonvanishing
locus is affine and satisfies `E ⊆ Y_s ⊆ W`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_sections_finite_subset_nonvanishingOpen_le_of_isAmple
    (hL : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple Y M)
    {E : Set Y} (hE : E.Finite) (W : Y.Opens) (hEW : E ⊆ W) :
    ∃ (m : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ m) (s : Mpow[m].sections),
      IsAffineOpen NV[m, s] ∧ E ⊆ (NV[m, s] : Set Y) ∧ (NV[m, s] : Set Y) ⊆ W

declarations.name: Ideal.inf_eq_bot_of_zeroLocus_union_eq_univ
declarations.doc:
In a reduced ring, ideals whose zero loci cover the spectrum have zero
intersection.
declarations.statement:
public theorem inf_eq_bot_of_zeroLocus_union_eq_univ
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsReduced A] (I J : Ideal A)
    (h : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) ∪
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) = Set.univ) :
    I ⊓ J = ⊥

declarations.name: Ideal.idealMap_quotient_bijective
declarations.doc:
If `V(I) ∪ V(J) = Spec A` in a reduced ring, the canonical map from `I`
to its extension in `A ⧸ J` is an isomorphism of `A`-modules.
declarations.statement:
public theorem idealMap_quotient_bijective
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsReduced A] (I J : Ideal A)
    (h : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) ∪
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) = Set.univ) :
    Function.Bijective (Algebra.idealMap (A ⧸ J) I)

declarations.name: Ideal.multipleQuotientMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
If `V(I) ∪ V(J) = Spec A`, the quotient map induces an isomorphism
`I • P ≅ I • (P ⧸ J • P)` for every flat `A`-module `P`. In particular this applies when
`P` is projective.
declarations.statement:
public theorem multipleQuotientMap_bijective
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [IsReduced A] (I J : Ideal A)
    {P : Type v} [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.Flat A P]
    (h : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) ∪
      PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A) = Set.univ) :
    Function.Bijective (multipleQuotientMap (P := P) I J)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleReducedDimensionOne.exists_isAmple_of_isReduced_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09NX].**  A Noetherian, reduced, separated scheme of topological Krull
dimension at most one carries an ample invertible sheaf.

The sheaf is the `M` glued from the components by Tag 09NE: its distinguished global section `t`
serves every point of the overlap `T`, at exponent one, and
`Stacks.AmpleReducedDimensionOne.exists_sections_of_notMem_componentOverlap` serves every point
off `T`.

The hypothesis is `≤ 1` rather than `= 1`, so this applies to schemes of dimension zero as well
and is stronger than the source's statement.

The name carries `isReduced` because
`StacksTag09NX.exists_isAmple_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one` already exists and is a *different*
theorem — Tag 09ND for an **integral** scheme, which is the first step of this proof rather than
its conclusion. Two declarations with that name-tail, one of them in a namespace called
`StacksTag09NX`, would be a twin-constant hazard, so the hypothesis
that distinguishes them is in the name.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_of_isReduced_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one (Y : Scheme.{u})
    [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian Y] [AlgebraicGeometry.IsReduced Y] [Y.IsSeparated]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (Y : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (M : Y.Modules)
      (_ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Y.presheaf Y.ringCatSheaf.2 M),
      AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple Y M

declarations.name: Stacks.LiftInvertible.exists_modulePullback_iso_of_isClosedImmersion_of_dimension_le_one
declarations.doc:
An invertible module on a closed subscheme of a scheme whose underlying space is Noetherian
and has dimension at most one is the pullback of an invertible module on the ambient scheme.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_modulePullback_iso_of_isClosedImmersion_of_dimension_le_one
    (X Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [NoetherianSpace X] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim X ≤ 1)
    (L : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing Z.toRingedSpace))
    [AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible Z.presheaf
      (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ _ (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) Z.IsSheaf) L] :
    ∃ (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (structureSheafRing X.toRingedSpace))
      (_ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf
        (Presheaf.isSheaf_comp_of_isSheaf _ _ (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat) X.IsSheaf) M),
      Nonempty ((modulePullback i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj M ≅ L)

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleNoetherianDimensionOne.exists_isAmple_of_isNoetherian_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09NZ].** A Noetherian separated scheme of topological Krull dimension at most
one carries an ample invertible module.

The reduction `Z` of `X` is Noetherian, reduced, separated and of dimension at most one, so it has
an ample invertible module by [Stacks, Tag 09NX]; that module is `i^* L` for an invertible module
`L` on `X` by [Stacks, Tag 09NY]; and `L` is ample because `i^* L` is, by the converse half of
[Stacks, Tag 09MS] applied to the surjective closed immersion `i : Z ⟶ X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_of_isNoetherian_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [AlgebraicGeometry.IsNoetherian X] [X.IsSeparated]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim (X : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (L : X.Modules)
      (_ : AlgebraicGeometry.SheafOfModules.IsInvertible X.presheaf X.ringCatSheaf.2 L),
      AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L
declarations.comment: with dimension at most one in place of the source's dimension one

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleNoetherianReduction.exists_isAmple_of_reduction
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09P0].** A scheme whose reduction is a Noetherian separated scheme of
dimension at most one has an ample invertible sheaf, granted the converse half of
[Stacks, Tag 09MW].

The hypotheses are on the reduction only; `X` itself is not assumed Noetherian, which is exactly
what distinguishes this from [Stacks, Tag 09NZ] and what forces Tag 09MW in place of
[Stacks, Tag 09MS].
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_of_reduction (X : Scheme.{u})
    (hdesc : AmpleDescendsAlongThickening.{u})
    [IsNoetherian (vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds X)).subscheme]
    [(vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds X)).subscheme.IsSeparated]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim ((vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds X)).subscheme : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (L : X.Modules) (hL : IsInvertibleModule X L), @IsAmple X L hL
declarations.comment: granted the converse half of Tag 09MW as `AmpleDescendsAlongThickening`

declarations.name: Stacks.AmpleNoetherianReduction.exists_isAmple_of_reduction_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09P0].** A scheme whose reduction is a Noetherian separated scheme of
dimension at most one has an ample invertible sheaf.

The hypotheses are on the reduction `X_red = (vanishingIdeal ⊤).subscheme` only; `X` itself is
not assumed Noetherian.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isAmple_of_reduction_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_one (X : Scheme.{u})
    [IsNoetherian (vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds X)).subscheme]
    [(vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds X)).subscheme.IsSeparated]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim ((vanishingIdeal (⊤ : Closeds X)).subscheme : Type u) ≤ 1) :
    ∃ (L : X.Modules) (hL : IsInvertibleModule X L), @IsAmple X L hL

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.connectingHom_gradedSplit
declarations.doc:
**The connecting homomorphism of the admissible sequence is the connecting morphism of the
graded splitting.** Both are `π d(s)`: the Hom differential of the differential graded category
is the graded commutator `d ∘ s - s ∘ d`, and its second term is killed by `π ∘ s = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectingHom_gradedSplit (z : Z.M) :
    (connectingHom (homOfCocycle A E.a) (homOfCocycle A E.b)
        (isAdmissibleShortExact_gradedSplit A E)
        (gradedSplitS A E) (gradedSplitPi A E)
        (gradedSplit_b_s A E) (gradedSplit_pi_a A E)
        (compatibleSplittings_gradedSplit A E).hker).val.toFun z =
      (DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.connectingHom E).1 z
declarations.comment: the connecting morphism of a graded splitting is the connecting homomorphism

declarations.name: CochainComplex.gradedSplitOfDegreewiseSplit
declarations.doc:
**A degreewise split short complex of cochain complexes is a graded-split short exact
sequence of the differential graded category of complexes.**
declarations.statement:
def gradedSplitOfDegreewiseSplit :
    DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact (A := dgCategory B) S.X₁ S.X₂ S.X₃
declarations.comment: a degreewise split short exact sequence of complexes

declarations.name: CochainComplex.connectingHom_gradedSplitOfDegreewiseSplit
declarations.doc:
**The connecting morphism of a degreewise split sequence of complexes is Mathlib's
`CochainComplex.cocycleOfDegreewiseSplit`.** The Hom differential of `s` is the graded
commutator `s ≫ d - d ≫ s`, and its second term dies against `π` because `π ∘ s = 0`, leaving
`(σ p).s ≫ d ≫ (σ q).r`.
declarations.statement:
theorem connectingHom_gradedSplitOfDegreewiseSplit :
    DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.connectingHom (gradedSplitOfDegreewiseSplit S σ) =
      (cocycleOfDegreewiseSplit S σ).1
declarations.comment: the connecting morphism of a degreewise split sequence of complexes

declarations.name: CochainComplex.dgShiftComparisonData
declarations.doc:
**Mathlib's shift supplies axiom (B)'s identification of Hom modules for the differential
graded category of complexes.** A degree `k + n` cochain `X ⟶ Y` is a degree `k` cochain
`X ⟶ Y[n]`; the identification multiplies the Hom differential by `(-1)^n` and leaves
composition on the right alone.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dgShiftComparisonData :
    DGCategory.ShiftComparisonData (dgCategory B)
declarations.comment: axiom (B)'s identification of Hom complexes, for complexes

declarations.name: DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.connectingHom
declarations.doc: The connecting morphism `π d(s)`, as a homogeneous morphism of degree one.
declarations.statement:
public def connectingHom {x y z : A.Obj} (E : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x y z) :
    A.Hom z x 1

declarations.name: DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.connectingHom_eq_neg_d_comp
declarations.doc: The alternative formula `δ = -d(π)s` for the connecting morphism.
declarations.statement:
public theorem connectingHom_eq_neg_d_comp {x y z : A.Obj}
    (E : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x y z) :
    connectingHom E =
      -A.comp (by omega : (0 + 1 : ℤ) + 0 = 1) (A.d E.π) E.s
declarations.comment: alternative formula for the connecting morphism

declarations.name: DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.connectingHom_closed
declarations.doc: The connecting morphism is a cocycle.
declarations.statement:
public theorem connectingHom_closed {x y z : A.Obj}
    (E : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x y z) : A.d (connectingHom E) = 0

The degree-one connecting cocycle remains closed after conversion to a map into

declarations.name: DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.connectingCocycle
declarations.doc: The actual connecting arrow `z ⟶ x[1]` in `Comp(A)`.

declarations.name: DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.associatedCompTriangle
declarations.doc:
The associated triangle in the category of complexes, with the arrow
`z ⟶ x[1]` given by `π d(s)`.
declarations.statement:
public def associatedCompTriangle {x y z : A.Obj}
    (S : ShiftAxiomB A) (E : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x y z) :
    letI : HasShift A.Comp ℤ := S.compShift
    Pretriangulated.Triangle A.Comp
declarations.comment: the associated triangle in the category of complexes

    (S : ShiftAxiomB A) (E : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x y z) :

declarations.name: DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.first_comp_zero_in_K
declarations.doc: The first two arrows compose to zero in the homotopy category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem first_comp_zero_in_K {x y z : A.Obj}
    (E : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x y z) :
    A.compK (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid y z) E.b)
      (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid x y) E.a) =
    Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid x z)
      (⟨0, A.d_zero⟩ : A.Cocycle x z)
declarations.comment: first composite vanishes in the homotopy category

declarations.name: DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.connecting_comp_zero_in_K
declarations.doc: The composite `y ⟶ z ⟶ x[1]` is zero in `K(A)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem connecting_comp_zero_in_K {x y z : A.Obj}
    (S : ShiftAxiomB A)
    (E : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x y z) :
    A.compK (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid z ((S.shiftFunctor 1).obj x))
        (connectingCocycle S E))
      (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid y z) E.b) =
    Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid y ((S.shiftFunctor 1).obj x))
      (⟨0, A.d_zero⟩ : A.Cocycle y ((S.shiftFunctor 1).obj x))
declarations.comment: second composite vanishes in the homotopy category

declarations.name: DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.comp_connecting_zero_in_K
declarations.doc: The composite `z ⟶ x[1] ⟶ y[1]` is zero in `K(A)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem comp_connecting_zero_in_K {x y z : A.Obj}
    (S : ShiftAxiomB A)
    (E : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x y z) :
    A.compK (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid ((S.shiftFunctor 1).obj x)
        ((S.shiftFunctor 1).obj y)) ((S.shiftFunctor 1).mapCocycle E.a))
      (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid z ((S.shiftFunctor 1).obj x))
        (connectingCocycle S E)) =
    Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid z ((S.shiftFunctor 1).obj y))
      (⟨0, A.d_zero⟩ : A.Cocycle z ((S.shiftFunctor 1).obj y))
declarations.comment: third composite vanishes in the homotopy category

declarations.name: DGCategory.GradedSplitShortExact.shifted_connecting_comp_zero_in_K
declarations.doc: The rotated composite `z[-1] ⟶ x ⟶ y` is zero in `K(A)`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem shifted_connecting_comp_zero_in_K {x y z : A.Obj}
    (S : ShiftAxiomB A)
    (E : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x y z) :
    A.compK (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid x y) E.a)
      (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid ((S.shiftFunctor (-1)).obj z) x)
        (shiftedConnecting S E)) =
    Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid ((S.shiftFunctor (-1)).obj z) y)
      (⟨0, A.d_zero⟩ : A.Cocycle ((S.shiftFunctor (-1)).obj z) y)
declarations.comment: rotated composite vanishes in the homotopy category

declarations.name: DGCategory.exists_coneTriangleMorphism
declarations.doc:
A homotopy-commutative square of complexes induces a morphism of their cone triangles, whose
cone component has a representative in the category of complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_coneTriangleMorphism (S : ConeSituation A)
    {x₁ y₁ x₂ y₂ : A.Obj}
    (f₁ : A.Cocycle x₁ y₁) (f₂ : A.Cocycle x₂ y₂)
    (a : A.Cocycle x₁ x₂) (b : A.Cocycle y₁ y₂)
    (hcomm : A.compK (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid y₁ y₂) b)
        (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid x₁ y₁) f₁) =
      A.compK (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid x₂ y₂) f₂)
        (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid x₁ x₂) a)) :
    ∃ c : A.Cocycle (S.cone f₁) (S.cone f₂),
      (A.compK
          (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid (S.cone f₁) (S.cone f₂)) c)
          (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid y₁ (S.cone f₁)) (S.coneSequence f₁).a) =
        A.compK
          (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid y₂ (S.cone f₂)) (S.coneSequence f₂).a)
          (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid y₁ y₂) b)) ∧
      (A.compK
          (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid (S.cone f₂)
            ((S.shift.shiftFunctor 1).obj x₂)) (S.coneSequence f₂).b)
          (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid (S.cone f₁) (S.cone f₂)) c) =
        A.compK
          (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid ((S.shift.shiftFunctor 1).obj x₁)
            ((S.shift.shiftFunctor 1).obj x₂))
            ((S.shift.shiftFunctor 1).mapCocycle a))
          (Quotient.mk (A.homotopySetoid (S.cone f₁)
            ((S.shift.shiftFunctor 1).obj x₁)) (S.coneSequence f₁).b))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.exists_isTop_and_isIso_colimit_ι
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09P8**, first half. A finite directed set `I` has a greatest element `i∞`, and
therefore every colimit over `I` is trivial: the structure map from the value at `i∞` to the
colimit is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isTop_and_isIso_colimit_ι {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [Finite I] [Nonempty I]
    [IsDirectedOrder I] {C : Type*} [Category C] (F : I ⥤ C) [HasColimit F] :
    ∃ i : I, IsTop i ∧ IsIso (colimit.ι F i)
declarations.comment: first half: a colimit over a finite directed set is trivial

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.SingleObj.isColimitRangeCocone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09P8**, second half. Let `e` be a left-absorbing element of a monoid `M`, so in
particular an idempotent. The colimit of a diagram of sets indexed by the single-object category
`SingleObj M` is the image of the idempotent `x ↦ e • x`, that is, of the map by which `e` acts.
For the source's index category — one object with one non-trivial morphism `e` satisfying
`e = e ∘ e` — take `M = WithZero Unit` and `e = 0`.
declarations.statement: def isColimitRangeCocone (he : ∀ x : M, e * x = e) : IsColimit (rangeCocone F e he)
declarations.comment: second half: the colimit over the one-object category on an idempotent

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.SingleObj.not_injective_ι_constDiagram
declarations.doc:
The colimit of `constDiagram X a` is the image of a constant map, a singleton, so its
structure map is not injective as soon as `X` has an element other than `a`. Together with
`instIsFilteredSingleObjOfMonoidWithZero` and the `FinCategory` instance on
`SingleObj (WithZero Unit)`, this is the second assertion of Stacks 09P8: a colimit indexed by a
*finite filtered* category need not be trivial.
declarations.statement:
theorem not_injective_ι_constDiagram {X : Type v} (a : X) (hX : ∃ x : X, x ≠ a) :
    ¬ Function.Injective
      ((rangeCocone (constDiagram X a) 0 fun x => zero_mul x).ι.app
        (star (WithZero Unit)))
declarations.comment: second half: the colimit need not be trivial

declarations.name: Algebra.IsGeometricallyIntegral.isDomain_tensorProduct
declarations.doc:
Let `k` be a field, let `S` be a geometrically integral `k`-algebra and let `R` be a
`k`-algebra which is an integral domain. Then `R ⊗[k] S` is an integral domain.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Algebra.IsGeometricallyIntegral.isDomain_tensorProduct (k R S : Type u) [Field k]
    [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [Algebra k R] [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    [Algebra.IsGeometricallyIntegral k S] : IsDomain (R ⊗[k] S)

declarations.name: CochainComplex.KFlat.property_of_coproducts_of_two_out_of_three_of_shifts
declarations.doc:
Every complex has a split filtered resolution whose graded pieces are
coproducts of shifts of the ring and whose filtration yields the canonical telescope triangle.
Moreover, a property of objects of `D(R)` that is preserved by coproducts, satisfies
two-out-of-three for distinguished triangles, and holds for every shift of `R`, holds for every
object of `D(R)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem property_of_coproducts_of_two_out_of_three_of_shifts {R : Type u} [Ring R]
    [Small.{v} R] :
    (∀ M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ, Nonempty (SplitFilteredFreeResolution M)) ∧
      ∀ (T : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R) → Prop),
        (∀ {I : Type v} (K : I → DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R)) [HasCoproduct K],
          (∀ i, T (K i)) → T (∐ K)) →
        (∀ (Δ : Triangle (DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} R))),
          Δ ∈ distinguishedTriangles →
            (T Δ.obj₁ → T Δ.obj₂ → T Δ.obj₃) ∧
            (T Δ.obj₁ → T Δ.obj₃ → T Δ.obj₂) ∧
            (T Δ.obj₂ → T Δ.obj₃ → T Δ.obj₁)) →
        (∀ k : ℤ, T (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (ModuleCat.{v} R) 0).obj
          (ModuleCat.of R (Shrink.{v} R)))⟦k⟧)) →
        ∀ K, T K

declarations.name: StacksDraft.Perfect.isPerfect_and_torAmplitude_of_flat_local_of_regular_closedFibre
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09PC.** Let `A → B` be a flat local homomorphism of local rings, let `a, b : ℤ` and
let `d ≥ 0` be an integer such that the closed fibre `B/m_A B` is regular of dimension `d`. Let `K`
be an object of the derived category of `B`-modules which is pseudo-coherent as a complex of
`B`-modules and whose derived fibre `K ⊗_A^L κ(m_A)` has cohomology only in the degrees `[a, b]`.
Then `K` is perfect as a complex of `B`-modules with Tor amplitude in `[a - d, b]`.

The source states the hypothesis over `A` as Tor amplitude in `[a, b]` and remarks that the weaker
condition on the derived fibre suffices; it is that weaker hypothesis which is used here. Tor
amplitude in the conclusion is recorded as in [stacks 068V]: by a flat representative supported in
the window, which by [stacks 0654] is exactly Tor amplitude, together with the termwise condition
on every bounded above flat representative. The derived fibre over `A` is computed on a bounded
above flat representative of the complex of `A`-modules underlying `K`, which is what the termwise
tensor product with `κ(m_A)` of such a representative is.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_and_torAmplitude_of_flat_local_of_regular_closedFibre [IsLocalRing B]
    [IsLocalHom (algebraMap A B)] [Module.Flat A B] (a b : ℤ) (d : ℕ)
    [IsRegularLocalRing (B ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A))]
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (B ⧸ Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) (maximalIdeal A)) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B))
    (hK : StacksDraft.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent K)
    (hfibre : ∀ F : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ, TorAmplitude.BoundedAbove F →
      TorAmplitude.IsComplexOfFlats F →
      Nonempty ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A B)).mapDerivedCategory.obj K ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) →
      ∀ i : ℤ, (i < a ∨ b < i) →
        IsZero ((TorAmplitude.tensorComplex F
          (ModuleCat.of A (maximalIdeal A).ResidueField)).homology i)) :
    IsPerfect K ∧ HasFlatRepresentative.{u, u} K (a - (d : ℤ)) b ∧
      ∀ E : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} B) ℤ, TorAmplitude.BoundedAbove E →
        TorAmplitude.IsComplexOfFlats E → Nonempty (K ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj E) →
          TorAmplitude.HasTorAmplitudeIn E (a - (d : ℤ)) b

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.DividedPowerStructure
declarations.doc:
A divided power structure on the positive even part of a strictly graded-commutative graded
algebra.
declarations.statement:
public structure DividedPowerStructure (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜]
    [IsStrictlyGradedComm 𝒜]

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.ExteriorOddVariable.equiv
declarations.doc: The odd-variable extension of `⋀[R] M` is `⋀[R] (M × R)`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def equiv :
    OddVariableExtension (exteriorGrade R M) 1 ≃ₐ[R] ExteriorAlgebra R (M × R)
declarations.comment: exterior algebra as an iterated odd variable extension

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.isCompatibleWithDifferential_exteriorDividedPowerStructure
declarations.doc:
The divided powers of `⋀[R] (Fin r → R)` are compatible with contraction by every `R`-linear
functional, hence with the Koszul differential of every finite sequence in `R`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isCompatibleWithDifferential_exteriorDividedPowerStructure (r : ℕ) :
    ∀ φ : Module.Dual R (Fin r → R),
      IsCompatibleWithDifferential (exteriorDividedPowerStructure R r)
        (CliffordAlgebra.contractLeft φ)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.existsUnique_oddVariableDividedPowerStructure
declarations.doc:
There is a unique divided power structure on an odd-variable extension which extends the
given divided powers on the coefficient algebra.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_oddVariableDividedPowerStructure
    (Aᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra Aᵢ] [IsStrictlyGradedComm Aᵢ]
    (gamma : DividedPowerStructure Aᵢ) (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (hd_odd : Odd d) :
    ∃! delta : DividedPowerStructure (OddVariableExtension.grade Aᵢ d),
      IsOddVariableDividedPowerExtension Aᵢ d gamma delta

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.oddVariableDividedPowerStructure_dpow
declarations.doc:
For `x` in the positive even part and `y` in the odd part, the `n`th divided power of
`x + yT` is `gamma_n(x) + gamma_(n - 1)(x)yT`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem oddVariableDividedPowerStructure_dpow
    (Aᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra Aᵢ] [IsStrictlyGradedComm Aᵢ]
    (gamma : DividedPowerStructure Aᵢ) (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (hd_odd : Odd d)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≠ 0) (x y : A) (hx : x ∈ positiveEvenPart Aᵢ)
    (hy : y ∈ oddPart Aᵢ) :
    (oddVariableDividedPowerStructure Aᵢ gamma d hd hd_odd).dpow n
        (inclusion Aᵢ d x + inclusion Aᵢ d y * generator Aᵢ d) =
      inclusion Aᵢ d (gamma.dpow n x) +
        inclusion Aᵢ d (gamma.dpow (n - 1) x * y) * generator Aᵢ d

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.OddVariableExtension
declarations.doc:
The odd-variable extension `A⟨T⟩`.  Its elements are pairs `(a, b)`, written
mathematically as `a + bT`.
declarations.statement: public abbrev OddVariableExtension (Aᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra Aᵢ] (d : ℕ)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.OddVariableExtension.grade
declarations.doc: The degree-`m` piece `A_m ⊕ A_{m-d}T` of the odd-variable extension.
declarations.statement:
public def grade (Aᵢ : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra Aᵢ] (d m : ℕ) :
    Submodule R (OddVariableExtension Aᵢ d)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.existsUnique_oddVariableExtension_ringHom
declarations.doc:
The mapping property of the odd variable extension of Tag 09PH, for ring homomorphisms. A
ring homomorphism out of `B⟨T⟩` which preserves degrees is determined by, and may be prescribed
by, its restriction to `B` together with the image of `T`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_oddVariableExtension_ringHom
    (h : B →+* D) (hgrade : ∀ (m : ℕ) (b : B), b ∈ ℬ m → h b ∈ 𝒟 m)
    (d : ℕ) (hodd : Odd d) (t : D) (ht : t ∈ 𝒟 d) :
    ∃! g : OddVariableExtension ℬ d →+* D,
      (∀ b : B, g (inclusion ℬ d b) = h b) ∧
      g (generator ℬ d) = t ∧
      (∀ (m : ℕ) (x : OddVariableExtension ℬ d), x ∈ grade ℬ d m → g x ∈ 𝒟 m)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.oddVariableExtension_ringHom_dpow
declarations.doc:
A degree-preserving ring homomorphism out of an odd variable extension which restricts to a
divided-power compatible map on the coefficients is itself compatible with divided powers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem oddVariableExtension_ringHom_dpow
    (h : B →+* D) (hgrade : ∀ (m : ℕ) (b : B), b ∈ ℬ m → h b ∈ 𝒟 m)
    (hdpow : ∀ (n : ℕ) (b : B), b ∈ positiveEvenPart ℬ → δ.dpow n (h b) = h (β.dpow n b))
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (hodd : Odd d) (t : D) (ht : t ∈ 𝒟 d)
    (g : OddVariableExtension ℬ d →+* D)
    (hg1 : ∀ b : B, g (inclusion ℬ d b) = h b) (hg2 : g (generator ℬ d) = t)
    (n : ℕ) (x : OddVariableExtension ℬ d) (hx : x ∈ positiveEvenPart (grade ℬ d)) :
    δ.dpow n (g x) = g ((oddVariableDividedPowerStructure ℬ β d hd hodd).dpow n x)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.EvenVariableAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The algebra of finite divided-power polynomials in one even variable over `A`.

The coefficient at `n` is the coefficient of the formal symbol `T⁽ⁿ⁾`.
declarations.statement: public structure EvenVariableAlgebra (A : Type v) [Ring A]

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.EvenVariableAlgebra.mul
declarations.doc: The binomially weighted convolution product.
declarations.statement: public def mul (x y : EvenVariableAlgebra A) : EvenVariableAlgebra A

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.EvenVariableAlgebra.grade
declarations.doc:
The degree-`m` piece after adjoining an even variable of degree `d`.

Its coefficient of `T⁽ⁿ⁾` lies in `𝒜 (m - n * d)` when `n * d ≤ m`, and is zero
otherwise.
declarations.statement:
public def grade (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A) (d m : ℕ) :
    Submodule R (EvenVariableAlgebra A)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.EvenVariableAlgebra.gradedAlgebra
declarations.doc: The shifted homogeneous pieces give an internal grading of the coefficient algebra.
declarations.statement:
public instance gradedAlgebra (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A) [GradedAlgebra 𝒜]
    (d : ℕ) : GradedAlgebra (grade 𝒜 d)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.EvenVariableAlgebra.strictlyGradedComm
declarations.doc: An even variable preserves strict graded commutativity, including vanishing odd squares.
declarations.statement:
public instance strictlyGradedComm (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A) [IsStrictlyGradedComm 𝒜]
    (d : ℕ) [Fact (Even d)] : IsStrictlyGradedComm (grade 𝒜 d)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.evenVariableDividedPowerStructure
declarations.doc:
The divided-power structure on the algebra obtained by adjoining an even
variable of positive degree.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def evenVariableDividedPowerStructure
    (d : ℕ) [Fact (Even d)] (hd : 0 < d)
    (γ : DividedPowerStructure 𝒜) :
    DividedPowerStructure (EvenVariableAlgebra.grade 𝒜 d)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.dpow_coeffEmbedding
declarations.doc: The new divided powers restrict to the original structure on `A`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dpow_coeffEmbedding
    (d : ℕ) [Fact (Even d)] (hd : 0 < d)
    (γ : DividedPowerStructure 𝒜) (n : ℕ) {x : A}
    (hx : x ∈ positiveEvenPart 𝒜) :
    (evenVariableDividedPowerStructure d hd γ).dpow n (coeffEmbedding x) =
      coeffEmbedding (γ.dpow n x)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.dpow_monomial_one
declarations.doc: The divided powers of the formal monomial `T⁽ⁱ⁾`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dpow_monomial_one
    (d : ℕ) [Fact (Even d)] (hd : 0 < d)
    (γ : DividedPowerStructure 𝒜) (n i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    (evenVariableDividedPowerStructure d hd γ).dpow n (monomial i (1 : A)) =
      monomial (n * i) (dividedPowerMonomialCoefficient n i • (1 : A))

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.dpow_positivePolynomial
declarations.doc:
The multinomial expansion for a finite sum of positive-exponent terms
whose coefficients are even.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dpow_positivePolynomial
    (d : ℕ) [Fact (Even d)] (hd : 0 < d)
    (γ : DividedPowerStructure 𝒜) (n : ℕ)
    (x : EvenVariableAlgebra A)
    (hzero : x.coeff 0 = 0)
    (heven : ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → x.coeff i ∈
      evenPart 𝒜) :
    (evenVariableDividedPowerStructure d hd γ).dpow n x =
      positivePolynomialDividedPower n x

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.dpow_coeff_add_positive
declarations.doc:
Adding a positive-even constant coefficient obeys the divided-power
binomial formula.
declarations.statement:
public theorem dpow_coeff_add_positive
    (d : ℕ) [Fact (Even d)] (hd : 0 < d)
    (γ : DividedPowerStructure 𝒜) (n : ℕ)
    {x₀ : A} (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ positiveEvenPart 𝒜)
    (x : EvenVariableAlgebra A)
    (hzero : x.coeff 0 = 0)
    (heven : ∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → x.coeff i ∈
      evenPart 𝒜) :
    (evenVariableDividedPowerStructure d hd γ).dpow n (coeffEmbedding x₀ + x) =
    ∑ ij ∈ Finset.antidiagonal n,
        coeffEmbedding (γ.dpow ij.1 x₀) *
      (evenVariableDividedPowerStructure d hd γ).dpow ij.2 x

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.evenVariableDividedPowerStructure_unique
declarations.doc:
Compatibility and the formal-monomial rule determine the divided-power
structure uniquely.
declarations.statement:
public theorem evenVariableDividedPowerStructure_unique
    (d : ℕ) [Fact (Even d)] (hd : 0 < d)
    (γ : DividedPowerStructure 𝒜)
    (δ : DividedPowerStructure (EvenVariableAlgebra.grade 𝒜 d))
    (hcompat : ∀ (n : ℕ) {x : A},
      x ∈ positiveEvenPart 𝒜 →
        δ.dpow n (coeffEmbedding x) = coeffEmbedding (γ.dpow n x))
    (hmonomial : ∀ (n i : ℕ), 0 < i →
      δ.dpow n (monomial i (1 : A)) =
        monomial (n * i) (dividedPowerMonomialCoefficient n i • (1 : A))) :
    δ = evenVariableDividedPowerStructure d hd γ

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.evenVariableAlgebra_ringHom_dpow
declarations.doc:
A degree-preserving ring homomorphism out of an even variable algebra which restricts to a
divided-power compatible map on the coefficients is itself compatible with divided powers.
declarations.statement:
public theorem evenVariableAlgebra_ringHom_dpow
    (h : B →+* D)
    (hdpow : ∀ (n : ℕ) (b : B), b ∈ positiveEvenPart ℬ → δ.dpow n (h b) = h (β.dpow n b))
    (d : ℕ) [Fact (Even d)] (hd : 0 < d) (t : D) (ht : t ∈ 𝒟 d)
    (g : EvenVariableAlgebra B →+* D)
    (hg1 : ∀ b : B, g (coeffEmbedding b) = h b)
    (hg2 : ∀ n : ℕ, g (monomial n (1 : B)) = δ.dpow n t)
    (hg3 : ∀ (m : ℕ) (x : EvenVariableAlgebra B),
      x ∈ EvenVariableAlgebra.grade ℬ d m → g x ∈ 𝒟 m)
    (n : ℕ) (x : EvenVariableAlgebra B)
    (hx : x ∈ positiveEvenPart (EvenVariableAlgebra.grade ℬ d)) :
    δ.dpow n (g x) = g ((evenVariableDividedPowerStructure d hd β).dpow n x)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.existsUnique_evenVariableAlgebra_ringHom
declarations.doc:
The mapping property of the even variable algebra of Tag 09PI, for ring homomorphisms. A
ring homomorphism out of `B⟨T⟩` is determined by, and may be prescribed by, its restriction to
`B` together with a choice of images for the divided powers of `T`, which must be the divided
powers of a single element of degree `d`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem existsUnique_evenVariableAlgebra_ringHom
    (h : B →+* D) (hgrade : ∀ (m : ℕ) (b : B), b ∈ ℬ m → h b ∈ 𝒟 m)
    (d : ℕ) (hd : 0 < d) (heven : Even d) (t : D) (ht : t ∈ 𝒟 d) :
    ∃! g : EvenVariableAlgebra B →+* D,
      (∀ b : B, g (coeffEmbedding b) = h b) ∧
      (∀ n : ℕ, g (monomial n (1 : B)) = δ.dpow n t) ∧
      (∀ (m : ℕ) (x : EvenVariableAlgebra B),
        x ∈ EvenVariableAlgebra.grade ℬ d m → g x ∈ 𝒟 m)

declarations.name: DividedPowers.TateResolution.IsCompatibleWithDifferential
declarations.doc:
