    letI : HasShift A.K ℤ := T.shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor A.K n).Additive := fun n => homotopyShiftAdditive A T n
    Pretriangulated A.K

declarations.name: DGCategory.distinguishedTriangles_homotopyPretriangulated
declarations.doc:
The distinguished triangles of the pretriangulated structure on `K(A)` are exactly the
triangles isomorphic to that of an admissible short exact sequence.
declarations.statement:
public theorem distinguishedTriangles_homotopyPretriangulated :
    letI : Preadditive A.K := homotopyPreadditive A
    letI : HasZeroObject A.K := homotopyHasZeroObject A T
    letI : HasShift A.K ℤ := T.shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor A.K n).Additive := fun n => homotopyShiftAdditive A T n
    (homotopyPretriangulated A T).distinguishedTriangles =
      {U | IsDistinguishedTriangle A T U}

declarations.name: DGCategory.admissibleMonomorphisms_octahedron
declarations.doc:
The octahedral diagram associated to two composable admissible monomorphisms.
The input exact sequences witness admissibility and fix the two quotient objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem admissibleMonomorphisms_octahedron
    (S : ConeSituation A)
    {x y z q₁ q₃ : A.Obj}
    (E₁ : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x y q₁)
    (E₃ : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) y z q₃) :
    letI : HasShift A.K ℤ := S.shift.kShift
    let T₁ := GradedSplitShortExact.associatedKTriangle S.shift E₁
    let T₃ := GradedSplitShortExact.associatedKTriangle S.shift E₃
    ∃ (q₂ : A.Obj)
      (E₂ : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) x z q₂)
      (E₄ : GradedSplitShortExact (A := A) q₁ q₂ q₃),
      let T₂ := GradedSplitShortExact.associatedKTriangle S.shift E₂
      let T₄ := GradedSplitShortExact.associatedKTriangle S.shift E₄
      (E₂.a.1 = A.comp (by rfl : (0 : ℤ) + 0 = 0) E₃.a.1 E₁.a.1) ∧
      (T₁.mor₁ ≫ T₃.mor₁ = T₂.mor₁) ∧
      (T₁.mor₂ ≫ T₄.mor₁ = T₃.mor₁ ≫ T₂.mor₂) ∧
      (T₄.mor₁ ≫ T₂.mor₃ = T₁.mor₃) ∧
      (T₂.mor₂ ≫ T₄.mor₂ = T₃.mor₂) ∧
      (T₂.mor₃ ≫ T₁.mor₁⟦1⟧' = T₄.mor₂ ≫ T₃.mor₃) ∧
      (T₄.mor₃ = T₃.mor₃ ≫ T₁.mor₂⟦1⟧')

declarations.name: DGCategory.homotopyCategory_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
The homotopy category of a differential graded category satisfying axioms (A), (B) and (C),
with the translation functors of axiom (B) and the triangles of admissible short exact sequences
as distinguished triangles, is a triangulated category.
declarations.statement:
public theorem homotopyCategory_isTriangulated :
    letI : Preadditive A.K := homotopyPreadditive A
    letI : HasZeroObject A.K := homotopyHasZeroObject A T
    letI : HasShift A.K ℤ := T.shift.kShift
    letI : ∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor A.K n).Additive := fun n => homotopyShiftAdditive A T n
    letI : Pretriangulated A.K := homotopyPretriangulated A T
    IsTriangulated A.K

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.sourceProjective
declarations.doc:
The source-projective objects of the homotopy category of right differential graded
`A`-modules: those from which morphisms are unchanged by passage to the derived category.
declarations.statement:
abbrev sourceProjective :
    ObjectProperty (DifferentialGradedModule.HomotopyCategory.{u, v, w} A)

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.sourceProjective_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** Source-projectivity is invariant under isomorphism in the
homotopy category.
declarations.statement:
instance sourceProjective_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms :
    ObjectProperty.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms (sourceProjective.{u, v, w} A)

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.sourceProjective_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The source-projective objects form a triangulated
subcategory of the homotopy category.
declarations.statement:
instance sourceProjective_isTriangulated :
    (sourceProjective.{u, v, w} A).IsTriangulated

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.sourceProjective_isSaturated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The triangulated subcategory of source-projective objects is
saturated.
declarations.statement:
instance sourceProjective_isSaturated :
    (sourceProjective.{u, v, w} A).IsSaturated

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.dualNumberAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The dual-number algebra, as a differential graded algebra
concentrated in degree zero.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualNumberAlgebra :
    DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} (DualNumber k)

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.dualNumberAlgebra_carrier
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The differential graded algebra has exactly the dual-number
ring as its underlying algebra.
declarations.statement: theorem dualNumberAlgebra_carrier : (dualNumberAlgebra k).A = DualNumber k

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.dualNumberAlgebra_algebraMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The scalar structure on the concentrated algebra is the
regular one.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualNumberAlgebra_algebraMap (r : DualNumber k) :
    cast (dualNumberAlgebra_carrier k)
      (algebraMap (DualNumber k) (dualNumberAlgebra k).A r) = r

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.dualNumberAlgebra_grading
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The differential graded algebra is concentrated in degree
zero.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualNumberAlgebra_grading (n : ℤ) :
    (dualNumberAlgebra k).grading n = if n = 0 then ⊤ else ⊥

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.dualNumberAlgebra_differential
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The differential graded algebra has zero differential.
declarations.statement: theorem dualNumberAlgebra_differential : (dualNumberAlgebra k).d = 0

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.dualNumberModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The doubly infinite complex of free rank-one dual-number
modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualNumberModule :
    DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} (dualNumberAlgebra k)

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.gradedFreeEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** An isomorphism from the graded module to a direct sum of
shifted copies of its regular module.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gradedFreeEquiv :
    (dualNumberModule k).M ≃ₗ[MulOpposite (dualNumberAlgebra k).A]
      (⨁ _ : ℤ, MulOpposite (dualNumberAlgebra k).A)

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.gradedFreeEquiv_mem_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The direct-sum coordinates identify each homogeneous piece
with its corresponding shifted copy of the regular module.
declarations.statement:
theorem gradedFreeEquiv_mem_iff (n : ℤ) (x : (dualNumberModule k).M) :
    x ∈ (dualNumberModule k).grading n ↔
      ∃ a : MulOpposite (dualNumberAlgebra k).A,
        gradedFreeEquiv k x =
          DirectSum.lof (MulOpposite (dualNumberAlgebra k).A) ℤ
            (fun _ => MulOpposite (dualNumberAlgebra k).A) n a

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.gradedPieceEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The chosen regular-module coordinates on a homogeneous
component.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gradedPieceEquiv (n : ℤ) :
    ((dualNumberModule k).grading n) ≃ₗ[DualNumber k] DualNumber k

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.dualNumberModule_differential
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** In the regular coordinates, the differential is multiplication
by `ε`.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualNumberModule_differential (n : ℤ) (x : (dualNumberModule k).grading n) :
    gradedPieceEquiv k (n + 1) ((dualNumberModule k).gradedDifferential n x) =
      DualNumber.eps * gradedPieceEquiv k n x

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.dualNumberModule_acyclic
declarations.doc: **Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The doubly infinite complex is acyclic.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualNumberModule_acyclic :
    DifferentialGradedModule.acyclic (dualNumberAlgebra k)
      ((DifferentialGradedModule.toHomotopyCategory (dualNumberAlgebra k)).obj
        (dualNumberModule k))

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.dualNumberModule_homotopy_id_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** The identity of the complex survives passage to the homotopy
category.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualNumberModule_homotopy_id_ne_zero :
    (𝟙 ((DifferentialGradedModule.toHomotopyCategory (dualNumberAlgebra k)).obj
      (dualNumberModule k))) ≠ 0

declarations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.dualNumberModule_not_sourceProjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09R0.** Graded freeness does not imply source-projectivity: the
acyclic graded-free module above is not source-projective.
declarations.statement:
theorem dualNumberModule_not_sourceProjective :
    ¬ sourceProjective (dualNumberAlgebra k)
      ((DifferentialGradedModule.toHomotopyCategory (dualNumberAlgebra k)).obj
        (dualNumberModule k))

registrations.name: Stacks.DifferentialGradedModule.SourceProjective.sourceProjective_iff_hom_acyclic_subsingleton
registrations.comment: acyclic_target_criterion

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.IsFinite
declarations.doc:
A differential graded module that is finitely generated as a right module over its
differential graded algebra.
declarations.statement:
public abbrev IsFinite {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R}
    (M : DifferentialGradedModule A) : Prop

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_factorThrough_finiteSubfiltration
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09R2.** Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra, let `E` be a compact
object of `D(A, d)` and let `P` be a differential graded `A`-module carrying a finite filtration
`0 = F₋₁P ⊆ F₀P ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ FₙP = P` by differential graded submodules whose graded pieces are direct
sums `F_{i+1}P/FᵢP ≅ ⨁_{j ∈ Jᵢ} A[k_{i,j}]` of shifts of the algebra. Then every morphism
`E ⟶ P` of `D(A, d)` factors through a differential graded submodule `P' ⊆ P` whose intersections
with the filtration have graded pieces the finite subsums `⨁_{j ∈ J'ᵢ} A[k_{i,j}]`, for finite
subsets `J'ᵢ ⊆ Jᵢ`.

The filtration of `P'` is produced as the pullback of that of `P`, and the identification of its
graded pieces with the finite subsums is compatible with the given identification of the graded
pieces of `P`, through the inclusion of the subsum.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_factorThrough_finiteSubfiltration (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R)
    (n : ℕ) (P : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A) (F : Filtration P ℕ)
    (_hzero : IsZero (F.obj 0)) (htop : IsIso (F.ι.app (n + 1)))
    (J : Fin (n + 1) → Type u) (k : ∀ i, J i → ℤ)
    (e : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), cokernel (F.diagram.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ i.val))) ≅
      ∐ fun j : J i => shift (regularModule A) (k i j))
    (E : derivedCategory' A) [IsCompactObject.{u} E]
    (f : E ⟶ (toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj P) :
    ∃ (P' : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A) (p : P' ⟶ P),
      Mono p ∧
      ∃ (F' : Filtration P' ℕ) (β : ∀ i : ℕ, F'.obj i ⟶ F.obj i),
        (∀ i : ℕ, IsPullback (F'.ι.app i) (β i) p (F.ι.app i)) ∧
        (∃ (J' : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), Finset (J i))
          (e' : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1),
            cokernel (F'.diagram.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ i.val))) ≅
              ∐ fun j : ↑(J' i) => shift (regularModule A) (k i j.val))
          (q : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1),
            cokernel (F'.diagram.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ i.val))) ⟶
              cokernel (F.diagram.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ i.val)))),
          (∀ i : Fin (n + 1),
            cokernel.π (F'.diagram.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ i.val))) ≫ q i =
              β (i.val + 1) ≫ cokernel.π (F.diagram.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ i.val)))) ∧
          (∀ i : Fin (n + 1),
            (e' i).hom ≫ Sigma.map' (fun j : ↑(J' i) => j.val) (fun _ => 𝟙 _) =
              q i ≫ (e i).hom)) ∧
        ∃ g : E ⟶ (toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj P',
          g ≫ (toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).map p = f

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.isCompactObject_iff_exists_retract_hasFiniteCellFiltration
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09R3.** *"Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded algebra. Let `E` be an object of
`D(A, d)`. The following are equivalent: (1) `E` is a compact object, and (2) `E` is a direct
summand of an object which is represented by a differential graded module `P` which has a finite
filtration `F_•` by differential graded submodules such that `F_iP/F_{i-1}P` are finite direct
sums of shifts of `A`."*

Condition (2) is read as: `E` is a retract of the image of a module with a finite cell filtration,
`DifferentialGradedModule.HasFiniteCellFiltration`. A retract is the same thing as a direct
summand here, the derived category of a differential graded algebra being idempotent complete
([Stacks, Tag 05QW]); the retract formulation is the one both implications produce and consume.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_iff_exists_retract_hasFiniteCellFiltration
    (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) (E : derivedCategory' A) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} E ↔
      ∃ P : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A, HasFiniteCellFiltration P ∧
        ∃ (i : E ⟶ (toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj P)
          (r : (toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj P ⟶ E), i ≫ r = 𝟙 E

declarations.name: Stacks.Examples.exists_isCompactObject_not_representable_by_finite_gradedProjective
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09R5].** *"There exists a differential graded algebra `(A, d)` and a compact
object `E` of `D(A, d)` such that `E` cannot be represented by a finite and graded projective
differential graded `A`-module."*

The algebra is `A = k[x, y]/(y²)` over `k = ZMod 2`, with `x` of degree `0`, `y` of degree `-1`
and `d y = x² + x`, and `E` is the summand of the regular module cut out by the idempotent given
by multiplication by `x` (Tag 09R4). The obstruction is
`Stacks.Examples.not_representable_by_finite_gradedProjective_of_retract_charTwoRegularModule`;
compactness of `E` enters only to discharge the first conjunct.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCompactObject_not_representable_by_finite_gradedProjective :
    ∃ (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{0, 0} (ZMod 2)) (E : derivedCategory' A),
      IsCompactObject.{0} E ∧
        ¬ ∃ P : DifferentialGradedModule.{0, 0, 0} A, IsFinite P ∧
            Stacks.DifferentialGraded.DGModule.IsProjectiveAsGradedModule.{0, 0, 0, 0}
              (Unbundled.module P) ∧
            Nonempty (E ≅ (toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj P)

registrations.comment: (1) the induced topology is the weakest one making the map continuous

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09R9.** Let `(A, d)` and `(B, d)` be differential graded algebras over a commutative
ring `R` and let `N` be a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule. Assume

1. the class of `N` in `D(B, d)` is a compact object, and
2. the canonical map `H^k(A) → Hom_{D(B,d)}(N, N[k])` of
   `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.cohomologyEndomorphismComparison` is bijective for every
   `k : ℤ`.

Then the derived tensor product `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` of Tag 09LS is fully faithful.

Full faithfulness is data — a chosen inverse to the action on morphism groups — so this is a
definition. It is Tag 07RB applied to the adjunction of Tag 09LT, whose unit is invertible by
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_unit_derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedHomFunctor`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorFunctor_fullyFaithful (N : Bimodule A B)
    [IsCompactObject.{u} ((toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule)]
    (h2 : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (N.cohomologyEndomorphismComparison k)) :
    (derivedTensorFunctor N).FullyFaithful

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_subsingleton_hom_of_isZero_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09RA.** For every compact object `E` of the derived category of a differential
graded algebra there are integers `a ≤ b` such that `Hom_{D(A, d)}(E, M) = 0` for every object `M`
whose cohomology `Hⁱ(M)` vanishes for all `i ∈ [a, b]`.

If no such interval existed, then for each `n` there would be an object `Mₙ` with vanishing
cohomology on `[-n, n]` and a nonzero morphism `E ⟶ Mₙ`. In each fixed degree only finitely many
of the `Mₙ` have nonvanishing cohomology, so
`DifferentialGradedModule.finite_setOf_ne_zero_of_isCompactObject` applies to the family and
contradicts the fact that all of the chosen morphisms are nonzero.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_subsingleton_hom_of_isZero_homology (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R)
    (E : derivedCategory' A) [IsCompactObject.{u} E] :
    ∃ a b : ℤ, a ≤ b ∧ ∀ M : derivedCategory' A,
      (∀ i : ℤ, a ≤ i → i ≤ b → IsZero (M.as.obj.as.toCochainComplex.homology i)) →
        Subsingleton (E ⟶ M)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_retract_isFiniteFreeAsGradedModule_of_isCompactObject
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09RB], the implication (1) ⟹ (2), in the corrected form that the source's own
proof establishes.** A compact object `E` of `D(A, d)` is a *direct summand* in `D(A, d)` of the
image of a differential graded `A`-module `P` which is *finite free* as a graded `A`-module and
satisfies `Hom_{K(A, d)}(P, M) = Hom_{D(A, d)}(P, M)` for every differential graded `A`-module
`M`.

The literal statement of the source — that `E` can be *represented by* such a `P`, with *finite
projective* in place of finite free — is **false**, and is **a mistake in the Stacks Project,
pending review**: it is contradicted by the source's own [Stacks, Tag 09R5], whose compact object
over the bounded algebra `A = k[x, y]/(y²)` of Tag 09R4 has no finite graded-projective
representative at all. That refutation is
`Stacks.Examples.not_forall_exists_finite_gradedProjective_of_isCompactObject`, in
`StacksFrontier/Examples/Algebra/CompactObjectNoFiniteProjectiveModel.lean`. The two differences
below are exactly what the argument of Tag 09R3 delivers, and the counterexample is consistent
with them: there `E = Ker(x)` *is* a direct summand of the regular module, which is finite free.

The statement is **unconditional**: the boundedness hypothesis "`A^n = 0` for `|n| ≫ 0`" of the
source is not assumed and is not used anywhere in the proof, which is part of why the literal
statement cannot be rescued by it.

The proof composes the two implications the chapter already has. [Stacks, Tag 09R3],
`DifferentialGradedModule.isCompactObject_iff_exists_retract_hasFiniteCellFiltration`, makes `E` a
retract of the image of a module `P` with a finite cell filtration; such a `P` is finite free as a
graded module, because its filtration is built out of finitely many finite direct sums of shifts
of the algebra and splits as a filtration of graded modules
(`DifferentialGradedModule.isFiniteFreeAsGradedModule_of_hasFiniteCellFiltration`); and it is
orthogonal on the left to the acyclic modules, so morphisms out of it are not changed by
localization (`DifferentialGradedModule.bijective_q_map_of_hasFiniteCellFiltration`, Tag 09KY),
which is the condition of [Stacks, Tag 09R0].

The converse holds too, as
`DifferentialGradedModule.isCompactObject_of_retract_isFiniteFreeAsGradedModule`, so the tag's
equivalence is restored by the correction; the registration of (2) ⟹ (1) stays on the source's own
spelling of condition (2), namely
`DifferentialGradedModule.isCompactObject_of_exists_finite_projective_representative`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_retract_isFiniteFreeAsGradedModule_of_isCompactObject
    (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) (E : derivedCategory' A)
    (hE : IsCompactObject.{u} E) :
    ∃ P : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A, IsFiniteFreeAsGradedModule P ∧
      (∀ M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A, Function.Bijective
        (((quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).map :
          ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj P ⟶ (toHomotopyCategory A).obj M) → _)) ∧
      ∃ (i : E ⟶ (toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj P)
        (r : (toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj P ⟶ E), i ≫ r = 𝟙 E
declarations.comment: (1) ⟹ (2), corrected: a compact object is a DIRECT SUMMAND of (the image of) a differential graded module which is finite FREE as a graded module and satisfies Hom_K = Hom_D; the literal statement, with 'represented by' and 'finite projective', is a mistake in the source — see the refutation in Examples/Algebra/CompactObjectNoFiniteProjectiveModel.lean

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.isCompactObject_of_exists_finite_projective_representative
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09RB], the implication (2) ⟹ (1).** *"Let `(A, d)` be a differential graded
algebra. Assume that `A^n = 0` for `|n| ≫ 0`. Let `E` be an object of `D(A, d)`. The following are
equivalent: (1) `E` is a compact object, and (2) `E` can be represented by a differential graded
`A`-module `P` which is finite projective as a graded `A`-module and satisfies
`Hom_{K(A, d)}(P, M) = Hom_{D(A, d)}(P, M)` for every differential graded `A`-module `M`."*

Condition (2) is read as the conjunction of: `P` is finite, that is finitely generated as a right
`A`-module (`DifferentialGradedModule.IsFinite`, Tag 09R1); `P` is projective as a graded module
(`Stacks.DifferentialGraded.DGModule.IsProjectiveAsGradedModule`, Tag 09K0); the localization
functor is bijective on morphisms out of the class of `P` into the class of every differential
graded module (Tag 09R0); and `E` is isomorphic in `D(A, d)` to the class of `P`.

The boundedness of `A` and the graded projectivity of `P` are hypotheses of the source statement
and are recorded here, but this implication uses neither: finiteness together with the comparison
of morphism groups already gives compactness.
declarations.statement:
theorem isCompactObject_of_exists_finite_projective_representative
    (A : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) (c : ℤ)
    (_hA : ∀ n : ℤ, c ≤ |n| → A.grading n = ⊥) (E : derivedCategory' A)
    (hE : ∃ P : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A, IsFinite P ∧
      Stacks.DifferentialGraded.DGModule.IsProjectiveAsGradedModule.{u, u, u, u}
        (Unbundled.module P) ∧
      (∀ M : DifferentialGradedModule.{u, u, u} A, Function.Bijective
        (((quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).map :
          ((toHomotopyCategory A).obj P ⟶ (toHomotopyCategory A).obj M) → _)) ∧
      Nonempty (E ≅ (toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj P)) :
    IsCompactObject.{u} E

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation
declarations.doc:
A directed inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes whose transition
morphisms are affine, equipped with a chosen limit cone and a chosen index.
declarations.statement:
structure AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation (I : Type v) [Preorder I]
    [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.homProjection_homTransition
declarations.doc:
**The cocone clause of the conclusion of Stacks 09RE.** Pushing a homomorphism from the
stage `i` to the stage `j` and then to the limit gives the same homomorphism `E ⟶ K` as pushing
it to the limit directly.

This holds for all `E₀` and `K₀`: it is the coherence of the two comparison
isomorphisms of derived pullback along the factorisations `f_{ji} ≫ f_{i0} = f_{j0}` and
`f_j ≫ f_{ji} = f_i`, together with the naturality of the second.
declarations.statement:
theorem homProjection_homTransition (i j : D.Stages) (h : i ≤ j)
    (g : stageObj E₀ i ⟶ stageObj K₀ i) :
    homProjection E₀ K₀ j (homTransition E₀ K₀ i j h g) = homProjection E₀ K₀ i g
declarations.comment: the maps to Hom(E, K) are compatible with the transition maps of the directed system, for all E_0 and K_0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.homTransition_homTransition
declarations.doc:
**The maps of the directed system of Stacks 09RE compose.** For `i ≤ j ≤ k` among the
stages, pushing a homomorphism from the stage `i` to the stage `j` and then to the stage `k`
gives the same homomorphism `E_k ⟶ K_k` as pushing it to the stage `k` directly. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.homProjection_homTransition` this says that
`i ↦ Hom_{D(𝒪_{S_i})}(E_i, K_i)` is a system over the stages and that the maps to
`Hom_{D(𝒪_S)}(E, K)` form a cocone on it, which is what makes the colimit the tag speaks of
well-posed.

Like the cocone clause, this holds for all `E₀` and `K₀`; it is the cocycle
identity of the comparisons `Lf_{i0}^* ⋙ Lf_{ji}^* ≅ Lf_{j0}^*`.
declarations.statement:
theorem homTransition_homTransition (i j k : D.Stages) (h : i ≤ j) (h' : j ≤ k)
    (g : stageObj E₀ i ⟶ stageObj K₀ i) :
    homTransition E₀ K₀ j k h' (homTransition E₀ K₀ i j h g) =
      homTransition E₀ K₀ i k (h.trans h') g
declarations.comment: the directed system whose colimit the tag takes: its transition maps compose, for all E_0 and K_0

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.isHomColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RE.** In Situation 09RD, let `E₀` and `K₀` be objects of `D(𝒪_{S₀})`, put
`E_i = Lf_{i0}^*E₀`, `K_i = Lf_{i0}^*K₀` for `i ≥ 0` and `E = Lf_0^*E₀`, `K = Lf_0^*K₀`.  If
either `E₀` is perfect and `K₀` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_{S₀})`, or `E₀` is pseudo-coherent and `K₀`
lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_{S₀})` and has finite Tor dimension, then

`colim_{i ≥ 0} Hom_{D(𝒪_{S_i})}(E_i, K_i) ⟶ Hom_{D(𝒪_S)}(E, K)`

is an isomorphism.

The index set lies in the universe of the schemes; over a larger index set the statement fails,
see `AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.exists_not_isHomColimit`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHomColimit
    (hcase :
      (Stacks.Cohomology.PerfectComplexes.IsPerfect
            (X := (D.stage D.base).toRingedSpace) E₀ ∧
          ∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (D.stage D.base).ringCatSheaf
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (D.stage D.base).Modules n).obj K₀)) ∨
        (AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.PseudoCoherence.IsPseudoCoherent
            (X := (D.stage D.base).toRingedSpace) E₀ ∧
          (∀ n : ℤ, SheafOfModules.isQuasicoherent (D.stage D.base).ringCatSheaf
            ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (D.stage D.base).Modules n).obj K₀)) ∧
          Stacks.Cohomology.TorAmplitude.HasFiniteTorDimension
            (D.stage D.base).toRingedSpace K₀)) :
    IsHomColimit E₀ K₀

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.perfect_isColimit
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks, Tag 09RF].** In the situation of [Stacks, Tag 09RD], the category of perfect
objects of `D(𝒪_S)` is the colimit of the categories of perfect objects of `D(𝒪_{S_i})`: the
comparison functor out of the colimit, induced by derived pullback along the projections, is

1. essentially surjective — every perfect object of `D(𝒪_S)` is isomorphic to the derived
   pullback of a perfect object of `D(𝒪_{S_i})` for some `i`; and
2. fully faithful — for perfect `E` and `K` on a stage `S_i`, the group
   `Hom_{D(𝒪_S)}(Lf_i^*E, Lf_i^*K)` is the filtered colimit over `j ≥ i` of the groups
   `Hom_{D(𝒪_{S_j})}(Lf_{ji}^*E, Lf_{ji}^*K)`.

A morphism of the colimit category between objects living at two stages is a morphism after
pullback to a common later stage, so the second clause, stated for two objects of one stage, is
the whole of full faithfulness.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfect_isColimit :
    (∀ (E : DerivedCategory D.limitScheme.Modules),
      IsPerfect (X := D.limitScheme.toRingedSpace) E →
      ∃ (i : I) (_ : D.base ≤ i) (Eᵢ : DerivedCategory (D.stage i).Modules),
        IsPerfect (X := (D.stage i).toRingedSpace) Eᵢ ∧
          Nonempty ((derivedPullback (D.projection i).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Eᵢ ≅ E)) ∧
    (∀ (i : I) (E K : DerivedCategory (D.stage i).Modules),
      IsPerfect (X := (D.stage i).toRingedSpace) E →
      IsPerfect (X := (D.stage i).toRingedSpace) K → IsHomColimit (D := D.atStage i) E K)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.isPerfect_transition
declarations.doc:
**Derived pullback along a transition morphism of the situation preserves perfectness.**
This is Stacks 09UA at `f_{ji}`, and it is what makes the transition functor on the categories
of perfect objects defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_transition {i j : I} (h : i ≤ j)
    (E : DerivedCategory (D.stage i).Modules) (hE : IsPerfect (X := (D.stage i).toRingedSpace) E) :
    IsPerfect (X := (D.stage j).toRingedSpace)
      ((derivedPullback (D.transition h).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)
declarations.comment: derived pullback along the transition morphisms of the situation sends perfect objects to perfect objects, so the transition functors of the colimit statement are defined; the colimit property itself is not included

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.isPerfect_projection
declarations.doc:
**Derived pullback along a projection of the situation preserves perfectness.** This is
Stacks 09UA at `f_i`, and it is what makes the comparison functor from the stage `i` to the limit
defined.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPerfect_projection (i : I)
    (E : DerivedCategory (D.stage i).Modules) (hE : IsPerfect (X := (D.stage i).toRingedSpace) E) :
    IsPerfect (X := D.limitScheme.toRingedSpace)
      ((derivedPullback (D.projection i).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E)
declarations.comment: derived pullback along the projections of the situation sends perfect objects to perfect objects, so the comparison functors of the colimit statement are defined; the colimit property itself is not included

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.perfectComparison_coherence
declarations.doc:
**The cocone coherence on the categories of perfect objects.** For `i ≤ j ≤ k`, comparing
through the stage `j` and comparing after composing the two transitions give the same
isomorphism from the functor out of `D_perf(𝒪_{S_i})` through the stage `k` to the functor out
of `D_perf(𝒪_{S_i})` directly. Together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.perfectTransitionComp_coherence` this is the statement that
the functors `AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.perfectProjection` form a coherent cocone over
the system of categories of perfect objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectComparison_coherence {i j k : I} (h : i ≤ j) (h' : j ≤ k)
    (E : PerfectDerivedCategory (D.stage i)) :
    ((D.perfectComparison h').app ((D.perfectTransition h).obj E)).hom ≫
        ((D.perfectComparison h).app E).hom =
      (D.perfectProjection k).map ((D.perfectTransitionComp h h').app E).hom ≫
        ((D.perfectComparison (h.trans h')).app E).hom
declarations.comment: the canonical cocone of the colimit statement: the functors between the categories of perfect objects induced by derived pullback along the projections, and their coherence with the transition functors. Neither full faithfulness nor essential surjectivity of the comparison out of the colimit is included

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.DescentSituation.perfectTransitionComp_coherence
declarations.doc:
**The system of transition functors on the categories of perfect objects is coherent.** For
`i ≤ j ≤ k ≤ l`, the two ways of composing the comparison isomorphisms of the three transitions
agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectTransitionComp_coherence {i j k l : I} (h : i ≤ j) (h' : j ≤ k) (h'' : k ≤ l)
    (E : PerfectDerivedCategory (D.stage i)) :
    ((D.perfectTransitionComp h' h'').app ((D.perfectTransition h).obj E)).hom ≫
        ((D.perfectTransitionComp h (h'.trans h'')).app E).hom =
      (D.perfectTransition h'').map ((D.perfectTransitionComp h h').app E).hom ≫
        ((D.perfectTransitionComp (h.trans h') h'').app E).hom
declarations.comment: the system of categories of perfect objects along the transition morphisms: the transition functors, their composition isomorphisms and the cocycle identity those satisfy. Neither full faithfulness nor essential surjectivity of the comparison out of the colimit is included

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.AffinePerfectLimit.exists_isPerfect_stage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RF**, the affine base case of essential surjectivity. Let `i ↦ R_i` be a filtered
diagram of commutative rings whose colimit is computed on underlying sets, with colimit cocone `c`,
and write `R = c.pt`, so that `Spec R` is the limit of the affine schemes `Spec R_i`. Then every
perfect object `E` of `D(𝒪_{Spec R})` is, for some stage `i`, the derived pullback along
`Spec R ⟶ Spec R_i` of a perfect object of `D(𝒪_{Spec R_i})`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_stage {J : Type u} [Category.{u} J] [IsFiltered J]
    (A : J ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [PreservesColimit A (forget CommRingCat.{u})]
    (c : Cocone A) (hc : IsColimit c) (E : DerivedCategory (Spec c.pt).Modules)
    (hE : IsPerfect (X := (Spec c.pt).toRingedSpace) E) :
    ∃ (j : J) (Ej : DerivedCategory (Spec (A.obj j)).Modules),
      IsPerfect (X := (Spec (A.obj j)).toRingedSpace) Ej ∧
        Nonempty ((derivedPullback (Spec.map (c.ι.app j)).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj Ej ≅ E)
declarations.comment: essential surjectivity of the comparison out of the colimit, in the affine base case of the source's induction: for a filtered system of rings with colimit R, every perfect object of D(𝒪_{Spec R}) is derived pullback of a perfect object at a stage. The induction over the quasi-compact opens of S_0 that globalises it is not included, and neither is full faithfulness

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RH.** A directed inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic
spaces over `S` whose transition morphisms are affine, equipped with a chosen limit cone and a
chosen index.
declarations.statement:
structure DescentSituation (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u})) (I : Type v) [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.isHomColimit_of_ringModel
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RI.**  In Situation 09RH, let `E₀` and `K₀` be objects of `D(𝒪_{X₀})`, put
`E_i = Lf_{i0}^*E₀`, `K_i = Lf_{i0}^*K₀` for `i ≥ 0` and `E = Lf_0^*E₀`, `K = Lf_0^*K₀`.  If
either `E₀` is perfect and `K₀` lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_{X₀})`, or `E₀` is pseudo-coherent and `K₀`
lies in `D_QCoh(𝒪_{X₀})` and has finite Tor dimension, then

`colim_{i ≥ 0} Hom_{D(𝒪_{X_i})}(E_i, K_i) ⟶ Hom_{D(𝒪_X)}(E, K)`

is an isomorphism.

The affine translation dictionary `model` is carried as an explicit hypothesis rather than
discharged; see "The carried hypothesis" in this file's module documentation for what it is and
why it is an input of the source's proof and not its conclusion.

The three clauses are read off the ring-level colimit computation of Stacks 09RE, which this
library proves: surjectivity is
`Stacks.FilteredColimitHom.exists_descends_derived`, eventual injectivity is
`Stacks.FilteredColimitHom.exists_le_eq_of_eq_derived`, and the cocone identity is the
compatibility of the dictionary with `RingModel.hcompat`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHomColimit_of_ringModel
    [∀ U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property).C,
      HasSheafify ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj
        (D.stage D.base).property).J.over U) AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [∀ U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property).C,
      ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj
        (D.stage D.base).property).J.over U).WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
    [∀ U : (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property).C,
      ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj
        (D.stage D.base).property).J.over U).HasSheafCompose
          (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    [(Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u}
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property).O).Additive]
    [∀ M, ((Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u}
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj
        (D.stage D.base).property).O).obj M).Additive]
    [∀ (M N : CochainComplex
        (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property) ℤ),
      HomologicalComplex.HasMapBifunctor M N
        (Stacks.SheafOfModules.Tensor.sheafTensor.{u + 1, u, u, u, u}
          (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property).O)
        (ComplexShape.up ℤ)]
    (T : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property))
    (hcase :
      ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj
            (D.stage D.base).property).IsPerfect E₀ ∧
          ∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property)
              n).obj K₀).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∨
        ((smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj
            (D.stage D.base).property).IsPseudoCoherent E₀ ∧
          (∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
            (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property)
              n).obj K₀).IsQuasicoherentOnSite) ∧
          Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct.HasFiniteTorDimension T K₀))
    (R : Type u) [Ring R] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    (model : RingModel sys E₀ K₀ R) :
    IsHomColimit sys E₀ K₀
declarations.comment: the affine ring-translation dictionary `model` is carried as an explicit hypothesis: the reduction of the sheaf-level statement to the ring-level colimit computation of Stacks 09RE, which runs through the induction principle 08GP, Mayer-Vietoris 08H9 and the small-etale-to-Zariski comparison 071Q, is not available in this library

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_descendedHom
declarations.doc:
**Fullness of the comparison out of the colimit, Stacks 09RJ.**  In Situation 09RH, let `E₀`
and `K₀` be perfect objects of `D(𝒪_{X₀})` and put `E_i = Lf_{i0}^*E₀`, `K_i = Lf_{i0}^*K₀` for
`i ≥ 0` and `E = Lf_0^*E₀`, `K = Lf_0^*K₀`.  Then every morphism `E ⟶ K` of `D(𝒪_X)` is the
image, under the map of Stacks 09RI, of a morphism `E_i ⟶ K_i` at some stage `i ≥ 0`.

The categories of perfect objects are full subcategories of the ambient derived categories, so
this is fullness of the comparison functor out of the colimit of the `D_perf(𝒪_{X_i})`.

This is the first half of the full faithfulness that the source's proof of Stacks 09RJ takes
from Stacks 09RI, and it is deduced from Stacks 09RI here.  The hypotheses `model`
and `hqcK₀` are carried; see "The carried hypotheses" in this file's module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_descendedHom
    (T : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property))
    (hqcK₀ : ∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property) n).obj
        K₀.obj).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (R : Type u) [Ring R] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    (model : RingModel sys E₀.obj K₀.obj R)
    (φ : limitObj sys E₀.obj ⟶ limitObj sys K₀.obj) :
    ∃ (i : D.Stages) (g : stageObj sys E₀.obj i ⟶ stageObj sys K₀.obj i),
      homProjection sys E₀.obj K₀.obj i g = φ
declarations.comment: fullness of the comparison out of the colimit of the categories of perfect objects, which the source's proof takes from Stacks 09RI; essential surjectivity, the other half of that proof, is not included

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.eventually_map_eq
declarations.doc:
**Faithfulness of the comparison out of the colimit, Stacks 09RJ.**  In Situation 09RH, with
`E₀` and `K₀` perfect objects of `D(𝒪_{X₀})` as above, two morphisms `E_i ⟶ K_i` at a stage
`i ≥ 0` whose images `E ⟶ K` in `D(𝒪_X)` agree already have equal images at some later stage.

Together with `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.exists_descendedHom` this says that the
hom-sets of `D_perf(𝒪_X)` between objects coming from the system are the filtered colimits of
the hom-sets at the stages, which is full faithfulness of the comparison out of the colimit of
the `D_perf(𝒪_{X_i})`.

This is the second half of the full faithfulness that the source's proof of Stacks 09RJ takes
from Stacks 09RI, and it is deduced from Stacks 09RI here.  The hypotheses `model`
and `hqcK₀` are carried; see "The carried hypotheses" in this file's module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem eventually_map_eq
    (T : Stacks.SheafOfModules.DerivedTensorProduct
      (smallEtaleRingedSite B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property))
    (hqcK₀ : ∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
      (Modules.{u, u} B S hS (D.stage D.base).obj (D.stage D.base).property) n).obj
        K₀.obj).IsQuasicoherentOnSite)
    (R : Type u) [Ring R] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    (model : RingModel sys E₀.obj K₀.obj R) (i : D.Stages)
    (g g' : stageObj sys E₀.obj i ⟶ stageObj sys K₀.obj i)
    (hgg : homProjection sys E₀.obj K₀.obj i g = homProjection sys E₀.obj K₀.obj i g') :
    ∃ (j : D.Stages) (h : i ≤ j), homTransition sys E₀.obj K₀.obj i j h g =
      homTransition sys E₀.obj K₀.obj i j h g'
declarations.comment: faithfulness of the comparison out of the colimit of the categories of perfect objects, which the source's proof takes from Stacks 09RI; essential surjectivity, the other half of that proof, is not included

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.perfectObjectsDescend_and_perfectHomsDescend
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RJ.** In Situation 09RH (`X = lim Xᵢ` along affine transition morphisms of
quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces) the category of perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)` is the
colimit of the categories of perfect objects of `D(𝒪_{Xᵢ})`: every perfect object on `X` is
`Lfᵢ^*Eᵢ` for some stage `i` and some perfect `Eᵢ`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.PerfectObjectsDescend`), and for perfect `Eᵢ`, `Kᵢ`
on `Xᵢ` the map `colim_{j ≥ i} Hom(Lf_{ji}^*Eᵢ, Lf_{ji}^*Kᵢ) ⟶ Hom(Lfᵢ^*Eᵢ, Lfᵢ^*Kᵢ)` is
bijective (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.PerfectHomsDescend`).

**Correction.** The statement carries the hypothesis `ChartsBounded` (the size bound
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ChartsBounded` on the chart systems of the stages), which the source does
not state: the sites here are `u`-small models of the big fppf site with a size cutoff, and the
bound is what keeps the limits of the affine charts of the stages inside the site
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ChartsBounded.sizeBound`). It holds for instance when `#I` is below the
cofinality of the cutoff (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.chartsBounded_of_lt_cof_ord`).
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectObjectsDescend_and_perfectHomsDescend (hb : ChartsBounded B S hS D.system) :
    D.PerfectObjectsDescend ∧ D.PerfectHomsDescend
declarations.comment:
Under the size bound `ChartsBounded` on the chart systems of the stages, which the
source does not state (the sites are size-bounded models of the big fppf site).

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.perfectObjectsDescend_and_perfectHomsDescend_of_mk_lt_cof_ord
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RJ at the hypotheses of Situation 09RH, with no bounded-charts hypothesis.** In
Situation 09RH, indexed by a directed set in the universe of the site with fewer elements than
the cofinality of the site's size cutoff, the category of perfect objects of `D(𝒪_X)` is the
colimit of the categories of perfect objects of `D(𝒪_{Xᵢ})`: essential surjectivity
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.PerfectObjectsDescend`) and full faithfulness
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.PerfectHomsDescend`).

The size bound `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ChartsBounded` that
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.perfectObjectsDescend_and_perfectHomsDescend` assumes,
and that the source does not state, is discharged here by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.chartsBounded_of_mk_lt_cof_ord`.  What is left is
`#I < B.cutoff.ord.cof`, which is not a weakening: it is refuted beyond that bound by
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/Limits/SectionsColimitLargeIndexCounterexample.lean`, and
`I : Type u` is refuted beyond it by
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Perfect/LimitHomDescent/Counterexample.lean`.

This carries `@[stacks 09RJ]` for **both halves** — essential surjectivity
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.PerfectObjectsDescend`) and full faithfulness
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.PerfectHomsDescend`) — at Situation 09RH's own
hypotheses.  The only restriction beyond the tag's is `#I < B.cutoff.ord.cof`, which this
formalization is counterexample-forced to carry.

The `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.ChartsBounded` bound that
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.DescentSituation.perfectObjectsDescend_and_perfectHomsDescend` assumes,
and which the source does not state, is discharged here.  That statement keeps its own
registration: `hI` implies `ChartsBounded` but not conversely, so it remains the more general
conditional form.
declarations.statement:
theorem perfectObjectsDescend_and_perfectHomsDescend_of_mk_lt_cof_ord
    (hI : Cardinal.mk I < B.cutoff.ord.cof) :
    D.PerfectObjectsDescend ∧ D.PerfectHomsDescend
declarations.comment: both halves, at the tag's own hypotheses

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.isRegularImmersion_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 09RK for the inner factor.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be immersions of
schemes with `X` locally Noetherian and `i` perfect.  If the composite `i ≫ j` is a regular
immersion, then `i` is a regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRegularImmersion_of_perfect (hji : IsRegularImmersion (i ≫ j)) :
    IsRegularImmersion i

declarations.name: Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.RegularIdealSheaf.exists_opens_isRegularImmersion_comp_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 09RK for the outer factor, in its neighbourhood form — the corrected statement
of a Stacks erratum.**  Under the same hypotheses there is an open
`V ⊆ Y` containing the image of `i` such that the immersion `V.ι ≫ j` of that open subscheme
into `X` is regular.

The source concludes instead that `j` itself is a regular immersion, and that is false.  Over a
field `k`, take `Z = Spec k`, `Y = Spec k ⊔ Spec k`, `X = Spec k ⊔ Spec k[ε]/(ε²)`, let `i` be
the inclusion of the first component of `Y`, and let `j` be the identity on the first component
and the reduced point `Spec k ↪ Spec k[ε]/(ε²)` on the second.  All three hypotheses hold: `X` is
the spectrum of the Noetherian ring `k × k[ε]/(ε²)`, and `i` and `i ≫ j` are inclusions of a
component, hence open immersions, hence regular immersions, so `i` is perfect.  Yet `j` is not a
regular immersion: on the second component its ideal is `(ε) ⊆ k[ε]/(ε²)`, and no weakly regular
sequence generates it, since every element of `(ε)` kills `ε ≠ 0`.  This is
`Stacks.Examples.not_forall_isRegularImmersion_of_perfect_of_isRegularImmersion_comp`.

The hypotheses control `j` only at the points of `i(Z)` — in the example the first component,
where `j` is an isomorphism — and the neighbourhood form below is exactly what the source's own
local-ring argument supplies.  See also the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_opens_isRegularImmersion_comp_of_perfect (hji : IsRegularImmersion (i ≫ j)) :
    ∃ V : Y.Opens, (∀ z : Z, i.base z ∈ V) ∧ IsRegularImmersion (V.ι ≫ j)
declarations.comment: j is a regular immersion near the image of i

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RL, the relative conclusion.**  Let `X ⟶ Y ⟶ S` be a commutative triangle of
morphisms of schemes with `S` locally Noetherian and `Y ⟶ S` locally of finite type.  If
`f : X ⟶ Y` is perfect and `X ⟶ S` is a local complete intersection morphism, then `f` is a local
complete intersection morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism_of_perfect {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ S) {h : X ⟶ S} (hcomm : f ≫ g = h) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Perfect f] (hh : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism h) :
    IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism f
declarations.comment: the morphism to the intermediate scheme is a local complete intersection morphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.koszulAt_of_perfect
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RL, the conclusion on the base.**  In the same situation, `g : Y ⟶ S` is Koszul at
the image of every point of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem koszulAt_of_perfect {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) {h : X ⟶ S}
    (hcomm : f ≫ g = h) [IsLocallyNoetherian S] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    [AlgebraicGeometry.Perfect f] (hh : IsLocalCompleteIntersectionMorphism h) (x : X) :
    KoszulAt g (f.base x)
declarations.comment: the intermediate scheme is Koszul over the base at every point of the image

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09RN.**  The conormal algebra `𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of a closed immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces: the inverse image along `i` of the sheaf of graded
`𝒪_X`-algebras `⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝓘ⁿ`, for `𝓘` the ideal sheaf of `i`.

Its degree-`n` piece is `i^*(𝓘ⁿ)`, which is the `𝒪_Z`-module the source describes as
`𝓘ⁿ/𝓘ⁿ⁺¹`; the module documentation records why, and that the identification is deferred, as
it is in the degree-one case `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalModule`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebra (i : Z ⟶ X) :
    SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.{u, u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS Z)
declarations.comment: the conormal algebra of a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09RN.**  The conormal algebra `𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of an immersion
`i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces: the conormal algebra of the closed immersion of `Z` into the
complement `X ∖ ∂Z` of the boundary of its image, through which `i` factors by Stacks 04CE.

Its degree-`n` piece is the inverse image along that closed immersion of the `n`-th power of
the ideal sheaf of `Z` in `X ∖ ∂Z`, which is the `𝒪_Z`-module the source describes as
`𝓘ⁿ/𝓘ⁿ⁺¹`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebraOfImmersion (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z₀) (i : Z₀ ⟶ X₀) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.{u, u}
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS (⟨Z₀, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS))
declarations.comment: the conormal algebra of an immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraPiece
declarations.doc:
**The homogeneous pieces of the conormal algebra of a closed subspace.**  The degree-`n`
piece `𝒞_{Z/X, n}` of the conormal algebra of a closed subspace `Z` of an algebraic space `X`
is the inverse image along the inclusion `i : Z ⟶ X` of the `n`-th power of the defining ideal
sheaf `𝓘_Z ⊆ 𝒪_X` of Stacks 03MB.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebraPiece (X : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)
    (Z : ClosedSubspaces B S hS X.1) (n : ℕ) :
    Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1.toFunctor Z.2.1
declarations.comment: the homogeneous pieces, as inverse images of the ideal powers, for a closed subspace

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraPiecePushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RP.**  For a closed subspace `Z` of an algebraic space `X` with inclusion `i` and
defining ideal sheaf `𝓘`, the direct image of the degree-`n` piece of the conormal algebra is the
degree-`n` graded piece of `𝓘`:

`i_*𝒞_{Z/X, n} = 𝓘ⁿ/𝓘ⁿ⁺¹`.

The degree-`n` piece is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraPiece`, the inverse image
`i^*(𝓘ⁿ)` of Stacks 09RN; in degree one it is the conormal module of Stacks 04CN, and in degree
zero the inverse image of the structure sheaf of `X`.  The identification with `𝓘ⁿ/𝓘ⁿ⁺¹` is the
inverse of the unit of Stacks 03LU, transported along
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.pullbackConormalGradedPieceIso`;
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isoConormalAlgebraPiece` records that it determines `𝒞_{Z/X, n}` up to
isomorphism, which is what makes the equation of the source an identification and not merely the
assertion that some module has that direct image.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isoConormalAlgebraPiece
declarations.doc:
**The degree-`n` piece of the conormal algebra is determined by Stacks 09RP.**  An
`𝒪_Z`-module whose direct image along the inclusion is `𝓘ⁿ/𝓘ⁿ⁺¹` is isomorphic to `𝒞_{Z/X, n}`,
because the direct image of modules along a closed immersion is fully faithful (Stacks 04CJ,
part (2)).  This is the uniqueness clause behind the equality sign of the source.

The source introduces 76.6.1.1 by saying that `𝒞_{Z/X, n}` is "characterized by the property"
`i_*𝒞_{Z/X, n} = 𝓘ⁿ/𝓘ⁿ⁺¹`; this is that characterization, and it is what licenses reading
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraPiecePushforwardIso` as the equality sign of the
source rather than as the weaker assertion that some module has that direct image.
declarations.statement:
def isoConormalAlgebraPiece (n : ℕ) (Cc : Modules.{u, u} B S hS Z.1.toFunctor Z.2.1)
    (e : (modulePushforward B S hS (subspaceInclusion B S hS X Z)).obj Cc ≅
      conormalGradedPiece B S hS X Z n) :
    Cc ≅ conormalAlgebraPiece B S hS X Z n
declarations.comment: the characterizing property 76.6.1.1 determines 𝒞_{Z/X, n} up to isomorphism

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraDegreeZeroIso
declarations.doc:
For a closed subspace `Z` of an algebraic space `X` with
inclusion `i` and defining ideal sheaf `𝓘`, the direct image of the structure sheaf of `Z` is the
quotient of the structure sheaf of `X` by `𝓘`:

`i_*𝒞_{Z/X, 0} = i_*𝒪_Z = 𝒪_X/𝓘 = 𝓘⁰/𝓘¹`.

The isomorphism is induced by the structure projection.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebraDegreeZeroIso :
    cokernel (definingIdealSheaf B S hS X Z).ι ≅ pushforwardStructureSheaf B S hS X Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.symmetricAlgebraToConormalAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09RQ, Equation 76.6.1.2.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic
spaces and let `A` be a sheaf of graded `𝒪_Z`-algebras which is the symmetric algebra on the
conormal module `𝒞_{Z/X} = (𝒞_{Z/X,*})_1`, with degree-one generator `ι`.  Then there is a
canonical unital homomorphism of sheaves of graded `𝒪_Z`-algebras

`Sym^*(𝒞_{Z/X}) ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}`,

the unique one extending the identity of the conormal module.

It exists because the degree-`(1,1)` multiplication of the conormal algebra is commutative, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebra_mul_one_one_comm`, which is exactly the condition the
universal property of the symmetric algebra tests a degree-one generator against.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def symmetricAlgebraToConormalAlgebra (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (A : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.{u, u} (structureRingSheaf B S hS Z))
    (ι : (conormalAlgebra B S hS i).piece 1 ⟶ A.piece 1)
    (hA : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.IsSymmetricAlgebra A ι) :
    SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.UnitalHom A (conormalAlgebra B S hS i)
declarations.comment: the canonical map from the symmetric algebra on the conormal module

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.symmetricAlgebraToConormalAlgebraOfImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09RQ for an immersion.**  The canonical map
`Sym^*(𝒞_{Z/X}) ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of Equation 76.6.1.2 for an immersion `i : Z ⟶ X`, taken through
the closed factorisation of Stacks 04CE which defines
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersion`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def symmetricAlgebraToConormalAlgebraOfImmersion
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀) (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z₀) (i : Z₀ ⟶ X₀)
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i)
    (A : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.{u, u}
      (structureRingSheaf B S hS (⟨Z₀, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)))
    (ι : (conormalAlgebraOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi).piece 1 ⟶ A.piece 1)
    (hA : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.IsSymmetricAlgebra A ι) :
    SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.UnitalHom A
      (conormalAlgebraOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi)
declarations.comment: the canonical map from the symmetric algebra, for an immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraEtaleRestrictionPieceIso
declarations.doc:
Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces, let `φ : U ⟶ X` be étale and let
`Z_U = U ×_X Z` with projections `p : Z_U ⟶ Z` and `i_U : Z_U ⟶ U`. Then the inverse image along
`p` of the degree-`n` piece of the conormal algebra of `i` is the degree-`n` piece of the conormal
algebra of `i_U`:

`(𝒞_{Z/X,*}|_{Z_U})_n = p^*(𝒞_{Z/X,*})_n ≅ (𝒞_{Z_U/U,*})_n`.

The isomorphism is the square comparison `p^*i^* ≅ i_U^*φ^*` of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.modulePullbackSquareCompIso`, then the inverse image along `i_U` of the
identification of `φ^*` with étale restriction of [Stacks Project, Tag 03LW], then the equality
`𝓘ⁿ|_U = 𝓘_Uⁿ` of the powers of the kernel ideal sheaves.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebraEtaleRestrictionPieceIso (p : ZU ⟶ Z) (iU : ZU ⟶ U) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (φ : U ⟶ X) (sq : IsPullback p iU i φ) (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) (n : ℤ) :
    (modulePullback B S hS p).obj ((conormalAlgebra B S hS i).piece n) ≅
      (conormalAlgebra B S hS iU).piece n
declarations.comment: the conormal algebra of an etale localisation, in each degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraEtaleRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RR.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces, let `φ : U ⟶ X` be
étale and let `Z_U = U ×_X Z`, with projections `p : Z_U ⟶ Z` and `i_U : Z_U ⟶ U`.  Then the
restriction `p^*𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of the conormal algebra of `i` is the conormal algebra of `i_U`, as
sheaves of graded `𝒪_{Z_U}`-algebras:

`𝒞_{Z/X,*}|_{Z_U} = p^*𝒞_{Z/X,*} ≅ 𝒞_{Z_U/U,*}`.

The isomorphism is canonical: it is the multiplicative composition comparison
`p^*i^* ≅ (i_U ≫ φ)^* ≅ i_U^*φ^*` of Stacks 03LU followed by the inverse image along `i_U` of the
identification `φ^*(⨁ 𝓘ⁿ) = ⨁ 𝓘_Uⁿ` of the graded algebras of the powers of the kernel ideal
sheaves, which is Stacks 03LW in each degree.

No hypothesis is imposed on `i` and `U` is an arbitrary algebraic space étale over `X`; for an
immersion `i` and a scheme `U` this is the statement of Stacks 09RR.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebraEtaleRestrictionIso (p : ZU ⟶ Z) (iU : ZU ⟶ U) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (φ : U ⟶ X) (sq : IsPullback p iU i φ) (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) :
    (gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS ZU) (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS Z)
        (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS p)).obj (conormalAlgebra B S hS i) ≅
      conormalAlgebra B S hS iU
declarations.comment: the conormal algebra of an etale localisation, as graded algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraEtaleRestrictionIso_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RR, functoriality in `U`.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a morphism of algebraic spaces and
let `φ : U ⟶ X`, `φ' : U' ⟶ X` be étale, with cartesian squares `Z_U = U ×_X Z` and
`Z_{U'} = U' ×_X Z`.  Let `ψ : U' ⟶ U` be a morphism over `X` and `q : Z_{U'} ⟶ Z_U` the
induced morphism, so that `q ≫ p = p'` and `q ≫ i_U = i_{U'} ≫ ψ`.  Then the identification
`𝒞_{Z/X,*}|_{Z_{U'}} ≅ 𝒞_{Z_{U'}/U',*}` of Stacks 09RR along `φ'` is the identification
along `φ`, restricted along `q`, followed by the identification along `ψ`:

`p'^*𝒞_{Z/X,*} ≅ q^*p^*𝒞_{Z/X,*} ≅ q^*𝒞_{Z_U/U,*} ≅ 𝒞_{Z_{U'}/U',*}`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalAlgebraEtaleRestrictionIso_comp (p : ZU ⟶ Z) (iU : ZU ⟶ U) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (φ : U ⟶ X) (sq : IsPullback p iU i φ) (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) (p' : ZU' ⟶ Z)
    (iU' : ZU' ⟶ U') (φ' : U' ⟶ X) (sq' : IsPullback p' iU' i φ')
    (hφ' : IsEtale B S hS φ'.hom) (ψ : U' ⟶ U) (hψφ : ψ ≫ φ = φ') (q : ZU' ⟶ ZU)
    (hqp : q ≫ p = p') (hqi : q ≫ iU = iU' ≫ ψ) :
    conormalAlgebraEtaleRestrictionIso B S hS p' iU' i φ' sq' hφ' =
      (gradedAlgebraPullbackCompIsoOfEq B S hS q p p' hqp.symm).app (conormalAlgebra B S hS i) ≪≫
        (gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS ZU') (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS ZU)
            (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS q)).mapIso
          (conormalAlgebraEtaleRestrictionIso B S hS p iU i φ sq hφ) ≪≫
        conormalAlgebraEtaleRestrictionIso B S hS q iU' iU ψ
          (isPullback_of_comp_eq B S hS sq sq' ψ hψφ q hqp hqi)
          (isEtale_of_comp_eq B S hS ψ hφ hφ' hψφ)
declarations.comment: functoriality in U of the identification of conormal algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersionEtaleRestrictionIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RR, for the conormal algebra of an immersion as defined in Stacks 09RN.**  Let
`i : Z ⟶ X` be an immersion of algebraic spaces, let `φ : U ⟶ X` be étale and let
`Z_U = U ×_X Z`, with projections `p : Z_U ⟶ Z` and `i_U : Z_U ⟶ U`; then `i_U` is an
immersion and

`𝒞_{Z/X,*}|_{Z_U} = p^*𝒞_{Z/X,*} ≅ 𝒞_{Z_U/U,*}`

as sheaves of graded `𝒪_{Z_U}`-algebras, where both conormal algebras are those of Stacks 09RN,
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersion`.

It is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraEtaleRestrictionIso` read through the
identification `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraIsoConormalAlgebraOfImmersion` on both
sides.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebraOfImmersionEtaleRestrictionIso (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z₀) (i : Z₀ ⟶ X₀) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i)
    {U ZU : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (p : ZU ⟶ ⟨Z₀, hZ⟩) (iU : ZU ⟶ U) (φ : U ⟶ ⟨X₀, hX⟩)
    (sq : IsPullback p iU
      (ObjectProperty.homMk i : (⟨Z₀, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ ⟨X₀, hX⟩) φ)
    (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) :
    (gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS ZU)
        (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS ⟨Z₀, hZ⟩) (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS p)).obj
        (conormalAlgebraOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi) ≅
      conormalAlgebraOfImmersion B S hS U.2 ZU.2 iU.hom (isImmersion_of_isPullback B S hS sq hi)
declarations.comment: the conormal algebra of an immersion, restricted to an etale U, as graded algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersionEtaleRestrictionIso_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RR, functoriality in `U`, for the conormal algebra of an immersion as defined in
Stacks 09RN.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be an immersion and let `φ : U ⟶ X`, `φ' : U' ⟶ X` be étale, with
cartesian squares `Z_U = U ×_X Z` and `Z_{U'} = U' ×_X Z`.  Let `ψ : U' ⟶ U` be a morphism over
`X` and `q : Z_{U'} ⟶ Z_U` the induced morphism, so that `q ≫ p = p'` and `q ≫ i_U = i_{U'} ≫ ψ`.
Then the identification `𝒞_{Z/X,*}|_{Z_{U'}} ≅ 𝒞_{Z_{U'}/U',*}` along `φ'` is the identification
along `φ`, restricted along `q`, followed by the identification along `ψ` for the immersion
`i_U`.
declarations.statement:
theorem conormalAlgebraOfImmersionEtaleRestrictionIso_comp (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z₀) (i : Z₀ ⟶ X₀) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i)
    {U ZU U' ZU' : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS} (p : ZU ⟶ ⟨Z₀, hZ⟩) (iU : ZU ⟶ U)
    (φ : U ⟶ ⟨X₀, hX⟩)
    (sq : IsPullback p iU
      (ObjectProperty.homMk i : (⟨Z₀, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ ⟨X₀, hX⟩) φ)
    (hφ : IsEtale B S hS φ.hom) (p' : ZU' ⟶ ⟨Z₀, hZ⟩) (iU' : ZU' ⟶ U') (φ' : U' ⟶ ⟨X₀, hX⟩)
    (sq' : IsPullback p' iU'
      (ObjectProperty.homMk i : (⟨Z₀, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS) ⟶ ⟨X₀, hX⟩) φ')
    (hφ' : IsEtale B S hS φ'.hom) (ψ : U' ⟶ U) (hψφ : ψ ≫ φ = φ') (q : ZU' ⟶ ZU)
    (hqp : q ≫ p = p') (hqi : q ≫ iU = iU' ≫ ψ) :
    conormalAlgebraOfImmersionEtaleRestrictionIso B S hS hX hZ i hi p' iU' φ' sq' hφ' =
      (gradedAlgebraPullbackCompIsoOfEq B S hS q p p' hqp.symm).app
          (conormalAlgebraOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi) ≪≫
        (gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS ZU') (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS ZU)
            (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS q)).mapIso
          (conormalAlgebraOfImmersionEtaleRestrictionIso B S hS hX hZ i hi p iU φ sq hφ) ≪≫
        conormalAlgebraOfImmersionEtaleRestrictionIso B S hS U.2 ZU.2 iU.hom
          (isImmersion_of_isPullback B S hS sq hi) q iU' ψ
          (isPullback_of_comp_eq B S hS sq sq' ψ hψφ q hqp hqi)
          (isEtale_of_comp_eq B S hS ψ hφ hφ' hψφ)
declarations.comment: functoriality in U, for the conormal algebra of an immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersionSquareMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 09RS] for a square of immersions, on the conormal algebras of
[Stacks Project, Tag 09RN].**  Let

```
Z --i--→ X
|        |
f        g
↓        ↓
Z' -i'-→ X'
```

be a commutative square of algebraic spaces over `S` with `i` and `i'` immersions.  There is a
canonical homomorphism of sheaves of graded `𝒪_Z`-algebras

`f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}`,

where `𝒞_{Z/X,*}` is the conormal algebra of the immersion `i`, that is of its closed
factorisation `i₀ : Z ⟶ X ∖ ∂Z` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersion`), and
likewise for `i'`.

It is the inverse image along `f` of the inverse of the isomorphism
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersionIso` for `i'`, then the composition
comparison `f^*𝟙^* ≅ f^*`, then the canonical map
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraSquareMap` of the commutative square with edges `i₀`,
`ι ≫ g`, `f` and `i'`; the last is built from `g^♯` exactly as in the source's proof.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebraOfImmersionSquareMap (i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳) (i' : 𝒵' ⟶ 𝒳')
    (f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒵') (g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳') (hsq : i ≫ g = f ≫ i') (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (hi' : IsImmersion B S hS i'.hom) :
    (gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS 𝒵) (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS 𝒵')
        (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f)).obj
        (conormalAlgebraOfImmersion B S hS hX' hZ' i'.hom hi') ⟶
      conormalAlgebraOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i.hom hi
declarations.comment: the canonical map f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*} for immersions i, i', on the conormal algebras of immersions of Tag 09RN

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraSquareMapOfPullbackHom
declarations.doc:
**The canonical map of conormal algebras of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RS], given the ambient
graded homomorphism.**  Let

```
Z --i--→ X
|        |
f        g
↓        ↓
Z' -i'-→ X'
```

be a commutative square of algebraic spaces, `hsq : i ≫ g = f ≫ i'`.  Write
`𝓘 = Ker(i^♯) ⊆ 𝒪_X` and `𝓙 = Ker((f ≫ i')^♯) ⊆ 𝒪_{X'}` for the kernel ideal sheaf of the
diagonal.  Given a homomorphism of sheaves of graded `𝒪_X`-algebras

`Ψ : g^*(⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝓙ⁿ) ⟶ ⨁_{n ≥ 0} 𝓘ⁿ`

on the ambient space, there is a canonical homomorphism of sheaves of graded `𝒪_Z`-algebras

`f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}`.

It is the composite of the two factors of the source's proof: the unconditional first factor
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraPullbackCompMap`, which carries `f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*}` into the
conormal algebra `𝒞_{Z/X',*}` of the diagonal and rests on the containment of kernel ideal
sheaves `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.kernelIdealSheaf_le_comp`, followed by the ambient factor
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraAmbientSquareMapOfPullbackHom`, which descends `Ψ` from
`X` to `Z` along the Stacks 03LU composition comparison.

`Ψ` is a hypothesis and not the conclusion: it is a homomorphism upstairs on the ambient space
`X` between the graded algebras of the powers of the two kernel ideal sheaves, whereas the
conclusion is a homomorphism downstairs on `Z` between the conormal algebras of the two vertical
arrows.  The module documentation of
`StacksFrontier/AlgebraicGeometry/Spaces/ConormalAlgebraAmbientGradedTransport.lean` records that no
such `Ψ` is constructed yet and what its construction is waiting for.

The statement takes `i` and `i'` to be arbitrary morphisms, where Stacks 09RS takes them to be
immersions; nothing here uses any property of them, so this is strictly more general and
specialises to the source's statement.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebraSquareMapOfPullbackHom (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') (f : Z ⟶ Z')
    (g : X ⟶ X') (hsq : i ≫ g = f ≫ i')
    (Ψ : (gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X)
          (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X') (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS g)).obj
        (kernelIdealGradedAlgebra B S hS (f ≫ i')) ⟶ kernelIdealGradedAlgebra B S hS i) :
    (gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS Z)
        (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS Z')
        (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f)).obj (conormalAlgebra B S hS i') ⟶
      conormalAlgebra B S hS i
declarations.comment: the canonical map, given the ambient homomorphism g^*(⨁ 𝓙ⁿ) ⟶ ⨁ 𝓘ⁿ

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraSquareMap
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 09RS]: the canonical map of conormal algebras of a commutative
square.**  Let

```
Z --i--→ X
|        |
f        g
↓        ↓
Z' -i'-→ X'
```

be a commutative square of algebraic spaces over `S`, `hsq : i ≫ g = f ≫ i'`.  There is a
canonical homomorphism of sheaves of graded `𝒪_Z`-algebras

`f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}`.

It is `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraSquareMapOfPullbackHom` at the ambient
homomorphism `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.kernelIdealGradedPullbackHom : g^*(⨁ 𝓙ⁿ) ⟶ ⨁ 𝓘ⁿ` induced
by `g^♯`, where `𝓘 = Ker(i^♯)` and `𝓙 = Ker((f ≫ i')^♯)`: the first factor
`f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X',*}` comes from the containment `Ker((i')^♯) ⊆ 𝓙`, and the second
factor `𝒞_{Z/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` is the inverse image along `i` of the ambient homomorphism, read
through the Stacks 03LU composition comparison `(f ≫ i')^* ≅ i^* g^*`.  This is the source's
proof: `g^♯` carries `g^{-1}((𝓘')ⁿ)` into `𝓘ⁿ`, and pulling back to `Z`, with
`i^{-1}g^{-1} = f^{-1}(i')^{-1}`, gives the map in each degree.

The statement takes `i` and `i'` to be arbitrary morphisms, where Stacks 09RS takes them to be
immersions; nothing here uses any property of them.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conormalAlgebraSquareMap (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X') (f : Z ⟶ Z')
    (g : X ⟶ X') (hsq : i ≫ g = f ≫ i') :
    (gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS Z)
        (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS Z')
        (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS f)).obj (conormalAlgebra B S hS i') ⟶
      conormalAlgebra B S hS i
declarations.comment: the canonical map f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*} of graded algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalAlgebraOfImmersionSquareMap_app_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 09RT], surjectivity, on the conormal algebras of immersions.**  Let

```
Z --i--→ X
|        |
f        g
↓        ↓
Z' -i'-→ X'
```

be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces with `i` and `i'` immersions.  Then the canonical map
`f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RS] between the conormal algebras of the
immersions of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RN]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersionSquareMap`) is surjective: it is an
epimorphism of `𝒪_Z`-modules in every degree.

The map is two isomorphisms followed by the canonical map of the square of the closed
factorisation of `i`, which is cartesian
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_immersionClosedFactorization_comp`), so that
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalAlgebraSquareMap_app_of_isPullback` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_conormalAlgebraOfImmersionSquareMap_app_of_isPullback {i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳} {i' : 𝒵' ⟶ 𝒳'}
    {f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒵'} {g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'} (sq : IsPullback i f g i') (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom)
    (hi' : IsImmersion B S hS i'.hom) (n : ℤ) :
    Epi ((conormalAlgebraOfImmersionSquareMap B S hS hZ hX hZ' hX' i i' f g sq.w hi hi').app
      n)
declarations.comment: surjectivity: for a cartesian square with i, i' immersions, the canonical map f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*} of Tag 09RS on the conormal algebras of immersions of Tag 09RN is surjective in every degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_conormalAlgebraOfImmersionSquareMap_of_isPullback_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 09RT], the flat case, on the conormal algebras of immersions.**  Let

```
Z --i--→ X
|        |
f        g
↓        ↓
Z' -i'-→ X'
```

be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces with `i` and `i'` immersions.  If `g` is flat, the
canonical map `f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RS] between the conormal
algebras of the immersions of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RN]
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.conormalAlgebraOfImmersionSquareMap`) is an isomorphism of sheaves of
graded `𝒪_Z`-algebras.

The map is two isomorphisms followed by the canonical map of the square of the closed
factorisation of `i`, which is cartesian
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isPullback_immersionClosedFactorization_comp`) with flat right edge
`ι ≫ g` (an open immersion is étale, hence flat, and flatness composes), so that
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_conormalAlgebraSquareMap_of_isPullback_of_isFlat` applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_conormalAlgebraOfImmersionSquareMap_of_isPullback_of_isFlat {i : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒳}
    {i' : 𝒵' ⟶ 𝒳'} {f : 𝒵 ⟶ 𝒵'} {g : 𝒳 ⟶ 𝒳'} (sq : IsPullback i f g i')
    (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i.hom) (hi' : IsImmersion B S hS i'.hom)
    (hg : IsFlat B S hS g.hom) :
    IsIso (conormalAlgebraOfImmersionSquareMap B S hS hZ hX hZ' hX' i i' f g sq.w hi hi')
declarations.comment: flat case: for a cartesian square with i, i' immersions and g flat, the canonical map f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*} of Tag 09RS on the conormal algebras of immersions of Tag 09RN is an isomorphism of graded algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalAlgebraSquareMap_app_of_isPullback
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 09RT], surjectivity.**  Let

```
Z --i--→ X
|        |
f        g
↓        ↓
Z' -i'-→ X'
```

be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces with `i'` (hence `i`) an immersion.  Then the canonical
map `f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RS] is surjective: it is an
epimorphism of `𝒪_Z`-modules in every degree.

In degree `n ≥ 0` the map is the inverse image along `i` of the degree-`n` ambient comparison,
preceded by two isomorphisms; that comparison is induced by pullback of regular functions
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isInducedByPullback_conormalAlgebraSquareAmbientComparison_app`), so its
inverse image along `i` is an epimorphism by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_modulePullback_map_of_isPullback`.  In negative degrees the target
vanishes.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_conormalAlgebraSquareMap_app_of_isPullback (sq : IsPullback i f g i')
    (hi' : IsImmersion B S hS i'.hom) (n : ℤ) :
    Epi ((conormalAlgebraSquareMap B S hS i i' f g sq.w).app n)
declarations.comment: surjectivity: for a cartesian square with i' (hence i) an immersion, the canonical map f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*} of Tag 09RS is surjective in every degree

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_conormalAlgebraSquareMap_of_isPullback_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 09RT], the flat case.**  Let

```
Z --i--→ X
|        |
f        g
↓        ↓
Z' -i'-→ X'
```

be a cartesian square of algebraic spaces with `i'` (hence `i`) an immersion.  If `g` is flat,
the canonical map `f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RS] is an isomorphism
of sheaves of graded `𝒪_Z`-algebras.

Degreewise this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_conormalAlgebraSquareMap_app_of_isPullback_of_isFlat`, whose
nonnegative degrees are `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_modulePullback_map_of_isPullback_of_isFlat`
for the ambient comparison; a degreewise isomorphism of sheaves of graded algebras is an
isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_conormalAlgebraSquareMap_of_isPullback_of_isFlat (sq : IsPullback i f g i')
    (hi' : IsImmersion B S hS i'.hom) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g.hom) :
    IsIso (conormalAlgebraSquareMap B S hS i i' f g sq.w)
declarations.comment: flat case: for a cartesian square with i' (hence i) an immersion and g flat, the canonical map f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*} of Tag 09RS is an isomorphism of graded algebras

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalAlgebraSquareMapOfPullbackHom_app_of_nonneg
declarations.doc:
**The surjectivity clause of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RT].**  The canonical map
`f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RS] is surjective in every nonnegative
degree.

The ambient comparison is surjective in every nonnegative degree by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_conormalAlgebraSquareAmbientComparison_app_of_nonneg`, and the
canonical map is in each degree the inverse image along `i` of the ambient comparison preceded by
two isomorphisms.

Three inputs are carried: that the ambient comparison carries the unit, and its surjectivity in
the degrees zero and one — the conclusions of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_structureSheafMap` and of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.epi_idealSheafMap`, the ideal-sheaf form of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04CQ]'s surjectivity clause, transported to this square.  The square being
cartesian is therefore not consumed, and neither is either vertical arrow being an immersion.
What is proved is that the three suffice: surjectivity propagates from the degrees zero and one
to every degree.  The module documentation says why none of the three is available in the
library, and why carrying the degree-one one is carrying 04CQ's conclusion and not this tag's.
declarations.statement:
theorem epi_conormalAlgebraSquareMapOfPullbackHom_app_of_nonneg (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X')
    (f : Z ⟶ Z') (g : X ⟶ X') (hsq : i ≫ g = f ≫ i')
    (Ψ : (gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X)
          (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X') (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS g)).obj
        (kernelIdealGradedAlgebra B S hS (f ≫ i')) ⟶ kernelIdealGradedAlgebra B S hS i)
    (hunit : SheafOfModules.sectionsMap
        ((conormalAlgebraSquareAmbientComparison B S hS i i' f g Ψ).app 0)
        ((gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X)
            (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X')
            (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS g)).obj
          (kernelIdealGradedAlgebra B S hS i')).one =
      (kernelIdealGradedAlgebra B S hS i).one)
    (h0 : Epi ((conormalAlgebraSquareAmbientComparison B S hS i i' f g Ψ).app 0))
    (h1 : Epi ((conormalAlgebraSquareAmbientComparison B S hS i i' f g Ψ).app 1))
    (n : ℤ) (hn : 0 ≤ n) :
    Epi ((conormalAlgebraSquareMapOfPullbackHom B S hS i i' f g hsq Ψ).app n)
declarations.comment: the surjectivity clause, in every nonnegative degree; the cartesian hypothesis is NOT consumed, three inputs being carried: hunit, h0 and h1, the degree-one one being Tag 04CQ's surjectivity clause in ideal-sheaf form transported to this square; the flat clause is isIso_conormalAlgebraSquareMapOfPullbackHom_app_of_isFlat

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_conormalAlgebraSquareMapOfPullbackHom_app_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**The flat clause of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RT].**  If `g` is flat — that is, if the morphism
of small étale ringed topoi it induces is flat in the sense of [Stacks Project, Tag 04JB] — then
the canonical map `f^*𝒞_{Z'/X',*} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of [Stacks Project, Tag 09RS] is an isomorphism in
every nonnegative degree.
