Flatness is consumed in the injectivity half, through the exactness of the inverse image along a
flat morphism.  Four inputs are carried: that the ambient comparison carries the unit, its
invertibility in the degrees zero and one — the conclusions of
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_structureSheafMap` and of the flat half of
[Stacks Project, Tag 04CQ], `AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isIso_idealSheafMap_of_isFlat`, transported
to this square — and the compatibility of the comparison with the embeddings of the powers of the
two ideal sheaves into the two structure sheaves, whose degree-one instance is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.idealSheafMap_comp_ι`.  The square being cartesian is therefore not
consumed, and neither is either vertical arrow being an immersion.  What is proved is that the
four suffice: surjectivity and injectivity propagate from the degrees zero and one to every
degree.  The module documentation says why none of the four is available in the library.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_conormalAlgebraSquareMapOfPullbackHom_app_of_isFlat (i : Z ⟶ X) (i' : Z' ⟶ X')
    (f : Z ⟶ Z') (g : X ⟶ X') (hsq : i ≫ g = f ≫ i')
    (Ψ : (gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X)
          (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X') (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS g)).obj
        (kernelIdealGradedAlgebra B S hS (f ≫ i')) ⟶ kernelIdealGradedAlgebra B S hS i)
    (hg : (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS g).IsFlat)
    (hunit : SheafOfModules.sectionsMap
        ((conormalAlgebraSquareAmbientComparison B S hS i i' f g Ψ).app 0)
        ((gradedPull (X := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X)
            (Y := smallEtaleRingedTopos B S hS X')
            (smallEtaleRingedToposHom B S hS g)).obj
          (kernelIdealGradedAlgebra B S hS i')).one =
      (kernelIdealGradedAlgebra B S hS i).one)
    (h0 : IsIso ((conormalAlgebraSquareAmbientComparison B S hS i i' f g Ψ).app 0))
    (h1 : IsIso ((conormalAlgebraSquareAmbientComparison B S hS i i' f g Ψ).app 1))
    (hι : ∀ n : ℤ, 0 ≤ n →
      (conormalAlgebraSquareAmbientComparison B S hS i i' f g Ψ).app n ≫
          (kernelIdealSheafZPow B S hS i n).ι =
        (modulePullback B S hS g).map (kernelIdealSheafZPow B S hS i' n).ι ≫
          structureSheafMap B S hS g)
    (n : ℤ) (hn : 0 ≤ n) :
    IsIso ((conormalAlgebraSquareMapOfPullbackHom B S hS i i' f g hsq Ψ).app n)
declarations.comment: the flat clause: an isomorphism in every nonnegative degree when g is flat, flatness consumed through exactness of the inverse image; the cartesian hypothesis is NOT consumed, four inputs being carried: hunit, h0, h1 (Tag 04CQ's flat half transported) and hiota (the n-th power analogue of idealSheafMap_comp_ι); see the module docs

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.immersionNormalCone
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09RU.  The normal cone `C_ZX = \underline{Spec}_Z(𝒞_{Z/X,*})` of an
immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces**, as an algebraic space affine over `Z`: the relative
spectrum (Stacks 081W) of the conormal algebra of Stacks 09RN.  Its structure morphism is affine
(this is the `AffineOver` property) and the direct image of its structure sheaf is `𝒞_{Z/X,*}`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.immersionNormalConePushforwardIso`).
declarations.comment: the normal cone C_ZX = Spec_Z(C_{Z/X,*}) of an immersion, as an algebraic space affine over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.immersionNormalConePushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09RU.  `C_ZX` is the relative spectrum of `𝒞_{Z/X,*}`**: for its
projection `π : C_ZX ⟶ Z`, `π_* 𝒪_{C_ZX} ≅ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` as sheaves of commutative
`𝒪_Z`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
def immersionNormalConePushforwardIso (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z₀) (i : Z₀ ⟶ X₀) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (immersionNormalCone B S hS hX hZ i hi).obj ≅
      conormalAlgebraSheafOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi
declarations.comment: the direct image of the structure sheaf of the normal cone C_ZX is the conormal algebra C_{Z/X,*}, i.e. C_ZX = Spec_Z(C_{Z/X,*})

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.immersionNormalBundle
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09RU.  The normal bundle `N_ZX = \underline{Spec}_Z(Sym(𝒞_{Z/X}))` of
an immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces**, as an algebraic space affine over `Z`: the
relative spectrum (Stacks 081W) of the symmetric algebra on the conormal sheaf `𝒞_{Z/X}` of
Stacks 04CN.  Its structure morphism is affine and the direct image of its structure sheaf is
`Sym(𝒞_{Z/X})` (`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.immersionNormalBundlePushforwardIso`).
declarations.comment: the normal bundle N_ZX = Spec_Z(Sym(C_{Z/X})) of an immersion, as an algebraic space affine over Z

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.immersionNormalBundlePushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09RU.  `N_ZX` is the relative spectrum of `Sym(𝒞_{Z/X})`**: for its
projection `π : N_ZX ⟶ Z`, `π_* 𝒪_{N_ZX} ≅ Sym(𝒞_{Z/X})` as sheaves of commutative
`𝒪_Z`-algebras.
declarations.statement:
def immersionNormalBundlePushforwardIso (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z₀) (i : Z₀ ⟶ X₀) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    pushforwardAlgebra B S hS (immersionNormalBundle B S hS hX hZ i hi).obj ≅
      conormalSymmetricAlgebraSheafOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi
declarations.comment: the direct image of the structure sheaf of the normal bundle N_ZX is Sym(C_{Z/X}), i.e. N_ZX = Spec_Z(Sym(C_{Z/X}))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isKoszulRegularImmersion_tfae
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 09RW.**  For an immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` into a locally Noetherian
algebraic space, Koszul-regularity, `H₁`-regularity and quasi-regularity agree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_tfae (_hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ X) (_hi : IsImmersion B S hS i)
    (hnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS i,
        IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS i,
        IsQuasiRegularImmersion B S hS i]

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isKoszulRegularImmersion_pullback_snd_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RX, the Koszul-regular clause.** The base change `Z ×_X X' ⟶ X'` of a
Koszul-regular immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` along a flat morphism
`g : X' ⟶ X` is a Koszul-regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_pullback_snd_of_isFlat (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {Z X X' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ X) (g : X' ⟶ X) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hi : IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS i) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd i g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isH1RegularImmersion_pullback_snd_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RX, the `H₁`-regular clause.** The base change `Z ×_X X' ⟶ X'` of an
`H₁`-regular immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` along a flat morphism
`g : X' ⟶ X` is an `H₁`-regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_pullback_snd_of_isFlat (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {Z X X' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ X) (g : X' ⟶ X) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hi : IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS i) :
    IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd i g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiRegularImmersion_pullback_snd_of_isFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RX, the quasi-regular clause.** The base change `Z ×_X X' ⟶ X'` of a
quasi-regular immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces over `S` along a flat morphism
`g : X' ⟶ X` is a quasi-regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_pullback_snd_of_isFlat (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u})
    (hS : B.Contains S) {Z X X' : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ X) (g : X' ⟶ X) (hg : IsFlat B S hS g)
    (hi : IsQuasiRegularImmersion B S hS i) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion B S hS (pullback.snd i g)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiRegularImmersion_iff_conormal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09RY.**  An immersion `i : Z ⟶ X` of algebraic spaces is a
quasi-regular immersion if and only if (1) it is locally of finite presentation, (2) its conormal
sheaf `𝒞_{Z/X}` is finite locally free, and (3) the canonical map
`Sym^*(𝒞_{Z/X}) ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X,*}` of Stacks 09RQ is an isomorphism in every degree, for every
symmetric algebra `Sym^*(𝒞_{Z/X})` on the conormal sheaf.

The proof reduces to the closed factorisation `Z ⟶ X ∖ ∂Z` of Stacks 04CE and its base changes to
the étale charts of `X ∖ ∂Z`, where the case of schemes, Stacks 063M, is run on the sections of
the conormal algebra over affine charts; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_iff_conormal (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X₀)
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z₀) (i : Z₀ ⟶ X₀) (hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion B S hS i ↔
      IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS i ∧
        SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOnSite (conormalModuleOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi) ∧
        ∀ (A : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.{u, u}
            (structureRingSheaf B S hS (⟨Z₀, hZ⟩ : AlgebraicSpaces B S hS)))
          (ι : (conormalAlgebraOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi).piece 1 ⟶ A.piece 1)
          (hA : SheafOfModules.GradedAlgebra.IsSymmetricAlgebra A ι) (n : ℤ),
          IsIso ((symmetricAlgebraToConormalAlgebraOfImmersion B S hS hX hZ i hi A ι hA).app
            n)
declarations.comment: the whole statement: an immersion of algebraic spaces is quasi-regular iff it is locally of finite presentation, its conormal sheaf is finite locally free, and the map of 09RQ from the symmetric algebra on the conormal sheaf is an isomorphism in every degree, for every symmetric algebra

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isQuasiRegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09RY, condition (1) in the direction out of quasi-regularity.** A quasi-regular
immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` is locally of finite presentation.

Each represented base change of `i` to an étale scheme chart of the target is a quasi-regular
immersion of schemes, hence locally of finite presentation by the case of schemes
[Stacks, Tag 063M]; local finite presentation is étale local on the source and target
[Stacks, Tag 04R3], so those chart conditions are the local finite presentation of `i`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isLocallyOfFinitePresentation_of_isQuasiRegularImmersion
    (B : BigFppfSite.{u}) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : B.Contains S)
    {Z X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ X)
    (_hIm : IsImmersion B S hS i) (h : IsQuasiRegularImmersion B S hS i) :
    IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS i
declarations.comment: the direction out of quasi-regularity, condition (1) only: a quasi-regular immersion of algebraic spaces is locally of finite presentation. Conditions (2) and (3) and the converse are not transported, because the case of schemes, Tag 063M, is itself carried only as conditions (1) and (2) out of quasi-regularity

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isSplitExactConormalSequenceOnEtaleCharts_of_isH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**[Stacks Project, Tag 09RZ].**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be morphisms of algebraic
spaces over `S` with `j` an immersion and `i` an `H₁`-regular immersion.  Then the conormal
sequence `0 ⟶ i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0` of [Stacks Project, Tag 06BD] is exact and
locally split, read on the étale scheme charts of `X`:  over every such chart the base changes of
`j` and of `i` are immersions of schemes whose conormal sequence is short exact and splits on a
neighbourhood of every point.

Over a chart `c` of `X` the pair of scheme immersions is the base change of `j` to `c` together
with the base change of `i` to the chart of `Y` that `j` pulls back from `c`.  That chart of `Y`
is étale, because étaleness of a morphism of presheaves is stable under base change, so
`H₁`-regularity of `i` gives it for the base change of `i`; the case of schemes,
[Stacks Project, Tag 063N] in the bundled form
`Stacks.AlgebraicGeometry.isSplitExactConormalSequence_of_isH1RegularImmersion`, then applies.

This is the hypothesis of the three clauses of [Stacks Project, Tag 09S1]; see
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isH1RegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence` and its
siblings.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSplitExactConormalSequenceOnEtaleCharts_of_isH1RegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    (hj : IsImmersion B S hS j) (hi : IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS i) :
    IsSplitExactConormalSequenceOnEtaleCharts B S hS i j
declarations.comment: both conclusions — exactness and local splitness — of the conormal sequence of Tag 06BD for an H₁-regular immersion, read on the étale scheme charts of X as `IsSplitExactConormalSequenceOnEtaleCharts`, which is how this development states every condition on algebraic spaces whose scheme analogue it localizes. The sequence has no left-hand map as a sequence of modules on Z in this development, so nothing is asserted about it on Z itself; the splitting is étale-local, Zariski-local on each chart of an étale cover, and is neither global nor claimed on a single chart

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isKoszulRegularImmersion_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S0, the Koszul-regular case.**  The composite of two Koszul-regular immersions of
algebraic spaces over `S` is a Koszul-regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_comp (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS i) (hj : IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS j) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS (i ≫ j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isH1RegularImmersion_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S0, the `H₁`-regular case.**  The composite of two `H₁`-regular immersions of
algebraic spaces over `S` is an `H₁`-regular immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_comp (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS i) (hj : IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS j) :
    IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS (i ≫ j)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiRegularImmersion_comp_of_isH1RegularImmersion
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S0, the mixed case.**  The composite of an `H₁`-regular immersion of algebraic
spaces over `S` and a quasi-regular immersion of algebraic spaces over `S` is a quasi-regular
immersion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_comp_of_isH1RegularImmersion (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    (hi : IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS i) (hj : IsQuasiRegularImmersion B S hS j) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion B S hS (i ≫ j)
declarations.comment: composition of an H₁-regular and a quasi-regular immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 09S1, clause (1).**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be representable morphisms
of algebraic spaces over `S` with `j` locally of finite presentation and with the conormal
sequence of Stacks tag 06BD exact and locally split on the étale charts of `X`.  If `i ≫ j` is a
quasi-regular immersion, so is `i`.

The sibling clauses are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isH1RegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence`, clause
(2) for `H₁`-regularity, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence`,
clause (3) for Koszul-regularity.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    (hjfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS j)
    (hcon : IsSplitExactConormalSequenceOnEtaleCharts B S hS i j)
    (hij : IsQuasiRegularImmersion B S hS (i ≫ j)) :
    IsQuasiRegularImmersion B S hS i
declarations.comment: (1) quasi-regularity descends to the first immersion, with the conormal hypothesis read on the étale charts of X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isH1RegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 09S1, clause (2).**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be representable morphisms
of algebraic spaces over `S` with `j` locally of finite presentation and with the conormal
sequence of Stacks tag 06BD exact and locally split on the étale charts of `X`.  If `i ≫ j` is an
`H₁`-regular immersion, so is `i`.

The sibling clauses are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence`, clause
(1) for quasi-regularity, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence`,
clause (3) for Koszul-regularity.
declarations.statement:
theorem isH1RegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    (hjfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS j)
    (hcon : IsSplitExactConormalSequenceOnEtaleCharts B S hS i j)
    (hij : IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS (i ≫ j)) :
    IsH1RegularImmersion B S hS i
declarations.comment: (2) H₁-regularity descends to the first immersion, with the conormal hypothesis read on the étale charts of X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 09S1, clause (3).**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be representable morphisms
of algebraic spaces over `S` with `j` locally of finite presentation and with the conormal
sequence of Stacks tag 06BD exact and locally split on the étale charts of `X`.  If both `j` and
`i ≫ j` are Koszul-regular immersions, so is `i`.

The sibling clauses are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isQuasiRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence`, clause
(1) for quasi-regularity, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isH1RegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence`, clause
(2) for `H₁`-regularity.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_of_comp_of_isSplitExactConormalSequence
    (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z) (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    (hjfp : IsLocallyOfFinitePresentation B S hS j)
    (hcon : IsSplitExactConormalSequenceOnEtaleCharts B S hS i j)
    (hj : IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS j)
    (hij : IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS (i ≫ j)) :
    IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS i
declarations.comment: (3) Koszul-regularity of the first immersion, with the conormal hypothesis read on the étale charts of X

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.isKoszulRegularImmersion_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian
declarations.doc:
**Stacks tag 09S2.**  Let `i : Z ⟶ Y` and `j : Y ⟶ X` be immersions of algebraic spaces over
a scheme `S` with `X` locally Noetherian.  Then the following are equivalent:

1. `i` is a Koszul-regular immersion and `j` is a Koszul-regular immersion near the image of `i`,
2. `i` and `i ≫ j` are Koszul-regular immersions,
3. `i ≫ j` is a Koszul-regular immersion and the conormal sequence
   `0 ⟶ i^* 𝒞_{Y/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/X} ⟶ 𝒞_{Z/Y} ⟶ 0` of Stacks tag 06BD is exact and locally split.

Conditions (1) and (3) are read on the étale scheme charts of `X`, as every condition on
algebraic spaces whose scheme analogue this development localizes.  The second clause of
condition (1) is Koszul-regularity of `j` on a neighbourhood of the image of `i`, not on all of
`Y`:  the source states it on all of `Y`, which is false, and the module documentation gives the
counterexample and the reason the cited scheme-level Stacks tag 0690 is itself pointwise.
declarations.statement:
theorem isKoszulRegularImmersion_tfae_of_isLocallyNoetherian (hZ : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Z)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X) (i : Z ⟶ Y) (j : Y ⟶ X)
    (_hi : IsImmersion B S hS i) (hj : IsImmersion B S hS j)
    (hnoeth : HasEtaleLocalProperty B S hS X (fun T : Scheme.{u} => IsLocallyNoetherian T)) :
    List.TFAE
      [IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS i ∧
          IsKoszulRegularImmersionNearImageOnEtaleCharts B S hS i j,
        IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS i ∧ IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS (i ≫ j),
        IsKoszulRegularImmersion B S hS (i ≫ j) ∧
          IsSplitExactConormalSequenceOnEtaleCharts B S hS i j]
declarations.comment: all three conditions, with the second clause of condition (1) — Koszul-regularity of j — localized to a neighbourhood of the image of i and read on the étale charts of X. The source states that clause on all of Y, which is false: for Z empty, conditions (2) and (3) hold for every j, while j need not be Koszul-regular. The localized clause is what the cited scheme-level Tag 0690 proves, that tag being stated at a point of Z

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorNatTrans
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S3**, the morphism of functors. A homomorphism `f : N ⟶ N'` of differential graded
`(A, B)`-bimodules induces `1 ⊗ f : - ⊗_A^𝐋 N ⟶ - ⊗_A^𝐋 N'`, a natural transformation of the
derived tensor functors of Tag 09LS on `D(A, d)`.

It is the descent of `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.ordinaryTensorNatTrans` along the localization:
`- ⊗_A^𝐋 N'` is a right Kan extension of ordinary tensoring with `N'`, so the transformation is
the unique one compatible with the two comparisons of Tag 09LS
(`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorNatTrans_counit`).
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorNatTrans {N N' : Bimodule A B} (f : N ⟶ N') :
    derivedTensorFunctor N ⟶ derivedTensorFunctor N'

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_derivedTensorNatTrans_app_shift_regularModule
declarations.doc:
**Clause (3) of the dévissage of Stacks 0FQE for `1 ⊗ f`**: for a homomorphism `f : N ⟶ N'` of
differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodules which is a quasi-isomorphism of right differential graded
`B`-modules, the transformation `1 ⊗ f : - ⊗_A^𝐋 N ⟶ - ⊗_A^𝐋 N'` is invertible at the class of
every shift `A[k]` of the regular module.

The shift `A[k]` is orthogonal on the left to the acyclic modules by Tag 09K1, so both comparisons
of Tag 09LS are invertible there and `1 ⊗ f` becomes the ordinary map `A[k] ⊗_A N ⟶ A[k] ⊗_A N'`,
which is the quasi-isomorphism `f[k]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorNatTrans_app_shift_regularModule {N N' : Bimodule A B} (f : N ⟶ N')
    (hf : QuasiIso ((forgetToCochainComplex B).map f.rightHom)) (k : ℤ) :
    IsIso ((derivedTensorNatTrans f).app
      (((toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj (regularModule A))⟦k⟧))
declarations.comment: the second assertion at the shifts A[k] of the algebra, where the quasi-isomorphism hypothesis enters

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_derivedTensorNatTrans_app_sigma
declarations.doc:
**Clause (1) of the dévissage of Stacks 0FQE for `1 ⊗ f`**: the transformation
`1 ⊗ f : - ⊗_A^𝐋 N ⟶ - ⊗_A^𝐋 N'` is invertible at a direct sum of objects of `D(A, d)` at which it
is invertible.

Both functors are left adjoints by Tag 09LT, hence preserve direct sums, so the component of
`1 ⊗ f` at `⨁ᵢ Kᵢ` is the comparison of the two colimit cocones induced by its components at the
`Kᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorNatTrans_app_sigma {N N' : Bimodule A B} (f : N ⟶ N')
    {ι : Type u} (K : ι → derivedCategory' A)
    (h : ∀ i, IsIso ((derivedTensorNatTrans f).app (K i))) :
    IsIso ((derivedTensorNatTrans f).app (∐ K))
declarations.comment: the second assertion at a direct sum, from the summands

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorTwoOutOfThree
declarations.doc:
**Clause (2) of the dévissage of Stacks 0FQE for the transformations `1 ⊗ f`.** The derived
tensor functors are exact and `1 ⊗ f` commutes with the translation, so its components form a
morphism of distinguished triangles, to which the five lemma of Tag 014A applies.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorTwoOutOfThree (A B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) :
    DerivedTensorTwoOutOfThree A B
declarations.comment: the second assertion along a distinguished triangle, two out of three

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.quasiIsoInvertsDerivedTensor
declarations.doc:
**The second assertion of Stacks 09S3.** A homomorphism `f : N ⟶ N'` of differential graded
`(A, B)`-bimodules that is a quasi-isomorphism of right differential graded `B`-modules induces
an isomorphism `1 ⊗ f : - ⊗_A^𝐋 N ⟶ - ⊗_A^𝐋 N'` of functors `D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem quasiIsoInvertsDerivedTensor (A B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R) :
    QuasiIsoInvertsDerivedTensor A B

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison_of_kFlat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09S4, first conclusion.** *"Let `R` be a ring. Let `(A, d)`, `(B, d)`, and
`(C, d)` be differential graded `R`-algebras. If `C` is K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules, then
(0BZ4) is an isomorphism."*

The map of Tag 0BZ4 is
`DifferentialGraded.derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison`, the canonical map
`(A ⊗_R B)_B ⊗_B^𝐋 {}_B(B ⊗_R C)_C ⟶ (A ⊗_R B ⊗_R C)_C` in `D(C, d)`, and K-flatness is
`CochainComplex.KFlat` (Tag 06XZ) of the complex of `R`-modules underlying `C`.

The source's argument is followed: on underlying complexes, tensoring over `B` with
`{}_B(B ⊗_R C)_C` is tensoring over `R` with `C`, so by Tag 06Y0 it carries quasi-isomorphisms to
quasi-isomorphisms; hence the plain tensor functor already computes the derived one and the
comparison of Tag 09LS is invertible everywhere, in particular at `(A ⊗_R B)_B`, which by
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison_iff` is the assertion.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison_of_kFlat
    (A B C : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R)
    (hC : CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (regularModule C).toCochainComplex) :
    IsIso (derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison A B C)
declarations.comment: the canonical map (0BZ4) is an isomorphism

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfKFlatAlgebra
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09S4, second conclusion.** *"Let `R` be a ring. Let `(A, d)`, `(B, d)`, `(C, d)`
be differential graded `R`-algebras. If `C` is K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules, then (0BZ4) is
an isomorphism and the conclusion of Lemma 0BZ5 is valid."* This is the second half: if `C` is
K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules, then for every differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N` and
every differential graded `(B, C)`-bimodule `N'` the composite of `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N` and `- ⊗_B^𝐋 N'`
is isomorphic to `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N''` for the differential graded `(A, C)`-bimodule
`N'' = Ñ ⊗_B Ñ'` of `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.compTensorResolution`, which is the conclusion
of Tag 0BZ5.

K-flatness of `C` is the only hypothesis, exactly as in the source. The first half of the tag,
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_derivedTensorBaseChangeComparison_of_kFlat`, supplies the sole
hypothesis of Tag 0BZ5 in the form
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfBaseChange`, whose own four inputs are
discharged there by the second assertion of Tag 09S3 twice, Tag 0BZ3 and the dévissage above.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfKFlatAlgebra
    (hC : CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (regularModule C).toCochainComplex)
    (N : Bimodule A B) (N' : Bimodule B C) :
    derivedTensorFunctor N ⋙ derivedTensorFunctor N' ≅
      derivedTensorFunctor (compTensorResolution N N')
declarations.comment: the conclusion of Stacks 0BZ5 is valid when C is K-flat as a complex of R-modules

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence_functor_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
For a homomorphism `φ : A ⟶ B` of differential graded `R`-algebras inducing an isomorphism
on cohomology, the functor `- ⊗_A^𝐋 B : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` of `derivedExtensionEquivalence φ hφ`
is a triangulated functor.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedExtensionEquivalence_functor_isTriangulated (φ : A.Hom B)
    (hφ : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (φ.cohomologyMap k)) :
    (derivedExtensionEquivalence φ hφ).functor.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the equivalence is one of TRIANGULATED categories: exactness of the functor - ⊗_A^𝐋 B : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d), under the source's hypothesis that φ is an isomorphism on cohomology and no other

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence_inverse_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
For a homomorphism `φ : A ⟶ B` of differential graded `R`-algebras inducing an isomorphism
on cohomology, the quasi-inverse `N ↦ N_A` of `derivedExtensionEquivalence φ hφ` is a triangulated
functor.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedExtensionEquivalence_inverse_isTriangulated (φ : A.Hom B)
    (hφ : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (φ.cohomologyMap k)) :
    (derivedExtensionEquivalence φ hφ).inverse.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: the equivalence is one of TRIANGULATED categories: exactness of the quasi-inverse, the restriction functor N ↦ N_A, under the source's hypothesis that φ is an isomorphism on cohomology and no other

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isEquivalence_derivedTensorFunctor_regular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S6**, in the form "`- ⊗_A^𝐋 B` is an equivalence". Let `φ : (A, d) → (B, d)` be a
homomorphism of differential graded algebras over a commutative ring `R` which induces an
isomorphism on cohomology algebras — that is, `H^k(φ) : H^k(A) → H^k(B)` is bijective for every
`k : ℤ`. Then extension of scalars `- ⊗_A^𝐋 B : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)`, the derived tensor product
with the regular differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule of Tag 0BYX, is an equivalence of
categories.

The functor is exact and `R`-linear before any hypothesis (Tags 09LR, 09LS and 09S7, all
instances), so this is the source's `R`-linear equivalence of triangulated categories; the
`R`-linearity is recorded separately at
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence_linear`.

This is Tag 09S7 for `N = B`. Its hypothesis (1) is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isCompactObject_q_regular`, its hypothesis (2) is
`DifferentialGradedModule.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_q_regularModule` verbatim, and its
hypothesis (3) is the hypothesis on `φ` through
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.bijective_cohomologyEndomorphismComparison_regular_iff`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_derivedTensorFunctor_regular (φ : A.Hom B)
    (hφ : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (φ.cohomologyMap k)) :
    (derivedTensorFunctor (Bimodule.regular φ)).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S6.** Let `φ : (A, d) → (B, d)` be a homomorphism of differential graded algebras
over a commutative ring `R` inducing an isomorphism on cohomology algebras. Then extension of
scalars `- ⊗_A^𝐋 B` is one half of an equivalence `D(A, d) ≌ D(B, d)` whose other half is
derived restriction of scalars `N ↦ N_A`.

The equivalence is `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorEquivalence` (Tag 09S7) for the
regular bimodule, whose quasi-inverse is derived Hom `RHom(B, -)`, transported along the
identification of `RHom(B, -)` with derived restriction of scalars
(`DifferentialGradedModule.DerivedHomData.functorIsoDerivedRestriction`, Example 22.33.2 of
Tag 0BYX). `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.changeInverse` leaves the functor untouched and replaces
the inverse by the isomorphic one, so both halves are what the source names:
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence_functor` and
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence_inverse` are both true by
`rfl`.

Both functors are exact: extension of scalars by Tags 09LR and 09LS, restriction of scalars as
the right adjoint of an exact functor (Tag 0A8D). Both are `R`-linear by
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence_linear`, so this is the source's
`R`-linear equivalence of triangulated categories.
declarations.comment: the equivalence of triangulated categories with restriction of scalars as quasi-inverse

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence_functor
declarations.doc: **The equivalence of Tag 09S6 goes by extension of scalars.**
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedExtensionEquivalence_functor (φ : A.Hom B)
    (hφ : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (φ.cohomologyMap k)) :
    (derivedExtensionEquivalence φ hφ).functor = derivedTensorFunctor (Bimodule.regular φ)
declarations.comment: the functor of the equivalence is extension of scalars

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence_inverse
declarations.doc:
**The quasi-inverse of Tag 09S6 is restriction of scalars.** This is the half of the
conclusion of Tag 09S6 that names the quasi-inverse: `N ↦ N_A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedExtensionEquivalence_inverse (φ : A.Hom B)
    (hφ : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (φ.cohomologyMap k)) :
    (derivedExtensionEquivalence φ hφ).inverse = derivedRestriction φ
declarations.comment: the quasi-inverse of the equivalence is restriction of scalars

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence_linear
declarations.doc:
**The equivalence of Tag 09S6 is `R`-linear.** This is the remaining half of the source's
conclusion that `- ⊗_A^𝐋 B : D(A, d) → D(B, d)` is an *`R`-linear* equivalence of triangulated
categories: both the functor and its quasi-inverse are `R`-linear.

The functor is `- ⊗_A^𝐋 B` by `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedExtensionEquivalence_functor`,
and `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_linear` (Tag 09S7) gives the `R`-linearity
of the derived tensor product with any bimodule, with no hypotheses; the quasi-inverse of an
`R`-linear equivalence is `R`-linear by `CategoryTheory.Equivalence.inverseLinear`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedExtensionEquivalence_linear (φ : A.Hom B)
    (hφ : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (φ.cohomologyMap k)) :
    (derivedExtensionEquivalence φ hφ).functor.Linear R ∧
      (derivedExtensionEquivalence φ hφ).inverse.Linear R
declarations.comment: the R-linearity of the equivalence and of its quasi-inverse

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isEquivalence_derivedTensorFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S7.** Let `(A, d)` and `(B, d)` be differential graded algebras over a commutative
ring `R` and let `N` be a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule. Assume

1. the class of `N` in `D(B, d)` is a compact object,
2. an object `X` of `D(B, d)` with `Hom_{D(B,d)}(N, X[n]) = 0` for every `n : ℤ` is zero, and
3. the canonical map `H^k(A) → Hom_{D(B,d)}(N, N[k])` of
   `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.cohomologyEndomorphismComparison` is bijective for every `k : ℤ`.

Then `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` is an equivalence of categories.

The functor is exact with no hypothesis at all — it commutes with the translation by
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_commShift` and preserves distinguished
triangles by `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_isTriangulated`, Tags 09LR and
09LS — so this is the source's equivalence of triangulated categories. What the clause string
excludes is the source's `R`-linearity of the functor, which is not proved here.

This is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isEquivalence_derivedTensorFunctor_of_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator`,
hypothesis (2) being weak generation of `D(B, d)` by the class of `N` ([Stacks, Tag 09SJ](3)).
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_derivedTensorFunctor (N : Bimodule A B)
    [IsCompactObject.{u} ((toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule)]
    (h2 : ∀ X : derivedCategory' B,
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (f : (toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule ⟶
        X⟦n⟧), f = 0) → IsZero X)
    (h3 : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (N.cohomologyEndomorphismComparison k)) :
    (derivedTensorFunctor N).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence of triangulated categories, not the R-linearity of the functor

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S7, as an equivalence with its quasi-inverse named.** Under the hypotheses of
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isEquivalence_derivedTensorFunctor`, the derived tensor product
`- ⊗_A^𝐋 N` is one half of an equivalence `D(A, d) ≌ D(B, d)` whose other half is the derived
Hom functor `RHom(N, -) : D(B, d) ⥤ D(A, d)` of Tag 09LI, with the unit and counit of the
adjunction of Tag 09LT as the two structural isomorphisms.

The source asserts only that `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N` *is* an equivalence and leaves the quasi-inverse
unnamed; this records which functor it is. The unit is invertible by
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isIso_unit_derivedTensorFunctor_adj_derivedHomFunctor` (the heart of
Tag 09R9), and the counit is invertible at every object because the functor is fully faithful and
essentially surjective, so every object of `D(B, d)` lies in its essential image. Again only the
equivalence is claimed, not its `R`-linearity.
declarations.statement:
def derivedTensorEquivalence (N : Bimodule A B)
    [IsCompactObject.{u} ((toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule)]
    (h2 : ∀ X : derivedCategory' B,
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (f : (toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule ⟶
        X⟦n⟧), f = 0) → IsZero X)
    (h3 : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (N.cohomologyEndomorphismComparison k)) :
    derivedCategory' A ≌ derivedCategory' B
declarations.comment: the equivalence, with RHom(N, -) as quasi-inverse; not the R-linearity

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_linear
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S7.** The derived tensor product `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` is `R`-linear.

This holds for every differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N`, with none of the hypotheses of
the tag: it is a property of the functor of Tag 09LS, not of the equivalence. Together with the
exactness recorded by `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_commShift` and
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_isTriangulated` (Tags 09LR and 09LS) it is
what makes the conclusion of Tag 09S7 an equivalence of `R`-linear triangulated categories.

Every object of `D(A, d)` is isomorphic to the image of an object of `K(A, d)` orthogonal on the
left to the acyclic modules, so `CategoryTheory.Functor.linear_iff` reduces the statement to
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor_map_smul_id_q`.
declarations.statement:
instance derivedTensorFunctor_linear (N : Bimodule A B) :
    (derivedTensorFunctor N).Linear R
declarations.comment: the R-linearity of the functor - ⊗_A^𝐋 N

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorEquivalence_linear
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S7.** Under the three hypotheses of that tag, the equivalence
`D(A, d) ≌ D(B, d)` of `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorEquivalence` is `R`-linear in
both directions: its functor is `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N`, which is `R`-linear, and the quasi-inverse of an
`R`-linear equivalence is `R`-linear.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedTensorEquivalence_linear (N : Bimodule A B)
    [IsCompactObject.{u} ((toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule)]
    (h2 : ∀ X : derivedCategory' B,
      (∀ (n : ℤ) (f : (toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule ⟶
        X⟦n⟧), f = 0) → IsZero X)
    (h3 : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (N.cohomologyEndomorphismComparison k)) :
    (derivedTensorEquivalence N h2 h3).functor.Linear R ∧
      (derivedTensorEquivalence N h2 h3).inverse.Linear R
declarations.comment: the R-linearity of the equivalence and of its quasi-inverse

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_isCompactObject_and_isWeakGenerator_of_derivedEquivalence
declarations.doc:
Let `(A, d)` and `(B, d)` be differential graded algebras over a commutative ring `R`, and
assume `A = H^0(A)`, i.e. that every homogeneous component of `A` outside degree zero vanishes. Let
`E : D(A, d) ≌ D(B, d)` be an `R`-linear, additive, shift-commuting equivalence. Then there is an
object `P` of `D(B, d)` such that

* `P` is a compact object of `D(B, d)`;
* an object `N` of `D(B, d)` with `Hom_{D(B,d)}(P, N[i]) = 0` for every `i : ℤ` is zero;
* `Hom_{D(B,d)}(P, P[i]) = 0` for `i ≠ 0`, and the endomorphism `R`-algebra of `P` is `A`;

and `E` sends the regular module `A` to `P`. Indeed `P` is the image of the regular module.

The degree-zero half of the third clause is an isomorphism of `R`-algebras `A ≃ₐ[R] End P`, which
is what the source's "equal to `A`" says: `End P` is `Hom_{D(B,d)}(P, P[0])` with the shift by
zero undone, and its ring structure is composition.

The source's condition (1) is an equivalence of `R`-linear triangulated categories. What is
assumed here is less: `Functor.IsTriangulated` is not used, only `Functor.Additive`, which it
implies, together with `Functor.CommShift ℤ` and the `R`-linearity that "`R`-linear" provides.
The final clause is the statement that the witness `P` may be taken to be `E(A)`, not the source's
final clause about the equivalence constructed from (2).
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isCompactObject_and_isWeakGenerator_of_derivedEquivalence
    (A B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra R) (hA : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → A.grading i = ⊥)
    (E : derivedCategory' A ≌ derivedCategory' B) [E.functor.Additive]
    [E.functor.Linear R] [E.functor.CommShift ℤ] :
    ∃ P : derivedCategory' B,
      IsCompactObject.{u} P ∧
      (∀ N : derivedCategory' B, (∀ (i : ℤ) (f : P ⟶ N⟦i⟧), f = 0) → IsZero N) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → ∀ f : P ⟶ P⟦i⟧, f = 0) ∧
      Nonempty (A.A ≃ₐ[R] End P) ∧
      Nonempty (E.functor.obj
        ((toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj (regularModule A)) ≅ P)
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (2), including the degree-zero clause as an R-algebra isomorphism A ≃ₐ[R] End P, with P the image of the regular module under the given equivalence; NOT (2) ⇒ (1) and NOT the source's final clause about the equivalence constructed from (2) — those are exists_derivedEquivalence_of_isCompactObject_and_isWeakGenerator and the iff derivedEquivalence_iff_exists_isCompactObject_and_isWeakGenerator, in the Converse file

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.exists_derivedEquivalence_of_isCompactObject_and_isWeakGenerator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S8, the implication (2) ⇒ (1), with the source's final clause.** Let `(A, d)` and
`(B, d)` be differential graded `R`-algebras with `A = H^0(A)`, i.e. with every homogeneous
component of `A` outside degree zero vanishing. Let `P` be an object of `D(B, d)` such that

* `P` is a compact object of `D(B, d)`,
* an object `N` of `D(B, d)` with `Hom_{D(B,d)}(P, N[i]) = 0` for every `i : ℤ` is zero,
* `Hom_{D(B,d)}(P, P[i]) = 0` for `i ≠ 0`, and
* the endomorphism `R`-algebra of `P` is `A`.

Then `D(A, d)` and `D(B, d)` are equivalent by an additive, `R`-linear, shift-commuting and
triangulated equivalence, **and that equivalence sends the regular module `A` to `P`** — the
source's final clause.

The proof replaces `P` by a property-(P) model `Q`, whose endomorphism differential graded algebra
`E = End(Q)` makes `Q` an `(E, B)`-bimodule satisfying the hypotheses of [Stacks, Tag 09S7], and
composes the equivalence that bimodule defines with the two equivalences of [Stacks, Tag 09S6]
attached to the quasi-isomorphisms `(A, d) ← (E', d) → (E, d)` out of the degree-`≤ 0` truncation
`E'` of `E`; see
`DifferentialGradedModule.exists_hom_nonpositiveEndomorphismDGA_to_concentrated` and
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.exists_derivedEquivalence_of_quasiIso_pair`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedEquivalence_of_isCompactObject_and_isWeakGenerator
    (A B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R)
    (hA : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → A.grading i = ⊥)
    (P : derivedCategory' B) (hcompact : IsCompactObject.{u} P)
    (hgen : ∀ N : derivedCategory' B, (∀ (i : ℤ) (f : P ⟶ N⟦i⟧), f = 0) → IsZero N)
    (hvan : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → ∀ f : P ⟶ P⟦i⟧, f = 0)
    (hend : Nonempty (A.A ≃ₐ[R] End P)) :
    ∃ G : derivedCategory' A ≌ derivedCategory' B,
      G.functor.Additive ∧ G.functor.Linear R ∧
        (∃ hs : G.functor.CommShift ℤ, letI := hs; G.functor.IsTriangulated) ∧
          Nonempty (G.functor.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj
            (regularModule A)) ≅ P)
declarations.comment: (2) ⇒ (1), by an additive R-linear shift-commuting triangulated equivalence, together with the source's final clause that the equivalence constructed in (2) sends A to P

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedEquivalence_iff_exists_isCompactObject_and_isWeakGenerator
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S8.** Let `(A, d)` and `(B, d)` be differential graded algebras over a commutative
ring `R` and assume `A = H^0(A)`. The following are equivalent.

1. `D(A, d)` and `D(B, d)` are equivalent as `R`-linear triangulated categories.
2. There is an object `P` of `D(B, d)` such that `P` is compact, an object `N` with
   `Hom_{D(B,d)}(P, N[i]) = 0` for all `i : ℤ` is zero, `Hom_{D(B,d)}(P, P[i]) = 0` for `i ≠ 0`,
   and the endomorphism `R`-algebra of `P` is `A`.

Condition (1) is spelled as the existence of an equivalence of categories whose functor is
additive, `R`-linear, commutes with the translation and is triangulated; the degree-zero clause of
(2) is an isomorphism of `R`-algebras `A ≃ₐ[R] End P`, which is what the source's "equal to `A`"
says, the ring structure on the right-hand side being composition.

The implication (1) ⇒ (2) is
`DifferentialGradedModule.exists_isCompactObject_and_isWeakGenerator_of_derivedEquivalence`, which
needs only additivity, `R`-linearity and commutation with the translation; the converse is
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule`
`.exists_derivedEquivalence_of_isCompactObject_and_isWeakGenerator`, which also proves the
source's final clause that the equivalence it constructs sends `A` to `P`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedEquivalence_iff_exists_isCompactObject_and_isWeakGenerator
    (A B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R)
    (hA : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → A.grading i = ⊥) :
    (∃ G : derivedCategory' A ≌ derivedCategory' B,
        G.functor.Additive ∧ G.functor.Linear R ∧
          ∃ hs : G.functor.CommShift ℤ, letI := hs; G.functor.IsTriangulated) ↔
      ∃ P : derivedCategory' B,
        IsCompactObject.{u} P ∧
          (∀ N : derivedCategory' B, (∀ (i : ℤ) (f : P ⟶ N⟦i⟧), f = 0) → IsZero N) ∧
            (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → ∀ f : P ⟶ P⟦i⟧, f = 0) ∧ Nonempty (A.A ≃ₐ[R] End P)
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (2), with (1) as an additive R-linear shift-commuting triangulated equivalence and the degree-zero clause of (2) as an isomorphism of R-algebras A ≃ₐ[R] End P

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_dgModule_iso_obj_q_regularModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S9.** The image `N = F(A)` of the regular module under a functor
`F : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` is represented by a differential graded `B`-module.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_dgModule_iso_obj_q_regularModule :
    ∃ N : DifferentialGradedModule B,
      Nonempty (F.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj (regularModule A)) ≅
        (toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N)
declarations.comment: N = F(A) is represented by a differential graded B-module

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.isCompactObject_obj_q_regularModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S9.** The image `N = F(A)` of the regular module under an additive equivalence
`F : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` is a compact object of `D(B, d)`: the regular module is compact
(`DifferentialGradedModule.isCompactObject_q_regularModule`) and compactness is invariant under
an additive equivalence.
declarations.comment: N = F(A) is a compact object of D(B, d)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_singleton_obj_q_regularModule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S9.** The image `N = F(A)` of the regular module under an additive equivalence
`F : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` commuting with the translation generates `D(B, d)`: an object receiving
only zero morphisms from the shifts of `N` is zero.

The regular module generates `D(A, d)` (`DifferentialGradedModule`
`.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_q_regularModule`), so it suffices to carry a vanishing hypothesis
on `K` back along `F`: a morphism `A ⟶ (F⁻¹K)[n]` becomes, under `F` and the commutation with
the translation, a morphism `N ⟶ K[n]`, hence vanishes, hence vanishes itself because `F` is
faithful. Then `F⁻¹K` is zero and so is `K`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_singleton_obj_q_regularModule
    [F.IsEquivalence] [F.Additive] [F.CommShift ℤ] :
    ObjectProperty.IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator (ObjectProperty.singleton
      (F.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj (regularModule A))))

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.cohomologyEquivDerivedHomObjRegular
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09S9.** For a fully faithful `F : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` commuting with the translation
and `N = F(A)` the image of the regular module, `H^k(A) = Hom_{D(B, d)}(N, N[k])` for every
`k ∈ ℤ`.

This transports the bijection `H^k(A) ≃ Hom_{D(A, d)}(A, A[k])` of
`DifferentialGradedModule.cohomologyEquivDerivedHom` along `F`, using the shift comparison
`DifferentialGradedModule.regularShiftCompare` at the source and the commutation of `F` with the
translation at the target.
declarations.statement:
def cohomologyEquivDerivedHomObjRegular [F.Full] [F.Faithful] [F.CommShift ℤ] (k : ℤ) :
    A.Cohomology k ≃
      (F.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj (regularModule A)) ⟶
        (F.obj
          ((toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj (regularModule A)))⟦k⟧)

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.exists_bimodule_of_derivedEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SA.** Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `(A, d)` and `(B, d)` be differential
graded `R`-algebras and let `F : D(A, d) ≌ D(B, d)` be an additive, `R`-linear,
shift-commuting equivalence. Assume

1. `A = H^0(A)`, i.e. every homogeneous component of `A` outside degree zero vanishes, and
2. `B` is K-flat as a complex of `R`-modules.

Then there is a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N` as in [Stacks, Tag 09S7]: the class of
`N` in `D(B, d)` is a compact object, it weakly generates `D(B, d)`, and the canonical map
`H^k(A) → Hom_{D(B,d)}(N, N[k])` of
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.cohomologyEndomorphismComparison` is bijective for every `k`.
Consequently `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` is an equivalence, and the class of `N` is `F(A)`.

Hypothesis (1) enters through
`DifferentialGradedModule.exists_hom_nonpositiveEndomorphismDGA_to_concentrated`, which needs the
vanishing of `Hom_{D(B,d)}(Q, Q[k])` for `k ≠ 0` and the identification of `A` with the
endomorphism algebra of the class of `Q`; hypothesis (2) enters only through Tag 09S4
(`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctorCompIsoOfKFlatAlgebra`), which composes the
three derived tensor functors of the proof into one.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bimodule_of_derivedEquivalence (A B : DifferentialGradedAlgebra.{u, u} R)
    (hA : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → A.grading i = ⊥)
    (hB : CochainComplex.KFlat.{u, u} (regularModule B).toCochainComplex)
    (F : derivedCategory' A ≌ derivedCategory' B) [F.functor.Additive]
    [F.functor.Linear R] [F.functor.CommShift ℤ] :
    ∃ N : Bimodule A B,
      IsCompactObject.{u}
          ((toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule) ∧
        (∀ X : derivedCategory' B,
            (∀ (n : ℤ) (f : (toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule ⟶
              X⟦n⟧), f = 0) → IsZero X) ∧
          (∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (N.cohomologyEndomorphismComparison k)) ∧
            (derivedTensorFunctor N).IsEquivalence ∧
              Nonempty ((toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule ≅
                F.functor.obj ((toHomotopyCategory A ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' A).Q).obj
                  (regularModule A)))
declarations.comment: the (A, B)-bimodule N as in Lemma 09S7, together with the equivalence it defines and the identification of its class in D(B, d) with F(A); the equivalence F is taken to be additive, R-linear and shift-commuting, Functor.IsTriangulated not being used

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_isPerfect_and_detectsZero_of_derivedEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SC, the implication (1) ⇒ (2).** Let `R` be a commutative ring and let `A` and `B`
be `R`-algebras, not assumed commutative. Let

`E : D(Mod-A) ≌ D(Mod-B)`

be an additive, `R`-linear, shift-commuting equivalence of the derived categories of right
modules. Then there is an object `P` of `D(Mod-B)` such that

* `P` can be represented by a finite complex of finite projective right `B`-modules, that is, `P`
  is perfect;
* an object `K` of `D(Mod-B)` with `Ext^i_B(P, K) = 0` for every `i : ℤ` is zero;
* `Ext^i_B(P, P) = 0` for `i ≠ 0`, and the endomorphism `R`-algebra of `P` is `A`.

The object `P` is produced by Tag 09S8 inside the differential graded world and carried across
the degree-zero comparison `DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence`; perfectness
is compactness by Tag 07LT.

The source's condition (1) is an equivalence of `R`-linear triangulated categories; what is
assumed here is less, namely additivity, `R`-linearity and commutation with the translation,
`CategoryTheory.Functor.IsTriangulated` not being used. The converse implication is not proved
here: see the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_isPerfect_and_detectsZero_of_derivedEquivalence
    (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Aᵐᵒᵖ) ≌ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ))
    [E.functor.Additive] [E.functor.Linear R] [E.functor.CommShift ℤ] :
    ∃ P : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ),
      StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect P ∧
      (∀ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ),
        (∀ i : ℤ, Subsingleton (P ⟶ K⟦i⟧)) → IsZero K) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → Subsingleton (P ⟶ P⟦i⟧)) ∧
      Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[R] End P)
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (2), with D(A) read as the derived category of right A-modules, clause (2)(a) as StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect, Ext vanishing as Subsingleton of the shifted Hom group and the degree-zero clause of (2)(c) as an isomorphism of R-algebras A ≃ₐ[R] End P; NOT (2) ⇒ (1), which needs CategoryTheory.Functor.IsTriangulated for DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence, and NOT part (3)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_bimodule_derivedTensorEquivalence_of_derivedEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SC, the implication (1) ⇒ (3).** Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `A` and `B`
be `R`-algebras, not assumed commutative, and assume `B` is flat as an `R`-module. Let

`E : D(Mod-A) ≌ D(Mod-B)`

be an additive, `R`-linear, shift-commuting equivalence of the derived categories of right
modules. Then there is a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N` over the degree-zero algebras
`degreeZero R A` and `degreeZero R B` such that

* `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(degreeZero R A, d) ⥤ D(degreeZero R B, d)` is an equivalence, and
* so is the functor `D(Mod-A) ⥤ D(Mod-B)` it induces along the degree-zero comparisons, which is
  what the source's `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(A) → D(B)` names.

The bimodule is the one of [Stacks, Tag 09SA], applied to the equivalence `E` conjugated into the
differential graded derived categories; its hypothesis `A = H^0(A)` holds because the degree-zero
grading vanishes away from degree zero, and its K-flatness hypothesis is supplied from flatness
of `B` over `R` by `DifferentialGradedModule.kFlat_regularModule_degreeZero_of_flat`.

The source writes "`(A, B)`-bimodule" with no differential graded qualifier. What is proved here
is the differential graded reading, which is what the proof the source cites — Tag 09SA, via
Tag 09S7 — actually yields; the literal ordinary-bimodule reading is strictly stronger, is not
established by anything the source cites, and is in fact false, by the self-injective
counterexample in the implementation notes of this file.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_bimodule_derivedTensorEquivalence_of_derivedEquivalence [Module.Flat R B]
    (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Aᵐᵒᵖ) ≌ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ))
    [E.functor.Additive] [E.functor.Linear R] [E.functor.CommShift ℤ] :
    ∃ N : DifferentialGraded.Bimodule (degreeZero R A) (degreeZero R B),
      (derivedTensorFunctor N).IsEquivalence ∧
        ((degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence (R := R) (S := A) (A := Aᵐᵒᵖ)).inverse ⋙
          derivedTensorFunctor N ⋙
            (degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence (R := R) (S := B)
              (A := Bᵐᵒᵖ)).functor).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: (1) ⇒ (3) under B flat over R, with N a DIFFERENTIAL GRADED (A,B)-bimodule -- the chapter's own unqualified sense in 09SA/09S7, which 09SC(3) cites, and the ONLY reading under which (3) is true. The literal ordinary-bimodule reading is not merely unproved but FALSE: such an N would be a one-sided tilting module with End_B(N) = A, hence projective and a progenerator over a finite-dimensional self-injective B, forcing A Morita equivalent to B -- so (3) would say derived equivalent self-injective algebras are Morita equivalent, refuted by Brauer tree algebras (Rickard). D(A) is the derived category of right A-modules. NOT (3) ⇒ (1)

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_derivedEquivalence_of_isPerfect_and_detectsZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SC, the implication (2) ⇒ (1).** Let `R` be a commutative ring and let `A` and `B`
be `R`-algebras, not assumed commutative. Let `P` be an object of `D(Mod-B)` such that

* `P` can be represented by a finite complex of finite projective right `B`-modules, that is, `P`
  is perfect;
* an object `K` of `D(Mod-B)` with `Ext^i_B(P, K) = 0` for every `i : ℤ` is zero;
* `Ext^i_B(P, P) = 0` for `i ≠ 0`, and the endomorphism `R`-algebra of `P` is `A`.

Then `D(Mod-A)` and `D(Mod-B)` are equivalent by an additive, `R`-linear equivalence which, for
some commutation with the translation, is triangulated.

The object `P` is carried back along the degree-zero comparison
`DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence` into `D(degreeZero R B, d)`, where
[Stacks, Tag 09S8] produces an equivalence with `D(degreeZero R A, d)`; conjugating that
equivalence by the two comparisons gives the conclusion, the comparisons being exact by
`DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence_functor_exact`. Compactness of `P` is its
perfectness, by Tag 07LT.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedEquivalence_of_isPerfect_and_detectsZero
    (P : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ))
    (hperf : StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect P)
    (hgen : ∀ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ),
      (∀ i : ℤ, Subsingleton (P ⟶ K⟦i⟧)) → IsZero K)
    (hvan : ∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → Subsingleton (P ⟶ P⟦i⟧))
    (hend : Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[R] End P)) :
    ∃ E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Aᵐᵒᵖ) ≌ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ),
      E.functor.Additive ∧ E.functor.Linear R ∧
        ∃ hs : E.functor.CommShift ℤ, letI := hs; E.functor.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: (2) ⇒ (1), the converse of DegreeZeroRickard's (1) ⇒ (2), with the same spellings: clause (2)(a) as StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect, Ext vanishing as Subsingleton of the shifted Hom group, the degree-zero clause of (2)(c) as A ≃ₐ[R] End P, and clause (1) delivered as an additive R-linear equivalence triangulated for SOME commutation with the translation, as in 09S8's own clause (1). D(A) is the derived category of right A-modules

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedEquivalence_iff_exists_isPerfect_and_detectsZero
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SC, the equivalence of (1) and (2).** Let `R` be a commutative ring and let `A`
and `B` be `R`-algebras, not assumed commutative. The following are equivalent.

1. `D(Mod-A)` and `D(Mod-B)` are equivalent by an additive, `R`-linear equivalence which, for some
   commutation with the translation, is triangulated.
2. There is an object `P` of `D(Mod-B)` which is perfect, for which an object `K` with
   `Ext^i_B(P, K) = 0` for all `i : ℤ` is zero, with `Ext^i_B(P, P) = 0` for `i ≠ 0` and with
   endomorphism `R`-algebra `A`.

The implication `(1) ⇒ (2)` is
`DifferentialGradedModule.exists_isPerfect_and_detectsZero_of_derivedEquivalence`, which needs
only additivity, `R`-linearity and commutation with the translation; the converse is
`DifferentialGradedModule.exists_derivedEquivalence_of_isPerfect_and_detectsZero`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedEquivalence_iff_exists_isPerfect_and_detectsZero :
    (∃ E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Aᵐᵒᵖ) ≌ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ),
        E.functor.Additive ∧ E.functor.Linear R ∧
          ∃ hs : E.functor.CommShift ℤ, letI := hs; E.functor.IsTriangulated) ↔
      ∃ P : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ),
        StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect P ∧
        (∀ K : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ),
          (∀ i : ℤ, Subsingleton (P ⟶ K⟦i⟧)) → IsZero K) ∧
        (∀ i : ℤ, i ≠ 0 → Subsingleton (P ⟶ P⟦i⟧)) ∧
        Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[R] End P)
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (2), with clause (1) as an additive R-linear equivalence of the derived categories of right modules which is triangulated for SOME commutation with the translation, clause (2)(a) as StacksDraft.Perfect.IsPerfect, Ext vanishing as Subsingleton of the shifted Hom group and the degree-zero clause of (2)(c) as an isomorphism of R-algebras A ≃ₐ[R] End P

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.exists_derivedEquivalence_of_bimodule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SC, the implication (3) ⇒ (1).** Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `A` and `B` be
`R`-algebras, not assumed commutative, and let `N` be a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule over
the degree-zero algebras for which the derived tensor functor

`- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(degreeZero R A, d) ⥤ D(degreeZero R B, d)`

is an equivalence. Then `D(Mod-A)` and `D(Mod-B)` are equivalent by an additive, `R`-linear
equivalence which, for some commutation with the translation, is triangulated.

The derived tensor functor is additive, `R`-linear (Tag 09S7) and exact (Tags 09LR and 09LS), so
conjugating it by the two degree-zero comparisons — exact by
`DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence_functor_exact` — gives the conclusion. No
flatness hypothesis is needed for this direction.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_derivedEquivalence_of_bimodule
    (N : DifferentialGraded.Bimodule (degreeZero R A) (degreeZero R B))
    (hN : (DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor N).IsEquivalence) :
    ∃ E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Aᵐᵒᵖ) ≌ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ),
      E.functor.Additive ∧ E.functor.Linear R ∧
        ∃ hs : E.functor.CommShift ℤ, letI := hs; E.functor.IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: (3) ⇒ (1), the converse of DegreeZeroRickardBimodule's (1) ⇒ (3), with N a differential graded (A,B)-bimodule over the degree-zero algebras and the hypothesis that its differential graded derived tensor functor is an equivalence; no flatness of B over R is needed for this direction. Clause (1) is delivered as an additive R-linear equivalence of the derived categories of right modules which is triangulated for SOME commutation with the translation

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.derivedEquivalence_iff_exists_bimodule
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SC, the equivalence of (1) and (3).** Let `R` be a commutative ring, let `A` and
`B` be `R`-algebras, not assumed commutative, and assume `B` is flat as an `R`-module. The
following are equivalent.

1. `D(Mod-A)` and `D(Mod-B)` are equivalent by an additive, `R`-linear equivalence which, for some
   commutation with the translation, is triangulated.
3. There is a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule `N` over the degree-zero algebras for which
   `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(degreeZero R A, d) ⥤ D(degreeZero R B, d)` is an equivalence.

The implication `(1) ⇒ (3)` is
`DifferentialGradedModule.exists_bimodule_derivedTensorEquivalence_of_derivedEquivalence`, which
is where flatness is used; the converse is
`DifferentialGradedModule.exists_derivedEquivalence_of_bimodule`, which needs no flatness. The
reading of "`(A, B)`-bimodule" is the differential graded one of
`StacksFrontier/Algebra/DifferentialGraded/Module/DegreeZeroRickardBimodule.lean`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedEquivalence_iff_exists_bimodule [Module.Flat R B] :
    (∃ E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Aᵐᵒᵖ) ≌ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} Bᵐᵒᵖ),
        E.functor.Additive ∧ E.functor.Linear R ∧
          ∃ hs : E.functor.CommShift ℤ, letI := hs; E.functor.IsTriangulated) ↔
      ∃ N : DifferentialGraded.Bimodule (degreeZero R A) (degreeZero R B),
        (DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.derivedTensorFunctor N).IsEquivalence
declarations.comment: the equivalence of (1) and (3) for B flat over R, with clause (1) as an additive R-linear equivalence of the derived categories of right modules which is triangulated for SOME commutation with the translation, and N a differential graded (A,B)-bimodule over the degree-zero algebras per 09SA/09S7 rather than an ordinary bimodule

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroHomotopyFunctor_isTriangulated
declarations.doc:
**The degree-zero comparison is exact on homotopy categories.** The functor
`K(degreeZero R S, d) ⥤ K(A)` carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles: a
distinguished triangle of `K(degreeZero R S, d)` is isomorphic to the triangle of an admissible
short exact sequence, whose image is a degreewise split short exact sequence of cochain
complexes.
declarations.statement:
theorem degreeZeroHomotopyFunctor_isTriangulated :
    (degreeZeroHomotopyFunctor R A (S := S)).IsTriangulated
declarations.comment: exactness of the degree-zero comparison on homotopy categories

declarations.name: DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroDerivedEquivalence_functor_exact
declarations.doc:
**The comparison equivalence of derived categories is exact.** For the commutation with the
shift that the localization of the homotopy category induces on it, the equivalence
`D(degreeZero R S, d) ≌ D(A)` carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles: it
lifts the exact functor `K(degreeZero R S, d) ⥤ D(A)` of
`DifferentialGradedModule.degreeZeroHomotopyFunctor_isTriangulated` along a localization of
pretriangulated categories, and such a lift is exact.
declarations.comment: exactness of the degree-zero comparison equivalence of derived categories

declarations.name: DerivedEquivalence.centerAlgEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Derived equivalent algebras have isomorphic centres.** Let `A` and `B` be algebras over a
commutative ring `R` whose derived categories are equivalent through an additive, `R`-linear,
shift-commuting equivalence `E`. If the canonical maps from `Z(A)` and from `Z(B)` to the
shift-compatible centres of `D(A)` and of `D(B)` are surjective — the step the Stacks project
defers to Rickard, assumed here and not proved — then `Z(A)` and `Z(B)` are isomorphic as
`R`-algebras, by transporting the shift-compatible centre along `E`.

The `@[stacks 09SD]` part string below says "the centre of `DerivedCategory (ModuleCat A)`". Read
that as the SHIFT-COMPATIBLE centre `CatCenter.shiftSubalgebra`, which is the correct object: the
full `CatCenter` of the derived category is too big, being `∏_{n : ℤ} k` over a field `k`, so the
hypothesis as originally stated here was unsatisfiable and has been replaced by surjectivity of
`ModuleCat.centerToShiftCenterDerived`. See the note on Tag 09SD at the top of this file.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def centerAlgEquiv
    (hA : Function.Surjective (ModuleCat.centerToShiftCenterDerived R A))
    (hB : Function.Surjective (ModuleCat.centerToShiftCenterDerived R B))
    (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ≌ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} B))
    [E.functor.Additive] [E.functor.Linear R] [E.functor.CommShift ℤ] :
    (Subalgebra.center R A) ≃ₐ[R] (Subalgebra.center R B)
declarations.comment: Z(A) to Z(B) by transporting the shift-compatible centre along the equivalence

declarations.name: DerivedEquivalence.algEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Derived equivalent commutative algebras are isomorphic.** A commutative algebra is its own
centre, so the isomorphism of centres of `DerivedEquivalence.centerAlgEquiv` is an isomorphism
`A ≃ₐ[R] B` when `A` and `B` are commutative. The same surjectivity of
`ModuleCat.centerToShiftCenterDerived` is assumed and not proved.

As for `centerAlgEquiv`, read "the centre of `DerivedCategory (ModuleCat A)`" in the part string
below as the SHIFT-COMPATIBLE centre; the full `CatCenter` there is too big and the hypothesis as
originally stated was unsatisfiable.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def algEquiv
    (hA : Function.Surjective (ModuleCat.centerToShiftCenterDerived R A))
    (hB : Function.Surjective (ModuleCat.centerToShiftCenterDerived R B))
    (E : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} A) ≌ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{v} B))
    [E.functor.Additive] [E.functor.Linear R] [E.functor.CommShift ℤ] :
    A ≃ₐ[R] B
declarations.comment: the commutative case: A to B, a commutative algebra being its own centre

declarations.name: isIdempotentComplete_iff_idempotents_have_cokernels
declarations.statement:
lemma isIdempotentComplete_iff_idempotents_have_cokernels :
    IsIdempotentComplete C ↔ ∀ {X : C} (p : X ⟶ X), p ≫ p = p → HasCokernel p

declarations.name: isIdempotentComplete_iff'
declarations.statement:
lemma isIdempotentComplete_iff' : IsIdempotentComplete C ↔
    ∀ (Z : C) (p : Z ⟶ Z), p ≫ p = p →
    ∃ (X Y : C) (b : BinaryBicone X Y) (_ : b.IsBilimit) (e : Z ≅ b.pt),
      e.hom ≫ b.snd ≫ b.inr ≫ e.inv = p

declarations.name: isIdempotentComplete_iff_hasBinaryProduct_proj
declarations.doc: The direct-sum characterisation (Stacks 09SH (3)), phrased with the biproduct `X ⊞ Y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isIdempotentComplete_iff_hasBinaryProduct_proj : IsIdempotentComplete C ↔
    ∀ (Z : C) (p : Z ⟶ Z), p ≫ p = p →
      ∃ (X Y : C) (_ : HasBinaryBiproduct X Y) (e : Z ≅ X ⊞ Y),
        e.hom ≫ biprod.snd ≫ biprod.inr ≫ e.inv = p

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.doc:
A property of objects `P` of a category `C` with zero morphisms and a shift by `ℤ` is a
*weak generator*, or simply a *generator*, if every object `K` receiving only zero maps from the
shifts of the objects satisfying `P` is zero; equivalently, if every nonzero object `K` admits an
integer `n` and a nonzero map `E ⟶ K⟦n⟧` from an object `E` satisfying `P`
(`isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_iff`).
declarations.statement: public def IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator (P : ObjectProperty C) : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_iff
declarations.doc:
A weak generator in the source's own words: `P` is a weak generator if and only if for every
nonzero object `K` there are an object `E` satisfying `P`, an integer `n` and a nonzero map
`E ⟶ K⟦n⟧`. For `P = ObjectProperty.singleton E` this is literally Definition
[Stacks, Tag 09SJ](3).
declarations.comment: (3), in the source's literal form: for every nonzero K an integer n and a nonzero map E ⟶ K⟦n⟧

declarations.name: Stacks.TriangulatedGenerators.hom_vanishing_iff_gen
declarations.doc:
Stacks tag `09SK` (Lemma 13.36.4). For objects `E, K` of a triangulated
category `D`, the following are equivalent:
1. `Hom(E, K[i]) = 0` for all `i : ℤ`;
2. `Hom(E', K) = 0` for all `E' ∈ ⟨E⟩`.
declarations.statement:
theorem hom_vanishing_iff_gen (E K : D) :
    (∀ i : ℤ, ∀ f : E ⟶ (shiftFunctor D i).obj K, f = 0) ↔
      (∀ E' ∈ gen E, ∀ f : E' ⟶ K, f = 0)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.IsClassicalTriangulatedGenerator.isZero_of_rightOrthogonal_shiftClosure
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SL**: a classical generator of a (pre)triangulated category is a weak generator.
If the triangulated envelope of an object property `P` is everything, then an object `Y` which
receives only zero maps from the shifts of the objects of `P` — equivalently, an object `Y` with
`Hom(X, Y⟦n⟧) = 0` for every `X` satisfying `P` and every `n : ℤ` — is a zero object.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_isHomotopyColimit_of_compactlyGenerated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SN**. Let `D` be a pre-triangulated category with direct sums and let `E : ι → D`
be a family of compact objects such that `⨁ E i` generates `D`, i.e. the only objects right
orthogonal to all shifts of the `E i` are the zero objects. Then every object `X` of `D` is a
derived colimit `X = hocolim Xₙ` of a system `F : ℕ ⥤ D` whose first term `F.obj 0` is a direct
sum of shifts of the `E i` and each of whose transition morphisms `Xₙ ⟶ Xₙ₊₁` fits into a
distinguished triangle `Yₙ ⟶ Xₙ ⟶ Xₙ₊₁ ⟶ Yₙ⟦1⟧` with `Yₙ` a direct sum of shifts of the `E i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_isHomotopyColimit_of_compactlyGenerated
    {ι : Type v} (E : ι → D) [∀ i, IsCompactObject.{v} (E i)]
    (hE : ∀ Y : D, ((ofObj E).shiftClosure ℤ).rightOrthogonal Y → IsZero Y) (X : D) :
    ∃ F : ℕ ⥤ D,
      IsHomotopyColimit F X ∧
      (⨆ J : Type v, ((ofObj E).shiftClosure ℤ).colimitsOfShape (Discrete J)) (F.obj 0) ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ Y : D,
        (⨆ J : Type v, ((ofObj E).shiftClosure ℤ).colimitsOfShape (Discrete J)) Y ∧
        ∃ (f : Y ⟶ F.obj n) (g : F.obj (n + 1) ⟶ Y⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
          Triangle.mk f (F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n))) g ∈ distTriang D

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.exists_fac_triangEnvelope_of_isCompactObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SP**. Let `D` be a triangulated category with direct sums, `E : ι → D` a family of
compact objects, and `X : ℕ → D` a system of cell attachments as in [Stacks, Tag 09SN]: `X 0` is
a direct sum of shifts of the `E i` and each `X (n + 1)` fits into a distinguished triangle
`Yₙ ⟶ X n ⟶ X (n + 1) ⟶ Yₙ⟦1⟧` with `Yₙ` a direct sum of shifts of the `E i`. Then every
morphism `φ : C ⟶ X n` from a compact object `C` factors as `C ⟶ Z ⟶ X n` with `Z` an object of
the triangulated envelope `⟨E_{i₁} ⊕ … ⊕ E_{i_t}⟩` of a finite direct sum of the `E i`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_fac_triangEnvelope_of_isCompactObject
    {ι : Type v} (E : ι → D) [∀ i, IsCompactObject.{v} (E i)] {X : ℕ → D}
    (hX₀ : (⨆ J : Type v, ((ofObj E).shiftClosure ℤ).colimitsOfShape (Discrete J)) (X 0))
    (hX : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ Y : D,
      (⨆ J : Type v, ((ofObj E).shiftClosure ℤ).colimitsOfShape (Discrete J)) Y ∧
        ∃ (f : Y ⟶ X n) (g : X n ⟶ X (n + 1)) (h : X (n + 1) ⟶ Y⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧),
          Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distTriang D)
    {C : D} [IsCompactObject.{v} C] {n : ℕ} (φ : C ⟶ X n) :
    ∃ (s : Finset ι) (Z : D), (ObjectProperty.singleton (∐ fun i : s ↦ E i)).triangEnvelope Z ∧
      ∃ (a : C ⟶ Z) (b : Z ⟶ X n), a ≫ b = φ

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Pretriangulated.IsCompactlyGenerated
declarations.doc:
A category `D` with a shift by `ℤ` is *compactly generated* if there is a family `E : ι → D`
of compact objects, indexed by a type `ι : Type w`, which is a weak generator: the only objects of
`D` receiving only zero maps from the shifts `(E i)⟦n⟧` are the zero objects. When `D` has direct
sums indexed by `Type w` this says that `⨁ E i` generates `D`, as in Definition
[Stacks, Tag 09SQ] — see `ObjectProperty.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_ofObj_iff`.
declarations.statement: public def IsCompactlyGenerated : Prop

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_ofObj_iff
declarations.doc:
A family of objects is a weak generator if and only if its direct sum is one: for a family
`E : ι → C` whose coproduct exists, the property of belonging to `E` is a weak generator exactly
when the single object `∐ E` is. This identifies the family-wise condition with the source's
condition on `⨁ E i` in Definition [Stacks, Tag 09SQ].
declarations.statement:
public theorem isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_ofObj_iff {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    [HasZeroMorphisms C] [HasShift C ℤ] {ι : Type w} (E : ι → C) [HasCoproduct E] :
    (ofObj E).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator ↔
      (ObjectProperty.singleton (∐ E)).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator
declarations.comment: the source's form of the generation condition: the direct sum ∐ E is a weak generator

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_iff_triangEnvelope_eq_isCompactObject_and_isCompactlyGenerated
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SR**. Let `D` be a triangulated category with direct sums and let `E` be a compact
object of `D`. Then `E` is a weak generator of `D` if and only if `E` is a classical generator of
the subcategory `D_c` of compact objects, i.e. the triangulated envelope `⟨E⟩` is exactly the
property of being a compact object, and `D` is compactly generated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_iff_triangEnvelope_eq_isCompactObject_and_isCompactlyGenerated
    (E : D) [IsCompactObject.{v} E] :
    (ObjectProperty.singleton E).IsWeakTriangulatedGenerator ↔
      (ObjectProperty.singleton E).triangEnvelope = IsCompactObject.{v, _, _} (C := D) ∧
        IsCompactlyGenerated.{v} D

declarations.name: DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.isEquivalence_derivedTensorFunctor_of_triangEnvelope_eq_isCompactObject
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09SS, first assertion.** Let `(A, d)` and `(B, d)` be differential graded algebras
over a commutative ring `R` and let `N` be a differential graded `(A, B)`-bimodule. Assume

1. the class of `N` in `D(B, d)` is a compact object,
2. `N` is a classical generator for `D_{compact}(B, d)`, that is, the triangulated envelope of the
   class of `N` is exactly the subcategory of compact objects of `D(B, d)`, and
3. the canonical map `H^k(A) → Hom_{D(B,d)}(N, N[k])` of
   `DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.cohomologyEndomorphismComparison` is bijective for every `k : ℤ`.

Then `- ⊗_A^𝐋 N : D(A, d) ⥤ D(B, d)` is an equivalence of categories.

This is [Stacks, Tag 09S7] with its hypothesis (2) replaced as Tag 09SS says it may be. Hypothesis
(2) above gives that the class of the regular module `B`, being a compact object of `D(B, d)`,
lies in the triangulated envelope of the class of `N`; since that class is a weak generator of
`D(B, d)`, so is the class of `N`, by
`CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_singleton_of_prop_triangEnvelope`. That
is hypothesis (2) of Tag 09S7.

As for Tag 09S7, the functor is exact and `R`-linear before any hypothesis (Tags 09LR, 09LS and
09S7), so this is the source's `R`-linear equivalence of triangulated categories, the
`R`-linearity being recorded at
`DifferentialGraded.Bimodule.linear_derivedTensorFunctor_of_isEquivalence`. The second
assertion of the remark — that a weak generator of `D_{compact}(B, d)` suffices once `RHom(N, B)`
is a compact object of `D(A, d)` — is the statement below,
`isEquivalence_derivedTensorFunctor_of_isWeakTriangulatedGenerator_isCompactObject`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isEquivalence_derivedTensorFunctor_of_triangEnvelope_eq_isCompactObject (N : Bimodule A B)
    [IsCompactObject.{u} ((toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj N.rightModule)]
    (h2 : (ObjectProperty.singleton ((toHomotopyCategory B ⋙ (quasiIsomorphisms' B).Q).obj
        N.rightModule)).triangEnvelope =
      IsCompactObject.{u, _, _} (C := derivedCategory' B))
    (h3 : ∀ k : ℤ, Function.Bijective (N.cohomologyEndomorphismComparison k)) :
