enters. That `Rπ_* E` again has quasi-coherent cohomology, so that Stacks 09VF applies to it, is
clause (1) of Stacks 08D5 by way of
`AlgebraicGeometry.preservesQuasicoherentOnAffineTarget`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_derivedPushforward
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ Y) (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    (hπ : π ≫ g = f) [IsFinite π] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g]
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (m : ℤ) :
    Scheme.Hom.IsPseudoCoherentFrom f E m ↔
      Scheme.Hom.IsPseudoCoherentFrom g
        ((RingedSpace.derivedPushforward π.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₃_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UL, part (1).** If the first term of a distinguished triangle of `D(𝒪_X)` is
`(m + 1)`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S` and the second is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`,
then the third is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₃_of_distinguished [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (m : ℤ)
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules)) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hE : IsPseudoCoherentFrom f T.obj₁ (m + 1)) (hE' : IsPseudoCoherentFrom f T.obj₂ m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom f T.obj₃ m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₂_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UL, part (2).** If the first and third terms of a distinguished triangle of
`D(𝒪_X)` are `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`, then so is the second.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₂_of_distinguished [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (m : ℤ)
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules)) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hE : IsPseudoCoherentFrom f T.obj₁ m) (hE'' : IsPseudoCoherentFrom f T.obj₃ m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom f T.obj₂ m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₁_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UL, part (3).** If the second term of a distinguished triangle of `D(𝒪_X)` is
`(m + 1)`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S` and the third is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`,
then the first is `(m + 1)`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_obj₁_of_distinguished [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (m : ℤ)
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules)) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hE' : IsPseudoCoherentFrom f T.obj₂ (m + 1)) (hE'' : IsPseudoCoherentFrom f T.obj₃ m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom f T.obj₁ (m + 1)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherent_obj₃_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UL, the "moreover" clause for the third term.** If the first two terms of a
distinguished triangle of `D(𝒪_X)` are pseudo-coherent relative to `S`, so is the third.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherent_obj₃_of_distinguished [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules)) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hE : IsPseudoCoherent f T.obj₁) (hE' : IsPseudoCoherent f T.obj₂) :
    IsPseudoCoherent f T.obj₃

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherent_obj₂_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UL, the "moreover" clause for the second term.** If the first and third terms of a
distinguished triangle of `D(𝒪_X)` are pseudo-coherent relative to `S`, so is the second.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherent_obj₂_of_distinguished [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules)) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hE : IsPseudoCoherent f T.obj₁) (hE'' : IsPseudoCoherent f T.obj₃) :
    IsPseudoCoherent f T.obj₂

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherent_obj₁_of_distinguished
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UL, the "moreover" clause for the first term.** If the last two terms of a
distinguished triangle of `D(𝒪_X)` are pseudo-coherent relative to `S`, so is the first.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherent_obj₁_of_distinguished [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (T : Triangle (DerivedCategory X.Modules)) (hT : T ∈ distinguishedTriangles)
    (hE' : IsPseudoCoherent f T.obj₂) (hE'' : IsPseudoCoherent f T.obj₃) :
    IsPseudoCoherent f T.obj₁

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isModulePseudoCoherentFrom_neg_one_iff_isFinitelyPresentedRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UM, the degree-minus-one clause.** For a morphism of schemes locally of finite
type, a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules is `(-1)`-pseudo-coherent relative to the base if and only if it
is quasi-coherent and finitely presented relative to the base.

Stacks 09UJ turns relative `(-1)`-pseudo-coherence into the local condition of Stacks 09UI at
every compatible pair of affine opens `U ⊆ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, where by Stacks 09V9(2) it says that the
direct image of `ℱ|_U` along a closed immersion `i : U ⟶ 𝔸ⁿ_V` over `V` is of finite
presentation. Finite presentation of `i_*(ℱ|_U)` gives quasi-coherence of `ℱ|_U`, and
quasi-coherence is local on `X`; it also gives relative finite presentation of `ℱ|_U` over `V`
by Stacks 09T8 and 09T9, which is the affine-pair criterion of Stacks 09T7. Conversely Stacks
09T7 restricts relative finite presentation to the pair, and Stacks 09T9 and 09T8 turn it back
into finite presentation of `i_*(ℱ|_U)` at a closed immersion of our own choosing.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isModulePseudoCoherentFrom_neg_one_iff_isFinitelyPresentedRelative
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) :
    IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom f F (-1) ↔
      (F.IsQuasicoherent ∧ IsFinitelyPresentedRelative f F)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isModulePseudoCoherentFrom_zero_iff_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UM, the degree-zero clause.** For a morphism of schemes locally of finite type, a
sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules is `0`-pseudo-coherent relative to the base if and only if it is of finite
type.

Stacks 09UJ turns relative `0`-pseudo-coherence into the local condition of Stacks 09UI at every
compatible pair of affine opens, where it is finiteness of type of the restriction of `ℱ` to the
source open; finiteness of type is inherited by restriction and is local on `X`, which gives the
two implications.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isModulePseudoCoherentFrom_of_pos
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UM, the positive degrees.** For a morphism of schemes locally of finite type,
every sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules is relatively `m`-pseudo-coherent whenever `0 < m`.

The affine open covering of the base is the family of all affine opens, and over each member the
covering of its inverse image is the family of all affine opens of `X` contained in it; the
closed immersions into affine space are the ones produced by
`AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isClosedImmersion_affineSpace_resLE`, and the local condition at each
of them holds because the restriction of a sheaf of modules is still concentrated in degree
zero.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsPseudoCoherentFrom.of_biprod_left
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UN, first summand.** If `E ⊕ K` is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S` then so is
`E`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.IsPseudoCoherentFrom.of_biprod_right
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UN, second summand.** If `E ⊕ K` is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S` then so is
`K`.

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_Q_of_locally_boundedAbove
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UP.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type, let `m` be
an integer and let `𝓕` be a complex of `𝒪_X`-modules which is bounded above on a neighbourhood of
every point. If `𝓕ⁱ` is `(m - i)`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S` for every `i`, then `𝓕` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`.

By Stacks 09UJ it is enough to check the local condition of Stacks 09UI at a compatible pair of
affine opens `U ⊆ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, and by Stacks 09VC it may be checked at any one closed immersion
`i : U ⟶ 𝔸ⁿ_V` over `V`. There it says that the complex `i_*(𝓕|_U)` on `𝔸ⁿ_V` represents an
`m`-pseudo-coherent object, which is the globally bounded above case of Stacks 09V7: the terms
are `m`-pseudo-coherent in their degrees because each `𝓕ⁱ` is relatively `(m - i)`-pseudo-coherent
at the same pair and the same closed immersion, and the complex is bounded above on all of the
quasi-compact `U`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_Q_of_locally_boundedAbove [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (m : ℤ)
    (F : CochainComplex X.Modules ℤ)
    (hbdd : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      IsZero ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj (F.X i)))
    (hterms : ∀ i : ℤ, IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom f (F.X i) (m - i)) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom f (DerivedCategory.Q.obj F) m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_homology_of_locally_boundedAbove
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type, let `m` be an integer and let
`E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` whose cohomology sheaves vanish in high degrees on a neighbourhood of
every point. If `H^i(E)` is `(m - i)`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S` for every `i`, then `E` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_homology_of_locally_boundedAbove [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (m : ℤ) (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hbdd : ∀ x : X, ∃ U : X.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i →
      IsZero ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor U.ι).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E)))
    (hcoh : ∀ i : ℤ, IsModulePseudoCoherentFrom f
      ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E) (m - i)) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom f E m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedPullback_of_torIndependent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UR.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)`
which is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`, and let `g : S' ⟶ S` be a morphism of schemes. If
`S'` and `X` are Tor independent over `S`, then the derived pullback of `E` to `X ×_S S'` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S'`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedPullback_of_torIndependentCharts`
with its chart hypothesis discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.chartTorIndependence_of_torIndependent`, so the Tor independence
assumed here is the one the source assumes.

No hypothesis beyond the source's is assumed. Stacks 0E23, the base change isomorphism stated
as `AlgebraicGeometry.DerivedBaseChangeIsoOfTorIndependent`, is proved —
`AlgebraicGeometry.derivedBaseChangeIsoOfTorIndependent`, from
`Stacks.Cohomology.ClosedImmersionBaseChange.isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap_of_torIndependent` — so
it is not needed as a hypothesis here. The tag for Stacks 09UR sits here rather than on
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedPullback_of_torIndependentCharts`,
because the source's hypothesis is Tor independence of `X` and `S'` over `S`, which is what this
statement assumes; the chart form that one assumes is strictly stronger-looking and is derived
here by `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.chartTorIndependence_of_torIndependent`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedPullback_of_torIndependent
    {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (m : ℤ)
    (htor : TorIndependent f g) (hE : f.IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m) :
    (pullback.snd f g).IsPseudoCoherentFrom
      ((derivedPullback (pullback.fst f g).toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_comp_derivedPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09US.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a pseudo-coherent morphism of schemes, let `g : Y ⟶ S` be
locally of finite type and let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_Y)` which is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative
to `S`. Then the derived pullback `Lf^*E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`.

The hypothesis on `f` is `AlgebraicGeometry.PseudoCoherent`, which by Stacks 067Y is the
conjunction of the two hypotheses of the source: `f` is locally of finite type and `𝒪_X` is
pseudo-coherent relative to `Y`.

No hypothesis beyond those of the source is needed. The appeal the source makes to Stacks 0E23,
through Stacks 09UR, is at a square whose horizontal morphism is flat — it is
`AlgebraicGeometry.AffineSpace.map` of a restriction of the flat projection `𝔸ᵈ_W ⟶ W` — and that
case of 0E23 is `AlgebraicGeometry.nonempty_derivedPullbackPushforwardIso`, proved in this file.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_comp_derivedPullback {X Y S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (g : Y ⟶ S) [PseudoCoherent f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (E : DerivedCategory Y.Modules)
    (m : ℤ) (hE : g.IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m) :
    (f ≫ g).IsPseudoCoherentFrom ((derivedPullback f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UT.** Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite type, let `g : Y ⟶ S` be
pseudo-coherent, let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `m` be an integer. Then `E` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `Y` if and only if it is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`.

The two implications are
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_comp` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_comp`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_comp (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (m : ℤ) :
    f.IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m ↔ (f ≫ g).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m
declarations.comment: the equivalence, with pseudo-coherence of g as a class

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_comp_of_isModulePseudoCoherent
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UT with pseudo-coherence of `g` in the shape of condition (3) of Stacks 067Y.**
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be locally of finite type and let `g : Y ⟶ S` be locally of finite type with
`𝒪_Y` pseudo-coherent relative to `S`. Then an object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` is `m`-pseudo-coherent
relative to `Y` if and only if it is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`.

The hypothesis is condition (3) of Stacks 067Y rather than
`AlgebraicGeometry.PseudoCoherent`; the two are interchangeable by the unconditional
`AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_iff_isModulePseudoCoherent`, so this is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_comp`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_comp_of_isModulePseudoCoherent {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (hg : ∃ hft : LocallyOfFiniteType g,
      letI := hft
      Scheme.Hom.IsModulePseudoCoherent g (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf))
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (m : ℤ) :
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType g := hg.choose
    letI : LocallyOfFiniteType (f ≫ g) := locallyOfFiniteType_comp f g
    f.IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m ↔ (f ≫ g).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m
declarations.comment: the equivalence, with the hypothesis in the shape of condition (3) of 067Y

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_derivedPushforwardRelative
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UU, the equivalence of clauses (1) and (2).** Let `i : X ⟶ P` be a closed immersion
of schemes and let `p : P ⟶ S` be locally of finite type. For an object `E` of `D(𝒪_X)` and an
integer `m`, `E` is relatively `m`-pseudo-coherent for `i ≫ p` if and only if the unbounded
derived pushforward `Ri_*E` is relatively `m`-pseudo-coherent for `p`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_pushforwardMapDerivedCategory` transported
along `Stacks.ClosedImmersion.derivedPushforwardIsoMapDerivedCategoryOfSchemes`, which identifies
the chosen total right derived functor
  `Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward` with the functor the
exact `i_*` induces on derived categories; relative `m`-pseudo-coherence depends only on the
isomorphism class of its argument.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_derivedPushforwardRelative {X P S : Scheme.{u}}
    (i : X ⟶ P) (p : P ⟶ S) [IsClosedImmersion i] [LocallyOfFiniteType p]
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (m : ℤ) :
    (i ≫ p).IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m ↔
      p.IsPseudoCoherentFrom
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward
          i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) m
declarations.comment: the equivalence of clauses (1) and (2), at a closed immersion

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.derivedPushforwardRelative_iff_pseudoCoherentFrom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UU, the equivalence of clauses (2) and (3).** Let `i : X ⟶ P` be a morphism of
schemes and let `p : P ⟶ S` be flat and locally of finite presentation. For an object `E` of
`D(𝒪_X)` and an integer `m`, the unbounded derived pushforward `Ri_*E` is relatively
`m`-pseudo-coherent for `p` if and only if it is `m`-pseudo-coherent on `P`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_of_pseudoCoherent` at the object
`Ri_*E`, together with
`AlgebraicGeometry.pseudoCoherent_of_flat_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`. Nothing about `Ri_*E`
beyond its being an object of `D(𝒪_P)` is used, and in particular no hypothesis on `i` is
needed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedPushforwardRelative_iff_pseudoCoherentFrom {X P S : Scheme.{u}} (i : X ⟶ P)
    (p : P ⟶ S) [Flat p] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p] (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (m : ℤ) :
    p.IsPseudoCoherentFrom
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward
          i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) m ↔
      RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherentFrom (X := P.toRingedSpace)
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward
          i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) m

declarations.name: relatively_compact_refinement
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UV.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact Hausdorff space and `U : I → Set X` an open cover.
Then there is an open cover `V : I → Set X` with the same index set such that
`closure (V i) ⊆ U i` for every `i`.

A quasi-compact Hausdorff space is normal, so the shrinking lemma applies once the cover has been
made point-finite: extract a finite subcover indexed by `J : Finset I` and replace `U i` by `∅`
for `i ∉ J`.
declarations.statement:
theorem relatively_compact_refinement
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [CompactSpace X]
    {I : Type*} (U : I → Set X) (hUopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
    (hUcov : ⋃ i, U i = Set.univ) :
    ∃ V : I → Set X, (∀ i, IsOpen (V i)) ∧ (⋃ i, V i = Set.univ) ∧
      (∀ i, closure (V i) ⊆ U i)

declarations.name: exists_cover_closure_subset_and_refines
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09UW**.
Let `(U i)` be an open cover of a compact Hausdorff space `X` and let `(W i k)` be, for each
`(p + 1)`-tuple `i` of indices, an open cover of `⋂ a, U (i a)`. Then `X` has an open cover
`(V j)` together with a map `α` of index sets such that `closure (V j) ⊆ U (α j)` and, for
every `(p + 1)`-tuple `j`, the intersection `⋂ a, V (j a)` is either empty or contained in
some `W (α ∘ j) k`.

The final clause is a disjunction because `K (α ∘ j)` may be empty; in that case
`⋂ a, U (α (j a))` is empty by hypothesis, so no `k` exists, and `⋂ a, V (j a)` is empty
too.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_cover_closure_subset_and_refines
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [CompactSpace X]
    {I : Type*}
    (U : I → Set X)
    (hUopen : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
    (hUcov : ⋃ i, U i = Set.univ)
    (p : ℕ)
    {K : (Fin (p + 1) → I) → Type*}
    (W : ∀ (i : Fin (p + 1) → I), K i → Set X)
    (hWopen : ∀ i k, IsOpen (W i k))
    (hWcov : ∀ i, (⋂ a, U (i a)) = ⋃ k, W i k) :
    ∃ (J : Type) (V : J → Set X) (α : J → I),
      (∀ j, IsOpen (V j)) ∧
      (⋃ j, V j = Set.univ) ∧
      (∀ j, closure (V j) ⊆ U (α j)) ∧
      (∀ (j : Fin (p + 1) → J),
        (⋂ a, V (j a)) = ∅ ∨
          ∃ k : K (fun a => α (j a)), (⋂ a, V (j a)) ⊆ W (fun a => α (j a)) k)

declarations.name: shrinking_open_covering
declarations.doc:
Stacks Project, Tag 09UX (Shrinking an open covering).

Let `X` be a Hausdorff and locally quasi-compact (in the Stacks Project sense,
i.e. weakly locally compact) topological space.  Let `Z ⊆ X` be a compact
subset.  Given an open cover `U : I → Set X` of `Z`, and for each
`(p+1)`-tuple `σ : Fin (p+1) → I` an open subset
`W σ ⊆ ⋂ k, U (σ k)` satisfying
`W σ ∩ Z = (⋂ k, U (σ k)) ∩ Z`, there exist open subsets `V : I → Set X`
with `Z ⊆ ⋃ i, V i`, `closure (V i) ⊆ U i` for every `i`, and
`⋂ k, V (σ k) ⊆ W σ` for every `(p+1)`-tuple `σ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem shrinking_open_covering
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X]
    {Z : Set X} (hZ : IsCompact Z)
    {p : ℕ} {I : Type*}
    (U : I → Set X) (hU : ∀ i, IsOpen (U i))
    (W : (Fin (p + 1) → I) → Set X) (hW : ∀ σ, IsOpen (W σ))
    (hcov : Z ⊆ ⋃ i, U i)
    (hint : ∀ σ, W σ ∩ Z = (⋂ k, U (σ k)) ∩ Z) :
    ∃ V : I → Set X,
      (∀ i, IsOpen (V i)) ∧
      Z ⊆ ⋃ i, V i ∧
      (∀ i, closure (V i) ⊆ U i) ∧
      (∀ σ : Fin (p + 1) → I, ⋂ k, V (σ k) ⊆ W σ)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechRefinement.cechDiagram
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09UZ.** Čech cohomology of an abelian sheaf in a fixed degree, as a
functor of the open covering: a refinement acts through the induced map of Čech complexes.
declarations.statement: def cechDiagram : OpenCoverSet X ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}
declarations.comment: the diagram of Čech cohomology over refinements

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechRefinement.colimitToCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09UZ.** The canonical comparison from the Čech cohomology of a
topological space — the colimit, over all open coverings, of the Čech cohomology of the
covering — to sheaf cohomology.
declarations.statement:
def colimitToCohomology :
    colimit (cechDiagram G p) ⟶
      (CechSite.derivedSectionsFunctor.{max u v} (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          (⊤ : Opens X) ⋙
        DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max u v} p).obj G

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechRefinement.ι_colimitToCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09UZ.** On each open covering, the comparison out of the colimit
restricts to the fixed-covering comparison of Stacks 03AX.
declarations.statement:
theorem ι_colimitToCohomology (U : OpenCoverSet X) :
    colimit.ι (cechDiagram G p) U ≫ colimitToCohomology G p =
      (CechSite.cechCohomologyToCohomology.{v} (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (hypercover U)
        (hypercover_mem_grothendieckTopology U) p).app G

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechRefinement.isIso_colimitToCohomology_one
declarations.doc:
The canonical comparison from the first Čech cohomology of a topological space — the
colimit, over all open coverings, of the first Čech cohomology of the covering — to the first
sheaf cohomology of an abelian sheaf is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimitToCohomology_one
    (G : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}) :
    IsIso (colimitToCohomology G 1)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.CechRefinement.isIso_colimitToCohomology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09V2.** Let `X` be a Hausdorff quasi-compact topological space and
`F` an abelian sheaf on `X`.  The canonical comparison of Stacks 09UZ from the Čech cohomology
of `X` — the colimit, over all open coverings of `X`, of the Čech cohomology of the covering —
to the sheaf cohomology of `F` is an isomorphism in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_colimitToCohomology
    (G : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max u v}) (n : ℤ) :
    IsIso (colimitToCohomology G n)
declarations.comment: the comparison of Stacks 09UZ is an isomorphism in every degree

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.isIso_cohomologyOfClosedMap
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-compact subset `Z` of a topological space `X` any two
distinct points of which have disjoint open neighbourhoods in `X`, the canonical map from the
colimit of the cohomology of an abelian sheaf `F` over the open neighbourhoods of `Z` to the
cohomology of the restriction of `F` to `Z` is an isomorphism in every degree.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_cohomologyOfClosedMap
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}) (p : ℕ) :
    IsIso (cohomologyOfClosedMap Z F p)

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.isIso_sectionsOfClosedMap
declarations.doc:
For a quasi-compact subset whose distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods in the
ambient space, the canonical restriction map from the sections on the open neighbourhoods of
`Z` to the global sections of the restriction of `F` to `Z` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_sectionsOfClosedMap (Z : Set X) (hZ : IsCompact Z)
    (hSep : ∀ x ∈ Z, ∀ y ∈ Z, x ≠ y →
      ∃ U V : Set X, IsOpen U ∧ IsOpen V ∧ x ∈ U ∧ y ∈ V ∧ Disjoint U V)
    (F : X.Sheaf (Type u)) :
    IsIso (sectionsOfClosedMap F Z)
declarations.comment: degree-zero comparison for sheaves of sets

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.ProperBaseChange.isIso_properBaseChangeMap
declarations.doc:
**Proper base change in topology.** For a closed separated morphism of ringed
spaces `f : X ⟶ Y` and a point `y` of `Y` with quasi-compact fibre, the canonical base-change
morphism from the stalk at `y` of the derived direct image to the derived sections on the fibre
is an isomorphism: for every bounded below complex `E` of `𝒪_X`-modules,

`(Rf_* E)_y = RΓ(f⁻¹(y), E|_{f⁻¹(y)})`

in the bounded below derived category of `𝒪_{Y,y}`-modules, naturally in `E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_properBaseChangeMap
    (hclosed : IsClosedMap (ConcreteCategory.hom f.hom.base))
    (hsep : IsSeparatedMap (ConcreteCategory.hom f.hom.base))
    (hcompact : IsCompact ((ConcreteCategory.hom f.hom.base) ⁻¹' ({y} : Set Y))) :
    IsIso (properBaseChangeMap f y)

declarations.name: Stacks.Cohomology.AbelianProperBaseChange.isIso_abelianBaseChange
declarations.doc:
**Proper base change for abelian sheaves on topological spaces, [Stacks, Tag 09V6].** For a
cartesian square of topological spaces

```
X' --g'--> X
|          |
f'         f
v          v
Y' --g---> Y
```

with `f` proper in the sense of [Stacks, Tag 005O] (5), the canonical base change morphism

`g^{-1} Rf_* ⟶ Rf'_* (g')^{-1}`

of `Stacks.Cohomology.BaseChange.abelianBaseChange` is an isomorphism of functors
`D⁺(X) ⥤ D⁺(Y')` on bounded below derived categories of abelian sheaves — hence an isomorphism
at every bounded below complex, naturally in it.

Both inputs of the criterion `Stacks.Cohomology.ProperBaseChange.isIso_baseChangeDerived` are
proved from properness.
They are the invertibility of the *underived* base change morphism
`Stacks.Cohomology.BaseChange.abelianSheafBaseChange`, `g^{-1} f_* ⟶ f'_* (g')^{-1}`, which is
`isIso_abelianSheafBaseChange_of_properMap` above — asked for by the criterion only at injective
sheaves, because both derived functors on its right-hand side are computed on a complex of
injectives, but proved at every abelian sheaf — and the vanishing
`R^{p>0} f'_*((g')^{-1} I) = 0` at an injective `I`, which is
`rightAcyclic_pushforward_pullback_of_injective`, together with the transfer of properness from
`f` to `f'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_abelianBaseChange (hcart : IsPullback g' f' f g)
    (hf : StacksDraft.Topology.IsProperMap.{u, u, u} (f.hom : X → Y)) :
    IsIso (BaseChange.abelianBaseChange f f' g g' hcart.w)
declarations.comment: derived proper base change for abelian sheaves: g^{-1} Rf_* ⟶ Rf'_* (g')^{-1} is an isomorphism of functors on D⁺ for f proper and the square cartesian; the underived base change morphism is inverted by isIso_abelianSheafBaseChange_of_properMap, the acyclicity R^p f'_* (g')^{-1} I = 0 for p > 0 is rightAcyclic_pushforward_pullback_of_injective, and properness of f' is isClosedMap_baseChange/isCompact_fiber_baseChange/isSeparatedMap_baseChange

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentComplexFrom_of_locally_boundedAbove
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09V7.** Let `X` be a ringed space, let `m` be an integer and let `𝒦` be a complex of
`𝒪_X`-modules which is bounded above on a neighbourhood of every point and whose term `𝒦^i` is
`(m - i)`-pseudo-coherent for every `i`. Then `𝒦` is an `m`-pseudo-coherent complex.

The hypothesis on the terms is turned into the form the induction uses by
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_singleFunctor_of_singleFunctor_zero`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_Q_of_locally_boundedAbove` is read back on
the complex through Stacks 08CC part (2).
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentComplexFrom_of_locally_boundedAbove (m : ℤ)
    (K : CochainComplex (OXMod.{u, u} X) ℤ)
    (hbdd : ∀ x : X.carrier, ∃ U : Opens X.carrier, x ∈ U ∧ ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ p : ℤ, b < p →
      IsZero ((restrictComplex K U).X p))
    (hK : ∀ i : ℤ, IsPseudoCoherentFrom
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) 0).obj (K.X i)) (m - i)) :
    IsPseudoCoherentComplexFrom K m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_homology
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09V8.** Let `X` be a ringed space, `m : ℤ` and `E` an object of the
derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules which is locally bounded above. If the cohomology sheaf `Hⁱ(E)`
is `(m - i)`-pseudo-coherent for every `i`, then `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_homology (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} X)) (m : ℤ)
    (hbdd : IsLocallyBoundedAbove E)
    (hcoh : ∀ i : ℤ, IsPseudoCoherentFrom
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) 0).obj
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) i).obj E)) (m - i)) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_singleFunctor_zero_neg_one_iff_isFinitePresentation
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a ringed space and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules.
Then `ℱ`, viewed in degree zero as an object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules, is
`(-1)`-pseudo-coherent if and only if `ℱ` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite presentation.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_singleFunctor_zero_neg_one_iff_isFinitePresentation
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)] (F : OXMod.{u, u} X) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) 0).obj F) (-1) ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation (R := structureSheafOfRings X) F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_singleFunctor_zero_iff_isFiniteType
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a ringed space and let `ℱ` be a sheaf of `𝒪_X`-modules. Then `ℱ`, viewed in degree
zero as an object of the derived category of `𝒪_X`-modules, is `0`-pseudo-coherent if and only if
`ℱ` is an `𝒪_X`-module of finite type.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_singleFunctor_zero_iff_isFiniteType
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (OXMod.{u, u} X)] (F : OXMod.{u, u} X) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) 0).obj F) 0 ↔
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteType (R := structureSheafOfRings X) F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedPushforwardOXMod
declarations.doc:
**The forward half of Stacks 09VA.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a morphism of ringed spaces whose
underlying continuous map is a closed immersion and such that `i_*𝒪_Z` is pseudo-coherent as an
`𝒪_X`-module. If `E ∈ D(𝒪_Z)` is `m`-pseudo-coherent then so is `Ri_*E`.

Pseudo-coherence is local on `X`. Away from the image of `i` the restriction of `Ri_*E` vanishes.
Around a point `i(z)` of the image, a strictly perfect approximation `𝒫 ⟶ 𝒦|_{i⁻¹U}` of a
complex `𝒦` representing `E` is pushed forward degreewise along `i|_{i⁻¹U}`; exactness of
pushforward preserves the two cohomological conditions, `(i|_{i⁻¹U})_*𝒫` is `m`-pseudo-coherent
because its terms are direct summands of powers of `(i|_{i⁻¹U})_*𝒪` and it is bounded, and the
target is `(Ri_*E)|_U`. Stacks 08CC part (1) in the form
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_approximation` finishes.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_derivedPushforwardOXMod
    (hi : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding i.hom.base)
    (hO : IsPseudoCoherent ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (OXMod.{u, u} X) 0).obj
      (pushforwardStructureModule i)))
    (m : ℤ) (E : DerivedCategory (OXMod.{u, u} Z)) (hE : IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom ((derivedPushforwardOXMod i hi).obj E) m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_derivedPushforwardOXMod
declarations.doc:
**The converse half of Stacks 09VA.** Let `i : Z ⟶ X` be a morphism of ringed spaces whose
underlying continuous map is a closed embedding and such that `i_*𝒪_Z` is pseudo-coherent as an
`𝒪_X`-module. If `Ri_*E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent for `E ∈ D(𝒪_Z)` then so is `E`.

Pseudo-coherence is local on `Z`, and the opens `i⁻¹W` for `W` open in `X` are a fundamental
system of neighbourhoods of a point of `Z`, so it is enough to produce, for each `z`, an open `W`
of `X` containing `i(z)` on which `E` becomes `m`-pseudo-coherent. Take for `W` an open on which
the cohomology of `Ri_*E` is bounded above
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.exists_isZero_homology_gt_derivedRestrict`); then the cohomology
of `E|_{i⁻¹W}` is bounded above as well, because `i_*` reflects zero objects
(`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isZero_homology_of_isZero_homology_derivedPushforward`), and
`AlgebraicGeometry.RingedSpace.isPseudoCoherentFrom_Q_of_derivedPushforwardOXMod_of_bounded'`
applies to `i|_{i⁻¹W} : Z|_{i⁻¹W} ⟶ X|_W`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_derivedPushforwardOXMod {Z X : RingedSpace.{u, u}}
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} Z)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{d} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X)]
    [∀ V : Opens X.carrier,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} (X.restrict V.isOpenEmbedding))]
    [∀ V : Opens Z.carrier,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} (Z.restrict V.isOpenEmbedding))]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : Topology.IsClosedEmbedding i.hom.base)
    (hO : IsPseudoCoherent ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} X) 0).obj
      (pushforwardStructureModule i)))
    (m : ℤ) (E : DerivedCategory (StrictlyPerfect.OXMod.{u, u} Z))
    (hE : IsPseudoCoherentFrom ((derivedPushforwardOXMod i hi).obj E) m) :
    IsPseudoCoherentFrom E m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_derivedPushforward_of_isFinite
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a finite morphism of schemes such that `f_*𝒪_X` is pseudo-coherent as an
`𝒪_Y`-module, that is, such that the object of `D(𝒪_Y)` it determines in degree zero is
pseudo-coherent in the sense of Stacks 08CB. Let `E` be an object of `D_{QCoh}(𝒪_X)`. Then `E` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent if and only if `Rf_*E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent.
declarations.statement:
theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_derivedPushforward_of_isFinite {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsFinite f]
    (hf : RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherent (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Y.Modules 0).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward f).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))))
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent)
    (m : ℤ) :
    RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherentFrom (X := X.toRingedSpace) E m ↔
      RingedSpace.IsPseudoCoherentFrom (X := Y.toRingedSpace)
        ((RingedSpace.derivedPushforward f.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isPseudoCoherentFrom_some_iff_forall_fin
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09VC.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of affine schemes locally of finite type, let
`E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `m` be an integer. Then `m`-pseudo-coherence of the derived
pushforward of `E` along *some* closed immersion of `X` into a finite-dimensional affine space
over `S` factoring `f` is equivalent to `m`-pseudo-coherence of the derived pushforward along
*every* such closed immersion.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isPseudoCoherentFrom_some_iff_forall_of_transport_fin`, whose
transport hypothesis is supplied by the two halves of Stacks 09VA —
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isPseudoCoherentFrom_pushforward_mapDerivedCategory` and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isPseudoCoherentFrom_of_pushforward_mapDerivedCategory` — and
whose side condition is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isPseudoCoherent_singleFunctor_pushforward_unit_affineSpace`.
Nothing is assumed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_some_iff_forall_fin {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X]
    [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (m : ℤ) :
    (∃ (n : ℕ) (i : X ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S),
      IsClosedImmersion i ∧
        i ≫ (AffineSpace.over (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S).hom = f ∧
          IsPseudoCoherentFromAfterPushforward i E m) ↔
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : X ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S),
        IsClosedImmersion i →
          i ≫ (AffineSpace.over (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S).hom = f →
            IsPseudoCoherentFromAfterPushforward i E m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isPseudoCoherentFromAfterPushforward_restrict
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09VD.** Let `S` be affine, let `V` be a standard open of `S`, let `X` be affine and
`f : X ⟶ V` locally of finite type, let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let `U` be an affine open
of `X`. If the equivalent conditions of Stacks 09VC hold for the pair `(X ⟶ V, E)`, then they hold
for the pair `(U ⟶ S, E|_U)`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exists_isPseudoCoherentFromAfterPushforward_affineOpen'` with
its three hypotheses discharged:
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pushforwardStructureSheafPseudoCoherentOver_basicOpen` at the
base `S` and at the base `V`, and
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pushforwardStructureSheafPseudoCoherentOver_affineSpace` for the
affine spaces over `V` mapping to the affine spaces over `S`. The last of the three is what needs
`V` to be a *standard* open.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFromAfterPushforward_restrict {S X : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsAffine S] [IsAffine X] (V : S.affineOpens) (hV : ∃ a : Γ(S, ⊤), V.1 = S.basicOpen a)
    (f : X ⟶ (V.1 : Scheme.{u})) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (U : X.affineOpens) (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (m : ℤ) :
    (∃ (n : ℕ) (i : X ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) (V.1 : Scheme.{u})),
      IsClosedImmersion i ∧
        i ≫ (AffineSpace.over (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) (V.1 : Scheme.{u})).hom = f ∧
          IsPseudoCoherentFromAfterPushforward i E m) →
      (∃ (n : ℕ) (i : (U.1 : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S),
        IsClosedImmersion i ∧
          i ≫ (AffineSpace.over (ULift.{u} (Fin n)) S).hom = U.1.ι ≫ f ≫ V.1.ι ∧
            IsPseudoCoherentFromAfterPushforward i
              ((restrictFunctor U.1.ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isPseudoCoherentFrom_some_iff_forall_standardCover
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09VE.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be a morphism of affine schemes locally of finite type, let
`E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` and let the basic opens of `g : Fin n → Γ(X, ⊤)` be a standard affine
open cover of `X`. Then the equivalent conditions of Stacks 09VC hold for every pair
`(X_{gⱼ} ⟶ S, E|_{X_{gⱼ}})` if and only if they hold for the pair `(X ⟶ S, E)`.

This is
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.isPseudoCoherentFrom_some_iff_forall_basicOpen'` with its
hypothesis `hOb` discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.pushforwardStructureSheafPseudoCoherentOver_basicOpen`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isPseudoCoherentFrom_some_iff_forall_standardCover {X S : Scheme.{u}}
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine S] (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (m : ℤ) {n : ℕ} (g : Fin n → Γ(X, ⊤))
    (hg : PrimeSpectrum.IsStandardOpenCoverOfSpectrum g) :
    (∀ j : Fin n, ∃ (k : ℕ) (i : (X.basicOpen (g j)).toScheme ⟶
        AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin k)) S),
      IsClosedImmersion i ∧
        i ≫ (AffineSpace.over (ULift.{u} (Fin k)) S).hom = (X.basicOpen (g j)).ι ≫ f ∧
          IsPseudoCoherentFromAfterPushforward i
            ((restrictFunctor (X.basicOpen (g j)).ι).mapDerivedCategory.obj E) m) ↔
      (∃ (k : ℕ) (i : X ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin k)) S),
        IsClosedImmersion i ∧
          i ≫ (AffineSpace.over (ULift.{u} (Fin k)) S).hom = f ∧
            IsPseudoCoherentFromAfterPushforward i E m)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.derivedSectionsPseudoCoherentComparison'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09VF.** Let `f : X ⟶ S` be locally of finite type, let `E` be an object of the derived
category of `𝒪_X`-modules all of whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent, and let `m` be an
integer. Then the following are equivalent:

1. `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`;
2. there are affine open coverings `S = ⋃ Vⱼ` and `f ⁻¹ᵁ Vⱼ = ⋃ Uⱼᵢ` such that each complex
   `RΓ(Uⱼᵢ, E)` is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `Γ(S, Vⱼ)`;
3. for every affine open `V ⊆ S` and every affine open `U ⊆ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, the complex `RΓ(U, E)` is
   `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `Γ(S, V)`.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.derivedSectionsPseudoCoherentComparison'_of_derivedSectionsSpec` with
its hypothesis discharged by
`AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.nonempty_iso_derivedSectionsSpec`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem derivedSectionsPseudoCoherentComparison' (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules)
    (hE : ∀ i : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.Modules i).obj E).IsQuasicoherent) (m : ℤ) :
    DerivedSectionsPseudoCoherentComparison' f E hE m

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_derivedPushforward_of_reductionImmersion
declarations.doc:
Let `f : X ⟶ S` and `g : Y ⟶ S` be morphisms of schemes locally of finite type and let
`i : X ⟶ Y` be a morphism over `S` which induces a closed immersion on reductions: there is a
closed immersion `j` of the reduction of `X` into the reduction of `Y` making the square with the
canonical immersions of the reductions commute. Let `E` be an object of `D(𝒪_X)` and `m` an
integer. Then `E` is `m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S` if and only if `Ri_*E` is
`m`-pseudo-coherent relative to `S`.

With the hypothesis on `i` weakened to a homeomorphism of `X` with a closed subset of `Y` the
equivalence fails, by
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.not_forall_isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_derivedPushforward`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem Scheme.Hom.isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_derivedPushforward_of_reductionImmersion
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ S) (g : Y ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] (i : X ⟶ Y)
    (hi : i ≫ g = f)
    (hred : ∃ j : X.nilradical.subscheme ⟶ Y.nilradical.subscheme,
      IsClosedImmersion j ∧
        j ≫ Y.nilradical.subschemeι = X.nilradical.subschemeι ≫ i)
    (E : DerivedCategory X.Modules) (m : ℤ) :
    Scheme.Hom.IsPseudoCoherentFrom f E m ↔
      Scheme.Hom.IsPseudoCoherentFrom g
        ((Stacks.Cohomology.DerivedAdjunctionOnRingedSpaces.derivedPushforward
          i.toLRSHom.toShHom).obj E) m
declarations.comment: corrected statement — Stacks erratum. The source's topological hypothesis, that i induce a homeomorphism of X with a closed subset of Y, makes the lemma false (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.not_forall_isPseudoCoherentFrom_iff_derivedPushforward, over the nodal curve A = {h ∈ k[s] | h(0) = h(1)} with B = k[s, 1/s]); it is replaced here by the hypothesis the source's proof actually uses, that i be a closed immersion on reductions, i.e. that A/rad(A) → B/rad(B) be surjective. Both directions, E and m arbitrary

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.pushforwardFunctor
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09VH.** Pushforward along a morphism of groupoid schemes, as a functor
on quasi-coherent modules equipped with groupoid descent data:  on objects it sends `(𝓕, α)` to
`(f_*𝓕, f_*α)`, and on morphisms it is the direct image of morphisms of modules.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pushforwardFunctor :
    QuasicoherentModule G ⥤ QuasicoherentModule H

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.pushforwardFunctor_obj_module
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09VH.** Pushforward along a morphism of groupoid schemes pushes the
underlying module forward along the map on objects.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforwardFunctor_obj_module (M : QuasicoherentModule G) :
    ((pushforwardFunctor f h).obj M).module =
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f.mapObjects.left).obj M.module

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.pushforwardFunctor_obj_alpha
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09VH.** The descent morphism of a pushed-forward module is the
pushed-forward descent morphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforwardFunctor_obj_alpha (M : QuasicoherentModule G) :
    Eq.ndrec (motive := fun X =>
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback H.target.left).obj X ⟶
        (Scheme.Modules.pullback H.source.left).obj X)
      ((pushforwardFunctor f h).obj M).alpha (pushforwardFunctor_obj_module f h M) =
      pushforwardDescent f h M

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.pushforwardFunctor_map_hom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09VH.** Pushforward of a morphism of quasi-coherent modules on a
groupoid scheme is the direct image of morphisms of modules.
declarations.statement:
theorem pushforwardFunctor_map_hom {M N : QuasicoherentModule G} (g : M ⟶ N) :
    (pushforwardFunctor_obj_module f h M) ▸
      (pushforwardFunctor_obj_module f h N) ▸
        (QuasicoherentModule.Hom.hom ((pushforwardFunctor f h).map g)) =
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f.mapObjects.left).map
        (QuasicoherentModule.Hom.hom g)

declarations.name: Stacks.Groupoids.GroupoidScheme.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09VH.** Pushforward along a morphism of groupoid schemes is right
adjoint to the pullback functor of Tag 03LJ:  on underlying modules the adjunction is the
inverse-image--direct-image adjunction along the map on objects, under which the two
compatibility conditions with the descent morphisms correspond.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackPushforwardAdjunction :
    pullbackFunctor f ⊣ pushforwardFunctor f h
declarations.comment: right adjointness to the pullback functor of Tag 03LJ

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.ConstantSpace.systemCosimplicialEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**A system of sheaves on the constant simplicial space on `X` is the same thing as a
cosimplicial sheaf on `X`.**
declarations.statement:
def systemCosimplicialEquivalence :
    SimplicialSheafSystem (constantSpace X) A ≌ CosimplicialObject (TopCat.Sheaf A X)
declarations.comment:
systems `(F_n, F(φ))` on the constant simplicial space `X_•` are cosimplicial
  objects in the category of sheaves on `X`

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.ConstantSpace.sheafCosimplicialEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**A sheaf on `X_{•,Zar}` is the same thing as a cosimplicial object in the category of
sheaves on `X`.** The equivalence is the description of Lemma 09VM
(`Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.sheafEquivalenceSimplicialSheafSystem`) followed by
`systemCosimplicialEquivalence`; the sheaf in degree `[n]` of the cosimplicial object attached to
a sheaf `F` is the restriction `F_n` of `F` to the opens of the `n`-th copy of `X`.
declarations.comment:
by Lemma 09VM a sheaf on `X_{•,Zar}` is the same thing as a cosimplicial object in
  the category of sheaves on `X`

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.cechNerveTerminalFrom_δ_π
declarations.doc:
**The face map `d^{n+1}_i` forgets the `i`-th coordinate.** On the simplicial object
`X_n = Y^{n+1}`, the `k`-th coordinate of `d_i` is the `(i.succAbove k)`-th coordinate, i.e. the
coordinates of `d_i(y_0, …, y_{n+1})` are those of `(y_0, …, y_{n+1})` with `y_i` left out.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechNerveTerminalFrom_δ_π {n : ℕ} (i : Fin (n + 2)) (k : Fin (n + 1)) :
    (cechNerveTerminalFrom Y).δ i ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => Y) k =
      Pi.π (fun _ : Fin (n + 2) => Y) (i.succAbove k)
declarations.comment: the face map `d^n_i` is the projection forgetting the `i`-th coordinate

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.cechNerveTerminalFrom_σ_π
declarations.doc:
**The degeneracy map `s^n_j` repeats the `j`-th coordinate.** On the simplicial object
`X_n = Y^{n+1}`, the `k`-th coordinate of `s_j` is the `(j.predAbove k)`-th coordinate, i.e.
`s_j(y_0, …, y_n) = (y_0, …, y_j, y_j, …, y_n)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem cechNerveTerminalFrom_σ_π {n : ℕ} (j : Fin (n + 1)) (k : Fin (n + 2)) :
    (cechNerveTerminalFrom Y).σ j ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin (n + 2) => Y) k =
      Pi.π (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => Y) (j.predAbove k)
declarations.comment: the degeneracy map `s^n_j` is the diagonal repeating the `j`-th coordinate

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.SimplicialOpen.toTopCat
declarations.doc:
**A morphism of `X_Zar` induces a continuous map.** An object `U ⊆ X_n` of the site of a
simplicial space is a topological space, and a morphism `U → V` given by `φ` induces the
continuous map `U → V` restricting `X(φ) : X_n → X_m`.
declarations.statement: def toTopCat : SimplicialOpen X ⥤ TopCat.{u}
declarations.comment: a morphism `U → V` of `X_Zar` given by `φ` induces a continuous map `U → V`

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.SimplicialOpen.toTopCat_map_comp_inclusion
declarations.doc:
The continuous map `U → V` induced by a morphism given by `φ` is the restriction of
`X(φ) : X_n → X_m`.
declarations.statement:
theorem toTopCat_map_comp_inclusion {U V : SimplicialOpen X} (f : U ⟶ V) :
    (toTopCat X).map f ≫ V.toOpens.inclusion' = U.toOpens.inclusion' ≫ X.map f.base
declarations.comment: the induced continuous map `U → V` is the restriction of `X(φ)`

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.componentPresheaf_isSheaf
declarations.doc:
**The restriction `F_n` of a sheaf on `X_Zar` to the opens of `X_n` is a sheaf on `X_n`.**
This holds for sheaves with values in any category.
declarations.statement:
theorem componentPresheaf_isSheaf {X : SimplicialObject TopCat.{u}} {A : Type w} [Category.{v} A]
    (F : Sheaf (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X) A) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) :
    TopCat.Presheaf.IsSheaf (componentPresheaf F.obj n)
declarations.comment: the restriction `F_n` of a sheaf `F` on `X_Zar` to the opens of `X_n` is a sheaf

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.SimplicialSheafSystem.transitionMap_comp
declarations.doc:
**`F(φ) ∘ F(ψ) = F(φ ∘ ψ)`.** The composite (Stacks 008L) of the `f`-maps `F(φ)` and `F(ψ)`
is the `f`-map of the composite. It is an `(X(φ) ≫ X(ψ))`-map while `F(φ ≫ ψ)` is an
`X(φ ≫ ψ)`-map, so the equality is heterogeneous.
declarations.comment: `F(φ) ∘ F(ψ) = F(φ ∘ ψ)`, composition of `f`-maps as in Sheaves 008L

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.sheafSystem
declarations.doc:
**The system `(F_n, F(φ))` of a sheaf on `X_Zar`.** A sheaf `F` on the site of a simplicial
space gives the sheaves `F_n` on the spaces `X_n`, obtained by restricting `F` to the opens of
`X_n`, together with the `X(φ)`-maps `F(φ) : F_m → F_n` formed by the restriction maps of `F`,
which satisfy `F(φ) ∘ F(ψ) = F(φ ∘ ψ)` and `F(id) = id`.
declarations.statement:
def sheafSystem :

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.isEquivalence_sheafToSimplicialSheafSystem
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09VM.** Let `X` be a simplicial topological space. The functor
`sheafToSimplicialSheafSystem` from sheaves on the site `X_Zar` of `X`
(`SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X`: opens of the spaces `X n`, morphisms over simplex
maps, coverings by open coverings inside one degree) to the category `SimplicialSheafSystem X A`
of systems `(F_n, F(φ))` of sheaves `F_n` on `X n` with `X.map φ`-maps `F(φ)` satisfying
`F(φ) ∘ F(ψ) = F(φ ∘ ψ)` and `F(id) = id`, which sends `F` to its restrictions to the degrees
and its restriction maps over simplex maps, is an equivalence of categories. The values are in
an arbitrary category `A`; sheaves of sets are the case `A = Type _`.
declarations.statement:
instance isEquivalence_sheafToSimplicialSheafSystem
    (X : SimplicialObject TopCat.{u}) (A : Type w) [Category.{v} A] :
    (sheafToSimplicialSheafSystem (X := X) (A := A)).IsEquivalence

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.SimplicialScheme.componentModulePushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09VP, part (1), for sheaves of modules on the total Zariski site.** The degree-`n`
component of the pushforward of a sheaf of `𝒪_V`-modules along a morphism `f : V ⟶ U` of
simplicial schemes is the pushforward of its degree-`n` component along `f_n : V_n ⟶ U_n`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def componentModulePushforwardIso (f : V ⟶ U) (G : Modules V)
    (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) :
    (componentModule U n).obj ((modulePushforward f).obj G) ≅
      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (f.app n)).obj ((componentModule V n).obj G)
declarations.comment: part (1) for sheaves of modules on the total Zariski site of a simplicial scheme

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.pushforwardComponentIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09VP, part (1).** The component in degree `n` of direct image along a
morphism of simplicial spaces is the direct image along its degree-`n` component.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pushforwardComponentIso
    {X Y : SimplicialObject TopCat.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) :
    letI : IsMorphismOfSites.{u} (SimplicialOpen.pullback f)
      (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X)
      (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology Y) :=
        SimplicialOpen.pullback_isMorphismOfSites f
    (SimplicialOpen.pullback f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
        (Type u) (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X)
        (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology Y) ⋙
      (sheafEquivalenceSimplicialSheafSystem X (Type u)).toEquivalence.functor ⋙
      SimplicialSheafSystem.componentFunctor X (Type u) n ≅
    (sheafEquivalenceSimplicialSheafSystem Y (Type u)).toEquivalence.functor ⋙
      SimplicialSheafSystem.componentFunctor Y (Type u) n ⋙
        TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward (Type u) (f.app n)

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.pullbackComponentIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09VP, part (2).** The component in degree `n` of inverse image along a
morphism of simplicial spaces is the inverse image along its degree-`n` component.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pullbackComponentIso
    {X Y : SimplicialObject TopCat.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) :
    letI : IsMorphismOfSites.{u} (SimplicialOpen.pullback f)
      (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X)
      (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology Y) :=
        SimplicialOpen.pullback_isMorphismOfSites f
    (SimplicialOpen.pullback f).sheafPullback
        (Type u) (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology X)
        (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology Y) ⋙
      (sheafEquivalenceSimplicialSheafSystem Y (Type u)).toEquivalence.functor ⋙
      SimplicialSheafSystem.componentFunctor Y (Type u) n ≅
    (sheafEquivalenceSimplicialSheafSystem X (Type u)).toEquivalence.functor ⋙
      SimplicialSheafSystem.componentFunctor X (Type u) n ⋙
      TopCat.Sheaf.pullback (Type u) (f.app n)

declarations.doc:

functor and assume `v` has a left adjoint `u : C ⥤ D`.  Then `u` is cocontinuous.

Cocontinuity of a left adjoint is equivalent to cover preservation of its right adjoint
(`Adjunction.isCocontinuous_iff_coverPreserving`), and a continuous functor preserves covering
sieves (`CoverPreserving.of_isContinuous`).
declarations.statement:

    u.IsCocontinuous J K

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Adjunction.isMorphismOfSites_of_isLeftAdjoint
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09VR, final assertion.** A continuous functor `v : D ⥤ C` which admits a left adjoint
defines a morphism of sites `f : C → D`, i.e. `v` is continuous and the induced pullback

Indeed a right adjoint is representably flat (`RepresentablyFlat.of_isRightAdjoint`: the comma
category `StructuredArrow X v` has an initial object, namely the unit of the adjunction), so this
is the criterion of Stacks 00X5 recorded as
`CategoryTheory.Functor.isMorphismOfSites_of_representablyFlat`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialObject.Truncated.hasPointwiseRightKanExtension_of_hasBinaryProducts_or_hasFiniteConnectedLimits
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a category.

* If `C` has products of pairs of objects, then every `0`-truncated simplicial object `F` of `C`
  admits a pointwise right Kan extension along `(Δ_{≤0} ⊆ Δ)ᵒᵖ`; equivalently `cosk_0` exists, as
  the right adjoint `Truncated.cosk 0` of `sk_0` ([Stacks, Example 0182]).
* If `C` has finite connected limits, then for every `k ≥ 1` every `k`-truncated simplicial object
  `F` of `C` admits a pointwise right Kan extension along `(Δ_{≤k} ⊆ Δ)ᵒᵖ`; equivalently `cosk_k`
  exists.
declarations.statement:
public theorem hasPointwiseRightKanExtension_of_hasBinaryProducts_or_hasFiniteConnectedLimits :
    (HasBinaryProducts C → ∀ F : SimplicialObject.Truncated C 0,
        (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion 0).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F) ∧
      ((∀ (J : Type) [SmallCategory J] [FinCategory J] [IsConnected J], HasLimitsOfShape J C) →
        ∀ (k : ℕ), 0 < k → ∀ F : SimplicialObject.Truncated C k,
          (SimplexCategory.Truncated.inclusion k).op.HasPointwiseRightKanExtension F)
declarations.comment: the two items of the remark, as the two conjuncts; "cosk_k exists" is spelled as the existence of the pointwise right Kan extensions along `(Δ_{≤k} ⊆ Δ)ᵒᵖ` that define `Truncated.cosk k`, and each hypothesis is an antecedent of its own item so that item (1) stays a claim about categories with products of pairs alone

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.nonempty_cechCohomologyZeroIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09VV.** Degree-zero Čech cohomology of a hypercovering of a presheaf is
the degree-zero cohomology of that presheaf with coefficients in the given sheaf of abelian
groups.

The source asserts an identification; the isomorphism realising it is `cechCohomologyZeroIso`,
of which this is the existence statement.

theorem nonempty_cechCohomologyZeroIso (J : Pretopology C)
    (G : Functor Cᵒᵖ (Type q)) (K : HypercoveringOf.{q, w} J G)
    (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)}) :
    Nonempty (cechCohomology J G K F 0 ≅ presheafCohomologyZero J G F)

injective abelian sheaf on a hypercovering of a presheaf vanishes.

    (I : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)})

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.cechCohomologyIsoOfInjective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09VW.** For a hypercovering `K` of a presheaf `G` and an injective
abelian sheaf `I`, the Čech cohomology `Ȟᵖ(K, I)` is the degree-zero cohomology `H⁰(G, I)` of `G`
when `p = 0` and is zero when `p > 0`.

The degree-zero branch is Tag 09VV's `cechCohomologyZeroIso`, which holds for every abelian sheaf
and needs no injectivity; the positive-degree branch is `cechCohomology_isZero_of_injective`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def cechCohomologyIsoOfInjective (J : Pretopology C)
    (G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type q) (K : HypercoveringOf.{q, w} J G)
    (I : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)})
    [Injective I] (p : ℕ) :
    cechCohomology.{q, w, v, u} J G K I p ≅
      if p = 0 then presheafCohomologyZero.{q, w, v, u} J G I else 0

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_hypercoverPresheafToDerivedSections
declarations.doc:
For a hypercovering `K` of a presheaf `G` on a site with equalizers and fibre products there
are a canonical map `ψ` from the sections over `G` to derived sections at the single complex, and
a map

`α : s(-(K)) ⟶ RΓ(G, -)`

in `D⁺(Ab)`, functorial in the abelian sheaf, compatible with the augmentation of `s(-(K))` by the
sections over `G`; and both are isomorphisms at every injective sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_hypercoverPresheafToDerivedSections :
    ∃ (ψ : (presheafSectionsFunctor.{q, w, v, u} J G K ⋙
          singlePlus AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)}) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Plus.Q ⟶
        presheafDerivedSectionsFunctor.{q, w, v, u} J G K)
      (α : hypercoverPresheafDerivedFunctor.{q, w, v, u} J G K ⟶
        presheafDerivedSectionsFunctor.{q, w, v, u} J G K),
      Functor.whiskerRight
            (epsNat (presheafSectionsFunctor.{q, w, v, u} J G K)
              (SemiRepresentable.sectionsComplexIntFunctor.{q, w, v, u} J.toGrothendieck
                K.toSimplicialObject)
              ((hypercoverPresheafAugmentation.{q, w, v, u} J G K).app)
              (fun {_ _} φ ↦ (hypercoverPresheafAugmentation.{q, w, v, u} J G K).naturality φ)
              (SemiRepresentable.isZero_sectionsComplexIntFunctor_obj_X.{q, w, v, u}
                J.toGrothendieck K.toSimplicialObject))
            DerivedCategory.Plus.Q ≫ α = ψ ∧
        (∀ F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)},
          Injective F → IsIso (ψ.app F)) ∧
        ∀ F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)},
          Injective F → IsIso (α.app F)
declarations.comment: the comparison map s(F(K)) ⟶ RΓ(G, F) in D⁺(Ab), functorial in F

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.exists_presheafCechCohomologyToCohomology
declarations.doc:
The comparison map of `exists_hypercoverPresheafToDerivedSections` induces, in every degree
`i`, a natural transformation

`Ȟ^i(K, -) ⟶ H^i(G, -)`

of functors from abelian sheaves to abelian groups, and these are isomorphisms at every injective
sheaf.

The source is the `i`-th cohomology of the complex `s(-(K))` itself, i.e. the Čech cohomology of
the hypercovering, and the target is the `i`-th cohomology of `RΓ(G, -)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_presheafCechCohomologyToCohomology :
    ∃ β : ∀ i : ℤ,
        (SemiRepresentable.sectionsComplexIntFunctor.{q, w, v, u} J.toGrothendieck
              K.toSimplicialObject ⋙
            HomologicalComplex.homologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)}
              (ComplexShape.up ℤ) i) ⟶
          (presheafDerivedSectionsFunctor.{q, w, v, u} J G K ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor
              AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)} i),
      ∀ (i : ℤ) (F : Sheaf J.toGrothendieck AddCommGrpCat.{max (max u v) (max q w)}),
        Injective F → IsIso ((β i).app F)
declarations.comment: the induced natural transformations Ȟ^i(K, -) ⟶ H^i(G, -)
