declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.derivedSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WJ, the spectral sequence.** For an object `K` of `D^+(C_total)` there is a
cohomological spectral sequence, functorial in `K`: the right derived functor, along the
localization of the bounded below homotopy category at the quasi-isomorphisms, of the spectral
sequence of the double complex `A^{q,p} = Γ(C_p, Z^q_p)` read from its first page.

A bounded below complex of injectives `I^•` representing `K` is exactly an object at which the
unit of this right derived functor is invertible
(`isIso_derivedSpectralSequenceUnit_app`), so the value at `K` *is* the spectral sequence of the
double complex `A^{q,p} = Γ(C_p, I^q_p)` of the source's proof.
declarations.comment: the spectral sequence for K in D^+(C_total), as a functor of K

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.derivedSpectralSequence_pageOneIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WJ, the first page.** `E_1^{p,q} = H^q(C_p, K_p)`: the first page of the spectral
sequence of Stacks 09WJ at `(p, q)` is the sheaf cohomology on the component site `C_p` of the
restriction of `K` to `C_p`, naturally in the object `K` of `D^+(C_total)`.

Together with `isZero_derivedPageOne_d_of_ne`, which pins the shape of
`d_1^{p,q} : E_1^{p,q} → E_1^{p+1,q}`, this is the first page and the first differential of
Stacks 09WJ.
declarations.comment: the first page E_1^{p,q} = H^q(C_p, K_p) for K in D^+(C_total), naturally in K

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isZero_derivedPageOne_d_of_ne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WJ, the first differential.** `d_1^{p,q} : E_1^{p,q} → E_1^{p+1,q}`: the
differential of the first page out of the bidegree `(p, q)` lands in the bidegree `(p + 1, q)`,
every other component being zero. Together with the type of
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.derivedSpectralSequence`, which provides
`d (p, q) (p + 1, q) : E_1^{p,q} ⟶ E_1^{p+1,q}`, this is the shape of `d_1` that Stacks 09WJ
asserts.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_derivedPageOne_d_of_ne (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}))
    (p q p' q' : ℤ) (h : (p', q') ≠ (p + 1, q)) :
    ((S.derivedSpectralSequence.obj K).page 1 le_rfl).d (p, q) (p', q') = 0
declarations.comment: the first differential d_1^{p,q} : E_1^{p,q} → E_1^{p+1,q} for K in D^+(C_total)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.derivedSpectralSequence_abutsTo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WJ, the convergence.** The spectral sequence of Stacks 09WJ abuts to
`H^{p+q}(C_total, K)`: its infinity page at `(p, q)` is the `p`-th graded piece of a finite
filtration of the sheaf cohomology of the total site in degree `p + q`.

Every object of `D^+(C_total)` is represented by a bounded below complex of injective abelian
sheaves -- the inclusion of the bounded below homotopy category of complexes of injectives into
`D^+(C_total)` is essentially surjective -- and at such a complex the convergence is
`derivedSpectralSequence_abutsTo_of_injective`.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedSpectralSequence_abutsTo
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u})) :
    CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.AbutsTo (S.derivedSpectralSequence.obj K)
      (fun n => (S.totalDerivedCohomologyFunctor n).obj K)
declarations.comment: the abutment H^{p+q}(C_total, K) for K in D^+(C_total)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cohomologySpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WJ, the spectral sequence.** For an abelian sheaf `F` on the total site of a
simplicial-site situation there is a cohomological spectral sequence, functorial in `F`: the
spectral sequence of the filtration by the simplicial coordinate of the double complex
`A^{q,p} = Γ(C_p, I^q_p)` of the chosen injective resolution of `F`, presented from its first
page.

The functor laws hold because filtered homotopic morphisms of double complexes induce the same
maps on the pages from the first on; an injective resolution is functorial only up to homotopy,
which is why the presentation starts at the first page.
declarations.statement:
def cohomologySpectralSequence :
    Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u} ⥤ CohomologicalSpectralSequence Ab.{u} 1
declarations.comment: the spectral sequence, for an abelian sheaf on the total site, functorial in it

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cohomologySpectralSequence_pageOneIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WJ, the first page.** `E_1^{p,q} = H^q(C_p, F_p)`: the first page of the spectral
sequence of the simplicial-site situation at `(p, q)` is the sheaf cohomology of the restriction
of `F` to the component site `C_p`, naturally in the abelian sheaf `F`.

Together with
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.pageOneIsoColumnHomology_hom_d`, which identifies
`d_1^{p,q} : E_1^{p,q} → E_1^{p+1,q}` with the differential of the complex of Stacks 0D77, this
is the first page and the first differential of Stacks 09WJ.
declarations.statement:
def cohomologySpectralSequence_pageOneIso :
    S.pageOneFunctor n q ≅ S.componentCohomologyFunctor ⦋n⦌ q
declarations.comment: the first page E_1^{p,q} = H^q(C_p, F_p) for an abelian sheaf, naturally in it

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.isZero_pageOne_d_of_ne
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WJ, the first differential.** `d_1^{p,q} : E_1^{p,q} → E_1^{p+1,q}`: the
differential of the first page out of the bidegree `(p, q)` lands in the bidegree `(p + 1, q)`,
every other component being zero. Together with the type of
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cohomologySpectralSequence`, which provides
`d (p, q) (p + 1, q) : E_1^{p,q} ⟶ E_1^{p+1,q}`, this is the shape of `d_1` that Stacks 09WJ
asserts.

What that differential *is* under the identification of the first page is
`CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.pageOneIsoColumnHomology_hom_d`: up to the sign
`(-1)^q`, the map induced on `H^q` by the differential of the complex of Stacks 0D77.
declarations.statement:
theorem isZero_pageOne_d_of_ne (F : Sheaf S.totalTopology Ab.{u}) (p q p' q' : ℤ)
    (h : (p', q') ≠ (p + 1, q)) :
    (((S.cohomologySpectralSequence).obj F).page 1 le_rfl).d (p, q) (p', q') = 0
declarations.comment: the first differential d_1^{p,q} : E_1^{p,q} → E_1^{p+1,q}

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSiteSituation.cohomologySpectralSequence_abutsTo
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WJ, the convergence.** The spectral sequence of the simplicial-site situation
abuts to `H^{p+q}(C_total, F)`: its infinity page at `(p, q)` is the `p`-th graded piece of a
finite filtration of the sheaf cohomology of the total site in degree `p + q`.

This is `sectionsSpectralSequence_abutsTo_total`, whose abutment is the cohomology of the total
complex of `A^{•,•}`, transported along the comparison of Stacks 0133 and read from the first
page.
declarations.statement:
theorem cohomologySpectralSequence_abutsTo :
    CategoryTheory.SpectralSequence.AbutsTo
      ((S.cohomologySpectralSequence).obj F) (S.totalCohomologyZ F)
declarations.comment: the abutment H^{p+q}(C_total, F) for an abelian sheaf

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.isMorphismOfSites_pullbackMap
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (1).** For a simplex map `φ : [m] ⟶ [n]` the base change functor
`v_φ = Over.pullback f_φ : C/U_m ⥤ C/U_n` along `f_φ : U_n ⟶ U_m` represents a morphism of
sites `C/U_n ⟶ C/U_m` between the localizations of `(C, J)` in the two degrees: it is
continuous and the induced pullback on sheaves of sets is exact.

This is Stacks 09W9 applied to `f_φ`, and it is the datum making the localizations `C/U_n`
into a simplicial object in the category whose objects are sites and whose morphisms are
morphisms of sites.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_pullbackMap {m n : SimplexCategory} (φ : m ⟶ n) :
    (Over.pullback (U.map φ.op)).IsMorphismOfSites
      (J.over (U.obj (op m))) (J.over (U.obj (op n)))
declarations.comment: part (1), each transition is a morphism of sites

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.pullbackMapId
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (1).** The transition morphism of sites attached to an identity simplex
map is the identity: base change along `f_{𝟙} = 𝟙 U_n` is isomorphic to the identity functor
of `C/U_n`.
declarations.statement:
def pullbackMapId (n : SimplexCategory) :
    Over.pullback (U.map (𝟙 n).op) ≅ 𝟭 (Over (U.obj (op n)))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.pullbackMapComp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (1).** The transition morphisms of sites are compatible with
composition of simplex maps: base change along `f_{ψ ≫ φ} = f_φ ≫ f_ψ` is isomorphic to base
change along `f_ψ` followed by base change along `f_φ`, by the canonical isomorphism
`W ×_{U_l} U_n ≅ (W ×_{U_l} U_m) ×_{U_m} U_n` of chosen fibre products.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.sheafPushforwardIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (1).** The morphism of topoi `Sh(C/U_n) ⟶ Sh(C/U_m)` attached to the
transition morphism of sites of a simplex map `φ : [m] ⟶ [n]` is the one attached to the
localization functor `j = Over.map f_φ`: the direct image of the cocontinuous functor `j` is
the direct image of the continuous functor `v_φ = Over.pullback f_φ`.
declarations.statement:
def sheafPushforwardIso {m n : SimplexCategory} (φ : m ⟶ n) :
    (Over.map (U.map φ.op)).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u)
        (J.over (U.obj (op n))) (J.over (U.obj (op m))) ≅
      (Over.pullback (U.map φ.op)).sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
        (J.over (U.obj (op m))) (J.over (U.obj (op n)))
declarations.comment: part (1), the transitions induce the localization morphisms of topoi

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.totalComparisonEquivalence
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (2).** The construction of Stacks 09WC applied to the simplicial object
in sites of part (1) reproduces the category `(C/U)_total`: the comparison functor, which is
the identity on objects and the bijection `totalHomEquiv` on morphisms, is an isomorphism of
categories.
declarations.statement: def totalComparisonEquivalence : Grothendieck (slices U) ≌ PullbackTotal U
declarations.comment: part (2), the comparison of the two total categories

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.pullbackTotalCoverings_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (2).** The two sites have the same covering families: a family of the
total category of Stacks 09WC is covering exactly when it is the image under the comparison of
a covering family of `(C/U)_total`. Both topologies are generated by these families.
declarations.statement:
theorem pullbackTotalCoverings_iff (𝒱 : Covering.{u, u, u} (PullbackTotal U)) :
    pullbackTotalCoverings J U 𝒱 ↔
      ∃ 𝒰 : Covering.{u, u, u} (Grothendieck (slices U)),
        SimplicialCoverings.total (slices U) (sliceCoverings J U) 𝒰 ∧
          𝒱 = ⟨(totalComparison U).obj 𝒰.1, 𝒰.2.map (totalComparison U)⟩
declarations.comment: part (2), the coverings of the two total sites agree

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.totalTopology_eq
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (2).** The total site of that situation is the site `(C/U)_total`: the
generic construction of the total site, applied to the simplicial family of sites `n ↦ C/U_n`,
gives the category `(C/U)_total` and the topology `totalTopology` on the nose.
declarations.statement: theorem totalTopology_eq : (situation J U).totalTopology = SimplicialOver.totalTopology J U
declarations.comment: part (2), the generic total site is (C/U)_total

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.isMorphismOfSites_augmentationPullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (3).** For an augmentation `a : U → X`, base change along
`a_0 : U_0 ⟶ X` is continuous with exact pullback on sheaves of sets, that is, it represents a
morphism of sites `a_0 : C/U_0 → C/X`. This is Stacks 09W9 applied to `a_0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMorphismOfSites_augmentationPullback :
    (Over.pullback (augmentationApp U a (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0)))).IsMorphismOfSites
      (J.over X) (J.over (U.obj (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))))
declarations.comment: part (3), a_0 is a morphism of sites

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.augmentationVertexCompat
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (3).** The functor `u_0 = Over.pullback a_0` representing the
augmentation satisfies the compatibility of Stacks 0D6Z part (A): the composites `u_φ ∘ u_0`
for the vertices `φ : [0] ⟶ [n]` of a simplicial degree agree, both being canonically
isomorphic to base change along `a_n`. Chosen fibre products make this an isomorphism rather
than the equality of functors the source writes, exactly as in part (1).
declarations.statement:
def augmentationVertexCompat (n : SimplexCategory) (φ ψ : SimplexCategory.mk 0 ⟶ n) :
    Over.pullback (augmentationApp U a (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))) ⋙
        Over.pullback (U.map φ.op) ≅
      Over.pullback (augmentationApp U a (op (SimplexCategory.mk 0))) ⋙
        Over.pullback (U.map ψ.op)
declarations.comment: part (3), the vertex compatibility of the augmentation

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.augmentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (3).** The augmentation `a_0 : C/U_0 → C/X` of the simplicial family of
sites `n ↦ C/U_n`: the localization functor `j_{a_0} = Over.map a_0` is cocontinuous and its
composite with the functor of any vertex of a simplicial degree is `j_{a_n}`, which does not
mention the vertex. By `isMorphismOfSites_augmentationPullback` and
`augmentationSheafPushforwardIso` this is the augmentation given by the morphism of sites
`a_0` of Stacks 0D6Z part (A): the two presentations of `a_0` give the same morphism of topoi
`Sh(C/U_0) ⟶ Sh(C/X)`.
declarations.statement: def augmentation : (simplicialSite J U).Augmentation (Cat.of (Over X)) (J.over X)
declarations.comment: part (3), a_0 is an augmentation of the simplicial site C/U

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.augmentationMorphismOfTopoi
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (3).** The morphism of topoi `a : Sh((C/U)_total) ⟶ Sh(C/X)` which the
augmentation `a_0` gives: the morphism of topoi of Stacks 0D70 attached to the augmentation of
the simplicial family of sites `n ↦ C/U_n` determined by `a_0`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def augmentationMorphismOfTopoi :
    MorphismOfTopoi (Sheaf (SimplicialOver.totalTopology J U) (Type u))
      (Sheaf (J.over X) (Type u))
declarations.comment: part (3), the morphism of topoi Sh((C/U)_total) to Sh(C/X) of the augmentation

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.augmentationMorphismOfTopoi_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WL part (3).** That morphism of topoi is the one above: its direct image is the
direct image of the cocontinuous functor `V/U_n ↦ V/X` of Stacks 09X8. The two are *equal*,
not merely isomorphic.
declarations.statement:
theorem augmentationMorphismOfTopoi_pushforward :
    (augmentationMorphismOfTopoi J U a).pushforward =
      (augmentationFunctor U a).sheafPushforwardCocontinuous (Type u)
        (SimplicialOver.totalTopology J U) (J.over X)
declarations.comment: part (3), the augmentation gives the morphism of topoi above

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.augmentationSheafLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WM, part (1).** The functor `a^{Sh}_! : Sh((C/K)_total) ⥤ Sh(C)` is left adjoint
to the inverse image `a^{-1} : Sh(C) ⥤ Sh((C/K)_total)` of the augmentation.

The inverse image of the augmentation is restriction along `j_total`, because `j_total` is
cocontinuous as well as continuous, and restriction along a continuous functor has a left
adjoint.
declarations.statement:
def augmentationSheafLowerShriekAdjunction :
    augmentationSheafLowerShriek J K ⊣
      (CocontinuousSimplicialSite.Augmentation.totalMorphismOfTopoi
        (augmentation J K)).inverseImage
declarations.comment: part (1): the left adjoint on sheaves of sets

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.augmentationAbelianLowerShriekAdjunction
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WM, part (2).** The functor `a_! : Ab((C/K)_total) ⥤ Ab(C)` is left adjoint to the
inverse image `a^{-1} : Ab(C) ⥤ Ab((C/K)_total)` of the augmentation, which on abelian sheaves as
on sheaves of sets is restriction along `j_total`.
declarations.comment: part (2): the left adjoint on abelian sheaves

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.augmentationInverseImageComponentIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WM, part (3).** The inverse image of the augmentation followed by restriction to
the simplicial degree `n` is the inverse image `a_n^{-1}` of the augmentation of that degree,
which by Stacks 0D8B is the inverse image of the morphism of topoi of the localization functor
`j_n : C/K_n ⥤ C`, that is restriction along `j_n`. So `a^{-1}ℱ` is in degree `n` the sheaf
`a_n^{-1}ℱ`.
declarations.statement:
def augmentationInverseImageComponentIso (n : SimplexCategory) :
    (CocontinuousSimplicialSite.Augmentation.totalMorphismOfTopoi
          (augmentation J K)).inverseImage ⋙ (situation J K).restrict n ≅
      (localizationMorphism J K n).inverseImage
declarations.comment: part (3): the inverse image in each simplicial degree

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.augmentationAbelianPushforwardFork
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WM, part (4).** The fork of the direct image `a_*𝒢` of an abelian sheaf on the
total site over the two maps `a_{0,*}𝒢_0 ⟶ a_{1,*}𝒢_1` attached to the two vertices of the
one-simplex, which are the two cofaces of the cosimplicial sheaf `n ↦ a_{n,*}𝒢_n`. Its map is the
canonical projection of `a_*𝒢` onto `a_{0,*}𝒢_0`, and it equalises the two because the
projections form a cone.
declarations.statement:
def augmentationAbelianPushforwardFork :
    Fork ((augmentationAbelianComponentDiagram J K G).map
        (SimplexCategory.const (SimplexCategory.mk 0) (SimplexCategory.mk 1) 0))
      ((augmentationAbelianComponentDiagram J K G).map
        (SimplexCategory.const (SimplexCategory.mk 0) (SimplexCategory.mk 1) 1))
declarations.comment: part (4): the direct image is the equalizer of the two vertex maps

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.augmentationAbelianPushforwardForkIsLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WM, part (4).** That fork is a limit: the direct image `a_*𝒢` is the equalizer of
the two maps `a_{0,*}𝒢_0 ⟶ a_{1,*}𝒢_1`.

The direct image is by construction the limit of the cosimplicial sheaf `n ↦ a_{n,*}𝒢_n` over the
whole simplex category, and the degree-zero leg of such a limit is a limit fork of the two maps
in degrees `0 ⇉ 1`, which is the dual of Simplicial, Lemma 14.20.2.
declarations.statement:
def augmentationAbelianPushforwardForkIsLimit :
    IsLimit (augmentationAbelianPushforwardFork J K G)
declarations.comment: part (4): the equalizer is a limit

registrations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.Initial
registrations.comment: the definition of an initial functor, and so of an initial subcategory

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.surjective_prodComparison_colim
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WQ (1).** If every pair of objects of `I` admits a common upper bound,
then for all set-valued diagrams `M, N : I ⥤ Type v` the canonical comparison
`colim (M ⨯ N) ⟶ colim M ⨯ colim N` is surjective.

Given a pair of elements, choose representatives at indices `i` and `j`, push both
along arrows into a common `k`, and pair them there; the resulting element of
`colim (M ⨯ N)` maps to the original pair.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_prodComparison_colim [HasColimitsOfShape I (Type v)]
    (h : ∀ x y : I, ∃ (z : I) (_ : x ⟶ z) (_ : y ⟶ z), True)
    (M N : I ⥤ Type v) :
    Function.Surjective (prodComparison (colim : (I ⥤ Type v) ⥤ Type v) M N)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.surjective_setColimit_to_addCommGrpColimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WR.** Let `I` be a nonempty category in which every pair of objects
has a common upper bound. Then for any diagram `M : I ⥤ AddCommGrpCat` the canonical
comparison from the colimit of the underlying sets to the underlying set of the
colimit in `AddCommGrpCat` is surjective.
declarations.statement:
theorem surjective_setColimit_to_addCommGrpColimit
    {I : Type u} [Category.{v} I] [Nonempty I]
    (hI : ∀ x y : I, ∃ (z : I) (_ : x ⟶ z) (_ : y ⟶ z), True)
    (M : I ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{w})
    [HasColimit (M ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat)] [HasColimit M] :
    Function.Surjective
      (colimit.desc (M ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat)
        ((forget AddCommGrpCat).mapCocone (colimit.cocone M)))

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.hasSpanCocone_component
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WS.** Each connected component of a category with span cocones again has
span cocones. Together with `CategoryTheory.instIsConnectedComponent` and
`CategoryTheory.decomposedTo` this exhibits such a category as a disjoint union of
connected categories with span cocones.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasSpanCocone_component {J : Type u} [Category.{v} J] (h : HasSpanCocone J)
    (j : ConnectedComponents J) : HasSpanCocone j.Component

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.colimMap_injective_of_span
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WT (1).** If every span in `I` admits a commutative completion, then a
componentwise-injective natural transformation between `Type`-valued diagrams over `I`
induces an injective map on colimits.
declarations.statement:
theorem colimMap_injective_of_span
    {I : Type u} [Category.{v} I] (hI : HasSpanCocone I)
    {M N : I ⥤ Type w} [HasColimit M] [HasColimit N]
    (α : M ⟶ N) (hα : ∀ i : I, Function.Injective (α.app i)) :
    Function.Injective (colimMap α : colimit M ⟶ colimit N)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Limits.exists_diagram_addCommGrp_colimMap_not_injective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WT (2).** The analogue of part (1) fails for `AddCommGrp`-valued diagrams:
there is a span-completing index category and a componentwise-injective natural
transformation of diagrams of abelian groups whose induced map on colimits is not
injective.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_diagram_addCommGrp_colimMap_not_injective :
    ∃ (I : Type) (_ : SmallCategory I) (_ : HasSpanCocone I)
      (M N : I ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{0}) (α : M ⟶ N)
      (_ : ∀ i : I, Function.Injective (α.app i)),
      ¬ Function.Injective (colimMap α)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsStronglyCartesian.comp_functor
declarations.doc:
If `θ : a' ⟶ a` is a strongly cartesian lift of `φ : b ⟶ F.obj a` along `F : A ⥤ B`, and `φ`
is in turn a strongly cartesian lift of `f : R ⟶ G.obj (F.obj a)` along `G : B ⥤ C`, then `θ` is a
strongly cartesian lift of `f` along `F ⋙ G`.

Taking `φ := F.map θ` and `f := G.map (F.map θ)`: strong cartesianness of `θ` for `F` together with
strong cartesianness of `F.map θ` for `G` implies strong cartesianness of `θ` for `F ⋙ G`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsStronglyCartesian.comp_functor (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ C)
    {a' a : A} {b : B} {R : C}
    (f : R ⟶ G.obj (F.obj a)) (φ : b ⟶ F.obj a) (θ : a' ⟶ a)
    [F.IsStronglyCartesian φ θ] [G.IsStronglyCartesian f φ] :
    (F ⋙ G).IsStronglyCartesian f θ

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFibered.comp_functor
declarations.doc:
A composite of fibred functors is fibred: if `F : A ⥤ B` and `G : B ⥤ C` are fibred, then so
is `F ⋙ G`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFibered.comp_functor (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ C)
    [F.IsFibered] [G.IsFibered] : (F ⋙ G).IsFibered

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.IsFiberedInGroupoids.comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WW.** The composition of two functors that are fibred in groupoids is
fibred in groupoids.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsFiberedInGroupoids.comp (p : 𝒜 ⥤ ℬ) (q : ℬ ⥤ 𝒞)
    (hp : p.IsFiberedInGroupoids) (hq : q.IsFiberedInGroupoids) :
    (p ⋙ q).IsFiberedInGroupoids

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Functor.isStack_comp_of_isInheritedTopology
declarations.doc:
Let `(𝒞, J)` be a site, let `p : 𝒳 ⥤ 𝒞` be a stack over `𝒞`, endow `𝒳` with the topology `J𝒳`
inherited from `(𝒞, J)` and let `q : 𝒴 ⥤ 𝒳` be a stack over `(𝒳, J𝒳)`. Then `𝒴` is a stack over
`𝒞`, along `q ⋙ p`; and if `p` and `q` define stacks in groupoids, that is if both are fibred in
groupoids, then `𝒴` is a stack in groupoids over `𝒞`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isStack_comp_of_isInheritedTopology (hp : p.IsStack J)
    (hJ𝒳 : IsInheritedTopology.{max u₂ v₂} p J J𝒳) (hq : q.IsStack J𝒳) :
    (q ⋙ p).IsStack J ∧
      (p.IsFiberedInGroupoids →
        q.IsFiberedInGroupoids → (q ⋙ p).IsFiberedInGroupoids ∧ (q ⋙ p).IsStack J)

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.isContinuous_id_zariski_qc
declarations.doc: A quasi-compact sheaf on a localized site is a Zariski sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_id_zariski_qc (X : S.category) :
    (Functor.id (Over X)).IsContinuous (S.zariskiTopology.over X)
      (S.qcSite.grothendieckTopology.over X)
declarations.comment: ε_X comes from the identity functor of LC/X, which is continuous

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.qcComparisonMorphism
declarations.doc: The change-of-topology morphism of topoi `ε_X : Sh(LC_qc/X) → Sh(LC_Zar/X)`.
declarations.statement:
def qcComparisonMorphism (X : S.category) :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (S.qcSite.grothendieckTopology.over X) (Type (max u t)))
      (Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over X) (Type (max u t)))
declarations.comment: the induced morphism ε_X : LC_qc/X → LC_Zar/X

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiComparisonMorphism
declarations.doc: The Zariski comparison morphism of topoi `π_X : Sh(LC_Zar/X) → Sh(X)`.
declarations.statement:
def zariskiComparisonMorphism (X : S.category) :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over X) (Type (max u t)))
      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) (Type (max u t)))

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.qcTopologicalMorphism
declarations.doc:
The comparison morphism of topoi `a_X : Sh(LC_qc/X) → Sh(X)`, defined as the composite
`π_X ∘ ε_X`.
declarations.statement:
def qcTopologicalMorphism (X : S.category) :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf (S.qcSite.grothendieckTopology.over X) (Type (max u t)))
      (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) (Type (max u t)))
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi a_X = π_X ∘ ε_X : Sh(LC_qc/X) → Sh(X)

declarations.name: IsQcCovering.of_isOpenEmbedding
declarations.doc:
**An open covering is a qc covering.** A jointly surjective family of open embeddings into a
locally quasi-compact space is a qc covering: a point `x` lies in the image of some `fᵢ`, which
is open, so `x` has a quasi-compact neighbourhood `K` inside that image, and `K` is the image of
the quasi-compact set `fᵢ⁻¹(K)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQcCovering.of_isOpenEmbedding {ι : Type*} {X : ι → Type*} {Y : Type*}
    [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (X i)] [TopologicalSpace Y] [LocallyCompactSpace Y]
    {f : ∀ i, X i → Y} (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenEmbedding (f i))
    (hsurj : ∀ y, ∃ i, y ∈ Set.range (f i)) : IsQcCovering f
declarations.comment: an open covering of an object of LC is a qc covering

declarations.name: IsQcCovering.of_iSup_eq_top
declarations.doc:
**An open covering `X = ⋃ Uᵢ` gives a qc covering `{Uᵢ → X}`**, for a locally quasi-compact
space `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem IsQcCovering.of_iSup_eq_top {ι : Type*} {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    [LocallyCompactSpace X] (U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (hU : iSup U = ⊤) :
    IsQcCovering (fun i => (Subtype.val : U i → X))
declarations.comment: an open covering of an object of LC is a qc covering

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.qcPretopology
declarations.doc:
**`LC` with its qc coverings is a site.** The qc coverings of Stacks 09X0 form a
pretopology on `LC`, by Stacks 09X1.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def qcPretopology : Pretopology LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u}
declarations.comment: LC with the collection of qc coverings forms a site

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.qcTopology
declarations.doc: The qc topology on `LC`: the Grothendieck topology generated by the qc coverings.
declarations.statement: def qcTopology : GrothendieckTopology LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.comap_precoverage_le_qcPrecoverage
declarations.doc:
**The qc topology is stronger than the usual one.** Every open covering of an object of
`LC`, i.e. every jointly surjective family of open embeddings, is a qc covering, because the
objects of `LC` are locally quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem comap_precoverage_le_qcPrecoverage :
    TopCat.precoverage.comap locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop.{u} ≤ qcPrecoverage
declarations.comment: the qc topology is stronger than the usual one

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.toGrothendieck_comap_precoverage_le_qcTopology
declarations.doc: The topology of open coverings of `LC` is coarser than the qc topology.
declarations.statement:
theorem toGrothendieck_comap_precoverage_le_qcTopology :
    (TopCat.precoverage.comap locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop.{u}).toGrothendieck ≤
      qcTopology
declarations.comment: the qc topology is stronger than the usual one, as topologies

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiTopology
declarations.doc: The Zariski Grothendieck topology, on the same category as the quasi-compact site.
declarations.statement:
def zariskiTopology
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) :
    GrothendieckTopology S.category
declarations.comment: the topology of the site LC_Zar

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.zariskiObjectCohomology
declarations.doc:
Cohomology of an abelian sheaf on the localized Zariski site `LC_Zar/X`, over an object `U`
over `X`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev zariskiObjectCohomology
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X : S.category)
    (F : Sheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})
    (U : Over X) (n : ℕ)
    [HasSheafify ((S.zariskiTopology.over X).over U) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v}]
    [HasExt.{a} (Sheaf ((S.zariskiTopology.over X).over U)
      AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v})] : Type a
declarations.comment: the cohomology H^n_Zar(U, H) over an object U of LC_Zar/X

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.opensToSlice
declarations.doc:
The open subsets of `X`, as objects over `X`: the functor `Opens X ⥤ LC_Zar/X` sending an
open `U` to the open immersion `U → X`. The accompanying property fixes the underlying map of
`U` as the open embedding with image exactly `U`, which determines the functor up to the unique
isomorphism over `X`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def opensToSlice
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X : S.category) :
    {F : Opens X.obj ⥤ Over X // ∀ U : Opens X.obj,
      Topology.IsOpenEmbedding ((F.obj U).hom : ((F.obj U).left).obj → X.obj) ∧
      Set.range ((F.obj U).hom : ((F.obj U).left).obj → X.obj) = U.1}
declarations.comment: the functor X_Zar → LC_Zar/X, U ↦ U

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.opensToSlice_isContinuous
declarations.doc:
The open-subset functor is continuous from the small Zariski site of `X` to the localized
Zariski site of `LC`, so it induces the comparison morphism of topoi.
declarations.statement:
theorem opensToSlice_isContinuous
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X : S.category) :
    (S.opensToSlice X).1.IsContinuous (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj)
      (S.zariskiTopology.over X)
declarations.comment: the functor X_Zar → LC_Zar/X is continuous

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.opens_hasPullbacks_and_hasTerminal
declarations.doc:
**`X_Zar` has fibre products and a final object.** The category of open subsets of a
topological space has fibre products (intersections) and a final object (the whole space).
declarations.statement:
theorem opens_hasPullbacks_and_hasTerminal (X : TopCat.{u}) :
    HasPullbacks (Opens X) ∧ HasTerminal (Opens X)
declarations.comment: X_Zar has fibre products and a final object

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.sheaf_opens_grothendieckTopology_eq
declarations.doc:
**`Sh(X_Zar) = Sh(X)`.** The sheaves on the small site `X_Zar` of open subsets of `X` are by
definition the sheaves on the topological space `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem sheaf_opens_grothendieckTopology_eq (X : TopCat.{u}) (A : Type*) [Category* A] :
    Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) A = TopCat.Sheaf A X

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.ofArrows_mem_zariskiPrecoverage_iff
declarations.doc:
**The coverings of `LC_Zar`.** A family of morphisms of `LC_qc` is a covering of `LC_Zar`
exactly when it is a covering of `LC_qc` all of whose members are open immersions. A family of
open immersions is a qc covering iff it is jointly surjective: a qc covering is jointly
surjective, and an open covering is a qc covering because the target is locally quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem ofArrows_mem_zariskiPrecoverage_iff {ι : Type*} {T : S.category}
    {Y : ι → S.category} (f : ∀ i, Y i ⟶ T) :
    Presieve.ofArrows Y f ∈ S.zariskiPrecoverage T ↔
      Presieve.ofArrows Y f ∈ S.qcSite.pretopology T ∧
        ∀ i, IsOpenEmbedding (f i : (Y i).obj → T.obj)
declarations.comment: the site LC_Zar: the coverings of LC_qc by open immersions

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.isContinuous_id_zariskiTopology_qc
declarations.doc:
**The identity functor `LC_Zar → LC_qc` is continuous**, because every covering of `LC_Zar`
is a covering of `LC_qc`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isContinuous_id_zariskiTopology_qc :
    (𝟭 S.category).IsContinuous S.zariskiTopology S.qcSite.grothendieckTopology
declarations.comment: the identity functor LC_Zar → LC_qc is continuous

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.qcSiteComparisonMorphism
declarations.doc:
**The morphism of sites `ε : LC_qc → LC_Zar`.** The identity functor `LC_Zar → LC_qc` is
continuous (`isContinuous_id_zariskiTopology_qc`) and its induced functor on sheaves of sets,
qc sheafification `qcSiteInverseImage`, is exact (`qcSiteInverseImage_preservesFiniteLimits`,
`qcSiteInverseImage_preservesFiniteColimits`); so it defines a morphism of sites, whose morphism
of topoi `Sh(LC_qc) → Sh(LC_Zar)` is this one.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def qcSiteComparisonMorphism :
    MorphismOfTopoi
      (Sheaf S.qcSite.grothendieckTopology (Type (max u t)))
      (Sheaf S.zariskiTopology (Type (max u t)))
declarations.comment: the morphism of sites ε : LC_qc → LC_Zar

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.opensToSlice_preservesFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**The functor `X_Zar → LC_Zar/X` commutes with fibre products and the final object.** The
functor `U ↦ (U → X)` is representably flat, so it preserves all finite limits; in particular it
carries intersections of opens to fibre products and `X` to the final object `id : X → X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem opensToSlice_preservesFiniteLimits (X : S.category) :
    PreservesFiniteLimits (S.opensToSlice X).1
declarations.comment: the functor X_Zar → LC_Zar/X commutes with fibre products and final object

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff
declarations.doc:
The category of Hausdorff, locally quasi-compact topological spaces and continuous
maps.
declarations.statement: abbrev LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff
declarations.comment: the category LC of Hausdorff and locally quasi-compact spaces

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.t2Space_and_locallyCompactSpace_iff
declarations.doc:
**The convention "Hausdorff and locally quasi-compact".** A topological space is Hausdorff
and locally quasi-compact (every point has a fundamental system of quasi-compact
neighbourhoods) if and only if it is *locally compact* in the sense often used in the
literature: Hausdorff, with every point having a quasi-compact neighbourhood.
declarations.statement:
theorem t2Space_and_locallyCompactSpace_iff (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] :
    T2Space X ∧ LocallyCompactSpace X ↔ T2Space X ∧ WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X
declarations.comment: Hausdorff and locally quasi-compact is the literature's locally compact

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.isSeparatedMap_hom
declarations.doc:
**Morphisms of `LC` are separated.** The source of a morphism of `LC` is Hausdorff, so the
morphism is a separated continuous map.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSeparatedMap_hom {X Y : LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsSeparatedMap f.hom
declarations.comment: any morphism of LC is a separated continuous map

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.isProperMap_iff_isUniversallyClosedMap
declarations.doc:
**A morphism of `LC` is proper iff it is universally closed.** Proper means separated and
universally closed, and every morphism of `LC` is separated.
declarations.statement:
theorem isProperMap_iff_isUniversallyClosedMap {X Y : LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    StacksDraft.Topology.IsProperMap.{u, u, w} f.hom ↔
      StacksDraft.Topology.IsUniversallyClosedMap.{u, u, w} f.hom
declarations.comment: a morphism of LC is proper iff it is universally closed

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.hasPullbacks
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WZ, the fibre-product clause.** The category of Hausdorff, locally
quasi-compact spaces has fibre products.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable instance hasPullbacks :
    HasPullbacks (LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u})

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.hasTerminal
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WZ, the final-object clause.** The category of Hausdorff, locally
quasi-compact spaces has a final object.
declarations.statement: public instance hasTerminal : HasTerminal LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.hasFiniteLimits
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WZ, the finite-limits clause.** The category of Hausdorff, locally
quasi-compact spaces has all finite limits: it has a final object and fibre products.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable instance hasFiniteLimits :
    HasFiniteLimits LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u}

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.compactSpace_pullback
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09WZ, the quasi-compactness clause.** Given morphisms `f : X ⟶ Z` and
`g : Y ⟶ Z` of Hausdorff, locally quasi-compact spaces with `X` and `Y` quasi-compact, the
fibre product `X ×_Z Y` in `LC` is quasi-compact.
declarations.statement:
theorem compactSpace_pullback {X Y Z : LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Z)
    (g : Y ⟶ Z) [CompactSpace X] [CompactSpace Y] :
    CompactSpace (pullback f g : LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u})

registrations.name: IsQcCovering
registrations.comment: qc coverings of locally quasi-compact Hausdorff spaces

declarations.name: isQcCovering_of_homeomorph
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X1** (1). If `X' → X` is an isomorphism in `LC`, that is, a homeomorphism of
Hausdorff locally quasi-compact spaces, then the singleton family `{X' → X}` is a qc covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQcCovering_of_homeomorph {X' X : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X'] [T2Space X'] [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X']
    [TopologicalSpace X] [T2Space X] [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X]
    (e : X' ≃ₜ X) :
    IsQcCovering (X := fun _ : Unit => X') (fun _ => (e : X' → X))

declarations.name: isQcCovering_comp
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X1** (2). If `f` is a qc covering of `Y` and each `g i` is a qc covering of `X i`,
then the family of composites `(i, j) ↦ f i ∘ g i j` is a qc covering of `Y`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQcCovering_comp {ι : Type*} {X : ι → Type*} {Y : Type*}
    {J : ι → Type*} {Z : ∀ i, J i → Type*}
    [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (X i)] [TopologicalSpace Y]
    [∀ i, T2Space (X i)] [∀ i, WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace (X i)]
    [T2Space Y] [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace Y]
    [∀ i j, TopologicalSpace (Z i j)]
    [∀ i j, T2Space (Z i j)] [∀ i j, WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace (Z i j)]
    (f : ∀ i, X i → Y) (hf : ∀ i, Continuous (f i))
    (g : ∀ i (j : J i), Z i j → X i)
    (hcov : IsQcCovering f)
    (hcov' : ∀ i, IsQcCovering (g i)) :
    IsQcCovering (X := fun p : Σ i, J i => Z p.1 p.2)
      (fun p => f p.1 ∘ g p.1 p.2)

declarations.name: isQcCovering_base_change
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X1** (3). If `f` is a qc covering of `Y` and `h : X' → Y` is a morphism of `LC`,
then the family of projections `pr_{X'} : X' ×_Y X i → X'` is a qc covering of `X'`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isQcCovering_base_change {ι : Type*} {X : ι → Type*} {Y X' : Type*}
    [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (X i)] [TopologicalSpace Y] [TopologicalSpace X']
    [∀ i, T2Space (X i)] [∀ i, WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace (X i)]
    [T2Space Y] [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace Y]
    [T2Space X'] [WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace X']
    (f : ∀ i, X i → Y) (hf : ∀ i, Continuous (f i))
    (h : X' → Y) (hh : Continuous h)
    (hcov : IsQcCovering f) :
    IsQcCovering (X := fun i => FiberProd h (f i))
      (fun i => FiberProd.prX' h (f i))

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.exists_boundedLCSubcategory
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X2, the bounded-subcategory clause.** Any prescribed small set of Hausdorff,
locally quasi-compact spaces is contained in a bounded full subcategory of `LC` which is
closed under existing countable limits and colimits and under the cardinal bound of
Equation 046U.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_boundedLCSubcategory
    (S₀ : Set LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u}) [Small.{u} S₀] :
    Nonempty (BoundedLCSubcategory S₀)

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactQcSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X2, the site clause.** The data defining the big quasi-compact site `LC_qc`.

Its objects form the cardinal-cutoff bounded subcategory supplied by
`Stacks.Topology.BoundedLCSubcategory`, with an additional representative condition for the
prescribed cardinal bound. Its chosen pretopology is represented by quasi-compact covering
families indexed in `Type w`, and every quasi-compact presieve has a combinatorially
equivalent chosen representative.
declarations.statement:
structure LocallyQuasiCompactQcSite
    (initialObjects : Set LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u})
    (bound : Cardinal.{u} → Cardinal.{u})

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.exists_locallyQuasiCompactQcSite
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X2, the covering-set clause.** On any prescribed bounded subcategory `LC_α` of
`LC` there is a set of quasi-compact covering families which forms a pretopology and contains a
combinatorially equivalent representative of every quasi-compact covering family; that is, the
quasi-compact site `LC_qc` exists on `LC_α`.

The set of coverings is the one generated by *all* quasi-compact families: the three site
axioms are Stacks 09X1, and the representative condition is satisfied by the family itself,
which is legitimate because the families on `LC_α` indexed in `Type (u + 1)` already form a
set.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_locallyQuasiCompactQcSite
    (S₀ : Set LocallyQuasiCompactHausdorff.{u})
    (B : BoundedLCSubcategory S₀) :
    ∃ S : LocallyQuasiCompactQcSite.{u, u + 1} S₀ Cardinal.stacksBound,
      S.boundedSubcategory = B

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactQcSite.mem_smallPretopology_iff_isQcCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X2, the smallness clause.** The small model really is the quasi-compact site: a
presieve of it is covering exactly when the sieve it generates, read in `LC_qc`, is refined by a
quasi-compact covering family.

The pretopology of the small model is the maximal one generating the transported topology, so
membership in it unwinds to membership of a generated sieve in the topology generated by the
chosen set `Cov` of quasi-compact coverings, which is `isCovering_iff_isQcCovering`.
declarations.statement:
theorem mem_smallPretopology_iff_isQcCovering {Y : S.smallSite} (R : Presieve Y) :
    R ∈ S.smallPretopology Y ↔
      ∃ E : PreZeroHypercover.{u + 1} (S.smallEquivalence.inverse.obj Y),
        S.IsQcCovering E ∧
          E.presieve₀ ≤
            ((Sieve.generate R).functorPushforward S.smallEquivalence.inverse).arrows
declarations.comment: the coverings of a small model of LC_qc are the quasi-compact coverings

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactQcSite.smallSheafEquiv
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X2, the topos clause.** Sheaves on `LC_qc` and sheaves on its small model are the
same, at any coefficients. The comparison is a dense subsite inclusion for the transported
topology, so restriction along it is an equivalence.
declarations.statement:
def smallSheafEquiv (A : Type t₁) [Category.{t₂} A] :
    Sheaf S.grothendieckTopology A ≌ Sheaf S.smallTopology A
declarations.comment: LC_qc and a small model of it have the same topos

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.qcDirectImageTopologicalInverseImageIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X3, the identification `ε_{X,*} a_X^{-1} = π_X^{-1}`.** Direct image along the
change-of-topology morphism undoes quasi-compact sheafification on the Zariski comparison
inverse images, because those are already quasi-compact sheaves.
declarations.comment: the identification eps_{X,*}a_X^{-1} = pi_X^{-1} on sheaves of sets

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.qcTopologicalInverseImage_fullyFaithful
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X3, full faithfulness of `a_X^{-1}`.** The inverse image along the comparison
morphism `a_X = π_X ∘ ε_X : Sh(LC_qc/X) → Sh(X)` is full and faithful on sheaves of sets.

This is the sentence Stacks 0DAG opens with, for the bottom horizontal arrow of the diagram of
Stacks 0DAF: `(h_{-1})^{-1}` is fully faithful with quasi-inverse `h_{-1,*}`.

Composing with `ε_{X,*}` gives `π_X^{-1}` up to the isomorphism
`qcDirectImageTopologicalInverseImageIso`; that composite is therefore fully faithful, and
`ε_{X,*}` is faithful, so `a_X^{-1}` is fully faithful.
declarations.statement:
theorem qcTopologicalInverseImage_fullyFaithful (X : S.category) :
    (qcTopologicalInverseImage.{u, w, t} S X).Full ∧
      (qcTopologicalInverseImage.{u, w, t} S X).Faithful
declarations.comment: full faithfulness of the composite inverse image a_X^{-1} on sheaves of sets

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.qcTopologicalAdjunction_unit_isIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X3, the quasi-inverse clause.** The unit of the adjunction
`a_X^{-1} ⊣ a_{X,*}` of the comparison morphism of topoi is an isomorphism: `a_{X,*}` recovers
every sheaf on the space from its inverse image.
declarations.statement:
theorem qcTopologicalAdjunction_unit_isIso (X : S.category) :
    IsIso (qcTopologicalMorphism.{u, w, t} S X).adj.unit
declarations.comment: the unit of a_X^{-1} is invertible on sheaves of sets

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.isSheaf_qc_germSectionsPresheaf
declarations.doc:
The presheaf on the localized quasi-compact site `LC_qc/X'` whose sections over
`h : W ⟶ X'` are the global sections of the germ-model inverse image `h^{-1}F` is a sheaf.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_qc_germSectionsPresheaf
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X' : S.category)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X'.obj) (Type (max u t))) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (S.qcSite.grothendieckTopology.over X')
      (germSectionsPresheaf S X' F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.isIso_toSheafify_comparisonInverseImage
declarations.doc:
The unit of quasi-compact sheafification is an isomorphism on the comparison inverse image
`π_{X'}^{-1}F`: `ε_{X'}^{-1}π_{X'}^{-1}F` is `π_{X'}^{-1}F`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_toSheafify_comparisonInverseImage
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X' : S.category)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X'.obj) (Type (max u t))) :
    IsIso (toSheafify (S.qcSite.grothendieckTopology.over X')
      ((comparisonInverseImage.{u, w, t} S X').obj F).obj)

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.isSheaf_germSectionsPresheaf
declarations.doc:
**The germ-model sections presheaf is a sheaf.** The presheaf on the localized Zariski site
`LC_Zar/X'` whose sections over `h : W ⟶ X'` are the global sections of the germ-model inverse
image `h^{-1}F` satisfies the sheaf condition for the localized Zariski topology: an open covering
of `W` by objects of the site and a family of germ sections agreeing on the overlaps determine a
unique germ section on `W`. This is the first assertion of Stacks 09X3.
declarations.statement:
theorem isSheaf_germSectionsPresheaf
    (S : LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.{u, w} S₀ Bound) (X' : S.category)
    (F : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X'.obj) (Type (max u t))) :
    Presheaf.IsSheaf (S.zariskiTopology.over X') (germSectionsPresheaf S X' F)

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.germSectionsPresheafIso
declarations.doc:
**The sections formula of Stacks 09X3 for the Zariski site, naturally in the object of the
localized site.** For an object `X'` of the locally quasi-compact Zariski site and a sheaf of sets
`F` on its space, the comparison inverse image `π_{X'}^{-1}F` is the germ-model sections presheaf

`(h : W ⟶ X') ↦ Γ(W, h^{-1}F)`,

as presheaves on the localized Zariski site `LC_Zar/X'`.

The identification is read off the universal property rather than computed on either side: the
germ-model sections sheaf corepresents morphisms out of the comparison inverse image
(`germSectionsMapOutProperty`), which the comparison inverse image corepresents by its own
adjunction, so the two agree.

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.qcCohomologyComparisonIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X4 for abelian sheaves.** For an object `X` of `LC_qc` and an abelian sheaf `F`
on the space underlying `X`, the cohomology of the localized quasi-compact site with
coefficients in `a_X^{-1}F` is the cohomology of the space with coefficients in `F`:

`H^n_{qc}(X, a_X^{-1}F) ≅ H^n(X, F)`,

naturally in `F`.
declarations.statement:
def qcCohomologyComparisonIso (n : ℕ) :
    qcTopologicalAbelianInverseImage.{u, w, v} S X ⋙
        (qcGlobalSections.{u, w, v} S X).rightDerived n ≅
      (spaceGlobalSections.{u, w, v} S X).rightDerived n
declarations.comment:
part (1): H^n(X, F) = H^n_qc(X, a_X^{-1}F) for an abelian sheaf F on X, naturally
in F, with cohomology read as the right derived functors of global sections

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.constantSheafQcCohomologyComparisonIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X4, the constant-sheaf example.** For an abelian group `A`, the cohomology of the
space `X` with coefficients in the constant sheaf on `A` is the cohomology of the localized
quasi-compact site with coefficients in its constant sheaf on `A`:

`H^n(X, A) ≅ H^n_{qc}(X, A)`,

naturally in `A`.
declarations.statement:
def constantSheafQcCohomologyComparisonIso (n : ℕ) :
    constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.obj) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} ⋙
        (spaceGlobalSections.{u, w, v} S X).rightDerived n ≅
      constantSheaf (S.qcSite.grothendieckTopology.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{max (u + 1) v} ⋙
        (qcGlobalSections.{u, w, v} S X).rightDerived n
declarations.comment: the example: H^n(X, A) = H^n_qc(X, A) for an abelian group A, naturally in A

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.LocallyQuasiCompactZariskiSituation.qcHypercohomologyComparisonIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X4 for bounded below complexes.** For an object `X` of `LC_qc` and `K` in
`D⁺(X)`, the hypercohomology of the space with coefficients in `K` is the hypercohomology of the
localized quasi-compact site with coefficients in `a_X^{-1}K`:

`H^n(X, K) ≅ H^n_{qc}(X, a_X^{-1}K)`,

naturally in `K`.
declarations.statement:
def qcHypercohomologyComparisonIso (n : ℤ) :
    spaceHypercohomology.{u, w, v} S X n ≅
      (qcTopologicalAbelianInverseImage.{u, w, v} S X).mapDerivedCategoryPlus ⋙
        qcHypercohomology.{u, w, v} S X n
declarations.comment:
part (2): H^n(X, K) = H^n_qc(X, a_X^{-1}K) for K in D^+(X), naturally in K, with
hypercohomology read as the cohomology of the right derived functor of global sections on D^+

declarations.name: proper_surjective_isQcCovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Tag 09X5 / Lemma 21.31.4.** Let `X` and `Y` be Hausdorff and
locally quasi-compact topological spaces (objects of `LC`) and let `f : X → Y`
be continuous (a morphism of `LC`). If `f` is proper and surjective, then the
family `{f : X → Y}` is a qc covering.
declarations.statement:
theorem proper_surjective_isQcCovering {X Y : Type*}
    [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
    [T2Space X] [LocallyCompactSpace X] [T2Space Y] [LocallyCompactSpace Y]
    (f : X → Y) (hproper : IsProperMap f)
    (hsurj : Function.Surjective f) :
    IsQuasiCompactCovering f

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.LocalizationAtPresheaf.hasPullbacks_and_hasEqualizers
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X6, the site `C/G` has fibre products and equalizers.** If `C` has fibre products
and equalizers, so does the localization `C/G` of `C` at a presheaf of sets `G`: the projection
`C/G ⥤ C` creates connected limits.
declarations.statement:
theorem hasPullbacks_and_hasEqualizers [HasPullbacks C] [HasEqualizers C] :
    HasPullbacks (CostructuredArrow (yoneda (C := C)) G) ∧
      HasEqualizers (CostructuredArrow (yoneda (C := C)) G)
declarations.comment: the site `C/G` of pairs `(U, s)`, `s ∈ G(U)`, has fibre products and equalizers

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.LocalizationAtPresheaf.sectionsOverPresheafSheafifyIso
declarations.doc:
**`H⁰(G, -) = H⁰(G^#, -)`** (Stacks 079X, observation (1), quoted in Stacks 09X6): the free
abelian sheaf functor inverts the sheafification map `G ⟶ G^#`.
declarations.comment: `H⁰(G, -) = H⁰(G^#, -)`, the functor whose derived functor is `RΓ(G, -)`

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.LocalizationAtPresheaf.derivedSectionsOverPresheafIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X6, `RΓ(G, E) = RΓ(C/G, j⁻¹E)`.** Let `C` be a site and `G` a presheaf of sets on
`C`, let `RΓ(G, -)` be the derived functor of `H⁰(G, -) = H⁰(G^#, -)`, maps out of `G` (Stacks
079X), and let `j : C/G ⥤ C` be the localization functor of Stacks 0791. Then

`RΓ(G, E) = RΓ(C/G, j⁻¹E)`

naturally in `E` in the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on `C`: the analogue of
Stacks 03F3 for the localization at `G`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSectionsOverPresheafIso [HasDerivedCategory (Sheaf J AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    [HasDerivedCategory (Sheaf (localizationTopology J G) AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
    [HasDerivedCategory AddCommGrpCat.{u}] :
    derivedSectionsOverPresheaf J G ≅
      ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda G).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u}
          (localizationTopology J G) J).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        Stacks.DerivedFunctor.totalRightDerived
          (Sheaf.Γ (localizationTopology J G) AddCommGrpCat.{u})
declarations.comment:
`RΓ(G, E) = RΓ(C/G, j⁻¹E)` for the localization functor `j : C/G → C`, the analogue
  of Tag 03F3; an isomorphism of functors on the unbounded derived category

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.LocalizationAtPresheaf.derivedGlobalSectionsLocalizationIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X6, `RΓ(C/G, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, a⁻¹E)`.** For a hypercovering `K` of a presheaf
of sets `G` on a site `C` with equalizers and fibre products, regarded as a hypercovering of the
site `C/G`, and the canonical augmentation `a : Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C/G)`, derived global
sections on `C/G` are derived global sections on the total site of the inverse image. This is
Stacks 0D8H for the site `C/G`, as the remark says.
declarations.statement:
def derivedGlobalSectionsLocalizationIso :
    Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsBase (Cat.of (CostructuredArrow (yoneda (C := C)) G))
        (localizationPretopology G P).toGrothendieck ≅
      Augmentation.derivedTotalInverseImage
          (hypercoveringSituation (localizationPretopology G P) (localizedHypercovering G P H))
          (Cat.of (CostructuredArrow (yoneda (C := C)) G))
          (localizationPretopology G P).toGrothendieck
          (hypercoveringAugmentation (localizationPretopology G P)
            (localizedHypercovering G P H)) ⋙
        Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsTotal
          (hypercoveringSituation (localizationPretopology G P) (localizedHypercovering G P H))
declarations.comment:
for a hypercovering `K` of `G`, `RΓ(C/G, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, a⁻¹E)` with `a` the
  canonical augmentation; an isomorphism of functors on the unbounded derived category, which
  contains `D⁺(C/G)`

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.LocalizationAtPresheaf.derivedSectionsOverPresheafInverseImageIso
declarations.doc: **Stacks 09X6, `RΓ(G, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, a⁻¹j⁻¹E)`.**
declarations.statement:
def derivedSectionsOverPresheafInverseImageIso :
    derivedSectionsOverPresheaf P.toGrothendieck G ≅
      (localizationInverseImage G P).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        Augmentation.derivedTotalInverseImage
            (hypercoveringSituation (localizationPretopology G P) (localizedHypercovering G P H))
            (Cat.of (CostructuredArrow (yoneda (C := C)) G))
            (localizationPretopology G P).toGrothendieck
            (hypercoveringAugmentation (localizationPretopology G P)
              (localizedHypercovering G P H)) ⋙
          Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsTotal
            (hypercoveringSituation (localizationPretopology G P) (localizedHypercovering G P H))
declarations.comment: `RΓ(G, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, a⁻¹j⁻¹E)` for a hypercovering `K` of `G`

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.LocalizationAtPresheaf.derivedSectionsOverPresheafCompositeIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X6, `RΓ(G, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, g⁻¹E)`.** Let `C` be a site with equalizers and
fibre products, `G` a presheaf of sets on `C` and `K` a hypercovering of `G`. Let
`g : Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C)` be the composition of the canonical augmentation
`a : Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C/G)` and of the localization morphism `j : Sh(C/G) ⟶ Sh(C)`. Then

`RΓ(G, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, g⁻¹E)`

naturally in `E` in the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on `C`, in particular for
`E ∈ D⁺(C)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedSectionsOverPresheafCompositeIso :
    derivedSectionsOverPresheaf P.toGrothendieck G ≅
      (compositeInverseImage G P H).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
        Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsTotal
          (hypercoveringSituation (localizationPretopology G P) (localizedHypercovering G P H))
declarations.comment:
for a hypercovering `K` of `G`, `RΓ(G, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, g⁻¹E)` with `g` the
  composition of `a` and `j`; an isomorphism of functors on the unbounded derived category, which
  contains `D⁺(C)`

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.LocalizationAtPresheaf.hypercoveringOfEquivLocalization
declarations.doc:
**A hypercovering of `G` is the same thing as a hypercovering of the site `C/G`.** Let `C` be a
site, given by a pretopology `J`, with equalizers and fibre products, and let `G` be a presheaf of
sets on `C`. Hypercoverings of `G` in `C` (Stacks 09VU) correspond bijectively to hypercoverings of
the localized site `C/G` of Stacks 0791: a hypercovering `K` of `G` goes to the simplicial object
`n ↦ {(K_{n,i}, s_{n,i})}` of `SR(C/G)`, where `s_{n,i}` is the restriction of the augmentation
`F(K_n) ⟶ G` to the summand `h_{K_{n,i}}`, and the three conditions of Stacks 09VU for `K` over `G`
are the three conditions for it over the final presheaf of `C/G`.
declarations.statement:
def hypercoveringOfEquivLocalization :
    HypercoveringOf.{v, w} J G ≃ HypercoveringOfTerminal.{w} (localizationPretopology G J)
declarations.comment:
a hypercovering of `G` in `C` is the same thing as a hypercovering for the site
  `C/G`, for the site `C/G` of Stacks 0791 (coverings: families whose image generates a covering
  sieve of `C`)

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.PresheafLocalization.mem_restrictedTopology_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X6**, the covering sieves of the localization of `C` at a presheaf `G`: a sieve of
an object `(U, s)` of `C/G` belongs to `j.restrictedTopology J`, for
`j = CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda G`, exactly when its image under `j` is a covering sieve of
`U`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_restrictedTopology_iff (X : CostructuredArrow (yoneda (C := C)) G) (S : Sieve X) :
    S ∈ (CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda G).restrictedTopology J X ↔
      S.functorPushforward (CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda G) ∈ J X.left
declarations.comment:
The remark's instruction to define `C/G` for a PRESHEAF of sets `G` exactly as in
  Stacks 0791: the coverings of `C/G` are those coming from coverings of `C`, and the topology they
  generate is already `j.restrictedTopology J`, with no sheaf hypothesis on `G`. Carried: nothing.
  Claimed: this covering characterisation, which is what fixes the topology appearing in
  `nonempty_sheafEquiv_over_sheafification`. Disclaimed: fibre products and equalizers of `C/G`
  (Mathlib's `CostructuredArrow.hasLimitsOfShape_of_isConnected`), the hypercovering
  correspondence, and the `RΓ` transfer statements.

declarations.name: Stacks.Sites.PresheafLocalization.nonempty_sheafEquiv_over_sheafification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X6**, the parenthetical claim: on a small site, the topos of sheaves on the
localization of `C` at a presheaf of sets `G` is the localization of the topos `Sh(C)` at the sheaf
`G^#`, that is, `Sh(C/G)` is equivalent to the slice category `Sh(C)/G^#`.
declarations.statement:
theorem nonempty_sheafEquiv_over_sheafification :
    Nonempty (Sheaf ((CostructuredArrow.proj yoneda G).restrictedTopology J) (Type u) ≌
      Over ((presheafToSheaf J (Type u)).obj G))
declarations.comment:
The parenthetical claim of the remark: the site `C/G` of pairs `(U, s)` with
  `s ∈ G(U)` for a PRESHEAF of sets `G`, with the coverings of `C`, satisfies
  `Sh(C/G) = Sh(C)/G^#`. Carried: Stacks 0791 (`Presheaf.IsSheaf.exists_sheafEquivalence_costructuredArrow_yoneda`) for the SHEAF `G^#`, supplying the right-hand equivalence. Claimed: the equivalence of categories, for a small site. Disclaimed: the rest of the remark — that `C/G` is a site with fibre products and equalizers (Mathlib's `CostructuredArrow.hasLimitsOfShape_of_isConnected`), that hypercoverings of `G` (Stacks 09VU) correspond to hypercoverings of `C/G`, and every `RΓ` transfer statement.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoOver
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X7**, granted the inputs the library does not have. For a site `C` with fibre
products, an object `X` of `C`, a simplicial semi-representable object `K` over `X` — in
particular a hypercovering of `X` — and the augmentation `a : Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C/X)` of
Stacks 0D8B read over the slice site, derived global sections over `X` are derived global
sections on the total site of the inverse image:

`RΓ(X, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, a⁻¹E)`.

The statement is an isomorphism of functors on the *unbounded* derived category of abelian
sheaves on `C/X`, so it holds at every object `E` of `D(C/X)` with no boundedness assumption,
which is the form the source states.

Three hypotheses are carried. `hunit` and `hacyclic` are the two inputs of Stacks 0D8L, the
statement over `C/X` of what Stacks 0D8G states over `C`: the first is the degree-zero
identification of Stacks 0D8K, that the underived unit `F ⟶ a_*a⁻¹F` is an isomorphism, and the
second is that `a⁻¹` of a K-injective complex computes `Ra_*`. `hΓ` is the underived identity
`Γ(C/X, a_*F) = Γ((C/K)_total, F)` on which the factorisation of Stacks 08J6 rests. The derived
content of Stacks 08J6 is *not* assumed: see the module docstring.
declarations.statement:
def derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoOver
    (hunit : IsIso (Augmentation.abelianTotalAdjunction (situationOver P K) (Cat.of (Over X))
      (P.toGrothendieck.over X) (augmentationOver P K)).unit)
    (hacyclic : Augmentation.InverseImageComputesDerivedPushforward (situationOver P K)
      (Cat.of (Over X)) (P.toGrothendieck.over X) (augmentationOver P K))
    (hΓ : Augmentation.abelianTotalPushforward (situationOver P K) (Cat.of (Over X))
          (P.toGrothendieck.over X) (augmentationOver P K) ⋙
        Sheaf.Γ (P.toGrothendieck.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{u} ≅
      Sheaf.Γ (situationOver P K).totalTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u}) :
    Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsBase (Cat.of (Over X)) (P.toGrothendieck.over X) ≅
      Augmentation.derivedTotalInverseImage (situationOver P K) (Cat.of (Over X))
          (P.toGrothendieck.over X) (augmentationOver P K) ⋙
        Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsTotal (situationOver P K)
declarations.comment:
RESTRICTED: granted the two inputs of Tag 0D8L — the underived unit F = a_*a⁻¹F
and the Ra_*-acyclicity of a⁻¹ of a K-injective complex — and the underived identity
Γ(C/X, a_*F) = Γ(total, F); stated for every simplicial semi-representable object over X,
hence for a hypercovering of X

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoOverOfHypercovering
declarations.doc:
Let `C` be a site with fibre products, `X` an object of `C`, `K` a hypercovering of `X` and
`a : Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C/X)` the augmentation of the simplicial family of sites
`n ↦ (C/X)/K_n`. Derived global sections over `X` are derived global sections on the total site of
the inverse image:

`RΓ(X, E) = RΓ((C/K)_total, a⁻¹E)`,

as an isomorphism of functors on the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves on `C/X`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoOverOfHypercovering :
    Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsBase (Cat.of (Over X)) (P.toGrothendieck.over X) ≅
      Augmentation.derivedTotalInverseImage (situationOver P K) (Cat.of (Over X))
          (P.toGrothendieck.over X) (augmentationOver P K) ⋙
        Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsTotal (situationOver P K)

declarations.name: Stacks.CategoryTheory.Hypercovering.IsHypercoveringAugmentation
declarations.doc:
An augmentation `a : U ⟶ X` of a simplicial object `U` of the site given by
the pretopology `J` is a *hypercovering of `X` in `C`* when `{U₀ ⟶ X}` is a covering, the
canonical morphism `U₁ ⟶ U₀ ×_X U₀` generates a covering, and the canonical morphism
`U_{n+1} ⟶ (cosk_n sk_n U)_{n+1}` generates a covering for every `n ≥ 1`, the coskeleton being
formed in the slice category `C/X`.
declarations.statement:
def IsHypercoveringAugmentation (J : Pretopology C) (U : SimplicialObject C)
    (a : U ⟶ (SimplicialObject.const C).obj X) : Prop
declarations.comment: the definition of the section: an augmentation of a simplicial object of the site is a hypercovering of `X` in `C` when the three displayed families are coverings

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.homEquivCommSq
declarations.doc:
A morphism `V/U_n ⟶ W/U_m` of `(C/U)_total` is a pair `(φ, f)` of a simplex map
`φ : [m] ⟶ [n]` and a morphism `f : V ⟶ W` of `C` such that the square formed with `V ⟶ U_n`,
`W ⟶ U_m` and `f_φ : U_n ⟶ U_m` commutes.
declarations.comment: a morphism (φ, f) : V/U_n → W/U_m of (C/U)_total is φ : [m] → [n] and f : V → W with commutative square

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.toAssociatedTotal_comp_totalForget
declarations.doc:
Under the identification of `(C/U)_total` with `(C/K)_total`, the localization functor
`j_total : (C/K)_total ⥤ C/X` is the functor `V/U_n ↦ V/X`: precomposed with
`(C/U)_total ⥤ (C/K)_total` it is `augmentationFunctor` on the nose.
declarations.statement:
theorem toAssociatedTotal_comp_totalForget :
    toAssociatedTotal U a ⋙
        SimplicialSemiRepresentable.totalForget (associatedSimplicialObject.{u} U a) =
      augmentationFunctor U a
declarations.comment: the morphism of topoi a is given by the cocontinuous functor V/U_n ↦ V/X: j_total of (C/K)_total is V/U_n ↦ V/X under the identification

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.associatedTotalEquivalence
declarations.doc:
The equivalence of categories `(C/K)_total ≌ (C/U)_total` between the total site attached
to `K` and the category whose objects are the `V/U_n` and whose morphisms are the pairs `(φ, f)`.
Its functor is `fromAssociatedTotal`, and its inverse is `toAssociatedTotal` by
`associatedTotalEquivalenceInverseIso`.
declarations.comment: the site (C/U)_total, with objects V/U_n and morphisms (φ, f), is (C/K)_total of Remark 0D8C: the equivalence of categories

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.associatedTotalEquivalence_isDenseSubsite
declarations.doc:
The equivalence `(C/K)_total ≌ (C/U)_total` identifies the topologies: it is a dense subsite
inclusion, so a sieve is covering exactly when its image is.
declarations.statement:
theorem associatedTotalEquivalence_isDenseSubsite :
    (associatedTotalEquivalence U a).functor.IsDenseSubsite
      (associatedTotalTopology U a J) (SimplicialOver.totalTopology J U)
declarations.comment: the site (C/U)_total is (C/K)_total of Remark 0D8C: the coverings agree

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.augmentationPushforwardIsoAssociated
declarations.doc:
The direct image of the augmentation `a : Sh((C/U)_total) ⟶ Sh(C/X)` given by
`V/U_n ↦ V/X` is the direct image of the morphism of topoi `Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C/X)` induced
by the total site of `K`, transported along `associatedTotalSheafEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
def augmentationPushforwardIsoAssociated :
    (augmentationMorphismOfTopoi J U a).pushforward ≅
      (associatedTotalSheafEquivalence U a J).inverse ⋙
        (SimplicialSemiRepresentable.totalLocalizationMorphism (J.over X)
          (associatedSimplicialObject.{u} U a)).pushforward
declarations.comment: the augmentation morphism of topoi a : Sh((C/U)_total) → Sh(C/X): the one of Remark 0D8C and the one of V/U_n ↦ V/X agree, direct images

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialOver.augmentationInverseImageIsoAssociated
declarations.doc:
The inverse image of the augmentation `a : Sh((C/U)_total) ⟶ Sh(C/X)` is the inverse image
of the morphism of topoi `Sh((C/K)_total) ⟶ Sh(C/X)` followed by
`associatedTotalSheafEquivalence`.
declarations.statement:
def augmentationInverseImageIsoAssociated :
    (augmentationMorphismOfTopoi J U a).inverseImage ≅
      (SimplicialSemiRepresentable.totalLocalizationMorphism (J.over X)
          (associatedSimplicialObject.{u} U a)).inverseImage ⋙
        (associatedTotalSheafEquivalence U a J).functor
declarations.comment: the augmentation morphism of topoi a : Sh((C/U)_total) → Sh(C/X): the one of Remark 0D8C and the one of V/U_n ↦ V/X agree, inverse images
