declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoAugmented'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09X9.** For a site `C` with fibre products, an object `X` of `C` and
a hypercovering `a : U ⟶ X` of `X` in `C` by a simplicial object `U` of `C`, with
`a : Sh((C/U)_total) ⟶ Sh(C/X)` the augmentation of Stacks 09X8, derived global sections over `X`
are derived global sections on the total site of the inverse image:

`RΓ(X, E) = RΓ((C/U)_total, a⁻¹E)`.

The statement is an isomorphism of functors on the unbounded derived category of abelian sheaves
on `C/X`, so it holds at every object `E` of `D(C/X)`.
declarations.statement:
def derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoAugmented'
    (h : IsHypercoveringAugmentation P U a) :
    Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsBase (Cat.of (Over X)) (P.toGrothendieck.over X) ≅
      Augmentation.derivedTotalInverseImage (totalSituation P U a) (Cat.of (Over X))
          (P.toGrothendieck.over X) (augmentationAugmented P U a) ⋙
        Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsTotal (totalSituation P U a)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.SimplicialSemiRepresentable.derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoAugmented_hom_app'
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09X9, the isomorphism is invertibility of the canonical comparison map.** At every
object `E` of `D(C/X)` the forward map of the isomorphism of Stacks 09X9 is derived global
sections over `X` applied to the canonical map `E ⟶ Ra_*a⁻¹E` of Stacks 0D8L, followed by the
derived factorisation `Ra_* ⋙ RΓ(X, -) ≅ RΓ((C/U)_total, -)` of Stacks 08J6.
declarations.statement:
theorem derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoAugmented_hom_app'
    (h : IsHypercoveringAugmentation P U a)
    (E : DerivedCategory (Sheaf (P.toGrothendieck.over X) AddCommGrpCat.{u})) :
    (derivedGlobalSectionsInverseImageIsoAugmented' P U a h).hom.app E =
      (Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsBase (Cat.of (Over X))
          (P.toGrothendieck.over X)).map
        ((Augmentation.derivedAugmentationUnit (totalSituation P U a) (Cat.of (Over X))
          (P.toGrothendieck.over X) (augmentationAugmented P U a)).app E) ≫
        (Augmentation.derivedGlobalSectionsPushforwardIso (totalSituation P U a)
          (Cat.of (Over X)) (P.toGrothendieck.over X) (augmentationAugmented P U a)
            (abelianTotalPushforwardGammaIsoOver P
              (associatedSimplicialObject.{u} U a))).hom.app
            ((Augmentation.derivedTotalInverseImage (totalSituation P U a) (Cat.of (Over X))
              (P.toGrothendieck.over X) (augmentationAugmented P U a)).obj E)
declarations.comment:
the forward map of the isomorphism is the canonical one — RΓ(X, -) of the
canonical map E ⟶ Ra_*a⁻¹E of Tag 0D8L followed by the derived factorisation of Tag 08J6

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.properHypercoveringSpectralSequence
declarations.doc:
Let `U` be a simplicial object of the category `LC` of Hausdorff, locally quasi-compact spaces
and let `a : U → X` be an augmentation. Let `F` be an abelian sheaf on `X` and let `F_n` be its
pullback to `U_n`. If `U` is a proper hypercovering of `X`, there is a canonical spectral sequence

`E_1^{p,q} = H^q(U_p, F_p)`

converging to `H^{p+q}(X, F)`.

Here `U = Y`, `X = T` and `a = b`; the proper hypercovering condition of Stacks Section 09XA is
`MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering properSurjective`. The spectral sequence is a functor of `F`,
its first page is identified with `H^q(U_p, F_p)` naturally in `F`, and it abuts to `H^n(X, F)`
(`SpectralSequence.AbutsTo`, the convergence of Stacks 01F2).
declarations.statement:
def properHypercoveringSpectralSequence
    (hyp : MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering ProperHypercovering.properSurjective ⟨Y, T, b⟩) :
    ProperHypercoveringSpectralSequence Y T b

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.ProperHypercovering.derivedGlobalSectionsIsoOfIsHypercovering
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09XC.** Let `U` be a simplicial object of `LC` and let `a : U → X` be an
augmentation. If `U` is a proper hypercovering of `X`, then

`RΓ(X, K) = RΓ(U_Zar, a^{-1}K)`

for `K ∈ D⁺(X)`, where `a : Sh(U_Zar) → Sh(X)` is the morphism of topoi of Lemma 09W4.

Here `U = Y`, `X = T` and `a = b`; the proper hypercovering condition of Stacks Section 09XA is
`MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering properSurjective`, `a^{-1}` is the inverse image of abelian
sheaves along the morphism of topoi of Stacks 09W4, extended to `D⁺` degreewise because it is
exact, and `RΓ(X, -)`, `RΓ(U_Zar, -)` are the right derived functors on `D⁺` of the global
sections functors of the space `X` and of the site `U_Zar`. The derived categories are arbitrary
models. The isomorphism is the canonical one: its forward map is the pullback on derived
sections, `RΓ(X, -)` of the unit `K → Ra_*a^{-1}K` followed by the factorization
`RΓ(U_Zar, -) = RΓ(X, -) ∘ Ra_*` of Stacks 08J6 (`derivedGlobalSectionsIsoOfIsHypercovering_hom`).
It is invertible because the unit is, by `isIso_derivedAdjunction_unit_app_of_isHypercovering`
(Stacks 09XS).
declarations.statement:
def derivedGlobalSectionsIsoOfIsHypercovering
    (hyp : MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering properSurjective ⟨Y, T, b⟩) :
    (Sheaf.Γ (Opens.grothendieckTopology (locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop.obj T))
        AddCommGrpCat.{u}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus ≅
      (abelianInverseImage Y T b).mapDerivedCategoryPlus ⋙
        (Sheaf.Γ (SimplicialOpen.grothendieckTopology (U Y))
          AddCommGrpCat.{u}).rightDerivedFunctorPlus

declarations.name: HenselianPair
declarations.doc:
A pair `(A, I)` is henselian if `I` lies in the Jacobson radical of `A` and every
factorization modulo `I` of a monic polynomial into coprime monic factors lifts to `A`.
declarations.statement: def HenselianPair (A : Type*) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) : Prop

declarations.name: idemMap_injective
declarations.doc:
The map on idempotents is injective when `I` is contained in the Jacobson
radical of `A`.
declarations.statement:
theorem idemMap_injective {A : Type*} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : IsContainedInJacobson I) : Function.Injective (idemMap I)

declarations.name: exists_monic_aeval_eq_zero_map_eq_of_sq_sub_mem_map
declarations.doc:
Stacks Tag 09XG, Lemma 15.9.9.

If `A → B` is an integral ring map, `I ⊆ A` is an ideal, and `b ∈ B` maps to an
idempotent in `B / IB` (equivalently, `b ^ 2 - b ∈ IB`), then there exist `d ≥ 1`
and a monic polynomial `f ∈ A[X]` with `f(b) = 0` and `f mod I = X ^ d * (X - 1) ^ d`
in `(A / I)[X]`.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_monic_aeval_eq_zero_map_eq_of_sq_sub_mem_map
    {A B : Type*} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.IsIntegral A B]
    (I : Ideal A) (b : B)
    (hb : b ^ 2 - b ∈ Ideal.map (algebraMap A B) I) :
    ∃ d : ℕ, 1 ≤ d ∧ ∃ f : A[X], f.Monic ∧ aeval b f = 0 ∧
      f.map (algebraMap A (A ⧸ I)) =
        (Polynomial.X ^ d * (Polynomial.X - 1) ^ d : (A ⧸ I)[X])

declarations.name: exists_integralClosure_quotient_prod_and_awayMap_bijective
declarations.doc:
Let `A → B` be a finite type map, let `I ⊆ A`, and suppose that `B / IB` is a product
`C₁ × C₂` for which the canonical map `A / I → C₁` is finite. If `B'` is the
integral closure of `A` in `B`, then `B' / IB'` decomposes as `C₁ × C₂'` compatibly
with `B / IB`. Moreover, there is a `g ∈ B'` whose class is `(1, 0)` and for which the
canonical map `B'_g → B_g` is an isomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_integralClosure_quotient_prod_and_awayMap_bijective
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.FiniteType A B]
    {C₁ : Type w} [CommRing C₁] {C₂ : Type x} [CommRing C₂]
    (e : (B ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A B)) ≃+* C₁ × C₂)
    (hfinite : ((RingHom.fst C₁ C₂).comp (e.toRingHom.comp
      (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap A B)) (algebraMap A B)
        Ideal.le_comap_map))).Finite) :
    ∃ (C₂' : Type v) (_ : CommRing C₂')
      (e' : ((integralClosure A B) ⧸
        I.map (algebraMap A (integralClosure A B))) ≃+* C₁ × C₂')
      (f₂ : C₂' →+* C₂),
      (∀ z,
        e (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap A B))
          ((integralClosure A B).val : integralClosure A B →+* B) (by
            rw [Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap]
            intro a ha
            simpa using Ideal.mem_map_of_mem (algebraMap A B) ha) z) =
          ((e' z).1, f₂ (e' z).2)) ∧
      ∃ g : integralClosure A B,
        e' (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap A (integralClosure A B))) g) = (1, 0) ∧
          Function.Bijective (Localization.awayMapₐ (integralClosure A B).val g)

declarations.name: henselianPair_tfae
declarations.doc:
The five characterizations of a henselian pair: lifting maps from étale algebras,
bijectivity on idempotents for finite or integral algebras, and Gabber's unique-root criterion.
declarations.statement:
public theorem henselianPair_tfae (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) :
    List.TFAE
      [HenselianPair A I,
        ∀ (A' : Type (max u v)) [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A'] [Algebra.Etale A A'],
          ∀ σ : A' →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I,
            ∃ τ : A' →ₐ[A] A, (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A I).comp τ = σ,
        ∀ (B : Type (max u v)) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B],
          InducesBijectionOnIdempotents (I.map (algebraMap A B)),
        ∀ (B : Type (max u v)) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.IsIntegral A B],
          InducesBijectionOnIdempotents (I.map (algebraMap A B)),
        IsContainedInJacobson I ∧
          ∀ (f : A[X]), f.Monic →
            ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n →
              ∀ a : Fin (n + 1) → I,
                f = X ^ n * (X - 1) +
                    ∑ i : Fin (n + 1), C (a i : A) * X ^ (i : ℕ) →
                  ∃! α : A, α - 1 ∈ I ∧ f.IsRoot α]

declarations.name: henselianPair_iff_of_zeroLocus_eq
declarations.doc: Two ideals with the same vanishing locus define henselian pairs simultaneously.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselianPair_iff_of_zeroLocus_eq
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I J : Ideal A)
    (hIJ : PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (I : Set A) = PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (J : Set A)) :
    HenselianPair A I ↔ HenselianPair A J

declarations.name: henselianPair_map_of_isIntegral
declarations.doc: An integral extension of a henselian pair is henselian along the extended ideal.
declarations.statement:
theorem henselianPair_map_of_isIntegral {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A]
    [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.IsIntegral A B] (I : Ideal A)
    (hI : HenselianPair A I) :
    HenselianPair B (I.map (algebraMap A B))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.openEqLocus
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XM, the open locus.** The largest open subscheme of `S` on which two global
sections of a sheaf on the small étale site of `S` agree: the supremum of the opens through
which only agreeing morphisms factor.
declarations.statement: public def openEqLocus : (B.inclusion.obj S).Opens

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.factorsThrough_openEqLocus_iff
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XM, the universal property.** A morphism of the big étale site factors through
the open equality locus exactly when the two sections agree after inverse image along the
induced morphism of small étale topoi.
declarations.statement:
public theorem factorsThrough_openEqLocus_iff (f : T ⟶ S) :
    (∃ g : B.inclusion.obj T ⟶ (openEqLocus B S F s t).toScheme,
      g ≫ (openEqLocus B S F s t).ι = B.inclusion.map f) ↔
      (smallEtalePullback B S T f).map s =
        (smallEtalePullback B S T f).map t

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zariskiInverseImageSectionsComparison
declarations.doc:
The section comparisons for all schemes over `S`, compatible with the canonical
small-pullback restriction maps. The family and the compatibility are chosen together.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def zariskiInverseImageSectionsComparison
    (B : BigZariskiSite.{u}) (S : B.Schemes) :
    { e : ∀ X : BigZariskiOver B S.1 S.property,
        (smallZariskiProjection B S).inverseImage ⋙
          (sheafSections (BigZariskiOver.topology B S.1 S.property)
            (Type (u + 1))).obj (Opposite.op X) ≅
        (smallZariskiBaseChange B X.hom).sheafPullback
            (Type (u + 1))
            (SmallZariski.topology B S.1 S.property)
            (SmallZariski.topology B X.left.1 X.left.property) ⋙
          Sheaf.Γ (SmallZariski.topology B X.left.1 X.left.property)
            (Type (u + 1)) //
      ∀ {X Y : BigZariskiOver B S.1 S.property} (g : Y ⟶ X)
        (F : Sheaf (SmallZariski.topology B S.1 S.property) (Type (u + 1))),
        (e X).hom.app F ≫ zariskiPullbackSectionsRestriction B S g F =
          ((smallZariskiProjection B S).inverseImage.obj F).obj.map g.op ≫
            (e Y).hom.app F }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.zariskiInverseImageSectionsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XN, pullback formula (Zariski case).** For a sheaf `F` on the small Zariski site
of `S` and a scheme `f : X ⟶ S` over `S`, the sections of `π_S⁻¹F` at `X` are the global
sections of the small Zariski pullback `f⁻¹F`, naturally in `F`. Restriction in `X` is recorded
by `AlgebraicGeometry.zariskiInverseImageSectionsIso_naturality`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def zariskiInverseImageSectionsIso
    (B : BigZariskiSite.{u}) (S : B.Schemes) (X : BigZariskiOver B S.1 S.property) :
    (smallZariskiProjection B S).inverseImage ⋙
      (sheafSections (BigZariskiOver.topology B S.1 S.property)
        (Type (u + 1))).obj (Opposite.op X) ≅
    (smallZariskiBaseChange B X.hom).sheafPullback
        (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallZariski.topology B S.1 S.property)
        (SmallZariski.topology B X.left.1 X.left.property) ⋙
      Sheaf.Γ (SmallZariski.topology B X.left.1 X.left.property)
        (Type (u + 1))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleInverseImageSectionsComparison
declarations.doc:
The section comparisons for all schemes over `S`, compatible with the canonical
small-pullback restriction maps. The family and the compatibility are chosen together.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def etaleInverseImageSectionsComparison
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : B.Scheme) :
    { e : ∀ X : BigEtaleOver B S.obj S.property,
        (bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S.obj S.property).inverseImage ⋙
          (sheafSections (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
            (Type (u + 1))).obj (Opposite.op X) ≅
        (smallEtaleBaseChange B X.hom).sheafPullback
            (Type (u + 1))
            (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
            (SmallEtale.topology B X.left.obj X.left.property) ⋙
          Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B X.left.obj X.left.property)
            (Type (u + 1)) //
      ∀ {X Y : BigEtaleOver B S.obj S.property} (g : Y ⟶ X)
        (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1))),
        (e X).hom.app F ≫ etalePullbackSectionsRestriction B S g F =
          ((bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S.obj S.property).inverseImage.obj F).obj.map g.op ≫
            (e Y).hom.app F }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.etaleInverseImageSectionsIso
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XN, pullback formula (étale case).** For a sheaf `F` on the small étale site of
`S` and a scheme `f : X ⟶ S` over `S`, the sections of `π_S⁻¹F` at `X` are the global sections
of the small étale pullback `f⁻¹F`, naturally in `F`. Restriction in `X` is recorded by
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleInverseImageSectionsIso_naturality`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def etaleInverseImageSectionsIso
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : B.Scheme) (X : BigEtaleOver B S.obj S.property) :
    (bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S.obj S.property).inverseImage ⋙
      (sheafSections (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (Type (u + 1))).obj (Opposite.op X) ≅
    (smallEtaleBaseChange B X.hom).sheafPullback
        (Type (u + 1))
        (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.left.obj X.left.property) ⋙
      Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B X.left.obj X.left.property)
        (Type (u + 1))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.smallSiteInverseImage_sections_and_isSheaf_fpqc
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XN.** Let `S` be a scheme, let `τ` be the Zariski or the étale topology and let
`π_S : (Sch/S)_τ ⟶ S_τ` be the projection from the big `τ`-topos over `S` to the small
`τ`-topos of `S`. For a sheaf `F` on the small `τ`-site of `S`:

1. the sections of `π_S⁻¹F` over a scheme `f : X ⟶ S` over `S` are the global sections on the
   small `τ`-site of `X` of the small-site pullback `f⁻¹F`, naturally in `F` and compatibly
   with restriction along any morphism of schemes over `S`;
2. the presheaf underlying `π_S⁻¹F` is a sheaf for the fpqc topology on the big `τ`-site
   over `S`.

The first component of the conjunction is the Zariski case, the second the étale case; the two
are the source's two values of `τ`, which are unrelated site structures here. Within each case
the sections formula is `AlgebraicGeometry.zariskiInverseImageSectionsComparison` resp.
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleInverseImageSectionsComparison` — the family of comparison isomorphisms
together with its compatibility with restriction — and the fpqc sheaf condition is
`AlgebraicGeometry.smallZariskiProjection_inverseImage_isSheaf_fpqc` resp.
`AlgebraicGeometry.bigEtaleToSmallEtale_inverseImage_isSheaf_fpqc`.
declarations.statement:
public noncomputable def smallSiteInverseImage_sections_and_isSheaf_fpqc :
    (∀ (B : BigZariskiSite.{u}) (S : B.Schemes),
        { e : ∀ X : BigZariskiOver B S.obj S.property,
            (smallZariskiProjection B S).inverseImage ⋙
              (sheafSections (BigZariskiOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
                (Type (u + 1))).obj (Opposite.op X) ≅
            (smallZariskiBaseChange B X.hom).sheafPullback
                (Type (u + 1))
                (SmallZariski.topology B S.obj S.property)
                (SmallZariski.topology B X.left.obj X.left.property) ⋙
              Sheaf.Γ (SmallZariski.topology B X.left.obj X.left.property)
                (Type (u + 1)) //
          (∀ {X Y : BigZariskiOver B S.obj S.property} (g : Y ⟶ X)
              (F : Sheaf (SmallZariski.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1))),
              (e X).hom.app F ≫ zariskiPullbackSectionsRestriction B S g F =
                ((smallZariskiProjection B S).inverseImage.obj F).obj.map g.op ≫
                  (e Y).hom.app F) ∧
            ∀ F : Sheaf (SmallZariski.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1)),
              Presheaf.IsSheaf
                ((Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.comap
                  (BigZariskiOver.toScheme B S.obj S.property)).toGrothendieck)
                ((smallZariskiProjection B S).inverseImage.obj F).obj }) ×'
    ∀ (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (S : B.Scheme),
      { e : ∀ X : BigEtaleOver B S.obj S.property,
          (bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S.obj S.property).inverseImage ⋙
            (sheafSections (BigEtaleOver.topology B S.obj S.property)
              (Type (u + 1))).obj (Opposite.op X) ≅
          (smallEtaleBaseChange B X.hom).sheafPullback
              (Type (u + 1))
              (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property)
              (SmallEtale.topology B X.left.obj X.left.property) ⋙
            Sheaf.Γ (SmallEtale.topology B X.left.obj X.left.property)
              (Type (u + 1)) //
        (∀ {X Y : BigEtaleOver B S.obj S.property} (g : Y ⟶ X)
            (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1))),
            (e X).hom.app F ≫ etalePullbackSectionsRestriction B S g F =
              ((bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S.obj S.property).inverseImage.obj F).obj.map
                  g.op ≫
                (e Y).hom.app F) ∧
          ∀ F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B S.obj S.property) (Type (u + 1)),
            Presheaf.IsSheaf
              ((Scheme.fpqcPrecoverage.comap
                (BigEtaleOver.toScheme B S.obj S.property)).toGrothendieck)
              ((bigEtaleToSmallEtaleMorphism B S.obj S.property).inverseImage.obj F).obj }

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.injective_supportedSections_obj
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XQ.** The sections with support in a closed subscheme of an injective abelian
sheaf on the small étale site of the ambient scheme form an injective abelian sheaf on the
small étale site of that subscheme.
declarations.statement:
public theorem injective_supportedSections_obj (I : SmallEtaleAbelianSheaf B X) [Injective I] :
    Injective ((supportedSections B i).obj I)

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isZero_rightDerivedPlus_supportedSections_pushforward
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XR.** The cohomology sheaves with support in a closed subscheme of the direct
image of an injective abelian sheaf on that subscheme vanish in positive degrees.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isZero_rightDerivedPlus_supportedSections_pushforward
    (G : SmallEtaleAbelianSheaf B Z) [Injective G] (p : ℤ) (hp : 0 < p) :
    IsZero (((supportedSections B i).rightDerivedPlus p).obj
      (((smallEtaleBaseChange B i).sheafPushforwardContinuous AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)
        (SmallEtale.topology B Z.obj Z.property)).obj G))

declarations.name: Stacks.Topology.Simplicial.ProperHypercovering.isIso_derivedAdjunction_unit_app_of_isHypercovering
declarations.doc:
Let `U` be a simplicial object of the category `LC` of Hausdorff, locally quasi-compact spaces
and let `a : U → X` be an augmentation. If `a : U → X` gives a proper hypercovering of `X`, then
for `K` in `D⁺(X)` the canonical map

`K ⟶ Ra_*(a^{-1}K)`

is an isomorphism, where `a : Sh(U_Zar) → Sh(X)` is the morphism of topoi of Stacks 09W4.

Here `U = Y`; the proper hypercovering condition of Stacks Section 09XA is
`MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering properSurjective`; `D⁺(X)` is the bounded below derived category
of abelian sheaves on `X`, for any model of the derived categories involved; `a^{-1}` is the exact
inverse image of abelian sheaves of the morphism of topoi of Stacks 09W4 applied degreewise, and
`Ra_*` is the right derived functor on bounded below derived categories of its direct image. The
canonical map is the unit at `K` of the adjunction `a^{-1} ⊣ Ra_*` (`derivedAdjunction`).

By Leray's acyclicity lemma (Stacks 015E) the statement reduces to the underived unit
`F ⟶ a_* a^{-1} F` being an isomorphism, which is Stacks 0DAG, and to `R^q a_*(a^{-1}F) = 0` for
`q > 0`, `isZero_rightDerived_abelianDirectImage_of_isHypercovering`, which is the computation of
the source through the diagram of Stacks 0DAF; see the module documentation.
declarations.statement:
theorem isIso_derivedAdjunction_unit_app_of_isHypercovering
    (hyp : MorphismProperty.IsHypercovering properSurjective ⟨Y, X, a⟩)
    (K : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology
      (locallyQuasiCompactHausdorffToTop.obj X)) AddCommGrpCat.{u})) :
    IsIso ((derivedAdjunction Y X a).unit.app K)

declarations.name: Topology.isHomeomorph_of_isSpectralMap_of_bijective
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XU.** Let `f : X → Y` be a spectral, bijective map of spectral topological
spaces. If generalizations or specializations lift along `f`, then `f` is a homeomorphism.
declarations.statement:
theorem isHomeomorph_of_isSpectralMap_of_bijective [SpectralSpace X] [SpectralSpace Y]
    {f : X → Y} (hspec : IsSpectralMap f) (hbij : Function.Bijective f)
    (hlift : GeneralizingMap f ∨ SpecializingMap f) : IsHomeomorph f

declarations.name: spectralSpace_inverseLimit
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XV**. The inverse limit of a directed inverse system of finite sober topological
spaces is a spectral topological space. Here a sober space in the sense of the Stacks project is a
space that is both `T0Space` and `QuasiSober`.
declarations.statement:
theorem spectralSpace_inverseLimit [Nonempty I] [IsDirectedOrder I] [∀ i, Finite (X i)]
    [∀ i, T0Space (X i)] [∀ i, QuasiSober (X i)]
    (hf : ∀ ⦃i j : I⦄ (h : i ≤ j), Continuous (f h)) :
    SpectralSpace (inverseLimit f)

declarations.name: Topology.spectralSpace_iff_exists_isClosed_withConstructibleTopology
declarations.doc:
A topological space is spectral if and only if it is homeomorphic to a subset of a product of
copies of the Sierpinski space which is closed for the constructible topology of that product.
declarations.statement:
theorem spectralSpace_iff_exists_isClosed_withConstructibleTopology (X : Type u)
    [TopologicalSpace X] :
    SpectralSpace X ↔
      ∃ (I : Type u) (S : Set (SierpinskiProduct I)),
        IsClosed[constructibleTopology (SierpinskiProduct I)] S ∧ Nonempty (X ≃ₜ S)

declarations.name: spectralSpace_iff_isDirectedInverseLimitOfFiniteSober
declarations.doc:
A topological space is spectral if and only if it is a directed inverse limit of finite
sober topological spaces.
declarations.statement:
theorem spectralSpace_iff_isDirectedInverseLimitOfFiniteSober
    (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] :
    SpectralSpace X ↔ IsDirectedInverseLimitOfFiniteSober X

declarations.name: IsTopologicalPartition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XZ**.
A *topological partition* of `X` is a set-theoretic partition of `X` all of whose
parts are locally closed.
declarations.statement: def IsTopologicalPartition (c : Set (Set X)) : Prop

declarations.name: local_Refines
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09XZ**.
A collection `P` of subsets of `X` *refines* a collection `Q` when every member of
`P` is contained in some member of `Q`.
declarations.statement: def local_Refines (P Q : Set (Set X)) : Prop

declarations.name: IsGoodStratification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09Y0**.
A *good stratification* of a topological space `X`, indexed by `I`, is a
family of subsets `S : I → Set X` which forms a partition (the sets are
pairwise disjoint, each nonempty, and their union covers `X`) and which
satisfies the frontier condition: if `S i ∩ closure (S j) ≠ ∅`, then
`S i ⊆ closure (S j)`.
declarations.statement:
structure IsGoodStratification {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] {I : Type*}
    (S : I → Set X) : Prop

declarations.name: Stratification
declarations.doc:
A *stratification* of a topological space `X`, indexed by a partially ordered type `I`, is an
indexed family `strata : I → Set X` whose members are pairwise disjoint and cover `X` (a partition
`X = ∐_{i} X_i`), and such that the closure of each stratum is contained in the union of the
strata at lower or equal indices.
declarations.statement:
structure Stratification (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X]
    (I : Type*) [PartialOrder I]

declarations.name: closedZ_of_locallyFiniteStratification
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09Y2** (1).
Let `X` be a locally finite stratification of `α` with partial order `≤` on `I`,
and for each `i` let `Z i = ⋃ (j ≤ i) X j`. Then each `Z i` is closed, and for
all `i, j` one has `Z i ∩ Z j = ⋃ (k ≤ i ∧ k ≤ j) Z k`.
declarations.statement:
theorem closedZ_of_locallyFiniteStratification [PartialOrder I] {X : I → Set α}
    (h : IsLocallyFiniteStratification X)
    (Z : I → Set α) (hZ : ∀ i, Z i = ⋃ j ∈ {j | j ≤ i}, X j) :
    (∀ i, IsClosed (Z i)) ∧
    (∀ i j, Z i ∩ Z j = ⋃ k ∈ {k | k ≤ i ∧ k ≤ j}, Z k)

declarations.name: locallyFiniteStratification_of_closedZ
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09Y2** (2).
Let `I` be a partially ordered set and `{Z i}` a family of closed subsets of `α`
that cover `α`, are locally finite, and satisfy
`Z i ∩ Z j = ⋃ (k ≤ i ∧ k ≤ j) Z k`. Then the sets `X i = Z i \ ⋃ (j < i) Z j`,
with the partial order `≤` on `I`, form a locally finite stratification of
`α`.
declarations.statement:
theorem locallyFiniteStratification_of_closedZ [PartialOrder I] {Z : I → Set α}
    (hclosed : ∀ i, IsClosed (Z i))
    (hcover : ⋃ i, Z i = Set.univ)
    (hlf : LocallyFinite Z)
    (hint : ∀ i j, Z i ∩ Z j = ⋃ k ∈ {k | k ≤ i ∧ k ≤ j}, Z k)
    (X : I → Set α) (hX : ∀ i, X i = Z i \ ⋃ j ∈ {j | j < i}, Z j) :
    IsLocallyFiniteStratification X

declarations.name: exists_finite_stratification_refining_finite_partition
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09Y3**.
Every finite partition of a topological space by locally closed subsets is refined
by a finite stratification.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finite_stratification_refining_finite_partition
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (P : TopPartition X ι) :
    ∃ (κ : Type) (_ : Finite κ) (_ : PartialOrder κ) (S : TopStratification X κ),
      S.toTopPartition.Refines P

declarations.name: exists_finiteStratification_refining_constructible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09Y4**.
If a topological space `X` is covered by a finite family `T₁, …, Tₙ` of
constructible subsets, then there exists a finite stratification `X = ⨆ Xᵢ` such
that each stratum is constructible and each `Tₖ` is a union of strata.
declarations.statement:
theorem exists_finiteStratification_refining_constructible
    {n : ℕ} (T : Fin n → Set X)
    (hT : ∀ k, Topology.IsConstructible (T k))
    (_hcover : ⋃ k, T k = Set.univ) :
    ∃ (𝒮 : FiniteStratification X),
      (∀ i, Topology.IsConstructible (𝒮.S i)) ∧
      (∀ k, ∃ I : Set 𝒮.ι, T k = ⋃ i ∈ I, 𝒮.S i)

declarations.name: main_theorem09Y5
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a Noetherian topological space. Any finite partition of `X` can be refined by a
finite good stratification of `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem main_theorem09Y5 (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X]
    [TopologicalSpace.NoetherianSpace X]
    (P : TopPartitionOpenCover.{u, v} X) (hP : P.IsFinite) :
    ∃ P' : TopPartitionOpenCover.{u, u} X,
      P'.IsFinite ∧ P'.IsGood ∧ P'.Refines P

declarations.name: isConnected_zeroLocus_add
declarations.doc:
For a henselian pair `(A, I)` and a prime ideal `p` of `A`, the closed subset
`V(p + I)` of `Spec(A)` is connected.
declarations.statement:
theorem isConnected_zeroLocus_add {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I p : Ideal A)
    (hI : HenselianPair A I) (hp : p.IsPrime) :
    IsConnected (zeroLocus ((p + I : Ideal A) : Set A) : Set (PrimeSpectrum A))

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleSetSheaf_of_hasFiniteQCSRepresentableCoequalizerPresentation
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09Y9, the implication from a presentation to constructibility.** Let `X` be a
quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme of a big étale site and let `F` be a sheaf of sets on
`X_étale` which is a coequalizer of two maps between finite coproducts of sheaves represented by
quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects of `X_étale`. Then `F` is a constructible sheaf of
sets.
declarations.statement:
public theorem isConstructibleSetSheaf_of_hasFiniteQCSRepresentableCoequalizerPresentation
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme) [CompactSpace X.obj] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X.obj]
    {F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1))}
    (hF : HasFiniteQCSRepresentableCoequalizerPresentation B X F) :
    IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X F
declarations.comment: the implication from a finite coequalizer presentation by representables of quasi-compact quasi-separated etale objects to constructibility, for sheaves of sets; the reverse implication, from constructibility to the existence of such a presentation, is not part of this statement

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_representable_epi_of_isConstructibleSetSheaf
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09Y9, the surjection half.** A constructible sheaf of sets on the small étale site
of a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme receives an epimorphism from a finite coproduct of
sheaves represented by quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects of the site.

This is `AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiCompact_of_isConstructibleSetSheaf_unconditional` followed by
the presentation of a quasi-compact sheaf by finitely many affine representables; both the
conservativity of geometric points and the finite affine covering it uses are theorems of the
library, so nothing is assumed.
declarations.statement:
public theorem exists_finite_representable_epi_of_isConstructibleSetSheaf
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme) [CompactSpace X.obj] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X.obj]
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1)))
    (hF : IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X F) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → SmallEtale B X.obj X.property),
      (∀ i, CompactSpace ((SmallEtale.toScheme B X.obj X.property).obj (U i)) ∧
        QuasiSeparatedSpace ((SmallEtale.toScheme B X.obj X.property).obj (U i))) ∧
      ∃ p : (∐ fun i ↦ (Sheaf.sheafifiedYoneda
        (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property)).obj (U i)) ⟶ F, Epi p
declarations.comment: the surjection half: a constructible sheaf of sets on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is the target of an epimorphism from a finite coproduct of sheaves represented by quasi-compact quasi-separated objects

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.isConstructibleSetSheaf_iff_hasFiniteQCSRepresentableCoequalizerPresentation_unconditional
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09Y9.** On a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme the
constructible sheaves of sets on the small étale site are exactly the sheaves admitting a
coequalizer presentation by finite coproducts of sheaves represented by quasi-compact and
quasi-separated étale objects.

Nothing beyond quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of `X` is assumed. Stacks 03S0 is
`AlgebraicGeometry.etaleFiniteStratificationExists` and the conservativity of geometric points of
Stacks 03PU is `AlgebraicGeometry.jointlyFaithful_smallEtaleSetPullback`, both theorems of the
library. Stacks 0245 is not used at all: the quasi-compactness step is
`AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasiCompact_of_isConstructibleSetSheaf_unconditional` above, which refines
the covering produced by étale-local representability instead of descending along it.
declarations.statement:
public theorem
    isConstructibleSetSheaf_iff_hasFiniteQCSRepresentableCoequalizerPresentation_unconditional
    (B : BigEtaleSite.{u}) (X : B.Scheme) [CompactSpace X.obj] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X.obj]
    (F : Sheaf (SmallEtale.topology B X.obj X.property) (Type (u + 1))) :
    IsConstructibleSetSheaf B X F ↔
      HasFiniteQCSRepresentableCoequalizerPresentation B X F

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.integralFiniteSystemOfIsIntegralHom
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09YA.** An integral morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` of algebraic spaces over `S`, with `Y`
quasi-compact and quasi-separated, presents `X` as a directed limit `X = lim X_i` of algebraic
spaces `X_i` finite and of finite presentation over `Y`.

The system is a directed inverse system of algebraic spaces over `Y` indexed by a nonempty
directed preorder, with a cone from `X` compatible with `f` which is a limit cone; every stage is
finite and of finite presentation over `Y`
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Space.IntegralFiniteSystem`).  The stages are the relative spectra
`\underline{Spec}_Y(𝒜_i)` (Stacks 081W) of the finite, finitely presented algebras of
Stacks 082C presenting `f_* 𝒪_X`.
declarations.statement:
def integralFiniteSystemOfIsIntegralHom (f : X ⟶ Y) (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hY : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS Y) (hf : IsIntegralHom B S hS f)
    (hYqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS Y)
    (hYqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal Y) :
    IntegralFiniteSystem B S hS f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsIntegralSurjectiveSchemeCover_and_refining
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09YB.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic
space over a scheme `S`. Then

1. there is a surjective integral morphism to `X` from the presheaf represented by an object of
   the big fppf site — a scheme over `S` — and
2. given a surjective étale morphism `p : U ⟶ X` from an algebraic space, such a cover can be
   chosen so that it factors through `p` on a representable open subspace neighbourhood of
   every one of its points.

**Both clauses are proved, over no hypothesis.** Clause (1) is the source's induction on a bound
for the degree of the geometric fibres of an étale chart, performed in
`StacksFrontier.AlgebraicGeometry.Spaces.IntegralSchemeCoverInduction`; clause (2) is deduced here
from clause (1) by the unconditional Stacks 0CP0.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsIntegralSurjectiveSchemeCover_and_refining
    (hZ : B.Contains (⊤_ Scheme.{u}))
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS hZ X) :
    ExistsIntegralSurjectiveSchemeCover B S hS X ∧
      ∀ (U : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U →
        ∀ p : U ⟶ X, IsSurjective B S hS p → IsEtale B S hS p →
          ∃ (Y : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj Y ⟶ X),
            IsSurjective B S hS f ∧ IsIntegralHom B S hS f ∧
              FactorsZariskiLocallyThrough B S hS p Y f

declarations.name: AlgebraicGeometry.Space.existsFiniteSurjectiveSchemeCover_and_refining
declarations.doc:
**Stacks Project, Tag 09YC.** Let `X` be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space
over a scheme `S`. Then

1. there is a surjective finite morphism of finite presentation to `X` from the presheaf
   represented by an object of the big fppf site — a scheme over `S` — and
2. given a surjective étale morphism `p : U ⟶ X` from an algebraic space, such a cover can be
   chosen so that it factors through `p` on a representable open subspace neighbourhood of every
   one of its points.

Clause (1) is a finite surjective scheme cover refined through an affine étale chart by Stacks
0CP0 and embedded in a finite cover of finite presentation; clause (2) is clause (1) refined by
Stacks 0CP0.
declarations.statement:
theorem existsFiniteSurjectiveSchemeCover_and_refining
    (X : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u)
    (hX : IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqc : IsQuasiCompactSpace B S hS X)
    (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B S hS B.contains_terminal X) :
    (∃ (Y : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj Y ⟶ X),
        IsSurjective B S hS f ∧ IsFinite B S hS f ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS f) ∧
      ∀ (U : (BigFppfOver B S hS)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u), IsAlgebraicSpace B S hS U →
        ∀ p : U ⟶ X, IsSurjective B S hS p → IsEtale B S hS p →
          ∃ (Y : BigFppfOver B S hS) (f : yoneda.obj Y ⟶ X),
            IsSurjective B S hS f ∧ IsFinite B S hS f ∧ IsFinitePresentation B S hS f ∧
              FactorsZariskiLocallyThrough B S hS p Y f

declarations.name: isConstructible_subtype_preimage_of_isRetrocompact
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09YF**.
If `T ⊆ X` is retrocompact, quasi-compact opens form a basis for the topology on `X`, and
`E` is constructible in `X`, then `E ∩ T`, as a subset of the subspace `T`, is constructible
in `T`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isConstructible_subtype_preimage_of_isRetrocompact
    {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X]
    (T : Set X) (E : Set X)
    (hT : IsRetrocompact T)
    (hbasis : TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis {U : Set X | IsOpen U ∧ IsCompact U})
    (hE : Topology.IsConstructible E) :
    Topology.IsConstructible (X := T) (Subtype.val ⁻¹' E)

declarations.name: isRetrocompact_of_isConstructible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09YH**.
Every constructible subset of a topological space is retrocompact.
declarations.statement:
theorem isRetrocompact_of_isConstructible {E : Set X} (h : IsConstructibleViaCompactOpens E) :
    IsRetrocompact E

declarations.name: isConstructible_preimage_subtypeVal_of_isConstructible
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09YI.** Let `X` be a topological space whose topology has a basis
of quasi-compact opens. For two constructible subsets `E, E'` of `X`, the
intersection `E ∩ E'` is constructible in `E` (i.e. its image as a subset of
the subspace `E ⊆ X`).

Equivalently in Lean: the preimage `(Subtype.val : E → X) ⁻¹' E'` is
constructible in the subspace topology of `E`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isConstructible_preimage_subtypeVal_of_isConstructible
    [PrespectralSpace X] {E E' : Set X}
    (hE : IsConstructible E) (hE' : IsConstructible E') :
    IsConstructible ((Subtype.val : E → X) ⁻¹' E')

declarations.name: isConstructibleSet_of_isConstructibleSet_in_constructible
declarations.doc:
Let `X` be a topological space with a basis
of quasi-compact opens. Let `E ⊆ X` be constructible in `X`, and let
`F ⊆ E` be constructible in the topological subspace `E`. Then `F`, viewed
as a subset of `X` via the inclusion `Subtype.val : E → X`, is
constructible in `X`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isConstructibleSet_of_isConstructibleSet_in_constructible
    (hX : PrespectralSpace X)
    {E : Set X} (hE : IsConstructibleSet E)
    {F : Set ↥E} (hF : IsConstructibleSet F) :
    IsConstructibleSet (Subtype.val '' F : Set X)

declarations.name: isConstructible_iff_isConstructible_preimage
declarations.doc:
**Stacks 09YK**.
For `X` a topological space whose topology has a basis of quasi-compact opens and
`E₁, …, Eₘ` a finite family of constructible subsets covering `X`, a subset `S ⊆ X` is
constructible in `X` if and only if its preimage in each `Eⱼ` is constructible in `Eⱼ`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isConstructible_iff_isConstructible_preimage
    (h_basis : IsTopologicalBasis { U : Set X | IsOpen U ∧ IsCompact U })
    {m : ℕ} (E : Fin m → Set X)
    (hE_cons : ∀ j, IsConstructible (E j))
    (hcover : (⋃ j, E j) = Set.univ)
    (S : Set X) :
    IsConstructible S ↔
      ∀ j, IsConstructible ((Subtype.val : ↥(E j) → X) ⁻¹' S)

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sites.InverseSystem.InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.exists_precoverage_of_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Colimits of sites.** Let `D` be an inverse system of sites with finite coverings over a
cofiltered index category (Stacks 0A34) — so each covering sieve of `D.J i` contains a finite
covering family, which is what makes the coverings of Stacks 00VH generate `D.J i` — and let the
functors `u i : D.C i ⥤ C` exhibit `C` as the colimit of the underlying categories: they are
compatible with the transition functors (`hu`), every object of `C` comes from some `D.C i`
(`hobj`), and the morphisms of `C` between objects coming from `D.C i` are the colimit over
`a : j ⟶ i` of the morphisms of `D.C j` between the transported objects (`hhom`, `hhom_inj`).

Then the families of morphisms of `C` that are images under the `u i` of the (finite) coverings of
the `D.C i` are the coverings of a site structure on `C` in the sense of Stacks 00VH: they contain
every one-element family given by an isomorphism, they are stable under refinement by coverings,
and for every covering of `X` and every `f : Y ⟶ X` the fibre products of the members of the
covering with `f` exist and again form a covering, of `Y`.

This is the form of Stacks 09YL that applies to an inverse system of étale sites;
`InverseSystemOfSites.exists_precoverage_of_colimit` below is its special case for a system all of
whose covering sieves happen to be finitely generated.
declarations.statement:
public theorem InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.exists_precoverage_of_colimit {C : Type w}
    [Category.{w'} C] (D : InverseSystemOfFiniteSites) (u : ∀ i, D.C i ⥤ C)
    (hu : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : i ⟶ j), D.u a ⋙ u i = u j)
    (hobj : ∀ X : C, ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i), (u i).obj Y = X)
    (hhom :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (f : (u i).obj X ⟶ (u i).obj Y),
        ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (g : (D.u a).obj X ⟶ (D.u a).obj Y),
          (u j).map g =
            eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) X) ≫ f ≫ eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) Y).symm)
    (hhom_inj :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (g₁ g₂ : X ⟶ Y),
        (u i).map g₁ = (u i).map g₂ → ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i), (D.u a).map g₁ = (D.u a).map g₂) :
    ∃ K : Precoverage C,
      -- the coverings of `C` are the images of the finite coverings of the `D.C i`
      (∀ (X : C) (R : Presieve X),
          R ∈ K X ↔
            ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i) (h : (u i).obj Y = X) (S : Presieve Y),
              S ∈ (D.J i).toPrecoverage Y ∧
                S ∈ Precoverage.finite (D.C i) Y ∧ R = h ▸ S.map (u i)) ∧
        -- Stacks 00VH (1): a one-element family given by an isomorphism is a covering
        K.HasIsos ∧
        -- Stacks 00VH (2): coverings are stable under refinement by coverings
        (∀ (X : C) (R : Presieve X) (T : ∀ ⦃Y : C⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X), R f → Presieve Y),
          R ∈ K X → (∀ ⦃Y : C⦄ (f : Y ⟶ X) (hf : R f), T f hf ∈ K Y) → R.bind T ∈ K X) ∧
        -- Stacks 00VH (3): the fibre products of a covering along any morphism exist, and cover
        ∃ _ : K.HasPullbacks,
          ∀ (X Y : C) (f : Y ⟶ X) (R : Presieve X) [R.HasPullbacks f],
            R ∈ K X → R.pullbackArrows f ∈ K Y

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sites.InverseSystem.InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.sections_colimit_pullback_of_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Sections of a colimit of sheaves on a colimit of sites.** In the situation of Stacks 0A34,
let the functors `u i : D.C i ⥤ C` exhibit the small category `C` as the colimit of the `D.C i`
(`hu`, `hobj`, `hhom`, `hhom_inj`) and let `K` be the collection of coverings of `C` of
Stacks 09YL (`hK`), so that each `u i` defines a morphism of sites `f_i : C → C_i`
(Stacks 0A35).

Let `F i` be a sheaf of sets on `(D.C i, D.J i)` for every `i`, and for `a : j ⟶ i` let
`ψ a : F i ⟶ f_{a,*}F j` be the adjoint of a map `φ_a : f_a^{-1}F_i → F_j` of sheaves on `D.C j`,
subject to the cocycle condition `hψ`. Let `G` be the colimit `colim_i f_i^{-1}F_i`, presented by
its universal property: `ι i` is the adjoint of the structure map `f_i^{-1}F_i ⟶ G` (`hι`) and
every compatible family of maps to a sheaf `H` on `C` factors uniquely through it (`hG`).

Then for every object `X` of `D.C i` the sections of `G` over `u_i(X)` are the filtered colimit
over the arrows `a : j ⟶ i` of the sections of `F j` over `u_a(X)`: the canonical maps `ρ a`
(`hρ`) are jointly surjective, and two sections of `F j` over `u_a(X)` with the same image under
`ρ a` agree after applying `ψ b` for some `b : k ⟶ j`.
declarations.statement:
public theorem InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.sections_colimit_pullback_of_colimit {C : Type w}
    [SmallCategory C] (D : InverseSystemOfFiniteSites.{u₁, u₂, w}) (u : ∀ i, D.C i ⥤ C)
    (hu : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : i ⟶ j), D.u a ⋙ u i = u j)
    (hobj : ∀ X : C, ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i), (u i).obj Y = X)
    (hhom :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (f : (u i).obj X ⟶ (u i).obj Y),
        ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (g : (D.u a).obj X ⟶ (D.u a).obj Y),
          (u j).map g =
            eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) X) ≫ f ≫ eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) Y).symm)
    (hhom_inj :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (g₁ g₂ : X ⟶ Y),
        (u i).map g₁ = (u i).map g₂ → ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i), (D.u a).map g₁ = (D.u a).map g₂)
    (K : Precoverage C)
    (hK :
      ∀ (X : C) (R : Presieve X),
        R ∈ K X ↔
          ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i) (h : (u i).obj Y = X) (S : Presieve Y),
            S ∈ (D.J i).toPrecoverage Y ∧ S ∈ Precoverage.finite (D.C i) Y ∧ R = h ▸ S.map (u i))
    -- the sheaves `F i` and, in adjoint form, the maps `φ_a : f_a^{-1}F_i → F_j`
    (F : ∀ i, Sheaf (D.J i) (Type w))
    (ψ : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i), (F i).obj ⟶ (D.u a).op ⋙ (F j).obj)
    -- the cocycle condition `φ_{b ∘ a} = φ_b ∘ f_b^{-1}φ_a`
    (hψ :
      ∀ {i j k : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (b : k ⟶ j) (V : D.C i) (x : (F i).obj.obj (op V)),
        (ψ (b ≫ a)).app (op V) x =
          (F k).obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (D.comp b a) V).symm))
            ((ψ b).app (op ((D.u a).obj V)) ((ψ a).app (op V) x)))
    -- `G = colim_i f_i^{-1}F_i`, presented by its universal property
    (G : Sheaf K.toGrothendieck (Type w)) (ι : ∀ i, (F i).obj ⟶ (u i).op ⋙ G.obj)
    (hι :
      ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (V : D.C i) (x : (F i).obj.obj (op V)),
        (ι i).app (op V) x =
          G.obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) V)))
            ((ι j).app (op ((D.u a).obj V)) ((ψ a).app (op V) x)))
    (hG :
      ∀ (H : Sheaf K.toGrothendieck (Type w)) (g : ∀ i, (F i).obj ⟶ (u i).op ⋙ H.obj),
        (∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (V : D.C i) (x : (F i).obj.obj (op V)),
            (g i).app (op V) x =
              H.obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) V)))
                ((g j).app (op ((D.u a).obj V)) ((ψ a).app (op V) x))) →
          ∃! h : G ⟶ H,
            ∀ (i : D.I) (V : D.C i) (x : (F i).obj.obj (op V)),
              (g i).app (op V) x = h.hom.app (op ((u i).obj V)) ((ι i).app (op V) x))
    (i : D.I) (X : D.C i)
    -- the canonical maps `F_j(u_a(X)) → G(u_i(X))`
    (ρ :
      ∀ {j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i), (F j).obj.obj (op ((D.u a).obj X)) → G.obj.obj (op ((u i).obj X)))
    (hρ :
      ∀ {j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (t : (F j).obj.obj (op ((D.u a).obj X))),
        ρ a t =
          G.obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) X)))
            ((ι j).app (op ((D.u a).obj X)) t)) :
    -- every section of `G` over `u_i(X)` comes from some level below `i`
    (∀ s : G.obj.obj (op ((u i).obj X)),
        ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (t : (F j).obj.obj (op ((D.u a).obj X))), ρ a t = s) ∧
      -- two sections with the same image agree at a further level
      ∀ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (t t' : (F j).obj.obj (op ((D.u a).obj X))),
        ρ a t = ρ a t' →
          ∃ (k : D.I) (b : k ⟶ j),
            (ψ b).app (op ((D.u a).obj X)) t = (ψ b).app (op ((D.u a).obj X)) t'
declarations.comment: weak-system variant (Stacks 00VH finite coverings): The sections over `u_i(X_i)` of the colimit `colim f_i^{-1}F_i` of a system of sheaves on an inverse system of sites are the filtered colimit of the sections `F_j(u_a(X_i))` over the arrows `a : j → i`.

declarations.name: CategoryTheory.Sites.InverseSystem.InverseSystemOfSites.sections_colimit_pullback_of_colimit
declarations.doc:
**Sections of a colimit of sheaves on a colimit of sites.** In the situation of Stacks 0A34,
let the functors `u i : D.C i ⥤ C` exhibit the small category `C` as the colimit of the `D.C i`
(`hu`, `hobj`, `hhom`, `hhom_inj`) and let `K` be the collection of coverings of `C` of
Stacks 09YL (`hK`), so that each `u i` defines a morphism of sites `f_i : C → C_i`
(Stacks 0A35).

`ψ a : F i ⟶ f_{a,*}F j` be the adjoint of a map `φ_a : f_a^{-1}F_i → F_j` of sheaves on `D.C j`,
subject to the cocycle condition `hψ`. Let `G` be the colimit `colim_i f_i^{-1}F_i`, presented by

declarations.statement:
public theorem InverseSystemOfSites.sections_colimit_pullback_of_colimit {C : Type w}
    [SmallCategory C] (D : InverseSystemOfSites.{u₁, u₂, w}) (u : ∀ i, D.C i ⥤ C)
    (hu : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : i ⟶ j), D.u a ⋙ u i = u j)
    (hobj : ∀ X : C, ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i), (u i).obj Y = X)
    (hhom :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (f : (u i).obj X ⟶ (u i).obj Y),
        ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (g : (D.u a).obj X ⟶ (D.u a).obj Y),
          (u j).map g =
            eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) X) ≫ f ≫ eqToHom (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) Y).symm)
    (hhom_inj :
      ∀ (i : D.I) (X Y : D.C i) (g₁ g₂ : X ⟶ Y),
        (u i).map g₁ = (u i).map g₂ → ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i), (D.u a).map g₁ = (D.u a).map g₂)
    (K : Precoverage C)
    (hK :
      ∀ (X : C) (R : Presieve X),
        R ∈ K X ↔
          ∃ (i : D.I) (Y : D.C i) (h : (u i).obj Y = X) (S : Presieve Y),
            S ∈ (D.J i).toPrecoverage Y ∧ S ∈ Precoverage.finite (D.C i) Y ∧ R = h ▸ S.map (u i))
    -- the sheaves `F i` and, in adjoint form, the maps `φ_a : f_a^{-1}F_i → F_j`
    (F : ∀ i, Sheaf (D.J i) (Type w))
    (ψ : ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i), (F i).obj ⟶ (D.u a).op ⋙ (F j).obj)
    -- the cocycle condition `φ_{b ∘ a} = φ_b ∘ f_b^{-1}φ_a`
    (hψ :
      ∀ {i j k : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (b : k ⟶ j) (V : D.C i) (x : (F i).obj.obj (op V)),
        (ψ (b ≫ a)).app (op V) x =
          (F k).obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (D.comp b a) V).symm))
            ((ψ b).app (op ((D.u a).obj V)) ((ψ a).app (op V) x)))
    -- `G = colim_i f_i^{-1}F_i`, presented by its universal property
    (G : Sheaf K.toGrothendieck (Type w)) (ι : ∀ i, (F i).obj ⟶ (u i).op ⋙ G.obj)
    (hι :
      ∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (V : D.C i) (x : (F i).obj.obj (op V)),
        (ι i).app (op V) x =
          G.obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) V)))
            ((ι j).app (op ((D.u a).obj V)) ((ψ a).app (op V) x)))
    (hG :
      ∀ (H : Sheaf K.toGrothendieck (Type w)) (g : ∀ i, (F i).obj ⟶ (u i).op ⋙ H.obj),
        (∀ {i j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (V : D.C i) (x : (F i).obj.obj (op V)),
            (g i).app (op V) x =
              H.obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) V)))
                ((g j).app (op ((D.u a).obj V)) ((ψ a).app (op V) x))) →
          ∃! h : G ⟶ H,
            ∀ (i : D.I) (V : D.C i) (x : (F i).obj.obj (op V)),
              (g i).app (op V) x = h.hom.app (op ((u i).obj V)) ((ι i).app (op V) x))
    (i : D.I) (X : D.C i)
    -- the canonical maps `F_j(u_a(X)) → G(u_i(X))`
    (ρ :
      ∀ {j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i), (F j).obj.obj (op ((D.u a).obj X)) → G.obj.obj (op ((u i).obj X)))
    (hρ :
      ∀ {j : D.I} (a : j ⟶ i) (t : (F j).obj.obj (op ((D.u a).obj X))),
        ρ a t =
          G.obj.map (eqToHom (congrArg op (Functor.congr_obj (hu a) X)))
            ((ι j).app (op ((D.u a).obj X)) t)) :
    -- every section of `G` over `u_i(X)` comes from some level below `i`
    (∀ s : G.obj.obj (op ((u i).obj X)),
        ∃ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (t : (F j).obj.obj (op ((D.u a).obj X))), ρ a t = s) ∧
      -- two sections with the same image agree at a further level
      ∀ (j : D.I) (a : j ⟶ i) (t t' : (F j).obj.obj (op ((D.u a).obj X))),
        ρ a t = ρ a t' →
          ∃ (k : D.I) (b : k ⟶ j),
            (ψ b).app (op ((D.u a).obj X)) t = (ψ b).app (op ((D.u a).obj X)) t'
